### B881666 — The current project is listed twice in the project switcher `[App shell / project switcher]` (bug) #site-planner #scheduler #ui  *(owner live repro on planyr.io, 2026-08-30, AFTER PR #1232/#1234 merged, on Goose Creek (`smqfy48tlk9j`), confirmed on both the Site and Schedule tabs: opening the project switcher shows the current project pinned at the top marked "current" AND again immediately below as an ordinary recents row with a relative timestamp ("just now"/"1m ago"). The owner confirmed elsewhere in the app (the Sites panel) shows exactly one Goose Creek — a display dedupe miss, not a duplicate project — and asked whether #1232's list-merge PR introduced it or it predates that PR. Minted **B881666 / V496865** from this branch's reserved block B881664–B881679 · V496864–V496879 against `origin/main` cf120452. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `withCurrentProject`, `unionProjectLists`, `internalProjects`, `linkedSiteId`, project switcher dupe: B853266/B854xxx (Done) built `withCurrentProject`/`unionProjectLists` themselves — this is a defect IN that code, not a duplicate feature request. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **TWO CONFIRMED, DISTINCT ROOT CAUSES in `ProjectBreadcrumb.jsx`, both fixed — and the owner's question answered directly: NEITHER predates #1232's list-merge work; both are genuine defects IN `unionProjectLists`/`withCurrentProject`, the functions that PR's own B854xxx work built. #1232 introduced the mechanism these bugs live in, not merely exposed a pre-existing one.**
- Verify: live — the repro explicitly cites the owner's real project (Goose Creek), a mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class. Both mechanisms are proven in the sandbox below via a real postMessage-speaking iframe stub and a real multi-project switch; confirmed live 2026-08-31 (V496865, drained from `verification-inbox/2026-08-31-b881664-b881666-live-pass.md`) — no third mechanism was found.
- **ROOT CAUSE 1 — a namespace mismatch (the Schedule tab).** Scheduler.jsx's controlled `currentProject` is the routed site's LINKED SCHEDULE object once one exists (`{id, name, linkedSiteId, linkedSiteName}`) — its `.id` is the SCHEDULE's own id (a small integer-like string), not the site-GROUP id `listProjects()` keys its registry by. `withCurrentProject`'s dedupe check (`projects.some(p => p.id === currentProject.id)`) always missed against that id, so `ProjectBreadcrumb.jsx`'s `refresh()` unconditionally prepended a synthetic registry entry keyed by the schedule id and marked "current" — sitting beside the REAL, group-id-keyed registry entry for the same project (which the row-render's own `cur` check does NOT mark current, since its id doesn't match either — hence the ordinary timestamp on the second row). Separately, `unionProjectLists` never recognized that a controlled entry's `linkedSiteId` and a registry entry's `id` can name the SAME real project — every linked schedule, not just the current one, fell into `extra` beside its own registry row.
- **ROOT CAUSE 2 — a stale closure (any workspace, kept-alive).** The mount effect that registers the "storage" event listener has deps `[controlled]` — a per-instance constant, since a kept-alive workspace's `ProjectBreadcrumb` never remounts on a later project switch — so that listener's `refresh()` call was permanently bound to whatever `currentProject` was at FIRST mount. A synthetic `notifyProjectsChanged()` storage event fired from anywhere in the app (a rename, a warm, another tab) after the user switched projects could re-derive `internalProjects` from the stale project.
- **THE FIX, three changes.** (1) `ProjectBreadcrumb.jsx`'s `refresh()` now resolves through `linkedSiteId` when present, reconciling against the SAME identity space the registry actually uses. (2) `refresh` always reads `currentProject` through a ref kept current every render, so no caller (a mount-time listener, an in-flight promise) can act on a stale value. (3) `unionProjectLists` (`projectModel.js`) now drops a controlled entry whose `linkedSiteId` names a project already covered by a registry row — the registry copy (richer: real timestamp) is the one shown, and `Scheduler.jsx`'s `selectSchedule` resolves a click on that registry row back to the correct schedule id before posting into the iframe (proven via a real click-through, not just a render check).
- **PROVEN RED before the fix, per house rule.** New `ui-audit/verify-project-switcher-dedupe.mjs`: CASE A (Schedule, a routed project with a linked schedule, the exact namespace-mismatch shape) — one "Goose Creek" row, and clicking it still correctly selects the schedule's own id in the iframe. CASE B (Site Planner, a mid-session project switch — Richfield then Goose Creek — followed by an external storage event, the exact stale-closure shape) — one "Goose Creek" row. `git stash`-ing the fix and rebuilding reproduces CASE A's defect exactly (2 "Goose Creek" rows).
- Files: `src/shared/ui/ProjectBreadcrumb.jsx`, `src/shared/projects/projectModel.js`, `src/workspaces/scheduler/Scheduler.jsx`. Tests: `test/projects.test.js` (3 new cases), `ui-audit/verify-project-switcher-dedupe.mjs` (new).
- Base: `origin/main` @ `cf120452`.
- **✅ V496865 (live) — PASSED 2026-08-31.** See VERIFICATION-DONE.md.

`[x]` **ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED at the source + mutation-proven in the sandbox.**
- Verify: sandbox — a deterministic, logged-out UI filtering bug with no timing/GIS/real-project-data dependency; fully provable headless per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK.

### B881667 — Unknown project sub-route shows the false "your tab is out of date" banner and never redirects `[App shell / routing]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #infra  *(owner live repro on planyr.io, 2026-08-30, AFTER PR #1232/#1234 merged, on a hard-reloaded tab explicitly confirmed to be on the new bundle: navigating to `#/project/<id>/review` (the real Review route is `/markup` — `/review` has never existed in any build) showed the "That part of Planyr is newer than the copy this tab has open — reload to get it." banner, the Site tab rendered underneath, and the URL kept reading `/review` forever. Instrumented by the owner (window error/unhandledrejection/resource-timing listeners): zero new resource requests, zero errors — nothing failed to load, because the route never existed to load. Minted **B881667** from this branch's reserved block B881664–B881679 against `origin/main` cf120452. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `shouldOfferReload`, `routeMiss`, `unknownModuleSlug`, `route-miss`, stale banner: B1373 built this mechanism; no prior item tracks this false-positive class. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED at the source + mutation-proven in the sandbox, sweeping the whole class of bad aliases, not one string.**
- Verify: sandbox — deterministic route-parsing logic with no timing/GIS/real-project-data dependency; the genuine-skew counterpart case is proven in the same harness.
- **ROOT CAUSE.** `shouldOfferReload` (`buildSkew.js`) treated a route miss (`unknownModuleSlug`) as sufficient on its own to show the reload banner, with **no check against the actual served build** — conflating two things that look identical from the inside: a slug shipped in a build newer than this tab's (a reload genuinely fixes it) and a slug that never existed in ANY build — a stale bookmark, an old shared link, a renamed route (no reload can ever fix it, because even the newest build still won't recognize it). Separately, the resolved fallback route was never written back to the address bar, so a bad link stayed in the URL bar forever even though the Site tab correctly rendered underneath it.
- **THE FIX, two parts.** (1) `shouldOfferReload` now requires **confirmed** build skew (`isBuildSkewed(loaded, served)`) before a route miss shows the banner at all — the same evidentiary bar every other reason in that function already meets, per its own "silent when it cannot know" contract. (2) Shell.jsx fires an immediate `/version.json` check the moment a route miss is seen (rather than waiting up to 20s for the routine poll), and once that check **proves** this tab is already current, corrects the visible URL to the resolved fallback route via `history.replaceState` — but **only** once skew is ruled out, so a genuine "newer build" deep link is never silently discarded before the user gets a chance to reload into it. On genuine skew the banner still shows and the URL is deliberately left untouched (a reload must still land on the real link).
- **PROVEN RED before the fix, per house rule.** New `ui-audit/verify-unknown-subroute.mjs` sweeps four aliases (`/review`, `/docs`, `/files`, `/plan` — the class, not the reported string) against the REAL, already-served `/version.json` (no faking needed — the build genuinely is current): no false banner, URL self-corrects to the project's Site tab, the Site Planner renders the routed project. A separate case serves a deliberately different build id via route interception: the banner DOES show, names `route-miss`, and the URL is left untouched. `git stash`-ing the fix and rebuilding reproduces the pre-fix defect exactly — all 4 aliases show the false banner and never correct the URL (8 assertions red).
- Files: `src/app/buildSkew.js`, `src/app/Shell.jsx`. Tests: `test/buildSkew.test.js` (updated — the corrected contract, both directions), `ui-audit/verify-unknown-subroute.mjs` (new).

### B866112 — Shared header's Dashboard breadcrumb is a dead no-op on Schedule, both routes `[Scheduler / header]` (bug) #scheduler #ui  *(owner's live repro on planyr.io, 2026-08-30, verbatim: "From LIBRARY, click 'Dashboard' in the breadcrumb: navigates to the map home… From NOTES: same, works. From SCHEDULE, both the global TASK REPORT route and after navigating in from another module: NOTHING. No navigation, no menu, no console error. I clicked it four times across two page states." Reported alongside — and as a second, independent instance strengthening — the B853266/B853267 Schedule-only switcher gap already fixed this same round. Owner theory offered: a second, stale copy of the shared header rendered only by Scheduler. Minted **B866112** from this branch's reserved block B866112–B866127 against `origin/main` d7560c2a. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `onGoDashboard`, `goDashboard`, `Dashboard crumb`, `dashboardNavActions`: no prior item touches the Dashboard button itself (B1050 covers the iframe's OWN internal reports-view sync, a different, still-correct behavior this fix preserves). Net-new.)*
`[x]` **AUDIT-FIRST — owner's "second header copy" theory disproved by direct source reading (as with the switcher round), but the underlying signal was right for the same reason: there is exactly ONE `AppHeader`/`ProjectBreadcrumb` in the codebase (`src/shared/ui/`), confirmed by grep with no second definition anywhere. What Scheduler actually has is its OWN local `goDashboard` handler wired into that ONE shared header's `onDashboard` prop, instead of the Shell's cross-workspace `onGoDashboard` every other workspace uses for that slot — a wiring gap, not a duplicated component.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **ROOT CAUSE.** `Shell.jsx` passes `onGoDashboard={goDashboard}` (→ `navigate({module:"site-planner", projectId:null})`, i.e. leave the workspace entirely and land on the Site Planner map home at hash `"#/"`) generically to every workspace. `Scheduler.jsx` never destructured that prop at all. Its own local `goDashboard` (B1050) does something narrower by design: clear the ROUTED project within Schedule and tell the embedded Gantt iframe to switch to its internal "reports" section — correct behavior for keeping a no-project Schedule state from showing a stale resolution panel, but it never leaves the module. On the global `/schedule` route — already showing that internal reports view with no project routed — calling it changes nothing observable, which is exactly the owner's "no navigation, no menu, no console error" report; the button was live and firing, just doing a no-op in that state.
- **FIX.** `Scheduler.jsx` now destructures `onGoDashboard` from its props, renames the old local handler to `goDashboardWithinModule` (body unchanged — the B1050 behavior is still needed and still runs first), and composes a new `goDashboard = () => { goDashboardWithinModule(); onGoDashboard?.(); }` — the same function name the header's `onDashboard` prop already referenced, so the wiring itself needed no further change. Pressing Dashboard on Schedule now behaves identically to every other workspace: it leaves the module and lands on the map home, on both the project-scoped and the global route.
- **Adjacent controls checked, per the owner's explicit ask ("check the same header's other controls… export, history, people, Automation and settings").** Read `ScheduleToolbar.jsx`'s `ScheduleCenter`/`ScheduleActions` in full: every control (zoom, `ExportMenu`, history/contacts/automation/format/settings) posts its own `planar:*` command to the iframe and is correctly gated on `toolbar.ready` — legitimately workspace-specific (Automation etc. have no equivalent on other workspaces), not a stale copy of anything shared. No defect found; no change made there.
- **Proven RED before the fix, per house rule.** New `ui-audit/verify-schedule-dashboard-crumb.mjs`: a real headless Chromium session against a real production build, with `/sequence/**` stubbed by a same-origin fixture speaking the real `postMessage` contract (no Supabase writes) — Case A (project-scoped `#/project/<id>/schedule`) and Case B (the global `#/schedule` route, the owner's exact no-project repro, using an unlinked stub project so the harness doesn't trip Scheduler's own legitimate carry-in effect). Both cases pass against the fixed build; re-run via `git stash`/rebuild against the pre-fix source and both go RED — the hash stays on `/schedule` instead of moving to `"#/"` — then `git stash pop` restored.

### B854832 — First paint of a plan whose aerial is not yet anchored blocks the main thread ~6.5s: Leaflet's own `_pruneTiles()` runs once PER TILE instead of once per burst `[Site Planner / map]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #perf  *(the owner's own production perf capture, build 396be34, plan smt7q6ar8egz "Concept A"/Richfield, 2026-08-29 20:44 UTC — five main-thread blocks of 428/512/550/591/606ms (~6.5s total; 25 long tasks totalling 6565ms in the 45s capture window) firing across the ~8s after opening a plan whose aerial had not yet been fetched, all five attributed to invoker "FrameRequestCallback" with an EMPTY sourceFunctionName. ALREADY RULED OUT by the dispatch's own prior evidence: element mount alone (zero long-animation-frame entries on a warm 161-element/2241-node mount), a warm plan switch (zero entries switching between two ALREADY-anchored plans), contours/terrain (no terrain-tile-timing event in the episode — not a B802400 recurrence), and a leaking tile cache (257 retained tiles is under `tileCacheLimit`'s cap). Minted **B854832 / V476144** from this branch's reserved block B854832–B854847 · V476144–V476159, against `origin/main` 396be34. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `_pruneTiles`, `throttleTilePruning`, `aerial re-anchor`, `FrameRequestCallback`, `tileLifecycle`: B802400 (contours/terrain tile timing, explicitly ruled out above) and B1121/NEW-6/NEW-7 (the existing `preserveTilesAcrossSetView`/`capTileCache`/`releaseLayer` tile-lifecycle work this item extends) are the nearest prior art; neither addresses per-tile `_pruneTiles` frequency. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED at the source + measured by direct instrumentation in the sandbox + CONFIRMED LIVE on the owner's own machine against production.**
- Verify: live — CLOSED. Confirmed 2026-08-30 on planyr.io, same hardware as the original capture: ZERO long-animation-frame blocks over the same transition that originally cost 6,565ms across five 428–606ms blocks. → **V476144**.
- **ROOT CAUSE, read directly from `node_modules/leaflet/dist/leaflet-src.js`, not guessed at.** `GridLayer._tileReady` branches on `this._map._fadeAnimated`. The Site Planner's map is constructed with `fadeAnimation:false` (an existing, unrelated, already-shipped setting) — so on the non-fade branch, **every single tile calls `this._pruneTiles()` the instant it finishes loading**, not once per burst: `tile.active = true; this._pruneTiles();`. `_pruneTiles()` is O(retained tiles) — three separate `for (key in this._tiles)` passes, the middle one walking up to 5 parent zoom levels and down 2 child levels (`_retainParent`/`_retainChildren`) for every tile that is "current" but not yet "active", which is the state of every tile still in flight during a burst. A re-anchor that brings up ~150+ new tiles in quick succession (the reported 90 → 257) therefore reruns that whole O(n) pass roughly once per tile that resolves — an O(tiles-loading × tiles-retained) cost — for a decision whose end state does not depend on how many times it ran in between (current tiles are never pruned; only what should no longer be retained is decided, and that decision doesn't change between two tiles resolving a millisecond apart).
- **THE FIX — coalesce, don't skip.** `tileLifecycle.js`'s new `throttleTilePruning(layer)` wraps a tile layer's `_pruneTiles` so repeated synchronous calls within one burst collapse into a single deferred run, via a MessageChannel-posted macrotask — **not** `requestAnimationFrame`, because Leaflet's OWN tile-ready path also schedules a `requestAnimFrame(this._pruneTiles, this)` once the burst's last tile resolves, and the browser runs every rAF callback due for a frame back-to-back with no yield in between, so an rAF-based defer here would just line up alongside Leaflet's own call and buy no separation — the same MEASURED reason `paintSchedule.js` already gives for using a macrotask instead of rAF (see its header, from B802400 round 5's own adversarial reproduction). Wired onto both the coarse backfill and the retina detail tile layers in `SitePlanner.jsx`, alongside the existing `preserveTilesAcrossSetView`. Every call still runs the real `_pruneTiles` exactly once, eventually — nothing is skipped, only coalesced. `fadeAnimation` itself is untouched (fixing the mechanism at its actual source rather than reintroducing the fade-stuck bug that setting exists to avoid).
- **A SECOND, SMALLER INEFFICIENCY IN THE SAME FILE, fixed alongside it because it's the same code path the brief pointed at directly ("`L.TileLayer._update`/`_setView`/`_tileReady` doing O(retained tiles) work").** `capTileCache` (the existing tile-cache-cap maintenance, B1427/NEW-7) called `map.getCenter()` and `map.project(center, z)` **once per retained tile** inside its distance-sort loop, even though the center is the same point for every tile in one call and the projection only differs when the zoom differs (normally one, occasionally two, distinct zooms are ever retained at once). At 257 tiles that was up to 257 redundant `getCenter`/`project` calls on every single "load"/"moveend" firing. Hoisted `getCenter()` out of the loop and memoised `project` per distinct zoom — now O(1) `getCenter` + O(distinct zooms) `project` instead of O(n) of each.
- **MEASURED, real Chromium, before vs after — `ui-audit/diagnose-aerial-reanchor-block.mjs` (new).** This sandbox cannot reach the real Esri/USGS hosts (egress-blocked, the same wall every GIS item here cites) or match the owner's CPU/GPU, so tile requests are fulfilled by `ui-audit/lib/fakeTile.mjs` (a real decodable PNG per tile — Chromium does the real decode/texture-upload work) with staggered latency, and the METRIC is a COUNT rather than a clock (this repo's own established idiom for exactly this class of question — B236592/B221763, "count invocations, not milliseconds" — because wall-clock LoAF timing in this sandbox is noisy in a way the owner's real capture is not). The harness opens a real, already-anchored plan (Goose Creek, `perfScenarioSite()`), lets it fully settle, then switches to the Richfield fixture (a different origin, so its tile grid is genuinely unfetched this session) and counts how many times the REAL underlying `_pruneTiles` algorithm executes during the switch — patched onto the shared Leaflet prototype via the already-existing Goose Creek layer, so the count is honest whether or not `throttleTilePruning` is wrapping it on top. **Three repeated runs each side, git-stash isolated (the same technique B802400 round 5 used for its own before/after):** pre-fix **183 / 183 / 183** real `_pruneTiles` executions per switch; post-fix **88 / 82 / 91** — a consistent ~52% reduction in how many times the O(retained-tiles) algorithm actually runs, for byte-identical final state either side (same tile count, same element count, same DOM node count — this changes only how many times a decision is redundantly repeated, never what ends up on screen).
- **What is NOT claimed.** This sandbox cannot reproduce the owner's exact 428–606ms per-block magnitude (his real network timing to Esri/USGS, his real CPU, his real GPU compositing are all unavailable here) or confirm the fix collapses his five blocks to something imperceptible — that needs his real browser on his real plan. What IS proven: the named mechanism is real (read from Leaflet's own vendored source, not inferred), it is directly triggered by this app's own `fadeAnimation:false` setting, and coalescing it measurably and consistently cuts the redundant work in a real browser without changing the rendered result.

### B862561 — Alt+hover reveals the whole stack under the cursor and lets you pick any of it `[Site Planner / canvas]` (feature) #site-planner #selection #keyboard  *(same owner chat block as B862560 — verbatim: "let's make it so that when I press alt and hover on something that I can pick all the things that are on top or behind it." Explicitly named as the replacement for the "Behind this" menu rows B862560 cuts. Minted **B862561** from this branch's reserved block against `origin/main` 3849d70. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `handleStackPick`, `stackAtPoint`, `Alt+click`, `stack picker`: B548822 built a DIFFERENT gesture (Alt+CLICK, single-target cycling) that this checks against and coexists with rather than duplicates; net-new.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED and self-verified this session, headless, against both a synthetic fixture and the owner's real Bain plan.**
- Verify: live — a new interaction/selection feature, mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class; done, see V483873.
- **CHECKED FIRST, per the brief's explicit instruction not to steal Alt from an existing shortcut.** Every existing `altKey` use in `SitePlanner.jsx`: Alt+Z (physical KeyZ) autosizes a text box/callout — different key, no conflict. Alt+click (no Shift/Ctrl/Meta) already cycles one level deeper into the hit stack at a point (`handleStackPick`, B548822) — a CLICK gesture; this feature is a HOVER gesture (no click needed to see the list), so the two coexist: holding Alt shows the list, and a click that lands on the canvas itself (not on the list, which is a separate floating overlay) still cycles the old way. Alt held during a drag-place bypasses grid snap (`altSnapOffRef`) — reads `e.altKey` on its own pointer events, untouched, and this feature is gated to `tool === "select"` so it never shows during a placement drag anyway.
- **THE MECHANISM.** A `keydown`/`keyup`/`pointermove` listener (mounted once, gated on `tool === "select"`, no menu open, and not while a text field is focused) computes `stackAtPoint(document.elementsFromPoint(x,y))` — the SAME ordered, deduped, chrome-skipping stack reader `handleStackPick` and the priority-rule already use, never a re-derivation — and renders a small floating list (a portal, not the shared `ContextMenu` component, since this is hover-driven and must carry no dismiss backdrop that would block the canvas underneath). Each entry is labeled the way a user would name it (`Building N` via `buildingNumbers`, `<stall depth>′ Trailer Parking`, `<pond name> <acreage> AC` via the same `pondDisplayNameFor`/`pondAreaLabelLine` the on-canvas label uses, else the plain type label). Hovering an entry highlights it on the map by reading the ALREADY-PAINTED DOM node's own `getBoundingClientRect()` (`data-feature="<kind>:<id>"`, the same key `featureStack` resolves) rather than re-deriving its screen geometry. Clicking an entry (or Enter, with Up/Down moving the highlight) calls `setSel(entry.target)` — `target` is already in the exact shape `sel` expects, the same shape `handleStackPick` already writes. Alt release or Escape dismisses; empty canvas computes zero entries and renders nothing (no empty box).
- **VERIFIED.** `e2e/markup-behind-building.spec.js`'s new NEW-2 describe block (4 tests, real Chromium): the picker names both the covering building and the behind-band markup topmost-first, picking the markup selects it WITHOUT moving it (still behind the plan), the covering element's own menu is then reachable again via the unchanged priority rule and its cross-band toggle brings the markup back in front, and hovering a feature with nothing behind it shows exactly one entry while empty canvas shows none. `ui-audit/verify-markup-over-building.mjs` re-run against the owner's real Bain plan (21/21): at a real overlap point the actual stack is FIVE deep (two road pieces, the markup, two parcels) — the picker reports all five correctly, topmost-first, richer than the simpler synthetic fixture and exactly the "reach a completely covered feature" case the brief asked for.

`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED and verified this session with a mutation-proven headless Playwright run — no Blocker needed (ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK: logged-out, no external GIS, fully reproducible in the sandbox with a locally-seeded no-schedule project).**

- **ROOT CAUSE, found by an Explore agent reading `Scheduler.jsx` + `ScheduleToolbar.jsx` + `navState.js`.** The empty state (`showEmptyState`) is gated on `ready` — flipped true either by the embedded scheduler's first real `planar:nav-state` message, or by two REVEAL FALLBACK timers (2.5s after iframe load, 6s absolute backstop) so a slow/broken embed doesn't spin forever. The right-hand toolbar (`ScheduleActions`/`ScheduleCenter`, gated on `toolbar.ready`) and "Link an existing schedule" (gated on the schedules list from `nav-state`) are driven by a SEPARATE `planar:toolbar-state` message with **no fallback of its own**. So on any load where `nav-state` (or a fallback timer) lands before `toolbar-state`, `ready` flips true, the empty state mounts, and the toolbar/link render as their EMPTY defaults — correctly self-healing the moment `toolbar-state` finally arrives and React re-renders, but with nothing forcing that re-render sooner. The owner's "opening/closing the switcher fixed it" was coincidental timing, not a real trigger.
- **THE FIX.** `toolbar.ready` now gets the SAME two fallback timers `ready` already had (`markToolbarReadyFallback`, gated so a REAL `toolbar-state` report always wins and is never clobbered), and `showEmptyState` is gated on `ready && toolbar.ready` (`iframeFullyReported`) instead of `ready` alone — so every signal the empty state depends on resolves on one schedule, and a slow/broken embed reveals no later than it already did.
- **VERIFIED, mutation-proven:** three new Playwright cases in `e2e/schedule-link-panel.spec.js` (nav-state-only / toolbar-state-first / fallback-only) drive the exact race via `postMessage`. Confirmed the fix's OWN test catches the pre-fix bug: reverted `Scheduler.jsx` alone, rebuilt, re-ran — 2 of 3 new cases went **red** (the toolbar was genuinely absent at the moment the empty state first became visible); restored the fix, rebuilt, re-ran — all 18 specs in the file (18 passed, 1 auth-setup skipped, as expected with no seeded account) pass. Full suite `npm test` green, `npm run lint` 0 errors, `npm run build` green, `node ui-audit/perf-bundle-audit.mjs` all budgets within band.

- **Recurrence: 2026-08-30 (×1) — owner re-verified live on production (deploy confirmed via a direct forensic bundle diff, not merely a merge check) and Richfield STILL read "Detention: checking flood data" against the header's "Flood data: not checked". FIXED, DEDUPE-FIRST — no new number.** The fix above only guarded the `requiredAcFt == null` branch; the "deliberately not touched" `usableAcFt == null` fallback was the ACTUAL branch Richfield hits, and the guarding assumption behind leaving it alone ("a resolved `req` implies a check already ran") is false in general: `req`/`drainCtxData` hydrates from `drainViewCtx?.ctx`, which can come from a RESTORED prior-check record (`settings.drainage.lastCheck`, `SitePlanner.jsx`'s `drainRestoredCtx`) independently of that same record's separate `.checkedAt` field, which `floodChecked` reads. A saved `lastCheck` record that carries enough for `hydrateDrainageContext` to rebuild a requirement but no valid `checkedAt` (e.g. one saved before B1442 reliably stamped it) resolves `requiredAcFt` while `floodChecked` correctly stays false — reproducing the owner's exact report. Gated the `usableAcFt == null` branch on `!d.floodChecked` too, matching the first branch and Buildability's own pattern; the genuine-loading case (`floodChecked: true`, pond volume still catching up) is unchanged and still covered by the pre-existing LOADING test. New regression test added naming the exact Richfield shape (`req` resolved, `floodChecked: false`) → `"not checked yet"`, never `"checking flood data"`. `npm test` full suite green (13,030+ tests), lint 0 errors, build green, bundle budget within band.

### B832388 — Lease comp detail view: total annual rent printed a raw float (`$4,783,022.4`) instead of formatted currency `[Site Planner / comps]` (bug) #comps #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-28, NEW-5, verbatim: "Total annual rent    $4,783,022.4" — ".65 x 613,208 x 12 printed straight out of the arithmetic." Same session as B832384/B832386. Minted **B832388** from this branch's reserved block against `origin/main` 44cc861. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `fmtMoney`, `totalRent`, currency formatting in `comps`: no prior item; net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — the detail view's total-rent row now formats as whole-dollar currency, matching the convention the create form's own live rent preview already used in the same file.**
- Verify: sandbox — a pure formatting-function fix, exhaustively unit-tested; no rendering ambiguity a browser could add on top of a deterministic string.
- **ROOT CAUSE.** `compFieldRows`'s lease branch formatted every dollar figure (Price, TI allowance, Total annual rent) through one shared `fmtMoney` helper using `{ maximumFractionDigits: 2 }` with no matching `minimumFractionDigits` — `toLocaleString` only CAPS the fraction digits, it doesn't pad them, so a non-round total like `4783022.4` printed with its one real decimal intact instead of being rounded to a consistent precision. The app's own convention elsewhere (`measure.js`/`SitePlanner.jsx`/`pondLabelText.js`/`yieldBar.js`) always pairs `minimumFractionDigits`/`maximumFractionDigits` so a formatter never floats between decimal counts depending on the input.
- **THE FIX, scoped narrowly.** Rather than change `fmtMoney` itself (still used for TI $/SF and Price, which are legitimately fractional per-SF rates and need their cents), added `fmtMoneyWhole` — real `Intl` currency formatting, `maximumFractionDigits: 0` — used ONLY for the derived `totalRent` row, matching the exact convention the create form's own live rent preview already used elsewhere in this same file (`toLocaleString(undefined, { style: "currency", currency: "USD", maximumFractionDigits: 0 })`). TI and Price are untouched.
- **VERIFIED** — `test/comps.test.js`: `.65 x 613208 x 12 = 4,783,022.4` renders as `"$4,783,022"` (not `not.toMatch(/\.\d/)`), and the existing Price/TI formatting tests still pass unmodified.
- Files: `src/shared/comps/lib/comps.js`, `test/comps.test.js`.
- Base: `origin/main` @ `44cc861`.

### B832389 — Comp date shown two different ways: raw ISO in the detail view, browser-native picker format in the edit form `[Site Planner / comps]` (bug) #comps #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-28, NEW-6, verbatim: "The detail view prints 'Date  2026-08-28' (ISO). The edit form shows the same value as '08/28/2026'." Minted **B832389** from this branch's reserved block against `origin/main` 44cc861. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `compDate`, date formatting in `comps`, `toLocaleDateString`: no prior item for this module; net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE, with an honest limit stated rather than papered over — the DETAIL VIEW now matches the app's own established read-view date convention; the EDIT FORM's native date picker was left alone, because it was never a second, invented format.**
- Verify: sandbox — a pure parsing/formatting function, unit-tested; the display half is a static string, no live browser needed.
- **WHAT I FOUND, before changing anything (AUDIT-FIRST).** `compFieldRows` pushed the raw `comp.compDate` string straight through — `"2026-08-28"`, no formatting at all. Every OTHER read-view date in this app (`FileBrowser.jsx`, `SiteReviewModal.jsx`, `MapFinder.jsx`) formats the same way: `toLocaleDateString(undefined, { year: "numeric", month: "short", day: "numeric" })` → `"Aug 28, 2026"`. The edit form's `<input type="date">` is the SAME native picker every other date-entry field in this app already uses (there is no custom text-based date field anywhere in the codebase) — its `"08/28/2026"` display is the browser's own locale rendering of that native control, not something this app's code chose or can restyle without replacing the picker with a non-native one (a materially bigger change, not what was asked, and a UX regression from the accessible native control).
- **THE FIX.** `compFieldRows` now formats `comp.compDate` through a new `fmtCompDate` helper before rendering: parsed by its Y/M/D parts (`iso.split("-").map(Number)`, the same date-only parsing idiom already used in `detentionRules.js`) into a LOCAL `Date`, never `new Date(iso)` directly — comp_date carries no time, so parsing the bare string as UTC and displaying it in a timezone behind UTC would print the wrong day. Detail view now reads `"Aug 28, 2026"`, matching the rest of the app. The edit form's native date input is unchanged.
- **HONEST RESIDUAL, stated per LOUD-FAILURE rather than claimed as full parity:** the two views still don't print byte-identical text — one is a formatted read-view string, the other is a native OS/browser-rendered picker whose exact text is outside this app's control. What WAS a real inconsistency (an app-wide convention on one side, a raw unformatted ISO string with no convention on the other) is now resolved; what remains is inherent to using an accessible native date control for editing, which every other date field in the app already accepts.
- **VERIFIED** — `test/comps.test.js`: `"2026-08-28"` → `"Aug 28, 2026"`; a January-1st date near a US-timezone UTC boundary (the case that would break a naive `new Date(iso)`) → `"Jan 1, 2026"`, proving the Y/M/D parsing rather than assuming it.
- Files: `src/shared/comps/lib/comps.js`, `test/comps.test.js`.
- Base: `origin/main` @ `44cc861`.

### B831600 (×2) — Selecting across table cells jumped and flashed `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui #selection  *(owner chat block 2026-08-28, Silvestri "Utility" note: "when I click and highlight stuff, it just jumps and flashes." Fixture: a 4-row × 1-col Outlook signature table, no class on `<table>`, nested several levels deep inside a list item — per `docs/NOTES-CARRY-FORWARD.md` §2, simplifying this fixture hides the defect. Minted **B831600** from this branch's reserved block B831600–B831615 against `origin/main` 142d614b. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `table`, `selectedCell`, `CellSelection`, `jump`, `flash`: no prior item.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE (×2) — root-caused with a real mouse drag (not a programmatic Range), fixed, and mutation-proven (the guard fails on the pre-fix code with the exact reported symptom). Round 1's fix reached production and immediately reopened; round 2's fix is synchronous by construction, proven red on round 1's own code, and held against three conditions round 1's guard never tested.**
- Verify: sandbox — reproduced and fixed headlessly with a real Chromium drag; no auth/live-GIS/real-project-data dependency (the fixture reproduces the reported shape exactly).
- **ROOT CAUSE, measured, not guessed.** `NoteToolbar`'s Table button group renders only `{inTable && (...)}`, so the instant the caret enters a table the toolbar wraps to an extra row (39px → 75px measured). The toolbar is a SIBLING of the scrollable mat in the same flex column, so the mat's own top edge — and everything painted inside it, the table included — slides down by that exact delta the moment you press the mouse down inside a cell. A drag that starts there has its target crawl out from under a STATIONARY pointer on the very first frame: instrumented before the fix, the native selection never extended across cells at all — `document.getSelection().isCollapsed` stayed `true` through the whole gesture, hopping between wrong text nodes (some OUTSIDE the table) on every mousemove, because each move's screen coordinates resolved against content that had silently moved since mousedown. Leaving the table reverts the bar and the sheet snaps back — the "flash".
- **ROUND 1's FIX, and why the first attempt was wrong.** `NoteEditor.jsx` adds a `ResizeObserver` on the toolbar that folds its measured height delta into the mat's own CSS `transform` (`translateY`), before paint — VIEWPORT-STABLE's prescribed shape. The first attempt compensated `scrollTop` instead (matching this file's existing zoom-compensation code nearby) and it was wrong for this case: zoom changes the CONTENT's height, so there is always scroll slack to absorb into; this shift changes the MAT's own box height, not the content's, so on a short note — exactly Michael's case — `scrollHeight - clientHeight` was already 0 and adding to `scrollTop` was clamped straight back to zero, measured with the table still moving the full 36px. A `transform` has no such floor.
- **VERIFIED (round 1), both directions.** `ui-audit/verify-notes-table-select.mjs`: a known-good control arm (a real drag across four plain paragraphs, no table) stays green throughout; the reported case (real drag across the Silvestri-shaped fixture) now shows zero frame-to-frame jump and the drag correctly builds a `CellSelection` (`.selectedCell` on all 4 cells, `editor.state.selection.empty === false`) where before it stayed collapsed. **Proved the guard goes RED on the unfixed code** (stashed the fix, rebuilt, re-ran): 4/7 checks failed with the exact reported shape (36px jump, collapsed selection, 0/4 selectedCell) — then restored the fix and re-confirmed 7/7 green.
- **Recurrence: 2026-08-28 (×2), same day — owner live-verified the merged round-1 build on planyr.io himself and it still jumped.** Hard numbers from a real drag on Silvestri > Utility, scroll position pinned and unchanged throughout (ruling out scroll re-anchoring): toolbar height flips 38.9px → 74.8px and the table moves the full 35.9px at the same moment, with no correction visible afterward — walking `.ProseMirror` up through `.planyr-note` found every ancestor's `transform` reading `none`. **ROOT CAUSE OF THE RECURRENCE, measured with a `requestAnimationFrame` sampler (the round-1 guard only ever sampled every ~45ms, 2–3 frames apart, and structurally could not catch this):** a `ResizeObserver` callback is a PASSIVE, after-the-fact mechanism, not the synchronous layout effect VIEWPORT-STABLE actually prescribes. On the round-1 build, the frame where the toolbar first measures its taller height still has the mat's `transform` empty and the content already down by the full delta — a real, visible one-frame jump, reproduced on demand — and only the NEXT frame corrects it. That is exactly "jump and flash"; under the owner's real machine (load, a longer-running drag, however Chrome scheduled the notification) the gap can stretch well past one frame, which is what reached production as a shift that never visibly corrected.
- **ROUND 2 FIX.** `inTable` is now computed inline in `NoteEditor.jsx` — the identical boolean `NoteToolbar` renders its extra row on — and the compensation runs in a `useLayoutEffect` keyed on it: a layout effect commits after the DOM mutation but before paint, in the SAME render as the toolbar's row change, so there is no frame in which one is true and the other is not. The `ResizeObserver` stays, now only as a fallback for OTHER causes of the same resize (a window resize changing button wrap, a webfont finishing its load), sharing one height/shift accumulator with the layout effect so the two paths never double-count a delta.
- **VERIFIED (round 2), against three conditions round 1's guard never tested, each proven RED on round 1's own merged code before being proven green on round 2's fix:** (1) the `requestAnimationFrame` race window itself — 1/60 frames raced on round 1's code, 0/60 on round 2's; (2) the scroller PINNED AT MAXIMUM SCROLL (an owner-named condition — his own report had scrollTop pinned with no slack left, the exact case round 1's rejected `scrollTop`-only attempt already failed under) in BOTH directions — entering the table (toolbar grows) and the mirror case, leaving it (toolbar shrinks, moving content the other way): 1/60 race frames each on round 1's code, 0/60 on round 2's, with `scrollTop` itself never moving at all (ruling out a scroll-based mechanism entirely); (3) a PLAIN PARAGRAPH after the table, asserting its own `getBoundingClientRect()` directly rather than inferring correctness from the table's rect: 1/60 race frames on round 1's code, 0/60 on round 2's. `ui-audit/verify-notes-table-select.mjs` grew from 7 to 16 checks across 6 sections. **A self-caught test bug along the way, corrected before it reported a false pass or fail:** the first version of the max-scroll check inferred "compensated" from whether `mat.style.transform` was non-empty, which is right for the GROWING direction but wrong for SHRINKING, whose correct settled state is net-zero (an empty transform) — it reported the shrink case as still racing on the FIXED build. Rewritten to compare the visible position against its own settled value, never against a specific CSS property's shape.
- **NOT COVERED, named rather than silently skipped:** a drag that starts outside the table and has to trigger the browser's own edge-autoscroll to reach a cell below the fold (a separate mechanism, layered on top of this compensation, not exercised here); two rapid successive enter/leave transitions inside one animation frame (the accumulator is additive by construction, but no test exercises more than one transition per sampling window); a table inside a positioned box (`noteAnchor`) triggering the same toolbar growth — only row-level (not frame-sampled) coverage exists for that combination, in `sweep-notes-table.mjs`.
- New bug family recorded in `docs/NOTES-CARRY-FORWARD.md` §5 (family 4, updated) and `src/workspaces/notes/CLAUDE.md`.
- Files: `src/workspaces/notes/components/NoteEditor.jsx`, `ui-audit/verify-notes-table-select.mjs`, `docs/NOTES-CARRY-FORWARD.md`, `src/workspaces/notes/CLAUDE.md`, `MAP.md`.
- Base: `origin/main` @ `142d614b` (round 1); reopened and re-fixed against `origin/main` @ `a5636140` (round 2).

### B831601 — "Convert table to text" — pull a table's rows out as plain lines `[Notes]` (feature) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-28: "what he is actually trying to do is get four lines of contact detail OUT of a table Outlook created. Right-click a table > Convert to text." Same session/fixture as B831600. Minted **B831601** from this branch's reserved block against `origin/main` 142d614b. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `convert table`, `isLayoutTable`, `table to text`: no prior item for the RIGHT-CLICK command; `isLayoutTable`/`tidyPastedFragment` in `notesPastePlain.js` already ship the PASTE half of this ask (B36051 amendment 2) — verified still working here, not reimplemented.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — new right-click command, one undo step, marks preserved; two real bugs found and fixed chasing it; the already-shipped paste half re-verified green.**
- Verify: sandbox — reproduced and fixed headlessly with real right-clicks and menu clicks; judged on the stored document per house rule.
- **THE COMMAND (`lib/notesTableToText.js`, new).** Each `tableRow` becomes one line: a plain paragraph, or — when the table is the ONLY content of a `listItem`/`taskItem` (Michael's exact Silvestri case) — a SIBLING list item at the same level, inserted in place of the item that held the table. When the table shares its list item with other content (e.g. a line above it), only the table is removed and the sibling lines are inserted right after, leaving the other content untouched. A multi-cell row joins its cells with a plain `" · "` separator; every inline node's marks (bold, links) ride straight through unchanged, since only the block containers are restructured. One ProseMirror transaction, so Ctrl+Z undoes the whole conversion in one press. Wired onto the document's right-click menu (`DocMenu` in `NoteEditor.jsx`) as "Convert table to text", offered only when the right-click actually landed inside a `<table>`.
- **BUG #1, found and fixed: a custom Tiptap command that builds its own `state.tr` reports success and does nothing.** `editor.commands.x()` (what a menu row's `onClick` uses) always dispatches the ONE `tr` object it built before calling the command function and threaded through as a prop — the `dispatch` callback it hands you is a no-op. The first version of `convertTableToText` called `state.tr` (a getter that returns a FRESH `Transaction` on every read) instead of destructuring `tr` from its own props, mutated that throwaway object, and `editor.commands.convertTableToText()` returned `true` while the stored document was byte-identical — caught by adding `window.__noteEditor.runCommand(name, ...args)` (gated behind the existing `__PLANYR_E2E` flag) and comparing the command's return value against storage.
- **BUG #2, found and fixed: a right-click's caret placement is asynchronous.** Measured on a plain paragraph, no table involved: the native DOM selection moved correctly on `mousedown`, but ProseMirror's own `state.selection` only catches up through a `selectionchange` listener that fires **~20ms after `contextmenu` has already run** — so the document menu, built synchronously inside `onContextMenu`, was reading wherever the caret used to be, not where the user just right-clicked. Fixed by resolving the click position with `editor.view.posAtCoords` and calling `setTextSelection` by hand in `onContextMenu`, unless the click landed inside the CURRENT selection (so Cut/Copy on an already-selected phrase is untouched). This is a general fix — it corrects every selection-dependent menu row (e.g. the Link/Remove-link label), not only the new one.
- **Focus comes home after the command runs** (`editor.commands.focus()`), matching the existing box-delete precedent (B421489) — a menu click leaves focus on the button it clicked, and Ctrl+Z cannot reach a document that is not focused.
- **The PASTE half of this ask was already shipped** (`notesPastePlain.js`'s `isLayoutTable`, B36051 amendment 2) — re-verified green rather than reimplemented: a pasted single-column table lands as plain paragraphs, not a table, in all three paste modes including the default.
- **VERIFIED.** `ui-audit/verify-notes-table-to-text.mjs`, 17/17: the reported case (table is the whole list item) converts to 4 sibling list items with bold and link marks intact and one Ctrl+Z restoring the table whole; a table sharing its list item with other content leaves that content untouched; a top-level table (no list) converts to plain paragraphs, never inventing list items outside a list context; the paste regression check passes.
- New bug families recorded in `docs/NOTES-CARRY-FORWARD.md` §5 (families 5–6) and `src/workspaces/notes/CLAUDE.md`.
- Files: `src/workspaces/notes/lib/notesTableToText.js` (new), `src/workspaces/notes/lib/notesExtensions.js`, `src/workspaces/notes/components/NoteEditor.jsx`, `ui-audit/verify-notes-table-to-text.mjs` (new), `test/notesModule.test.js`, `docs/NOTES-CARRY-FORWARD.md`, `src/workspaces/notes/CLAUDE.md`, `MAP.md`.
- Base: `origin/main` @ `142d614b`.

### B839840 — Bin shows "permanently deleted" for a page that was simply never written `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui #persistence  *(owner chat block 2026-08-28, verbatim: "I created an empty page and binned it. Its bin card read 'Its writing was permanently deleted and cannot be brought back'. An older empty page in the same bin reads 'Empty — nothing was ever written in it'. The scary copy should only appear when writing actually existed and was purged." Same session as B831600(×2)/B831602(×2). Minted **B839840** from this branch's reserved block B839840–B839855 against `origin/main` a5636140. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `permanently deleted`, `collectBinFacts`, `gone:`, `everTouched`: B350002/B357011/B357012 built `collectBinFacts` and its `gone` flag but never distinguished "never written" from "destroyed" — this is a genuine gap in that flag's own definition, not a duplicate of any of the three.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — the discriminator moved from the body (which cannot tell the two states apart) to the tree's own timestamps (which can), proven red on the pre-fix code and green after, both headlessly (the pure function) and in the real UI (a live click-through into the Bin view).**
- Verify: sandbox — reproduces headlessly with real localStorage + a real Bin-view render; no auth/live-GIS/real-project-data dependency.
- **ROOT CAUSE.** `collectBinFacts` (`lib/notesStore.js`) set `gone: text.length === 0 && !anyStored && pageIds.length > 0` — "empty, and no body found on this device for any page in the cascade." `anyStored` is `true` only when `readPage()` finds a stored body, and `readPage` explicitly returns `null` for "a page that has never been written" (its own doc comment) — which is EXACTLY the state of a page created and binned before its first autosave debounce ever ran. So `!anyStored` was true for two unrelated situations that happen to look identical from the body alone: a page whose content was genuinely destroyed (the original B357011-era motivation — a real server-side purge, or `deletePages` clearing a body it once had), and a page that never had anything to lose in the first place. The bin showed the first sentence for both.
- **THE FIX.** `updatedAt` on a tree node moves off `createdAt` ONLY through `touchPage`, and (per `Notes.jsx`'s `handleSaved`, which the real editor calls only after `writePage` actually lands a save — never on a keystroke) that is the tree's own honest record of "a write really happened here at some point." `collectBinFacts` now also tracks `touched` per id during its existing tree walk and requires `everTouched` (at least one page in the cascade shows `updatedAt !== createdAt`) before `gone` can be true. Without that proof, an empty/bodyless page reads as "Empty — nothing was ever written in it", never as destroyed.
- **VERIFIED, both the pure function and the real UI, proven red on the old code first.** `test/notesBinFacts.test.js`: a never-touched page (created via `addPage`, no `writePage` call at all) now reads `empty:true, gone:false` — reverting the fix to `!anyStored` alone flips this to `gone:true`, confirmed by stashing the fix and re-running (1 failure, exact assertion); a page that WAS touched (`writePage` + `touchPage`, matching what a real save does) and then lost its body (`deletePages`) still correctly reads `gone:true`. `ui-audit/verify-notes-bin-never-written.mjs` drives the real Bin view with three seeded rows — a never-written page, an older page with a stored-but-empty body, and a genuinely touched-then-purged page — and confirms the exact on-screen copy: the first two both read "Empty — nothing was ever written in it", the third still reads "Its writing was permanently deleted and cannot be brought back".
- **An existing test's own fixture needed the same correction.** `test/notesAnchorPrune.test.js`'s "a container whose only child is PURGED" case built its "purged" simulation the same way `collectBinFacts` used to judge it — a page with no body and no `touchPage` call — which is indistinguishable from "never written" under the corrected rule. Updated to call `touchPage` on the child first, so the fixture actually simulates a write that landed and was then lost, matching what the test's own name claims.
- New bug family recorded in `docs/NOTES-CARRY-FORWARD.md` §5.7 and `src/workspaces/notes/CLAUDE.md`.
- Files: `src/workspaces/notes/lib/notesStore.js`, `test/notesBinFacts.test.js`, `test/notesAnchorPrune.test.js`, `ui-audit/verify-notes-bin-never-written.mjs` (new), `docs/NOTES-CARRY-FORWARD.md`, `src/workspaces/notes/CLAUDE.md`, `MAP.md`.

### B825233 — A machine-checked gate on the verification queue: pending V# items with no `Blocker:` wall, and pending V# items past a staleness threshold `[Infra / CI]` (task) #infra #testing  *(same owner chat block, 2026-08-28: `CLAUDE.md` already states "a V### with no Blocker: wall is a mis-classification, not a to-do" and ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK already requires driving such a check headless the same session — nothing ever enforced either rule; 130 of 211 pending items were found carrying no `Blocker:` at the time of the owner's own audit. Minted **B825233** from this branch's reserved block against `origin/main` 90a6ac6f. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `verification queue`, `Blocker: ceiling`, gate names adjacent to `panel-copy-budget`: no prior item builds a machine check over `VERIFICATION.md`'s own queue health (distinct from its drift against `BACKLOG.md`, which B638/B645 already cover). Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — `scripts/verification-queue-audit.mjs` (report + ratchet gate), wired into `build.yml` alongside the other drift guards; current numbers reported below.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **THE SCRIPT.** `scripts/verification-queue-audit.mjs` parses every `### V###` heading inside `VERIFICATION.md`'s `## 🔲 Needs verification` section, classifies each block `failed` (carries an explicit ❌) or `open` (everything else — deliberately inclusive, since this file spans years of formats and a real chunk of still-owed items never spell the ⏳ emoji), extracts every `` `Blocker: <kind>` `` tag present, and takes the NEWEST ISO date mentioned anywhere in the block as a "last touched" proxy (an item with no date at all is reported as `noDate`, never guessed into either bucket).
- **THE THRESHOLD — 60 days, chosen and justified, not defaulted.** The measured distribution has a real break there: of the dated pending items in the owner's own audit, 125 clustered in the 31–60 day band (one or two `improve`-cadence cycles) and 60 sat past it — the genuinely neglected tail (capped by a 436-day outlier). A 30-day line would flag the entire routine backlog and say nothing useful; 60 days isolates only the items that survived more than two full monthly cycles untouched.
- **THE GATE IS A RATCHET, deliberately, matching this repo's own `perf-ratchet.mjs`/`panel-copy-budget.mjs` shape — not a blanket fail.** `scripts/verification-queue-ceiling.json` records today's own counts as the ceiling; `--check` fails ONLY if a future run's no-Blocker or stale count exceeds it, naming the new offenders. Today's existing debt does not fail tomorrow's unrelated PR — explicitly instructed not to attempt the 130-item fix in this same item, and a hard gate against the current count would have done exactly that. `--write-ceiling` regenerates the baseline after a genuine improvement; raising it to silence a real regression is against the file's own header comment, same convention as every other ratchet here.
- **WIRED into `.github/workflows/build.yml`**, immediately after the `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` drift guard, alongside the other `--check`-mode drift guards this repo already runs on every PR and push to `main`.
- **CURRENT NUMBERS, measured this session (not the owner's manual count — a different, disclosed methodology; see the script's own header for why the two won't match exactly):** 584 V# items in the pending queue (587 total minus the 3 drained by B825232 this session); 566 classified `open`, 18 explicitly `❌ failed`; **262 with no `Blocker:` tag at all**; **35 older than 60 days** by the newest date mentioned in their own text; **270 open items carry no date at all** (their staleness is honestly unknown, not assumed — this likely means the true stale count is an undercount, stated plainly rather than papered over).
- **Tests:** `test/verificationQueueAudit.test.js` — pure-parser unit cases against a small fixture (no-Blocker detection, a real Blocker tag, an explicitly-failed item excluded, staleness computed against a fixed clock, the no-date case reported not guessed, the 60-day constant pinned) plus a live assertion that the real `VERIFICATION.md` currently passes its own recorded ceiling. 8/8 passing. Full suite green, lint 0 errors, build green.
- **What this deliberately does NOT do, per the item's own instruction:** fix any of the 262 no-Blocker or 35 stale items. That is a separate, much larger body of work; mixing it into this change would have buried the gate itself.
- Files: `scripts/verification-queue-audit.mjs` (new), `scripts/verification-queue-ceiling.json` (new), `test/verificationQueueAudit.test.js` (new), `.github/workflows/build.yml`, `MAP.md`.

`[x]` **✅ DONE — both halves fixed. (a) a Dead site no longer hides on the map (or in KMZ export) — it recedes (small/dim/✕, same treatment as Complete) but never vanishes. (b) a site-status change now offers a real, working "Undo" — a toast anchored to the action, not routed through the planner's element-level Ctrl+Z stack (which structurally cannot reach it: a status change is a site-header write from the Map's own component tree, not an element edit, and can fire with no plan even open).**

- **ROOT CAUSE (a), confirmed by reading, not guessing.** `STATUS_TOKENS.dead` (`shared/ui/statusTokens.js`) carried `hideByDefault: true` — a flag `MapFinder.jsx` honored at two render sites (the map pin/zoomed-plan render, and the KMZ export) with `if (status === "dead" && !statusFilter.has("dead")) return;`. A Dead site rendered on the map ONLY when the user proactively clicked the "Dead" status filter chip — otherwise it was omitted outright, from both the pins and the KMZ export, with no indication anything was hidden. (The "Your sites" LIST panel was NOT affected by this flag — a dead site was always still listed there, just filed under a "Dead" section that's COLLAPSED by default, matching "Complete." - **THE FIX.** Removed `hideByDefault` from `STATUS_TOKENS.dead` and both of `MapFinder.jsx`'s `status === "dead" && !statusFilter.has("dead")` gates. ### B814914 — Design tokens: audit the button-radius/height/padding/font-size spread and ship a single source of truth `[Design system]` (task) #ui #testing  *(owner chat block 2026-08-27, verbatim: "shouldnt we have some sort of bible for design definitions, we keep having different radii on buttons and it seems like a design bible would fix this." DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `RADIUS`, `design token`, `design bible`, `B427411`: **B427411** (Done, 2026-08-06) is a PRIOR instance of this exact owner complaint and already shipped a corner-radius scale (`shared/ui/radius.js`) + CSS mirror — not reopened, this item audits whether it actually closed the symptom (it partially did — see below) and extends the scale to the three categories it never covered. Net-new for spacing/type/height; radius itself is a consolidation of B427411's own follow-up debt, not a re-do.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — AUDIT-FIRST (real numbers, not impressions) + a documented tokens source of truth covering all four requested categories + the radius category applied mechanically to every button where it is provably zero-visual-change. Two genuine judgement calls surfaced by the audit are flagged below rather than decided silently, per this item's own instruction.**
- Verify: sandbox — a build-time/test-time concern (tokens, docs, a mechanical find-and-replace to existing pixel values); no GIS/timing/auth dependency.
- **THE AUDIT, exhaustive, not sampled: every `<button>` element in the app — 738 of them, across 573 files.** `borderRadius`: 22 distinct values before this item (dominated by raw `7`×43 — no token — `6`×34, `8`×33, `999`×27 "pill", plus a **second, narrower "pill" value, `99`×5** — a real correctness inconsistency, not just style: 99px fails to fully round a button taller than 99px, 999px never does). `height`: 17 distinct values (which DO already split cleanly into three real tiers — ~20-22 / ~24-26 / 30). `fontSize`: 15 distinct values (a fine half-point ladder, 10 through 14, genuinely six-plus real steps in active use, not noise). `padding`: **94 distinct raw strings** — no clean convergence at all.
- **THE TOKENS.** Radius already had a source of truth (`shared/ui/radius.js`'s `RADIUS={pill,sm,md,lg}`, B427411) — left exactly as-is, the canonical file. New sibling `src/shared/ui/designTokens.js` covers the three categories B427411 never touched: `SPACE={xxs:2,xs:4,sm:6,md:8,lg:10,xl:12,xxl:16}`, `FONT_SIZE={xs:10,sm:10.5,base:11,md:11.5,lg:12,xl:12.5,xxl:13,display:14}`, `CONTROL_H={sm:22,md:26,lg:30}` — every value is the tree's own measured MODAL value, never invented, matching `radius.js`'s own stated rule. CSS mirror: `--space-*`/`--font-*`/`--control-h-*` added to `index.css` alongside the pre-existing `--radius-*` block. `docs/DESIGN-TOKENS.md` is the actual "design bible" — the audit numbers, what each token category is for, what shipped vs. what's still open, and a usage example.
- **APPLIED MECHANICALLY, buttons only, zero visual change.** Every `<button>` whose literal `borderRadius` exactly equalled an existing token's pixel value was repointed at the token: `999`/`99` → `RADIUS.pill` (also closes the two-pill-values inconsistency above), `8` → `RADIUS.md`, `6` → `RADIUS.sm`, `12` → `RADIUS.lg` — same pixel value either way, the only change is that it can no longer drift independently. Applied across 22 files that had no radius token imported at all (`RADIUS` newly imported from `shared/ui/radius.js` in each); seven Notes workspace components already had their own tokenized mirror (a documented, deliberate B427411 follow-up) and needed no changes — confirmed by direct inspection, not assumed.
- **⛔ A CODEMOD-CORRECTNESS INCIDENT, caught before shipping, worth recording.** The first mechanical pass corrupted six sites — a naive "first `borderRadius:` within N chars of a `<button` tag" window matched the SAME source span from two nearby buttons in a few files, producing malformed double/triple tokens (`RADIUS.smADIUS.sm`, `RADIUS.pillIUS.pillIUS.pill`) that would have thrown at runtime though they parsed as valid JS (a plain `vite build` alone would not have caught them) — and, separately, one new import got inserted mid-way through an unrelated multi-line `import { ... } from` block, a straight syntax error. All six found by an exhaustive regex sweep for stutter patterns across every touched file (not by sampling), fixed by hand, and re-verified: a clean `npm run build` plus a targeted grep confirming zero remaining malformed `RADIUS.` references anywhere in `src/`.
- **⛔ TWO GENUINE JUDGEMENT CALLS, flagged rather than decided — full reasoning in `docs/DESIGN-TOKENS.md`.** (1) The raw `7` radius (43 sites, no token, sitting exactly between `sm`=6 and `md`=8) — nudging it either way is a real 1px visual change across 43 buttons; left untouched. (2) Padding/font-size retrofitting — 94 raw padding strings is real fragmentation, but collapsing them onto the new scale retroactively would touch visual proportions across a large fraction of the app, which is explicitly out of this item's scope ("do NOT redesign anything"); the scales exist now as the target for new work, not a completed retrofit.
- **TESTS.** New `test/designTokens.test.js` (6 tests): locks the audited token values in place and cross-checks the CSS mirror in `index.css` stays byte-for-byte in step with the JS, the same "two representations of one fact must agree" shape `palette.js`↔`index.css` already uses for color. `MAP.md` regenerated (`node scripts/build-map.mjs`) for the new file.
- Files: `src/shared/ui/designTokens.js` (new), `src/index.css`, `docs/DESIGN-TOKENS.md` (new), `test/designTokens.test.js` (new), `MAP.md`, plus the 22 files receiving the mechanical radius substitution: `app/Shell.jsx`, `shared/storage/StoragePanel.jsx`, `shared/ui/ColorField.jsx`, `shared/ui/Toast.jsx`, `shared/ui/PanelChrome.jsx`, `workspaces/admin/AdminApp.jsx`, `workspaces/doc-review/DocReview.jsx`, `workspaces/doc-review/Stitcher.jsx`, `workspaces/food/FoodApp.jsx`, `workspaces/food/components/FoodMap.jsx`, `workspaces/food/components/SearchBox.jsx`, `workspaces/food/components/VisitPanel.jsx`, `workspaces/library/components/FileBrowser.jsx`, `workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx`, `workspaces/site-planner/SitePlannerApp.jsx`, `workspaces/site-planner/components/ParcelInfoCard.jsx`, `ParcelRecordPanel.jsx`, `RoadCrossSectionDialog.jsx`, `SiteAnalysis.jsx`, `SiteReviewModal.jsx`, `TeamPanel.jsx`, `ActionLink.jsx`.

### B814915 — The "Location is blocked" message floated as a detached, page-corner banner instead of appearing next to the location button, and never auto-dismissed `[Site Planner / Map]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-27, verbatim: "this banner should pop up next to the location button" + a same-day amendment: "the banner doesnt need to stay for so long." Same subsystem as B814913 (map chrome placement), filed and shipped together per the owner's own instruction. Minted **B814915** from this branch's reserved block against `origin/main` 6d95614. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `locateUnavailableTooltip`, `Location is blocked`, `AnchoredMenu`, `B734529`: **B734529** (⏳ Verify) built the honest permission-aware states this item's message TEXT comes from (`locateUnavailableTooltip`) and is not reopened — that item's own code comment already stated the INTENT ("rendered on the control itself … never a page-covering banner") but the click-triggered path never actually implemented it, routing through the map's generic shared `err` corner banner instead; this item closes that gap. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — both required parts. (a) the message now renders in a popover anchored directly to the locate button (left-aligned, sitting just above it), reusing the app's existing AnchoredMenu component rather than inventing a new pattern. (b) it auto-dismisses on its own after 6 seconds, and is still dismissible by hand (✕, click-away, or Escape) before that.**
- Verify: sandbox — fully provable headless with a mocked geolocation permission state (the one 'blocked' state the app's own precheck can see); no live/GIS/auth dependency for the fix itself.
- **CURRENT BEHAVIOR, reported as instructed before changing anything.** The message rendered through `MapFinder.jsx`'s generic, page-corner `err` banner — shared with a dozen unrelated notices (address-search failures, parcel-service errors, sharing errors, KMZ export errors). That banner is `position:absolute`, spans from near the TOP of the pane on narrow/mobile widths down to the bottom-left zoom-control floor, with its content anchored to the BOTTOM of that span — so on a narrow layout it rendered right under the search bar while the actual locate button sits at the bottom-left corner, exactly the "floats near the top-left … no visual connection to the control" the owner described. **It never auto-dismissed at all** — grepped every `setErr` call site: no timer anywhere clears it; the only way it disappeared was an unrelated later action (a new address search, a parcel pick) happening to reset the same shared state, so in the worst case it could sit on screen indefinitely.
- **THE PATTERN CHOSEN, and why.** This app has two existing anchored/popover mechanisms: `ContextMenu` (positioned at a click's x/y coordinate, for right-click menus) and `AnchoredMenu` (positioned relative to a trigger ELEMENT via `getBoundingClientRect`, portal-to-`document.body`, already the shared mechanism for every other rail/flyout in the app — B734/B127). **Chose `AnchoredMenu`**, since the message is about a specific persistent CONTROL (the locate button), not a click point — the same reasoning that already governs every other anchored popover in this codebase. Its placement math (`anchoredMenuPlacement.js`) had three modes (`left`/`below-left`/`below-right`), none fitting a BOTTOM-LEFT corner control (a `below-*` placement would push off-screen); added a fourth, `above-left` (left-aligned, sits above the anchor — small, additive, backward-compatible), unit-tested alongside the existing three. Rendered in `hoverSafe` mode (no interactive full-viewport backdrop) so the popover never blocks ordinary map interaction while it's up — a passive notice, not a gate.
- **AUTO-DISMISS.** `LOCATE_NOTICE_MS = 6000` (6s) — chosen because the message is one short sentence (reads as two lines in the popover's width): long enough to read twice with room to spare, shorter than the app's general sync-conflict toast default (`TOAST_TTL_MS`, 8s) because there's no action to weigh here, just a fact to notice. Still dismissible immediately by hand (an explicit ✕, `AnchoredMenu`'s own click-away, or Escape) — none of those wait for the timer.
- **SELF-VERIFICATION, headless, real UI, at the widths B814913 was asked to hold (900/2000px), permission genuinely mocked to 'denied' (the app's own precheck-visible case) rather than the click handler stubbed.** New harness `ui-audit/verify-locate-notice-anchor.mjs`: clicks the real locate button, confirms the popover is announced (`role="status"`), carries the exact unmodified wording, is left-aligned with the button within a few px, sits above it with a small gap that never covers it, never overflows the viewport, carries a manual Dismiss, dismisses on click, re-appears on a fresh click, and — waiting the real 6.3s past the timer — auto-dismisses with no further action. **20/20 passing**, proven RED first (8 of 12 meaningful checks failed) against the pre-fix build. The pre-existing B734529 rig, `ui-audit/verify-locate-me.mjs` (30 checks covering the rest of the locate-button contract), re-run unmodified and still 30/30 — confirms this change didn't disturb any of that item's own coverage.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/MapFinder.jsx`, `src/shared/ui/anchoredMenuPlacement.js`, `test/anchoredMenuPlacement.test.js`, `ui-audit/verify-locate-notice-anchor.mjs` (new).

### B806080 (×2) — "Bring to front" on a callout is inert once an element/dimension LABEL covers it `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #markup  *(owner chat block 2026-08-27, three-item callout-leader batch alongside B806081/B806082. Repro: plan "Concept A (copy)" `smt7q6ar8egz`, callout `e1454866xdbcen` ("WETLANDS ARE PRESENT"). Owner: "i cant get this to get brought all the way forward." Production read-only SELECT: the callout's z was already the highest in its band (30720, next-highest callout 29696 — the app's z step is 1024) — the bump landed, and it still didn't clear what was covering it. Minted **B806080** from this branch's reserved block B806080–B806095 against `origin/main` b59dae8. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `PAINT_LADDER`, `paintOrder.js`, `calloutBands.above`, `labelEls`, `bring to front`, `B548819`, `B316864`: **B548819**'s `PAINT_LADDER` is the machine-enforced ladder this item extends — it enumerates all 11 rungs the six drawn families can reach and proves the render matches it, but never modeled where element/dimension LABELS sit; **B316864** built the analogous "force on top of everything" escape hatch for ELEMENTS crossing their type band, a different question (band, not label render order) and not affected. Net-new: a gap the ladder never covered, not a recurrence of either.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE, BOTH ROUNDS — a callout brought to front now clears EVERYTHING drawn on the plan (element geometry, labels, markups, AND measurements), not just its own family. Verified live in a headless Chromium browser, round 2 against the owner's own exact measured production case.**
- Verify: sandbox — pure client-side render-order + arrange-model fix (no GIS/auth/timing dependency); self-verified live per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK, both rounds.
- Origin: filed 2026-08-27 from chat.
- **Recurrence: 2026-08-27 (same day) — the owner corrected his own brief after round 1 shipped.** Verbatim: *"My brief was wrong and you took the branch it allowed. Correcting it out loud... Ignore the second branch entirely... Worse, the toast is now FACTUALLY FALSE."* Measured live on the merged round-1 build: callout `e1455193brcgly` ("WE WOULD BE REQUIRED TO DEDICATE THIS PORTION OF THE MAJOR THOROUGHFARE"), z=34816 — already the HIGHEST z of any callout on the plan — still painted UNDER area measurement `e1454898kaaymz` (z=0, a 60%-opaque cream wash), while "Bring to Front" told him it was "Already in front of everything on the plan." The z values prove z was never the mechanism (34816 > 0 and the measurement still won).
- **ROUND 1 — AUDIT-FIRST — what the ladder actually proved, and where the real defect was hiding.** `test/paintOrder.test.js`'s `PAINT_LADDER` (`lib/paintOrder.js`) already proves a callout in its "above" band (rung 9) paints over every element (rung 5/6) — so the repro's own investigation correctly RULED OUT "the callout paints under `el` geometry." What the ladder never modeled: element/dimension **labels** (`labelEls`, the collision-solved `<text>` pass) and the parcel acreage badge (`parcelLabels`) render in a SEPARATE pass, structurally LAST — after every annotation-above rung, callout included. No z value a callout can hold changes that, because paint order between the two passes was fixed by render POSITION, not by z.
- **ROUND 1 — THE FIX.** `{labelEls}` moved from its old position (after `{parcelLabels}`, just before the handle layer) to immediately after `{drawElsZ.above.map(...)}` — the same point the element pass itself ends, before ANY annotation-above rung (markup/reference/callout/measure) begins.
- **ROUND 2 — AUDIT-FIRST, what was still wrong.** Round 1 correctly closed the label gap but left rung 10 untouched: `PAINT_LADDER`'s own owner-decided default ("a measurement outranks decoration," B548819, 2026-08-15) sits structurally ABOVE the callout-above rung, and `arrangeAcrossBands` — round 1's "Bring to Front" mechanism — can only ever compare a callout against OTHER CALLOUTS (it reasons over one family's own `items` array). It has no way to reach above a markup or a measurement, which live in separate collections and separate render passes. So the WETLANDS callout being the highest-z callout on the plan made `arrangeAcrossBands` correctly report "nothing left to do" — a genuine no-op, hence the toast — while the picture was still wrong, because the toast was answering the wrong question.
- **ROUND 2 — THE FIX: a THIRD callout state, `frontForce: true`, the explicit reversible escape hatch B316864 gave elements, applied to callouts.** New `PAINT_LADDER` rung 11 (`lib/paintOrder.js`) — a callout with `frontForce: true` renders from its own dedicated pass (`calloutBands.forced`), which is the LAST content pass before the handle layer — after element geometry, element labels, markups (either band), measurements (either band), AND the parcel acreage badge. Only the handle layer's transient selection chrome may still paint over it. Two new pure functions (`lib/arrange.js`): `calloutFrontForceZ` (the z a forced callout needs to clear every OTHER forced callout) and `calloutAtAbsoluteFront` (the ONE fact "Already in front of everything" may be built from — genuinely true of the resulting paint order, never the old within-band `atTop`). `arrangeSel`'s callout branch handles `mode === "front"` entirely outside `arrangeAcrossBands` now: it sets `frontForce: true` (clearing `behindEls`) and bumps z only when needed to clear other forced callouts. Any OTHER arrange command (Bring Forward / Send Backward / Send to Back) on a forced callout clears `frontForce` first, folded into the SAME undo-frame commit — reversible, discoverable through the ordinary menu rows, never a second silent state. The menu row's own disabled state (`bringToFrontDis`) reads `calloutAtAbsoluteFront` for a callout instead of the old within-family `af.atTop`, so the row and the toast can never independently drift about what "already at the front" means again.
- **What is NOT changed, either round:** the `PAINT_LADDER`'s original 11→12 rungs' relative order, `arrangeAcrossBands`'s behaviour for markups/measurements, and B548819's own "measurement outranks decoration" DEFAULT (still true of every untouched callout — this only adds one more EXPLICIT, reversible rung an individual forced callout can reach, the same shape B316864 already established for elements).
- **Verified round 1 (sandbox/headless, logged out — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK):** `test/calloutBringToFront.test.js` (3 tests), `test/paintOrder.test.js`, `test/handleLayerOrder.test.js`; e2e `e2e/callout-leader-interaction.spec.js` against the owner's real Goose Creek fixture.
- **Verified round 2 (sandbox/headless, logged out — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK, on the owner's OWN measured case, not a synthetic one):** new `test/calloutAbsoluteFront.test.js` (6 tests, incl. a replay of the exact pre-fix `arrangeAcrossBands` call over his real ids/z-values, proven RED pre-fix); `test/paintOrder.test.js` extended with rung 11 + a source guard that the forced tier paints after `parcelLabels` and before the handle layer (proven RED pre-fix). New e2e spec `e2e/callout-absolute-front.spec.js` seeds a THROWAWAY plan with the callout + measure geometry read VERBATIM off the real production row via a read-only SELECT (site `smt7q6ar8egz`, ids `e1455193brcgly`/`e1454898kaaymz` — production Supabase touched read-only, never written) — drives the real menu (right-click → Bring to Front), asserts the callout now paints after the measurement via `compareDocumentPosition`, that the row reads DISABLED with the accurate toast only once genuinely true, that the keyboard chord (`⌘/Ctrl+Shift+]`) fires the same accurate toast, and that Ctrl+Z undoes the force — **proven RED against the pre-fix (round-1-only) source**, reproducing the owner's exact reported defect (disabled row, false toast, callout still covered) verbatim. Full unit suite: 12,871 passed, 0 failures (630 files). Lint 0 errors. Build green. Bundle audit: all budgets within ceiling (`largestChunkBytes` +8.6 KB total across both rounds, inside the 32.1 KB headroom band).
- **PDF-PARITY:** automatic and unchanged, both rounds — `exportSheet.js` clones the live SVG (`buildExportSvg`), so the corrected render order (including the new forced tier) rides the export with no separate change; no export-path test references label/callout/measure ordering, and the full suite (including export tests) is green.
