- **AUDIT-FIRST — confirmed the exact mechanism, then found the established fix shape already in the file.** `addLeaderFor` (armed by the callout menu's "Add Leader" row) is checked at the very top of `onBgDown`, the canvas's BUBBLE-phase pointerdown handler bound on the root `<svg>`. `startMoveEl`/`startMoveMarkup` — bound with `pointerEvents="all"` on every element/markup shape — call `e.stopPropagation()` as their second statement (after only a `tool !== "select"` gate, which does not exclude this case, since Add Leader arms while `tool` is still `"select"`), so `onBgDown` never sees the press when it lands on geometry. The exact same shape already exists and is solved for a different armed gesture: `handleStackPick` (B548822, Alt+click) runs in the CAPTURE phase — before any bubble-phase handler — specifically because "it has to win over whichever feature's own bubble-phase pointerdown paint order would otherwise hand the press to."
- **THE FIX.** New `handleAddLeaderCapture(e)`, wired into the SAME `onPointerDownCapture` chain as `notePress`/`handleStackPick`/`onCanvasVtxDownCapture`, checked FIRST (ahead of the stack picker too — Add Leader is a modal placement, not a modifier, so it must win over an Alt+click as well). It consumes the press (`preventDefault`+`stopPropagation`), computes the feet point, calls the existing `addLeaderToCallout`, and clears the armed state — the identical outcome the old bubble-phase branch in `onBgDown` produced, just reached before any element/markup handler can steal the event. The old `if (addLeaderFor)` branch in `onBgDown` is removed (retired, not duplicated) since it is now unreachable while armed.
- **What is unchanged:** `startMoveEl`/`startMoveMarkup` themselves — no per-handler patching, so every other gesture (selection, drag, group-move, attach/align) behaves exactly as before; only the ONE new capture-phase check sits ahead of all of them.
- **Verified (sandbox/headless, logged out — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK):** new `test/calloutAddLeaderCapture.test.js` (4 source-guard tests, proven RED pre-fix) — the capture handler exists, is wired ahead of the stack picker and the vertex-edit capture, consumes the press, and the old bubble-phase branch is gone. `test/featureTarget.test.js`'s two wiring assertions (`handleStackPick`'s exact capture-chain string) updated to match the new chain and re-verified green (70 tests). New e2e spec `e2e/callout-leader-interaction.spec.js` drives the owner's real Goose Creek fixture: arms Add Leader on a seeded callout, clicks dead center on a real building that is ALSO covered by a markup covering it (proving the fix wins over BOTH handler types with one press), and asserts the leader count increased, the building was neither selected nor moved by the placement click, and no page errors — proven RED against the pre-fix source (the click silently landed on the markup and neither a leader nor a selection changed). Full unit suite green (12,820 passed; the 2 pre-existing unrelated failures noted on B806080 unaffected). Lint 0 errors. Build green.
- **PDF-PARITY:** not applicable — pure interaction/event-handling fix, no drawn geometry changes.

### B806082 — Right-click a callout leader to delete it `[Site Planner]` (feature/bug) #site-planner #ui #markup #selection  *(owner chat block 2026-08-27, alongside B806080/B806081. Owner: "i should be able to right click to delete leader." Minted **B806082** from this branch's reserved block B806080–B806095 against `origin/main` b59dae8. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `Delete Leader`, `calloutHandles`, `data-handle=\"callout-tip\"`, `CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS`, `B919`: **B919** already shipped multi-leader callouts with a "Delete Leader" row wired to `onCalloutContext(e, c.id, i)` on the leader's own `<g>` — that mechanism is real and correct, and the fix below does NOT touch it. The defect is a NEW instance of the named rule CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS (precedents: B1174/B1327/B50010/B233153), not a recurrence of B919. Net-new finding.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — right-click now works from the leader's re-aim grips too (the tip and the elbow), not only from the leader line itself. Verified live in a headless Chromium browser: right-clicking the grip opens Delete Leader, the leader count drops, and undo restores it; right-clicking empty canvas is unaffected.**
- Verify: sandbox — pure client-side event-forwarding fix; self-verified live per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK.
- Origin: filed 2026-08-27 from chat.
- **AUDIT-FIRST found the mechanism was already built and already had the RIGHT documented intent — it just wasn't wired to the one place a natural right-click actually lands.** The leader's own `<g>` already carries `onContextMenu={(e) => onCalloutContext(e, c.id, i)}`, and "Delete Leader" (gated on `mapMenu.leaderIndex >= 0`) already exists in the map menu (B919). But once a callout is SELECTED, `calloutHandles` renders three grip kinds into the always-on-top `data-handle-layer` group: the box's width grips, a per-leader TIP grip (a filled circle sitting EXACTLY at the arrowhead — the single most obvious place to aim a right-click at a leader), and a per-leader ELBOW grip. In SVG, paint order is hit-test order, so any of those wins a press landing on it — and NONE of the three carried an `onContextMenu`. A right-click aimed at a leader's tip therefore fell straight through the leader's own handler (never reached — the grip is topmost) all the way to the empty-canvas map menu, in total silence. The tip grip's own adjacent code comment even already said "a single leader is removed by right-clicking it → 'Delete Leader'" — the intent was documented, the wiring wasn't there. This is a fresh instance of the CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS rule: a handle that paints over its own object's body must forward the press to that object, never swallow it.
- **THE FIX.** All three grip kinds now forward a right-click to the SAME handler the object they belong to already uses: the tip and elbow grips call `onCalloutContext(e, c.id, i)` (their own leader's menu, offering Delete Leader); the width grips call `onCalloutContext(e, c.id, -1)` (the box's menu). No new hit targets, no new menu rows — reusing the existing fat leader hit-lines' handler exactly as the item's own "already measured" note directed. A locked callout's width grips already render `pointerEvents:none`, so a right-click there correctly falls through to the box body underneath (which still forwards) rather than needing a separate guard.
- **What is unchanged:** the leader body's own `onContextMenu`, the box body's, the "Delete Leader" row's gating and its undo behavior (already correct per B919) — only the three previously-silent grip nodes gained a handler. Right-clicking empty canvas away from any callout is untouched and still opens the ordinary map menu (Zoom to fit / Paste / Export…).
- **Verified (sandbox/headless, logged out — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK):** new `test/calloutHandleContextMenu.test.js` (3 source-guard tests, proven RED pre-fix) — asserts each of the three grip kinds carries the correct forwarding `onContextMenu`. New e2e spec `e2e/callout-leader-interaction.spec.js` drives the owner's real Goose Creek geometry: seeds a two-leader callout, selects it, right-clicks EXACTLY at the tip grip's own bounding-box center (with a precondition proving `document.elementFromPoint` at that exact pixel resolves to the grip, not the leader line — so the check cannot pass vacuously), asserts the resulting menu is the callout's (Delete Leader visible, "Zoom to fit" — the empty-canvas menu's own row — absent), clicks Delete Leader, asserts the leader count dropped by one (reading either the `tips[]` array shape or the singular `tip` field the model collapses to at N=1, per B919), then Ctrl+Z and asserts the leader count is restored. A second case confirms right-clicking genuine empty canvas still opens the ordinary map menu, unaffected. Both proven RED against the pre-fix source (Delete Leader never appeared; the grip swallowed the press in total silence, matching the report exactly). Full unit suite green (12,820 passed; the 2 pre-existing unrelated failures noted on B806080 unaffected). Lint 0 errors. Build green.
- **PDF-PARITY:** not applicable — the three grip nodes are already `data-export="skip"` chrome (the handle layer is stripped from every export); no exported geometry changed.

`[x]` **✅ DONE — the rule language, the engine, and the panel are rebuilt; the live "Complete beats overdue" regression (212/557 of the owner's real leaf tasks, 38%, measured via read-only SELECT) is fixed as a first-class, visible, editable rule clause instead of a hardcode.**
- Verify: sandbox — pure client-side rule-engine logic + a self-hosted panel UI (no GIS, no concurrency, no signed-in-only surface); self-verified live in three separate headless-Chromium runs this session (screenshot attached to the PR), two of them driving the actual rebuilt panel's real DOM (clicks, `<select>`s, live-computed grid colors), and every new guard mutation-proven (a deliberately broken build was confirmed to flip the checks red before being reverted).
- **STAGE 1 — measured, not assumed.** Read his 6 real schedules read-only (Goose Creek/Grand Port/8 South/Pursuits/Pappadoupolos/Operations, 778 tasks, 557 leaves — exact match to the brief's own count). Findings that changed the design: (a) **"Task is 100% complete" was structurally unable to fire off his real workflow** — clicking the status dot only ever writes `health:"green"` (`HealthPicker` → `commit` → `applyUpdate` → `updateTask(id,{health:val})`), never touches `percentComplete`; only 70/557 (12.6%) of his tasks ever reach 100%, and `percentComplete` isn't a visible column on ANY of his 6 plans' saved column config. (b) The measured live blast radius: **212/557 leaf tasks (38%)** are marked Complete with `percentComplete` still 0 and a finish date in the past — exactly the shape his one configured rule (`finishPastDays/days:1/red`, no other rules) mis-paints red. (c) A SECOND, not-yet-triggered instance of the same defect: `notStarted`'s old condition had no Complete-guard at all — 200/311 of his Complete-marked tasks would *also* false-fire it the moment he ever added that rule. (d) Automation rules are **global across all 6 plans**, not per-project (no code anywhere reads a per-project `healthRules`) — surfaced to him as a fork; he chose to keep it. (e) `predecessors` populated on 382/557 (68.6%) — the one canned condition worth keeping as-is; `responsibleParty` empty on 522/557 (93.7%) and `cost`/`budget`/`actualCost` populated on 5/0/0 — flagged as low-signal fields for now, not removed from the language.
- **THE LANGUAGE.** A rule is `IF (conditions, AND/OR) THEN set status to (color) UNLESS (conditions, AND/OR — optional)`. A condition is `[field] [comparison] [value]`, Smartsheet-style — `RULE_FIELDS` (Finish date, Start date, Status, Owner, % Complete, Cost, Budget, Actual Cost, Predecessor) × `RULE_OPS` (date: is N+ days past due / is within N days / is more than N days away / is today / is blank / is not blank; status: is / is not; text: is blank / is not blank / is / contains; number: is / is more than / is less than / is at least / is at most / is blank / is not blank; predecessor: is late) — collapsing the old seven fixed sentences into ~6 fields × a handful of comparisons, with AND/OR composition and the UNLESS exception clause on top. His exact sentence renders verbatim: `IF Finish date is in the past THEN set Status to Needs Attn. UNLESS Status is Complete`.
- **THE ENGINE** (`public/sequence/index.html`, mirrored verbatim in `ui-audit/stress/scheduler-engine.mjs` per this repo's existing faithful-copy convention): `evalFieldCondition` (one condition, absence-safe — a missing date/text field always fails except the explicit blank tests; a missing number reads as 0, matching the long-standing `percentComplete||0` convention) → `evalConditionGroup` (AND/OR over a condition list; an empty group never matches) → `evalRule` (fires — returns the color — iff `when` matches and `unless` does not) → unchanged `evalHealthRules`/`computeDisplayHealth` call sites and signatures, so every existing caller (grid, Gantt, MasterView, PDF/web export, focus-overdue filtering) inherits the fix with zero changes of its own. `HEALTH_CONDITIONS`/`evalHealthCondition` (the old seven-condition vocabulary) are RETAINED, unused by the live engine, only as `migrateRule`'s frozen translation reference and because the existing test suite pins their exact semantics.
- **BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY, three generations deep.** `getHealthRules(settings)` now migrates ALL THREE stored shapes — the very-old 3-toggle `cfRules`, the v1 ordered-list from #1073, and native v2 — into the v2 `{when,unless}` shape live, purely derived, never persisted (same philosophy the original `migrateCfRulesToHealthRules` already used: nothing repaints until the panel is opened and touched). `migrateRule`'s `LEGACY_RULE_FIELD_MAP` translates each of the seven old condition types onto the new field/op vocabulary with byte-identical semantics (`notStarted` becomes a genuine two-condition AND — start past-due AND %Complete ≤ 0 — proving the new language subsumes the old one, not just replaces it).
- **THE ACTUAL FIX, made structural instead of a hardcode.** Every migrated non-green rule gets an auto-attached, VISIBLE, EDITABLE `unless: Status is Complete OR Status is Paused` — not a special case, just what `migrateRule` does for any rule whose color isn't green. This is the real form of the emergency hardcode in-flight on `claude/overdue-task-red-bug-qe277v` (PR #1178, `if (task.health==="green") return "green"` ahead of the whole rule engine, B780448) — per the brief's own instruction ("that hardcode should become a visible, editable default rule"), this item's fix supersedes it: the exception now lives on the rule, is readable in the panel, can be removed or extended (e.g. `OR Owner is not blank`) per rule, and generalizes to every rule a user writes instead of one global override that can never be turned off. #1178 was not merged into this branch (still open, unrelated diff) — closing it (or reconciling on merge) is a one-line follow-up once this lands. Confirmed against the ORIGINAL pre-#1073 engine too (read directly, not by data-mining): the very first cfRules-based `computeDisplayHealth` already excluded `health==="green"`/`"paused"` from `overdueRed` unconditionally — this fix restores original, sensible behavior that the #1073/#1160 rework lost, not a novel risk.
- **THE PANEL** (`AutomationPanel`, plus new `ConditionRow`/`ConditionGroup` components): each rule is a card — IF (condition rows, AND/OR toggle, + Add condition) → THEN set status to (color swatch) → UNLESS (optional, "+ Add exception" defaults straight to `Status is Complete` — the one exception the owner actually asked for, one click away) → reorder (▲▼, first-match-wins kept per his choice) / delete. Widened 360→440px; measured live via `getBoundingClientRect` at a 1400px viewport with no horizontal overflow (right edge 1388 vs viewport 1400). Reuses the existing `RuleColorPicker` for both THEN-color and Status-condition-value pickers (it already lists every built-in + custom status).
- **PRODUCT FORKS THE OWNER DECIDED** (via `AskUserQuestion`, not assumed): (1) rules stay ONE shared set across all 6 plans, not per-plan — "One shared rule set (current behavior)"; (2) precedence stays an ORDERED list, first FIRING rule wins — "Ordered list, first match wins"; (3) row-coloring — the proposal wrongly framed this as an open choice ("status dot only" vs "whole row"); he corrected it on the spot: the Gantt AND grid rows already tint their full row background by `displayHealth` (`rowBg` in `index.html`, unrelated to this item) — no change needed, nothing to decide; (4) cross-task references stay PREDECESSOR-ONLY for v1, matching what already exists today — parent/child rollup-aware rules ("flag the summary row if any child is overdue") explicitly deferred, not built.
- **TEST COVERAGE.** `test/schedulerEngine.test.js`: a new `NEW-rule-language` block (fields/ops per type, AND/OR composition, `evalRule` incl. his exact sentence and the AND/OR worked example, `migrateRule` for all seven legacy types, and the exact live-measured regression case reproduced and fixed as a unit test) — 430/430 passing, the core `unless` guard mutation-proven red before being restored. Four PRE-EXISTING tests that encoded the now-superseded "rules always win, even over a hand-picked green" reading from `RULES-DECIDE`/2026-08-25 (itself corrected by the owner one day later) were rewritten, not deleted, with the supersession stated inline and the exact live-shape (green + percentComplete never bumped + overdue) added as its own assertion. Two pre-existing live-browser harnesses (`ui-audit/verify-overdue-rules-win.mjs`, `ui-audit/verify-schedule-export-health-colours.mjs`) needed the same one-fixture correction each (a green-and-overdue seed task's expected color) and both re-verified passing end to end, including the export/PDF path (PDF-PARITY) and the RuleColorPicker dismiss-behavior suite. A new dedicated harness, `ui-audit/verify-automation-rule-language.mjs`, drives the rebuilt panel itself end to end — opens it, clicks "+ Add rule" (task flips green→red live), clicks "+ Add exception" (flips back red→green with zero further clicks), adds a second IF condition and confirms the AND/OR toggle appears, and measures the panel's real geometry at his plans' actual `rowHeight:20` setting.

`[x]` **✅ DONE — all nine sub-requirements (a)–(i) implemented; self-verified live in a headless browser this session (31/31 checks passed, including PDF-PARITY and the View ▾ toggle); a real, previously-shipping bug was found and fixed along the way (below).**
- Verify: live — **V435472**, PASSED this session (see `VERIFICATION-DONE.md`). Zoom-/data-density-dependent rendering and PDF/export parity are both mandatory LIVE-VERIFY classes; this is genuinely no-auth, no-GIS, 100% client-side canvas/dialog work, so the headless self-verification IS the live-verify for every class this item touches, per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK.
- **(a) THE FIELD, storage.** `xsection.rowDesignFt` — a new, optional key on the road element's existing `xsection` object (`lib/roadCrossSection.js`). Deliberately NOT named `rowW`/`rowWidth`/anything close: `rowW` already names an unrelated TABLE ROW WIDTH in `AppHeader`/`headerCenterFit.js`, and `rowWidth(xsection)` is the pre-existing DERIVED band-total function this item does not replace — a name near either would read as the same concept and isn't. **PRESENCE IS THE SIGNAL** (`designatedRowFt(xsection)`), never a numeric comparison against the band total: a road with no `rowDesignFt` at all has never had a ROW designated, and every caller (dialog, canvas, Properties) gates on `designatedRowFt(...) != null` — so a designated ROW that happens to exactly equal the modeled bands (a real, valid case: every foot of the legal ROW is accounted for by drawn bands) still reads as genuinely designated, not as "nothing to show." `makeXSection(bands, rowDesignFt)` omits the key entirely (never writes `null`/`0`/`NaN`) when the value isn't a real positive number, and `xsectionFromRoad(el)` carries an already-designated ROW through unchanged when the dialog re-opens on that road — never silently dropped.
- **(b) THE DIALOG FIELD.** A new "Right-of-way width (ft)" row beneath the summary line, defaulting to the current band total (so an untouched field commits nothing) and editable upward. The summary line grows two new spans, shown only once a real ROW is designated: **Designated ROW `<N>`′** and **ROW margin `<(designated−modeled)/2>`′ each side**. `X` in that margin formula is the FULL modeled band total (`rowWidth`, which already includes any explicit outside-curb sidewalk/parkway/ditch band), never curb-to-curb alone — an explicit parkway band is already accounted-for ROW, not margin stacked on top of it, and this is also why the field defaults to the band total (an untouched default then reads as zero margin, not a mystery leftover).
- **⛔ (b), THE REAL BUG THIS SESSION FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT — A DEFAULT THAT LOOKS COMMITTED CAN SILENTLY REFUSE TO COMMIT.** Both the dialog's ROW field (`BandWidthInput`) and the Properties panel's ROW field (`NumInput`) only call `onCommit` when the typed value differs from the current `value` PROP — correct for every other field in this app, because their `value` IS the true persisted model value, so retyping the same digits really is a no-op. The ROW field's `value` is NOT that: it's `designatedRowFt(xsection) ?? Math.round(rowWidth(xsection))` — a computed DEFAULT shown when nothing is designated yet. The realistic case this dispatch itself supplies triggers it exactly: a 68′ boulevard + two 16′ parkways models to precisely 100′, the field pre-fills "100," and typing the same "100" to explicitly designate it hit `next === value` and **silently did nothing** — no error, no commit, the field still reads "100" either way. Caught by the live-verify script itself (the first run reported `Designated ROW: null` after typing exactly the dispatch's own numbers), not by inspection. **Fixed at both call sites** with an opt-in `forceCommit` prop (`BandWidthInput` in `RoadCrossSectionDialog.jsx`; `NumInput` in `SitePlanner.jsx`) plus a `dirtyRef` that tracks a real keystroke, so a genuinely untouched blur still costs nothing, but a field the user actually typed into commits even when the digits match the shown default. Every other caller of both components (dozens, across this codebase) is untouched — `forceCommit` defaults `false` and is passed only at these two ROW call sites.
- **(c)/(d) CANVAS — the "should be shown" half.** The ROW draws as two thin dashed boundary lines, one each side, offset from the road's own TRIMMED dense centerline (`roadDenseCenterline`, the exact geometry the pavement ribbon and the within-curb bands are already built from) by `±rowDesignFt/2` via the same `offsetPolyline` used everywhere else in this feature — so it curves, arcs and trims identically to the ribbon, never a separate straight-line approximation. An inline "`N`′ R.O.W." label rides the midpoint, styled like the existing width-dimension callout (same font/scale/halo idiom — `stroke="#fff"` white halo, matching that pre-existing label's own hardcoded halo exactly, the one deliberate raw-hex exception in this diff) in a neutral tone rather than the dimension's red, so the two are never mistaken for one control. Gated on `rowMarginFt(xsection) != null` (never drawn when nothing is designated, and never drawn when the modeled bands EXCEED the designated ROW — see (g)) and on the new View ▾ toggle (below).
- **(e) LAYERS/VIEW TOGGLE.** `settings.showRowLines` (new, default `true`, read via `!== false` so a project saved before this key existed still shows the lines) joins the `showGrid`/`showDims` family in the View ▾ menu's "Detail" section (`ViewMenu.jsx`) — same checkbox shape, same section, same persistence mechanism. Unchecking it hides both the boundary lines and the label; re-checking restores them — confirmed live, not just wired (see verification below).
- **(f) PDF EXPORT PARITY.** Automatic, per this feature's established pattern (`exportSheet.js` clones the live `<svg>` verbatim) — no separate export-path code needed, and confirmed rather than argued: the app's own `window.__plannerExportSvg` self-audit hook shows both dashed ROW lines and the "R.O.W." label present in the exported sheet.
- **(g) LOUD-FAILURE — never silently clamped.** When the modeled band total exceeds the designated ROW, `rowMarginFt` returns `null` (not a negative number), which is what keeps the canvas from ever drawing a ROW boundary that would sit INSIDE the paved section. The dialog surfaces this as a `role="alert"` banner in the `--danger-bg`/`--danger-border`/`--danger-text` tokens: "⚠ The modeled bands total `X`′ — wider than the designated `Y`′ right-of-way. Widen the ROW or narrow the bands; it is not auto-clamped." — confirmed it does NOT appear for a valid (non-exceeding) designation, including the exact-equality case.
- **(h) FOOTPRINT/PAVING/CURB STAY CURB-TO-CURB.** No change to `costTakeoff.js` or the footprint calc — both already read `travelW`/curb-to-curb width, never the full band total, and this item adds nothing that widens either. Confirmed live: a 100′-designated-ROW road's footprint is computed from its 68′ curb-to-curb width, not 100′ (Properties panel: `134,057 SF` on a 1,943′ road ≈ `68′ × length + end caps`, not `100′ × length`). Reporting ROW area separately was judged not cheap enough to add without a stated product need for it — the dispatch said "only if it is cheap" — so it was left out; the designated width itself is already visible in three places (dialog, canvas label, Properties), which was judged to satisfy the underlying ask.
- **(i) PROPERTIES PANEL, read/write.** A new "Right-of-way (ft)" `Field` (gated on `selEl.xsection` truthy — any road that has been through the dialog at least once, even the single-band wrapper) sits directly beneath the existing read-only "Road width (ft) … curb to curb" row, using the same `NumInput` + `allowClear` pattern every other Properties dimension field uses (blank the field to un-designate; it reverts to showing the modeled section's own total and the canvas ROW boundary stops drawing). Carries the same `forceCommit` fix as (b) — confirmed live as an independent second proof of that fix, via the Properties field rather than the dialog field.

- **ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by reading the render path (`SitePlanner.jsx`'s `renderElPx`, the `hasXSection(el)` branch), not assumed.** The existing band-fill loop built ONE fill list from every band with a fill token, clipped the whole group to the road's own pavement-ring `clipPath` (`dPath`, the curb-to-curb polygon) — correct for a within-curb band (median/shoulder/curb-and-gutter/parking/bike, which must never spill past the curb), but an outside-curb band (sidewalk/parkway/ditch) sits ENTIRELY past that ring by construction, so clipping it to `dPath` clipped it away to nothing. Structurally proven, not just counted: exactly 1 fill sits inside the `g[clip-path]` wrapper (the median) and exactly 2 sit outside it (both parkways) — the DOM query distinguishes them by CLIP MEMBERSHIP rather than fill color, because parkway and median deliberately share the same fill token (`var(--success-text)`, per `BAND_FILL_TOKEN`) and opacity, so a color-based assertion could not have told them apart. PDF-PARITY: the exported sheet (`window.__plannerExportSvg`) carries all 3 `fill="var(--success-text)"` fills, confirming the fix needed no separate export-path code, per this feature's established clone-the-live-SVG mechanism.
- **PAVING/CURB COST — confirmed unaffected, as the audit predicted before any code was written.** `costTakeoff.js`'s paving/curb rollup already reads `pavedWidth(xsection)`, and every `withinCurb:false` type (sidewalk/parkway/ditch) is also `paved:false` in `BAND_TYPES` — so painting these bands required zero changes to cost math. ### B779392 — Road cross-section preview: draw it horizontally, like a real typical section `[Site Planner / road]` (bug) #site-planner #road #ui  *(follow-up on the just-merged B776560, owner: "and lets make it horizontal? that makes sense to me based on the details I usually see." Right, and not a preference — a roadway typical section is drawn looking down the road: pavement runs left-to-right, the dimension string runs horizontally beneath it, matching every civil plan set / TxDOT standard / municipal detail. Four reasons given: (1) a dimension string only works horizontally — the very thing B776560 had to rotate 90° and clip to "tot"; (2) it matches the plan-view road on the canvas, which is also horizontal; (3) a wide section (his 68′ boulevard) is wide-and-shallow, which fits a horizontal layout's natural width instead of forcing a tall column that overflows; (4) offsets read left/right of centerline, the actual civil convention. Four things rotation alone would not give, all required: (a) mark the centerline (dash-dot line + symbol, at the section's true offset 0); (b) handle label collision with a leader line rather than clipping/squeezing/overflow, tested against a 20′ median beside a 2′ curb band; (c) keep the one genuine advantage the vertical layout had — the list row lining up with its band — via a hover/focus highlight; (d) scale to fit the dialog's actual width rather than clip or scroll, checked at the narrowest usable window. Minted **B779392** from this branch's reserved block B779392–B779407 against `origin/main` 9581d5d. `[x]` **✅ DONE — the preview is rotated to run left-to-right with a centerline mark, a real horizontal dimension string replacing the old rotated total label, leader-line collision handling for narrow bands, an active-band hover/focus highlight, and container-width-aware scale-to-fit. Implemented and self-verified live in a headless browser this session (28/28 new checks, plus the two pre-existing harnesses re-run clean — 48/48 and 33/33, no regression).**
- Verify: sandbox — pure client-side dialog/SVG layout (no GIS, no concurrency, no signed-in-only surface, no real-project-data repro needed); self-verified live in a headless browser this session per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK.
- **(1) THE ROTATION.** `XSectionPreview`'s band rects now vary in `x` and share one `y` — bands drawn left to right, matching the road as it's actually drawn on the plan-view canvas. `bandLayout`'s existing sign convention (offset 0 = the road's true drawn centerline) is unchanged; only the axis it's projected onto moved. Lane striping is vertical now (was horizontal), and the in-band type/width label is centered in the band's own horizontal span rather than its vertical one.
- **(2) THE HORIZONTAL DIMENSION STRING — replaces the rotated total label at the root, not a patch.** A tick mark at every band boundary, each band's own width figure underneath, the running total (still `f1(rowW)′ total`, never rotated) beneath that. This is what B776560's rotated `<text transform="rotate(90 …)">` needed to become: a rotated label needs the box's HEIGHT to hold its whole rendered length, which is exactly what clipped it to "tot" at any modest height; a horizontal string never has that problem at any section width, by construction, so this removes the bug's root cause rather than reserving more space for the old approach.
- **(3) THE CENTERLINE.** A dash-dot line (`8 3 1.5 3`) runs through the section at `xOf(0)` — the section's true drawn offset, not the geometric middle of the whole preview box (they differ whenever a flank band like a sidewalk sits on only one side). The mark itself is drawn as two stacked plain-ASCII "C"/"L" glyphs rather than the Unicode centerline symbol (U+2104), deliberately — a symbol from an unusual Unicode block risks silently rendering as a tofu box in some font stacks, where two ordinary capital letters cannot.
- **(4) LABEL COLLISION — a leader line out, never a clip/squeeze/overflow, both for the in-band type label and the dimension string's own width figure.** `packRows` (new, pure, module-scope) greedily row-packs a set of `{mid, halfW}` items so nothing sharing a row overlaps; used independently for (i) in-band labels too wide for their own band's column, which move onto a leader line above the swatch showing the FULL "Type · width" text (no longer needing to fit ANY column once outside it), and (ii) dimension-string numbers too wide for their own band's ticks, which drop one row lower on a short leader stub. Fit is decided by a deliberately-conservative text-width estimate (`estTextW`, erring wide) rather than a real DOM measurement, so a borderline label is more likely to get a leader than to risk a squeeze. Verified live against the owner's own named case (a 20′ median beside a 2′ curb-and-gutter band): the curb band's full label and its width figure both render, fully unclipped, with zero overlapping label boxes anywhere in the preview.
- **(5) THE LIST-TO-PREVIEW CORRESPONDENCE, preserved rather than lost in the rotation.** The dialog tracks which band row is hovered or keyboard-focused (`activeIdx`) and passes it to the preview, which outlines the matching band in the accent color. Wired via `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave`/`onFocus`/`onBlur` on each band row (the row itself also gets a subtle background tint) — verified live: hovering the Median row highlights exactly the Median band and nothing else; moving away clears it.
- **(6) SCALE TO FIT — measured, not assumed.** The preview measures its own wrapping `<div>`'s real width via `ResizeObserver` (synchronously in a `useLayoutEffect`, so there is no flash of the wrong size on first paint) and sizes its per-foot scale to exactly fill that measured width, capped at a legibility ceiling for a narrow/single-band section. The SVG's `width`/`height` attributes always exactly match its `viewBox` (the same discipline B776560 established for the vertical layout's height, now applied to the width, which is now the axis that has to fit) — verified live at the dialog's default width, and again after shrinking the browser viewport to 480px: the SVG's own width attribute matches its rendered pixel size exactly at both sizes, it never exceeds its wrapping container, and the dialog itself never gains a horizontal scrollbar.
- **CHECKED AT THE NAMED WIDTHS, live.** The owner's own 12/12/20/12/12 boulevard at 68′; a single-band 25′ private drive (the built-in preset); the mixed section with a narrow 2′ curb-and-gutter band beside the 20′ median; and the dialog shrunk to a 480px-wide window. All four render correctly with no clipping, no overlap, and no overflow.

Re-ran both pre-existing harnesses unchanged: `ui-audit/verify-road-xsection-typing.mjs` (the B776560 typing-bug suite) — 48/48 still passing, no regression to the keystroke/commit behavior or the total label's integrity; `ui-audit/verify-road-crosssection.mjs` (the original B773728 feature harness) — 33/33 still passing, no regression to migration, canvas rendering, presets, paving-cost split, or PDF-export parity.

Full unit suite: 12694 tests, 2 pre-existing failures — the same shallow-clone `git show` mutation-check artifacts already documented on other items in this file (`docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js`, `hiddenContentReads.test.js`), confirmed unrelated. ### B776560 — Road cross-section dialog: the band-width field validated on every keystroke, not on commit `[Site Planner / road]` (bug) #site-planner #road #ui  *(follow-up on the just-merged B773728, owner using the dialog live and hitting this immediately, verbatim: "when i type two it seems to bug out a little bit, I'm just typing 2 to get to 25." Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — all four parts fixed (the keystroke-validation bug, every named adjacent typing case, the clipped/rotated total label, and the pavement-area wording), implemented, unit-tested, and self-verified live in a headless browser this session by actually typing into the real dialog (48/48 checks, including the exact "type 2 then 5" repro).**
- Verify: sandbox — pure client-side dialog/input logic (no GIS, no concurrency, no signed-in-only surface, no real-project-data repro needed); self-verified live in a headless browser this session per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK, driving real Playwright keystrokes rather than reasoning about the handler, per the owner's own explicit instruction.
- **(1) THE RULE, applied: A PREFIX OF A VALID NUMBER IS NOT AN ERROR — validate on blur/Enter/commit, never on keystroke.** The band-width field is now `BandWidthInput` (`RoadCrossSectionDialog.jsx`), a local draft/commit input mirroring `SitePlanner.jsx`'s established `NumInput` contract: a local `draft` string the user types into, `onChange` only ever updates that draft, and `bands` (the committed model the preview/totals read) is written ONLY on blur or Enter. No error styling of any kind is shown on this field — an unparseable draft at commit silently reverts to the last committed value, and a below-minimum one is silently clamped up, never blocking or flagging a keystroke. `type="text"` + `inputMode="decimal"` (not native `type="number"`), matching the codebase's established safe-numeric-input idiom.
- **(2) EVERY NAMED ADJACENT CASE, handled and individually named in a test — none paints red or disturbs the preview mid-type.** `parseWidthDraft` (new, pure, `lib/roadCrossSection.js`) is the commit-time-only parser: returns `null` (never an error, never committed) for an empty field, a lone ".", "0" on the way to "0.5", a trailing "12." on the way to "12.5", and a moment of pasted-odd text — and returns the real number for a leading zero like "08" (a legitimate way of having typed "8") and for "12." itself (`Number("12.")` is unambiguously 12, so committing right there takes that plain reading rather than reverting). `MIN_BAND_WIDTH_FT` (0.1, matching the field's pre-existing floor) is applied only at commit via `Math.max(MIN_BAND_WIDTH_FT, n)` — never mid-type.
- **(3) THE PREVIEW HOLDS COMMITTED GEOMETRY, as a byproduct of (1), not a separate mechanism.** `XSectionPreview` reads straight from the `bands` state, which the draft/commit split now only ever updates on a real commit — so mid-edit, the preview and every derived total (Section width, Total ROW width, Pavement area) provably hold the LAST COMMITTED geometry, verified live by typing "2" then "5" and asserting the dialog body text is byte-identical to the pre-edit baseline until blur.
- **(4) THE PREVIEW'S OWN "giant numeral in an empty box" bug, fixed at the actual root — a viewBox/CSS-size mismatch, not narrowness itself.** The old preview derived its SVG `viewBox` height from content (`h = rowW * scale`) while separately clamping the CSS *display* height into `[60, 280]`, so a narrow section's tiny viewBox got stretched by the browser to fill a much taller box — every fixed-unit font size (labels, the total) stretched right along with it. **First fix attempt (an `aspectRatio` CSS trick with `width: 100%`) was tried, MEASURED, and REJECTED**: it reproduced the same class of blow-up, just driven by the dialog's own wide container instead of by `rowW` (glyphs measured 3–4x their authored size). The shipped fix renders the SVG at its own FIXED pixel size — `width={CONTENT_W} height={PREVIEW_H}`, exactly matching its `viewBox`, so 1 authored unit is always exactly 1 real CSS px whenever the dialog has room for it (which it always does, `min(720px, 100%)` wide) — and only ever SHRINKS, never grows, via `maxWidth: 100%` + `height: auto` on a narrower viewport. The per-foot scale is capped at a legibility ceiling and otherwise sized to exactly fill the fixed height, so content height never exceeds the box — a narrow section renders a shorter, vertically-centered band stack instead of an oversized one. Measured live: a 2′ single-band section's own label glyph now renders at 11px (was reading as an "enormous numeral" before the fix); a normal 24′ section's glyph renders at 13px — consistent, not disproportionate.

Verified live, each with the label's own bounding box measured against the SVG's: the single-band default (24′), a genuinely narrow section (2′), and the owner's own 12/12/20-median/12/12 boulevard (68′) all render the label horizontal, fully unclipped, reading the whole word ("68′ total", never "tot").
- **(6) "Pavement area … per 100 ft of road" — judged genuinely ambiguous, not left alone.** The qualifier used to sit BEFORE the number as a parenthetical ("Pavement area (per 100′) 200 SF · 22.2 SY"), easily skimmed past and misreadable as the road's real total area. Moved to directly follow the number and spelled out as a rate ("Pavement area 200 SF · 22.2 SY per 100 ft of road") — reads unambiguously as a unit on the figure itself. (The owner's brief allowed "if it already is [clear], say so and change nothing" — this is the case for changing it, stated rather than silently done.)

- **THE EXISTING MODEL, as measured (a full Explore-agent audit of `SitePlanner.jsx` + every `lib/road*.js` file), and what this extends rather than parallels:** `travelW` (pavement, curb-face-to-curb-face) drives `roadStripRing`/`roadCurbLines` (via `bufferPolyline`/`offsetPolyline`) → the dissolved-network junction math (`roadNetwork.js`) → the impervious-area rollup (`roadStripArea`, in SF) and the paving-cost rollup (`costTakeoff.js`'s `roadQuantities`/`costRollup`, in SY — a SEPARATE derivation from the SF figure, both keyed off the same width). `curb` is the fixed 6″ curb auto-added outside `travelW`. `curbType`/`curbedSides`/`panWidth`/`"Barrier curb"` are COST-ONLY vocabulary (`costTakeoff.js`'s `CURB_TYPE_META`) with no geometric effect on the drawn curb line. `driveTee`/`tee` are junction curb-return params at a road→drive/road→road connection, untouched by this work. `pavingSy` is a cost-rollup figure only, never read by impervious/stormwater math (that reads `roadStripArea` independently, in SF).
- **THE DESIGN, chosen to make `travelW` a DERIVED mirror rather than adding a parallel width concept:** `el.xsection = { bands: [{type, w}, …] }` (new, optional, additive field — `lib/roadCrossSection.js`). Every band type carries `withinCurb` (contributes to the curb-to-curb total — a grass median counts, since curbs bound the whole divided section, not just the asphalt) and `paved` (contributes to the ASPHALT total the cost rollup should price — a median does NOT count, same idea as the existing curb-and-gutter pan trim in `costTakeoff.js`, generalized). `curbToCurbWidth(xsection)` is written back onto `el.travelW` every time the section is edited (`setRoadXSection`), so `roadStripRing`/`roadCurbLines`/the dissolved network/`roadStripArea` all keep reading `el.travelW` completely unchanged — **zero edits needed to any of that machinery.** `pavedWidth(xsection)` feeds a new `roadPavedWidth(el)` that the cost rollup call sites now use instead of the raw `travelW`, so a median's footage is correctly excluded from priced asphalt. `hasXSection(el)` (in the pure lib, not a component-local helper — `renderElPx` is a MODULE-LEVEL function outside the planner component's closure and needs the same predicate) is the one gate every consumer shares.
- **BAND TYPES (the brief's stated minimum, all ten):** travel lane, median, centre turn lane, shoulder, curb-and-gutter, parking lane, bike lane, sidewalk, parkway/landscape strip, ditch/swale — `BAND_TYPES` in `lib/roadCrossSection.js`.

- **CANVAS RENDERING — distinct fills for pavement/median/shoulder, lane striping, collapses to a plain strip when sub-pixel.** Inside `renderElPx`'s existing centerline-road branch, gated on `hasXSection(el)`: band boundaries are computed as offsets from the centerline (`bandLayout`, same sign convention `roadCurbLines` already uses for ±travelW/2) and drawn as `offsetPolyline` strips for the WITHIN-CURB bands only (median/shoulder/curb-and-gutter/parking/bike get a distinct theme-token fill — `var(--success-text)` for median, etc., the same "borrow a named token for a schematic" idiom `PondSection.jsx` already uses; travel/turn-lane bands stay plain asphalt, cued by striping instead). Lane markings (`bandStripeMarks` — a deliberately SIMPLIFIED striping convention, not a MUTCD plan: solid yellow either side of a median/turn lane, dashed white between same-direction travel lanes, double yellow at the one true-centerline seam of a fully undivided road, solid white at a shoulder/parking/bike edge) are drawn the same way. The whole decoration group is clipped to THIS road's own pavement ring via an inline SVG `<clipPath>` (the exact idiom already used for the overlay-crop feature, `SitePlanner.jsx:16826`), so it can never spill past the drawn pavement even at a junction — a lighter-weight substitute for the precise per-neighbour stripe trim the outer curb lines get, stated as a known approximation rather than hidden (median-openings-AT-junctions is B773729's job). Root cause: `entry.destructive` (Delete's flag, added so a destructive refusal explains itself on every press rather than once per episode, B742368-era work) forced a hint on every keystroke that cleared a selected building's field, because "selected building + destructive key + refused" is true of every digit anyone clears before typing a new one. The CHROME message ("panel owns the keyboard, click the plan, then press Delete") keeps its remedy — there it is correct, since that state exists precisely so a user can click the plan and delete a still-selected object.

Extending the harness (parcelSelect: false in its fixture, so a press on the seeded parcel's boundary fires the real `parcel-select-hint` toast — every bottom-centre toast on this surface shares one `toastPill` object, so proving this one proves them all) found the toast overlapping the scale bar and the calibration badge at every narrow width tested — **287px² / 986px² at 750px, up to 4354px² / 3790px² at 420px.** Fixed by deriving `toastPill`'s `bottom` from the SAME `canvasPillBottom(...)` helper the Standards "Applied · Undo" toast already uses, so it clears the identical furniture set. **One structural wrinkle, not a functional one:** `canvasPillBottom` needs `furnPlates`/`FURNITURE_ROW`/`calibPlace`, all computed well after `toastPill`'s original declaration point — moving that computation to a top-level `const` there collided with `hiddenContentReads.js`'s sweep (a line-span heuristic that attributes the entire render body to "the last top-level const before the JSX `return`", which was `calibPlace`; inserting a new one after it silently stole that attribution and made both `calibPlace` stale and the new name UNDECLARED). ### B755808 — Site Planner toolbar reads as three unrelated control systems `[Site Planner / ui]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(owner's words: "this is horrendous UI." The three controls at the top right of the Site tab — File-with-caret, the undo/redo pair, and the fullscreen glyph — each used a different container language, a different optical weight and a different icon family. Measured live from the DOM: File = 0.93px solid rgb(215,221,229) outline, 3px radius, 29px tall; undo/redo = a filled grey slab with transparent per-button borders, 8px radius, 30px tall; fullscreen (Zoom to fit) = no container at all. Minted **B755808 / V421632** from this branch's reserved block B755808–B654255 / V421632–V332559 against `origin/main` 540ef8f. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done (grep + `BACKLOG_OPEN.md`) for `toolbar`, `File-with-caret`, `undo/redo`, `fullscreen glyph`, `chrome language`, `grey slab`, `container treatment`: no prior item covers the container/system defect (B632176 is an unrelated Food-module clipping bug; B7379/B7776 are older toolbar layout notes, already resolved, that never named this defect). Net-new. Scope note (given with the report): B1148 already rebuilt the ICONS — undo/redo are the standard curved-arrow MDI pair, Zoom-to-fit is the four-corner "fit" glyph, Layers is stacked sheets — and this item does not touch them, only the CONTAINERS and the SYSTEM around them.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — implemented and self-verified live in a headless browser this session (9/9 checks passed); Verify: live per LIVE-VERIFY (zoom-/data-density-dependent rendering is the nearest named class for pixel-level chrome, and the task explicitly called for a live verify), closed the same session per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK (a logged-out, no-GIS UI check is Claude-doable and must not be parked).**
- Verify: live — **V421632**, PASSED this session (see `VERIFICATION-DONE.md`).
- **ROOT CAUSE, confirmed in the code (AUDIT-FIRST), not assumed.** The bar's three groups were built at three different times by three different passes and never reconciled onto one shared style: File's button hardcoded its own `borderRadius: 3` (a one-off, from the earlier B727504 "give File a border" pass) while `dGhost` — the shared ghost-button style every other chrome button on this bar already used — carries `borderRadius: 8`; the Undo/Redo pair was wrapped in its own `<div style={{ background: "var(--hover-chrome)", borderRadius: 10, padding: 2 }}>` (a filled pill, unique to that one group); Zoom-to-fit had no wrapper styling at all. `var(--hover-chrome)` is the same token a *hover* state washes any chrome button with, and it sits close enough to the disabled-icon fade (`.tb-icon-btn:disabled { opacity: .38 }`, dimming the SAME `fill="currentColor"` glyph) that a disabled Undo/Redo pair read as one indistinct grey smear rather than two clearly-off controls — exactly defect (2) in the report. The icon SHAPES themselves (`components/icons.jsx`) were already consistent — all four (`UndoIcon`/`RedoIcon`/`ZoomFitIcon`/`LayersIcon`) are `fill="currentColor"` MDI paths from the B727504 pass — so the "heaviest blackest strokes on fullscreen, faintest on undo/redo" read was the CONTAINERS (grey-on-grey pill vs. bare glyph on transparent chrome), not the glyphs; no icon path was touched, per the report's explicit scope note.
- **THE FIX — one chrome system, defined once and applied to all three groups, not one control nudged.** Two new shared constants, `TB_H = dIcon.height` (30) and `TB_R = dGhost.borderRadius` (8) — deliberately reusing the values the icon buttons and the app's default ghost button ALREADY used, rather than inventing new numbers, so the fix is "make File match the app's existing standard," not "invent a fourth number everyone must now match." **(1) File** now sets `height: TB_H, borderRadius: TB_R` instead of its one-off 3px radius / implicit ~29px height, so it sits on the exact same height/radius grid as the icon buttons. **(2)** The Undo/Redo group's filled-pill wrapper (`background`/`borderRadius: 10`/`padding: 2`) is removed entirely — the pair now renders bare, exactly like the Zoom-to-fit button beside it, with no container to ever carry a disabled-adjacent color; grouping is by the bar's existing `vSep` 1px divider only (File | History | View), never a filled tray. **(3)** Optical weight and icon-family consistency fall out of (1)+(2) for free — once all three groups share the same bare/icon-button treatment on the same transparent chrome background, the icons (already identical MDI stroke weight from B1148) read at the same weight; no glyph was redrawn. **(4)** Height/radius/baseline are now identical by construction (30px / 8px / one shared vertical center — proven ±2px in the live check below). **(5)** Icon families — untouched, per the scope note; already correct. **(6)** File's caret is de-emphasized to match the muted-token convention every other disclosure caret in this app already uses (`railHint`'s `PAL.chromeMuted`, the plan-caret at the breadcrumb) — `fontSize: 9` + full ink color → `fontSize: 10.5` + `color: PAL.chromeMuted`, plus the flex `gap` between "File" and the caret widened from 5 to 6 for real spacing — rather than a solid full-weight triangle jammed against the word. ### B763472 — Schedule row drag: killed the middle "reparent" band, unified before/after depth resolution, and fixed the grip↔ID-number spacing `[Scheduler]` (bug) #scheduler #ui  *(owner report, #1107 live regression 4 days after ship, verbatim: "moving tasks up and down on the schedule is kinda finicky... I tried to move a task above another task, and it somehow put it as a subtask for the task that it was hovering above." Owner refined the fix across the session: first "kill the middle band, two outcomes only"; then the depth rule "match the row above, but never shallower than the row below"; then "drop the drag grip/number spacing" and "there should be a visual so I actually know I'm moving something" — all three folded into one PR per his instruction.)*
`[x]` **Measured, fixed, and re-measured — band geometry, depth resolution, grip spacing, and drag visual feedback.**
- Verify: sandbox — extensive REAL-mouse-driven headless Chromium testing (never synthetic dispatchEvent), at his exact row height (20px) and the slider max (34px), against a fixture shaped like his reported scenario. 46/46 checks pass, including a mutation battery proving every new guard is discriminating (not just green). No auth/GIS dependency for this module (standalone JSON import/export), so this is fully Claude-doable per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK, not deferred.
- **STEP 1 — BAND TABLE (measured, not assumed).** OLD (#1107, three-band): before/after each 30% of ROW_H, reparent ("into") the middle 40%. At his 20px rows: before/after = 6.0px each, into = 8.0px — the riskier outcome was the BIGGER target. NEW (this fix): before/after 50%/50%, no into band, at every row height 20–34.
- **STEP 2 — PIXEL SWEEP, real drags, every 1px, both row heights, OLD source (pinned at pre-fix commit `0903bc8`) vs NEW.** OLD@20px: into=7px, before=7px, after=6px (into ≥ either individual band, confirming the reported bug quantitatively). NEW@20px and NEW@34px: **zero** "into" outcomes across the full sweep — a drag can no longer reparent by vertical position alone.
- **THE FIX, three parts, all in `public/sequence/index.html` (`GridView`'s `startRowDrag`):**
  1. **Two outcomes only.** `computeAndPaint`'s frac split is now `<0.5`/`>=0.5` (before/after), no middle band. Making a task a subtask is what indent (Shift+Alt+Right / right-click menu) is for; drag no longer overlaps that job.
  2. **Depth rule, unified.** New `resolveDropParent(gapIndex)` resolves depth from the GAP (the pair of rows bounding the drop point), not from whichever half of whichever row the cursor happened to be over — the old code derived depth from "before" and "after" independently and could disagree with itself on the exact same gap, which is the actual mechanism behind "drop above X reparents into X." Rule: match the row above, clamped to never be shallower than the row below (the row below can only be deeper if it's the row above's own first child — a flattened depth-first walk steps at most one level deeper — so landing any shallower would silently ADOPT that child into the dropped row's new subtree). Verified via **child-count-before/after** on every affected parent at all 5 owner-named insertion points (expanded-parent→first-child, last-child→next-section, below a collapsed group, above the first row, below the last row of the whole schedule) — zero silent adoption in every case.
  3. **Real bug the pixel sweep caught mid-implementation:** the dragged row(s) are still physically present in `tasks` at their old array position during the drag (only dimmed, never removed, per the zero-DOM-churn design) — so a gap immediately beside the drag's OWN start could resolve "the row above/below" to the dragged row itself, and `moveSelectionToDestination` silently fell back to "end of the list" when asked to insert after a row it had just excluded. Fixed by skipping the blocked/dragged set when finding the true row above/below.
- **VISUAL FEEDBACK (owner, verbatim: "there should be a visual so that I actually know that I'm moving something... professionally done").** Audited what existed: a plain 2px full-width insertion line + (pre-fix) a same-color outline on the "into" target — no depth cue at all. Now: the insertion line is **depth-aware** — it starts at the exact x-offset the dropped row's own name text would start at (same `4+level*14` formula the name column itself uses), so a sibling-level drop and a nested drop are visibly different lines, not the same line at two heights; a small leading dot for legibility at 20px rows; the dragged row(s) get a dashed "in-flight" outline in addition to the existing dim. Pre-existing and left unchanged: grip visible before press (`.rowgrip` opacity), grabbing cursor during drag, edge auto-scroll. Confirmed (not just assumed) that auto-scroll doesn't fight the #1101/B463922 scroll-anchor effect — that effect is keyed on the `tasks` array reference, which never changes mid-drag (zero re-renders), so there's no concurrent write; measured post-drop scroll state is sane (check I2). Screenshots at his 20px row height (at-rest grip, mid-drag sibling-depth line, mid-drag nested-depth line) sent with the PR.
- **GRIP↔ID-NUMBER SPACING (owner, verbatim: "not a ton more space, but... enough that it makes sense").** Was `paddingLeft:4` on a number sitting directly under an 8px-wide grip strip — touching. Now `paddingLeft:12` (clears the grip + a small gap). Measured: gap 0→4px; ID cell still exactly 30px (the gap came from padding, not a widened cell); a REAL 3-digit id (his actual row numbers — built a 121-task fixture since ids auto-renumber to sequential 1..N on every load) is NOT truncated at either row-height extreme. A 4-digit id is PROJECTED (font-metric calculation, not yet DOM-verifiable — no project has 1000+ tasks) to need ~9px more column width; flagged, not silently clipped, not a regression against anything that worked before. Grip's own hit area untouched (still exactly 8px, pointer-events always on, opacity hover-gated only) — re-verified row-range select still works (badge + selected-cell background color), the exact thing an earlier version of this grip broke.
- **ADJACENT CASES, all measured:** dropping above the first row (top-level) · below the last row of the whole schedule (lands at that row's own depth — accepted consequence, outdent unchanged) · onto a collapsed group header (beside it, never inside, never force-expanded) · a parent-with-children dropped near another parent-with-children (subtrees stay separate) · a multi-row selection (moves as one block) · dropping onto the row directly adjacent to the source (the smallest possible move, and the one he described doing) · a genuine no-op drop (pushes no spurious undo entry — one Ctrl+Z after it lands on the exact same state as one Ctrl+Z with no drag at all).
- **UNDO:** one Ctrl+Z fully reverts a depth-changing drop, confirmed.
- Files: `public/sequence/index.html` (drag logic + visual feedback + grip spacing); `ui-audit/verify-schedule-row-move.mjs` (extended, not duplicated — band table, pixel sweep, depth-resolution measurement, grip-spacing checks, screenshots, mutation battery, all folded into the existing NEW-ROWMOVE harness).

DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `toastPill`, `flashWarn`, `overlapWarn`, `success-green`, `#15803d`, `#7f1d1d`: no prior item. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — the shared-styling claim was confirmed in code (not assumed), the color rule itself had a real bug fixed alongside it, and ~24 blocking-refusal call sites now carry the error color; findings from the audit are reported below.**
- Verify: sandbox — pure client-side rendering logic; self-verified live in this session's headless run (the color of both a refusal toast and a completed-action toast was read via `getComputedStyle`, not assumed).
- **CONFIRMED IN CODE FIRST, per the owner's own caveat.** The one bottom-center toast pill every `flashWarn(...)` call renders through (`SitePlanner.jsx`, near `toastPill`) picks its background from the message TEXT: `overlapWarn.startsWith("⚠") ? "#7f1d1d" (red) : "#15803d" (green, default)`. A call site that refuses a requested action but doesn't happen to prepend `⚠` therefore renders in the SAME green as a genuine success toast, or as the "● Scaled · county GIS" affirmative status chip the owner compared it to (a different component, `rgba(22,101,52,0.92)` — visually the same family of green, confirming the READING even though it's a separate element). This is exactly the shape B742368's own old refusal was in before this item's fix.
- **A SECOND, independent bug in the color rule itself, found while confirming the first.** `.startsWith("⚠")` misses any message that EMBEDS a warning mid-string rather than leading with it — e.g. `"All 3 deeds placed.${bad.length ? " ⚠ Verify: …" : ""}"` — which never starts with `⚠` even when it does carry one, so it also rendered green. Changed to `.includes("⚠")`, which catches both without touching any call site's wording.
- **THE AUDIT — every one of the 130+ `flashWarn(...)` call sites in `SitePlanner.jsx` was read and classified as a genuine blocking refusal/failure (needs `⚠`), a completed action (correctly green, left alone), or a neutral in-flight mode prompt ("Click the far side of the ditch.", left alone — not this report's shape).** ~24 of the clearest, highest-traffic refusals now carry the `⚠` prefix: both `place.mode === "refuse"` (LOUD-FAILURE) sites, the reshape self-intersection revert (B742369), footprint dock-wall-corner guards, "Couldn't delete/copy/duplicate/re-render/reach the hydrant source/sample 3DEP/form a shape/build that easement" failures, "No parcel/county-parcel/building/bearings…" and "Select a pond/plotted deed boundary first" preconditions, "That's already gone", "That drawing is locked", "This tab is read-only", pond-sizing refusals including the one that already says "refusing" outright, and the lock-toggle failure messages. **What was deliberately left green:** every message reporting a COMPLETED action even with a caveat (e.g. "Aligned…", "Pasted…", "Rotated the deed… ⚠ the fit is loose" — the embedded `⚠` there now correctly reddens it via the `.includes` fix, without touching its wording), and neutral step-by-step mode instructions during an armed multi-click flow (those aren't refusals and aren't this report's shape).
- **What was NOT touched, named rather than left silent.** A further ~80–100 lower-traffic `flashWarn` sites were read and judged either already-correct (a completed action) or genuinely borderline ("Already at the front/back", "Nothing to reorder…" — a no-op status rather than a stopped user action) and were left as-is rather than mechanically prefixed; a full char-by-char relabeling of every remaining site was judged disproportionate to this report's shape (a green refusal reading as success) versus the size of the file, and is not filed as a separate item since nothing here rises to a blocking, misleading-as-success defect on the scale of what was fixed.
- **LIVE VERIFICATION, this session (`ui-audit/verify-b872-round2.mjs`).** B742368's now-completed "Cleared 4 corner bump-outs… entered reshape mode" toast reads `rgb(21,128,61)` (the success green — correct, it's a completed action, not a refusal) and B742369's mid-drag `"⚠ Reshape held…"` toast reads `rgb(127,29,29)` (the error color) — the two are now visually distinguishable exactly as the report asked, read via `getComputedStyle` on the real rendered pill, not assumed from source.
- **TESTS.** No pure library changed (this is component-local rendering + message-string edits); full unit suite unaffected (12500/12503 passing, 2 pre-existing unrelated shallow-clone failures — see B742369). Lint 0 new errors. Build green.

### B742372 — Shift-clicking an end wall to add a footprint control point shifted the reported area by 1 SF with zero drag `[Site Planner / footprintEdit]` (bug) #site-planner #geometry  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25, "NEW-5" — same production drive as B742368. Verbatim: footprint edit mode → shift-click an end wall to add a control point → drag nothing → label goes 417,600 SF to 417,601 SF; expected: inserting a vertex on an existing edge is geometrically a no-op and must not move the reported area — "snap the inserted point exactly onto the segment, or round the displayed area consistently, so the number does not change without a user action." Minted **B742372** from this branch's reserved block against `origin/main` a618d07. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `insertVtx`, `control point`, `snapPt`, `shift-click`, `projectOntoLine`: `projectOntoLine` (footprintEdit.js) is a DIFFERENT thing — an INFINITE-line projection for a dock-wall corner sliding along its wall; this is a FINITE-segment projection for a freshly inserted vertex. No prior item. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — root-caused, fixed with a new shared pure helper, and unit-tested with the exact reported repro shape (an angled edge, not just an axis-aligned one).**
- Verify: sandbox — pure geometry, no LIVE-VERIFY class applies (not GIS, not concurrency, not zoom/timing-dependent rendering, not export parity, and the repro needs no real project data — the bug reproduces on any angled edge with any snap setting). A live click-through would add confidence but not proof beyond what the unit tests already establish byte-exactly; not driven live this session (see note below).
- **ROOT CAUSE.** `insertVtx`'s shared control-point inserter (used by every editable layer — parcel/el/measure/ease/markup, Shift-click AND the right-click "Add control point" menu) computed the click's already-on-the-edge point (`edge.pt` from the pure hit-test, exact), then called `snapPt()` on it — which rounds `x` and `y` INDEPENDENTLY (to the grid, or to 0.01 ft with snap off). Rounding two coordinates separately moves a point off whatever line it was on unless that line happens to be grid-aligned — invisible on an axis-aligned wall, a small kink (and therefore a small polygon-area change) on an angled one, which an end wall on a reshaped building often is.
- **THE FIX.** A new pure `projectOntoSegment(a, b, p)` in the shared `lib/ringMath.js` (a leaf module, imports nothing) — the closest point on the FINITE segment between the two flanking (unmoved) ring vertices, clamped to the segment. `insertVtx` now re-projects the snapped point through it before splicing, using the segment's ACTUAL current neighbors from whichever array is being edited — so the insert always lands exactly on the line regardless of what snapping did to it. Distinct on purpose from `footprintEdit.js`'s existing `projectOntoLine` (an INFINITE-line projection, for a dock corner that is meant to slide arbitrarily far along its wall) — a freshly inserted control point must never land outside its two neighbors, which only a finite-segment projection guarantees.
- **TESTS.** New `test/ringMath.test.js` (8) — `projectOntoSegment`: identity when already on the segment, snapping an off-line point back onto an AXIS-ALIGNED edge, the exact repro shape on an ANGLED edge (proven via collinearity, not just "close enough"), clamping at both endpoints (never extrapolates past them), the degenerate zero-length-segment case, and the reported invariant itself — inserting a control point at a naively-snapped, slightly-off-line position leaves a ring's shoelace area EXACTLY unchanged (`toBeCloseTo(before, 9)`), the same numeric shape as 417,600 → 417,601. `test/footprintEdit.test.js` (23, pre-existing, unchanged/green).
- **Why no live click-through.** The exact numeric repro (angled-edge collinearity + before/after area equality to 9 decimal places) is fully captured by the unit tests above; this session's live time went to B742369's per-frame drag guard, which is the item where a live check adds evidence a unit test cannot (a race/timing shape). If a future session wants belt-and-suspenders, the right-click "＋ Add control point" menu item (`vtxMenu`) is the lower-effort live path — it doesn't need pixel-perfect Shift-click positioning the way the raw gesture does.
- **Housekeeping.** `MAP.md` regenerated (`node scripts/build-map.mjs`) for the new `ringMath.js` export — `test/mapDrift.test.js` was red before this and is green after.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/ringMath.js`, `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx`, `test/ringMath.test.js` (new), `MAP.md`.
- Base: `origin/main` @ `a618d07`.

- Origin: owner chat block, 2026-08-25 (amendment to the same-day filing above, explicitly moved in scope this session).
- **ROOT CAUSE, confirmed against the real code and the real rows, not reasoned in the abstract.** `pushHistory()` (`SitePlanner.jsx`) is the ONLY call in this codebase that opens an operation (`opTrackerRef.current.beginOperation`, `operationEnvelope.js`) — it is called from ~190 sites and covers every interactive drawing/editing gesture (parcel split, parcel merge, deed promotion, JSON import, version restore, clipboard paste, Standards-apply all correctly call it — verified one by one, not assumed). `envelopeNow()` (read at ENQUEUE time inside `elementSync.js`'s diff) falls back to `"unknown"` whenever nothing is open. The gap is never "the duplicate flow" specifically — it is any code path that changes the canvas's collections OUTSIDE a `pushHistory()`-covered gesture, because that state change still feeds the SAME autosave-diff effect every real edit does. `duplicatePlan`/`newPlanSameParcel`/`newSiteFromMap` (`SitePlannerApp.jsx`) only call `saveSite()`, which (per `cloudSync.js`'s `slimForCloud`) writes the `sites` metadata row and STRIPS every element collection — the parcels/elements they carry forward never touch `site_elements` until the plan is opened and `SitePlanner.jsx`'s `refetchReplace` seeds it from zero (or partial) server rows. THAT reconcile call is the one true funnel every never-synced-local-content path shares (duplicate, same-parcel, new-site-from-map, and a migrated legacy site alike) — confirmed by pulling the 7 "impossible" rows directly: they are HCAD-attributed parcels + a road carried forward by an earlier `newPlanSameParcel`/multi-parcel site seed, not a duplicate at all.
- **THE FULL AUDIT — every write path that can create a `site_elements` row, and which ones open an operation:**
  - Plan duplicate / new plan (same parcel) / new site from map / migrated legacy site (`SitePlannerApp.jsx`, `storage.js`) — write only the `sites` row; the actual `site_elements` seed happens in `refetchReplace` on first mount — **GAP, fixed**.
  - "Take over editing here" (`takeOverEditing`) — a cross-device/cross-session union-merge reconcile with no gesture and no operation open — **GAP, fixed**.
  - Undo / redo (`applySnapshot` via `undo()`/`redo()`) — `endOperation()` is never called anywhere, so an undo/redo rode whichever operation was last begun (often the very edit it reverts) instead of its own — never literally `"unknown"` (some operation is always open by the time anything is undoable) but a real misattribution — **fixed**.
  - The Standards-apply toast's own "Undo" button (`applyAllStd`) — a direct state revert with no fresh operation, and not on the Ctrl+Z stack at all — **fixed**.
  - Parcel split (`performSplit`), parcel merge/combine (`mergeParcels`), deed promotion to parcel (`promoteDeedToParcel`), JSON site import (`importJSONFile`), version-history restore (`restoreVersion`), same-plan and cross-plan clipboard paste — all already call `pushHistory()`/`ctx.pushHistory()` — **already covered, no gap** (split/merge use the generic `"edit"` kind rather than `"split"`/`"merge"` specifically; a labeling-quality gap the vocabulary's own header already calls deliberately-deferred future work, not an `"unknown"` bug).
  - Cross-tab local convergence (the `storage` event handler) — fires only when `!isCloudActive()`, at which point no element-sync engine exists to write through — **not a gap** for this bug.
  - Overlay import (DXF/PDF/DWG) — never touches `els`/`parcels`/etc. at all — **not a `site_elements` write path**.
  - Template / library placement — **no such feature exists** in this codebase.
- **THE FIX**, all in `SitePlanner.jsx`: `refetchReplace`'s seed reconcile and `takeOverEditing`'s union-merge state set now call `opTrackerRef.current.beginOperation("create")` before touching state; `undo`/`redo` and the Standards-toast "Undo" each mint their own fresh operation instead of inheriting whatever was last begun.
- **CI GUARD, so this cannot silently regrow:** `test/opEnvelopeSeedCoverage.test.js` (new) — a behavioral proof of the `beginOperation`/`envelopeNow` contract, a source-guard/wiring test for each of the four fixed call sites (mutation-proven: reverting any one of the four fixes turns its guard red), and a pinned count of the total `.reconcile(` call sites in `SitePlanner.jsx` (currently exactly 2) so a THIRD, unaudited one cannot appear without a human extending this guard.
- **NOT BACKFILLED, deliberately:** the 3,324 legacy `op_kind: null` rows across 67 plans (first seen 2026-06-19, before B712225 shipped the envelope columns at all) pre-date this mechanism entirely and are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE — they describe writes from before the envelope existed, not a defect in it. Left alone; nobody should chase them.
- Sandbox evidence: `npx vitest run test/opEnvelopeSeedCoverage.test.js test/operationEnvelope.test.js` — 30/30 green; full-repo `npx vitest run` — 606/608 files, 12516/12518 tests, the same 2 pre-existing unrelated shallow-clone failures (`docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js`/`hiddenContentReads.test.js`, both `git show <hash>` against a commit outside this environment's shallow clone depth) present before this change. `npm run build` green. `node scripts/build-map.mjs --check` clean (no exported-symbol change). `npm run check-mint` clean (amendment — no new id minted).
