- Verify: live — two-tab timing/concurrency, the LIVE-VERIFY class this item names itself. CLOSED.
- Origin: owner chat block, 2026-08-23. Implemented and shipped this session (STANDING RULE #1).
- **Recurrence 1 (2026-08-24, round 2 → REVERTED as PR #1142):** round 1 (below, mechanism kept — it was real) did not close the bug. Live re-test on the deployed build (a fresh throwaway, `smt6igj8ppr4`) showed the blast radius GREW to 12 of 14 members, all under the DELETING tab's own delete-operation envelope. Diagnosed (correctly, as far as it went) as `batchSpansAssembly`'s atomicity gate never triggering for delete cascades (`rootIdOf(cur, e.id)` falls back to the op's own id when `cur` is null, which it always is for a delete) — fixed via an `opRoot` helper reading the shadow instead. **This shipped as PR #1142 and made things WORSE, live, on the owner's very next test**, with tab B completely IDLE: the delete became a near-total silent no-op (12 of 13 members never died at all; the building stayed fully drawn in both tabs and survived a reload). **REVERTED same-session as PR #1143** the moment this was reported — the owner independently confirmed the revert live before this round's fix was written. The atomicity work itself was not wrong on its own terms; it simply was not the mechanism, and restoring it is now correctly sequenced to land AFTER this round's fix (see the note under "what round 2 leaves for later" below).
- **Recurrence 2 (2026-08-24, same day, POST-REVERT — i.e., round 1's fix ALONE, no round-2 code involved):** the owner re-ran the live two-tab check against the reverted (round-1-only) build and found the SAME resurrection, worse than the original report: **ALL 13 bonded children** came back alive ~0.56s after the host's tombstone, every one under a DIFFERENT op_id carrying `op_kind: "unknown"` (no operation tracker window open at all), and — contradicting an earlier, unverified claim of this item's own — the residue did **NOT** self-heal on a reload of the deleting tab; it was measured as still alive and still painted after a full reload. **The self-heal claim is retracted here; do not rely on it.** This is round 1's own fix caught failing on a case it was never built to cover (see "what round 1 actually fixed, and what it does not reach" below) — round 1 remains real and is kept, but it closes only ONE of several stale-canvas windows, and production evidence shows the OTHERS fire routinely.
- **WHAT ROUND 1 ACTUALLY FIXED, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH.** `reconcileElems`'s stale-`stateRef.current`-after-`drainRemote()` race is real and stays fixed — but it only closes the case where a tombstone's canvas removal was BUFFERED (`busyRef.current` true: a gesture, even an incidental pan, in flight on the OBSERVING tab). The owner's actual round-2/round-3 repro runs had tab B **completely idle** — no gesture, nothing ever entered `pendingRemoteRef`, so round 1's fold is a no-op with nothing to fold. A `!shad`-shaped stale read reaches `elementSync.reconcile()` from AT LEAST three other doors round 1 cannot touch: **(a)** a plain React state-update lag between the realtime handler's direct (unbuffered) `applyRemoteInstr` call and `stateRef.current` catching up before the next scheduled diff; **(b)** the canvas seam's own heal-pass write (`assemblyGuard`'s `setEls(guarded)` at the "canvas" `useEffect`) — a PLAIN-VALUE `setState` dispatched in the same React batch as a realtime tombstone's FUNCTIONAL `setEls(fn)` removal, which React's `basicStateReducer` treats as a REPLACEMENT of whatever state exists at apply time, silently discarding the removal (confirmed reproducible on a TORN plan specifically — the production fixture plans in this repo's live check carry an un-persisted tear, so this seam fires continuously during the tombstone burst); **(c)** `refetchReplace`'s `sub()` fold, which re-appends any dirty non-delete entry `model.els` lacks even after `seed()` has dropped the row's tombstone from the shadow. All three converge on the SAME missing invariant round 3 (below) closes directly, which is why patching call sites kept failing.
- **THE ROUND-3 ROOT CAUSE, confirmed against PRODUCTION TELEMETRY (a separate `client_errors` capture on `smt6imo0gda0`, not merely reasoned from source) via a dedicated Opus investigation this session, then independently verified against the current source line-by-line before any fix was written.** `elementSync.js`'s `shadow` Map holds LIVE rows only; its absence means two DIFFERENT things the diff engine could not tell apart — "the server has never seen this element" and "the server holds this element as a TOMBSTONE, and the canvas has not caught up yet" — and `reconcile()`'s `!shad` branch (the "brand-new element → create" path) unconditionally assumed the FIRST. `create` is the one op class with no rev guard, and the server (`site_elements.sql`) deliberately AUTO-RESTORES a create over a same-kind tombstone (continues the rev rather than rejecting it) — a documented, correct behavior for a genuine "delete, then undo" (the comment already sitting beside the old code said so). So ANY stale-canvas window — not just the one round 1 fixed — turns a completed delete into a resurrection, minted with no operation envelope open (matching the owner's `op_kind:"unknown"` observation exactly).
- **THE FIX.** A never-pruned "delete floor" (`maxDeleteRev`, which already existed for a DIFFERENT purpose — the B812/round-4 refetch-resurrect guard — and was only ever populated for THIS tab's own deletes) is now recorded on EVERY tombstone this engine learns of: a foreign delete via `applyRemoteRow` (previously `shadow.delete(key)` with nothing recorded), and a tombstoned row read back from `seed()` (previously silently skipped). `reconcile()`'s `!shad` branch now REFUSES to mint a create against a floored key — reporting `element-create-fabricated` (LOUD-FAILURE, the exact mirror of the pre-existing `element-delete-fabricated` guard) and routing the refusal back through the SAME `onRowsCanonical` channel the delete-side refusal already uses (extended to carry `el: null` as a "remove this from the canvas" instruction, wired in `SitePlanner.jsx` to `applyRemoteInstr({action:"remove",...})`) — so a phantom element is actively corrected off the canvas rather than left to linger. **This closes all three doors above at once**, because it does not depend on WHICH stale-canvas window produced the create — it is asked at the one place every one of them funnels through.
- **THE REGRESSION THIS ALMOST SHIPPED, caught by this session's OWN pre-existing test suite (not by a live check) before any code was pushed.** A blanket refusal of every floored create would have silently broken Undo/Redo of a Delete — `applySnapshot` (the undo/redo seam) restores a whole prior canvas snapshot generically, with no notion of "which of these ids used to be deleted," and its post-restore diff would hit the SAME `!shad` branch with no distinguishing signal from a stale-canvas resurrection. Caught by an existing `elementSync.test.js` case (`"the delete floor for reconcileSeedRows survives >15s (never-pruned) and clears on re-create"`) going from green to red the moment the naive refusal was added. Fixed with a SECOND, narrower, one-shot exemption (`allowResurrect(items)`, mirroring the existing `noteLocalAuthority()` stateful-call pattern) that `applySnapshot` stages — immediately before its own SYNCHRONOUS `flushElems` call, so nothing else can interleave — for every id the restored snapshot holds; consumed (or not) and CLEARED at the end of that one diff pass, never left to linger. The pre-existing B673 "Restore" toast action (`restore()`) was already a distinct, correctly-exempted signal and needed no change. The property-based fuzz harness `ui-audit/session-group-cas.mjs` (an hour of simulated real-engine editing, including its own undo/redo actions) caught the SAME gap in ITS simulated client — updated to mirror the real client's new contract identically, rather than weakening the invariant to pass it.
- **HONESTY, at the time round 3 shipped — per the owner's explicit instruction not to overclaim.** This was NOT reproduced live before shipping round 3 — this sandbox has no signed-in credentials, a standing, previously-disclosed constraint. What WAS certain at ship time: the mechanism was confirmed against REAL PRODUCTION DATA (a `client_errors` capture showing the exact resurrection events, the exact `cls:"create"` op class, and the exact timing), not merely inferred from source; the fix was proven via unit tests that fail red on the OLD `!shad` logic and pass on the new one; and the regression risk this fix could have introduced (breaking Undo of Delete) was found and closed BEFORE shipping, not after. Round 1 and round 2 both shipped on a fully green suite and both failed on the owner's very next live test — that history is why this write-up stayed longer and more explicit than usual, and why `V380768` was re-armed for a third live pass rather than marked done on the sandbox evidence alone.
- **LIVE VERIFICATION, 2026-08-25 — THE FIRST CLEAN RUN IN THE WHOLE FAMILY. Owner-run, verbatim (see `VERIFICATION-DONE.md` → `V380768` for the full report).** Site `smt81yugdrc0`, plan "ZZ throwaway 6 round3 (Claude test)" (a fresh duplicate of Concept A) in Grand Port. Two tabs, same account, presence "2 here", tab B **completely idle**. Deployed chunk `SitePlannerApp-cTEiEGRr.js`, confirmed to carry `stale-cache-overruled` and `stale-canvas-removed`.
  - **DELETE:** host `e271` DEAD, all 13 bonded children DEAD (every one `op_kind: "delete"`), **zero survivors**, **zero rows with `op_kind: "unknown"`** (the B712225 gap is closed on this path too), **zero conflict toasts** in either tab (a DOM observer on `[data-testid="sync-toast"]` was armed in both before the delete), building and its whole assembly gone from the canvas in BOTH tabs.
  - **UNDO (the adjacent case, checked deliberately — this is the near-miss this round's own fix could have broken, see "the regression this almost shipped" above):** Ctrl+Z in tab A restored host + all 13 children, alive, zero dead, zero `op_kind: "unknown"`, one op_kind across the set; the idle tab B picked the restore up correctly. So the one-shot `allowResurrect` exemption over the delete floor works exactly as designed: a deliberate restore passes, a stale-canvas re-mint does not.
  - **The full progression, measured live on the deployed build each time:** pre-#1141 → host deletes, 3 permanent orphans. #1141 (round 1) → host deletes, 12–13 orphans. #1142 (round 2) → **HOST DOES NOT DELETE** — one bump-out dies, everything else alive, permanent; a production regression, reverted as #1143. ### B719779 — Crop a placed site-plan overlay/reference — non-destructive, reversible `[Site Planner / overlay]` (feature) #site-planner #export #perf  *(owner request, verbatim: "whenever we place a site plan over, the ability to crop that site plan would be very helpful because we sometimes don't need all the white space." Minted **B719779 / (no V# — Verify: sandbox, fully self-verified this session, see below)** from this branch's reserved block B719776–B719791 against `origin/main` 98cfd3e. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `crop`, `trim`, `clipPath`, `overlayCrop`, `sheetOverlays`, `overlayPdf`, `B72`, `B461`, `B654`: **B494050** is the PRINT CROP (the export frame around hidden CONTENT, a different thing — that's what area of the SHEET gets drawn; this is what area of ONE PLACED IMAGE shows) and untouched; no prior item lets the user trim a placed reference's own picture. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — implemented, tested (46 unit + wiring tests, pure geometry proof included), and self-verified live in a headless browser this session, including the mandatory PDF-PARITY export check.**
- Verify: sandbox — no LIVE-VERIFY class applies (not GIS, not concurrency, not signed-in-only; PDF-PARITY is the one class that could apply and it was DRIVEN, not assumed — see below) — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK: a logged-out, no-external-GIS canvas + export check is Claude-doable here and was driven, not deferred.
- **THE DATA MODEL.** `o.crop = { x, y, w, h }` in IMAGE PIXELS (the same unit as the existing `imgW`/`imgH`), additive to the `sheetOverlays` record — the persisted raster (`src`/`storageKey`/`idbKey`) is **never touched**, so widening or clearing the crop later recovers exactly the original picture with no re-import. Sparse, matching every other overlay/settings flag in this codebase: no `crop` key at all = the full image, and a crop that normalizes back to covering the whole image collapses to `null` rather than persisting a no-op rect (`overlayCrop.normalizeCrop`).
- **THE DISPLAY MECHANISM — literally what was asked for.** `SitePlanner.jsx`'s `renderSheetOverlay` renders an SVG `<clipPath>` (a `<rect>` sized/positioned via the new pure `cropClipRectScreen`) and applies it to the placed `<image>`'s `clip-path` attribute, ONLY when `hasCrop(o)` — an uncropped overlay renders byte-identically to before this feature (proven: a source-guard test asserts the `<image>`'s `href`/box are untouched, and the live check below confirms no `<clipPath>` node exists for an uncropped overlay). The persisted raster (`o.src`, and the transient hi-res zoom raster `hiresById[o.id]`) are both left as the FULL image; only the DISPLAY is clipped, which is what non-destructive means here.
- **THE PANEL UI.** Four feet-based edge-trim fields (Left/Top/Right/Bottom) in the References panel, available for both PDF-sheet and plain-image overlays (not gated on `o.sheet`), converting to/from the image-px `crop` rect via `overlayCrop.cropTrimFeet`/`cropFromTrimFeet` — this app is feet-everywhere-internal at the UI boundary, never raw pixels. Commits through the SAME `patchOverlay` helper Opacity/Rotate/Width already use (one undo frame per edit session via `onFocus → pushHistory()`, live typing otherwise). A "Reset crop" action (visible only while cropped) clears the field entirely — reversible in one click, no re-import.
- **PDF-PARITY (the one LIVE-VERIFY-class candidate here) — DRIVEN, not argued from source.** `exportSheet.js`'s `buildExportSvg` clones the live `<svg>` wholesale (the same "an export is a document, not a screenshot" mechanism this repo's other overlay features already rely on for parity — B131/B654/B461's z-order/lock/knockout all ride the same clone), and the export's blob→persisted-src href swap (`inlineImages`) sets `href` in place without touching any other attribute — so the `<clipPath>` + its `clip-path` reference on the `<image>` were expected to survive into the export automatically, with zero new plumbing in `exportSheet.js`. **Confirmed, not assumed:** the live check below calls the real E2E `window.__plannerExportSvg()` hook (the same one B719408/measure-export-lod use) after applying a crop and asserts the returned sheet HTML carries the SAME `clipPath` id and the SAME `clip-path="url(#…)"` reference on the exported `<image>`. It does.
- **RASTERISATION COST — WHAT WAS SHIPPED, AND WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT, stated so a later session doesn't assume more than was built (see `overlayCrop.js`'s own header for the full derivation).** A clipped-out region is never painted to the framebuffer by the browser's own compositor, so a heavily-cropped overlay genuinely costs less to paint/composite on every pan and zoom, and that saving carries into the export via the same clone — this is real, not hand-waved. What was investigated and explicitly NOT attempted: shrinking the PDF.js re-raster the overlay's zoomed-in "hi-res" tier produces (`overlayPdf.rasterizePageHiRes`, the B251136/B251137 hot path). The math for a crop-aware PDF.js render is genuinely correct (`page.getViewport({scale, offsetX, offsetY})`, verified against `pdfjs-dist`'s own `PageViewport` constructor and proof-tested — see `test/overlayCrop.test.js`'s worked derivation, kept even though the wiring wasn't shipped) — but wiring it safely also needs the hi-res `<image>`'s on-screen box AND the export's blob-swap to agree on a crop-shaped box instead of the whole-image box they share today, and this repo's own guidance on that exact code path is "read both headers before touching either" (B251136/B251137). Not a change to make without the visual-diff tooling to prove a wrong transform doesn't silently stretch a real placed drawing — flagged loudly rather than attempted half-built, per STANDING RULE #1's own carve-out for a genuine blocker.
- **TESTS.** `test/overlayCrop.test.js` (21) — pure geometry: clamping, the sparse no-crop convention, the screen clip-rect formula (incl. the tl-offset case), and the feet-trim round-trip. `test/overlayCropWiring.test.js` (10) — source guards proving the clipPath is wired into the render body, the panel reads/writes through the pure module (never inline arithmetic), commits through `patchOverlay`, and that crop travels through copy/duplicate/paste for free (a plain field on an already-spread record).
- **LIVE VERIFICATION (this session, headless Chromium, logged out).** New harness `ui-audit/verify-b719776-overlay-fixes.mjs` (kept in the repo) seeds a synthetic 1000×800 ft image overlay, drives the four trim fields through the real panel, and asserts against the REAL rendered DOM: no clipPath while uncropped → typing L/T/R/B (100/50/200/80 ft) persists the exact expected crop rect (`{x:100,y:50,w:700,h:670}`) → a `<clipPath>` renders, is referenced by the `<image>`'s `clip-path` attribute, and sits strictly inside the image's own (unchanged) box → the real export hook's output carries the same clip → Reset crop clears the stored crop AND removes the clipPath from the DOM. **17/17 checks passed** (screenshot: `ui-audit/screens/crop-applied.png`).

### B725218 — Add a "locate me" map control, honest about GPS vs. IP-guess accuracy `[Site Planner / Map]` (feature) #site-planner #ui #mobile  *(owner chat block, part (b) of a mobile-improvements lap — "every map service does this." Minted **B725218** from this branch's reserved block B725216–B725231 / V393760–V393775 against `origin/main` 040c7cb (fetched fresh at ship time). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `locate`, `geolocation`, `you are here`, `Leaflet.*locat`: no prior item. Net-new. Branch `claude/ios-pinch-zoom-locate-telemetry-3bxz1b`.)*
`[x]` **DONE — a "locate me" button on the Site map snaps to the browser's reported position via Leaflet's `map.locate()`, permission-gated, with an accuracy circle drawn only when the fix is tight enough to be honest.**
- Verify: live → **V393761 ✅ PASSED 2026-08-25** (owner confirmed on-device — a real phone's GPS chip lands inside the honesty threshold as designed)
- **Where it lives.** `MapFinder.jsx`: a 3rd Leaflet control stacked in the bottom-left corner, directly below the existing zoom +/− control (every other corner is already claimed per `mapChromeStack.js`'s own rule — a control belongs beside the map's other controls, not fighting a panel for a corner). Plain `L.DomUtil`/`L.DomEvent`, not an `L.Control` subclass (this file's first custom control; a bespoke class buys nothing a closure doesn't already). `mapChromeStack.js`'s `ZOOM_CONTROL_CLEARANCE_PX` (the room a bottom-left banner must leave under the control stack) bumped 84 → 128px to account for the 3rd button, so nothing that reads that constant needs its own change.
- **⛔ Ordering gotcha, measured not assumed:** Leaflet stacks a LATER-added `bottomleft` control ABOVE an earlier one, not below — adding the locate control after the zoom control put it above +/− (measured: locate.y=784 < zoom.y=826 in an 900px-tall viewport). Reordered to add locate BEFORE zoom, confirmed below it (locate.y=858 > zoom.y=782). Noted in the code with the measurement, so a future reader doesn't "fix" it back.
- **The honesty rule (the actual ask).** A phone's GPS fix is genuinely precise (tens of feet); a laptop with no GPS chip falls back to Wi-Fi/IP-based positioning, reported through the SAME `accuracy` field but potentially miles off. Both must not be drawn the same way. New pure module `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/locateMe.js`: `shouldShowAccuracyCircle(accuracyMeters)` gates the accuracy-circle draw at **500 m** (above ordinary GPS/Wi-Fi noise, below "this only knows roughly which side of town"); below the threshold, the map draws a "you are here" dot + a proportionally-sized accuracy ring; at or above it, the map still centers on the best guess available (never silence) but shows an honest "Location is approximate (accuracy ±N mi)" toast instead of a ring that would overstate confidence. `formatAccuracyFt`/`locateErrorMessage` are the other two pure leaves (feet-below-a-mile / miles-above formatting per this app's convention; every `GeolocationPositionError.code` → a plain-English sentence, never a raw browser message, never silent).
- **Permission + failure handling.** No `window.prompt`/`confirm`/`alert` (KEY DECISIONS). A press shows a spinning/dimmed pressed state (the existing `spin` keyframe in `index.css`, applied inline — this is a raw Leaflet DOM node, not React) so a press never reads as inert; a 2nd press while one is in flight is a no-op, not a 2nd request. Denied / timed-out / unavailable all surface through the map's existing bottom-left error-toast slot (`setErr`) — reused rather than inventing a second notice mechanism.
- **Theme:** the marker/circle color is `PAL.accent` (`var(--accent)`), matching this file's own existing precedent for Leaflet vector-layer color (the "Selected parcels" highlight at line ~1348 already passes a `var(--...)` string straight to `L.polygon`'s `color` option) — not a raw hex.
- **Guards:** `test/locateMe.test.js` (12, the three pure functions incl. the threshold boundary, the mile/feet switch, and every error code). Headless `ui-audit/verify-locate-me.mjs` (`npm run build && npm run preview`, then `BASE_URL=… node ui-audit/…`) — 6/6, three arms: a mocked tight (15 m) fix draws map markup and shows NO approximate-location toast; a mocked vague (5 km) fix shows the honest approximate notice; a denied/unavailable fix shows an error toast, never silence. Full-repo `npx vitest run` 12,368/12,368 green, lint 0 errors, build green (`MapFinder.jsx`'s lazy chunk unaffected).
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/locateMe.js` (new), `src/workspaces/site-planner/MapFinder.jsx`, `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/mapChromeStack.js`, `test/locateMe.test.js` (new), `ui-audit/verify-locate-me.mjs` (new).

### B725217 — No gesture telemetry existed anywhere; add a sampled `event:pinch` recording surface `[Shared / telemetry]` (feature) #telemetry #mobile #site-planner #doc-review  *(owner chat block, part (c) — "three pinch fixes have now shipped into a hole where nothing observes the outcome, which is why this keeps recurring." Minted **B725217** from this branch's reserved block against `origin/main` 040c7cb. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `event:pinch`, `gesture telemetry`, `pinch.*telemetry`: `client_errors`'s existing `event:<kind>` convention (B279/B468) had never been used for touch/pointer/gesture data at all — confirmed by reading every `reportClientEvent(` call site in the tree. Net-new, additive to the existing channel. Branch `claude/ios-pinch-zoom-locate-telemetry-3bxz1b`.)*
`[x]` **DONE — every pinch surface (Site Planner canvas, Doc Review Markup canvas, Stitcher) now reports one `event:pinch` row per gesture via the EXISTING `client_errors` channel (`reportClientEvent`, B279) — same dedup/rate/session caps, same fail-safe guarantee, no new table.**
- Verify: sandbox (pure decision/formatting logic, unit-tested; the network path rides B279's already-verified sink) — no live-only dimension of its own; rode on V393760/V393761's on-device pass incidentally (2026-08-25, owner confirmed) rather than needing its own live check.
- **Fields recorded, exactly as asked:** `surface` (site-planner / doc-review / stitcher), `source` (touch — every surface now drives its pinch off native touch, see B725216), `fingers` (finger count at gesture start, tracked through a 3rd-finger rebaseline), `outcome` (`completed` / `cancelled` / `anomaly`), `reason` (only on a non-completed outcome — `touchcancel` / `blur` / `hidden` / `pointercancel-during-pinch`), and `ms` (gesture duration).
- **Sampling, per the explicit ask ("log cancels and anomalies, not every successful pinch, or it will flood the table"):** `shouldLogPinch` always logs a `cancelled` or `anomaly` outcome; a clean `completed` gesture logs at **2%** — enough for a baseline rate to compare cancellations against without flooding the table the way B270912's `event:perf` audit found routine rows already had.
- **The `anomaly` outcome is the diagnostic payoff, and it's why this is more than a counter.** B555's whole premise was that iOS Safari fires a spurious `pointercancel` on the first finger the instant a second lands — B555 makes that harmless (the pointer handlers already bail while `touchCountRef ≥ 2`), but nothing has ever recorded whether it's STILL HAPPENING. Every surface now watches for exactly that: a `pointercancel` arriving while a native-touch pinch already owns the gesture is recorded as `outcome:"anomaly", reason:"pointercancel-during-pinch"` — always logged (never sampled), because it's rare and it's the one signal that would tell a future session "the B555 root cause is still firing, it's just being caught" versus "it stopped happening entirely."
- **Module:** `src/shared/telemetry/gestureTelemetry.js` — pure `shouldLogPinch`/`pinchEventDetail`, impure fire-and-forget `recordPinchGesture` (never throws — same guarantee as every other telemetry entry point). Wired at each surface's natural gesture-end points: the native `touchend`/`touchcancel` handler (completed vs. cancelled), and the existing blur/visibility/pointercancel abort path (cancelled vs. anomaly, by reason).
- **Guards:** `test/gestureTelemetry.test.js` (9 — the sampling boundary, the payload shape, the cancel-reason/duration inclusion rules). Full-repo suite + build green (see B725216's evidence, same session).
- Files: `src/shared/telemetry/gestureTelemetry.js` (new), `test/gestureTelemetry.test.js` (new), plus the wiring in the three files listed under B725216.

### B725216 — iOS pinch-zoom was only ever fixed on the Site Planner canvas (B555) — the Doc Review Markup canvas was still pointer-driven and the Stitcher had NO pinch at all `[Site Planner + Doc Review / mobile]` (bug) #site-planner #doc-review #mobile #ui  *(owner chat block, part (a) — "audit every pinch surface... migrate everything still driving pinch from pointer events onto native touch." Minted **B725216** from this branch's reserved block B725216–B725231 / V393760–V393775 against `origin/main` 040c7cb (fetched fresh at ship time — `npm run next-id -- --against-main`, 29 in-flight peer branches read, B727504 already claimed elsewhere and stepped over). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `pinch`, `touch`, `gesture`, and read B554/B555/B331/B271 in full before writing a line of code (all four in `BACKLOG-DONE.md`). Branch `claude/ios-pinch-zoom-locate-telemetry-3bxz1b`.)*
`[x]` **DONE — every pinch surface in the app now drives its two-finger pinch off native touch events, reusing the SAME shared `pinchZoom`/`midpoint`/`distance` engine (`shared/viewport/viewportTransform.js`) B555 already proved correct — only the event source changed, at every surface. Plus a 3-point hardening audit of B555 itself and a resolved audit discrepancy on a phantom file.**
- Verify: live → **V393760 ✅ PASSED 2026-08-25** (owner confirmed on-device — all 4 surfaces + the off-canvas page-zoom suppression; this also closed the never-duplicated V168/V169 on the same evidence — see VERIFICATION-DONE.md. V170, a different feature (tap-select behavior), was not part of this checklist and stays open.)
- **AUDIT-FIRST — what each surface actually did before this, read from the code, not assumed:**
  | Surface | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Site Planner canvas | Native touch (B555, 2026-06-28) | Unchanged — hardened, see below |
  | Doc Review Markup canvas | **Pointer events**, gated on `pointerType==='touch'` (B331, 2026-06-21 — predates B555's discovery that iOS pointer multi-touch is unreliable) | **Migrated to native touch** |
  | Doc Review Stitcher | **No pinch at all** — pan/draw on plain pointer events, zoom only via wheel/trackpad (B551's pointer-capture recovery is a different bug class — never had two-finger zoom) | **New capability**: native-touch pinch added |
  | MapFinder / Leaflet (Site map) | Leaflet's own internal touch handling, which predates the Pointer Events API and never used it | **Confirmed correct as-is — no code change.** Leaflet's multi-touch was never in the B555 bug class to begin with. |
  | `site-planner/components/ParcelDrawing.jsx` (named by both B271 and B737 as a 3rd canvas needing the same pointer-capture fix) | **Does not exist.** `git log --all -- "*ParcelDrawing*"` returns nothing, on any ref, ever. | **No code to migrate — the file is a phantom.** B737 (2026-07-18, still open/unbuilt) independently reached the identical conclusion for the same filename; this is a second, independent confirmation, not a new finding. The real "parcel drawing overlay" (mark up a PDF/photo attached to a parcel) is unbuilt per B737 — nothing here to touch. Flagging per AUDIT-FIRST rather than silently skipping a named target. |
- **The migration itself (Doc Review + Stitcher), mirroring B555's exact shape:** `onTouchStart/Move/End/Cancel` handlers drive the pinch baseline + a per-frame `requestAnimationFrame` throttle; the existing pointer handlers (`onDown`/`onMove`/`onUp`) gain a top-of-function bail — `if (e.pointerType === "touch" && touchCountRef.current >= 2) return;` — so nothing fights the pinch, exactly as B555 already established. Doc Review's B331-era `touchPinchedRef` stray-tap suppression (a pinch's last finger-lift must not read as a click) is preserved, re-implemented against a finger COUNT instead of a pointer-id Map. Stitcher's `abortGesture` (B551, blur/visibility/pointercancel recovery) is extended to also drop an in-flight pinch, matching B555's own `abortGesture` treatment.
- **B555 hardening — the three specific checks asked for, each with a finding:**
  1. **`touchCountRef` release when a finger lifts outside the canvas, or on a scroll-chaining `touchcancel`.** **No bug found.** Native touch events target the element the touch STARTED on for the whole gesture (unlike pointer events, which follow the current element under the finger and need explicit `setPointerCapture`) — a lift or cancel anywhere on screen still fires on the canvas's own handler. `onTouchCancel` is already wired to the same teardown as `onTouchEnd` on all three surfaces. Verified by reading the spec-guaranteed behavior + the existing shipped `verify-planner-pinch.mjs` harness, which already exercises this.
  2. **A pending `requestAnimationFrame` throttle left across a component re-mount, swallowing the first pinch after.** **Real gap, fixed.** `pinchRafRef` (SitePlanner) had no unmount cleanup — unlike the adjacent `frameRaf`, which already gets one — so a pinch mid-gesture at unmount (a plan switch remounts the canvas per `planClipboardStore`'s own header) left a stale scheduled frame. Low real-world severity (a fresh mounted instance gets brand-new refs, so nothing was actually stuck) but a genuine inconsistency against the file's own established cleanup discipline; added the missing `useEffect` cleanup, mirrored in the new Doc Review/Stitcher code from the start.
  3. **B554's document-level `gesturestart`/`gesturechange`/`gestureend` `preventDefault` vs. the canvas's `touch-action: none`.** **No bug found.** WebKit's `Gesture*` events and standard `Touch*` events are parallel, independent event streams — preventing the former (to stop Safari's own page-zoom/tab-overview) does not suppress or delay the latter. Verified by reading `index.html`'s B554 script + every canvas's touch wiring; no interaction exists between the two mechanisms.
- **Guards:** existing `test/viewportTransform.test.js` (18) + `test/viewportRobustness.test.js` (10, fuzzed finite-output proof) unaffected — the shared engine's semantics didn't change, only its callers. `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js`'s B551 source guard updated to match the extended `abortGesture` signature (still asserts the pointerId is passed through). Full-repo `npx vitest run` — **12,368/12,368 green** (confirmed after `git fetch --unshallow` resolved two pre-existing shallow-clone `git show` artifacts unrelated to this change — `docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js`/`hiddenContentReads.test.js`, verified via `git stash` + rerun on a clean tree before touching anything). Lint 0 errors on every touched file. Build green.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx`, `src/workspaces/doc-review/DocReview.jsx`, `src/workspaces/doc-review/Stitcher.jsx`, `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js`.

### B719408 — Easements (and encumbrances) had ZERO appearance properties — make colour, fill and hatch editable `[Site Planner / markup]` (feature) #site-planner #markup #ui #export  *(owner request, verbatim: "I should really be able to modify easements, like the colors, fill, hatch." AUDIT-FIRST confirmed against production (Supabase `lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi`): 26 easements across 13 plans, `kind:"easement"`, a rich domain model (mode/width/easeType/status/holder/recording/exclusive/parcelId/notes/restrictsBuildings/restrictsPaving/centerline/pts/z) and confirmed literally zero appearance fields — colour came entirely from a fixed per-`easeType` lookup (`easementColor`) and the hatch was ONE hardcoded `<pattern>` per type in `SitePlanner.jsx`, with no override mechanism anywhere. No element type in the app had an editable colour/fill/hatch before this (elements have a TYPE default + per-object fill/stroke override via `planStyle.elStyle`, but no hatch choice; markups have per-object stroke/fill but no hatch). Minted **B719408 / V387952** from this branch's reserved block B719408–B719423 / V387952–V387967 against `origin/main` 4d7cf8d. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `easement`, `encumbrance`, `hatch`, `fill`, `colour`, `appearance`: **B705200** (Done) queried the same production easement/encumbrance records for an unrelated vertex-handle bug and is not a duplicate; **B150–B153** built the easement tool itself; **B935/B620/B435536** are label placement/behaviour, not appearance; **B831/B753/B1092** are pipeline-corridor/GIS features, not styling. Net-new — nothing in either file covers editable easement/encumbrance appearance.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — appearance model designed + implemented + shipped this session, LIVE-VERIFIED on the owner's real Bain "Concept A - Quiddity DIA" plan (17/17 checks passed).**
- Verify: live (LIVE-VERIFY classes hit: zoom-/data-density-dependent rendering — the hatch tile's screen-constant-px behaviour; PDF/export parity — the pattern surviving `buildExportSvg`'s clone) → **PASSED same session, V387952 (full record in `VERIFICATION-DONE.md`)**.
- **DESIGN DECISION 1 — per-TYPE default + per-ELEMENT override (both, not either/or), because the brief asked for an explicit recommendation.** Recommended and shipped: styling defaults off `easeType` (so every pipeline easement in a drawing set looks alike out of the box — what a real plan set wants), and any individual easement can override fill/stroke/fillOpacity/hatch independently (so a specific conflicting or sensitive easement can still be called out). This exactly mirrors the precedent `planStyle.elStyle` already set for elements (`el.fill ?? base.fill`) rather than inventing a third styling shape — a consistency argument, not just convenience. Owner can override to type-only or per-element-only by saying so; the "↺ Reset to type default" button in Properties is the undo path either way.
- **DESIGN DECISION 2 — status (existing/proposed) does NOT get a new appearance channel, and its existing effect is UNCHANGED.** It already drives ONE thing today — proposed easements dash their outline, existing ones are solid — and that predates this work. Flagged explicitly for the owner: several drafting offices use the OPPOSITE convention (existing = dashed/hidden-line since it's often buried and unconfirmed by this survey, proposed = solid/definite). Deliberately left as-is rather than flipped, because flipping it would silently re-style all 26 production easements (100% currently `status:"existing"`, i.e. all solid today) with no user action taken — that read as too large a silent visual change for a session that wasn't asked to touch status semantics. It is a one-line change (`SitePlanner.jsx`'s `proposed ? dashZoom(...) : undefined` on the easement polygon) if the owner wants it flipped. Fill/hatch/colour are NOT status-driven — status stays a pure dash cue, appearance stays purely type/override-driven, so the two questions ("what kind of easement" and "is it built yet") don't compete for the same visual channel.
- **DESIGN DECISION 3 (asked for explicitly) — encumbrances (`kind:"encumbrance"`, the metes-and-bounds deed/title objects, e.g. Grand Port's `e1454610zupcbv`/`e1454611zupcbv`) share the identical appearance model.** They already carried `fill`/`stroke`/`fillOpacity` fields (stamped at creation in `buildEncumbranceMarkup`) that the renderer silently never read for `fill`/`fillOpacity` (only `stroke`/`weight`/`dash` were live) — dead data on every encumbrance ever drawn. Wiring those two fields up is a DISCLOSED SIDE EFFECT: Grand Port's two encumbrances already carry non-default `fillOpacity` (0.14 / 0.10 for the except-hole) from creation, so they will now show a faint colour wash matching their own outline colour that they did not show before. Judged as "the feature the stored data always implied and never got wired to" rather than a regression, and flagged here for the owner to weigh — reversible in one line (`ENCUMBRANCE_DEFAULT.fillOpacity` in `easements.js`) if he'd rather it stayed off until touched.
- **IMPLEMENTATION.** New shared, reusable primitive (built generically on purpose, per the brief's "consider whether it should extend to other element types" — only easement/encumbrance are WIRED to it this session, nothing else touched): `src/shared/style/hatchPatterns.js` — a pure hatch catalog (none/diagonal/diagonalReverse/cross/horizontal/vertical/dots) as tile specs, no JSX. `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/easements.js` gains `easementStyle(e)`/`encumbranceStyle(e)` resolvers (type default, per-element override, `hasOverride` flag) and `easementPatternId`/`encumbrancePatternId` (shared type pattern id when unedited, a per-element id once styled — keeps pattern count bounded to types + actually-edited easements, not one per easement). `SitePlanner.jsx` gets ONE generic `HatchPatternDef` module-scope renderer (MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS) that replaces the old hand-authored per-type `<pattern>` blocks with byte-identical output, plus dynamically-rendered per-element override patterns (only for easements/encumbrances a user has actually styled), plus new Properties-panel fields (Fill color / Fill opacity / Hatch / Outline color / "↺ Reset to type default") for both the easement panel and a new encumbrance-specific block in the generic markup panel.
- **HATCH SCALING WITH ZOOM (asked for explicitly).** Every hatch tile — type-default AND per-element — is defined in constant SCREEN-PIXEL space (`patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"`, no scale ancestor reaches it, because the planner projects feet→screen px before drawing rather than scaling an SVG group) — the exact same technique every pre-existing pattern in this app already uses (`pat-berm`/`pat-trailer`/`pat-sidewalk`/`pat-landscape`). This means a hatch tile's apparent size never changes with zoom: it cannot coarsen into a solid block zoomed in or thin into aliased mush zoomed out, by construction. LIVE-VERIFIED (not just argued from source): the harness read a styled easement's `<pattern>` width/height before and after a real 6-notch wheel-zoom-in gesture on the owner's real Bain plan — unchanged (`{"w":"7","h":"7"} -> {"w":"7","h":"7"}`).
- **PDF-PARITY (asked for explicitly).** `exportSheet.js`'s `buildExportSvgRaw` clones the live `<svg>` verbatim (only strips `data-export="skip"` nodes), so every pattern — including a per-element override pattern — is carried into the export automatically, by construction; no export-specific pattern handling was written or needed. ### B710736 — Bare-domain boot lands in the Food tab instead of the Site Planner: "open where I left off" restores a module with no active project `[App Shell / Routing]` (bug) #infra #ui #food  *(owner report, reproduced live and root-caused in the owner's own signed-in browser before this session started: `localStorage["planyr:lastRoute:v1"]` held exactly `{"module":"food","projectId":null,"cross":false}`, and planyr.io redirected to `#/food` on every bare-domain visit. Contrast case supplied in the same report: `{"module":"site-planner","projectId":"smsrpaiqu5sv","cross":false}` restores correctly. Minted **B710736** from this branch's reserved block B710736–B710751 against `origin/main` 0531fe7. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `lastRoute`, `open where I left off`, `bare domain`, `food tab`, `seedBootRoute`, `pickBootRoute`: no prior item. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — general rule shipped (not a food-only patch), every module audited, adjacent cases checked, live-driven against the real built app.**
- Verify: sandbox (pure client-side routing/localStorage logic — no timing/race, multiwriter, GIS, zoom-density or PDF-export dimension, so this is not a LIVE-VERIFY class; verified instead with a headless Chromium session against the real production build, `vite preview`, per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK)
- **MECHANISM (AUDIT-FIRST).** `Shell.jsx` has exactly ONE write site for the pointer — `useEffect(() => writeLastRoute(route), [route])` — so every navigation (tab click, breadcrumb pick, programmatic `navigate()`) persists whatever route is currently active, with no per-module opt-out. `lastRoute.js`'s `pickBootRoute` then seeds an empty-hash boot from whatever was last stored, with the only existing exemption being the plain default dashboard (`{module:"site-planner", projectId:null}` → `buildHash` gives `"#/"`, a no-op). Food has no project concept at all (`src/workspaces/food/CLAUDE.md`: *"No projects, no cross-workspace navigation — this module is deliberately outside the Site Planner's project model"*), so any visit to it — even a stray click — writes `{module:"food", projectId:null}` as the pointer, and the very next bare-domain boot restores exactly that.
- **(1) GENERAL RULE — a stored pointer is only seeded when it names somewhere SPECIFIC.** Added `isWorthRestoring()` in `src/app/lastRoute.js`, consulted by `pickBootRoute`: a non-default module with **no active project AND not in a deliberate cross-project view** is refused — it's a generic placeholder (a project picker, an empty canvas, "nothing selected") indistinguishable from just landing on the default workspace, so seeding it never restores anywhere the user was actually working. `cross:true` is explicitly exempted — it's a real, user-toggled destination (Notes' "All Notes" dashboard, a cross-project Library tree), not a dead end, and blocking it would have thrown away a working, designed feature the food bug never touched.
  - **⚠ DISCREPANCY FLAGGED, per AUDIT-FIRST.** The brief's stated premise — *"a module with no project is not a place worth returning to"* — is not literally true for Notes' "All Notes" dashboard, Library's project picker, Doc Review's blank canvas, or Scheduler's dashboard: each is a genuine, designed, reachable destination (see the audit table below), not a broken state. The rule is applied anyway, uniformly, because (a) a generic module-with-no-project landing is still a worse bare-domain default than falling through to the Site Planner (which resumes ITS OWN last plan internally via `resumeAllowed`/`pickResumeTarget` — so "fall back to the last real project" happens for free), and (b) every one of those states stays exactly one click from the header crumb, so nothing becomes unreachable — only what gets auto-restored on a fresh tab changes. Flagging this explicitly rather than silently overriding the brief's stated reasoning.
- **(2) FOOD'S PARTICIPATION — DECIDED: excluded outright, both directions.** Food stays reachable by direct URL (`#/food` still parses and mounts it; nothing in `route.js` changed) but never becomes the restored default, and — going further than "don't restore it" — **a visit to Food no longer even overwrites the stored pointer** (`shouldPersistRoute()` in `lastRoute.js`, checked inside `writeLastRoute`). Reasoning: Food is a private personal side product the owner built for himself (place-tracker, ratings, notes on where he's eaten) that happens to live in the same app shell as the professional tool he sends to brokers, lenders and his team — it has no project model to restore INTO even in principle. Not writing it means a food visit is now transparent to "resume": open a project, check Food, close the tab — you come back to the project, not to a fallback default. This is strictly better than merely refusing to seed it, and was cheap to add.
- **(3) EVERY MODULE AUDITED — table produced BEFORE the code change, per the brief's explicit instruction not to fix Food alone and stop:**

  | Module | Writes a `projectId`? | What a `null` projectId MEANS in that module | Bare-domain restore with `projectId: null` (pre-fix) | Bare-domain restore with `projectId: null` (post-fix) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `site-planner` (default) | Yes, when a project is open | No project = the plain dashboard; the module resumes its OWN last plan internally via `resumeAllowed` | Already a no-op — `buildHash` collapses to `"#/"`, no distinct seed | Unchanged (already correct; this module was never the bug) |
  | `doc-review` (Review) | Yes, when a project/file is open | "No drawing open — Browse the Library" empty state (B496) | Restored the empty state | **Not restored — falls through to default boot** |
  | `library` | Yes, when a project is picked | Project picker ("pick a project") when signed in and not cross-project | Restored the picker | **Not restored — falls through to default boot** |
  | `scheduler` | Yes, via `onProjectChange`/route carry-in | "genuine no-current-project state" — a link/dashboard panel | Restored the panel | **Not restored — falls through to default boot** |
  | `notes` | Yes, when a project is open | Deliberately meaningful: the Dashboard IS the all-projects view (`notes/CLAUDE.md`: *"every project's pages, grouped under the project's name"*) — reached via `cross:true`, not a bare `projectId:null` | Restored the all-projects view | **Not restored when `cross:false`** (a bare no-project Notes state is still a generic placeholder); **still restored when `cross:true`** (the deliberate all-projects view is exempted, see (1) above) |
  | `food` | No — `FoodApp.jsx` never reads a `projectId` prop at all; structurally outside the project model | N/A — there is no "no project" STATE, the whole module has no project axis | **Restored `#/food`, the reported bug** | **Never restored, and no longer even written to the pointer** (decision (2)) |
- **(4) ADJACENT CASES CHECKED:**
  - **Project since deleted / access lost.** Unaffected by this fix — the guard only fires on a `null` projectId; a stale-but-non-null id still seeds exactly as before. Existing per-module handling is uneven and pre-existing (not touched, not regressed): the Site Planner has an explicit self-heal (`routeMissing` + a signed-in retry, falls to the map/dashboard); Library, Doc Review and Notes fall back to a generic `"Project"` label when the id isn't found locally rather than distinguishing "deleted" from "not yet cached" (Notes is the most careful of the three — it explicitly names an unresolved lookup rather than mislabeling it "no project"). Recorded here as a known, pre-existing gap — out of scope for this item, which is specifically the null-projectId restore bug.
  - **First-ever visitor, no key at all.** `readLastRoute()` returns `null` → `pickBootRoute` returns `null` (its existing `!stored` guard, untouched) → normal empty-hash boot. Verified live: clearing `localStorage` entirely and reloading throws nothing and seeds nothing.
  - **The `/landing/` front-door redirect (`index.html`).** Untouched and unaffected by construction: it tests for keys matching `/^planarfit:/` or `/^sb-.*-auth-token$/`; `planyr:lastRoute:v1` matches neither pattern, so it was never part of its "returning user" signal before or after this change. (Could not be driven live end-to-end — the redirect script's own first line is `if (navigator.webdriver) return;`, so it deliberately never fires under Playwright/automation; confirmed by direct code read instead.)
- **Fix:** `src/app/lastRoute.js` (`isWorthRestoring`, `shouldPersistRoute`, `PROJECTLESS_MODULES`, wired into `pickBootRoute` and `writeLastRoute`), `src/app/Shell.jsx` (comment only — the write effect already routes through the new guard).
- **Tests.** `test/lastRoute.test.js` — 12 new cases (RED confirmed against the pre-fix code before implementing, per AUDIT-FIRST — all 8 new/changed assertions failed cleanly first), covering: every project-scoped module refuses to seed with `projectId:null, cross:false`; a real project id still seeds normally for all of them; `cross:true` still seeds despite `projectId:null`; Food is refused even with a project id or cross mode; `shouldPersistRoute` excludes only Food. Full suite: `npm test` → 588/591 files, 12,268/12,271 tests green — the 3 pre-existing failures (`mapDrift` fixed by regenerating `MAP.md` for the new exports; `docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js` and `hiddenContentReads.test.js` fail on this shallow clone's missing git history — `git show <hash>` for a commit predating the shallow fetch depth — reproduced identically on a clean `git stash` of this branch, unrelated to this change). `npm run lint` → 0 errors. `npm run build` → green.
- **Live-driven verification (ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK — logged-out, no external GIS, fully Claude-doable).** Built the app, served it with `vite preview`, drove a real headless Chromium against it (script discarded after use, not committed): (a) `{food, null}` no longer restores `#/food`; (b) `{food, "some-id"}` still never restores; (c) `{library, null}` no longer restores the picker; (d) `{doc-review, "real-project"}` still restores normally; (e) `{site-planner, "smsrpaiqu5sv"}` — the owner's own healthy case from the report — still restores normally; (f) navigating from a real project INTO Food and reloading shows the pointer still names the real project, untouched; (g) a from-scratch clean boot with no stored key at all boots without error. All 7 checks passed.
- Base: `origin/main` @ `0531fe7`.


### B286001 — Mid-gesture, line weights and text do NOT counter-scale: deliberate, deferred, and filed so closing B1449 cannot bury it `[Site Planner / UI]` (task) #site-planner #perf #ui  *(filed 2026-08-09 from the owner chat block that CLOSED B1449, whose instruction was explicit: "One thing stays OPEN: line weights and text do not counter-scale mid-gesture. If that is not already filed, file it as its own B# marked deliberate-and-deferred, so closing B1449 does not bury it." Minted **B286001** from this branch's reserved block B286000–B286015, against origin/main cf4f77b. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `counter-scale`, `vector-effect`, `non-scaling-stroke`, `ANCHOR_MAX_K`, `stroke weight`, `mid-gesture`, `B1449`, `B1360`, `B1440`, `B1345`: the trade is DESCRIBED in three places — B1449's own "COUNTER-SCALING STROKES AND TEXT MID-GESTURE: NOT DONE" bullet, B1360's increment-2 risk column, and V56000's watch-item 2 — but **it has never had an item of its own**, which is exactly the burial the owner named. **B1360** stays Open and owns increments 3–5; it is not re-opened or superseded by this. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE 2026-08-23 — CLOSED ON BRANCH (b) OF ITS OWN STOPPING RULE: the owner confirmed the mid-gesture picture is a non-issue in real use. Recorded as a design decision, NOT as work that was completed.**
- Verify: live (any change here is zoom-dependent rendering by definition — LIVE-VERIFY)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-09 from chat
- **WHAT IT IS.** While the wheel is turning, the drawing is emitted once at the anchor view and carried by one group transform `translate(tx ty) scale(k)`. A group `scale` scales EVERYTHING inside it, so line weights, text and the level-of-detail tier the frame started at grow and shrink with the picture until the gesture settles and the frame re-bakes (~180 ms after the last notch). The owner was told this and accepted it; V56000's watch-item 2 asked him to look at exactly this and he answered *"I think we're good."*
- **WHY IT WAS NOT DONE, with the cost, unchanged from B1449's report.** **Text** has no mechanism short of re-emitting every `font-size` — which IS the cost B1449 removes, so it is self-defeating. **Strokes** could ride `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"`, but that is an attribute on every stroked node in the tree; applying it per-gesture is the same re-emit, so it would have to be unconditional — and unconditional changes the EXPORT path's authored weights, which is a PDF-PARITY problem on a surface where a line weight is a drafting convention rather than a preference.
- **WHAT ALREADY BOUNDS IT, so this is not unbounded drift.** `ANCHOR_MAX_K = 2` — about six detents — past which the anchor is dropped and the frame re-bakes at the live view. So the worst the picture can be off is one doubling, for the length of one gesture.
- **⛔ WHAT MUST NOT BE TOUCHED IF THIS IS EVER PICKED UP** (owner instruction, verbatim scope on the B1449 closure): do NOT re-open the anchored-zoom transform, do NOT change `k = view.ppf / anchor.ppf`, and do NOT touch the byte-identical-at-`k === 1` property that makes B1440's pan path unchanged by construction. Any work here is ADDITIVE to the render body, and `test/viewAnchor.test.js` is the arbiter.
- **STOPPING RULE.** This closes one of two ways, both of them results: (a) the owner reports that the mid-gesture picture bothers him in real use, at which point it becomes a real defect with a real repro and a named cost; or (b) it is confirmed a non-issue at his next substantive zoom-behaviour review, and it moves to Done as a recorded design decision. It is NOT a to-do waiting for capacity, and it must not be picked up speculatively — the trade was accepted on the record.
- **⛔ HOW IT CLOSED, and which branch of the stopping rule fired — named, because the rule requires it.**
  **Branch (b): *confirmed a non-issue at his next substantive zoom-behaviour review.*** Not branch (a),
  and nothing was implemented. The owner, unprompted, 2026-08-23: ***"Zoom feels fine to me as it is
  right now - no changes needed. I will flag it if that changes."*** That is a direct answer to
  V56000's watch-item 2, which is the question this item was carved out of — and it is his SECOND
  answer to it (2026-08-09: *"I think we're good."*), given after a fortnight of real use rather than
  on the day it shipped, which is the difference between an impression and a verdict.
- **THE DISPOSITION, BY NAME (STANDING RULE #2 enforcement).** **(3) — asked him whether it was a
  problem and took his answer as the verdict.** Legitimate here for a reason worth stating rather than
  assuming: this was never a reproducible-or-not question. The behaviour is DETERMINISTIC, fully
  characterised, deliberately introduced and machine-guarded — nothing was unknown about *what* the
  drawing does mid-gesture. The only open question was whether it bothered him, and the only
  instrument for that is him. **No null was involved and none was relied on**, which is precisely the
  situation clause 2 exists to keep apart from a failed reproduction.
- **VERIFY: LIVE — DISCHARGED BY THE OWNER'S OWN LIVE USE.** It never carried a `V###` and did not
  need one: the check was *"does this bother you on your own plans"*, run for a fortnight on the
  production build on his own machine. No sandbox pass could have substituted, and no `Blocker:` was
  ever in the way of him answering.
- **⛔ WHAT THIS CLOSURE DOES NOT SAY.** It does not say counter-scaling was attempted, and it does not
  retire the cost analysis above — that stands, and is the reason to re-read this item rather than
  re-derive it if the subject ever returns. **His "I will flag it if that changes" is now the standing
  condition**, so a future session must not reopen this speculatively; a fresh report from him would be
  a new item with a real repro, exactly as branch (a) says. `ANCHOR_MAX_K = 2` and the byte-identical-
  at-`k === 1` property remain the invariants `test/viewAnchor.test.js` arbitrates.
- **Tests.** None changed — no code was touched. This is a record, not a release.

  - **ETJ:** Simonton **5.781%** (5.173 ac) / Fulshear **5.197%** (4.650 ac) — both comfortably above the 0.5% floor (`CITY_SHARE_MIN`), reproducing B689904's recorded 5.78%/5.20% independently, to three decimal places, on a query run fresh this session.
- **STALE CACHE — ruled out, not assumed.** The badge tooltip's "As of 5d ago" is the SWR cache's age label (`etj_hgac`'s TTL is 7 days), not a claim the underlying boundary is stale. This session's live query, run today against the same H-GAC layer, returned shares matching the recorded numbers to three decimal places — the cached answer and a fresh pull agree, so there is no stale-and-wrong boundary hiding behind the age label.

- Verify: sandbox
- **⛔ READ FIRST — A PRIOR SESSION'S "REPRODUCTION" OF THIS BUG WAS FALSE AND HAD TO BE RETRACTED** (`docs/B463922-SCROLL-JUMP-HANDOFF.md`, now updated with this resolution). It clicked a collapse toggle Playwright itself had to auto-scroll into view, and reported the DRIVER's own scroll as a +477px app jump. This session's numbers are proven the app's, not the driver's: every click went through `visibleClick` (throws rather than clicking anything not already on screen, verified with `targetVisibility` first) and every `scrollTop` change was captured via a patched setter (`installScrollWitness`) so a real app write is distinguishable from a driver reaching an off-screen target.
- **STEP 1 — REPRODUCED, CLEANLY, MEASURED.** Staged the owner's exact scenario: a row clicked once a while ago (selected, no editor open) sitting below a collapsed group, both simultaneously on screen; then expand the group. A real, app-owned `scrollTop` write was captured (`182→326`): the toggled row and its 6 new children were thrown OFF SCREEN ABOVE by exactly 144px — 6 rows × 24px, the height of what was revealed — while the stale, merely-clicked-on selection held its screen position instead. That is the owner's report to the pixel.
- **ROOT CAUSE.** The existing B463922 anchor-preservation effect holds the row the user is "working on" fixed on screen across any list re-layout, priority: selected row while on screen, else top-of-viewport. Correct for protecting a live edit against an unrelated background change (still true and unchanged). Wrong for a click whose entire point is to REVEAL rows: a stale `selectedId` — clicked at some earlier point, nothing being typed — outranked the group that was just clicked, so the reveal lost to a click from minutes ago.
- **THE FIX.** The expand toggle's `onClick` records which row it's expanding (`expandAnchorRef` — expand-only; collapsing reveals nothing, so it needs no protection and that path is untouched). The scroll-anchor effect prefers that row over `selectedId` UNLESS a cell editor is genuinely open elsewhere (`edit != null`) — an active edit still wins, so the vaguer, separately-reported complaint ("sometimes if I'm editing cells... I'll jump") stays covered by the ORIGINAL, unmodified protection. A companion ref (`suppressSelChaseRef`) tells the second "keep selectedId visible" effect to sit out that one render, so it doesn't immediately chase the stale selection back into view and undo the reveal.

### B643104 — Schedule grid: changing the row-height slider throws the on-screen row out of the rendered window `[Schedule]` (bug) #scheduler #ui  *(self-discovered while sweeping B463922 for "any other instances" per the owner's own instruction — NOT itself owner-reported, and NOT the same bug: different trigger (a Format-panel settings change, not a click on the schedule), different mechanism (an ABSENT compensating scroll write, not a wrong one). Minted **B643104** from this branch's reserved block B643104–B643119 via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `ROW_H`, `rowHeight`, `FormatPanel`, `heldRowHRef`, `row-height`: no prior item; filed here rather than folded into B463922 so a future search for this specific defect finds it.)*
`✅` **Done — shipped in the same commit as B463922 (×2), same PR (#1101). Split into its own item on request so it has its own record.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **ROOT CAUSE — an ABSENT write, not a wrong one.** `ROW_H` is reassigned per-render at `public/sequence/index.html:5505` (`ROW_H = Math.min(34, Math.max(20, data.settings?.rowHeight || 24));`), and every row's rendered position reads it directly at render time (`style={{top:ri*ROW_H, ...}}`, e.g. line 9251). Pre-fix, nothing recomputed the container's `scrollTop` when `ROW_H` changed — the raw pixel offset stayed exactly what it was, now describing a completely different row than before the resize. This is the opposite failure shape from B463922: that bug was an app write firing with the WRONG delta; this one is no write firing at all where one was needed.
- **MEASURED, pre-fix (formal harness, `ui-audit/verify-grid-row-hold.mjs`, section "B548xxx — a row-height change must not throw the view out of the rendered window," run against commit `bbec97ea`, the parent of the fix):** `✗ row-height — row 156 is no longer rendered (was at 399px)`. Not a large delta — the row left the render window entirely (the virtualiser dropped it, since nothing told it to look at the new area).
- **MEASURED, post-fix, same row, same selection state:** `✓ row-height — selected row 156 held its place across the resize (399px → 399px)` — held exactly, Δ 0px.
- **THE FIX.** A second `useLayoutEffect`, keyed on `ROW_H` (`heldRowHRef` tracks the previous value), using the same anchor priority as B463922's effect — the selected row while it's on screen, else the row at the top of the viewport — and one unified formula, `el.scrollTop = Math.max(0, st + anchor*(ROW_H - prevRH))`, where `anchor` is either the selected row's integer index or the top-of-viewport row's fractional index. The same formula covers both cases; holding a specific row's index fixed across a uniform per-row rescale is algebraically the same operation whether that index is a whole selected row or a fractional viewport edge.
- **RELATED TO, NOT PART OF, B463922.** Both were found in the same sweep and ship in the same commit, but they are different bugs: B463922 is triggered by a click and caused by a wrong anchor choice; this one is triggered by a settings change and caused by a missing compensation entirely. See B463922 for the click-anchor bug and the sweep that found this one.
- **⛔ NOT CI-ENFORCED**, same as B463922: `ui-audit/verify-grid-row-hold.mjs` is not invoked anywhere in `build.yml`. See also **B643105** — this specific file has no static validation in CI at all, which is a larger, separate finding.
- Files: `public/sequence/index.html` (`GridView`: `heldRowHRef`, the row-height `useLayoutEffect`), `ui-audit/verify-grid-row-hold.mjs` (the row-height section).
- Base: `origin/main` @ `3eb34b639c3c9a0904985c5b75b4804727898871`.

Minted **B623680** LATE via `--against-main` from this branch's reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `carry-forward`, `handoff`, `session`, `context`, `one task per session`, `STANDING RULE #3`, `TRAPS.md`: **STANDING RULE #3** (`CLAUDE.md`) states the one-task-per-session rule and says a brief is the cheapest part; **`ui-audit/TRAPS.md`** collects harness traps for the whole repo. Neither is a Notes-specific carry-forward, and neither was wired to load automatically for this module. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — shipped this session. Documentation, so no live-verify; the WIRING is machine-enforced.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **⛔ THE FAILURE IT CORRECTS, in the owner's own words, because the diagnosis is the value:** the project rule is one task per session, then archive. It was ignored for a week — everything went into ONE session, which ended up re-reading roughly **half a million tokens of history on every dispatch**. *"The reason I kept justifying it is the real bug: everything a new session would need to know existed only in this session's memory, so starting fresh always looked expensive. I wrote it up — and then put it somewhere a Claude Code session does not read."* **A carry-forward filed where no session reads it is the same mistake wearing a different hat.**
- **WHAT LANDED:** `docs/NOTES-CARRY-FORWARD.md` — the instrument traps that have each produced a confident FALSE finding about working code, the Richfield "Utilities" fixture (simplifying it hides the defects, and that is measured rather than cautionary: all 17 Tab cases passed before AND after the B519680 fix because every one used a flat list), the storage keys and the standing `live_but_purged` SQL check, the scratch-page hygiene rules for his live account, the verification bar, and the three recurring bug families.
- **WIRED AT BOTH DOORS:** the always-loaded `CLAUDE.md` (so it is read before the module pointer and before the code) **and** `src/workspaces/notes/CLAUDE.md` (which auto-loads inside the folder). Both are asserted, so the wiring cannot quietly come loose again — which is precisely how this failed the first time.
- **⛔ AND ONE CLAIM WAS CORRECTED AGAINST THE REPO'S OWN MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN COMMITTED AS GIVEN.** The source text said *"keyboard events do not register at all in this app."* Measured (SYNTHETIC-KEYS-DONT-EDIT, `CLAUDE.md`): the handler is bound to `window` and `new KeyboardEvent(…)` defaults to `bubbles: false`, so a synthetic event on `document` never reaches it — while the same event with `{ bubbles: true }`, or dispatched on `window`, works fine. The app never checks `isTrusted`. **A false fact inside an always-read document is exactly the failure mode the document exists to prevent**, so the precise mechanism is in the file and a guard pins it. The rule the owner wanted — never trust a synthetic keystroke, drive real input — is unchanged and is what the file says.
- **THE ANTI-ROT GUARDS (`test/notesModule.test.js`), all four mutation-proven:** the file exists and still carries each of its sections · `CLAUDE.md` points at it · the module pointer points at it · **every repo path it names still exists** (a document that confidently names a deleted harness sends the next session hunting for it, which is worse than silence) · and the corrected synthetic-key mechanism may not be replaced by the overstated one. ⛔ The last guard distinguishes a **quoted correction** from an **assertion** — the file deliberately quotes the wrong claim in order to correct it, so a blunt ban would have forbidden the fix along with the fault.
- **KEEPING IT CURRENT is the mechanism, not an aspiration:** a new instrument trap or bug family goes into that file **in the same commit that discovers it**, never left in a session's memory. Stated in the file, in both pointers, and on this item.
- Files: `docs/NOTES-CARRY-FORWARD.md` (new), `CLAUDE.md`, `src/workspaces/notes/CLAUDE.md`, `test/notesModule.test.js` (6 guards).

`✅` **Done — shipped this session. Measured first: the dialog was NOT broken at any tested width. Retracting the suspected bug and shipping the missing coverage instead — `ui-audit/verify-successor-complete.mjs` 102/102, two new mutation proofs.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **THE MEASUREMENT, not an impression.** Rendered the real modal (real headless Chromium, the app's own responsive header — the desktop Version-History button above the 768px `isMobile` breakpoint, the overflow-menu route below it) at seven widths and drove the interaction, not just the geometry: **1600** (desktop baseline) · **768** (the app's own `isMobile` breakpoint) · **430** (widest common phone) · **393** (mainstream iPhone/Android) · **375** (iPhone SE/mini) · **360** (most common Android width worldwide) · **320** (narrowest real phone floor). At every one: the footer never overflows its container, neither button's label wraps, the "N updates pending" label never collides with either button, the card never clips outside the viewport, and — the strongest proof — **Update Successors was actually clicked at each width and the resulting status change (`In Progress`) was confirmed**, not just its bounding box measured. Nothing here needed a fix.
- **THE ONE THING THAT WAS ALMOST A FALSE POSITIVE.** A fine sweep (every 5px, 320–500) found the two buttons — both spreading the identical `FOOTER_BTN_STYLE` object — differ by exactly **±0.015625 CSS px (1/64 px)** at roughly a quarter of the widths in the 340–460px range where they're actively shrinking, alternating sign. That is Chromium's own LayoutUnit rounding when two independently-shrinking same-basis flex items land on a fractional remainder — not a design defect, and reproducible with `flex:'1 1 0'` equal-split math too (an odd number of 64ths still can't split evenly). It is at least an order of magnitude below one device pixel on any real screen at any DPR. The new width-sweep check asserts equal size with a **0.1px tolerance** (6x that measured floor, still ~1,000x tighter than anything the mutation below produces) rather than bit-identical `===`, and says why inline rather than silently loosening a bar.
- **TWO NEW MUTATION PROOFS, each independently falsifiable.** (1) Removing the card's `maxWidth:'94vw'` clamp alone did NOT reproduce an overflow — measured live, because the card is the sole flex item in the backdrop's centering flex row and default `flex-shrink:1` already contains it. Only pairing that removal with `flexShrink:0` (defeating both mechanisms) reproduces a real viewport overflow at 320px, while the 1600px case stays green (480 < 1600 regardless) — proving the overflow check is discriminating, not a blunt instrument, and documenting a real finding along the way: the card is doubly protected against horizontal overflow. (2) Pinning a `minWidth:130` onto only the Update button (a plausible real mistake) produces a 57.5px inequality at 320px while both stay at 150px at 1600px — proving the equal-width check is discriminating in the other direction.
- **⛔ SAID OUT LOUD, AS ASKED: A3's pixel comparison (and every new check in this item) is NOT in the CI-required `build` check.** Read `.github/workflows/build.yml` directly rather than assumed: it runs lint, the drift/mint guards, `npm test` (vitest — this is where the FOOTER_BTN_STYLE *source-regex* anchor in `test/schedulerEngine.test.js` lives, and that one IS CI-gated), `npm run build`, and the perf-bundle audit. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — shipped this session. Reproduced live, fixed, mutation-proven in `ui-audit/verify-schedule-export-health-colours.mjs` (`--mutate-dropdown` flips only the 2 dropdown checks; all 12 colour-parity checks + Gantt + export stay green).**
- Verify: sandbox
- **THIS WAS A MEASURE-FIRST TASK, NOT A REDESIGN.** Owner instruction: fix the one clear bug, measure whether automation is even doing anything on his real schedules, and bring options — do not invent a second panel design. Nothing below the fix was shipped; the panel-layout and override-badge sections are options he picks from, not code.
- **THE THREE NUMBERS, from his real production data (read-only Supabase query, 529 leaf tasks across 6 plans):** healthOverride is true on **302 (57%)**; a rule actually decides the colour on **29 (5.5%)**; not overridden and matching no rule (falls through to raw/stale stored colour) on **198 (37%)**. His live `settings.healthRules` holds exactly **one** rule — `finishPastDays` days=1 → red — confirmed from storage, not guessed off his screenshot. **Said loudly, as he asked: automation is effectively not running on his schedules — it decides about 1 task in 18.**
- **THE MECHANISM, traced in code:** `updateTask` sets `healthOverride:true` any time `health` is written without the caller also passing `healthOverride` itself (`if ('health' in updates && !('healthOverride' in updates)) u.healthOverride = true;`). Every ordinary status pick — the grid dot, the status pill — routes through this, so **the badge is set by normal use, not by a deliberate lock gesture**, which is why it marks 57% of his schedule and why he can't read it as a signal.
- **THE BUG ITSELF:** `RuleColorPicker`'s dropdown rendered inline (no portal) inside `AutomationPanel`, whose own `onMouseDown={stopPropagation}` — the same pattern every side panel here uses — ate every mousedown inside the panel before it could reach the picker's own outside-click listener. Measured live: a click on the panel's blank space, or on a DIFFERENT rule row's own `<select>`, left the dropdown open and floating over that control; only a click outside the whole panel closed it.
- **THE FIX, matching how every other menu here behaves (HealthPicker/StatusPicker):** portal the dropdown to `document.body` as `position:fixed` with `{...MENU_STOPS_GRID}` on the menu's own root (not the panel's), **and** listen for the outside click in the capture phase — the one piece no other picker needed, because no other picker sits inside a panel that blanket-stops propagation. Confirmed live: blank-panel click, another row's control, and outside-the-panel click all now close it correctly; picking a colour still applies and closes; the panel itself never closes by accident.
- **OPTIONS DELIVERED, NOT IMPLEMENTED** (screenshots + measured numbers handed to Michael in chat/artifact): three panel-layout alternatives (sentence-per-rule, current row + a live count, summary strip above unchanged rows) and three override-badge alternatives (keep as-is, show only when it would differ from automatic — 202/302 still would, 100/302 wouldn't — or drop the concept). He picks; nothing here is wired to a decision.
- Files: `public/sequence/index.html` (`RuleColorPicker`). Harness: `ui-audit/verify-schedule-export-health-colours.mjs` (new `--mutate-dropdown` switch alongside the existing `--mutate-rollup`; added `Supabase set error` to its BENIGN console filter since this is the first scenario in the file to mutate state through a real UI click rather than pre-seeded data).
