### B590017 — The menu runs off the bottom of the screen and hides "Delete this box" behind the taskbar `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-17, NEW-2 — *"you can't see everything on the menu because the delete part is hidden behind my start menu or task bar."* Minted **B590017** from the same block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `menu`, `placement`, `viewport`, `innerHeight`, `clamp`, `B539651`, `B1367`: B539651 built the menu and never positioned it against its own measured size; B1367 is the RAIL's row menu, a different surface. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — shipped this session. Measured at four positions down a 620px window.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **⛔ THE OLD RULE WAS A GUESS, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DEFECT:** `top: Math.min(at.y, innerHeight - 420)` — a hard-coded **420px estimate of the menu's own height**, never checked against what rendered. A menu taller than the guess still ran off the bottom, and the row that fell off was the LAST one, which is `Delete this box`.
- **WHAT LANDED:** `placeMenu` is a PURE rule over the MEASURED assembly, applied in a **layout effect** (before paint, so the menu is never seen in the wrong place and then corrected). Prefer below-right of the pointer · **FLIP above** when it will not fit below · clamp into the viewport with a margin · a menu taller than the viewport starts at the TOP, because clamping the bottom would push the first rows off. `visualViewport` is preferred over `innerHeight` deliberately: on a maximised window it already excludes the taskbar, which is exactly his case.
- **⛔ THE WHOLE ASSEMBLY IS MEASURED, STRIP INCLUDED** — measuring only the list would reproduce the same class of error one layer down.
- **MEASURED:** at screen y=499 and y=579 in a 620px window the menu **flips** and `Delete this box` lands at 493 and 573 — fully on screen. Mutation-proven: restoring the 420 guess fails 7 tests and **2,046 placements** in the property sweep.
- Files: `components/NoteEditor.jsx` (`placeMenu` + the layout effect). Tests: `notesMenuPlacement` (13, incl. a grid sweep of every pointer position × four menu heights). Harness: `verify-notes-menu-layout`.

### B590018 — With several boxes selected, dragging one moved only that one `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-17, NEW-4 — *"if I select multiple things and then I grab one of them to move it, it should move all of the items together."* Minted **B590018** from the same block. DEDUPE-FIRST — **B421494** SHIPPED marquee multi-select and its group drag, and is Done. This is not a recurrence of it: that group drag was correct and is untouched. It was simply unreachable from the one affordance built for moving a box. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — shipped this session. `verify-notes-menu-layout` §3, judged on the stored document.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **⛔ HE GUESSED THE CAUSE AND WAS RIGHT ABOUT ITS SHAPE** — *"check the drag does not silently drop the selection on pointerdown."* Close: the selection was never dropped, the group drag was never **reached**. `beginGroupDrag` exists and is wired to the MAT's press handler, but the grip calls `preventDefault()` on `pointerdown`, which suppresses the compatibility `mousedown` the mat listens for. So grabbing a box **by its grip** — the one control built for moving it — was the single path the group drag could not see, and marquee-select was pointless for the thing people select for.
- **WHAT LANDED:** the grip reads the live selection **from the DOM** (`[data-selected="1"]`, the same attribute the stylesheet paints the ring with, so the boxes that move are exactly the boxes he can see are selected) and moves the whole set through the existing `moveSelection` rule and `moveNoteAnchors` command — ONE delta for the set, ONE undo frame.
- **MEASURED:** three boxes, all three moved by **90,50 · 90,50 · 90,50** — the same delta, so the arrangement is preserved exactly — and one Ctrl+Z returned all three.
- **⛔ AND AN INSTRUMENT FAILURE WORTH RECORDING, because it produced a confident false finding about working code:** `page.mouse.click` accepts `button`/`clickCount`/`delay` and **silently ignores `modifiers`** (that option belongs to `locator.click`). Every Shift+click replaced the selection instead of adding to it, one box ended up selected, and the harness reported *"the group drag moves only one box"*. An option a driver quietly drops is indistinguishable from a feature that does not work.
- Files: `lib/notesAnchorNode.js` (the grip's group branch). Harness: `verify-notes-menu-layout` §3.

### B583008 — A box NARROWED while it was being dragged, then sprang wide again on release `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(owner chat 2026-08-15, NEW-1, with a screenshot caught mid-gesture. Minted **B583008** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B583008–B583023. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `placeAnchor`, `moveNoteAnchor`, `drag`, `narrow`, `clamp`, `B539648`, `B434417`, `B400177`, `B391073`, `B421490`: **this IS the same root as B539648** and he guessed as much — but B539648 is Done and shipped, and this is the clamp surviving in a path that item did not touch, so per the recurrence rule it takes its own number and cross-links rather than re-opening a correct fix. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — shipped this session. 30/30 in `ui-audit/measure-notes-drag-width.mjs`, mutation-proven in both directions.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **HIS REPORT:** *"when I grab this, it's normally wider if I let go, but when I grab it, it shortens up."* His screenshot catches "High Voltage Planning Study" wrapped onto TWO lines while the button is down; one line at rest.
- **THE CAUSE, AND IT IS HIS HYPOTHESIS 1 EXACTLY:** the move drag ran `placeAnchor`, whose whole job is *"narrow the block to the space available"* — `w = max(floor, min(preferred, hostWidth − left − pad))`. Dragging rightward shrank `room`, so the box reflowed under his hand; on release `moveNoteAnchor` commits only x/y, so the stored width came straight back and it sprang wide again. **B539648 replaced "narrow it" with "grow the page" at PLACEMENT and in the RESIZE drag, and the move drag kept the old rule.**
- **HIS HYPOTHESES 2 AND 3 ARE REFUTED, with evidence, so they are not re-opened:** the width source does NOT change (the stored `w` is untouched throughout — measured), and there is NO transform swap or drag layer (`computed transform: none` on every editing host, printed by `diagnose-notes-caret-bounds`). It was one function call.
- **THE FIX IS A SEPARATE FUNCTION, NOT A FLAG:** `moveAnchorPoint` has no width arithmetic in it at all, so a move cannot resize by any route. A boolean on `placeAnchor` would have left the arithmetic sitting in the move path for somebody to re-enable.
- **⛔ AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THE HARNESS WAS VACUOUS — IT WENT GREEN ON THE DEFECT.** It read the box five times during the drag with a 60 ms pause between reads. `fitAnchorBox` runs from a ResizeObserver and re-derives the rendered width from `data-anchor-w`, so a narrowing written to `style.width` alone is undone on the very NEXT FRAME: the box really does reflow, repeatedly, for one or two frames per pointer move, and a reader arriving 60 ms later always finds it restored. The measurement had to move onto the FRAME CLOCK (a `requestAnimationFrame` sampler inside the page). With teeth it reports `160–300` and the words wrapping 1 → 2 lines, on the right-edge cases, in both drag directions, at both zooms — and stays green on the mid-page cases that never failed. A second instrument bug was caught in the same pass: comparing unzoomed `style.width` against zoomed `getBoundingClientRect` failed every 200% row, including the correct ones.
- Files: `lib/notesBoxResize.js` (`moveAnchorPoint`), `lib/notesAnchorNode.js` (the grip's move handler). Tests: `notesBoxResize` (+6, incl. the contrast assertion that `placeAnchor` still narrows and a move does not). Harness: `measure-notes-drag-width` (30).

### B583009 — The Windows text-cursor indicator lands up and to the left: the writing surface was exposed as a GENERIC container, not a text control `[Notes]` (bug — accessibility) #notes #ui #a11y  *(owner chat 2026-08-15, filed as an accessibility item on his instruction — *"treat it as an accessibility bug, not a cosmetic one. He relies on this."* Minted **B583009** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `aria`, `role`, `accessib`, `caret`, `screen reader`, `contenteditable`, `B464049`, `B1392`, `B316`–`B320`: **B464049** is a focus-vs-error COLOUR collision and **B1392** owns the keyboard-trap escape that rides this element's accessible name — neither is about how the editing surface is exposed. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — shipped this session. 20/20 in `ui-audit/verify-notes-caret-a11y.mjs`, with a known-good arm.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **HIS REPORT:** *"Can you make it so that my cursor shows where it should… those little red marks are where my cursor goes. It's just an accessibility thing that I've added to my PC, but it doesn't seem to match very well on this module."* That is Windows 11's **Text cursor indicator**, which takes its rectangle from the accessibility layer and never from what is painted.
- **⛔ THE HYPOTHESIS IN THE BRIEF IS REFUTED, WITH MEASUREMENTS, AND THAT REFUTATION IS PART OF THE ANSWER.** It proposed that the boxes are CSS-`transform`-positioned, so Chrome would report their untransformed bounds. They are not: `computed transform: none` on every editing host, and painted geometry equals layout-tree geometry **to the pixel** at 80%, 100% and 200% zoom, scrolled and not (`diagnose-notes-caret-bounds`). The geometry this module controls was never wrong.
- **WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, dumped from the real accessibility tree:**

        note-title  →  role=textbox   editable=plaintext   multiline=false   ✅
        note-body   →  role=GENERIC   editable=richtext    multiline=—       ⛔

  The page title was a proper text control and the writing surface was not — a generic node that merely happens to be editable. **A generic node exposes no text pattern for a platform client to read a caret rectangle out of**, so the OS falls back to the bounds of the editable REGION, whose top-left corner is up and to the left of any box placed on the page. That is the direction he photographed, and it explains why the offset grows the further into the page the caret sits. Fix: `role="textbox"` + `aria-multiline="true"` (a textbox that does not say it is multiline is treated as a single-line field, whose caret rect is one line's geometry). Now `role=textbox editable=richtext multiline=true`.
- **⛔ THE HONEST LIMIT, stated rather than implied:** this repo runs on Linux and cannot read Windows' UI Automation. The harness proves the module now exposes a real multiline text control with a real caret, and that its painted and layout-tree geometry agree everywhere measured. It does NOT prove what Windows then draws. If he still sees the markers misplaced after this, the next step is his machine, not this code — and that is a `V###`-shaped question, not a null.
- **THE KNOWN-GOOD ARM IS THE PAGE TITLE** (DRIVER-SCROLL-IS-NOT-APP-SCROLL clause 6): it was already correct before the fix, so it is a value known independently of the code under test. If it ever stops reporting `textbox`, the harness is reading the tree wrongly and exits **2 as VACUOUS** rather than scoring the unknown arm.
- Files: `components/NoteEditor.jsx` (`editorProps.attributes`). Harnesses: `verify-notes-caret-a11y` (20), `diagnose-notes-caret-bounds` (the geometry refutation).

### B583010 — Pressing Enter dropped the formatting of the line above — both the block attributes AND the inline marks `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(owner chat 2026-08-15, NEW-1. Minted **B583010** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `Enter`, `splitBlock`, `splitListItem`, `inherit`, `storedMarks`, `deriveBlockSizes`, `B532640`, `B532641`, `B532642`, `B36051`, `B291536`: **B532641** ADDED the block-level font size he suspected and is Done and correct — this is a hole that change opened rather than a defect in it, and `notesBlockKeys` owns BACKSPACE at a block boundary, not Enter. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — shipped this session. 38/38 in `ui-audit/audit-notes-enter-inherit.mjs`.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **HIS REPORT:** *"it doesn't seem like when I start a new line, it carries the formatting (at least the text size of what's directly above it)."* **He called the cause and was right about the mechanism** — ProseMirror asks `defaultBlockAt` for the new node when the caret is at the END of a block, and a default block has default attributes by definition.
- **AND IT WAS WORSE THAN HE THOUGHT — BOTH TIERS WERE LOST, not just the block one.** Measured before a line was written: block `fontSize` 22 → null · run `fontSize` 22px → null · marks `bold+textStyle` → none · colour `#B8418C` → null.
- **THE SHAPE IS WHY IT READ AS INTERMITTENT:** a split in the MIDDLE keeps everything and a split at the START keeps everything. Only a split at the END loses it — which is the one people do constantly.
- **⛔ AND THE FIX WAS COMPLETE AND COMPLETELY INVISIBLE UNTIL TWO THINGS STOPPED UNDOING IT.** The handler ran, the chain returned `true`, and the attributes were still null. `deriveBlockSizes` (B532641's housekeeping pass) runs one transaction later, saw a brand-new **EMPTY** block, decided its runs disagreed, and wrote `null` over the size the split had just inherited — while ProseMirror cleared `storedMarks` in the same breath. So an empty block now KEEPS the size it was given, and the pass hands the stored marks back. **A pass that only means to adjust a block attribute must not also decide what the next keystroke looks like.** Found by probing whether the handler ran at all, rather than by re-reading it.
- **A THIRD DEFECT IN THE SAME FAMILY, found by the same harness:** `hardBreak` was counted as an unsized run, so **Shift+Enter** silently reset its own paragraph's line box to the default height while every word kept its size — a formatting bug wearing a spacing bug's clothes.
- **THE EXCEPTION HE NAMED IS PRESERVED AND ASSERTED IN THE SAME RUN:** Enter on an EMPTY list item still leaves the list. The rule declines for that case, for a range split, for a caret that is not at the end, and for a code block — so everything it does not claim behaves exactly as before.
- **TWO OF THE HARNESS'S OWN CASES WERE INSTRUMENT BUGS AND ARE RECORDED AS SUCH:** a positioned box takes TWO presses (press 1 selects, press 2 puts the caret in), and the list case could not prove it had reached the empty item until it was driven the way a person actually does it (Enter, Enter).
- Files: `lib/notesEnterInherit.js` (new — the pure decision + the handler), `lib/notesExtensions.js` (registration at priority 200, the empty-block skip, the stored-marks hand-back, the `hardBreak` skip). Tests: `notesEnterInherit` (12). Harness: `audit-notes-enter-inherit` (38).

### B561520 — Schedule health automation: an ordered list of rules, not three fixed toggles `[Schedule]` (feature) #scheduler #ui  *(owner report, verbatim: "the automation should be kinda more customizable too. right now it's kinda just got three options, but the intent was for it to act more like Smartsheet or Microsoft Project where I can pick what makes something get marked red." `✅` **Done — shipped this session. 381/381 in `test/schedulerEngine.test.js` (44 new), full suite green, golden test zero-diff against the real production plan.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **STEP 1 MEASUREMENT, reported before any design work:** the automation lived in `public/sequence/index.html`'s `computeDisplayHealth`, gated by exactly **three** independent boolean toggles in `settings.cfRules` (`AutomationPanel`, three `Toggle` rows) — `overdueRed` (end date passed + <100% complete → red, excluding a task already green/paused/red), `dueSoonYellow` (not-started + due within 7 calendar days → yellow), `completeGreen` (≥100% → green, unconditional). Confirmed the owner's "three options" count exactly. Pulled the REAL production document (`planar_data.hs-v1`, Supabase project `lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi`) via the Supabase MCP: 738 tasks / 6 projects, `cfRules: {overdueRed: true}` only — the other two toggles have **never been turned on** for any of his real plans.
- **THE ENGINE:** `HEALTH_CONDITIONS` — a finite, 7-entry vocabulary (`finishPastDays(N)`, `finishWithinDays(N)`, `finishToday`, `notStarted`, `predecessorLate`, `noOwner`, `complete`), each a pure fact-check on a leaf task, no formula parser, no composer. `settings.healthRules` is an ordered `{id,type,days?,color}[]`; `evalHealthRules` walks it top-down, first match wins. `getHealthRules` prefers a plan's own `healthRules`; absent that, `migrateCfRulesToHealthRules(cfRules)` derives the EXACT old 3-toggle behavior live (never persisted), so an existing plan's automation keeps behaving exactly as before until the owner touches the new editor.
- **STEP 3.A — MANUAL OVERRIDE, the highest-risk regression named in the brief.** New per-task `healthOverride` flag. `computeDisplayHealth` checks it FIRST and, if set, returns the raw stored `health` — skipping the rule engine AND the meeting-bound/deadline-row risk blocks (an override beats every kind of automation, not just the new one). Set automatically by `updateTask` whenever `health` is written directly (StatusPicker, the grid/master-view cell, the right-click menu, and the health-cascade-to-descendants path when a parent's color is bulk-applied to its children); cleared by picking the new **"Automatic"** entry (⚡, sentinel `AUTO_HEALTH`) now at the top of every status picker (`HealthPicker`, `StatusPicker`, `HealthDropMenu`). A locked task shows a small gray ring badge (`OverrideBadge`) at the corner of its status dot. Survives a reload: `normalizeToV9` seeds the flag ONCE (idempotent via `_v9`), only for a task where it's `undefined` — a value the user later clears to `false` is never re-derived from `health` on a later load. Mutation-proven three ways (removed the override check, removed the per-task `=== undefined` guard, removed the `predecessorLate` null-map guard — each demonstrated red before being reverted).
- **STEP 3.B — DEFAULTS REPRODUCE TODAY'S BEHAVIOR EXACTLY, proven against the real plan, not a fixture.** `ui-audit/stress/golden-health-migration.mjs` runs the OLD `computeDisplayHealth` (copied verbatim, frozen) and the NEW engine over every one of the 528 real leaf tasks in the pulled production snapshot, under the plan's actual `cfRules`. **Zero differences.** (The one theoretical divergence — old `completeGreen` recolored even a green/red/paused task unconditionally, the new override skips it — was checked against the real data: one `paused`+100%-complete task exists, but `completeGreen` has never been enabled on any real plan, so the combination that would differ has never fired. Documented, not silently papered over.)
- **STEP 3.C — ABSENCE NEVER WEARS THE COSTUME OF AN ANSWER.** Every date/predecessor condition explicitly fails (never silently passes) on a missing `end`, `start`, or unresolved predecessor — asserted with dated-vs-undated task pairs side by side for all three (`finishPastDays`, `notStarted`, `predecessorLate`). **Group headers:** the engine is NEVER called on a parent/summary row — every real call site (GridView, GanttView, MasterView, Focus) branches `hasChildren`/`isSummary` before reaching it and shows `computeRolledHealth`'s worst-of-children result instead, which reads each child's RAW `.health`, never a rule-computed value — so B463072's stale-leftover trap (a parent's own `durValue`/`durUnit` vs. its rolled span) can't reach a health rule at all; asserted directly (a parent's rolled color reflects children's raw health, not what a rule would have computed) plus a source-text check pinning the branch.
- **ADJACENT CASES, all checked and asserted, none needing to be asked about:** milestones (duration-0, start===end) evaluate finish-date rules like any other leaf · a 100%-complete task can only ever match the `complete` condition (every date/owner condition gates on `<100%`, so a finished task can't light up as overdue or not-started) · a task with no dates at all + an empty rule list shows its raw stored health · reordering the SAME two rules for a task both would match flips the winner (`red` first vs. `yellow` first) — proving ordering, not a precedence table, is the whole mechanism.

### B557520 — A picture is a CANVAS OBJECT: dropped where you drop it, moved, resized from any edge or corner `[Notes]` (feature) #notes #ui #files #persistence  *(owner chat block 2026-08-15, NEW-1 — *"I feel like I should just be able to drop a picture in there and move it around, like, however I want to, like a proper canvas."* Minted **B557520** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B557520–B557535. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `image`, `picture`, `drop`, `canvas`, `noteAnchor`, `resize`, `handle`, `B1311`, `B391073`, `B400177`, `B434417`, `B539648`, `B539650`: **B1311** built the INLINE picture (an id in the document, the bytes in IndexedDB) and is Done — this is that picture becoming a POSITIONED object, which no item covered. **B539650** is the eight-handle ask and genuinely overlaps: this item DELIVERS it for picture boxes and delivers east/west for text boxes, so B539650 is NARROWED rather than duplicated — see its amended block below. Net-new number, deliberately.)*
`✅` **Done — shipped this session. 30/30 in `ui-audit/measure-notes-picture-canvas.mjs`, plus 77 unit checks.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **HIS ARCHITECTURAL INSTRUCTION IS THE WHOLE DESIGN, and it was followed rather than improved on:** *"the positioned anchor you already have is a box at an (x, y) with a width that happens to hold TEXT. Generalise it to hold CONTENT — text or an image. Then everything already built and hard-won comes free and stays consistent… A parallel 'image object' implementation would be a second copy of every bug we have spent two days finding once."* So there is still exactly ONE placed node and ONE placement command; press-to-place, the selection ring, the drag grip, Delete, the right-click menu, undo, the stored round trip, the sync and the tombstone cascade were all inherited, not rewritten.
- **WHAT LANDED:** a dropped file becomes a positioned box AT THE DROP POINT (several at once are staggered so none hides under another) · it keeps the picture's proportions on arrival · eight handles on a picture box, corners holding the ratio, edges stretching, **Shift inverting that**, left/top moving the anchor with the size · the same floors as a text box · Delete and the right-click menu remove it, with no × on the object · position and size survive a reload, ride the print sheet, and Markdown carries the picture and NAMES the lost placement.
- **⛔ THE DEFECT THAT MADE THE WHOLE FEATURE INERT, AND IT WAS ONE GUARD CLAUSE.** `NoteEditor.jsx` opened with `if (el.closest(".planyr-sketch-host, .planyr-note-image, .planyr-note-file")) return;` — correct when a picture could only ever be INLINE ("a picture is an object you select rather than page you write on"), and fatal the moment a picture can BE a box's content: every press on a picture box returned before the selection logic, so the box was never selected, and **every handle is gated on the selection**. All eight were painted, correctly positioned, correctly labelled, correctly cursored — and completely dead. **Every unit test passed and every DOM reading said the control was present and correct.** What said otherwise was eight harness rows reading `400×200 → 400×200`.
- **⛔ AND THE SECOND ONE, WHICH IS THE SAME SPECIES: `overflow: hidden` ON THE BOX CLIPS ITS OWN HANDLES.** They straddle the border box by design — that is what makes them grabbable — so clipping the anchor leaves them LAID OUT (a perfectly sensible 10px square, in a perfectly sensible place, which `getBoundingClientRect` will confirm) but not hit-testable: `elementFromPoint` at a handle's own centre answers the EDITOR. Clip the picture, never the frame. **Both are CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS inverted** — not chrome swallowing a press, but the box swallowing its own chrome — and neither is visible to anything short of a real mouse.
- **AND A THIRD FINDING, ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN THE APP:** the first right-edge leg aimed its drop at the SCROLLER's right edge and got no box at all. ProseMirror runs `posAtCoords` FIRST and returns before `handleDrop` when it is null, so a drop past the sheet is not a case the app can have. Written into the harness so nobody re-derives it. (This is trap 2 from `measure-notes-right-edge`'s own header — the sheet is not the canvas — arrived at from the other side, in a harness written by the session that had just read that warning.)
- **WHAT WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN INHERITED**, because four properties were true only by luck of an earlier design and an inherited property nobody has checked is a coincidence (`test/notesPictureCanvas.test.js`): the empty-box PRUNE must not eat a box holding no text (it does not — `anchorIsEmpty` is a whitelist, and this is exactly the "unknown must mean keep" case arriving) · the PURGE CASCADE must reach a picture nested one level deeper than any before it (`assetIdsInDoc` recurses) · Markdown must carry the picture AND name the lost position · and a note with no pictures in it must round-trip **byte-identical** (`h: null` renders nothing, so nothing migrates).
- **THE TRAPS IT DID NOT REPEAT, all named in the code:** the gesture commits its own record and never `dom.style` (B434417) · the attributes move with the style during a drag or the ResizeObserver fit undoes it in real time (B421490 ×2) · the node view tracks the LIVE node rather than the closure's (B400177, generalised from attrs to content) · a press that did not drag forwards to the box (B539652), now shared by all eight handles rather than the one that was reported.
- **PANEL-BREVITY:** not applicable — no yield/pond panel copy touched.
- Files: `lib/notesBoxResize.js` (new — the pure rule + the geometry constants, which MOVED here so a resize and a placement cannot hold two copies of the floor), `lib/notesAnchorNode.js` (the `h` attribute, `setNoteAnchorBox`, content-carrying placement, the eight-handle view), `lib/notesImageNode.js` (the positioned drop), `components/NoteEditor.jsx` (the guard clause, the image-box stage 2, the CSS), `lib/notesPrint.js` (PDF-PARITY, both DOM shapes). Tests: `notesBoxResize` (63, mutation-proven), `notesPictureCanvas` (14). Harness: `measure-notes-picture-canvas` (30).

### B548816 — The measurement did not render behind the markup; it rendered INTO it — two element classes shipped the same default colour `[Site Planner / markup]` (bug) #site-planner #markup #ui  *(owner report 2026-08-15, arriving as a seventh "layers are broken" and RETRACTED as such by the dispatcher before any code was touched. Minted **B548816** from this branch's reserved block B548816–B548831 against `origin/main` 8612b20. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `B421`, `B820`, `B671`, `B293072`, `B293073`, `B548064`, `behindEls`, `arrangeAcrossBands`, `send to back`, `z-order`, `#c2410c`, `ANNOT_STROKE`, `PAL.accent`: the whole layering lineage is about ORDER and none of it is about COLOUR; **#1066 (B548064–B548066) closed the markup-vs-building half two days ago and is NOT re-opened — it is working, and this run re-proves it.** Net-new.)*
`[x]` **⛔ THE RETRACTION IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THIS ITEM. "The measurement is behind the markup" was measured and is FALSE.** It is on top, it was always on top, and any fix that reordered anything would have been wrong. What is true:

        the measurement's default ink   PAL.accent   = #C2410C = rgb(194, 65, 12)
        the markup family's default FILL tools.matrix = #c2410c = rgb(194, 65, 12)

  Identical. A measurement is a 1.5px hairline plus a 10% tint, so painted over a solid slab of its own colour there is nothing left to see. **Camouflaged, not buried.**
- **⛔ WHY EVERY PROBE MISSED IT, THIS SESSION'S OWN INCLUDED.** `diagnose-band-ordering.mjs` seeds markups in deliberately loud colours (#c02020 red, #2020c0 blue) so it can tell them apart — and against those the measurement is perfectly legible. **Only the DEFAULT collides, which is to say only what a real user actually draws.** Same species as B820's four correct-but-wrong-case fixes: the fixture hid the defect. The new harness seeds a markup with NO colour for exactly this reason.
- **THE RULE, in the owner's words, now enforced rather than described:** an element whose job is to display a number must never be able to disappear into another element, and two different element classes must not share a default colour. `src/shared/theme/familyInk.js` is the one table; `test/familyInk.test.js` checks it **pairwise in CIEDE2000, not by string inequality** — #c2410c and #c3420d are also "different colours" and camouflage just as completely. Bar: **ΔE00 ≥ 10**, an order of magnitude over the classical JND, chosen before the candidates were measured.
- **THE NEW INK IS MAGENTA `#A21CAF`, and the obvious alternative was measured and REJECTED.** Doc Review already gives its measure kinds a teal ink (#0e7490) and adopting it here was the tidy answer — but teal sits **9.1 ΔE00 from the detention-pond stroke**, under the bar, and a measurement drawn around a pond is one of the commonest things on these plans. Trading one camouflage for another is not a fix. Magenta clears every element colour and every other annotation ink by ≥25 ΔE00, and is the traditional dimension colour on a civil sheet.
- The `accent` OPTION is **removed** from `measureStyle`, not merely un-passed: a caller handing it the app accent is the defect, and a silently-ignored option would let it walk back in. A measurement carrying its own colour keeps it — this is the fallback only.
- **Teeth, both directions:** the unit guard is re-run against the colour that actually shipped and must REJECT it; the live harness was run with the fix reverted (exit 1, "❌ CAMOUFLAGED", ΔE00 0.0) and with it in place (exit 0, ΔE00 42.8).
- Verify: live (V303184) — PDF-PARITY: the export clones the live SVG, so the sheet inherits the ink; the printed check is the pending half.

### B548818 — The measurement chip is sized by guesswork: measure the text `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(owner report 2026-08-15 — the plate is far wider than the text in it. `[x]` **The estimate was `widest line by CHARACTER COUNT × (fontSize × 0.6)` — two compounding errors.** A character count says "1" and "M" are the same width; 0.6 em overstates a face that draws figures at ~0.55 em. A chip full of digits is the worst case, which is why it was the one reported.

- Each line is measured at the size AND weight it is painted at — headline bold, name/detail at the subordinate size with its 0.02 em tracking. **Letter-spacing is real width and `measureText` does not report it**, so both measurers now add it; a measurer blind to it under-sizes exactly the lines that carry it.
- `test/labelWidthMeasured.test.js` includes the case a character count gets BACKWARDS rather than merely imprecise: six of the narrowest glyphs against three of the widest.

  > **When a user says a feature "never works" and it demonstrably works in the case you tested, YOU TESTED THE WRONG CASE.** The variable is never the command — it is what the command is being asked about. Go and find the case they are in. Do not close the loop on your own fixture.
  Two operational clauses come with it, because the rule on its own is a caution and cautions rot: **(a)** a live check must state a closure condition that someone other than the owner can meet, and a `V###` whose only stopping rule is a fact the owner holds is **mis-written, not blocked**; **(b)** a harness for a reported symptom carries a **PRECONDITION that refuses to report a score** unless the reported configuration is really present — the two in `verify-markup-over-building.mjs` are exactly that, and without them a tidy fixture reports PASS on a dead implementation.
- **RELATION TO THE EXISTING RULES, stated so this is not read as a duplicate.** ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK says a Claude-doable check may not be deferred; STANDING RULE #2 says an owner-reported symptom may not be closed on a null. Both were FOLLOWED here — V91632 was run, by the cohort, on his real plan, and it passed honestly. Neither rule asks the question this one does: **was the check pointed at the case that was reported?** That is why it is a third rule and not a clause on either.
- **GUARD.** `test/verificationClosability.test.js` sweeps `VERIFICATION.md` and fails on any active `V###` whose text defers its closure to the owner ("only he knows", "only Michael knows", "he'll have to tell us"…) without a named `Blocker:`. The sweep is proven on the real sentence: it is asserted to flag V91632's own wording verbatim.

### B539648 — The right edge CRUSHED a box to one character wide instead of letting the page grow `[Notes]` (bug, HIGH) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-14, with a screenshot of "High Voltage Planning Study" rendered ONE LETTER PER LINE against the right margin. **He named the cause as an instruction of his own**, which is recorded on this item rather than glossed. This is not a recurrence of either: both did what they promised, and the promise had no usable floor. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED, and measured with his own test.**
- Verify: sandbox — `ui-audit/measure-notes-right-edge.mjs` runs the sweep he specified; 11 unit cases in `test/notesAnchorZoom.test.js`.
- **HIS REPORT:** *"it's not letting me expand this box out to the right… it seems like there's a wall where when I go past it, it squeezes my text box down to where it's literally one character wide. And it's on the right side of the canvas."*
- **⛔ THE CAUSE, AND HE DIAGNOSED IT HIMSELF.** When the block used to JUMP LEFT away from the click he asked for *"if it will not fit, NARROW the block to the space available — do not slide it sideways."* **Right about not sliding, wrong about narrowing with no floor.** `ANCHOR_MIN_WIDTH` was **32 px** — about two characters at the note's own text size — so a press near the margin left a few pixels of room and the box was narrowed to them. The old comment on that constant actively defended the small number: *"a narrow column at the far edge is a choice he is allowed to make."* A column nobody can read or type in is not a choice; it is the failure.
- **THE FIX, in three parts, and it mirrors what the page already did VERTICALLY.** (a) The floor is **160 px** — about twenty characters, close to the 180 default, and written down with its reasoning. (b) **`anchorExtentX`**, the horizontal twin of `anchorExtent`: past the floor the block does not narrow, **the page grows to the right and scrolls**. Its absence WAS the bug — vertically the sheet had always stretched to hold a block past the bottom, horizontally there was no equivalent, so the only way to keep a block on the sheet was to squeeze it. (c) The resize drag is **no longer capped at the page edge** — pulling right grows the page instead of stopping dead.
- **HIS TEST, VERBATIM, AND ITS RESULT.** *"place a box at increasing x across the full width in small steps and assert the stored width never drops below the floor, and that beyond the floor the scrollable canvas width increases instead."* Measured across 17 steps: rendered width **180 → 172 → 160 and never below**; the canvas held at 1232 while the box fit and then grew **1257 → 1333 → 1421 → 1509 → 1597**; the **left edge was kept at every single step**. His screenshot's case now wraps into **~2 lines instead of ~27**. Dragging the handle rightward: stored width **180 → 660**, canvas **1232 → 1257**.
- **⛔ HIS ORIGINAL ACCEPTANCE TEST IS UNTOUCHED AND STILL PASSES**, which is what makes this safe: *"assert stored left equals click x minus editor left, for EVERY step. No clamping band anywhere."* Raising the floor spends the PAGE's width, never the block's position.
- **⛔ AND A FEEDBACK LOOP I CREATED AND THEN CLOSED, recorded because it SETTLED rather than oscillated.** The first version measured the available room from `dom.clientWidth` — the very element the extent then widens. The fit narrowed a box to the room, the extent widened the editor to hold it, the next measure read the wider editor as "the room"… It converged on a stable wrong number, which is worse than failing, because it looks correct. The denominator is now the SCROLLER's width, which is the one thing in the chain a box cannot change.
- **⛔ AND THREE INSTRUMENT ERRORS BEFORE THE HARNESS COULD BE BELIEVED**, all of them TRAPS.md trap 2 (the wrong baseline): it found the scroller by an inline-style substring and matched an outer wrapper that cannot scroll; it then compared the box against the SHEET's right edge when growth is only owed past the VISIBLE CANVAS; and it started the drag case too far from the edge for a drag to need any room. All three reported correct behaviour as broken.

### B539651 — A real right-click menu, and no delete button on selection `[Notes]` (bug/feature) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-14, NEW-3. Minted **B539651**. DEDUPE-FIRST: **B434416/B434418** built the two-stage selection and moved the controls OFF hover onto selection — this changes what selection reveals and what right-click offers; **B1367** is the RAIL's row menu, a different surface. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED — driven with real right-clicks, judged on the STORED document (26/26).**
- Verify: sandbox — `ui-audit/verify-notes-context-menu.mjs`.
- **WHAT SHIPPED.** The delete × is **gone from the box entirely** — selecting a box shows the ring and the resize handle and nothing destructive. Delete/Backspace still removes it. **Right-clicking a box** offers `Delete this box`, last and separated because it is the destructive one. **Right-clicking the document** gives Word's menu: cut · copy · the three paste modes · bold · italic · underline · strikethrough · bullets · numbering · increase/decrease indent · link. A box's menu is **the document's plus its own action**, because right-clicking a box is still right-clicking inside text.
- **THE ITEMS ARE A TABLE, NOT MARKUP**, which is what lets the two contexts be one component rather than two menus that drift apart. Every row cancels `mousedown`: a menu that steals the selection cannot act on it, and the failure is SILENT — the command runs against an empty range and looks like a dead button.

- **MEASURED, not asserted:** Underline from the menu reaches the stored document · Bullets from the menu reaches the stored document · the document menu offers no `delete-box` while the box menu does · `Delete this box` removes it from storage · **and Ctrl+Z brings it back**, because focus comes home after the delete (the B421489 trap).

And then the right click should have the normal formatting option, like it's a Word document or an email… Just copy Word."*
- **THE SCOPE:** selecting a box shows the ring and the resize handles and **no delete ×** · Delete/Backspace still deletes · right-click on a box offers Delete plus its text formatting · right-click in the document gives a Word/Outlook-style menu — cut, copy, paste (the three paste modes already exist), bold, italic, underline, font, size, colour, highlight, bullets and numbering, indent and outdent, link.
- **THE STOPPING RULE IT CLOSED ON:** the delete × gone from selection · both menus driven by a real right-click in a harness · every item asserted against the STORED document. All three met.


### B539652 — ⛔ FOUND WHILE FIXING B539648: clicking into an existing box puts the words in the WRONG box `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(found 2026-08-14 by running the owner's own acceptance harness `verify-notes-anchor-zoom` §10 while landing B539648. **PRE-EXISTING — proven, not assumed:** the same check fails identically on a build with B539648's changes stashed out, so this is a finding rather than a regression. Minted **B539652**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `two-stage`, `anchor`, `handle`, `B434416`, `B434418`, `B391073`, `CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS`: **B434418** moved the box's controls off hover onto SELECTION, which is what makes press 2 land on a control that press 1 summoned. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED — and his acceptance harness is 40/40 for the first time.**
- Verify: sandbox — `ui-audit/verify-notes-anchor-zoom.mjs` §10 is the repro and is red today.
- **THE MEASUREMENT.** Type into box A, then box B, then box A again, entering each with the two-stage press. The markers come back `["2","3"]` — the second and third both landed in the wrong block.
- **⛔ IT IS AN INSTANCE OF A NAMED RULE — CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS, clause 4: chrome mounted by the FIRST press is invisible to any check that reads the DOM before the interaction.** Press 1 selects the box, which is what REVEALS the resize handle (B434418 moved the controls off hover onto selection); press 2, at the same point, then lands on a handle that did not exist when the gesture began. The harness aims at the bottom-right corner, which is exactly where that handle appears.
- **THE FIX IS AT THE RESOLVER, NOT ON THE OBJECT (clause 5).** A handle is chrome belonging to its box, so **a press on it that did not DRAG is transparent** — it forwards to the box and puts the caret where it landed, which is what press 2 was always for. A press that DID drag is a resize and is untouched. The handle keeps its own gesture; it just stops swallowing the one gesture it was never meant to take. This also preserves the existing rule that a press which never moved writes nothing.
- **RESULT:** `verify-notes-anchor-zoom` **40/40** — the owner's own acceptance harness fully green for the first time.

### B539653 — ⛔ MY OWN ARROW-KEY GATE SILENCED THE SECOND ESCAPE, so a box could not be deselected from the keyboard `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(found 2026-08-14 by `verify-notes-box-selection` while landing B539651 — six rows across three window sizes. **A REGRESSION IN B519681**, which shipped earlier the same session. `[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED. Caused by me, in the fix for his arrow-key report.**
- Verify: sandbox — `ui-audit/verify-notes-box-selection.mjs`, 91/91.
- **THE DEFECT.** B519681 made every global binding in the module decline while there is a live caret in editable text — correct, and correct in **the two states that were measured**. The two-stage box gesture has a THIRD state nobody measured: Escape #1 backs out of editing, Escape #2 deselects — and **after #1 the editor still HOLDS FOCUS**. Measured at every step: `activeElement` is the ProseMirror div, `isContentEditable` true. So the gate declined Escape #2 and the box could never be deselected from the keyboard.
- **⛔ THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THE FIX WAS WRONG AND THE HARNESS SAID SO.** It assumed the blur had landed and only required focus to be inside the selection's own host. It changed nothing, because focus never left. **Reasoning about the state twice cost two builds; probing it took one.**
- **THE RULE:** the gate exists so a binding cannot steal a key the person typing NEEDS. **Escape is not one of those** — a caret has no use for it — so it is named in `UNGATED_KEYS` and never gated. Every key the caret DOES want is still gated in that same state, asserted both ways.
- **⛔ IT DOES NOT REOPEN B434418's "HANDLED TWICE":** that defect was Escape running in the mat AND the window binding, and the mat's call was deleted then. There is still exactly one handler; this only stops the gate from silencing it.

### B519680 — ⛔ REGRESSION IN B512672: Shift+Tab moved an ANCESTOR, so one keypress dragged whole branches the user never touched `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-14, WITH A SCREENSHOT, on his live MUD 377 note. Minted **B519680** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B519680–B519695 against origin/main 55dcdb5. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `Tab`, `indent`, `outdent`, `sinkListItem`, `liftListItem`, `nodesBetween`, `B512672`, `B454480`, `B1392`, `B291536`.** **B512672** is the change that introduced this, shipped in #1050 roughly an hour before he hit it — this is a REGRESSION IN it, filed on its own number rather than as a recurrence because B512672's own promise (Tab indents a first item) is correct and shipped; what is broken is which items the command applies to. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED. Caused by me, in the change that merged an hour before he reported it.**
- Verify: sandbox — reproduced and fixed against a browser-driven fixture built from his screenshot (`ui-audit/diagnose-notes-outdent.mjs`), plus five depth cases in `test/notesListIndent.test.js`. Mutation-proven.
- **HIS REPORT, verbatim:** *"I'm trying to press shift tab to promote MUD ATTORNEY: BRIAN YATES, that line. I'm trying to promote it to the left, but it takes Dustin O'Neal, the phone number, and the email with it."*
- **⛔ THE TELL, AND IT IS THE THING THAT NAMES THE BUG.** Dustin O'Neal and its two children are not MUD ATTORNEY's DESCENDANTS — they are its NEPHEWS, sitting under a sibling branch. A lift capturing preceding siblings or following siblings cannot produce that. **Only an ANCESTOR moving can**, because an ancestor takes its entire subtree, including branches above and beside the pressed line. He was right that the screenshot alone could not distinguish the three candidate bugs, and right to demand the document diff.
- **THE CAUSE, one line.** `itemsInSelection` asked `doc.nodesBetween(from, to)` for every `listItem`. **`nodesBetween` visits every node whose range CONTAINS the position** — so a collapsed caret in a level-three bullet returns that bullet AND its parent AND its grandparent, and the command moved all of them.
- **MEASURED, before any fix** (`diagnose-notes-outdent`, his exact four-level outline including the smaller font on "Dustin O'Neal" that he flagged): Tab on **"Active"** — one line, caret collapsed — produced `Active [indent=1]` **and `MUD 377 [indent=1]`**. One keypress, two items, one of them a parent nobody pressed on.
- **THE FIX: an item moves when the selection is inside ITS OWN text, not merely somewhere beneath it.** The walk collects TEXTBLOCKS in the range and maps each to its NEAREST indentable ancestor. A collapsed caret yields exactly one item; a range across two bullets yields both; a range genuinely spanning a parent's text and its child's text yields both, which is right because both lines were selected. **STRUCTURE ONLY, NEVER GEOMETRY** — he asked for that explicitly, having noticed the odd line out carries a smaller font; nothing in this path reads a rendered size, position or box.
- **⛔ AND THE COVERAGE HOLE THAT LET IT SHIP, which is the more useful finding.** All 17 cases in `test/notesListIndent.test.js` passed **before and after** the fix. Every one used a FLAT list, where an item has no indentable ancestor — so the bug was unreachable by construction and the suite could not tell the broken build from the fixed one. **Depth was the variable that mattered and nothing had any.** Five nested cases added; mutation-proven (restoring the old walk turns 2 red).
- **THE MIRROR CASES he asked for, all measured on his structure and all correct:** Shift+Tab on an item WITH children (they follow, attached, nothing else moves) · on an item with following siblings (they stay) · on the last item of a nested list · on the first item of a nested list · his own case · and Tab as the inverse, with the indent/outdent round-trip **byte-identical**.

### B532640 — "Single" line spacing was 1.65, so the control looked inert and nothing could be made compact `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-14, measured on his live Richfield "Utilities" note. Minted **B532640–B532642** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, from this branch's reserved block B532640–B532655 against origin/main d4a88a0. **DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `spacing`, `line-height`, `lineHeight`, `notesSpacing`, `density`, `compact`, `B391076`, `B823`.** **B391076** built the per-paragraph spacing control and is the direct ancestor — it shipped the control, and this is the finding that its DEFAULT was the loosest option it offered, which no case in it could have caught. Not a recurrence: that item's promise (a working per-paragraph control) is intact. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED.**
- Verify: sandbox — measured before and after with `ui-audit/measure-notes-spacing.mjs`, which reports rendered row heights rather than computed properties.
- **HIS REPORT:** *"you see how I made some text smaller? I was hoping to just make the spacing smaller so I can save space and see more information on screen. I put this on single line spacing. It gets this default single line spacing. So I'm not really sure. Is this a line spacing issue?"*
- **MEASURED, and he was right on both counts.** 15px text in a **24.75px** line box — a ratio of **1.65**, where Word and OneNote call roughly **1.15** single. So the loosest setting in the control's own list was ALSO its default, and picking "Single" changed nothing because he was already on it. **A control whose default option is the loosest one it offers reads as inert**, which is exactly what he experienced.
- **THE SCALE IS REBASED so the names mean what they say:** `Default` (the note's density) · **`Single` = 1.15, and it is now the tightest** · `1.15` → 1.3 · `1.5` · `Double` = 2.0. Every named value above Single is asserted to be looser than it, so the list cannot go dishonest again.
- **MEASURED AFTER:** every ordinary row **24.75px → 17.25px**, a ratio of exactly 1.15. That is roughly **30% less vertical space per line**, which is the "see more information on screen" he asked for.
- **⛔ EXISTING NOTES REFLOW, DELIBERATELY, AND HE IS TOLD IN THE SESSION REPLY — he asked to be.** Every note written before today carries no explicit spacing, so it inherits the density and gets tighter the moment this ships. That is the decision: it is what he asked for ("must actually tighten his notes today"), it loses no content, and it is reversible per-note and per-paragraph. **The alternative was refused:** stamping 1.65 onto every existing paragraph to freeze them would write a setting nobody chose into thousands of blocks and leave him unable to tighten an old note without re-selecting all of it.
- **PDF-PARITY.** The number lives once, as `SINGLE` in `lib/notesSpacing.js`. The editor takes it through a custom property; the print sheet **interpolates the literal**, because paper has no theme and `test/notesRoundTwo.test.js` rightly forbids a CSS custom property in the sheet.

### B532641 — Line height was pinned to the block's own font, so smaller text did not make a shorter row `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-14, the half underneath B532640 and the thing he was actually trying to do. Minted **B532641** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST: same search as B532640; **B391076** owns the control, **B1371** put font size on the toolbar row. Neither is "the row does not shrink". Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED.**
- Verify: sandbox — `ui-audit/measure-notes-spacing.mjs`, row heights before and after, plus 6 pure cases in `test/notesSpacing.test.js`.
- **HIS REQUIREMENT:** *"Measured: 15px text in a 24.75px line box. Expected: the line box scales with the text, so a smaller run or a smaller paragraph produces a shorter row and he actually saves space."*
- **⛔ THE CAUSE, AND THE CSS LOOKED CORRECT THE WHOLE TIME — which is why nobody found it by reading.** The stylesheet already used a proportional multiplier. The size a person picks lands on an **inline span**, while the **block** stays at the default 15px — and a block's line box can never be shorter than its own font's **strut**. Measured: a paragraph whose every word was set to 11px rendered at **24.75px**, exactly as tall as the 15px paragraph above it. **Bigger text grew the row (a 22px run made it 36.3px); smaller text could not shrink it.** Asymmetric, and invisible to the CSS.
- **THE FIX: the block carries its own size when its runs all agree.** `blockFontSize` is the pure decision — every run at one size wins; any unsized run, or two different sizes, returns null. It is applied by `deriveBlockSizes` as an **`appendTransaction`**, so it holds for EVERY document rather than only for text typed after today — which matters, because the smaller text he was looking at was already there.
- **MEASURED AFTER, and it satisfies all three of his sub-requirements:** a whole paragraph at 11px → row **17.25 → 12.64px**, where in proportion it would be 12.65 · **mixed sizes on one line: tallest run wins** (22px + 9px → 25.3px, block unchanged) · **lists follow the same rule** (a small list item shrank identically). Headings and positioned boxes take the same line-height.
- **IT IS IDEMPOTENT, which is the loop guard rather than a counter:** `deriveBlockSizes` returns false when every block already agrees with its runs, and `appendTransaction` returning null ends the round.

### B532642 — A one-click Compact density for a whole note `[Notes]` (feature) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-14, NEW-3 — his actual goal, in his words "save space and see more information on screen". - **ONE ACTION FOR THE WHOLE NOTE.** `Whole note: Comfortable` / `Whole note: Compact`, first in the spacing menu because it is the thing he actually wants — per-paragraph controls make him do it a line at a time. One choice moves the line height AND the gap between list items together.
- **⛔ THE DECISION THAT MADE IT SAFE, AND IT REVERSED THE DEFERRAL ON THIS ITEM: THE DENSITY LIVES ON THE DOCUMENT, NOT ON THE TREE.** This item was first filed as deferred, on the stated ground that it needed a per-note stored field — the tree schema, `migratePageNode` and the cloud merge — which is precisely what caused **B342996 ×3** the same day (a new per-node field `migratePageNode` silently destroyed on every read). **That reasoning was examined again rather than accepted, and it was wrong about the mechanism:** a `doc`-node attribute set through ProseMirror's own `setDocAttribute` rides the DOCUMENT, which this module's own stated principle says is saved, synced, printed and exported for free. It touches no tree code at all, so the risk that justified deferring simply does not exist on that path. **A blocker that dissolves when you check it was never a blocker.**
- **MEASURED, end to end:** a row **17.25 → 15.30px** on picking Compact · **15.30px after a full reload**, so it persists with the note · the printed sheet carries the compact line height and **no CSS custom property** (paper has no cascade to inherit from).

Both print call sites pass it — the editor's from the note's own document, and a branch print from the ROOT note's, because one sheet has one line height and the root is the note the person asked to print.
- **GUARDS:** 5 cases in `test/notesSpacing.test.js` — the two members and which is tighter, Comfortable being exactly `SINGLE` so the two names cannot drift apart, an unknown id RENDERING rather than throwing (a stored document must always open), the default being a real member, and `densityStyle` handing out both numbers together.

### B512673 — The three harness traps that keep coming back, written down `[Infra / CI · testing]` (task) #testing #infra  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13, in the same message as B512672: "Worth a short note in the repo about the ones that are reusable traps: reads landing before the save, comparing against the wrong baseline, and picking the option that means 'do nothing'." Minted **B512673** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `harness`, `trap`, `debounce`, `baseline`, `instrument`, `FOREGROUND-OR-VOID`, `SYNTHETIC-KEYS-DONT-EDIT`, `B1439`, `B454481`: the two named RULES in `CLAUDE.md` cover their own traps and are cross-referenced rather than repeated; nothing on the board is the short reference note itself. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **⛔ SHIPPED — `ui-audit/TRAPS.md`.**
- Verify: sandbox (it is a document)
- **WHY IT IS WORTH A FILE.** All three share one shape: **the harness was wrong, and its output looked exactly like a product finding.** A crash costs ten minutes; a plausible wrong answer gets written onto a backlog item and acted on. Between them these three produced **43 false findings in one session** — 16 from reads racing the 600 ms save debounce, 11 from the wrong baseline, and the rest from a null verdict nobody had split into its causes.

### B391074 — A page title could not be edited: it re-applied itself as you backspaced `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #ui  *(owner chat block, 2026-08-12 — NEW-3, with the exact question asked: at what character count does it snap back, and does it restore the default or the previous value. `[x]` **✅ DONE 2026-08-12**

- Origin: filed 2026-08-12 from chat.
- **THE ANSWERS TO HIS TWO QUESTIONS.** It snaps back at **zero non-whitespace characters** — not earlier — and it restores **the DEFAULT**, "Untitled page", never the previous value.
- **THE CAUSE.** `renameNode` coerced a blank name to the default, and the title field is a CONTROLLED input that writes on every keystroke. So deleting the last character wrote "Untitled page" straight back and the field re-rendered with all thirteen characters restored. There was no way to clear it.
- **THE FIX IS WHERE THE DEFAULT LIVES.** `renameNode` stores what it is given, including nothing; `commitTitle` applies the default when the field is LEFT (blur, Enter, or Tab into the page); the rail shows a dimmed placeholder for a page that is momentarily unnamed and **never writes it back**. A blank title is a legal momentary state and costs nothing — since B342992 a title is never load-bearing for identity or reachability.
- **THE GUARD WAS AMENDED RATHER THAN DELETED.** "No exported op can mint a titleless node" now reads "a page may be blank WHILE YOU TYPE and may never SETTLE blank", and asserts all three: the rename may leave it empty, the commit fills it, and the rail never shows it empty.

Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE 2026-08-13 — a bridge run that comes back with fewer described paths is REFUSED, at the point the loss happens, and the guard is mutation-proven against the real PR #978 data. `Verify: sandbox`.**
- Verify: sandbox — a merge-resolution guard with no runtime surface; unit suite + the mutation runs are the whole proof.
- Origin: the owner's instruction, 2026-08-13, verbatim: *"assert the description count never decreases across a bridge run, and mutation-check that guard — break it deliberately, confirm red, say what the mutation was."*
- **⛔ WHY THE FIX ALONE WAS NOT ENOUGH, which is the owner's point and it is correct.** B384432 corrected the seed, but the failure it replaced was **SILENT**: the bridge printed `✅ … MAP.md (regenerated)` while dropping 48 of `main`'s one-liners, and only an unrelated `--check` in a later step noticed. A future change to `build-map.mjs`'s preservation, to the `- **\`path\`** — desc` line format, or to the seed re-opens exactly that hole **with the report still green**. That is the blind-instrument class sitting inside the fix for it.
- **THE GUARD: `lostDescriptions(ours, theirs, result)`, wired as a POST-CONDITION** in the same shape as the script's existing duplicate-id rollback — check the RESULT, and refuse rather than report a success it did not earn (LOUD-FAILURE). On a loss the ledgers are restored, nothing is staged, and the message names the file and the paths.
- **⛔ THE PRECISION THAT STOPS IT BEING A NUISANCE.** A path legitimately vanishes when the merge DELETED or RENAMED that file, and the fresh scan is right to drop it. So the check is scoped to paths the regenerated file **STILL LISTS** — described before, present now, `TODO — describe` now. That is exactly the PR #978 shape (all 48 files still existed; only their descriptions were gone) and it cannot fire on a deletion.
- **⛔ MUTATION-PROVEN TWICE, AND THE FIRST ONE IS AGAINST REAL DATA RATHER THAN A CONSTRUCTED CASE.**
  - **Mutation A — restore the pre-fix seed.** Driving `lostDescriptions` over the two ACTUAL `MAP.md` sides of the PR #978 merge (ours `d0728b1`, theirs `651849d`): `git checkout --ours` → **48 lost, guard RED**; the union seed → **0 lost, guard GREEN**. The 48 matches the count measured live when the defect was found, so the guard reports precisely the real failure.
  - **Mutation B — drift the line format** (`- **\`path\`**` → `- **ZZZ\`path\`**`), simulating `build-map.mjs` changing its output shape. **2 tests RED**, including the anti-rot check. This is the mutation that matters most: with a drifted regex `lostDescriptions` returns `[]` for everything and the guard becomes a permanent green that can never fail. Restoring the regex → 22/22 green.
- **⛔ AND THE ANTI-ROT CHECK IS PART OF THE GUARD, NOT AN EXTRA.** `parses the REAL committed MAP.md` asserts the parser finds >400 descriptions in the real artefact with zero TODOs, so a format change **reddens** the guard instead of silently disarming it. A guard nobody has seen fail is a guard that rots green (VIEW-INDEPENDENT-ONCE §6, same failure mode).
- **The real-data mutation is deliberately NOT committed as a test.** CI checks out at depth 1 and could not reach `d0728b1` / `651849d`, so a history-dependent test would pass **vacuously** — the exact rot this guard exists to prevent. The committed cases are its structural mirror; the real numbers are recorded here.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `test/resolveLedgers.test.js` **22 green** (+5): the PR #978 shape reported, the union seed green on the same two inputs, the deleted-file case that must NOT fire, the TODO-on-both-sides case, and the anti-rot parse. Lint 0 errors.
- Files: `scripts/resolve-ledgers.mjs`, `test/resolveLedgers.test.js`.

### B384432 — The ledger bridge SEEDED A GENERATED FILE FROM ONE SIDE and dropped 48 of main's MAP.md descriptions `[Infra / CI]` (bug) #infra #testing  *(found 2026-08-13 while unsticking PR #978 on the owner's instruction — the bridge's FIRST outing on a PR it did not author, which is exactly what he asked it to be tested as. Minted **B384432** from this branch's reserved block B384432–B384447 against freshly-fetched `origin/main` 651849d. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `resolve-ledgers`, `B296224`, `MAP.md`, `build-map`, `--ours`, `checkout --ours`, `generated`, `doc-pointer`, `mapDrift`, `B779`, `B780`, `B290251`: **net-new, and deliberately NOT a B296224 recurrence.** B296224 is the CONFLICT RATE and its bridge is the remedy; this is a data-loss defect INSIDE that shipped remedy, in the half — the generated pair — that B296224's own text called the part that "cannot be got wrong by concatenation". Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE 2026-08-13 — a generated file is now regenerated from a seed built out of BOTH merge sides, so no side's preserved, hand-authored content can be dropped. `Verify: sandbox`.**
- Verify: sandbox — a merge-resolution script with no runtime surface; the unit suite plus the live PR #978 measurement is the whole proof.
- Origin: found 2026-08-13 while carrying out the owner's ITEM 2 ("use the bridge and report whether it works"); fixed the same session.
- **⛔ THE DEFECT IN ONE LINE: "GENERATED" WAS READ AS "FULLY DERIVED", AND IT IS NOT.** Step 3 of the bridge ran `git checkout --ours` on `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` and `MAP.md` before regenerating them. `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` really is a pure function of `BACKLOG.md`, so the seed is irrelevant there. **`MAP.md` is not** — it carries a hand-authored one-line responsibility per path, and `build-map.mjs` PRESERVES those by parsing the copy already on disk. Seeding that parse from ONE side therefore discards every description the other side wrote.
- **THE MEASUREMENT, on a real PR rather than a constructed case.** PR #978 had sat four days; the test-merge against `main` was the pure ledger-only pattern the bridge was built for — `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` and `MAP.md` the only two conflicts, `BACKLOG.md` / `VERIFICATION.md` / `SitePlanner.jsx` / the tests all auto-merging, **zero source conflicts**. The bridge ran and reported `✅ Resolved 0 ledger file(s) … MAP.md (regenerated)`. **`node scripts/build-map.mjs --check` then went RED: 48 files that `main` describes came back as `TODO — describe`.** A merge the bridge had just declared resolved would have gone red in CI, and the 48 one-liners another session wrote would have been silently gone — which is the precise failure the script's own header says it exists to be incapable of.
- **THE FIX: `seedGenerated()` — the seed is BOTH SIDES CONCATENATED, theirs then ours.** Correct because the generator rebuilds the file from a FRESH SCAN and reads the seed only for its preserved-content map, keyed by path, so a path appearing twice costs nothing. Order is theirs-then-ours because that map is last-write-wins: a path both sides describe keeps OURS, the branch's own wording for its own file. `seedSide()` strips conflict markers and drops `TODO — describe` lines, so an undescribed side cannot clobber a described one. When the stages are gone (already staged, or a re-run) it recovers the two sides from `HEAD` / `MERGE_HEAD` instead of quietly seeding from a half-written file.
- **⛔ THE DISTINCTION THAT MUST SURVIVE: the seed is an INPUT to the generator, never the committed output.** Concatenation is safe precisely because nothing concatenated is kept — pinned by a test, since conflating the two is how a `MAP.md` with every path listed twice would get committed.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `test/resolveLedgers.test.js` **17 green** (+5): the one-side-only description (the PR #978 loss, directly), the TODO-clobber case, the ours-wins ordering, marker stripping, and the seed-is-not-output guard. **The mutation proof is the field measurement itself** — the pre-fix code was run against the real PR #978 merge and produced the 48-description loss above; the post-fix seed regenerates `MAP.md` at **505 files, 0 awaiting a description**, and `--check` passes.
- **PR #978's own merge was resolved with the corrected seed**, and its tree came out byte-identical to the resolution a concurrent session pushed independently — an accidental but real cross-check.
- **⛔ AND THE FIX ALONE WAS NOT ENOUGH — the PROPERTY is now asserted at runtime under `B384433`.** This item corrected the seed; nothing stopped it regressing silently. B384433 adds the post-condition (`lostDescriptions`) that REFUSES a run which comes back with fewer described paths, mutation-proven against the real PR #978 sides at 48-lost-before / 0-lost-after.
- Files: `scripts/resolve-ledgers.mjs`, `test/resolveLedgers.test.js`.

### B377888 — A stale delete re-applies onto elements CREATED after it, and ate the owner's truck court `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #sync  *(owner chat block 2026-08-12, arrived as NEW-1. Minted **B377888 / V173456** LATE via `--against-main` from this branch's reserved block B377888–B377903 against `origin/main` c219e4e; code, tests and commits keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `delete-reapplied`, `delete wins`, `B673` (the matrix itself), `B757`, `B812`, `B1115`, `B1116`, `B1117`, `B1120`, `B742`/`B743` (the delete no-op family) and `B1340`: **net-new.** B673 WROTE the matrix and this is the row it never had; B742/B743 are the opposite defect (a delete that does nothing); B757/B812 are self-echo identity, not delete arbitration. Not a recurrence of any of them.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE 2026-08-13 — V173456 PASSED on the owner's real eight-hour session: zero re-applied deletes, deletes perfectly paired, and the assembly now leaves as one atomic group. The `delete-vs-create` guard itself remains UNPROVEN IN FIELD and is marked so.**
- **✅ LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-13 — V173456 PASSED on eight hours of the owner's own work on Richfield / Concept A, read first-hand and read-only from `public.client_errors` + `public.site_elements` (nothing written).** Since 14:30Z: `element-delete-reapplied` **0** — the defect never fired again — and `delete-attempt`/`delete-outcome` **7 / 7**, perfectly paired, so no delete was lost between the two seams.
- **⛔ THE INVERSE OF THE ORIGINAL DEFECT, MEASURED.** At 16:19:33 one Delete keypress naming ONE id (`e1454939cgzlnc`) logged `removed:9, locked:0` — the host and all eight bonded children — and all nine rows carry the **IDENTICAL `deleted_at` 2026-08-12 16:19:33.33175**. One atomic group removal at a single microsecond, against the original bug's PARTIAL apply where 2 of 5 members died **1.1 s apart** in a race. The assembly now travels as a unit on the way out, which is the property **B1341** is chasing. It repeated three more times the same session — `22:38:23.479687` (10 rows), `22:39:54.189099` (1), `22:45:06.855268` (9) — each a whole group at one microsecond. Four group removals, zero partial applies.
- **⛔ WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED, and must not be rounded up (owner instruction, 2026-08-13).** `element-delete-vs-create-dropped` has **ZERO production rows**. That guard — the branch that drops a delete whose base predates the row's existence — is **DEPLOYED AND UNEXERCISED IN THE FIELD**, proven by `test/deleteVsCreate.test.js` and the conflict matrix, **not by a live save**. It proves itself the next time two tabs actually race. This item closes on the OBSERVED behaviour above, not on that guard having fired.
- Verify: live → **V173456** — concurrency / multi-writer is a mandatory LIVE class, and the repro cites real project data.
- Origin: filed 2026-08-12 from chat; shipped the same session.
- **THE MEASURED INCIDENT.** Two tabs on plan `smsdrvzr9gzx`. Tab A created a building assembly (host + 2 truck courts + 2 trailer rows). Tab B held a delete formed before those ids existed. Tab B's delete lost its CAS and `elementSync.js`'s *"delete WINS — re-issue at the fresh rev"* branch stripped the stale rev and re-issued against the NEW rows: at **13:38:49.543–546 three deletes were re-applied to rows 1.75 s old**, and `e1454940cgzlnc` and `e1454943cgzlnc` died.
- **⛔ THE RULE, and why "delete wins" is right and was still wrong here.** Delete-vs-EDIT is two writers disagreeing about a row that EXISTS, and removal is the less recoverable intent, so it is the one that should not need re-doing. Delete-vs-CREATE is not that: the delete is a decision about a row that no longer exists, and re-issuing it kills something it was never about. **A delete whose base rev predates the row's creation must be DROPPED, not re-issued.**
- **⛔ AND THE SIGNAL IS NOT THE ONE THE REPORT NAMED, which is worth recording because it changes the fix.** There is no `created_at` on `site_elements` and the RPC returns none, so "predates the row's creation" cannot be read off the wire. Two client-side observations replace it, and the SECOND is the one that catches the measured case:
  - **BY REV / BY CLOCK** — the tab saw the element come into existence (a live row for a key its shadow had never held) at a rev above, or a moment after, the one the delete targets. Recorded BEFORE the pending branch in `applyRemoteRow`, because the case that matters is precisely the one where a delete for that key is already queued.
  - **⛔ BY PROVENANCE — the diff INVENTED the delete.** `reconcile` mints a delete for exactly one reason — the shadow holds an element and the collections do not — and it cannot tell "the user deleted this" from "a row arrived from another tab and never reached the canvas". `applyRemoteRow` writes the shadow entry ITSELF, so if the upsert it returns is dropped on the way (a snapshot applied over it, a gesture buffering it, a remount) the next diff issues a delete for an element this tab NEVER HELD. That delete's base is not stale — it has no base at all. Such a key is tracked until a diff proves the canvas has genuinely shown the element; until then a delete for it is refused and the row is handed BACK to the canvas instead.
- **THREE SEAMS, because one was not enough and the reason generalises.** The conflict-result branch is the obvious one. **`opFor` sends a delete at the shadow's CURRENT rev, not the rev it was formed against** — so a delete whose shadow was advanced by `applyRemoteRow` while it sat queued does not lose its guard at all: it goes out expecting exactly the row that was just created and **the server ACCEPTS it, in total silence, with no conflict anywhere.** So the question is asked (a) in the DIFF, (b) before the op is BUILT, and (c) after a refusal. The unload keepalive is filtered too — it has no result handler, so a delete that lands there is unobservable by construction.
- **The matrix row (the item asked for one test per direction).** `conflictToasts.js` gains `delete-vs-create-dropped`: the DELETER is told, because the element visibly comes back and an object reappearing unexplained is the worst reading of a correct outcome; the CREATOR sees nothing, because their create simply stands and there is no event on that side.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `test/deleteVsCreate.test.js` (7) drives the real engine on the owner's real geometry, one test per direction and one per seam, **including the two controls that make it a guard rather than a blanket** — create-then-delete still re-issues at the fresh rev, and delete-vs-edit with no observed birth is byte-for-byte its pre-change self. `test/conflictMatrix.test.js` +2. Full suite green.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/elementSync.js`, `lib/conflictToasts.js`, `test/deleteVsCreate.test.js`, `test/conflictMatrix.test.js`.

### B385043 — A Notes bin test indexed into a CLOCK-SORTED list, so CI went red on a commit that passed five local runs `[Notes / testing]` (bug) #notes #testing #infra  *(found 2026-08-13 by CI going red on PR #1008 — a branch that touches nothing in Notes. Minted **B385043** from that branch's reserved block B385040–B385055. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `flake`, `flaky`, `intermittent`, `known-red`, `notesBinPurge`, `trashEntries`, `deletedAt`, `B267538`, `B266080`, `B266081`, `B1310`: **B267538/B266081** own the CI lane's known-red LEDGER and the sandbox-vs-CI calibration — this is not a lane artefact, it is a real order dependence in one assertion, and it would misreport on any machine; **B1310** built the Notes bin this tests and is correct. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **FIXED 2026-08-13. Verify: sandbox — the mechanism was measured, the fix runs green six consecutive times, and the slow-clock case is now FORCED by a guard rather than waited for.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **THE MECHANISM, MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED.** `trashEntries` sorts **newest first** on `deletedAt`, a millisecond stamp, and the `binnedThree` fixture bins three pages in a tight loop — so which entry is `[0]` is decided by how fast the machine is. Forcing the clock forward one millisecond between the three deletions, with nothing else changed, moves the answer: **all three in one millisecond → `sort` is stable → `[0]` is `"a"`; three distinct stamps → `[0]` is `"c"`.** The assertion `expect(liveIds(stale)).toEqual(["a"])` was therefore only ever true on a fast run. CI drew the slow case and reported `[ 'c' ]`.
- **⛔ IT IS PRE-EXISTING ON `main`, and that is worth stating plainly** — the identical line is at `test/notesBinPurge.test.js:183` on `origin/main`, and the branch it blocked touches no Notes code. It was found because it happened to fail under an unrelated PR, which is exactly how a latent flake surfaces.
- **THE FIX — name the entry you mean.** `entryForPage(tree, pageId)` looks the bin entry up BY the page it holds. The test's subject was never *which* entry (it is "a stale client restored one of them, and the merge refuses it"), so indexing a time-sorted list was expressing something it did not mean. Rule recorded at the helper: **index into a clock-sorted list only when the ORDER is the thing under test.**
- **THE GUARD FORCES THE CASE RATHER THAN HOPING FOR IT.** A new test spins the clock to give the three deletions distinct stamps, asserts that precondition really holds, then asserts BOTH halves in one place: the old `[0]` really does pick `"c"` under it, and the named lookup still means `"a"`. A run on a fast machine covers the same-millisecond tie for free, so between them both tie-break outcomes are exercised on every run. Six consecutive local runs green; full suite 536 files / 10,818 tests green.
