- **Full report: `docs/PERF-PLAN-SWITCH.md` §6–§9.** New: `liveEntryPoints` in `ui-audit/lib/heapSnapshot.mjs` (5 unit tests), wired into `ui-audit/diagnose-plan-switch.mjs`.
- **⛔ THE SECOND ATTEMPT'S NAMED HOLDER IS REFUTED, and the reason generalises.** `holderOf` stops at the first retainer that is not FLAGGED detached — sound only if "not flagged" implies "alive", and it does not: **V8 sets `detachedness` on DOM WRAPPERS ONLY.** A closure that is itself garbage, reachable only from inside the dead island, satisfies the stopping rule perfectly. The `native_bind` holding the overlay file `<input>` as its third bound argument is exactly that: **React DOM builds that shape for every non-delegated listener** (`listenerWrapper.bind(null, domEventName, eventSystemFlags, targetContainer)`, three arguments, third is the element) and an `<input>` gets one for `invalid`. It points at the input because it was MADE for the input, and the pair is a cycle inside the island. **This is the THIRD correction in the family** — the shortest path is the wrong question → a native node is not a holder → a JS object reachable only from inside the island is not a holder either.
- **THE COMPLEMENTARY QUESTION, which cannot fail that way.** Walk FORWARD from the GC roots refusing to pass through any detached node; everything reached is provably alive; the leak is the edges crossing into the island. Two load-bearing rules: the handle tables are **not traversed through** (every DOM wrapper is in one, so a walk through them names the table — the same always-true, never-useful answer), and a detached node is recorded and never expanded, so the result is the island's BOUNDARY.
- **THE RESULT: 6 crossings out of 357,982 live nodes, every one of them Leaflet, every one WEAK.** Each is a `CSSStyleDeclaration` pointing at `leaflet-tile-container leaflet-zoom-animated` (×2), `leaflet-layer`, `leaflet-container leaflet-touch` and two plain `<div>`s — and each of those bottoms out at `(Traced handles)` through a **`weak:` edge**, which does not retain. **Not one SVG node, not one panel, not one rail button.** So (a) nothing in live JS strongly references the island, which with §5's clean listener census and clean cleanup sweep puts the reference on the **Blink side**; and (b) **§4's ruling-out of Leaflet should be treated as re-opened** — its evidence was that container and tile COUNTS return, and a returning count means a new container replaced the old one, not that the old one was released. Two of the six crossings carry the class **`leaflet-zoom-animated`**, and an animation still attached to a detached element is held by Blink and invisible to every JS-side check made so far.
- **WHERE A FOURTH ATTEMPT STARTS:** `document.getAnimations()` before and after the cycle, counting animations whose `effect.target` is detached — a direct test of the hypothesis above needing no snapshot at all. Then a listener census on the Leaflet CONTAINER, which every census so far has missed (all of them looked at `window` and `document` only, and Leaflet registers on neither).
- **Tests.** 5 new cases in `test/heapSnapshot.test.js`, incl. a scene built so a naive implementation gets each rule wrong differently: it must name the live holder, must NOT name the dead-but-unflagged closure (the exact mistake, asserted against `holderOf` in the same test), must refuse to traverse the handle tables, must report the boundary not the interior, and must answer UNKNOWN — never zero — on a snapshot with no detachedness column.

`[x]` **✅ FOURTH ATTEMPT (2026-08-07) — RESOLVED, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THERE IS NO PRODUCT BUG. The leak was the measuring harness's own undisposed `ElementHandle`. Fix + regression guard shipped. Everything below the FOURTH ATTEMPT block is the superseded record of attempts 1–3.**
- Verify: live

- **WHAT WAS MEASURED.** Load plan A → load plan B → return to A: **`rendererNodes` 4,184 → 5,156 → 8,114 (+93.9% against A's own first load)** while `documentNodes` (3,297 → 3,252) and `canvasNodes` (2,446 → 2,421) both came back to where they started, and `jsEventListenersCdp` was released (−1.2%). **Renderer-wide nodes nearly doubling while ATTACHED nodes stay flat is the signature of DOM the renderer is still keeping alive that is no longer in the document.** Retained heap +5.6%.
- **⛔ REPRODUCED, NOT A FLUKE — four independent runs, each a fresh page load doing one A→B→A** (ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK: this half is Claude-doable here, so it was driven here rather than filed as owed):

  | run | `rendererNodes` A₀ → B → A₁ | Δ | `documentNodes` A₀ → A₁ | `canvasNodes` A₀ → A₁ | retained heap Δ |
  | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
  | 1 | 4,184 → 5,156 → 8,114 | **+93.9%** | 3,297 → 3,252 | 2,446 → 2,421 | +5.6% |
  | 2 | 2,523 → 3,537 → 4,973 | **+97.1%** | 1,811 → 1,806 | 976 → 976 | +8.0% |
  | 3 | 2,529 → 3,537 → 4,973 | **+96.6%** | 1,811 → 1,806 | 976 → 976 | +10.8% |
  | 4 | 2,547 → 3,537 → 4,973 | **+95.2%** | 1,811 → 1,806 | 976 → 976 | +9.2% |

  Runs 2–4 land on the **identical** A₁ figure (4,973) from near-identical starts, which is about as reproducible as a browser measurement gets. Listeners are released every time (+0.3 to +2.7%); the ATTACHED node counts come back to where they started every time, so the residue is entirely in nodes the renderer is holding that the document no longer contains.
- **WHY IT IS STILL NOT CONVICTED, stated rather than implied.** `rendererNodes` counts every node the renderer is keeping alive, which includes nodes held only by a JS reference — that is a weaker claim than "detached DOM", and the honest counter-evidence is **B1433's ZERO detached nodes read from V8's own `detachedness` flag** (measured across interaction on one plan, which does not cover a switch). Each run above is also ONE round trip on a fresh load, so this shows a switch leaves a residue; it does **not** yet show the residue COMPOUNDS across several switches in one session, which is the version of the question that matters for the owner's symptom.
- **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and both halves are cheap:** (1) a full heap snapshot through `ui-audit/lib/heapSnapshot.mjs`'s detachedness reader at A₀ and again at A₁ — a non-zero count with a class name on it turns this from a signature into a mechanism; (2) three round trips inside ONE page load (a small harness change) to see whether it compounds. If it compounds, this is a genuine per-switch leak and it feeds straight into the one row the **B1435** audit could not answer — whether major-GC pause time scales with the live set on a 278 MB tab.
- **WHY IT MATTERS TO THE OWNER'S SYMPTOM.** Plan/revision switching is one of the axes that rises through his session and resets on reload — the exact shape of *"reload and it's quick; a minute or two later it's lagging."*
- **⏱ SECOND ATTEMPT — `docs/PERF-PLAN-SWITCH.md`, instrument `ui-audit/diagnose-plan-switch.mjs`.** The item asked for "one real attempt … if it still cannot be named, say so plainly and record what the second attempt ruled out, so a third does not start from zero." Four things are settled that were open, and one is not.
  1. **IT IS NOT THE HARNESS.** Every probe here sets `window.__PLANYR_E2E`, arming four `window.__planner*` hooks that were never nulled on unmount — a genuine candidate for the whole signature. The `--no-e2e` control runs the identical cycle without them and leaks **IDENTICALLY**: 7,026 detached nodes, 1,173.4 KB, `rendererNodes` +326.2%, `jsEventListeners` +55.1%, on both arms. **B1439 is a product bug.**
  2. **THE DETACHED DOM IS REAL, and B1433's zero does not cover this.** From V8's own `detachedness` flag: **0 → 2,342 nodes / 391.1 KB** across one A→B→A, while every attached counter returns exactly. B1433 measured zero across INTERACTION on one plan — a different lifecycle.
  3. **IT COMPOUNDS — the version of the question B1439 said mattered.** ×1 → 2,342 nodes / +108.7% `rendererNodes`; ×3 → **7,026 nodes / 1,173 KB / +326.2%**, heap +37%. **Linear at ~2,342 nodes and ~106 listeners per round trip, released never.** Nothing plateaus, so this is not "the previous plan is held until the next replaces it" — every plan opened in a session is still there. It is the only thing measured anywhere in the speed program that grows **without bound inside one session**, which is the exact shape of the owner's report.
  4. **WHAT IS HELD is the WHOLE previous `SitePlanner` tree, not just its canvas** — 78 detached `<svg>` roots (the rail's inline icons), `<button data-rail-tab="standards">`, `<button data-rail-tab="references">`, the panel divs, and 1,187 `SVGRectElement`.
  5. **HALF-NAMED, and the half that is named is new.** Two holder classes, from a proper reverse-graph search: a **bound function** (`native_bind`) holding the overlay's file `<input>` as its third bound argument, and a plain **`Array`** holding a detached `<div>` — from either root the whole tree is reachable by ordinary DOM edges. **No source line**, because there is no `.bind(` in `src/` taking a DOM node (the one site-planner match is `fetch.bind(globalThis)`). **⛔ So no fix is shipped — B1434's rule.**
  - **Two methodological corrections are recorded, because each produced a confident WRONG answer first.** (a) The **shortest retaining path is the wrong question** for a detached node: every DOM wrapper is one edge from V8's handle table, so `(GC roots) → (Traced handles) → node` is always available and never distinguishes a leak from a live element — the first run returned exactly that for every class. (b) **A `native` node is not a holder either**: Blink hangs `SVGAnimatedLength` / `CSSStyleDeclaration` / `Text` / `InternalNode` off every element and those are NOT flagged detached, so "the first non-detached retainer" answered *the element's own width attribute*. `holderOf` traverses THROUGH both and reports only a JS-side holder — or refuses, with a stated reason.
  - **RULED OUT, so a third attempt starts here:** not the harness (1) · **not a listener left on a long-lived target** — `DOMDebugger.getEventListeners` on `window` and `document`, with the registering script position on every row, is **net +0 on both**, so the ~106 listeners/cycle are on the detached nodes themselves and are a CONSEQUENCE, not the cause · **not a missing `removeEventListener`/`disconnect()`/`clearInterval` in app code** — an exhaustive sweep of `site-planner/**`, `shared/**` and `app/**` for all seven asymmetry classes found ZERO (every module-level registry returns an unsubscribe and every consumer uses it) · **not Leaflet** (`leafletContainers` and `leafletTiles` return exactly; `releaseLayer` intact) · **not `window.__planner*`**, though those four hooks WERE a real retention path and are **nulled on unmount as of this dispatch** so no future measurement is taken through them.
  - **WHERE A THIRD ATTEMPT SHOULD START:** the `Array` holder — a plain JS array with a detached `<div>` at index 1, the cheapest thing left to identify and certainly ours or a dependency's rather than an engine artifact. The tool to do it with now exists (`holderOf` + `retainerIndex`, 21 unit tests).
- **Tests added by the second attempt.** `test/heapSnapshot.test.js` grows the edge-walking half: `to_node` is a BYTE OFFSET not a node index · an `element`/`hidden` edge's name is an ARRAY INDEX not a string-table offset · every retainer is recorded, not just the first in node order · `holderOf` names the first non-detached NON-NATIVE holder and REFUSES to invent one when every retainer is detached, native or a handle table.

- **⛔ FOURTH ATTEMPT (2026-08-07) — CLOSED. `docs/PERF-PLAN-SWITCH.md` §12–§16.** The mechanism is
  named, proven by making the leak conditional, fixed, and guarded.
  - **THE CAUSE IS ONE IGNORED RETURN VALUE IN THE INSTRUMENT**, not a line of app code:
    `await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="planner-canvas"]')`, called after every route change
    by every harness in this family. `waitForSelector` **returns an ElementHandle**, which is a
    strong V8 global handle in the inspector's object group; Playwright never disposes it and
    ignoring the return value does not either. A Blink `Node` holds its **PARENT** strongly, so one
    undisposed handle on the canvas `<svg>` pinned the whole detached shell above it. It accounts for
    the quantities exactly: ~1,171 nodes is one app shell, ×2 per round trip is the 2,342, ×3 cycles
    is the 7,026, and it is linear because one handle is stranded per switch.
  - **PROVEN CONDITIONALLY** — two arms, one line apart. Handle ignored: `0 → 3,377` detached,
    `rendererNodes 2,378 → 6,112`, listeners `577 → 736`. Handle **disposed**: `0 → 0` detached,
    `rendererNodes 2,379 → 2,379`, listeners `578 → 578`. **Flat on every counter B1439 was filed on.**
  - **HOW IT WAS NAMED — one heap rule §8 had backwards.** §8 refused to traverse handle tables, so
    it could only ever conclude "nothing live points into the island". The right rule is *skip WEAK
    edges*, not *skip handle tables* — a `weak:` edge does not retain, which is why §8's six
    crossings explained nothing, while an inspector-side retention IS a strong handle-table edge.
    Re-run that way the entire island has **exactly two** strong crossings, both
    `(Global handles) ──internal:N / DevTools console──▶ SVGSVGElement`. One per switch.
  - **ALSO RULED OUT, all null results, all recorded (§14):** §9's step 1 **animations** —
    `getAnimations()` is 0 before AND after, and switching mid-flight vs switching only once the page
    is provably animation-free leaks identically (2,342 each) · §9's step 3 **listeners beyond
    window/document** — `getEventListeners` at `depth:-1` over the whole live tree, **net +0** ·
    **observers / ranges / focus** — constructors wrapped before app code, 0 observers left observing
    a detached element, no stale range, `activeElement` = BODY · **conservative stack pinning**, which
    nearly became a fourth wrong answer: a forced purge drains 2,343 → 1 while 13 `collectGarbage`
    calls do nothing, but both natural allocation pressure AND a precise cache-neutral
    `gc({execution:'async'})` move it not at all, so the retention was real and the purge freed it by
    releasing the inspector's object group.
  - **SHIPPED.** `ui-audit/lib/waitRelease.mjs` (disposes in a `finally`; deliberately never returns
    the handle) · the contaminated harnesses fixed — `diagnose-plan-switch.mjs`,
    **`session-axes.mjs`** (its `switchPlan` stranded one per switch, so **its plans-axis memory
    numbers were measuring this defect** — including the `rendererNodes +93.9%` reading this item was
    filed from, now retired) and `interaction-degradation.mjs` · the **regression guard**
    `ui-audit/verify-plan-switch-release.mjs` (`npm run perf:planswitch`), measured green at guarded
    `0 → 0` detached / `rendererNodes 2378 → 2378` with its control arm dirty at `0 → 1035`.
  - **THE GUARD CANNOT ROT GREEN**, which is the point given three attempts hid from ordinary checks:
    it runs a second arm that strands a handle **on purpose**, and if that arm comes back clean it
    FAILS as *not observing* rather than passing; and it refuses to report unless the plan switch is
    proven by the drawn-element count changing. Tests: `test/planSwitchRelease.test.js` (the pure
    verdict table incl. both anti-rot cases) and `test/harnessHandles.test.js` (static: a script that
    measures retention may not call bare `page.waitForSelector`; the file list is derived from what
    each script does, and the test asserts that list is non-empty).
  - **⚠ WHAT THIS DOES NOT EXPLAIN, said plainly.** B1439 was the only confirmed defect matching the
    owner's *"reload is quick, a minute or two later it's lagging"*, and it is now retired — **that
    symptom is unexplained again**, and nothing here addresses it. The memory readings that pointed
    at plan switching came through the contaminated harness and **need re-taking**. See **B1121**.
  - **METHODOLOGICAL LESSON — the fourth in this family** (§4a's two, §6's one): *the instrument's own
    protocol handles are part of the measured heap.* §1 asked exactly the right question and built
    `--no-e2e` to answer it, but varied the app-side `__PLANYR_E2E` hooks rather than the
    harness-side handles. Clearing one candidate is not clearing the instrument.

- **THE MEASUREMENT, RE-RUN AND INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED THIS SESSION — eight samples, both event types.** Push→`main`: `87f0438` 00:52:01Z→00:52:04Z **3 s** · `020265f` 00:37:10Z→00:37:14Z **4 s** · `fdcb02d` 00:29:05Z→00:29:09Z **4 s** · `ad09957` 00:21:12Z→00:21:15Z **3 s** · `cd9c94c` 00:12:51Z→00:12:56Z **5 s**. `pull_request`: #932 synchronize `5f89818c` 00:26:55Z→00:27:06Z **11 s** · #939 opened `a45af00` 00:18:01Z→00:18:27Z **26 s** · #940 opened `4edf282` 00:34:10Z→00:34:54Z **44 s**. Every commit timestamp read from `git show -s --format=%cI` against `origin/main`, every run time from the Actions API `run_started_at` — the owner's figures reproduced exactly, not taken on trust.
- **WHY THE PUSH ROWS ARE EXACT AND THE PR ROWS ARE UPPER BOUNDS, stated rather than glossed.** For a squash merge GitHub writes the merge commit at the instant it merges, so its **committer** timestamp *is* the push moment. For a `pull_request` event the committer timestamp is when the commit was written locally and precedes the push by however long the session took to get there — so those three figures are at or above the true lag. The worst number in the table is therefore 44 s, and the truth is below it.
- **THE ORIGINAL MEASUREMENT IS KEPT, NOT DELETED — it was real that afternoon** (PR #931's `Nudge CI` `94c4efb` pushed 22:29:23Z, `build` started 22:59:27Z; the same gap on #933 and on runs 2338/2339). What changed is that it is now scoped to the incident that produced it — the four-hour Actions outage of 2026-08-06 and the queue backlog it left — instead of being written as a property of this repository.
- **THE LIVELOCK ARGUMENT IS RESTATED SO IT NO LONGER DEPENDS ON THE PERIOD, which is the stronger claim and the one that survives.** The old §2 argued "the loop's period (~30 min) is far longer than the rate at which the mark advances", which makes the ratchet sound like a race that a big enough head start could win — and that reading is exactly what produced #931's *"chosen ~850 clear of the mark so it survives the lag"*. The period-independent form: the rule passed a branch only if its ids were strictly above the maximum held by any *other* in-flight branch, so for two branches A is green iff `a > b` and B is green iff `b > a` — **both cannot hold at once**. With `n` branches, `n − 1` are red by construction and the only remedy the rule offers turns the green one red. **Set the lag to the 3 s now measured and it still livelocks**; it would just have burned its ninety-eight thousand ids in minutes. There is no lead large enough when the finish line is defined by where the other runners are.
- **THE ADVICE THAT DEPENDED ON THE FALSE CLAIM IS THE PART THAT ACTUALLY MATTERED, and it is rewritten in both places it appears** — §4 of the doc and the always-loaded `CLAUDE.md` block. It used to read *"a PR showing `Expected` for the first half hour is NORMAL — wait it out"*, which on an ordinary day tells a session to sit through twenty-nine minutes of a genuine fault. Now: a minute or two is just delivery · longer is worth **looking** at (does the run exist at all? is the whole repo's queue backed up?) · and **renumbering is never the response either way**, because the verdict no longer changes with time.
- Files: `docs/CI-REQUIRED-CHECK.md` (status line, §2 Stage B + "Why the two together are lethal", §3, §4) · `CLAUDE.md` (the mint-block rule's "Why this changed" + consequence (b)).

### B226401 — A required check may never fail on a prediction about a peer branch: the outage's SHAPE, guarded `[Infra / CI]` (task) #infra #testing  *(filed 2026-08-07 from the owner chat block as NEW-2. Minted from the same reserved block as B226400; see it for the shared DEDUPE-FIRST search. Additionally searched for an existing guard on the mint verdict's fatality: `test/mintGuard.test.js` pins the verdict's BEHAVIOUR case by case and `test/mintGateE2E.test.js` pins the CLI's exit codes — neither asserts a property over the class of possible predicates, so both pass unchanged if `BELOW` is reintroduced under a new name. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE 2026-08-07 (sandbox) — the shape is now a property CI re-proves on every build, mutation-checked both ways (17 tests green).**
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-08-07 from chat
- **THE INVARIANT, one sentence, at the top of `test/mintFatality.test.js` because that is the only place it is enforced rather than described:** *a fatal mint verdict may only ever name an id that is HELD RIGHT NOW — present on origin/main or on a live peer branch — and never an id judged against an AGGREGATE of peer state such as a maximum, a mean, or a high-water mark.*
- **THE LETHAL SHAPE, named as three stacked properties rather than as one bad line** (this is what the guard is really about): the check is **REQUIRED** — an unsatisfied required context offers no merge control to anyone, not even an administrator, so the repo cannot recover from the GitHub side · its verdict depends on **ANOTHER UNMERGED BRANCH**, state no branch controls and that moves without any action by the branch being judged · and **THE ONLY REMEDY WORSENS THE CONDITION FOR EVERY PEER**. Any one alone is survivable; the three together have no fixed point.
- **GUARDED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS, because either alone can be fooled.** `ui-audit/lib/mintFatality.mjs` is the pure engine. **(1) Behavioural** — drives the real `mintVerdict` through a battery of 21 probes built so every aggregate of peer state (max · mean · min · count · high-water) is wildly out of line with the ids being judged, in **both directions**, and asserts the fatal set is exactly the ids something actually holds. It tests the property, not the spelling, so it catches aggregate predicates nobody thought to name. **(2) Structural** — asserts the decision loops that produce `offenders` (`mintVerdict` **and** `announceVerdict`) mention no aggregate identifier at all, which catches a reintroduced predicate that is dormant on every probe because it sits behind a flag, an env var or a date. Comments are stripped first: `check-mint.mjs` discusses `claimedMax` at length precisely *because* it was removed, and a guard that fired on its own explanation would be uninstallable — that exemption is itself a test case.
- **THE ANTI-ROT HALF IS EXPLICIT.** `missed-collision` fails the guard when an id genuinely present on `origin/main` comes back non-fatal — so a verdict function that has quietly stopped failing on anything cannot pass. Without it this guard would go permanently green the moment the gate broke, which is the failure mode **VIEW-INDEPENDENT-ONCE §6** names.
- **MUTATION-CHECKED BOTH WAYS, the way `test/requiredChecks.test.js` does for the ruleset contract** (`test/mintFatality.test.js`, 17 tests): the real repo passes, and each rejected shape goes red — the reinstated `claimedMax` predicate (naming **B3005**, the exact id whose rejection started the cascade, as *unfounded*) · a **mean** of peer ids · **out-of-block made fatal** (no aggregate in sight, still a prediction — and the reason the invariant is worded as "held right now" rather than "not an aggregate") · a gate that never fails · `ok` disagreeing with its own offender list · a verdict function that throws · source the structural half cannot read (**LOUD-FAILURE**: it refuses rather than reporting a pass).
- **SCOPE STATED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR A LOOPHOLE.** The announcement check is fatal and is *not* exempted — it needs no exemption, because it reads only this branch's own working tree, so its verdict is a present self-contained fact with no peer state in it. It is scanned by the structural half alongside `mintVerdict`.
- Files: `ui-audit/lib/mintFatality.mjs` (new) · `test/mintFatality.test.js` (new) · `docs/CI-REQUIRED-CHECK.md` §3 (points at the guard) · `CLAUDE.md`. Runs in the required build via `npm test`; no new build step and no new dependency.

### B225984 — Auto-merge froze the squash commit message at ARM time, so a renumbered PR landed on `main` announcing retired ids `[Infra]` (bug) #infra #testing  *(found 2026-08-07 the moment PR #931 merged, by reading `git log` on main. Minted **B225984** from this branch's reserved block (B225984–B225999). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `announce`, `commit subject`, `check-mint`, `auto-merge`, `renumber`, `B779`, `B6864`, `B6867`, `#865`, `#866`: **B779's announcement check** (`idsNamedIn` in `check-mint.mjs`) owns exactly this defect for the commit **this branch pushes**, and it WORKED — it rejected the stale subject and the subject was corrected before the push. This is the same defect arriving through a door that check cannot see. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE 2026-08-07 (sandbox) — mechanism proven by elimination, procedure fixed, and the one bad commit recorded because it cannot be unwritten.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **THE DEFECT, on `main` right now.** `fdcb02d` ("…(#931)") announces **B3001/B3002 · B3003 · B3004 — V1501/V1502** in its subject and throughout its body. The **files it merged are correct** — `BACKLOG.md` carries `### B221760`–`### B221763` and `VERIFICATION.md` carries `### V23408`/`### V23409`. So the id space is sound and `test/idUniqueness.test.js` is green; what is wrong is the only number a human reads in `git log --oneline` or in the PR list. This is the **#865/#866 defect** that B779's announcement check exists to prevent.
- **THE MECHANISM, and it is not the one the announcement check guards.** GitHub's auto-merge captures the squash commit **title and body when auto-merge is ARMED**, not when it fires. PR #931 armed auto-merge while its ids were still `B3001–B3004` (the third of six ratchet-era renumbers). Every later renumber updated the branch, the headings, the commit subject and the PR title — and none of them updated GitHub's frozen copy. Proof by elimination: the PR title at merge time was `B221760/B221761 · B221762 · B221763 — V23408/V23409` (set by this session, and the merged **files** match it), yet the merge commit reads `B3001`; the only place that string ever existed was the PR title several hours earlier.
- **THE FIX — one binding step, added to `CLAUDE.md` → *Workflow & deploy* and to `docs/CI-REQUIRED-CHECK.md` §5: after ANY change to a PR title, DISABLE and RE-ENABLE auto-merge.** Re-arming is what makes GitHub re-snapshot the message. Renumbering always changes the title, so this fires on exactly the branches most at risk.
- **⛔ WHY NO MACHINE GUARD WAS BUILT, stated rather than quietly skipped.** The obvious guard — scan `git log` on `main` for ids naming no heading — is **weak by construction here**: `actions/checkout` fetches depth 1, so in CI it would scan one commit, pass trivially and rot into a permanent green. That is the exact failure mode **VIEW-INDEPENDENT-ONCE §6** names ("fails if a registered one was never OBSERVED"). Making it real would mean `fetch-depth: 0` on every build to catch a defect that only a title edit can cause. The honest answer is a procedure step, and this bullet is here so nobody re-litigates it.
- **The scan was still RUN, once, by hand, and its result is the baseline:** across all 59 commits this shallow clone holds, **`fdcb02d` is the only commit on `main` naming an id that has no heading.** Stated with its limit — a deeper clone could hold more, and this session could not see them.
- **B3001–B3004 / V1501–V1502 are BURNED — never file a different feature under them.** They now name this work in main's history and nothing else. The practical risk is small because reserved blocks anchor **above** main's maximum (`ringFloor`), so `next-id` cannot hand out a number that low; the burn is recorded so the reasoning survives the tool.

Bidding higher buys one branch a merge and charges the cost to everyone forever; the branches that renumber back down leave no scar at all. So the discipline here is: take the gate's recommendation plus a small non-round offset, and if that loses, WAIT for the storm to settle rather than bid. If this recurs the fix is a repo-level one — the gate RESERVING an id at mint time, so the race cannot exist — not larger numbers. Note also that CI never got past `check-mint` on this branch, so the CI-side lint/test/build steps are unproven THERE; they are green locally and reported as such, not as CI results (B1140: gaps are free, and a third renumber pass costs more than a gap) because ids were moving by tens per minute while the post-outage CI backlog held this PR open. ### B1430 — Corrected the falsified "uncapped store" comment and wrote the tiering rule down `[Core / docs]` (task) #persistence #infra  *(owner chat block 2026-08-06 as NEW-4. Minted **B1430** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `localDb`, `uncapped`, `idbPersist`, `TIER`, `B474`: B474 WROTE the header being corrected. Net-new — a rule, not a re-fix.)* — ✅ DONE 2026-08-06 (`Verify: sandbox`)
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-06.** Verify: **sandbox** — a doc/comment correction with a machine-checked companion (the `TIER-BY-REBUILDABILITY` guards land with B1427–B1429).
- Origin: filed 2026-08-06 from the owner chat block (NEW-4)
- **THE FALSIFIED COMMENT.** `lib/localDb.js`'s header called the store "durable, uncapped" and "a store that can't fill". Both are false, and that framing is what let a ~5 MB tier and a ~10 GB tier be reasoned about as ONE thing for a year. Replaced with the measured numbers (IndexedDB **35.9 MB / 10,275.9 MB quota, 0.3%, persisted: true**; localStorage **3.88 MB / ~5 MB hard cap, ~78%**, 156 keys) and the two facts that follow: the quota is a real, finite, disk-derived number that can be SMALL on a full disk; and **`SitePlannerApp.jsx:25` calls `idbPersist()`, so this origin is PERSISTENT — the browser will NEVER evict it for us.** That is correct for data safety (a user's only copy of a raster is not the browser's to throw away) and it is precisely why a budget is not optional: nothing else is going to clean up after us.
- **THE NAMED RULE — `TIER-BY-REBUILDABILITY`, in `/CLAUDE.md` under Engineering rules**, so it can be invoked by name in a brief like every other rule here. Four binding parts: **(1)** the two tiers differ by three orders of magnitude and are never summed, never reported combined, and never called "uncapped"; **(2)** the small store is for irreplaceable work only — a cache competing with it is a priority inversion; **(3)** a budget is not optional even in the large store, because the origin is persistent; **(4)** no eviction may ever cost data that cannot be rebuilt — every reclaimable class declares a rehydration source, and reference images declare `rebuild: null` (B474's raster hazard). Plus the corollary: **measure, don't reason** — nothing knew its own size before B1429, which is why the first diagnosis of this crisis was wrong by three orders of magnitude.
- **Folder pointers updated in the same commit** (the doc-pointer audit rule): `src/shared/CLAUDE.md` gains the `storage/` entry with the no-workspace-imports constraint and why it exists; `src/workspaces/site-planner/CLAUDE.md`'s `gisCache.js` line now states the tier, the synchronous-`read()`-is-L1-only consequence, and that the budget is B1162's unchanged.

### B1426 — "28x slower" was measured on an endpoint the app never calls `[Site Analysis / GIS]` (task) #gis #perf  *(owner audit 2026-08-04: "TxDOT's AADT layer takes 4,657 ms just to return metadata, against a 166 ms median across all 43 sources. It is the slowest thing in the registry by 28x." Arrived as provisional NEW-6. Minted **B1426** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `aadt`, `timeoutMs`, `GIS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`, `B789`, `B1079`, `B445`: **B789** set the FEMA per-source timeout and **B1079** the BKDD cold-start one — the same mechanism, different rows, neither about this one. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-05. `Verify: sandbox` — measured before and after, as instructed.**
- Verify: sandbox — `test/siteAnalysis.test.js` (5 new)
- Origin: filed 2026-08-05 from the owner chat block (NEW-6)
- **The honest answer is more specific than the report, and it matters.** 4,657 ms was the **service METADATA endpoint** (`?f=json`, a 19 KB payload). The screening path never calls it — that number is a cold first connection to TxDOT's ArcGIS Online org, and it does not describe anything a user waits for. Re-measured 2026-08-05: **cold 1,302 ms, warm 40–124 ms**.
- **In the request the app ACTUALLY makes** — the buffered proximity `/query` — aadt is **410 ms** (median of three) against a **113 ms** median for its six peers (lpst 94 · rail 112 · airports 113 · epaCleanups 122 · substations 101 · transmission 219). So it IS the slowest row, by about **3.6x, not 28x**, and the cause is that it is a large statewide point layer on a busy shared org rather than anything we are doing wrong. Reporting 28x would have sent the next session hunting for a bug that is not there.
- **So the fix is volume, not a rewrite.** Every proximity source fired TWO requests per screen: the features (capped at 100) and a separate `returnCountOnly` for the exact total. ArcGIS reports truncation via `exceededTransferLimit` — below the cap and untruncated, **the features ARE the population**, so the second request asks the agency for a number we already hold. Measured on the Goose Creek ring: **seventeen sources, thirty-four requests → seventeen**, and on every one the feature count already equalled the reported total. The wall-clock win is small (the two ran concurrently) and that is not the point: the point is request volume against **metered** agency services — H-GAC's org was returning HTTP 429 "API calls quota exceeded" during this same audit, and halving what we ask for is the only lever we have on that.
- aadt also gets its own **6 s abort cap** so the registry's slowest row cannot spend the shared 9 s budget and stall the panel behind it; it degrades to an honest "unknown" instead. The truncated and at-the-cap cases still fetch the exact count, which is what keeps every reported number identical.

### B1379 — A load-time repair that MOVES nothing was never written back to disk `[Site Planner / storage]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence  *(found 2026-08-03 by driving B1377's repair in a headless browser — the open question flagged on B1377 and as step (a) of V671, now settled and CLOSED in the sandbox rather than left for the live pass. Minted **B1379** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, late, on a branch restarted from the merged main (PR #903). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `bondedHealWatch`, `persistHeal`, `assembly-tear-persisted`, `HEAL_TEAR_TOL_FT`, `B1340`, `B1118`, `B1377`: **B1340** BUILT `persistHeal` for exactly the failure this is an instance of ("a heal that lives only in memory is precisely why the owner's plan kept fixing itself on screen while the STORED copy stayed torn") and is deliberately NOT re-opened — its mechanism is correct and untouched; what it could not anticipate is a repair with no distance to measure. **B1118** is the cloud-side twin (the heal's `exempt` set, so a repaired element diffs and commits) and is unaffected. **B1377** shipped the repair this exposes and stays in ⏳ Verify. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-03.** The Goose Creek sidewalk repair now reaches the saved file, not just the screen.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: found 2026-08-03 while verifying B1377 (the flagged step (a) of V671)
- **The defect.** `bondedHealWatch.flush()` decides whether a load-time repair is worth persisting by measuring how far it MOVED a child (`healMoveFt` → `HEAL_TEAR_TOL_FT`). That is the right question for a torn assembly, where the distance is both the severity and the proof. It is the wrong question for **B1377**'s repair: restoring a bonded pad's `sideParkSide` changes its IDENTITY and not one coordinate, and minting the deleted 5 ft sidewalk back into the void ADDS an element with no previous position to measure against. Both scored **0 ft**, so `wasTorn` came back false, `loadSite`'s `persistHeal` branch never fired, and the plan rendered repaired while the stored record kept its wreckage — the precise failure `loadSite`'s own comment was written about, arrived at from the other direction.
- **The fix.** Severity at this seam is now **structural as well as metric**: `STRUCTURAL_HEAL_KINDS` (`orphan-pad-retagged`, `orphan-pad-strip-restored`) always persist. They are reported on their OWN telemetry event (`assembly-orphan-pad-repaired`) rather than folded into `assembly-tear-detected`, because "N bonded children up to X ft off their host" is simply untrue of a repair that moved nothing, and a message that overstates what happened is how a real signal stops being read.
- **⚠ THE METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING — the first version of this item's tests PASSED against the unfixed code.** They seeded the damaged plan through `saveSite`, which **renormalizes on WRITE**, so the record on disk was already repaired and the load path was never exercised at all. It was caught only because a mutation that should have turned them red did not. Tests for a LOAD-path repair must plant the raw bytes straight into the store; the helper now says so in a comment, next to the `plant()` it provides.
- Tests: `test/orphanWallPads.test.js` +3 (24 total) — the damaged plan's restored sidewalks are asserted **on disk** and not merely in memory, re-opening re-mints nothing, and a plan needing no structural repair is not re-written on open (no `updatedAt` churn on every route lookup). Mutation-checked: reverting `isStructuralHeal` turns two of the three red.

### B1375 — Exploding a parking field stripped every bond role tag off the pieces `[Site Planner / splitParkingRows]` (bug) #site-planner #selection  *(owner chat 2026-08-03, provisional NEW-1, with a root cause proven against the live production DB. Minted **B1375** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE, as the last step before push. Branch `claude/goose-creek-sidewalks-naovyl`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `splitParkingRows`, `explodeParkingBands`, `sideParkSide`, `HOST_ROLE_TAGS`, `bondRemap`, `B472`, `B1124`: **B472** BUILT the Explode and is the code this corrects, not a recurrence of it (it shipped the geometry, which is right; the bond identity was never in it); **B1124** is the COPY path's twin defect — a duplicated set remapping only `attachedTo` — and is the reason `HOST_ROLE_TAGS` already existed for this fix to reach for; **B499** covers the load-time heal for bonded children keyed ON the tag, which is what went blind. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-03.** Explode now hands every piece the whole identity of the field it came from.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-08-03 from chat (NEW-1)
- **The defect, in one line:** `splitParkingRows` built each piece with only `cfg` and `attachedTo` copied off the source field, so a 60 ft double-loaded module became `parking 18 / paving 24 / parking 18` with **`sideParkSide` and every other `HOST_ROLE_TAG` dropped**. The pieces stayed bonded to the building and kept rendering; they simply stopped meaning anything.
- **What that cost:** every lookup and every heal keyed on the role tag went blind — `empSidePark`, `sideParkingOn`, `empSideAddTitle`, `normalizeWallKids` / `hostOf` (which admit a child only when it is a wall-strip type **or** carries `sideParkSide`), and the side-parking heal in `normalizeHostRuns`. The untagged pieces therefore never re-flushed when their host moved or resized — a live suspect for the recurring *"the parking is entirely separated from the building"* reports — and the aisle lane was written as bare `paving` bonded to a building with no role at all: a bonded child with no identity. The destructive consequence is **B1376**.
- **The fix:** `lib/bondRemap.js` gains `carryHostRoleTags(src, clone)` — the ONE tag-carry helper for any path that replaces an element with fresh-uid children — and both Explode branches (stall rows AND aisle lanes) spread ONE `bond` object built from it, so no future edit can give the rows an identity the aisles do not get. `sideParkFit` and the new `sideParkPiece` joined `HOST_ROLE_TAGS`: both are measured against the host, so both must travel with it or not at all.
- **The set is now modelled, not just tagged.** `lib/dogEar.js` `sideParkStack` is the one derivation of a wall's outward parking stack — pads ordered inner→outer (by `sideParkPiece`, falling back to their own perpendicular offsets for every plan already on disk) each with the cumulative gap it must clear. `relayoutWallKids`, `normalizeWallKids` and `normalizeHostRuns` all read it, so an exploded set lays out as ONE wall kid. It is byte-identical for a single un-exploded field.
- **Fleet impact at time of fix (live DB, non-deleted sites):** 12 host buildings across 9 plans and 6 sites carried untagged exploded pieces — Goose Creek ×4 plans, Silvestri, Sylvestri, Katz, Hoffmeister, RICHEY. Those are repaired by **B1377**.
- Tests: `test/orphanWallPads.test.js` (21, on real production geometry; mutation-checked 3 ways — disabling the repair, dropping the stack model, and dropping the intent stamp each turn it red).

### B1376 — The "−" ladder deleted a sidewalk while a full parking field was still on that wall `[Site Planner / growEmployeeSide]` (bug) #site-planner #selection  *(owner report 2026-08-03: "go check out the goose creek plans, their missing sidewalks for some reason, figure that out" — provisional NEW-2. Minted **B1376** via `--against-main`, late. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `growEmployeeSide`, `empSidePark`, `removeFeature`, `deletePlan`, `B246`, `B743`: **B246** built this ladder and is the code corrected here; **B743 / `deletePlan.js`** is the DELIBERATE delete path and is a different surface entirely — this is a growth control removing the wrong thing, not Delete doing nothing. Net-new, and the destructive consequence of B1375.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-08-03.** One click can no longer reach the sidewalk while pavement is bonded to that wall.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-08-03 from chat (NEW-2)
- **Proven on the live DB, not inferred.** On Goose Creek "Plan II — 220K, 440K, 700K" (site `sms69x8rb2qk`) and both copies (`sms93hmiy4nl`, `sms93j3sfc04`), two host buildings had 1 sidewalk instead of 2: `e1454629danlgq` lost `e1454689dshobp` (tombstoned 2026-07-29 21:36:28) and `e1454729ykduhm` lost `e1454744tcmstb` (2026-07-30 14:49:29). **Both were SOLO single-row commits with the host alive and untouched** — not a cascade, not a merge. The four intact hosts on the plan still have both sidewalks, and the two damaged hosts are exactly the two whose side-parking field had been EXPLODED.
- **The mechanism.** `empSidePark(b, side)` found side parking strictly by `x.sideParkSide === side`, so after the Explode it returned `undefined`. `growEmployeeSide(b, side, -1)` then fell past `else if (park)` into its last branch, `else if (sw) removeFeature(sw.id)` — **and deleted the sidewalk with a full parking field still sitting on that wall.** The ladder is meant to walk rows → remove parking → remove sidewalk; the missing tag made the middle rung invisible, so one click jumped to the end. `removeFeature` then called `relayoutWallKids` to pull the parking back flush now the strip was gone, and skipped the same untagged pieces — the physical receipt: `e1454736ykduhm` still sat with its inner face **5.00 ft** off the wall of `e1454729ykduhm`, the empty sidewalk slot, unchanged.
- **The fix, in two halves.** (a) *"What is on this wall?"* is answered by **GEOMETRY** — `sideParkPadsOn` returns every bonded, non-stack, non-strip pad whose side resolves to this wall, with the tag only as a fast path, which is the same forgiving test `empSideSidewalk` has always used (and precisely why the sidewalk stayed visible while the parking vanished). `sideParkingOn`, `empSidePark`, `empSideAddTitle`, `employeeSideHasAny` and `ownedSidePark` all read it. (b) The ladder is **structurally incapable** of reaching the sidewalk: that rung is now the `else` of `pads.length`, so a future tag-loss bug degrades to a rung that does nothing instead of one that destroys geometry. On an exploded set "−" peels the outermost piece (the dock-stack LIFO idiom next door) and "+" appends a stall row beyond it, matching its neighbour's hand-trimmed run.
- Tests: `test/orphanWallPads.test.js` — the geometric lookups, the guarded ladder, and source guards asserting the strict tag test is gone from every one of them.

### B1357 — Does the SAME gesture get more expensive over a session? Measured, with a control and a stated floor `[Infra / Testing]` (task) #infra #testing #perf #site-planner  *(owner chat 2026-07-31, provisional NEW-6, appended to the phase-2 speed block mid-session. Minted LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `retention`, `memory`, `long session`, `degrade`, `tile cap`, `B1121`, `B1160`, `B1161`, `B1162`, `B1331`: those five all BOUND something that was unbounded, which is a good reason to bound it and is not evidence that it caused anything; **B1331** is the only one that measured its suspect (the undo stack, innocent at 0.4 MB). Nothing has ever measured whether the cost of a gesture actually moves over a session. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped — the harness and the reading. `ui-audit/perf-harness.mjs --long-session`, protocol in `ui-audit/lib/longSession.mjs`, decision layer unit-tested in `test/longSession.test.js` (15 tests).**
- **THE READING, on the reference Goose Creek plan at 4x CPU throttle.** `hold` arm (**the plan never changes**, so anything that moves is retention): 5 rounds of pan / zoom / travel to unvisited map area / panel open-close / select-deselect. Wheel median **116.7 → 133.4 ms**, inside the measured ±12.5% floor. JS heap **29 → 30.1 MB**, no trend. Canvas DOM nodes **967 → 948** (down). Document nodes flat. Drawn elements flat at 64 — the control holding. `grow` arm (20 paving elements added through the real draw tool): wheel **100 → 150 ms** with canvas nodes **967 → 1,068** and document nodes **1,838 → 1,948**, correlating at **r=0.93** (document nodes) and **r=0.83** (canvas nodes).
- **THE ANSWER: on this evidence the cost tracks HOW MUCH IS DRAWN, not how long the session has run.** Same plan, same gestures, twenty minutes apart → no move that clears the floor. Add twenty elements → the cost rises in lockstep with node count. "The plan got bigger" is load and is not a bug; the retention story is not supported here.
- **THE ONE COUNTER THAT DOES MOVE, repeatably, in BOTH arms and unexplained:** DOM-commit deliveries per pointermove, **2.2 → 7.6–9.3** across three separate runs. It is a STEP between rounds 1 and 2 rather than a gradual trend, which points at a session STATE left behind by the workload (a panel, a selection) rather than unbounded growth. Not chased in this PR — recorded, so the next pass starts from a number. **Owned by B1359's sibling work; if it is still there after that, it gets its own item.**
- **⛔ THE SUSPECT THIS CANNOT EXERCISE, stated rather than routed around.** No basemap tile DECODED in any run (`tilesLoaded` 0 → 0): this sandbox blocks the external tile hosts, and decoded map imagery is the largest single suspect for the owner's ~278 MB tab. Nothing here clears or convicts it. **V539 stays open**, and **V518 stays open** — its acceptance terms are retained-tile count and decoded bytes, neither of which exists in a run where no tile decodes.
- **THREE DEFECTS IN THIS HARNESS, each found by running it and each fixed:** (1) a **zero noise floor** — a steady pan reports the identical quantised median every repeat, so the spread is 0 and a later 16.8 vs 16.7 reads as a regression; the floor is now never smaller than one frame quantum. (2) **one endpoint is not a trend** — the same `hold` arm reported "within-noise (+0.1%)" and "SLOWER (+14.3%)" on consecutive runs, so a move is only called real when the last TWO checkpoints clear the floor in the same direction (`unsustained` otherwise). (3) the `grow` arm **added nothing** on its first run (the draw button was addressed by a selector that does not exist) and silently degenerated into a second copy of `hold`; it now reports that in a named block instead.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: owner chat 2026-07-31 (speed program phase 2, provisional NEW-6)

### B1358 — The boot-chunk guard was a RACE and could silently pass `[Infra / Testing]` (bug) #infra #testing #perf  *(found 2026-07-31 while verifying B1349's fix — it nearly certified an unverified fix, which is why it takes its own number. Minted via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across `siteRouteChunks`, `perf-harness`, `frame sampling`, `B1086`, `B1344`, `B1163`: **B1086** is the hidden-tab frame-sampling trap, **B1344** the empty scene and the no-op gesture, **B1163** the allowlist's own defect. `[x]` **Fixed.**
- `runtime.siteRouteChunks` snapshotted the requested-chunk list the instant the time-to-first-drag gesture returned. A boot-path `import()` fired from a React mount effect is only in that list if it has been REQUESTED by that moment — so the metric was a race against the machine's own speed.
- **Measured within one session on one build:** all five B1349 intruders reported when time-to-first-drag was 7.1 s, and NONE of them once the container warmed up and the same figure fell to 4.4 s. A guard that reads clean because the box got faster is worse than no guard.
- Fix: the snapshot now waits a fixed settle window with **no gesture in it**, which is B1349's own definition of the defect ("in flight on an idle page, no gesture, four seconds of idle").

### B1354 — Size the cost of the 20 `feDropShadow` filter regions with a real paint profile `[Site Planner / UI]` (task) #site-planner #perf #ui  *(filed 2026-07-31 from the speed program's "RECORDED, NOT FOR THIS PR" list — **filed deliberately, NOT implemented**, and deliberately as a MEASUREMENT task rather than a fix. Minted via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `feDropShadow`, `filter`, `shadow`, `raster`: nothing covers it. Net-new.)*
- One filter region per building (four render sites), each forcing an offscreen buffer and a gaussian blur of the group's whole bounding box **every frame**, each wrapping a group with up to ~160 door rects, and each under a **non-integer rotation** straight out of the data (e.g. `rot 178.543241069641`) which defeats raster caching.
- **Do not guess and do not remove the shadow.** This needs a Chrome paint profile with the `filter` attribute A/B'd to size it; the drop shadow is how a building reads as a building and its removal is a drawing-quality downgrade, which the owner's standing constraint forbids.
`[x]` **MEASURED 2026-07-31. RECOMMENDATION: leave the shadows alone. Nothing shipped, which is the correct outcome for a measurement task.**
- **HOW.** `ui-audit/diagnose-zoom-cost.mjs --mutate nofilter` strips the `filter` attribute from every canvas node and re-strips after each React commit (a one-shot strip silently undoes itself on the first frame and would report the baseline as the A/B). Interleaved against an unmutated control, 4 reps each, 4x throttle, the same wheel gesture the harness drives.
- **THE NUMBER.** All 20 filter regions removed: paint/raster residual **1,027 → 819 ms** across the gesture (−20% of the paint half), total task time **6,880 → 6,285 ms** (−8.6%), frame median **166.6 → 158 ms**. So the drop shadows are about **3% of the frame** — real, and nowhere near the 5× the target needs.
- **THE SUB-FINDING THAT SETTLES THE OBVIOUS CHEAPER FIX: the blur is not the cost.** `--mutate noshadowdefs` keeps every filter reference intact (so the region is still established and the offscreen buffer still allocated) and zeroes the `feDropShadow` — residual **1,050 ms vs the 1,027 ms control**, i.e. no change at all. The cost is ESTABLISHING the filter region, not the gaussian. So "soften the shadow" / "reduce `stdDeviation`" buys nothing, and there is no visually-identical alternative at this size of prize.
- **RECOMMENDATION: do not touch them.** Removing or weakening the shadow is a DESIGN change — the shadow is how a building reads as a building — for ~3% of a frame. That is Michael's call and this item does not ask him to make it.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (speed program, recorded item (d))

### B1319 — The inline number editor was four times the size of the chip it edits, floated over the drawing, and showed the value twice `[Site Planner / numEdit]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #selection  *(owner chat 2026-07-31 with a screenshot of a clicked setback chip: "I hope I don't have to explain what's wrong with that." Provisional NEW-1; minted **B1319 / V641** LATE via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main` as the last step before push — code, tests, harness and commit keep the provisional `NEW-1` label. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `numEdit`, `inline numeric`, `inline editor`, `spinner`, `in-place`, `window.prompt`, `B146`, `B431`, `B654`, `B911/B912`, `B1184–B1187`, `B463`, `B618`: **B146** CREATED this editor (as the replacement for `window.prompt`), **B431/B654** converted the last two `prompt` callers onto it, **B912** made the dimension number open it, **B463/B618** built the app's own NumInput / RotationStepper steppers it should have been reusing. Every one of them added a CALLER; not one ever owned how the field LOOKS or WHERE it sits. Net-new, not a recurrence. Coordinated with the setback-chip strand rather than colliding: **B1184–B1187** (PR #874) own the chip's declutter, anchoring, plate width and quieting, and **B1191/B1214** its roles — this changes only what happens AFTER a chip is clicked, reads the chip's metrics from a new module instead of re-declaring them, and leaves the anchor maths, the declutter guards, the plate style and the role vocabulary untouched.)*
`[x]` *(implemented + verified headless 2026-07-31 — see **NEW-1/V** in `VERIFICATION.md`, 74/74 checks.)*
- Verify: live — zoom-dependent rendering, so it carries a `V###`; every strand of it was DRIVEN HERE (logged out, local fixture, two zooms × both themes, all three floating callers), so the entry lands PASSED rather than pending.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-1)

**The defect — five things, all visible in one frame.** (1) **SIZE:** the editor was `W=96 · H=30 · fontSize 13` while the setback chip it edits is a 26 × 15 pill with 9.5 px text — roughly four times the thing it edits, in every dimension. (2) **THE VALUE TWICE:** it rendered at `bp.y - H - 8`, i.e. ABOVE the anchor, so the editor's "25" and the chip's "25′" were on screen simultaneously, one right above the other. (3) **IT COVERED THE WORK:** it landed on the building, the setback line and the setback drag handles — the exact geometry you are looking at while deciding the number. (4) **NATIVE SPINNERS:** a bare `input type="number"`, so the browser painted its own chevrons; they match nothing else in the app, which already has its own steppers (B463/B618). (5) **STYLING THAT MATCHED NOTHING:** a 2 px accent border, a `ui-monospace` face and a heavy drop shadow, none of which appear on any other control in the planner.

- **THE FIX IS AN IN-PLACE EDIT, and that is what removes four of the five faults at once.** Clicking a setback chip turns THAT CHIP into the field: the pill stays where it is, at its size, and its text becomes editable with the value selected so typing replaces it. Nothing grows, nothing moves, nothing is covered — and the value appears exactly once, because the chip IS the editor. The static chip is SUPPRESSED while its editor is open (`pill` returns the field INSTEAD of the plate+text, an early return rather than a sibling), so the two can never both paint.
- **`lib/numEditBox.js` is the new pure home for WHERE the editor paints and AT WHAT SIZE** — the chip's metrics (`SETBACK_CHIP`, `setbackChipPlateW`) moved there from the render site, so the plate and the field cannot drift apart, and the guard test measures the editor against the REAL chip rather than a copy of its numbers. `numEditFitsSpawn` states the invariant this item exists to keep; the old 96 × 30 box fails it, which is what makes the guard non-vacuous.
- **The editor is SHARED, so the fallback had to be designed, not left behind.** Road width, element dimension, overlay trace length and aerial calibration have no chip to become. Those keep a small FLOATING field — same component, same tokens, same absence of spinners — brought from 96 × 30 @ 13 px down to 54 × 18 @ 10.5 px, and OFFSET up-and-to-the-side of the anchor instead of centred over it, so the dimension being measured stays readable.
- **The native spinners are gone app-wide, not per-field** (`index.css`: `appearance: textfield` + both `-webkit-*-spin-button` pseudo-elements), so a number input added tomorrow cannot reintroduce them. At 15 px the right stepper is **no visible buttons at all**: ArrowUp/ArrowDown nudge by one, Shift by ten, clamped at zero (`nudgeNumEditValue`), with the browser's own step suppressed so a nudge can't double.
- **Restyled to the app's own control tokens:** one-pixel border, `NUM_FONT` with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (the same pair the chips already use, so the digits sit exactly where the chip's digits sat), no drop shadow. The focused-input treatment is the app's shared one from `index.css` (accent border + a soft ring), which is the point — it now matches every other input in Planyr instead of being the only control with a shadow.
- **`display:block` on the field is load-bearing, and the harness is what caught it.** An `<input>` is inline-level, so inside a `<foreignObject>` it sits in a line box and the strut above it put the field **5 px below** the plate it replaces — the first harness run measured `Δ 0.00, 5.00` and failed. A block box has no strut; the check now reads `Δ 0.00, 0.00`. Same trap B1140 hit with the contour hover label.
- **Every behaviour that already worked is kept:** Enter commits · Escape cancels · blur commits · the full-canvas backdrop click commits · and the **Alt-click override of a single segment inside a grouped run** (the run opener's closure is untouched; it only gained the `chipKey` third argument). The chip key is passed FROM the pill and never re-derived in the opener, so the field and the chip it replaces cannot disagree about which one it is.
- **MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS:** `components/NumEditField.jsx` is defined at module scope, not inside the planner's render body, and the focus+select runs in a mount-only `useLayoutEffect` (an inline `ref` callback would re-fire every keystroke and re-select mid-edit).
- **Guards (the three the brief asked for, plus the behaviours).** `test/numEditInPlace.test.js` — 21 tests: the field is never larger than its spawn across every chip text the app can produce (with the OLD box asserted to FAIL the same invariant), it lands exactly on the plate's rect, the chip and the field are never both in the DOM, the floating fallback is at chip scale and offset off its anchor, the app-wide spinner suppression is present for both engines, and the nudge/commit/cancel/Alt-click behaviours hold. `ui-audit/verify-numedit-inplace.mjs` — the live pass, below.
- **PANEL-BREVITY: n/a** — no yield or pond panel copy touched. Net copy change in the product is **negative**: the editor now shows a number and nothing else.
- **Bundle:** inside band, no ratchet raise needed (`perf:bundle` green; the two new modules are ~1 KB of code and land on a route that already imports the render site).
- **✅ VERIFIED HERE, 2026-07-31 — headless Chromium, logged out, `ui-audit/verify-numedit-inplace.mjs`, 89/89 checks** (see **V641** in `VERIFICATION-DONE.md`). Five passes: light + dark × fit + zoomed-in on a synthetic parcel, and a fifth on the owner's REAL 60-vertex Weld County boundary (`test/fixtures/weldParcelProduction.json`). Measured, not eyeballed: `chip 26.0×15.0 @9.5px → field 26.0×15.0 @9.5px`, `Δ 0.00, 0.00` from the plate's own rect; 8 chips → 7 + 1 field (never both); 15/16 grips answer a press at their own centre DURING the edit, identical to the baseline before it, and 0 grips under the field; `appearance: textfield` on every number input on the page; all three floating callers at `54×18 @10.5px`, spinner-free and offset off their anchor. Screenshots before / during / after each pass in `ui-audit/screens/numedit-*.png`. Nothing pending — no auth, live-GIS or real-data wall applies, so this goes straight to Done rather than parking.

### B1310 — A delete you cannot take back: give Notes the same 30-day bin every project already has `[Notes]` (bug) #notes #persistence  *(filed 2026-07-31 from an owner review of B1290. Minted **B1310** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, deliberately JUMPING CLEAR of the next free number: 55 in-flight branches were on the remote and the previous four notes dispatches each lost the id race. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `notes`, `bin`, `undo`, `recently deleted`, `restore`: the Site Planner's project bin (`listDeletedProjects` / `restoreDeletedProject` / `purgeExpiredDeletedProjects` in `storage.js`) is a different store and a different unit; nothing covered Notes. Net-new.)*
`[x]` One inline tick on a notebook destroyed every section, page and body under it, **forever** — no undo, no bin, no export-first prompt. Deleting a PROJECT bins it for 30 days; Notes now matches that standard.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (NEW-2)
- **DELETE IS NOW A MOVE.** `deleteNode` lifts the node into `tree.trash` with `{ kind, node, parentId, index, title, deletedAt, pageIds }`. An **Undo** bar appears at the moment of the delete (not a dialog — house rule), the rail gains a **Bin** view with Restore / Delete forever / Empty, and a 30-day sweep runs lazily on load.
- **TOMBSTONE-DELETES IS INTACT, NOT WEAKENED — this is the part to read before changing anything here.** The FULL cascade of orphaned page ids is still computed by the same walk at the moment of the delete, and is stamped on the entry. What changed is WHEN it executes: `notesStore.purgePages` is the one call site that frees bytes, and it clears the body **and every image** of every id on that entry. Nothing can be resurrected in between, because no read path looks in `trash` (`findPage` / `allPageIds` / `recentPages` / search all skip it), so a future merge or sync sees exactly what it saw before.
- **Two restores that are easy to get wrong, both handled and both tested:** a node whose PARENT is also binned restores the parent first (recursively); a node whose parent is gone for good lands in a named **"Recovered notes"** home rather than being refused. A restore must never fail into nothing — refusing one would make the bin as lossy as the delete it replaced.
- **The bin cannot leak storage.** The load-time orphan sweeps (`sweepOrphans` for bodies, `sweepImagesOfMissingPages` for pictures) are handed the union of LIVE **and** BINNED page ids — a sweep that knew only the live tree would destroy exactly what a restore needs, which is the trap this pairing exists to avoid.
- Guards: `test/notesRoundTwo.test.js` (bin lifecycle, both restore paths, the corrupt-entry case, purity, migration) + `ui-audit/verify-notes.mjs` §19, which drives the whole thing in a real browser and asserts the bodies are STILL ON DISK after the delete and gone only after "Delete forever".

### B1311 — A note that can hold a picture, without base64 eating the whole browser store `[Notes]` (feature) #notes #persistence #files  *(filed 2026-07-31 from an owner review of B1290; minted with B1310 in one `--against-main` run. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched for `image`, `paste`, `screenshot`, `IndexedDB`, `notes`: the Doc Review / Library file tier (`reviewStore` / Drive) is a different thing entirely — that is a document you OPEN, this is a picture INSIDE a note. Net-new.)*
`[x]` Paste or drag a picture into a page and it stays there — a cropped survey, a site photo, a screenshot of a flood map.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (NEW-1)
- **THE CONSTRAINT, AND THE HONEST ANSWER TO IT.** Notes persist in localStorage — a few megabytes for the WHOLE origin, shared with every other workspace — and base64 costs a third more than the bytes it carries. Two phone photos would exhaust it and every save after that would fail, in every notebook. So the **document holds an image ID and the bytes live in IndexedDB** (`lib/notesImageDb.js`, hundreds of megabytes), behind the same one storage seam. A data URL rather than a Blob, deliberately: JSON-able (so cloud sync lifts it through the same seam), already the form the Markdown export has to inline, and no object-URL lifetime to leak.
- **Downscaled once, at intake** (`lib/notesImageIntake.js`): capped longest edge, then encoded BOTH as PNG and as JPEG with the smaller winning — which lands on PNG for flat screenshots and JPEG for photographs without either being hard-coded. GIF and SVG pass through untouched; a canvas would flatten an animation to one frame and an SVG to a fixed raster, which is a silent downgrade of what the user pasted.
- **Ceilings are enforced at the STORE, not at the paste site,** so no future intake path can bypass them: `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` per picture and `MAX_NOTEBOOK_IMAGE_BYTES` per notebook. Over either is a NAMED, VISIBLE refusal on the existing one error channel (LOUD-FAILURE) — never a paste that quietly does nothing.
- **Markdown export inlines each picture as a data URL**, so an exported note is self-contained; a picture whose bytes are gone is written as a named broken reference AND reported in the lossiness notice. The source-scan guard is satisfied in the same commit: `noteImage` is in `NOTE_MD_HANDLED` and has a case in the exporter.
- **A missing image is a VISIBLE broken block, never a blank gap** — the node view says so in words, and the same is true on the printed sheet.
- Delete cascade: `purgePages` reads each purged page's body, collects its image ids and destroys those bytes with it (B1310's purge is the one call site).
- Guards: `test/notesRoundTwo.test.js` (the real store over `fake-indexeddb` — ceilings, scoping, usage, the cascade, the sweep that spares binned pages) + `ui-audit/verify-notes.mjs` §11–§14 (a real clipboard paste, the proof the bytes are in IndexedDB and NOT in localStorage, the export, and the broken state after the record is deleted out from under the note).

### B1312 — Nothing recorded when a note was last touched `[Notes]` (feature) #notes  *(filed 2026-07-31 from an owner review of B1290; minted with B1310. DEDUPE-FIRST: no prior item covers note timestamps or a recent view.)*
`[x]` A page node was literally `{ id, title }` — no timestamp anywhere in the module — so the rail could not show "edited 2h ago", there was no sort by recent, and after a few weeks the only way to find yesterday's note was to remember its name.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (NEW-3)
- `createdAt` / `updatedAt` on the PAGE node only — the tree is read on every render and rewritten on a 400 ms debounce, so it stays titles-and-numbers; two integers per page is the whole cost, and bodies stay out of it as before.
- **`null` is a real value and means UNKNOWN.** Every page written before this honestly has no time; inventing "just now" at upgrade would be a lie the rail repeats forever and would put the oldest notes at the top of Recent. So a migrated page shows no time and sorts last. The migration is additive in both directions.
- **`updatedAt` is stamped on the write that actually LANDED**, not on a keystroke: the editor's flush calls back only when `writePage` returned true, so a page cannot claim it was edited at a moment storage refused to record it (LOUD-FAILURE's quieter cousin).
- Rendering: a relative time on the page row (in the same slot the hover controls use, so a row is never taller for having one), an "Edited 5h ago" line in the page header with the exact moment on hover, and a new **Recent** view in the rail. `lib/notesTime.js` is the one formatter, so the three surfaces cannot disagree.

### B1315 — Search found the page and then abandoned you on arrival `[Notes]` (feature) #notes #ui  *(filed 2026-07-31 from an owner review of B1290; minted with B1310.)*
`[x]` Body search worked, but opening a hit dropped you at the top of the page with no indication of WHERE the phrase was, no way to step between matches, and no quick way out — Esc did nothing.
