### B1290 — Notes: a fifth workspace — OneNote-shaped notebook › section › page beside a full rich-text document page `[Notes]` (feature) #notes #ui #persistence #export #perf  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, verbatim: "I wanna create a notes module. Kinda like OneNote. but better. have have all the same formatting features as Word and OneNote, and I should be able to make tables too. Ideally it will print to a recognized format like markdown or something butt thats not nearly as important as functionality." Owner also chose a DOCUMENT page over a free-form canvas, and notes that live BOTH attached to a project AND loose. Minted **B1290** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Branch `claude/planyr-notes-workspace-2ygi6h`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `notes`, `notebook`, `OneNote`, `rich text`, `editor`: **B613** is the Site Planner's per-site notes PANEL (a plain textarea on a site) and `verify-notes-sheet-labels.mjs` is Doc Review sheet metadata — different features, different data, neither is a workspace. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE 2026-07-30 — shipped and driven end-to-end in a real browser (53/53 headless checks).** A fifth lazily-loaded workspace at `src/workspaces/notes/`, magenta-plum accent, reachable from the header beside Site / Schedule / Review / Library.
- Verify: sandbox — the whole module is exercisable logged out, so it was DRIVEN here rather than parked (**ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK**). The one genuinely auth-blocked strand — that account A's notes are invisible to account B in the same browser — is **V630**.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **THE DECISION EVERYTHING ELSE FOLLOWS FROM: store the DOCUMENT MODEL (ProseMirror JSON), never Markdown.** Markdown cannot express a merged table cell, a text colour, a font size, a highlight or a checked task — so storing Markdown would have capped the editor at what Markdown can spell, which is the exact inverse of the functionality-first ordering the owner asked for. Markdown is an **export**, and an honest one: what it can say it says (GFM pipe tables, task lists, code fences, quotes, links), what it cannot falls back to the inline-HTML subset every renderer passes through (`<u>`, `<mark>`, `<span style>`, a full `<table>` for merged cells), and `docToMarkdown` **RETURNS the list of constructs that needed a fallback** so the UI names them after an export instead of letting the user discover the gap in another app.
- **THE TREE.** notebook › section › page. A notebook carries an optional `projectId` or `null` for loose; binding at the NOTEBOOK level (not the page) makes "everything on Goose Creek" a one-line filter, and a **loose notebook is visible from inside EVERY project** — a scratch notebook you cannot reach from where you are working is one you stop using. A new notebook is born with a section and a page, so there is nothing to create before typing.
- **THE TREE HOLDS NO PAGE BODIES.** The tree is one storage key; each page body is its own (`planyr:notes:tree:v1:<scope>` / `planyr:notes:page:v1:<scope>:<pageId>`). One blob holding every note would mean every keystroke's autosave rewrites every note ever written — a cost that grows for the rest of the notebook's life. `<scope>` is the signed-in user's id or the literal `local`, so two accounts on one machine never read each other's notes.
- **THE EDITOR: Tiptap, headless, with the entire UI hand-rolled on Planyr theme tokens.** Justified against the repo's dependency rule in the module header: a rich-text engine is not a contenteditable div — selection across nested lists and table cells, undo over compound transactions, Word/Outlook paste normalisation and a serialisable document model are a multi-month build with a permanent bug tail. All packages MIT, all bundled (nothing fetched at runtime), and the whole set rides the lazy editor chunk. **We hand-roll the entire UI and never the engine.**
- **THE TOOLBAR** — headings 1–4 via a block-style select, font family, font size, bold/italic/underline/strike/inline code, text-colour and highlight swatch popovers, clear formatting, four alignments, bulleted/numbered/checkbox lists with indent and outdent, quote, code block, divider, link, insert table, undo/redo, export to Markdown — plus a **TABLE group that renders only when the caret is genuinely inside a table** (row above/below, delete row, column left/right, delete column, merge-or-split, toggle header row, delete table). Every active state is read from `editor.isActive(...)` and **never mirrored into React state** (a mirrored copy drifts the moment the caret moves by any route the toolbar did not originate). Every control cancels `mousedown`, or "select a word, click Bold" would bold nothing.
- **⛔ THE TWO BUGS THE LIVE CHECKS CAUGHT — the component shape IS these fixes, and both are guarded.**
  **(1) Switching pages inside the save debounce LOST the last thing typed.** The obvious flush — ask the outgoing editor for its document on the way out — is a bet on React hook-cleanup ORDER, and it loses: the editor's own cleanup can win, and the flush then queries a destroyed instance. So `onUpdate` snapshots the document as **plain JSON at edit time** (`pendingRef` holds `{id, doc}`) and the flush writes that OBJECT — by then there is nothing left to ask anybody for. The parent additionally **keys the editor by page id**, so a page switch unmounts the instance and its cleanup flushes. `beforeunload` runs the same flush.
  **(2) Reopening a note containing a TABLE crashed the workspace into its error boundary** — `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'commands')`, from an effect calling `editor.commands.setContent` against an instance whose command manager was already null. The keyed remount **removes that effect entirely** and the whole class with it: each page gets its own instance, reads its initial content once via a `useState` initialiser, and has its own undo history — which also kills the stale-undo-stack bug where undo walked you into another page's text. There is deliberately **no "sync content on pageId change" effect**, and a source guard fails the build if one appears.
- **A THIRD BUG, found by the harness during this session and fixed the same way.** The tree's flush effect was keyed on `tree`, so every tree change ran the PREVIOUS effect's cleanup — which cleared the freshly-scheduled write timer *and* wrote the tree from its stale closure. Creating the first notebook therefore persisted the EMPTY tree and cancelled the real write, so the notebook vanished on reload. Same discipline applied: capture the value in a ref at edit time, keep the flush referentially stable so it registers once. **A debounce and an effect that both own the same write is a race; only one of them may.**
- **LOUD-FAILURE.** A full quota, a disabled store or a private-mode browser must never look like a clean save. Every failure path broadcasts through `onNotesStorageError` and renders as a named banner; every write returns a boolean that drives the Unsaved/Saved/Not-saved badge. There is no swallowed catch in the store, and a source guard asserts it. The header reads **"Saved on this device"** and does **not** imply sync — sync is **B1291** and is not built.
- **TOMBSTONE-DELETES.** `deleteNode` returns the FULL cascade of orphaned page ids (deleting a notebook orphans every page under every one of its sections), and the caller clears every one. Proven live: deleting a section took the localStorage page-body key count 2 → 0.
- **NO DIALOG BOXES.** Rename is an inline field (Enter commits, Esc cancels); delete asks with an inline "Delete? ✓ ✕" row on the row itself. Guarded across all eight module files.
- **SEARCH covers page titles AND page BODIES**, merged with titles first and an excerpt on body hits — titles pure in `notesModel`, bodies through the store via `docToText`.
- **CHROME.** New `--accent-notes` **#B8418C** (magenta-plum) + `--on-accent-notes` + `--accent-notes-text` (#8C2F69 light / #F0A6D2 dark), mirrored into `shared/theme/palette.js` with a test keeping the two in step. **The hue was picked to clear two hard floors at once, not by eye:** white body text on the fill is **5.03:1** (AA text) AND the fill clears **3.46:1** on the DARK chrome. The first plum tried, #A03270, passed the first (6.59) and FAILED the second (2.64). Because the fill carries real body text (the selected page row, active toolbar toggles) it is audited as **TEXT** contrast — five new pairs in `ui-audit/contrast-audit.mjs`, all green in both themes.
- **BUNDLE — load-bearing, and the gate fails without it.** The editor is pulled by `lazy(() => import("./components/NoteEditor.jsx"))` **from the workspace root**, inside a Suspense, so the notebook tree paints before the engine downloads. **Measured in this container:** Notes route **554.6 KB**, with the engine a separate on-demand chunk of **463.8 KB** that is not fetched at all until a page is actually opened (asserted live). New `bundle.notesRouteJsBytes` budget wired into `ROUTE_KEYS`, the audit and the ratchet. **`bundle.totalJsBytes` was RAISED** with the measurement on the record: `origin/main` measured **3929.9 KB** in this same container against this branch's **4411.9 KB**, so **the whole +482.0 KB delta is the new workspace** — that metric counts every emitted chunk *by design*, which is what makes it the honest catch-all, so no further splitting reduces it. **A future rise in it WITHOUT a new route is a regression.** `siteRouteJsBytes` moved **+1.0 KB** (the header tab) and `largestChunkBytes` is **byte-identical to main** — the Site route, which is what the owner's slowness complaint was about, is untouched. The owner has explicitly accepted this growth: a new module is supposed to add weight.
- **THE TRAP WORTH KNOWING, recorded because it costs a red CI run to rediscover:** importing `shared/ui/controls.jsx` from Notes makes the bundler hoist a THIRD shared chunk **onto the Site route** (five chunks where the allowlist permits four) and the perf audit goes red. The two radius values are re-declared locally, with a source-scan test asserting the copies still match `controls.jsx`.
- **REGISTRATION — a new workspace touches EIGHT places and missing one fails quietly** (the Library shipped with a generic "Loading…" until B524). Shell `WORKSPACES` (+ a new `userId` prop so a workspace can scope per-account storage without pulling the auth client onto its route) · route `MODULE_BY_SLUG`/`SLUG_BY_MODULE` · `modulePrefetch` `IMPORTERS` · `moduleAccent` · `moduleLoaderTheme` `LOADER_SKINS` · `AppHeader` tab + icon + both accent maps · `bundleMetrics` `ROUTE_KEYS` · the budget entry. **The checklist is itself a test.**
- **EVIDENCE.**
  - `ui-audit/verify-notes.mjs` — **53/53** against the REAL built app (headless Chromium, `vite preview`): the tab opens and the engine arrives *behind* the tree (and is not fetched at all until a page opens) · one click makes a typeable notebook · typing reaches that page's own key and the badge reads Unsaved → Saved · bold, heading, checklist and table all write the real document model · the table controls appear only inside a table and row/column insertion change the model · **an edit made a split second before switching pages is not lost, and page 1's text does not bleed into page 2** · a reload restores the text, the table and both pages **without crashing** · search finds a page by a phrase that appears only in its BODY · a clean page exports with NO lossiness notice while an underlined one falls back to `<u>` **and says so** · deleting a section clears every page body (2 → 0 keys) · the Markdown export downloads a real file carrying the heading, the bullet, the task list and the table.
  - **The headline guard was FALSIFIED to prove it has teeth:** with the per-page remount key removed and rebuilt, the run went red — and the split-second assertion was then TIGHTENED, because the marker alone still survived while page 1's text bled into page 2. It now asserts the page contains only its own text.
  - `test/notesModel.test.js` **61** · `test/notesMarkdown.test.js` **66** · `test/notesModule.test.js` **67**. Full suite green · lint 0 errors · build green · MAP.md, BACKLOG_OPEN.md, doc-pointer, contrast and panel-copy-budget checks all green.
  - Two real bugs were caught by these suites and fixed in the source rather than papered over in the test: `safeFileName` left a leading `..` on `../../etc/passwd` (the dot-strip ran before separators were flattened), and the inline-code path inserted a **zero-width space** to break a backtick fence — silently altering the user's code, and rendering the file unreadable as text. It now widens the fence per GFM instead, with a test asserting no export contains a zero-width space.
  - The module-guard suite initially failed on its own *comments* — the files document the rules they obey ("never `window.prompt`") — so the scanners were fixed to read **code, not prose**. That also closes the hole where a real violation could have hidden inside a comment.
- **Follow-up filed, deliberately not built here: B1291** (cloud sync). Every read and write already goes through the one storage seam, so it is a change there and nowhere else.
- Files: `src/workspaces/notes/` (`CLAUDE.md`, `Notes.jsx`, `components/NotesTree.jsx`, `components/NoteEditor.jsx`, `components/NoteToolbar.jsx`, `lib/notesModel.js`, `lib/notesStore.js`, `lib/notesMarkdown.js`, `lib/notesExtensions.js`), `src/app/Shell.jsx`, `src/app/route.js`, `src/app/modulePrefetch.js`, `src/shared/ui/AppHeader.jsx`, `src/shared/ui/moduleAccent.js`, `src/shared/ui/moduleLoaderTheme.js`, `src/shared/theme/palette.js`, `src/index.css`, `ui-audit/contrast-audit.mjs`, `ui-audit/lib/bundleMetrics.mjs`, `ui-audit/perf-bundle-audit.mjs`, `ui-audit/perf-budgets.json`, `ui-audit/verify-notes.mjs`, `scripts/perf-ratchet.mjs`, `test/notesModel.test.js`, `test/notesMarkdown.test.js`, `test/notesModule.test.js`.

### B1240 — AUDIT ONLY: what datum are setbacks measured from? `[Site Planner]` (task) #site-planner #entitlements  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-6, explicitly scoped "report, do not fix". Minted **B1240** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — **B1191** assigns regulatory ROLES to setback edges and **B1192** the boundary styling; both are about how a setback is LABELLED and neither touches what it is measured FROM. Net-new, and closed by its own report.)*
`[x]` **DONE 2026-07-30 — the audit ran, the answer is below, and NO code changed (as instructed).**
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-6)

**THE ANSWER: setbacks are measured from the PARCEL BOUNDARY AS DRAWN. There is no right-of-way line anywhere in the codebase.**

- `lib/parcelOffset.js` `offsetPolygon(points, setbacks)` insets the parcel ring by the per-edge setback value and nothing else; `setbackRingArea` and the buildable envelope both read that one derivation. The ring's points are whatever geometry was imported or drawn — for an assessor-sourced parcel, the fee polygon exactly as the county publishes it.
- **A repo-wide search for right-of-way handling returns nothing.** No ROW width, no half-width, no dedication, no centerline offset — the strings do not appear in the planner's libraries at all.
- **The nearest thing that exists is NOT this.** `lib/setbackRoles.js` reads real road geometry to decide whether an edge is a Front / Street side / Rear / Side — but a role is a LABEL, and by construction it never writes a setback VALUE. It cannot move the envelope, which is precisely the non-negotiable that item was built under.
- **So the owner's premise holds.** Where a section-line county road runs as a public easement and the fee (and therefore the assessor polygon) reaches the centerline, the buildable envelope is short by roughly half the ROW width along that frontage — 15–25 ft of setback origin error on a typical 30–50 ft county road, in both Texas and Colorado.

**What a fix would involve, and its size (filed, NOT implemented — the owner has judged the acreage effect not worth fixing):**
1. **Getting the ROW line at all is the whole problem, and it is a DATA problem, not a geometry one.** Nothing currently fetched carries it. The candidates are each partial: a county road centerline layer plus a published ROW width per classification (the `thoroughfare/` spine already does exactly this for Houston's MTFP — §42-122 widths by road class — so the pattern exists but only for one jurisdiction); a recorded plat or ROW-dedication instrument (not machine-readable); or the surveyor's line off an imported drawing (already possible today by hand-tracing).
2. **A per-edge ROW offset on the parcel record** — an additive `rowOffsetFt` beside the existing per-edge setback, applied before the setback inset. Small, and it fits the existing model.
3. **The honesty layer is the expensive half.** An inferred ROW line must be visibly labelled as inferred and must never silently move a number the owner is reading — the same provenance discipline as the WSE providers (`SourceTag` / basis popovers), plus a way to say "this frontage's ROW is unknown".
4. **Rough size: one focused session for the per-edge offset + its provenance on ONE jurisdiction's road data; materially more to generalise.** It is NOT a net-vs-gross area feature and must not become one — that was explicitly ruled out.
### B1209 — Setback chip text inherited the setback LINE's colour, so a bright-green line made the numbers unreadable `[Site Planner / parcel]` (bug, regression) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-1. **AMENDS the B1184–B1187 strand (PR #874 / V547): the chip GROUPING fix worked — thirty-plus chips down to four on the owner's Weld parcel — and is NOT re-opened.** Minted **B1209** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`, LATE, as the last step before push. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the chip/colour family: **B1187** made the chip's ink near-black by DEFAULT, **B1100** made the setback line's colour settable and made the chip follow it, **B1192** changed the default colour to the property-line green, **B1184** grouped the chips. B1187 and B1100 are the two halves that collided: B1100's "the chip takes the line's colour with it" was applied to the chip's TEXT as well as its border, so B1187's black ink only ever showed on a parcel that had never been recoloured. This is a genuine REGRESSION of B1187's intent through B1100's mechanism, filed on its own number because neither of those items is wrong about what it meant to do.)*
`[x]` **DONE — verified here 2026-07-31 (Verify: live → V565 **PASSED**, headless Chromium, both themes).** The chip's numerals are always the theme ink token; the setback colour rides the LINE and the chip's BORDER only.
- Verify: live — V565 PASSED 2026-07-31 (archived to `VERIFICATION-DONE.md`)
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-1)
- Amends: B1184–B1187 / V547 (not re-opened) · B1100 (the colour-follows-the-line rule, now scoped to the border)

**The report.** *"The text is bright green, and I thought we talked about the text just being black, and the outline of the thing. So I don't know what happened here — because when I clicked reset setback line then the text went black."* His parcel's setback line is bright green; the chip renders on a white plate, so bright-green numerals on white are barely legible, and **Reset setback line** put the colour back to the near-black default, which is exactly why resetting "fixed" it.

**Cause, confirmed in the code rather than inferred.** The chip was `<rect … stroke={sbCol}>` + `<text … fill={sbCol}>` with `sbCol = pc.sbStroke || PAL.chipInk`. One value drove both the border and the text, so the label's contrast was a function of a decoration the user is free to set to anything.

**The fix.** The chip draws from `setbackChipStyle(PAL.chipInk)` — plate white, border and text `canvasChipInk` (`#15171C`, the same token in both themes). Nothing on the chip reads `pc.sbStroke` any more; the setback LINE still carries the user's colour (B1100), its chip never follows. Because the plate is white in both themes and the ink is one token, the contrast is a fixed **17.9:1** everywhere, which the tests assert rather than assume. **"Darken the user's colour" was considered and rejected** — it still fails on a pale yellow or a near-white, and it leaves legibility depending on a decoration.

**Deviation from the brief, stated rather than buried.** The brief said the colour "belongs on the setback LINE and on the chip's border only". While this was in flight, `setbackChipStyle` landed on `main` and took the border off the line colour **as well** — same reason, one step further: a saturated border on a chip this small reproduces exactly the green-on-white unreadability the ink default was minted to end. That is **kept** rather than reverted; NEW-3's quieting then rides on top as an opacity, which is what makes the border read as the neutral hairline the brief's own item 3 asked for. The bug the owner reported — unreadable numerals that went black when he reset the line — is fixed either way.

> **Tests / verification.** `test/setbackChipQuiet.test.js` — the WCAG contrast of the ink on the plate in light AND dark, that the two themes share the token, and that four real colours a user can pick from the setback colour field (bright green, pale yellow, near-white, cyan) each fail on that plate — the reason the ink token, not a derived colour, is the fix; plus source guards that neither `fill={sbCol}` nor its `const sbCol = selParcel.sbStroke` source can return. `test/setbackChipInk.test.js` (main's guard, retargeted where NEW-3 moved the factory's end) still pins the whole render site to `setbackChipStyle`. Headless: `ui-audit/verify-setback-chip-quiet.mjs` seeds the owner's parcel WITH his bright green and asserts, off the live DOM in both themes, that neither the text nor the border follows it while the setback RING still does.

### B1210 — Setback chips survived to county zoom, where one full-size chip was the loudest thing on the screen `[Site Planner / parcel]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-2. AMENDS B1184's declutter guards; that item is Done and live-verified and is not re-opened. Minted **B1210** via `--against-main`, late. DEDUPE-FIRST — **B1184** added the two screen-space guards this sits on top of, **B121/B951** are the label declutter tier, **B911** the dimension LOD gate, **B880** the sub-pixel setback-ring gate: every one of those is RELATIVE to the thing it measures, which is precisely why none of them could fix this. Net-new gate, not a recurrence.)*
`[x]` **DONE — verified here 2026-07-31 (Verify: live → V565 **PASSED**).** Chips now ride the shared annotation zoom floor and reveal with every other callout and dimension.
- Verify: live — V565 PASSED 2026-07-31
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-2)

**The report + the screenshot.** Zoomed out until the whole 62-acre parcel is a thumbnail against several square miles of county, a full-size **"Front · 25′"** chip is the single largest, loudest thing on screen. *"The setback chip is showing as the only thing I can see when I zoom out — it's kind of pointless at this zoom."*

**Cause.** Both shipped guards are **relative to the parcel**: `CHIP_MIN_EDGE_PX` drops a chip whose anchor edge is too short *on screen*, and `CHIP_MIN_SEP_PX` thins neighbours. On a 62-acre lot the longest run is ~1,700 ft, which clears the edge bar at **any** zoom (at county zoom it is still ~34 px), and separation never applies to a lone survivor. Nothing about the parcel got smaller relative to itself, so no relative guard could ever hide the last chip.

**The fix — an ABSOLUTE floor, and deliberately the one that already exists.** `setbackChipsVisible(ppf, { editing })` gates on `dimCalloutVisible` — the same `DIM_CALLOUT_MIN_PPF` floor every other callout and dimension rides — so the chips leave and return **with** the rest of the annotation instead of standing alone over an empty county. Both relative guards still run after it. The **one exception is deliberate**: a parcel whose setbacks are actively being edited (the user has drilled into *By side* / *Per segment*, or has an inline value editor open) keeps its chips at any zoom, because at that moment they are the edit surface, not annotation.

> **Tests / verification.** `test/setbackChipQuiet.test.js` — hidden at county zoom, shown at working zoom, exactly equal to `dimCalloutVisible` across a zoom sweep, the editing exception, and the arithmetic showing why the relative edge guard alone cannot hide a big parcel's longest chip. Headless: chips are counted at three zooms on the real geometry (plan → overview → back), in both themes, with screenshots.

**What shipped.** The chip is a **control, not a headline**:

### B1212 — Setback chips and the lot's grab band rendered UNDER the buildings, so a setback over a building could not be edited `[Site Planner / z-order]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #selection  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-4. Minted **B1212** via `--against-main`, late. DEDUPE-FIRST — **B820** owns the per-element Arrange z-order, **B671** the `z` stacking key, **B619/B569** the selection chrome: none of them governs where a PARCEL's interactive chrome sits relative to the site elements. **B420** made the setback line a second grab target for the lot — that is the affordance this raises, not one it duplicates. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **DONE — verified here 2026-07-31 (Verify: live → V565 **PASSED**).** A selected lot's setback chrome renders above every site element, and drops back the moment it is deselected.
- Verify: live — V565 PASSED 2026-07-31
- Origin: filed 2026-07-31 from chat (owner block, provisional NEW-4)

**The report.** *"It's annoying if I have a building already there because now I can't edit it because it's behind the building. If I'm already doing the work of clicking on the parcel, then the options to edit the setbacks should be above the elements."* On his Weld plan the buildings sit hard against the setback line, so the chips and the lot's grab band land under a building's fill and the click never reaches them.

**Cause.** Paint order. The chips and the setback-ring grab band were emitted in the parcel band of the canvas — **before** the element pass — so anything drawn later covered them. (The parcel's vertex handles were already in the selection-chrome layer, which is why *those* always worked; the inconsistency is what made this read as arbitrary.)

**The fix.** Both move into the existing `data-export="skip"` **selection-chrome group** at the end of the canvas, and only for the **SELECTED** parcel: selection is the signal of intent, so the lot's controls win for exactly as long as it is selected. Order inside the group is deliberate — grab band first, then the chips (so a chip keeps its own click target over the band), then the vertex handles last (the smallest targets are never covered). Every other parcel keeps its grab band exactly where it was.
- **Only the INTERACTIVE chrome moved.** The setback ring, its casing, the parcel outline and the parcel fill all stay in the parcel band, so a selected lot can never hide a building.
- **The export path is unaffected**, and this is asserted rather than assumed: the chips still carry `data-export="skip"` and the group they moved into is itself `data-export="skip"`, so `exportSheet`'s one `querySelectorAll('[data-export="skip"]').remove()` still strips them.
- **Stated trade-off:** while a lot is selected, a press within the grab band along its setback ring moves the LOT even where a building is painted there. That is the behaviour asked for, it is scoped to the selected lot, and deselecting restores the old order.

> **Tests / verification.** `test/setbackChipQuiet.test.js` source guards — the chips and the band render after the element pass, inside the chrome group, in that order, with the handles last; the ring / casing / outline are still BEFORE the chrome group; the export-skip attribute survives the move. Headless: with a building deliberately covering the whole interior, **8 of 8 chips sit over the building**, every one is the topmost element at its own centre, and clicking one opens its inline editor.

**The report.** *"If I double click on the parcel, it shows the owner as Forestar USA, and then the next line is just the owner as Forestar USA again. And then the legal description is probably too much information — there should probably just be a dot dot dot and a dropdown so that we can see the rest of the information."*

**(a) The duplicate — cause, and it is NOT the one the brief predicted.** The brief's hypothesis was that the matcher emits one row per matching COLUMN (e.g. `OWNER_NAME` **and** `NAME_CARE`, which the Weld-shaped records really do both carry). **That is not what happens, and the code says so:** `apprRows` walks `APPR_FIELDS` **once per LABEL** with a used-key set, so it is already one row per logical FIELD, first matching column wins — for every field, not just Owner. The actual defect was one layer up: the panel rendered a dedicated **Owner headline** *and then* the curated list, which contains an Owner row. Two renderers, one fact. (Worse, the headline used a **local copy** of the Owner regex rather than the shared field map, so the two could have disagreed about which column the owner comes from.)
**The fix.** The headline reads the shared `ownerName(attrs)`, and the list is built by `parcelPanelRows`, which drops any row that merely repeats the headline. The one-row-per-field property is now **guarded** rather than merely true (`test/parcelPanelRows.test.js`), including on a record offering several candidate columns per field. Only an EXACT repeat of the headline is dropped — three money rows all reading `$0` are three real facts and all three survive.

**(b) The long tail.** The default view is **Situs address · Account / ID · Acreage**. Everything else — Land value, Improvement value, Total value, Land use, Zoning, Year built and the unbounded metes-and-bounds **Legal** description — folds behind one **closed** `More details (n)` disclosure, with the Legal value height-capped so it scrolls in place instead of growing the panel. The separate "All county fields" expander is untouched.

**One derivation, two hosts — the choice, stated.** The planner panel and B1166's map-search card **share `appraisal.splitCuratedRows`** (which rows, in what order, formatted how) on top of the `apprRows` field resolution they already shared; `parcelCardRows` is now a one-line call into it. They do **not** share a component: one is a floating card over the map with its own dismiss/plan actions, the other a docked panel Section. Sharing the derivation is what stops them drifting; sharing the component would have forced a props-shaped compromise on both. `test/parcelPanelRows.test.js` pins the sharing itself, and `ui-audit/verify-parcel-card-height.mjs` re-run 13/13 proves the card is unchanged by the refactor.

**Paid for its own bytes.** The panel's two Sections moved into `components/ParcelDataPanel.jsx` behind `LazyPanel` (the B1064 tranche): they only ever render for a lot that came from a county identify, and they were riding the planner's boot chunk for every session. With `ParcelInfoCard` also made lazy, this change is a **net −2.2 KB on the largest chunk** despite adding six features — measured against a stashed build of the same base.

> **Tests / verification.** `test/parcelPanelRows.test.js` — 11 cases on a Weld-shaped synthetic record (owner exactly once; a second owner-ish column never becomes a second row; one row per logical field, for every field; three `$0` rows all survive; the three-row default; Legal never in the default view and always last in the tail; nothing curated is lost; the empty case; and the shared-derivation pins). Headless: the owner headline appears **once**, the default view is exactly the three rows, and the fold is **closed** with 5 rows behind it — in both themes.

### B1188 — Single click on a pond opened the left inspector, and any drag closed it: the panel's open/closed state was DERIVED from the selection `[Site Planner / interaction]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #selection #pond  *(owner chat block 2026-07-30, provisional NEW-1: "not sure why but single clicks open up the left menu on ponds, fix that, and check other elements, measurements, parcels, buildings, etc." — then the amendment that named the root cause: "I click on the pond, it automatically pops the menu open — the properties menu open. And then if I click-click and drag anywhere on screen, the menu disappears. So weird behavior." Minted **B1188** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Branch `claude/pond-click-inspector-audit-e17dlm`.)*
`[x]` **DONE — sandbox-verified 2026-07-30 (Verify: sandbox; ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK — this is a logged-out, no-external-GIS UI check, so it was DRIVEN here, not parked).** Single click now only selects, on every type; a double-click opens the inspector; and no pointer gesture on the canvas — click, drag, marquee, pan or deselect — can change whether the left panel is open.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat (owner NEW-1 + same-turn amendment)
- **DEDUPE-FIRST — this AMENDS B750 and REVOKES B875's exception; it is not net-new behaviour and not a recurrence.** Searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for click · double-click · select · inspector · panel-open. **B750** ("Clicking an element auto-opened its Properties menu; make single-click SELECT and double-click OPEN Properties", Done, V263 PASSED) is the STANDING CONVENTION and the audit confirmed the codebase already documents it — so per the owner's own instruction ("unless your audit shows the codebase already has a different documented one — in which case follow THAT"), B1188 enforces B750 rather than inventing a contract. **B875** ("Pond discoverability: click / label / right-click reach the pond inspector") deliberately carved a pond-shaped hole in B750 — that hole IS the owner's bug, and it is closed here. **B656** made parcel selection auto-open the Parcel panel — the second, unreported violation the audit found. **B948** (location-based callout double-click) and **B912** (dimension single-vs-double) are consistent with the contract and are preserved unchanged. Not a B750 recurrence: B750's fix stuck; later items re-opened the door beside it.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — the state model, and why one defect produced both symptoms.** B750 implemented "a plain click must not open Properties" with a marker, `propsFor`, that had to keep MATCHING the current selection (`propsMatches`) for the panel to render, plus an effect that cleared it whenever the selection moved. So the panel's open/closed state was never owner-owned — it was a function of the selection, and it flapped in both directions: any path that set the marker (B875's pond reveal, B656's parcel effect) opened the panel on a plain click, and any deselect — a click-drag on empty canvas is a deselect — evaporated a panel the owner had opened himself. The owner's read was exactly right; both halves are one bug.
- **THE FIX — separate the two pieces of state, structurally.** `propsFor` / `propsMatches` are **deleted**. The inspector is open exactly when the DOCK holds it (`leftPanel === "properties"`) on desktop, or when the phone companion overlay is up (`narrowProps`) — both already owner-toggled. `companionOpen` is now `narrow ? narrowProps : leftPanel === "properties"`, with **no reference to `sel` at all**. One explicit `openInspector()` (double-click on any type, the pond reveal, the right-click "Properties…" row, the ✎ pill) and one explicit `closeInspector()` (the ✕, Esc, the rail tab) are the ONLY two things that can change it. The dock takeover moved out of a selection-keyed `useLayoutEffect` and into `openInspector` itself. Selection now chooses the panel's BODY only: with nothing selected it renders the pre-existing "Nothing selected" state — widened from the Properties TAB to ANY open inspector, and given its own ✕ — so a deselect swaps contents instead of vanishing.
- **Removed, by name, so they cannot come back:** the parcel auto-open effect (`if (sel?.kind === "parcel") setLeftPanel("parcel")`), the phone effect `if (!companionSel) setNarrowProps(false)`, the marker-clearing effect, and B875's `revealPondSel` plain-click branch (both the locked and unlocked paths).
- **Per-type conformance (the owner asked us to check them all).** POND — plain click selects only; the double-click still routes through `revealPondInspector`, so B875's scroll+flash onto the pond card is preserved, as are the map label (now double-click, single click selects), the right-click menu rows and Enter. PARCEL — single click selects; a DOUBLE-click opens the Parcel panel (a parcel's inspector IS that list+detail destination), via a new `openParcelPanel()`; checked before the locked/unlocked split so it works on the county-pulled locked default too. BUILDING / PAVING / PARKING / TRAILER / ROAD / EASEMENT / LINE / RECTANGLE / ELLIPSE / POLYGON / POLYLINE / MEASUREMENT / CALLOUT / TEXT — already conformant under B750; every one now routes its double-click through the single `openInspector`. Callout keeps B948's location split (text interior edits in place, border opens the inspector).
- **THE CONTRACT IS NOW DECLARED ONCE AND MACHINE-CHECKED.** `e2e/clickContract.table.js` is the single table (type · label · which surface its double-click opens), shared by both halves of the net. `test/clickContract.test.js` reads the planner's OWN `DRAW_TYPES` / `MARKUP_TOOLS` registries and **fails until a newly added selectable type has a row**, then pins the invariants at source level: no `setPropsFor` / `propsMatches` may return, `companionOpen` must not mention the selection, exactly one `setLeftPanel("properties")` exists and it is inside `openInspector`, and neither removed effect may reappear. `e2e/click-contract.spec.js` drives the REAL app per type: panel closed + single click → still closed; panel open on ANOTHER tab + single click → still that tab (no takeover on select); double click → the declared surface; **panel open + click-drag on empty canvas → still open** (the owner's second symptom, in the regression net verbatim); panel open + deselect → still open, showing "Nothing selected". Plus a case proving the rail button and ✕ still work and are the only things that do. The left rail tabs gained `data-rail-tab` so "which panel holds the dock" is one observable fact.
- **Sandbox evidence (headless Chromium, logged out, `vite preview` of a production build).** New `click-contract` spec **11/11** across pond · building · paving · trailer · road · easement · rectangle markup · measurement · parcel, plus a NARROW (phone) case — a tap only selects, the ✎ pill is the explicit open, a deselect leaves the companion up on the empty state — and the affordances case. Full unit suite **6628** green (incl. the updated `bugHuntGuards` / `measureWiring` source guards and the new `clickContract` suite) · lint 0 errors on the changed file (identical warning set to baseline) · build green · `MAP.md` / `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` / doc-pointer / contrast / panel-copy-budget checks all green. Its `e2e/canvas-click-pan-jump.spec.js` asserted "the panel closing on a background click is intended" — the very selection-derived visibility this item removes — so that one assertion now reads "stays open on Nothing selected, canvas edge unmoved". B1175's fix STANDS and still protects the drag/pan paths; its invariant (the drawing does not move) is unchanged and now holds trivially, because there is no dock swap left for a gesture to race: `canvas left 380 → 380 → 380 · offX -266 → -266 → -266`. `main`'s new `startMeasChip` double-tap (B1174) was also routed through the one `openInspector`, and its source guard updated with it.
