### B1140 — The hover elevation tag is drawn UNDER the mouse pointer, which covers the number `[Site Planner / GIS]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #ui  *(owner chat 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-1. Minted **B1140** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the hover/contour family (`B1087`, `B1088`, `B1095`, `B1096`, `contourLabelText`, `CONTOUR_HOVER_CLASS`, "hover label"): **NOT a recurrence of B1095** — B1095's hit-test and its VALUE are correct and stay untouched. This is a net-new PLACEMENT item against the shipped build.)* *(RENUMBERED TWICE before merge, and the second time into a DELIBERATELY GAPPED block (B1140–B1143 / V530, skipping B1136–B1139): main merged three PRs while this branch was in flight — #860 took B1130/B1131/V523 and #862 took B1132/V524, each the number `next-id` had just reported. The B779/B780 uniqueness guard caught both collisions RED before merge, exactly as designed. Leaving a gap costs nothing (`next-id` reads the max) and breaks a loop that had already cost two renumber passes. Code and tests carried the provisional NEW-1/NEW-2 labels throughout, so only heading lines and three comment references ever moved.)*
`[x]` **DONE — sandbox-verified 2026-07-30 (Verify: sandbox).** The tag is offset off the pointer and flips at every edge, driven and asserted in a real browser on real Katy LiDAR.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-30 from chat
- **Report.** Tsakiris, Contour lines (1 ft) on, z17+. Hover any contour: the tag paints AT the cursor and the pointer glyph — a large grab hand while the Pan tool is armed, which is most of the time — sits on top of the number. Owner: *"my mouse shows a grab and it ends up covering the elevation that I'm trying to see."*
- **Fix.** `contours.js` gains the pure placement decision (`hoverLabelPlacement` / `hoverLabelSize` / `HOVER_LABEL_GAP_PX`): the tag's NEAR EDGE sits a fixed number of SCREEN pixels off the pointer (so the clearance is identical at every zoom), default up-and-right, and the quadrant FLIPS — up-left, down-right, down-left — for the first one whose whole rect fits. Nothing fits (a box barely bigger than the tag) → the least-bad quadrant is clamped inside the box, and a clamp that would slide the tag back under the glyph re-flips the other axis instead. The gap is sized against the LARGEST cursor glyph in use (grab/grabbing), not the arrow.
- **The box is the VISIBLE canvas, not the container.** `terrainLayers.visibleBox` measures the clip parent against the overscanned map container, so the tag can't be silently cut off by the clip (container coordinates run well past what the user can see). A bottom band is reserved for the furniture the planner floats over its own bottom edge — the coordinate/elevation chip bottom-left, the scale bar and zoom cluster bottom-right. The right-hand **Tools rail needs no reserve**: it is a flex SIBLING of the canvas, so it is outside this box already.
- **One trap worth recording:** an in-flow `inline-block` sits on the marker div's LINE BOX, so the inherited font's baseline strut pushed the tag a few px below the anchor — invisible when a label is merely centred "about" its point, decisive when the placement is exact arithmetic against a canvas edge. The offset variant is `position:absolute;left:0;top:0` so its top-left IS the anchor. Permanent index labels keep the historic centred markup byte for byte.
- **Everything B1095 shipped is preserved and re-asserted:** one tag at a time, own sublayer cleared every move, same white-halo style and size, the ≤40 px no-double-stamp rule, the z16 gate, the shared throttled mousemove (no second listener), and B1087's supersession guard. The hover key now carries the pointer's whole-pixel position, because the tag is anchored at the CURSOR — without it the tag would sit still while the pointer moved along one contour.
- **Tests.** `test/pointerRegistration.test.js` (15 cases on the pure placement: default quadrant, every edge and corner, the reserved bottom band, a tiny box, screen-invariance, the width over-estimate) **including an explicit "B1095's placement would have FAILED this" case** so the guard can't be vacuous. `e2e/contour-hover-elevation.spec.js` gains a browser test that runs a lap just inside all four canvas edges with contours ON and asserts, per painted tag: it never intersects the pointer glyph's footprint, never leaves the visible canvas or the reserved bottom row, and that BOTH flips actually fired (else "never clipped" could pass vacuously). Stale frames are detected and skipped rather than asserted.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` 6364 green · lint 0 errors · build green · the whole `contour-hover-elevation` spec file green (7 tests, incl. the pre-existing one-label/no-ghost/no-double-stamp assertions).
- **One residual, stated rather than implied:** the glyph clearance is asserted against a stated pointer footprint (headless Chromium renders no cursor bitmap). An OS "large cursor" accessibility setting draws a bigger hand than that; if that ever comes up, the gap is one named constant.

### B1143 — The boundary magnet's reach was unbounded in FEET, so a placed point could be yanked tens of feet at overview zoom `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #coordinates #ui  *(found 2026-07-30 by B1141's audit item (d). Minted **B1143** via `--against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST: no existing item covers the boundary magnet's world reach; the road-connect magnet's own cap is `ROAD_CONNECT_MAX_FT` (B945/B949/B961) and is the precedent this follows, not a duplicate.)* *(RENUMBERED TWICE before merge, and the second time into a DELIBERATELY GAPPED block (B1140–B1143 / V530, skipping B1136–B1139): main merged three PRs while this branch was in flight — #860 took B1130/B1131/V523 and #862 took B1132/V524, each the number `next-id` had just reported. The B779/B780 uniqueness guard caught both collisions RED before merge, exactly as designed. Leaving a gap costs nothing (`next-id` reads the max) and breaks a loop that had already cost two renumber passes. Code and tests carried the provisional NEW-1/NEW-2 labels throughout, so only heading lines and three comment references ever moved.)*
`[x]` **DONE — sandbox-verified 2026-07-30 (Verify: sandbox).**
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: found 2026-07-30 during B1141
- **What was wrong.** The first point of a measurement (and of a Line markup) snaps onto a nearby parcel boundary on purpose, so a setback measurement can begin on the property line. Its tolerance was a pure screen distance with **no world cap**: about two feet at a working zoom, and roughly **70 ft at the overview zoom real layout is done at**. So a click could be pulled tens of feet onto a property line with nothing on screen to say so — from the seat, indistinguishable from *"my point landed five, ten, fifteen feet from where I clicked."* Caught by the B1141 harness, which reported a 4.5 ft east pull as if it were a transform error; it is not, it is this.
- **Fix.** `lib/edgeConstrain.js` now owns the tolerance: `edgeLockTolFt(ppf) = min(EDGE_LOCK_PX / ppf, EDGE_LOCK_MAX_FT)` — screen tolerance, capped in the world, the same idiom the road-connect magnet already uses. Both call sites move to it (the snap itself and the Shift-lock angle recovery, which must agree or the lock would be recovered from a point that wasn't snapped). Holding **Alt** still bypasses the snap entirely. The **Split** tool's separate boundary snap is deliberately left uncapped: a split has to land ON the line, so being pulled there is the intent, not a surprise.
- **Tests.** `test/pointerRegistration.test.js` — a working zoom is the plain screen tolerance; the overview zoom is capped (with the pre-fix reach asserted at >80 ft, so the guard has teeth); a zero/negative/NaN scale can never yield a nonsense tolerance.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` 6364 green · lint 0 errors · build green · the constants moved into the pure lib so the cap is unit-tested rather than buried in `SitePlanner.jsx`.

### B1130 — Point features in a vector overlay render as Leaflet's DEFAULT marker, so substations paint as broken-image glyphs labelled "Mark" `[Site Planner / vectorOverlay]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #ui  *(owner-reported 2026-07-29 from chat with a screenshot: the Electric layer on over an aerial, two broken-image icons labelled "Mark" standing where the substations should be. Arrived as provisional "ITEM 1"; minted **B1130** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat. DEDUPE-FIRST: searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `marker`, `pointToLayer`, `broken.image`, `"Mark"` — nothing. The closest prior item is **B695** (hover/click identify + labels for the cached BOUNDARY layers), which is a different mechanism on different layers and explicitly noted that `featureLayerOptions` builds its layers `interactive:false` without changing it. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **Shipped — a GeoJSON POINT with no `pointToLayer` fell through to `L.marker` + an unresolvable `L.Icon.Default`.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **Root cause, confirmed in code.** Leaflet's documented default for a GeoJSON Point with no `pointToLayer` is `L.marker(latlng)` wearing `L.Icon.Default`, and nothing in this repo ever configured `L.Icon.Default`'s image paths for the bundler (`grep`: no `Icon.Default`, no `marker-icon` reference anywhere in `src/`). So the icon's PNG 404s, the browser paints its broken-image glyph, and the marker's alt text — the string `"Marker"` — is clipped by the icon box to read **"Mark"**. Every *other* `L.marker` call site passes an explicit icon (`MapFinder`'s `sitePinIcon`, `terrainLayers`' `labelIcon`, `vectorOverlay`'s label `divIcon`), which is why ONLY GeoJSON point features were affected — and substations are points.
- **⚠ THE REPORT NAMED ONE FILE; THERE WERE THREE PATHS, and the live one was not the file named.** The brief traced it to `vectorOverlay.js:207`'s `L.geoJSON(null, {…})`. That call is genuinely defective, but it is **latent** — every `VECTOR_SOURCES` row today is polygon or line. What actually painted the owner's glyphs is **`layerRequest.js:78` `featureLayerOptions`**, the esri-leaflet path: `hifld_substations` is `kind: "esriFeature"`, and esri-leaflet delegates to `L.GeoJSON.geometryToLayer(geojson, this.options)`, so it inherits the same default. That path also affects `env_cleanups`, `faa_airports` and `txdot_aadt` — all point layers, all broken the same way, none of them mentioned in the report. A third site (`vectorOverlay.js`'s `cachedPipelineLayer`) was found by the guard test after the first two were fixed.
- **Fix.** `mapSymbols.js` (new) owns a `pointToLayerFor(cfg, opacity)` returning a styled `L.circleMarker` in the source's own colour + weight, matching how `evidenceLayers.js` already draws OSM power points; the pure options half is `layerRequest.pointSymbolOptions` (kept leaflet-free so it unit-tests in the node env). Applied at all three construction sites. `EL.featureLayer` is now built in exactly ONE place (`layers.buildFeatureLayer`).
- **Two follow-on defects the fix exposed, both fixed here.** (a) `L.geoJSON` applies its `style` option to circleMarkers too, so the boundary style's `fillOpacity: 0.02` hit-area fill would have flattened a point to near-invisible — `baseStyle` / `styleFeature` are now geometry-aware (`isPointFeature`). (b) the flat `setOpacity` shim sent `{opacity}` only, which dims a stroke but not a disc's FILL, so a dimmed substation stayed solid; it now re-derives a point's whole symbology.
- **Belt and braces.** `installDefaultMarkerIcon()` points `L.Icon.Default` at the real bundled PNGs (imported so Vite resolves them — all three inline as `data:` URIs under the 4 KB limit, verified in `dist/`) and deletes Leaflet's `_getIconUrl` path-guessing hook, so any future accidental default marker degrades to an honest pin instead of a broken image.
- **Guard (the brief's, plus what it caught).** `test/pointSymbology.test.js` — 17 assertions: the pure symbol options, and a STRUCTURAL lock that `EL.featureLayer` has exactly one construction site and every `L.geoJSON` passes a `pointToLayer`. **That structural assertion is what found the third defective call site** (`cachedPipelineLayer`), which neither the report nor the initial fix covered. DOM-level assertions (zero `img` with a default-icon src, zero `alt="Marker"`, zero failed-to-load images, zero marker-pane images, and a Point producing a circleMarker) live in `e2e/layer-point-hover-identify.spec.js` because leaflet cannot be imported in the node test env — 8/8 passing, both themes screenshotted.
- **Bundle budget (`ui-audit/perf-bundle-audit.mjs`) — paid with optimization, and this is the part worth reading.** The naive fix imports leaflet's three marker PNGs; each is under Vite's 4 KB `assetsInlineLimit`, so all three base64-inline into the planner chunk — **~6 KB of JS on the site route's critical path, permanently, for images that should never be fetched at all.** Both Vite-5 ways of emitting them as files were tried and neither works here (`?no-inline` is a **Vite 6** feature — on Vite 5 it silently resolves to nothing, which leaves the fallback BROKEN rather than merely heavy; and `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` against a `node_modules` path emits nothing either). So the requirement was re-read instead of brute-forced: what it has to guarantee is that an accidental default marker degrades to a **real pin**, not that it is byte-identical to Leaflet's blue one. A hand-authored teardrop SVG data URI does that in **~400 bytes instead of ~6 KB** — same guarantee, no vendored copies of a dependency's assets to drift out of sync with the leaflet version. `shadowUrl: null` so the fallback never appends a second `<img>` that can itself fail to load.
- Also: `hitFeature` (`vectorLayers.js`) gained Point / MultiPoint support. Without it a substation was **unhittable** on the planner canvas — the click/hover identify could reach lines and bands but never a point asset. Recorded as a tolerance hit so an exact polygon containment still wins the two-pass ordering.

### B1110 — `detVerdict` / `detTone` / `detSub` are computed by every branch of the detention verdict block and read by none `[Site Planner / Yield]` (bug) #yield #ui  *(minted via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST: no existing item covers this block's dead stores. Found 2026-07-29 while verifying B1104 against the SHIPPED bundle rather than the source.)*
`[x]` **✅ Done 2026-07-29 (sandbox) — DECIDED: DELETED, not wired up. And a guard for the whole class shipped alongside (B1128).**
- **The decision this item asked for, and the reasoning.** The item said *"decide, don't just delete."* Decided: **delete.** Rendering the verdict text next to the chip would put the requirement pair in the panel TWICE — the verdict strip (G1) already carries it, and PANEL-BREVITY rule 5 is explicit that the same sentence may not render in more than one place. So a dead store whose surface has moved on gets removed, not rehomed. `detVerdict`, `detTone` and `detSub` are gone; every branch now assigns only `detChip`, and `test/deadStores.test.js` asserts the three names cannot come back as declarations.
- **The related bug found while doing it, which was bigger than this item.** The item recorded that `detChip` *is* consumed. It is — but only to derive a tone and a status word: **the chip STRING never reached the DOM either.** The detention group's closed face read `"{N} ponds · check"`, so on a Colorado site nothing on screen said Colorado at all, and the verdict strip separately rendered a permanent "checking flood data" spinner. Both fixed as **B1127**; `detChip` is now passed to the group header (for the unavailable kind only, so no Texas panel changes).
- **Correction to this item's own note, and to `BACKLOG.md`'s B1104 render line.** Both recorded that "what reaches the screen is the `N/A · CO` chip in warn tone plus the explicit line". That was **wrong on both halves**: the chip string was not rendered, and the line renders inside the collapsed "Assumptions & method" fold, not on the visible face. The lesson the item drew — that verifying against the built bundle beats a source-level assertion — holds, and this is a second instance of it: reading the source said the chip rendered, and it did not.
- Verify: sandbox — green build, `npm test` 373 files green, and `test/deadStores.test.js` guards the regression
- **How it surfaced, which is the useful part.** `ui-audit/verify-colorado-guard.mjs` asserts the guard's copy is present in the shipped JS. One string it expected — the verdict text — was **absent from every built chunk** while its sibling chip string was present. The minified output shows why: in `SitePlanner.jsx`'s detention verdict block (~line 22093) every branch assigns `detVerdict`, `detTone` and `detSub`, but only **`detChip`** is ever read (the group header + `detShort`). The minifier drops the rest as dead stores.
- **Not a Colorado regression** — it affects the Texas branches identically (the band branch's ``${f1(req.bandAcFt[0])}–${f1(req.bandAcFt[1])} ac-ft`` is discarded the same way). It looks like leftovers from the v3 A2/A3 rework, whose own comment says the requirement pair "lives once, in the verdict strip (G1)" — the locals stayed behind when the surface moved.
- **Decide, don't just delete.** Either the verdict TEXT should render alongside the chip (in which case wire it up — it is genuinely more informative than a 3-letter chip), or it should not (in which case remove ~15 dead assignments and the two unused locals). Both are small; the wrong move is leaving code that reads as if it renders when it does not, because that is how a claim like "the panel reads `not in Colorado yet`" gets written down and believed.
- **Lesson worth keeping:** a source-level assertion would never have caught this. Verifying against the built bundle did.

### B1127 — Every Colorado site's verdict strip read "Detention: checking flood data" — a permanent spinner for a number that is never coming `[Site Planner / Yield]` (bug) #yield #ui #floodplain  *(minted via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Found 2026-07-29 while auditing B1105's render path before building on it. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done: **B1110** is the neighbouring dead-store item and is NOT this (that one is unread locals; this is a missing branch in a different module, `lib/yieldVerdicts.js`); **B1104** built the guard whose state this defect suppressed. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ Done 2026-07-29 (sandbox — proved in a real headless browser, logged out, with every GIS endpoint blocked).**
- Verify: sandbox
- **The defect.** `yieldVerdicts.detentionVerdict` had no branch for `req.kind === "unavailable"`. That kind matches none of the numeric branches, so it fell through to `loadingRow` — pill `…`, sentence **"checking flood data"**, `loading: true` — **permanently, on every Colorado site.** The Colorado guard's whole purpose is a NAMED state rather than a wait: its own code comment says "UNKNOWN" was rejected because it "would read as *we could not look it up*, inviting the reader to wait for a number that is never coming". A spinner does exactly that, only worse.
- **Why nothing caught it.** The carrier was correct the whole time; 26 guard unit tests passed; the shipped-bundle harness passed (the copy WAS in the right chunk). Nobody asserted what the *strip* rendered. Reproduced mechanically in four lines of Node before any code was changed, then in the browser.
- **A second, compounding half.** `SitePlanner.jsx` computed `detChip = "N/A · CO"` and never passed it to the group header — it only fed a tone comparison — so the detention group's closed face read `"{N} ponds · check"` and **nothing on screen said Colorado**. The one honest line lived inside the collapsed "Assumptions & method" fold. So the state was invisible on the two surfaces a reader actually looks at.
- **Fix.** A named `unavailableDetentionRow`: pill `N/A`, `loading: false` explicitly, `short:false`/`action:false` (nothing is wrong with the design, so no ⚡ Optimize cure is offered), `sortRank 2.5` so it sits below real verdicts and above "not checked yet", carrying the components and what each still needs. MHFD names its two volumes in the row itself ("MHFD WQCV + EURV — not carried yet"). `detChip` is now passed to the group header **for the unavailable kind only**, so no Texas panel changes, and the closed face reads a named state instead of a check verdict.
- **PANEL-BREVITY.** The new sentence is assembled from a computed subject so the budget counts ONE string, not one per regime: `12 lines / 595 chars → 12 / 595`, zero growth.
- **Evidence.** `test/mhfdDetention.test.js` carries the regression guard (asserts `loading` falsy, no "checking flood data", and that Texas rows stay byte-identical) · `ui-audit/verify-b1105-mhfd-panel.mjs` asserts it **in the DOM** across a Denver plan, a Larimer plan and a Texas plan · golden master green.

### B1128 — The dead-store ratchet: no NEW computed-but-never-read value may land `[Tooling / CI]` (task) #testing #ui  *(minted via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Filed and shipped 2026-07-29 from the B1105 dispatch's "propose a cheap guard for the whole class" instruction. DEDUPE-FIRST: **B1110** is one instance of the class, not a guard for it; no existing item enables `no-unused-vars` or ratchets it. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ Done 2026-07-29 (sandbox).**
- Verify: sandbox
- **Why.** Four "computed but never rendered" defects in five dispatches (see **B1126** for the full class analysis). The variable half is statically detectable and this repo simply never enabled the rule: `eslint.config.js` is deliberately minimal and carries **no `no-unused-vars`**, so a local assigned in every branch and read in none compiles, minifies and ships silently — exactly B1110.
- **Why a RATCHET, not a clean gate.** Turning the rule on as an error fails in **136 places (90 in `src/`)**, mostly harmless (unused icon components, destructured setters). So `ui-audit/dead-store-baseline.json` freezes the count **per file** and it may only go DOWN: a new dead store fails immediately, existing ones get paid off whenever a session is in that file anyway. No false-positive tax, and the class stops recurring from today. `--update` **refuses to raise a total** — a new one must be fixed, not blessed.
- **Scoped deliberately to "assigned a value but never used".** Unused imports and unused params are cosmetic and would triple the baseline, burying the signal.
- **⭐ IT CAUGHT A REAL ONE WITHIN MINUTES OF EXISTING, from a concurrent session.** Merging `main` (PR #858, the trailer-court / inspector work) turned this test red immediately: **two NEW dead stores** that landed before the guard existed — an `alongUnit` ALONG-wall helper in `SitePlanner.jsx` that nothing called, whose own comment claimed it kept "screen math and layout math" in agreement (precisely the dead code that reads as load-bearing and is not), and an `nx` in `siteModel.js`'s alongLen heal where only the across component is read. Both fixed here rather than banked — and note the guard **would not let me bank them**: `--update` refuses to raise a total, by design. The `alongUnit` deletion also names where the live derivation is, so a future caller takes the one copy instead of reviving a second that can drift. This is the class going non-recurring in practice, not just in principle.
- **Ships as** `ui-audit/dead-store-audit.mjs` (report / `--check` / `--update`) + `test/deadStores.test.js`, so `npm test` carries it. Honest about its limit: it catches the unread-VARIABLE shape, **not** the unmounted-JSX shape — that half is **B1126**.

### B1129 — A Denver site lost its MHFD answer whenever the GIS endpoints were down `[Site Planner / detention]` (bug) #yield #gis #floodplain  *(minted via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Found 2026-07-29 by the B1105 DOM harness, which failed for exactly this reason. DEDUPE-FIRST: no existing item covers the regime resolution's input precedence. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ Done 2026-07-29 (sandbox — proved headless with every external host blocked, which is the whole point).**
- Verify: sandbox
- **The defect, and why it mattered more than it looks.** `coRegime` resolved from the **identified** county only — `drainCtxData.authority.jurisdiction.county`, which comes from the drainage GIS context. With that context unresolved (external hosts blocked, a county service down, a plan opened offline) the regime was null, the fail-closed seam did its job, and a Denver site silently dropped to the blanket "not available in Colorado" guard instead of its MHFD answer. That **directly contradicts the principle the entire Colorado tier is built on**, stated in `siteRegion.js`'s own header: the guard has to hold when every GIS endpoint is down, *because that is exactly when a site is most likely to fall through to a default*.
- **Fix.** The plan's OWN saved county is the fallback; the identified county still wins when it exists, because it is the better fact. Applied consistently to the regime, the evaluator's county argument and the jurisdiction note.
- **Why this cannot introduce a wrong answer.** `coloradoRegimeFor` maps Colorado county slugs and nothing else, so the `county` field's well-known Harris default (the B1091 warning in the Site Planner folder pointer) returns **null** and falls straight through to the hard guard — and `computeMhfdDetention` re-checks membership against whatever it is handed and refuses a non-member. The fallback can only ever ADD a correct resolution.
- **Evidence.** `ui-audit/verify-b1105-mhfd-panel.mjs` asserts "the regime resolved with all GIS endpoints down (plan's saved county)" against a seeded Denver plan in a browser with no network, and asserts a Larimer plan still names no district.

### B1125 — Building properties panel goes unresponsive: double-click won't open it, the ✕ won't close it `[Site Planner / inspector]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #selection  *(owner chat 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-3. Minted **B1125**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched `propsFor` / `dockMemo` / `propsTab` / "Close properties" across Open, ⏳ Verify and Done: **B750** made the inspector explicit-open, **B733** gave it a docked tab and **NEW-1 (single-occupancy dock)** added the takeover memo. This is the seam BETWEEN those three; no prior item reports a dead close control. Not a recurrence. Verify: **sandbox** — reproduced AND fixed in a headless browser, logged out, single clean tab → Done.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.** Both directions respond, and Escape is now a guaranteed way out.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Report (owner, verbatim).** "I'm clicking X on element to close, or on the properties menu to close out the building properties, and it's literally not responding. And before that, I was double clicking on the building to open the properties menu and it wasn't responding either."
- **REPRODUCED FIRST, as asked — and the condition matters.** A single clean tab, logged out, on a blank site: draw a building → click the rail's **Properties** tab → double-click the building (panel opens) → click ✕ → **the panel does not close.** `e2e/inspector-close.spec.js` failed on `main` at exactly that assertion (panel count 1, expected 0) and passes on this branch. **The second-tab concurrent-writer condition was NOT required** — the bug is deterministic state logic, so there was no race to chase. (No `client_errors` telemetry for the window, consistent with that: nothing throws.)
- **Root cause — the seam between B733 and the NEW-1 takeover.** The ✕ only dropped the explicit-open marker (`setPropsFor(null)`). That suffices while the inspector holds the dock through its takeover memo, but the panel ALSO renders through `propsTab && companionSel` — and **any deliberate rail click clears the memo** (`setDockMemo(null)`), while the relinquish in the takeover layout effect is guarded by `if (memo)`. So `leftPanel` stayed `"properties"`, the second branch kept rendering, and every click landed, every handler ran, and nothing changed. The "double-click won't open" half is the same stuck panel seen from the other side: with the panel already up (and stuck), a double-click produces no visible change either. The relinquish can't simply be un-guarded — it must NOT fire when the tab was opened deliberately with nothing selected, or the docked Properties tab could never stay open at all. So dismissal is now explicit.
- **Fix.** ONE `closeInspector()` shared by the ✕ and the keyboard: it drops the marker AND releases the dock — back to the panel the inspector replaced when there is a memo, otherwise to nothing — so the panel is gone either way, which is what ✕ promises. **Escape is now a guaranteed escape hatch**: it closes the inspector first (element stays selected, matching ✕) and consumes the key; a second Escape falls through to the existing catch-all deselect. The panel's visibility is mirrored to `inspectorShowingRef` during render because the window keydown listener's dep list does not include `leftPanel` — the ref is the live truth, the render branch and the ref are one fact.
- **Investigated in the order the brief specified, and (1) was real too — hardened.** With a colour picker open, `document.elementFromPoint` over the building returns `AnchoredMenu`'s click-away backdrop: `position:fixed; inset:0` at z-index 4000, covering the whole app including the panel ✕. Correct while a visible menu needs dismissing (it costs one click), indefensible otherwise — and it WAS reachable otherwise: `placeMenu` returns null for a zero-sized anchor (its host rail/panel gone `display:none`), and the old code left a stale `pos` standing, so an invisible layer could swallow clicks with nothing on screen to explain it. The backdrop is now gated on the menu actually being placed, and a stale `pos` is cleared when the anchor stops being measurable. **The Standards sticky footer was NOT a suspect on inspection** — it is a real flow sibling (`flex:none`), not an overlay, so it cannot intercept anything. (2) re-render churn was not the cause: the panel opens and closes fine with the element nodes being re-rendered underneath.
- **Tests.** `e2e/inspector-close.spec.js` (3, logged out): ✕ closes the inspector when the Properties rail TAB holds the dock, and it re-opens on the next double-click · Escape closes it · double-click opens and ✕ closes while element rows are replaced underneath. `e2e/single-occupancy-dock.spec.js` re-run green (the takeover/restore contract is unchanged).
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` 6299 green (375 files) · lint 0 errors · build green · 5 e2e specs green in a real headless Chromium.

### B1094 — Moving a building splits its bonded assembly across transactions `[Site Planner / sync]` (bug) #site-planner #sync #persistence #selection  *(owner chat block 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-1, diagnosed live against production and reproduced twice on Tsakiris / Concept A (`smrjdgmlinea`). Minted **B1094 / V509** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`; code, tests and commits keep the provisional `NEW-1` label per the house rule. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the element-sync family (**B671** the write engine, **B672** the read cutover, **B673** the conflict matrix, **B757**/**B812** the self-echo guards, **B901** the keepalive flush, **V229 #5** the stale-tab clobber, plus `attachedTo` / `assemblyOf` / `refitChildren`): **NOT a recurrence.** Every prior item made an INDIVIDUAL element's commit correct; none of them gives the engine any notion that a host and its `attachedTo` children are one object. Net-new. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ THIS ITEM'S OWN STRAND PASSED LIVE 2026-07-29 — but V509 STAYS OPEN (its B1098 half failed; see the recurrence below).**
- **✅ Live evidence (owner, signed in on planyr.io, real Tsakiris / Concept A `smrjdgmlinea`, deployed bundle `index-BEEc4smO.js`):** dragged Building 1 (`e25duuwgj`) ~218 ft west / ~223 ft north → **exactly ONE `commit_elements` call, 12 ops, every assembly member, all at post-gesture coordinates, uniform delta, matching the canvas exactly.** Pre-fix the same gesture produced two commits 1.7 s apart with the later one carrying pre-gesture coordinates. The gesture-atomicity guarantee this item exists for is CONFIRMED.
- **Why it is not Done:** V509 covers this item AND B1098, and B1098's half re-tore the assembly through a straggler batch minted AFTER the undo's flush. The fix for that (see B1098 ×2) touches the same read path, so this item is re-verified on the same live pass rather than closed early — MERGED ≠ LIVE, and a partial pass is not a pass.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Repro (owner, measured against production `site_elements`).** Drag Building 1 (`e25duuwgj`, 11 bonded children) any distance, release, do nothing else. Local React state is CORRECT — all 12 members translated by the same delta, read straight off the fiber. But the server receives the move in **two transactions ~1.7 s apart**, and the later one carries **pre-gesture** `cx/cy` for the members it covers (14:06:10.969 wrote 7 members moved; 14:06:12.689 wrote `e56/e57/e62/e63/e64` unmoved). The original incident spread 12 rows over FIVE transactions in 9 s. Result on screen: the building ~2,000 ft east, off the parcel, with an empty drive loop and orphaned dock squares where it used to be.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST).** `elementSync.js` has no notion of `attachedTo`. A batch is *whatever happens to be dirty* at the instant `flush()` runs, and each op carries the payload **captured when the diff enqueued it**. So an assembly can straddle transactions in two independent ways: a member that reaches the dirty queue late goes out in its own later commit, and a member whose op was minted before the gesture ships the pre-gesture bytes. Neither is recoverable afterwards — `flush()` also returns early while any commit is `inflight`, which widens the window rather than closing it.
- **Fix — two guarantees, both in `flush()`, immediately before the batch is built.**
  - **(a) CLOSURE.** `closeAssemblies()` — if ANY member of an assembly is dirty, every member whose LIVE data disagrees with the shadow joins the same batch. The assembly root is the same `rootIdOf` rule `planClipboard` and the delete/nudge paths already use (`attachedTo` when bonded, else self), so there is one definition of "assembly" in the codebase. One gesture → one commit → N+1 ops.
  - **(b) FRESHNESS.** `freshen()` — every op's data is re-read from the live canvas at flush time through a new injected `liveCollections()` provider, so a payload captured before the gesture can no longer reach the wire, whatever queued it (a deferred cascade, a transport-failure requeue, the pending-edit journal). The z the diff ASSIGNED to a z-less new element is preserved across the refresh.
  - Both are **opt-in**: a caller that supplies no `liveCollections` (every existing test) gets the pre-fix engine byte for byte.
- **Tests.** `test/assemblyTear.test.js` — a host + 5 bonded children dragged 241 ft commits **exactly one batch of 6 ops, every one at post-gesture coordinates**; a member the differ never saw is CLOSED INTO the same commit rather than dribbled out later; a queued pre-gesture payload is re-read at flush time; an unbonded element pulls nothing extra in. `e2e/assembly-move-integrity.spec.js` drives the REAL canvas logged out — a building with a 5+-member assembly (dock stack, car-parking pair, bump-outs) translates every member by the same delta and Ctrl+Z returns them all, zero page errors.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` 6055 green · lint 0 errors · build green · `npx playwright test e2e/assembly-move-integrity.spec.js e2e/ctrlz-undo.spec.js e2e/building-reshape.spec.js` green.
- **What is still owed (V509).** The signed-in half — the sandbox's egress proxy CORS-blocks the Supabase auth handshake, so no commit can be observed here: that a real drag produces ONE `commit_elements` call carrying the whole assembly at post-gesture coordinates, and that the row set afterwards is internally consistent.
- **✅ LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-29 (owner, two runs on the deployed atomic build, 22:36 + 22:38 UTC, real Tsakiris / Concept A). V509 PASSED — archived.** `p_atomic` true and `applied` true on every multi-member commit, no `atomic-request-lost` alarm, rows canonical after both runs. Known-and-benign residual on record: 4–5 commits per gesture instead of 2 — all atomic, all coherent, so redundant rather than partial.

### B1098 (×2) — Undo never flushes, so it races the in-flight commit — and a STRAGGLER batch after the undo re-tears the assembly `[Site Planner / sync]` (bug) #site-planner #sync #persistence  *(owner chat block 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-2, same diagnosis session as B1094. Minted **B1098**; shares **V509** — one signed-in drag-then-undo pass proves both, as the two defects compound on the same gesture. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched the flush family (**B671** `flushGesture`, **B901** the keepalive unload flush, **B315** the mid-drag cancel, `applySnapshot` / `flushElems`): **NOT a recurrence.** B901 wired the UNLOAD flush; no prior item treats undo/redo as a gesture boundary. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ RE-OPENED then RE-SHIPPED 2026-07-29 — V509 PENDING and MUST be re-verified live after this ships.**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Repro.** Drag a building, then press Ctrl+Z within ~2 s. `applySnapshot` restores the full pre-move state locally but never calls `flushElems()` — unlike every other gesture end (`onUp`). The undo therefore trails on the engine's ~750 ms debounce while the move's batches are still going out, and the server ends up with a mix of moved and restored members. Ctrl+Z is not the CAUSE of the tear (B1094 is) but it reliably makes it worse.
- **Fix.** An undo/redo is a gesture boundary and commits immediately. `applySnapshot` now flushes — **against the SNAPSHOT, not `stateRef`**: React has not re-rendered when the handler runs, so `stateRef` still holds the state being undone and diffing it would have re-committed the move. `reconcileElems`/`flushElems` take an explicit state override, and a new `syncStateOverride` ref installs that snapshot for the engine's `liveCollections()` read for the duration of the synchronous flush (without it B1094's freshen pass would have re-read the stale `stateRef` and undone the undo). `drainRemote()` is skipped on a snapshot flush — a snapshot already knows what the canvas holds. Covers redo and the Esc mid-drag cancel (`cancelActiveMove`) by construction; no-ops when the plan isn't cloud-synced.
- **Tests.** `test/assemblyTear.test.js` — restoring a snapshot and flushing commits ON THE SPOT (one more commit, **zero pending timers**) and carries the whole assembly at the restored coordinates; plus two anti-drift source guards (that `applySnapshot` flushes with `s`, and that the override reaches the engine's live read). `e2e/ctrlz-undo.spec.js` (5 pre-existing logged-out cases) re-run green, so the local undo path is unregressed.
- **What is still owed (V509).** The signed-in race itself: drag, Ctrl+Z inside ~2 s, and confirm the rows settle to the pre-move geometry with no mixed state.

---
- **Recurrence (×2) — 2026-07-29, owner live verification of V509 on planyr.io, signed in, real Tsakiris / Concept A (`smrjdgmlinea`), deployed bundle `index-BEEc4smO.js`. Arrived as chat "NEW-1"; AMENDS B1094 + B1098. Per the recurrence rule this takes NO new B# — it re-opens this one.**
- **Repro (measured, in-page `fetch` hook + `site_elements.updated_at`).** Drag a building, press Ctrl+Z within ~2 s:
  - `t=300873 ms` — the drag commits: **1 batch, 12 ops, moved coordinates. Correct.**
  - `t=331961 ms` — Ctrl+Z commits **IMMEDIATELY**: 1 batch, 12 ops, pre-move coordinates. **The flush itself works — this is the B1098 behaviour and it is right.**
  - `t=335893 ms` — a **THIRD** batch, 2 ops: `e29duuwgj:872,178` and `e30duuwgj:1343,-237` — the **PRE-UNDO (moved)** coordinates.
  - Rows: 10 members restored in one txn (15:39:29.755), `e28` alone at 15:39:35.646 correct, **`e29` + `e30` at 15:39:37.650 holding the MOVED values** — the bottom trailer strip and the right sidewalk stranded 218 ft west / 223 ft north of the building. Owner repaired both by hand; the record has been coherent and quiet since 15:52.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — the brief's two named fixes were ALREADY IN PLACE, and neither could have prevented this. Recorded rather than silently "fixed", because it changes where the defect is.** (1) `closeAssemblies` already runs for EVERY batch, not only gesture flushes — it is called unconditionally at the top of `flush()`. (2) `freshen` is already unconditional and already reads live canvas bytes at flush time regardless of `syncStateOverride` (that ref only shortens the window during the synchronous snapshot flush). **Both ran, and both were correct.** The straggler was 2 ops precisely BECAUSE closure works: only those two elements genuinely disagreed with the server, so there was nothing else to fold in. And `freshen` faithfully sent what the canvas held. **The canvas itself was wrong** — which is upstream of the write path entirely.
- **ROOT CAUSE — a buffered remote instruction with a FROZEN payload, replayed across the undo.** A `postgres_changes` row that arrives while `busyRef` is true (mid-gesture, and the flag outlives pointer-up by a render) is converted to a canvas instruction **at arrival time** — `const instr = eng.applyRemoteRow(row)` — and parked in `pendingRemoteRef` with its `el` payload frozen (`SitePlanner.jsx`, the B672 mid-gesture buffer). It is applied at the next `drainRemote()`. If an undo lands in between, that drain writes **pre-undo geometry** back onto a canvas the user has just restored, for whichever elements happened to be in the buffer — and the next diff dutifully commits the re-torn canvas as a fresh edit. Two elements were in the buffer; hence 2 ops, hence pre-undo coordinates, hence ~4 s later.
- **Fix — the applied snapshot is the authority, on BOTH the buffered and the live path.**
  - **Buffered (the measured path).** `applySnapshot` now drops every buffered **UPSERT** minted before it — those describe a world the user has explicitly discarded. A buffered **REMOVE is KEPT**: a remote tombstone is not undone by a local undo, and dropping it would resurrect a deleted element (**TOMBSTONE-DELETES**).
  - **Live (the same hole, one beat later).** An echo can also arrive in the window right after the restore, with no buffering involved. `elementSync` now carries a **local-authority epoch**: `noteLocalAuthority()` (called by `applySnapshot`) bumps it, and every serialization this tab puts on the wire is tagged with the epoch it was sent in. In `applyRemoteRow`, a row whose bytes are **ours, sent at an older epoch** adopts the rev into the shadow but is **kept off the canvas** — so it cannot resurrect what the user just undid. The shadow then disagrees with the canvas, which is correct: the next reconcile re-asserts the SNAPSHOT's geometry, **assembly-closed, as one batch**. A foreign row, or an own echo from the current epoch, is completely unaffected (the B672 stale-seed re-true still works).
- **The invariant now enforced, in the owner's words:** no batch may leave with a payload older than the most recently applied snapshot — enforced at the source, by never letting that payload reach the canvas in the first place.
- **Tests.** `test/assemblyTear.test.js` — the exact sequence the brief asked for: commit A (moved) → `applySnapshot` to pre-move → commit B (restored, 6 ops, whole assembly) → **the delayed echo of A**, which must be `ignore`d, after which **no third commit carries A's payload** and any batch that does go out is at post-snapshot coordinates. **This test FAILS on the pre-fix engine** (verified by disabling the epoch guard), so it is a guard rather than a decoration. Plus: a late FOREIGN row still upserts and its correction commits assembly-closed; an own echo from the CURRENT epoch still upserts (the stale-seed re-true is unregressed); and a source guard that the buffered **remove** survives the snapshot while upserts do not.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `npm test` 6117 green (367 files) · lint 0 errors · build green · `npx playwright test e2e/assembly-move-integrity.spec.js e2e/ctrlz-undo.spec.js` 6/6 green.
- **What is still owed (V509).** The same signed-in drag-then-undo pass that found this, re-run on the deployed fix: the drag as ONE batch, the undo as ONE immediate batch, and **NO third batch of any size** in the following 30 s — with `site_elements` settling to the pre-move geometry for every assembly member.
- **✅ LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-29 (owner, two runs on the deployed atomic build, 22:36 + 22:38 UTC, real Tsakiris / Concept A). V509 PASSED — archived.** `p_atomic` true and `applied` true on every multi-member commit, no `atomic-request-lost` alarm, rows canonical after both runs. Known-and-benign residual on record: 4–5 commits per gesture instead of 2 — all atomic, all coherent, so redundant rather than partial.

### B1119 — "Is it deployed?" was being answered from the wrong file, and the answer was wrong `[Infra / deploy verification]` (bug + task) #infra #testing  *(owner deploy-chase 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-none — raised as "nothing to file unless you find a real defect in the build config". **There is no build-config defect: the build fired and #852 deployed on time.** The defect is in the VERIFICATION METHOD, which is worth more than a config bug because it silently inverted the answer. Minted **B1119**. Verify: **sandbox** — and stronger than sandbox: the tool was run against LIVE production and passed. → Done.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.** `ui-audit/verify-deploy.mjs` answers "is this change actually served?" correctly, and `VERIFICATION.md` carries the procedure so the next session doesn't re-derive it.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **The report.** planyr.io had served `assets/index-iy2BZyRK.js` unchanged since before #852 merged — same hash, same 507,528 bytes, sampled at 19:04, 19:20, 19:42 and 21:24 with `cache:'no-store'` — and that bundle does not contain `p_atomic`. Read as ~2.5 h with no build, i.e. the automation-token hiccup again.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — the deploy had happened. The METHOD was wrong, in two independent ways.** **(a)** Vite content-hashes **every chunk separately**, so the entry chunk's hash is UNCHANGED across a deploy whenever its own bytes didn't change. A stable index hash is evidence of **nothing**. **(b)** `p_atomic` lives in `lib/elementApi.js`, which is part of the **lazy `SitePlannerApp-*.js`** chunk — it was never going to appear in `index-*.js` on any build, deployed or not. Walking the real module graph found it immediately: **`p_atomic` IS SERVED, in `assets/SitePlannerApp-C4rK_NtZ.js`**, alongside `noteLocalAuthority`, `onRowsCanonical` and the "This tab is out of date" copy. `src/` at the verifying HEAD is byte-identical to the deployed `678d58d`.
- **Also worth stating, because it was the proposed remedy:** a GitHub Actions nudge could not have fixed this even if it had been a real stall. Cloudflare Pages deploys through **its own GitHub App connection** (`CLAUDE.md`: "there is no Cloudflare workflow file in this repo"); the `Build` workflow is only the PR status check and publishes nothing. Nudging Actions has no effect on whether Pages builds.
- **Fix — a script, because a markdown warning would rot.** `ui-audit/verify-deploy.mjs [--origin=…] [--json] <marker…>` walks index.html → entry chunk → every hashed chunk the entry names, reports which chunk carries each marker, and exits non-zero if any is absent. It also warns, on a miss, that the marker may simply be **minify-unsafe** — a local function name like `closeAssemblies` is renamed by the build and can never be found, which is the same false negative in a new costume. `VERIFICATION.md`'s self-verification section now carries the procedure and the one-line rule: **a green build check and the served bytes are different claims; only report "deployed" off the bytes.**
- **Evidence.** Run live against production this session: 20 chunks walked, all four markers found, exit 0. The pre-fix hand method (grep the entry chunk for `p_atomic`) returns a false negative on the same, correctly-deployed origin — which is what makes the script a guard rather than a convenience.

### B1099 — A torn assembly never converges: the client re-pushes its own copy over a foreign row `[Site Planner / sync]` (bug) #site-planner #sync #persistence  *(owner chat block 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-3 — the SECOND confirmed defect, found while repairing the data by hand: after all 12 rows were fixed in SQL at rev+1, the running client ignored all 12 realtime rows and immediately queued 3 commit batches pushing its own copy back. Minted **B1099 / V510**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched **B673** (the conflict matrix this amends), **B757** + **B812** (the self-echo guards audited here), **B672** (`applyRemoteRow`), **V229 #5**: **NOT a recurrence** — B757/B812 exist to make our OWN echo invisible and both did their job; nothing before this asks whether a row the client did NOT author may win. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V510 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: auth`, two writers on one plan).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Repro (owner, measured).** Change an element's `cx/cy` directly in `site_elements` with rev+1 while a client has that site open → the client's live state does not change and it queues commit batches pushing its own copy back. Once torn, whichever client holds the stale copy keeps winning, forever.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST) — two independent holes, either sufficient.**
  - **(a) `atOrBelowOwnHighWater` classified by REV ARITHMETIC ALONE.** B812 (Angle 4) rightly claims any row at/below our own high-water rev as our echo — but only a row we could have WRITTEN. A genuine foreign row whose rev lands under our high-water (an out-of-band repair; a writer whose rev fell below ours after a stale refetch rolled our shadow backward) was swallowed as a self-echo. Now a row stamped with a DIFFERENT `updated_by` is never treated as our echo. **Fails open** — no `selfUid`, or no `updated_by` on the row, behaves exactly as before, so every B757/B812 guarantee is untouched.
  - **(b) "pending local wins" applied to DERIVED churn.** The B673 matrix keeps local data on canvas and re-commits it over a conflicting row. That is right for an edit the user just made by hand — but most pending ops on a bonded plan are app-DERIVED relayout output (the paving/sidewalks/parking a building edit re-fits, tagged `direct: false` since B673's NEW-1 pass). Re-pushing derived geometry over another writer's deliberate row IS the non-convergence.
- **Fix — derived churn never beats a foreign row, in BOTH halves of the loop.** In `applyRemoteRow`: when the only pending op is derived and the row is genuinely foreign (bytes we never sent, not semantically equal, a rev we never produced), the row WINS — our derived op is dropped, its bytes and rev are adopted, and it goes to the canvas as an `upsert`. In `processResults`: a DERIVED op that loses a rev race is **not re-committed** — the remote rev is adopted with our bytes as the diff baseline, so there is no re-push and no ping-pong. **A pending DIRECT user edit still wins and still toasts** — the B673 matrix is unchanged where it was right.
- **Tests.** `test/assemblyTear.test.js` — a higher-rev foreign row carrying bytes this client never sent is ADOPTED (the exact stale-shadow + high-water state that swallowed it); our own echo in the same rev band is STILL ignored; a foreign row beats a pending derived op and nothing re-pushes the stale copy; a foreign row still LOSES to a pending direct edit, loudly. The 65 pre-existing `test/elementSync.test.js` cases (the whole B673/B757/B812 matrix) stay green.
- **What is still owed (V510).** Genuinely multi-writer: two signed-in sessions on one plan (or one session plus a SQL repair) — the foreign row must reach the other client's canvas and STAY there, with no re-push within the following minute.
- **✅ LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-29 (owner, signed in on planyr.io against the real Tsakiris / Concept A record `smrjdgmlinea`; deployed bundle `index-BEEc4smO.js`, re-confirmed on `index-Cv48ev1o.js`). V510 PASSED — moved to `VERIFICATION-DONE.md`.** Wrote `e62sascnh` `cy` −298.85 → −297.85 directly in `site_elements` at rev+1 while the client had the plan open: the client **adopted it on the canvas within 8 s and issued NO re-push**, and it also adopted a SQL repair of `e29`/`e30`. Pre-fix the client ignored 12 foreign rows and immediately queued 3 batches pushing its own copy back.

### B1097 — Bonded-child geometry is never healed on the `site_elements` read path `[Site Planner / Site Model]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #sync  *(owner chat block 2026-07-29, provisional NEW-4 — why the owner's plan stayed broken across reloads. Minted **B1097 / V508**. DEDUPE-FIRST — this is the same class as **B1012** (the road cleanup that ran on only ONE of the two read paths) and it CLOSES most of **B499** (the deferred load-time self-heal for the other bonded children), which is cross-referenced and scope-reduced below rather than duplicated. Related: **B363** / **B487** / **B1038** / **B1039** (the three normalizers this now runs on both paths). Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat.)*
`[ ]` **⏳ merged — V508 PENDING (Verify: live — `Blocker: real-data`, the owner's own Tsakiris record).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST, confirmed in the code).** `normalizeBondedRotations` / `normalizeDogEarPositions` / `normalizeWallKids` run only inside `createSiteModel` — the site-record BLOB path. `rowsToModel`, the path that actually builds the model from `site_elements` on a signed-in plan, ran only `migrateRoads`. So a drifted or torn child was never repaired on load. Exactly the B1012 shape: one fix, two read paths, only one of them wired.
- **Fix.** One shared `normalizeBondedChildren(els, onHeal)` in `siteModel.js`, called by BOTH `createSiteModel` and `rowsToModel` — so the two paths can never disagree again. It runs the three existing normalizers plus a new one.
- **New pass — `normalizeStrandedZones`.** The three existing normalizers re-derive a child that has DRIFTED; none can see a child that is simply somewhere else. This one detects an offset that is **impossible for the child's kind** and re-fits it. Impossible is MEASURED, never guessed: a dock-stack member sits flush outward from its host's wall, so its centre can never exceed `host half-diagonal + the whole chain's depth + its own half-diagonal + slack`; a wall kid can never exceed `host half-diagonal + its own half-diagonal + slack` (`strandedFromHost`, exported and unit-tested). Only members PAST the reach are re-fitted, through the same pure `layoutZoneByKind` the canvas lays the stack out with, using each member's own stored depth (translation-invariant, so a resized court keeps its depth) and the chain head's along-wall span when the head is still where it belongs. Everything inside the reach is returned **by identity** — the idempotency contract B499 asked for, and why this is safe to run on every load and every refetch. A side-parking row's along-wall slide is user intent and is still never normalised (the B1039 owner rule) — **unless** the row is stranded, in which case that number is wreckage and the re-fit re-centres it.
- **LOUD-FAILURE.** `onHeal` reports every re-fit; `refetchReplace` forwards it to `reportClientEvent("bonded-children-healed", …)` with the count and the first 20 records. A silent repair is a repair nobody can audit.
- **Tests.** `test/assemblyTear.test.js` — a host committed 2,000 ft away with a stranded dock zone, trailer strip and sidewalk left behind: all three re-fit to the host on load and the heal REPORTS all three; a correct record is returned byte-identical (no load-time churn); a second read changes nothing (idempotent); a torn side-parking row is re-centred while one still on the wall keeps its 60 ft slide; `strandedFromHost` never fires on the outermost legal stack member. The 44 `test/elementRows.test.js` + `test/bondedRotation.test.js` + `test/dogEarReanchor.test.js` + `test/wallKidDrift.test.js` cases stay green.
- **Cross-ref — B499 scope reduced again.** Its remaining ask ("`dockZones.layoutZoneByKind`/`relayoutSide` → a load pass with an idempotency proof") is now DONE for the stranded case, which is the one with a confirmed live repro. What is still open under B499 is the general dock-stack re-derive for a host RESIZED on disk — deliberately not attempted here, because unlike a tear it can churn correct records.
- **What is still owed (V508).** That the owner's own Tsakiris / Concept A record opens whole. His rows were repaired in SQL, so a fresh tear is not expected — the live check is that a deliberately re-torn assembly on a real signed-in plan comes back whole on reload, and that a healthy plan reports NO heals (no churn).
- **✅ LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-29 (owner, signed in on planyr.io against the real Tsakiris / Concept A record `smrjdgmlinea`; deployed bundle `index-BEEc4smO.js`, re-confirmed on `index-Cv48ev1o.js`). V508 PASSED — moved to `VERIFICATION-DONE.md`.** Tore `e26duuwgj` (the top truck-court apron) 2,086 ft east / 277 ft north in SQL, then loaded the plan in a fresh tab: it rendered at 1117.20, −336.35 — the correct offset from its host — and the heal was **written back in ONE transaction** at 15:43:50, together with canonical re-fits of `e31`/`e56`/`e57` of a few feet each. **No churn since.**

### B1100 — The setback line had NO style controls at all, while the parcel boundary beside it had a full set `[Site Planner / standards]` (feature) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-07-29, provisional ITEM 1 / NEW-1. Minted **B1100** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`; code and tests keep the provisional `NEW-1` label per the house rule. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the setback / parcel-style family (**B929** the parcel style defaults this mirrors, **B1060** the Standards apply engine, **B1070** the panel footer, **B880** the setback ring's zoom behaviour, **B214**/**B215** the per-edge setback editor and its pills, **B420** the setback line as a second grab target, **B721** the per-edge cross-link): **NOT a recurrence of any of them.** B880 changed how the ring SCALES; nothing has ever made its colour, weight or style settable. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat as ITEM 1.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.** The setback line now carries the same three standards as the parcel boundary — colour, line weight and line style — as plan defaults in Standards → Parcels and as a per-parcel override in the selected-parcel panel.
- Verify: **sandbox** — proven by unit tests + a logged-out headless drive of the real canvas (below). → Done.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat as ITEM 1
- **The report.** "For the parcel standards, we've got the parcel line, then we have also got the setback line. I should have all the same tools available to edit the setback line as well as the parcel line."
- **What it was.** The ring was hardcoded at the ONE place it was drawn — `stroke={PAL.setback} strokeWidth={strokeZoom(1.25, zk)} strokeDasharray={dashZoom("7 6", zk)}` — with no user control of any kind, and its dimension chip hardcoded to the same colour. Meanwhile `PARCEL_STD_KEYS` gave the boundary `stroke` / `weight` / `dash` / `fill` / `fillOpacity`, surfaced as Outline color · Line weight · Line style · Fill new parcels.
- **What it is.** Three new parcel keys — `sbStroke` / `sbWeight` / `sbDash` — following the boundary pattern **end to end**: stamped at creation via `parcelDefaultStyle`, listed in `PARCEL_STD_KEYS` so the retroactive **Apply** picks them up and its object count stays honest, and overridable per parcel from the selected-parcel panel (with its own **Reset setback line**, mirroring **Reset outline**). The dimension chip now follows the setback line's colour instead of staying hardcoded, so recolouring the line takes its numbers with it.
- **ONE derivation, so the ring and its chip can't drift.** `planStyle.setbackLineStyle(pc, PAL.setback)` resolves colour + weight + dash for both, and `setbackDashArray` scales the dash off the weight so a heavier line keeps its rhythm. It is pure, which is what lets the "nothing changes on upgrade" claim be a unit test instead of a screenshot.

Hierarchy comes from weight + uppercase letter-spacing, never from fading text toward the background (theme rule).

### B1072 — Recents filled up with the shades the cursor passed OVER, not the colours actually used `[shared/ui/colorRecents]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #markup  *(owner chat block 2026-07-29, provisional ITEM 4 — AMENDS the just-shipped **B1061**. Minted **B1072**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for `pushRecent` / recents / `pickSnapRef` / **B567**: **NOT a recurrence** — B1061 introduced the list; this is a defect in WHEN it records, which no prior item covers. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat as ITEM 4.)*
`[x]` **DONE — headless-verified 2026-07-29 (Verify: sandbox).**
- **The report.** "When I just scrolled my mouse over some colours, it filled up the entire colour swatch. That's not really the intent, it's to actually use stuff that I used."
- **Root cause (confirmed, and the comment in the code was WRONG about it).** `livePick`'s `onChange` called `pushRecent(e.target.value)`. The code claimed `change` "fires once, when the wheel CLOSES" — in the real browser it fires repeatedly as the cursor moves through the spectrum, so one drag pushed every intermediate shade and filled all ten slots with near-identical colours.
- **Fix — ONE entry per picking SESSION, recorded at commit.** `notePick(v)` remembers the value the open session is on (recording nothing); `commitPick()` at the session boundary records exactly one entry — the colour it settled on. The boundary is the wheel's blur, a new focus, and the picker closing or unmounting, so a session can't leak past the picker's life. Live preview still recolours the object on every event — that behaviour is intentional and untouched.
- **The discrete paths are unchanged:** a swatch click and the multi-select path each push one entry per click, as they should.
- **GUARD, as specified.** `test/colorRecents.test.js` drives N live events + one commit and asserts the list grew by **exactly one**, equal to the final value, with no intermediate present — plus a regression WITNESS test showing the old one-push-per-event behaviour consuming six slots from one drag. Both are new API on this branch, so the suite does not run on current `main`. A source guard also fails if `pushRecent(e.target.value)` ever returns to the wheel handlers, and `e2e/…swatches.spec.js` drives six real `input`/`change` events in Chromium and asserts one stored entry.

### B1062 — The map-lock gate asserted SCALE but never POSITION, and the surviving one-pixel registration residual was unnamed `[Site Planner / Map]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #coordinates #testing  *(V478 live-pass follow-up, 2026-07-29. Minted **B1062** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done across the map-lock family (**B1043** the projection fix this verifies, `B65`, `B183`, `B821`, `B837`, `B933`, plus `diagnose-map-lock`, `lockOffsetPx`, "epsilon", "residual"): **NOT a recurrence of B1043** — B1043's mixed-latitude-model defect is confirmed FIXED by this same live pass (the accumulation criterion passed decisively). This is the GAP that pass exposed in B1043's own regression guard, plus the adjudication of what it left behind.)*
`[x]` **DONE — sandbox-verified 2026-07-29 (Verify: sandbox).** The V478 live pass on the owner's signed-in Sylvestri / "Concept C" found criterion (b) — non-accumulation — passing decisively: an out-and-back excursion of ~44,000 ft repeated twice returned **identical to the hundredth of a foot** (−36.51 / −36.51 / −36.47 / −36.47 ft both times), against ~−4.3 ft per trip and compounding before B1043. But it also found a **constant ~36.5 ft latitude residual** (longitude exactly 0.00 ft, probe pixel widths unchanged, so positional and not a scale error) that neither guard caught.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: V478 live pass, 2026-07-29

**Why neither guard caught it (AUDIT-FIRST, reconciled against the code, not the claim).** `ui-audit/diagnose-map-lock.mjs` asserted *"the basemap sits at exactly the drawing's scale at start, far and back"* — three SCALE assertions plus a map-CENTRE return, and no assertion that a real out-and-back GESTURE returns the DRAWING to its starting lock. `test/mapLock.test.js` asserts the round-trip invariant analytically over the pure model, which by construction cannot see a quantisation that lives in Leaflet's commit path. The residual lived exactly in that seam.

**Adjudicated: it is (i) a genuine bounded quantisation, NOT the reporting harness — and it is ONE SCREEN PIXEL, not 36 feet.** The live probe was zoomed out to ~36.7 ft per screen pixel, which is the only reason a one-pixel offset reads as 36.5 ft; the error is constant in PIXELS, so it shrinks with the zoom (inches at a working site zoom) and can never put a pond over a freeway. Driven both ways in the sandbox against the real page:
- **A pure PAN is exactly lossless and does not move the registration at all.** A mouse drag moves the view by whole pixels, so the pan the basemap needs is a whole number and Leaflet's rounding is the identity. Replaying the live harness — 4 × 300 px drags out, settle, 4 back, **twice** — returns **0.0000 px**, as does an exactly-symmetric programmatic out-and-back and a single long 98,000 ft excursion. So the live residual did **not** come from the panning, and the harness-asymmetry hypothesis is **refuted for the pan path**.
- **A ZOOM commit does move it.** Leaflet can only place the basemap on whole screen pixels — `_getNewPixelOrigin` ends in `._round()`, the map pane's position is integer, and `panBy` rounds its offset — while the drawing's offsets are arbitrary floats. Every `setView` re-snaps the basemap onto a fresh whole-pixel grid and the registration hops to a new sub-pixel remainder: **measured wandering between 0.25 and 0.74 px across repeated zoom commits, never growing.** Bounded by half a pixel at any instant and a whole pixel between two instants — which is exactly the 36.5 ft (= 1.0 px) the live pass measured.

**Deliberately NOT compensated, and the reasoning is recorded so it is a decision rather than an omission.** The only two ways to remove the last sub-pixel are to leave a permanent fractional transform on the tile wrap — which resamples, i.e. **softens**, the aerial, the one thing B1049/V483 forbade buying anything with — or to nudge the drawing's own view offsets, which would destroy the exactly-reversible pan B1043 exists to guarantee. A sub-pixel offset is a better outcome than either. What it is owed is a **committed bound**, which is what this item ships.

**The gate now asserts POSITION, with the epsilon committed rather than implicit** (`ui-audit/diagnose-map-lock.mjs`):
- `LOCK_EPSILON_PX = 1.0` — how far the drawing may sit from the imagery at any instant or between any two instants. Stated in **pixels, not feet**, because the quantisation is a pixel-domain effect and a feet threshold would be meaningless at one zoom and vacuous at another; the feet equivalent is printed alongside every reading so the number stays legible.
- `PAN_EPSILON_PX = 0.001` — a pure pan has no rounding to do, so an out-and-back pan must return **exactly**. This is the tight one, and it is the assertion the original B1043 defect would have failed outright.
- New readings per state: the **instantaneous** drawing-vs-imagery offset (`lockOffsetPx`'s idea, measured against the LIVE Leaflet map rather than the pure model, so it sees what the unit test cannot), and the live session's own **per-element geo probe** — the lat/lng the basemap assigns at each drawn element's screen centre.
- New phases: the live harness replayed (4 × 300 px out, settle, 4 back, **twice**, with an explicit accumulation check between the two trips), and a **zoom** out-and-back repeated three times, since zoom commits are the only path that re-snaps the basemap.

**Two harness traps, both hit here, both now written down in the file so the next person does not re-chase them:**
- **Anchor by geometry signature, never by a held DOM reference** (the live session's own finding — B1047's culling removes and RE-CREATES off-screen elements, so a held reference goes stale mid-excursion). Extended: the signature must also be **unique or discarded** — a `rect` laid out by a transform carries no `x`/`y` attribute, so a naive signature degenerates to one string for many elements and the harness silently compares element A against element B. That mis-anchoring read as a **perfectly constant 1.72 px "residual"** until the uniqueness filter went in.
- **The SVG and the Leaflet container are separate, non-coincident boxes** (a few hundred pixels apart in this layout). Comparing an SVG-local coordinate with a container-local one without that delta reads as a huge constant "error" that is pure frame mismatch — it showed up as 386 px.

**Teeth, verified both directions this session — the position half is not vacuous.** Re-injecting B1043's original mixed model (linear-in-latitude position + zoom re-derived at the panned-to centre) makes the gate FAIL on `far: the drawing sits 2.236 px off the imagery (epsilon 1 px)` **as its own failure line**, independent of the scale assertions; restoring the fix returns it to PASS. This also forced a real change: the excursion was lengthened from one drag (~25,000 ft) to **four (~98,000 ft, the scale of the live repro)** — at the short distance the re-injected defect sat at **exactly 1.00 px**, right on top of the quantisation floor and indistinguishable from it, so the guard would have missed the very bug it exists to catch.

**One code change, with honest scope.** `exactContainerPoint` (new, `lib/mapLock.js`) is `latLngToContainerPoint` without Leaflet's snap; `SitePlanner.jsx` now uses it to aim the pan commit and to build the live gesture transform. Leaflet's public `latLngToContainerPoint` rounds the projection, so aiming a pan with it rounds once there and again inside `panBy`. **It measured as no change, and provably cannot be one on an even-sized container** — `round(round(w) - k) === round(w) - k` for integer `k`, and half-the-size is then an integer. It removes the odd-dimension case (where the two roundings can disagree by a pixel) and removes a rounded input from the gesture transform, which is fractional by nature and never wanted one. **It is explicitly NOT the source of the V478 residual** — that is Leaflet's zoom-commit snap, which no call-site change can reach. Recorded this way rather than as a fix so a later reader does not mistake it for one.

**Checks:** `test/mapLock.test.js` 13 → **17 cases** (the new four pin `exactContainerPoint`'s frame shift, its even-container no-op — so the "it moved nothing" claim is machine-checked rather than remembered — its odd-container difference, so the helper can't decay into ceremony, and its half-pixel floor). Full suite **5788 green**, lint 0 errors, build green, `MAP.md` regenerated.

### B1044 — NEW-2: site-map memory/slowness baseline — MEASURED; the driver list is recorded and the leak question is closed `[Site Planner / Map]` (task) #site-planner #perf  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-2 — the measurement PARENT for the perf family. Minted **B1044**. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched the perf family across Open + ⏳ Verify + Done: **NOT a recurrence.** This item is ANSWERED by the owner's measurements rather than patched; per the brief its patch scope folds into B1045–B1049 rather than shipping the same change twice.)*
`[x]` **DONE 2026-07-28 (Verify: sandbox — the deliverable is a recorded verdict, not code).** Live-measured on a signed-in Chrome session against production planyr.io — Sylvestri / "Concept C — Full 275' Frontage", jurisdiction Unincorporated/Harris-edge Tomball, aerial ON, 148 elements, dpr 2.15, viewport 1600x465.

**Verdict: it is NOT a leak.** The full sampled series (usedJSHeapSize MB / heap cap MB / domNodes / svgEls / tile `<img>`) — baseline 65.5 / 89.2 / 5708 / 4579 / 387 · idle5 52.0 / 77.9 / 5708 / 4579 / 387 · pan20 68.2 / 137.0 / 5769 / 4579 / 446 · overlays_on 71.3 / 143.5 / 7261 / 5361 / 497 · overlays_off 82.7 / 133.5 / 6012 / 4581 / 497 · pan20b 63.4 / 131.0 / 5879 / 4581 / 365 · idle5b 64.3 / 83.6 / 5716 / 4581 / 387. Heap falls at idle, recovers after churn, and tiles prune below baseline; after a full cycle (40 pan/zoom gestures, 23 overlays on and off, a long drift excursion) the tab returns to domNodes +8, svgEls +2 and tile `<img>` exactly at baseline. Peak heap 134.6 MB. **This is footprint + per-frame churn, not retention.**

**Driver list, with sizes:**
1. **Tile footprint dominates.** Basemap container 2018x1025 = 3.9x the visible pixel area before retina; 105 tiles at the working zoom vs ~12–15 for a bare viewport; ~3.5 MB of aerial per scenario load across five zoom levels, 53% of it transitional. → **B1049**.
2. **Per-frame render churn.** Heap CAPACITY swinging 89 → 143 MB with USED heap flat; median frame 20 ms, p90 80 ms, p99 140 ms, max 320 ms over 1,525 drag frames. → **B1046** (allocation) + **B1047** (frame time).
3. **Overlay raster tiles not released on toggle-off** — 0 of 51. → **B1048**.
4. **The SVG is not a memory driver** (4,579 elements, flat across every phase) but IS the frame-time driver. → **B1047**.

**~420 MB of the reported 555 MB lives outside the JS heap** — decoded tile bitmaps and their GPU copies — which is why B1049 outranks B1047 for memory.

**Measurement blockers, recorded so a later harness doesn't rediscover them:** (a) `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` is unavailable on planyr.io (no cross-origin isolation), so full-tab memory is NOT directly measurable from that surface — the non-JS share is inferred, not observed; (b) cross-origin tile responses carry no `Timing-Allow-Origin`, so `transferSize` is 0 and every byte figure comes from re-fetching sampled tile URLs rather than resource timing; (c) the default resource-timing buffer is **250 entries and it filled during load**, silently pinning tile counts — any harness built for NEW-8 must call `performance.setResourceTimingBufferSize()` before measuring or it will under-report; (d) no DevTools heap snapshots from that surface — the sampled-counter series is the substitute.
- `Verify: sandbox` · `#site-planner #perf`
- `Origin: filed 2026-07-28 from chat (provisional NEW-2)`
