### B1018 — A deleted site is RESURRECTED by any second client's "heal the split" re-push, and comes back GUTTED (elements cascade-deleted) `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug) — SILENT DATA LOSS #site-planner #persistence #sync #auth  *(owner-reported 2026-07-28, arrived as provisional NEW-1 — "I swear I delete sites and they don't actually delete". Root cause proven LIVE against production Supabase (`lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi`) from an owner-chat Cowork session; full evidence table in the project doc `claude/handoff-2026-07-28-deleted-sites-resurrect-second-client-heal-the-split.md`. Minted **B1018 / V464** via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Branch `claude/deleted-sites-resurrect-bug-q589c3`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for delete / tombstone / resurrect / merge / pull across `mergePulledSites`, `cloudDelete`, `readSiteTombs`, `recentlyDeleted`: **NOT a B372 recurrence** (B372's single-client unmount-flush path was re-verified CLEAN live this session — deleting an open project landed, `DELETE /rest/v1/sites?id=eq.…&select=id` → 200, DB row count 0, list 39 → 38, survived a hard reload with the tombstone pruned), and not B757 (which added the durable tombstone this item shows is client-local-only). Net-new cross-CLIENT defect; lineage B124 / B126 (never-drop-local-work) → B372 (delete honesty) → B757 (durable tombstone) → **B792** (the `doc_reviews` soft-delete pattern this reuses).)*
`[x]` **DONE — ✅ V464 LIVE VERIFIED PASS 2026-07-28 (owner-chat Cowork session, Michael's SIGNED-IN Chrome "Personal (CyberPower)" against production planyr.io + production Supabase `lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi`).** A delete on any client now stays deleted on every client, and never destroys content — proven against the REAL server, not only the two-cache harness.
- **Repro (proven end to end against production).** Signed in on two clients (Michael runs two Chrome browsers; the header presence pill read "2 here" the whole session). Delete a project on client A — it deletes correctly: cloud row gone, B757 durable tombstone written, then **pruned on A's next pull precisely because the cloud confirmed the removal**. Client B — untouched, not even open on that site — runs `pullCloud` → `mergePulledSites`, which builds the merged map from its LOCAL cache first (the B124 never-drop-local-work guarantee), hits `!(id in cloudAt)`, classifies it as "a push that didn't land", and `cloudUpsert`s it straight back. Deleted `sms3z8jwlyf0` (DB count verified 0), reconstructed exactly what a second client's localStorage looks like (site still in `planarfit:sites:cloud:<uid>`, tombstone store `{}`), then did ONE page load with **zero user action** → the row was back at `version 1` with the stale pre-delete `updated_at`, and `site_elements` for it counted **0**.
- **Severity is SILENT DATA LOSS, not a cosmetic reappearance.** `site_elements_site_id_fkey` is `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so the hard delete destroyed all 4 building rows and the re-push restored only the slim `elementsInRows` header (B672). The project card returns and the site plan inside is **empty**.
- **Three distinct holes, all closed.** (1) **Tombstones were client-local and never server-side** — `planarfit:sites:deltomb:v1:<uid>` lives in one browser's localStorage and is never replicated, so every other client was structurally entitled to resurrect. (2) **The deleting client disarmed itself at the worst moment** — `mergePulledSites` did `if (!cloudIds.has(id)) { tombClear.push(id); continue; }`, discarding its only evidence of the delete the instant the cloud confirmed removal, i.e. right before client B's re-push arrived; that is why the resurrection was permanent rather than a one-time flicker. (3) **`saveSite` ignored the durable tombstone** — it gated only on the per-tab in-memory `recentlyDeleted` Set and never consulted `readSiteTombs()`, so a second tab in the SAME browser (or the same tab after a reload) could re-create a deleted row locally.
- **Fix — soft-delete `sites`, the pattern B792 already shipped for `doc_reviews`.** New `src/workspaces/site-planner/db/sites_soft_delete.sql` adds `sites.deleted_at` + two partial indexes (the bin listing, and a live-rows index so every read's new `deleted_at is null` stays fast); RLS deliberately unchanged and reviewed — soft delete rides UPDATE (owner **or** any team member, matching B792's recoverable-trash semantics) while the permanent purge still rides the stricter DELETE policy (owner/team-admin). **Applied to production via MCP this session and confirmed** (`deleted_at` column + `sites_deleted_at_idx` + `sites_live_updated_at_idx` all present). `cloudDelete` becomes `UPDATE … SET deleted_at = now()`, keeping B372's `.select("id")` zero-row honesty and the `reportClientEvent` telemetry; `cloudHardDelete` is split out for the purge + the pre-migration degrade; `cloudRestore` un-bins. `cloudList` filters `deleted_at is null` at every fallback tier, and — the actual fix — `pullCloud` additionally fetches `cloudDeletedRows` and hands `mergePulledSites` the server's deleted id set, so **"the cloud is missing this row" becomes "the cloud says this row is deleted"**, a fact every client reads. `toPush` excludes it and heal-the-split can never resurrect. **B124 is intact**: a genuinely local-only, never-pushed site carries no tombstone and is not server-deleted, so it still heals (unit-locked).
- **LOUD-FAILURE on the new fetch.** If the deleted-id fetch itself fails we cannot tell "never landed" from "deleted", so the cloud-absent half of heal-the-split is **suspended for that pull** (nothing local is dropped; the heal simply waits) and a `cloud-read-failed` telemetry event fires. A pre-migration DB reports `supported:false` and everything degrades to today's hard delete.
- **TOMBSTONE-DELETES, independently of the migration.** `saveSite` now checks `readSiteTombs(activeUser)` alongside `recentlyDeleted` (hole 3), and the durable tombstone **survives a 30-day grace window** (`SITE_TOMB_GRACE_MS`, matching the retention) instead of clearing the moment the cloud confirms (hole 2) — so even a pre-migration peer's resurrection gets **re-killed rather than adopted**. A server-reported delete also writes a local tombstone on the receiving client (`tombAdd`), so a still-mounted planner's late flush can't re-create it before the next pull.
- **Elements survive (no cascade fires) → a real Recently deleted → Restore bin.** New store API (`listDeletedProjects` / `restoreDeletedProject` / `purgeDeletedProject` / `purgeExpiredDeletedProjects`, re-exported through `shared/projects/projects.js`) and a **"↺ Recently deleted · N"** section in the shared project switcher (`ProjectBreadcrumb`) with per-project **Restore** and a confirm-gated **Delete forever** — the only user-facing hard delete. The bin groups plans into PROJECTS (a project is a site group), matching how delete is offered. A lazy 30-day purge runs when the bin is listed. Because the delete was soft, **restore returns the project WHOLE**, not the gutted shell the bug produced. The delete confirms in both surfaces (breadcrumb + `MapFinder`) now tell the honest new story instead of the no-longer-true "This can't be undone."
- **Sandbox-verified, and the guard was PROVEN to have teeth (B372 precedent).** New `test/siteSoftDelete.test.js` (16 cases) includes a **two-cache harness** — two independent localStorage backings over an in-memory `sites` + `site_elements` server — replaying the exact live repro: client A creates + pushes + deletes, client B does ONE zero-action load. **Fixed:** the row stays binned, B's list is empty, and its 4 elements survive. **Teeth:** re-running the identical steps with the guard disabled (hard delete + no server-deleted set — the pre-fix world) resurrects the row at **`version 1` with 0 elements** and the project card returns, reproducing the live evidence exactly. Plus the required units: a cloud-absent-but-server-tombstoned id must NOT enter `toPush`; a local-only never-pushed site MUST still heal; the `saveSite` durable-tombstone gate; the grace window; the fail-safe `healAbsent`. New `e2e/project-delete-bin.spec.js` drives the REAL app headless **logged out** (2/2 green): the confirm promises a restore and no longer says "can't be undone", the delete sticks across a full reload (the new gate doesn't over-block), a sibling project survives, and the bin correctly does not render logged out.
- **Field note (kept deliberately).** Five stale `ZZ-THROWAWAY-TEST` / `ZZ-COWORK-*` sites remain in Michael's production account, **re-confirmed live this session** — two (`smrtxjchsybc` at `version 2`, `smrjyrxf7600` at `version 6`) carry `updated_at` days after creation, consistent with having been deleted by an automated session and resurrected by this bug. Not purged: they are useful corroboration.
- **✅ LIVE VERIFIED 2026-07-28 — V464 PASS (this closes the `Blocker: auth` gap flagged at implementation time).** **Deploy confirmed first**, per the B1007 lesson — the LAZY chunks were fetched, not the entry hash: `SitePlannerApp-Bb6MSq2r.js` carries "Recently deleted" + `deleted_at`, and `AppHeader-CRx4-0U4.js` carries "Recently deleted" + "Delete forever". **Subject deliberately MULTI-PLAN** so the run exercised `deleteSiteGroup`, not a single row: project `ZZ-THROWAWAY-TEST 2026-07-13` (group `smrjyrxf7600`) = `smrjyrxf7600` (Concept A, version 6, 5 elements) + `smrtxjchsybc` (Concept B, version 2, 4 elements), 9 `site_elements` rows total.
  1. **Confirm copy — PASS.** Live dialog reads "'ZZ-THROWAWAY-TEST 2026-07-13' and all of its plans move to Recently deleted. You can restore it from the project switcher for 30 days." The old "This can't be undone." is gone from the live surface.
  2. **Soft delete + elements survive — PASS.** After the delete both rows are still present with `deleted_at` set (`2026-07-28 14:09:55.825+00` / `.821+00`), **versions unchanged at 6 / 2**, and **all 9 `site_elements` rows intact (5 + 4)** — the cascade never fired. Locally both plans left the cache and both ids were tombstoned.
  3. **THE DECISIVE ONE — cross-client resurrection is dead. PASS.** Replayed the exact scenario that produced the original live evidence: both records injected back into `planarfit:sites:cloud:<uid>` with the tombstone store reset to `{}` (a faithful second device — it has the site cached and never saw the delete), then ONE page load with **zero user action**. Pre-fix this resurrected the row at `version 1` with 0 elements. Post-fix: **`resurrectedA:false, resurrectedB:false`**, cache count fell 46 → 44 (the stale rows were DROPPED, not pushed), and the client **wrote its own tombstones for both ids from the server-reported delete** — the `tombAdd` path firing exactly as specified. Server side afterwards: both rows still `deleted_at` set, **versions still 6 / 2 (no re-push, no version churn)**, 9 elements still intact.
  4. **Recently deleted bin — PASS.** The switcher shows "↺ Recently deleted · 1" with "Restorable for 30 days — everything in the project comes back with it." The two plans group correctly as ONE project entry ("ZZ-THROWAWAY-TEST 2026-07-13 · 3m ago") with Restore and the confirm-gated Delete forever.
  5. **Restore returns it WHOLE — PASS.** Both rows back with `deleted_at` NULL, **versions still 6 / 2, all 9 elements present**, both back in the local cache (44 → 46), tombstone store cleared. The actual project, not the gutted empty shell the bug produced.
  - **Also re-confirmed:** site `sms3z8jwlyf0` — the one the original diagnosis hard-deleted before the fix existed — is intact on production with its 4 buildings (restored from a pre-delete backup during that session).
- **⚠️ NOT exercised live, stated honestly rather than implied green:** the **lazy 30-day purge** and the **Delete forever** path. There is no way to age a row 30 days on a live account, so both remain **sandbox-only** coverage (`test/siteSoftDelete.test.js` — the purge hard-deletes only past-retention rows and leaves fresh ones, and `purgeDeletedProject` removes the rows). Neither is a LIVE-VERIFY class (no timing/concurrency/GIS/zoom/export/real-data dependence) and neither can resurrect or destroy anything the verified paths didn't already cover, so B1018 closes on the passes above with this caveat on the record.
- **Field note stands:** the remaining stale `ZZ-*` sites were left in place as corroboration, and `ZZ-THROWAWAY-TEST 2026-07-13` is back exactly as it was.

### B962 — Opening a left-rail panel squishes the drawing for one frame (the "screen flash" on click element → Yield) `[Site Planner / map]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #perf  *(owner chat 2026-07-22: "when i click on an element and then click on yield, the screen flashes. fix and ship." Branch `claude/element-yield-flash-7kcbj4`. Minted **B962** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. DEDUPE-FIRST: distinct from **B933** (aerial ghost on a toggle — the basemap half; still 0 ghosts here, unchanged) and **B837** (the canvas left-edge pan-compensation — after-settle correct); this is a SEPARATE, previously-unguarded flash: the SVG **viewBox width** lagging the element width by one frame. The B837 spec measures only after a 500 ms settle, so it never caught this 1-frame squish.)*
`[x]` **FIXED + fully sandbox/headless-verified this session (logged out, real Chromium, per-animation-frame — no live blocker). Verify: sandbox → Done.** Reproduced the owner's exact flow headless and recorded every animation frame: opening Yield (with or without an element selected) had ONE frame where the drawing scaled to ~0.69 of its width and the fixed feet point jumped ~146px, then snapped back. After the fix: ratio stays 1.000 and the feet point holds at 0px across every frame.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-22 from chat.
- **Root cause (traced + confirmed per-frame):** the planner SVG is `width:100% viewBox="0 0 size.w size.h"`. When a docked panel opens it steals width from the in-flow canvas, so the SVG **element** shrinks IMMEDIATELY (flex layout). But `size.w` — which drives the **viewBox** width — was fed ONLY by a `ResizeObserver`, which reports the new width a frame LATER. For that one frame the old (wider) viewBox rendered into the freshly-narrowed element → the whole drawing squished sideways (clientWidth/viewBoxW ≈ 0.69), then the RO fired and it snapped back. B933 had already killed the *aerial* half of this flash (same-zoom re-center pans, no tile-wipe/ghost); this is the residual *SVG* half.
- **What changed (`SitePlanner.jsx` only — pure geometry untouched):** the existing `useLayoutEffect` that pan-compensates the canvas left-edge (B837) now ALSO measures the wrap's real width (`getBoundingClientRect`, same triggers) and calls `setSize` synchronously — so the viewBox width lands in the SAME pre-paint commit as the reflow (and as the offX compensation). A functional bail (`s.w===w && s.h===h ? s : …`) keeps steady-state re-runs a no-op; the `ResizeObserver` got the same bail so its now-redundant callback doesn't force an extra render. VIEWPORT-STABLE (a): measure the real edge, fold the delta in the same frame — the panel-open twin of B837's pan.
- **Verified (sandbox/headless, logged out — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK; no live blocker):** NEW `e2e/panel-open-squish.spec.js` records the SVG's clientWidth/viewBoxW ratio + a fixed feet point every animation frame across an element-selected Yield open, and asserts ratio stays ≈1 (worst < 0.03) and the feet point never jumps (> 3px) — it **fails on the reverted build** (deviation 0.308) and **passes with the fix**. Existing `panel-toggle-flash` (B933, 0 aerial ghosts), `panel-toggle-viewport` (B837, no after-settle jump), and `yield-panel-layout` specs all still green. Full unit suite 4978 green + lint 0 errors + build green; `MAP.md`/pointer/index drift clean (no source file added/renamed; e2e specs aren't MAP-tracked).

This session built the tier's **first live consumer**. ⚠ Standing discrepancy left in place: `VECTOR_SOURCES.wetlands.query.url` still points at the dead `fwspublicservices` host (dormant row, no runtime consumer — repoint it if/when NWI vectors get wired).

Engine additions (`lib/vectorLayers.js`, all pure + unit-tested): **detail tiers** (`pickTier`) with **server-side generalization** (`maxAllowableOffset` — the agency thins vertices before the wire, replacing client Douglas–Peucker for tiered pulls, which is the brief's per-zoom simplify done cheaper), tier-stamped cache keys (`vectorKey`), and **outward grid-snap** (`snapBbox`) so pans reuse entries.
- **Cache design (measured live 2026-07-07 via curl):** county coarse tier = ONE statewide source-level entry (`vec:jur_county:all@0.002`, 254 counties, **337 KB** @0.002° ≈ 200 m — fits the 512 KB `maxEntryBytes` cap, so no per-county split; the brief's open question, answered empirically); ETJ coarse = one H-GAC-region entry (608 features, **204 KB** @0.001°); city is always bbox-scoped (statewide too heavy; a metro cell ≈ **120 KB**). Fine tiers (z≥12/13) are bbox-scoped @0.0002° on a snap grid. TTLs: county 30 d, city/ETJ 14 d (annexations/SB2038 move these occasionally; SWR shows age either way). Per B96's own note, the **refreshed-age stamp folded into the B236 vintage line** — one surface: `as of: <vintage> · refreshed <age> (updating…)`, stale in `--warn-text` (the standalone age chip is gone).
- **Never-blank fallback (the decideVectorOrImage intent, adapted):** boundaries are always-vector (no image service exists) — `minVectorZoom:0`/`maxAreaDeg:∞` so no gate can flip them; a **failed pull with nothing cached** engages the injected live fallback = the previous esri-leaflet `featureLayer` path **with its B287 retry/backoff**, LOUD through the same status channel (`liveFallback`, dependency-injected from `layers.js` so `vectorOverlay` stays esri-leaflet-free). A cold-cache fetch failure now THROWS in `fetchCached` instead of resolving a silent null (LOUD-FAILURE). B176 invariant preserved: same `GIS_SOURCES` endpoints as the jurisdiction identify — the line you see is the line the identify reports.
- **Verified here (sandbox):** 48 vectorLayers unit tests (tiers/snap/keys/onFresh/cold-throw/registry) + headless with a seeded cache + the TxDOT host BLOCKED: boundaries painted in **~50 ms with zero network**, one statewide cache entry (`vec:jur_county:all@0.002p4`), folded age line rendering, toggle-off clears clean, zero page errors. The correctly-shaped statewide query (no envelope + `maxAllowableOffset=0.002`) observed leaving the browser before the sandbox proxy reset it — the live leg is V234.
- **🔍 Adversarially reviewed (2026-07-07, 4 dimensions; verify agents hit the session token cap so every finding was verified BY HAND against the code): 18 raw findings → 10 root causes confirmed, all fixed same-session.** The theme: the overlay's race guards and the fallback's honesty. Fixed: (1) `engageFallback` + the zoom-gate branch now bump the request `seq` — an in-flight fetch can no longer paint stale vectors OVER the live fallback or BELOW the zoom gate; (2) a SUPERSEDED request's failure no longer latches `lastVectorError` (and a successful pull clears it) — a mid-pan blip can't permanently downgrade the layer to the fallback; (3) the fallback layer gets the `setOpacity` shim esri-leaflet FeatureLayers lack (the opacity slider was dead after engagement) and reports "loading", not a false-healthy "loaded", right after the failure that engaged it; (4) the basemap status dot keys off `tileload` — Leaflet fires layer-`load` even when EVERY tile errored, which showed green over a gray canvas; (5) a DFW-scale city cell measured **560 KB stored** (over the 512 KB cap → silent L1-only) — the widest city tier now thins at 0.003°/3 dp with a mid tier at z11–12; (6) cache keys stamp `precision` too (`@0.002p4`) so a registry retune busts the cache instead of serving old-detail geometry for a TTL; (7) the identify popover closes on toggle-off/fallback (it used to outlive the layer); (8) a FAILED background refresh clears `lastKey` so the next map move retries (was: "(updating…)" forever with no retry); (9) cold pulls no longer paint twice (swr's cold-fetch `onFresh` is skipped via the `lastKey` guard); (10) select mode neutralizes the interactive fill's `cursor:pointer` (`.pf-select-mode` + `pf-boundary-hit`, index.css) so the +/− parcel cursor survives — B98 extends to the cursor. **Accepted as documented limitations:** gisCache's oldest-write-first eviction could recycle the standing statewide entry under a full 3 MB namespace (a later re-pull, not a failure — changing B96's shared eviction policy would touch the identify/overpass consumers), and an over-cap entry staying L1-only is graceful degradation by design.
> **Dedup:** consumes B96's cache exactly as it anticipated; keeps B287's retry as the fallback leg; does NOT collide with B371 (analysis-side offline pre-cache, still Later) or B629 (parcels).

### B685 — Library upload was PDF-only; accept ANY file type `[Library / Doc Review]` (bug) #library #files #filing #doc-review  *(owner chat 2026-07-06 — "it doesn't let me upload non pdfs, i should be able to upload any file type." Implemented + shipped; LIVE-CONFIRMED via V227 on 2026-07-21. Branch `claude/file-upload-types-aj45dn`. DEDUPE-FIRST — no prior item; B664 was folder-aware drops, B685 is the type gate itself. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + live-confirmed (V227).** The Library's upload (drop zone, "Choose files" picker, and folder drop) now takes **any** file type — DWG, images, spreadsheets, Word docs, ZIPs — not just PDFs.
- Verify: live → **V227 — ✅ CONFIRMED PASS 2026-07-21** (Cowork, live on Bain `smr9olizi5ue`, signed in + Drive connected): the core non-PDF round-trip works — a `.png` uploads, files under "Other" with a PNG chip, does NOT stick in "Reading title block…", and downloads with the correct original filename/bytes. Two sub-claims (whole-folder mixed drop + junk-skip note; PDF title-block regression) left untested → spun to **V398**. See VERIFICATION-DONE.md V227.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-06 from chat
- **Root cause:** `isAcceptedFile` (`shared/files/uploadQueue.js`) gated on `application/pdf` / `.pdf`; the `<input accept="application/pdf">` also hid non-PDFs in the OS picker; `partitionAccepted` skipped every non-PDF in folder drops.
- **Fix:** `isAcceptedFile` now accepts any non-empty file (only empty/unreadable is rejected, honestly). New pure helpers `isPdfName` + `isJunkFile`; `partitionAccepted` now skips only OS/app junk (dotfiles, Thumbs.db, `~$` lock files, zero-byte) on folder sweeps, files everything else of any type. `<input accept>` removed. Copy generalized ("Choose files", "any file type is welcome", etc.).
- **PDFs keep their powers:** title-block auto-filing + sheet stitching still run for PDFs only (`processItem` skips the title-block read for non-PDFs so pdf.js never chokes on a DWG). A non-PDF inside a project is FILED as "Other" (visible in the tree, re-file anytime) rather than dumped into Needs-filing; cross-project (no project) it still needs a home.
- **Storage correctness:** `guessContentType(name,type)` (`reviewStore.js`) derives a sensible MIME from the extension when the browser hands back an empty `file.type` (dragged CAD), so Drive/Supabase don't mislabel a DWG as a PDF; item label strips any extension, not just `.pdf`.
- **Open behavior:** the markup canvas only renders PDFs, so clicking a non-PDF in the Library **downloads** it (Drive-first, Supabase-fallback; loud on failure) instead of opening a blank canvas; a small type chip (DWG/XLSX/…) marks non-PDF rows. `DocReview.fetchSourceBytes` guards the resume-last-doc path so a non-PDF (or corrupt PDF) shows a clear note instead of stalling. Filename threaded onto the file-facts index (`sourceFile`) so the Library can tell PDF from not without a round-trip.
- **Tests:** rewrote `test/uploadQueue.test.js` acceptance/junk/partition cases + `isPdfName`/`isJunkFile`; added `guessContentType` cases to `test/docPersistence.test.js`. Full suite green (2831), build green, lint clean, logged-out headless smoke renders root/Library/Review with no JS errors.

DEDUPE-FIRST: cross-linked to B821/B837 — distinct ROOT CAUSE (their ghost, not a wipe), supersedes their toggle-path approach; a new cross-linked number, per the B821-vs-B65 precedent.)*
`[x]` **ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED at the source + headless-proven + owner-confirmed live.** Clicking a drawn element/parcel or opening a left-rail panel used to make the aerial photo flash/blink for a moment. Fixed and now confirmed clean on the live site.
- Verify: live — CLOSED. Owner confirmed 2026-07-21 on planyr.io: clicking between elements/parcels and opening/switching/closing the left-rail panels no longer flashes or blinks the aerial.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-21 from chat ("…screen flash a ton").
- **AUDIT-FIRST correction of B821's diagnosis:** B821 blamed a "docked-panel resize → un-ghosted `setView` tile-wipe." Instrumented in a headless build, a panel toggle actually fires **zero** `viewprereset` — Leaflet converts a same-zoom, in-viewport `setView({animate:false})` into an internal `panBy`, so it never wipes on a toggle. The real flash is the **ghost B837 added**: B837 made the `sizeChanged` branch ALWAYS `spawnGhost()` (a full `wrap.cloneNode(true)` of the tile layer) before re-syncing; that frozen clone sits on top at the PRE-shift position and drops up to 5 s later, so every click shows the aerial off-position then snap back.
- **Fix (`SitePlanner.jsx` basemap view-sync effect):** `viewprereset` (the wipe) only needs to fire on a ZOOM change. A panel/rail toggle and a pure-pan settle are same-zoom re-centers, so `commit()` now moves with `map.panBy` (translates the pane, lazy-loads only the newly exposed edge tiles, never wipes) and spawns NO ghost. The ghost is reserved for a genuine zoom change (setView really wipes → B65's snapshot masks it). `sizeChanged` now calls `invalidateSize({pan:false})` (resize with no pan/wipe) then re-centers through the no-wipe commit. Supersedes B821/B837's wipe-then-mask for the toggle path; B65's zoom-gesture ghost is left intact.
- **Named rules:** AUDIT-FIRST (instrumented the real event flow, corrected the prior claim in code); LIVE-VERIFY (aerial paint with real tiles → V392, now PASSED); VIEWPORT-STABLE (the drawing must not jump — B837's geometric invariant re-run green). No `MAP.md` change (inline effect edit; the one new file is an e2e spec, not a `src/` module).
- **Verified (sandbox/headless, logged out — ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK):** new `e2e/panel-toggle-flash.spec.js` seeds a located site, exposes the backdrop map behind a `window.__PLANYR_E2E` hook (never runs in prod), and counts ghost clones appended to the map clip across open/switch/switch/close → **0** (reintroducing the ghost makes it fail at 2, proving the guard bites). `e2e/panel-toggle-viewport.spec.js` (B837 no-jump) + `click-behavior` + `measure-select` + `context-menu-viewport` all green; full unit suite + lint 0 errors + build green (SitePlannerApp/DocReview still separate lazy chunks).
- **✅ V392 CONFIRMED PASS 2026-07-21 (owner, live on planyr.io):** with the aerial ON over a real located site, clicking features/parcels and opening/switching/closing the left-rail panels no longer flashes, blinks, or shows the aerial off-position-then-snap. Subsumes B821's V310 + B837's V328 toggle-flash halves.

### B931 — Site Planner callout / text-box text still overflows its box for wide all-caps text `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #markup  *(owner-reported 2026-07-21 in chat with a fresh Site Planner screenshot ("Sylvestri / Concept A") — "I'm still dealing with the issue of text appearing outside of its box," the callout "COULD ADD VLOUME TO ADJACENT MASON BASIN" spilling past its rect. `[x]` **FIXED + verified this session (build green · 4776 unit tests · real logged-out canvas e2e).** A callout / text box whose text is wide — long all-caps lines like the owner's "COULD ADD VOLUME TO ADJACENT MASON BASIN" — drew its text straight past the right/left edge of its box. The box hugged the text too tightly, so the annotation looked broken.
- Verify: sandbox — CLOSED. Callout rendering is data-independent and fully reachable on a blank site with no auth/GIS/real-data → per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK it was reproduced + driven headless here (new e2e places the exact all-caps string on the real logged-out Site Planner canvas and asserts the committed `<text>` is strictly narrower than its `<rect>`). Verified at three zoom levels. The fix touches the box-sizing math shared by the committed SVG render AND the inline editor (they read the SAME `calloutLayout`), so screen ↔ editor cannot drift; the PDF/print export clones the same committed `<text>`/`<rect>` JSX, so PDF-PARITY holds by construction (no separate export sizing path).
- Origin: filed 2026-07-21 from chat.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST):** B913's `calloutLayout` (`src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/calloutLayout.js`) sized the AUTO-width box from a flat `line.length * charW` estimate with `charW = fontPx * 0.56` — a monospace guess. The committed `<text>` renders in proportional **Inter**, where wide glyphs (all-caps M/W/A) run well past 0.56·fontPx, so the estimate under-sized the box and the real glyphs spilled out. This is the SAME class of bug B909 fixed for the Doc Review shared engine — but the Site Planner callout path never adopted the real-measurement module. (B918's "already fixed by B913" claim was therefore wrong; corrected there.)
- **Fix:** `calloutLayout` now measures REAL glyph widths via the shared `src/shared/markup/textWrap.js` `bestMeasurer` (a real `<canvas>` `measureText` in the browser, matching the app's Inter face to sub-pixel precision; the per-char heuristic in Node so the module stays pure/Node-testable) — bold/italic fed through so heavier glyphs size wider. AUTO width hugs the widest REAL line; EXPLICIT (dragged) width now wraps via `wrapText` (width-based, mirroring the editor's soft-wrap) instead of the old char-count `wrapLines`. The flat `charW` remains only as the coarse floor inside `minCalloutWidthFt`.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** recurrence of the Site Planner half of the callout-overflow class (B918 punted it as "fixed by B913"; B913 introduced the flat estimate). Not the Doc Review half (B918, separate `MarkupRenderer`/`textWrap` path — unaffected).
- **Verified (sandbox/headless):** unit — `test/calloutLayout.test.js` updated to real measurement + a new invariant test (the AUTO box encloses every line at ppf 0.2/0.35/0.9) + a proof the box is now wider than the old flat estimate; full suite green (4776). e2e — new `e2e/dim-callout-edit.spec.js` "B929" places the exact all-caps string on the logged-out canvas and asserts the committed `<text>` fits inside the box `<rect>`. Build green; MAP/doc-pointers clean.

### B881 — Bottom map furniture overlaps when a docked panel narrows the map pane (scale bar ↔ "● Scaled" badge ↔ coordinate chip) `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(Claude-spotted 2026-07-18 while diagnosing the setback bug — owner's Mueschke Rd screenshot, Parcels panel docked; handoff `handoffheaderandfurnitureglitches.md` NEW-1. - **✅ V362 CONFIRMED PASS 2026-07-21** (Cowork verification round, live on planyr.io — Bain / Concept A, Parcels panel docked to narrow the map pane, two zooms ~1,000 ft & ~500 ft): the graphic scale bar, "● Scaled" calibration badge, north arrow and coordinate chip all stayed clear/legible with ZERO overlap on the scale-bar numbers. Live zoom-/data-density gate met → moved to BACKLOG-DONE.
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — zoom-/data-density-dependent rendering; the sandbox proves geometry headless, but the live docked-panel eyeball on planyr.io is the class's gate) → V362.** On the in-planner Site map, with the Parcels panel docked (map pane collapsed to ~250–300 px), the graphic scale bar, the "● Scaled" calibration badge, and the lat/long+elevation coordinate chip piled onto each other — "Scaled" overlapped the `500 / 1,000` scale numbers into an unreadable mush.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-18 from the header/furniture handoff (Claude-spotted, NEW-1).
- **Root cause:** the bottom furniture was corner-pinned by fixed offsets in `SitePlanner.jsx` — coordinate chip `left:10 bottom:8`, calibration badge `left:56 bottom:40`, scale bar `right:14 bottom:40`, north arrow `left:14 bottom:40`. B609 verified the chip clears the `bottom:40` band, but nothing accounted for the **badge (`left:56`) and the scale bar (`right:14`) sharing that row**. The badge is the one text-width item (the scale bar auto-caps to the viewport, the north arrow is tiny), so as the pane narrows its right edge runs into the scale bar's left edge.
- **Fix (width-aware, pure + measured):** new pure `calibBadgePlacement` in `sheetFurniture.js` decides — from the true pane width, the measured badge width, and the scale-bar plate dims — whether the badge would collide; when it would, the badge **lifts to its own row just above the scale bar** (clearing the bar below AND the bottom-right zoom controls above, which start at `bottom:100`) and its width is **capped so it truncates with an ellipsis** instead of overflowing. Wide panes keep the original bottom-row layout unchanged. The badge's natural width is measured in a `useLayoutEffect` off the label's `scrollWidth` (cap-independent → no raise↔measure oscillation; pre-paint so no flash — VIEWPORT-STABLE). The coordinate chip also gets a `maxWidth` + ellipsis so it can't run off a narrow pane. The true (unclamped) pane width is now tracked as `size.rawW` (the existing `size.w` is clamped to 320 for the coordinate math).
- **Verified (sandbox):** new unit tests in `test/sheetFurniture.test.js` (+5: `calibBadgePlacement` — wide keeps `bottom:40`, never raises before measure, lifts+clears the zoom row when narrow, and **ZERO badge/scale-bar/zoom overlap across paneW 240→1200 × badge 120–260 × bar 120–240**). Headless harness `ui-audit/bottom-furniture-harness.*` + `bottom-furniture-verify.mjs` drives the REAL furniture plates at 6 pane widths (260→800) and asserts no pairwise bounding-box overlap among scale bar · badge · north arrow · coordinate chip · zoom controls — **91/91 checks, 0 page errors**; screenshots confirm the badge lifts+ellipsizes at ≤320 px and rides the normal row at ≥360 px. Full suite (4260) + lint + build + MAP/backlog-index green.
- **⏳ V362 (live):** see VERIFICATION.md — on planyr.io, open a site, dock the Parcels panel to narrow the map pane, zoom so the scale bar reads ~1,000 ft, and confirm the scale bar, "● Scaled" badge, north arrow and coordinate chip all stay clear/legible (repeat at two zooms).
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** net-new — no prior item makes the bottom furniture width-aware (B609 relocated the coordinate chip but only checked the `bottom:8` vs `bottom:40` bands, not the same-row badge↔bar case). Relatives (not dupes): B609 (chip relocation), the `sheetFurniture.js` export-quality NEW-1 (a different, export-frame concern).

### B930 — Info "ⓘ" popover flashes rapidly while hovering (Yield "Sources ⓘ" + Layers-panel per-row ⓘ) `[App-wide / UI]` (bug) #ui #site-planner  *(owner-reported 2026-07-21 in chat with a screenshot of the Yield → "Sources ⓘ" legend — "when you hover it flashes a ton", same for the Layers-tab per-row "i". Minted **B930** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Branch `claude/info-icon-hover-flash-2ku7ju`.)*
`[x]` **FIXED + sandbox-verified this session (build green · 4774 unit tests · headless proven on the REAL component, both pre-/post-fix, logged-out).** Resting the pointer on either hover-opened info popover — the Yield panel's "Sources ⓘ" legend (`SourcesLegend`) and every Layers-panel row's ⓘ (`RowInfo`, also the `SourceTag` "Basis" ⓘ) — made the popover strobe open/closed continuously instead of opening once and staying put.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST):** every one of these popovers renders through the shared `AnchoredMenu`, whose click-away layer is a **full-viewport transparent backdrop** (`position:fixed; inset:0; z-index:4000`, pointer-events default = **auto**) that sits *above* the little ⓘ trigger. On hover-open the backdrop instantly covers the trigger, so the browser fires `mouseleave` on the button → the 160 ms close timer arms → the popover closes → the backdrop unmounts → the trigger is exposed under the still-stationary pointer → `mouseenter` fires → it reopens → the backdrop covers it again → loop. Every micro-movement of a real hand re-armed the cycle, so it flickered many times a second. (Click-opened `AnchoredMenu` consumers never hit this — they have no `mouseleave`-driven auto-close on the trigger.)
- **Fix (`src/shared/ui/AnchoredMenu.jsx` + the two hover consumers):** added an opt-in **`hoverSafe`** mode to `AnchoredMenu`. When set, it renders **no interactive backdrop** (so nothing can steal the pointer off the trigger) and instead dismisses on any document `mousedown` (capture) whose target is outside **both** the anchor (its own click still toggles) and the panel (its content isn't click-away). `RowInfo.jsx` and `SourcesLegend.jsx` now pass `hoverSafe`. Escape-to-close and the pure placement math are untouched; **all click-opened consumers keep the default backdrop unchanged** (AccountControl, ProjectBreadcrumb, AppHeader, ContextMenu, ScheduleToolbar, FloatingPanel, DocReview, SitePlanner), so this is additive and scoped to the two hover popovers.
- Verify: sandbox — CLOSED. A logged-out hover interaction with no auth/GIS/real-data wall → per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK it was reproduced + driven headless here. Bundled the **real** `RowInfo` (esbuild) and rested the pointer on the ⓘ with tiny real-hand jitter for ~1.5 s: the **pre-fix** build (hoverSafe off) opened the popover **11×** / closed it **10×** in that single hover (the strobe); the **fix** opened it **1×** / closed **0×** and it stayed visible. Click-away outside still closes it; the trigger's own click still toggles it. Not filed for a live pass — the component behaviour is identical wherever the ⓘ renders.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-21 from chat.
- **Named rules:** AUDIT-FIRST (traced the real `mouseleave`↔backdrop cycle in the component, not the report's wording). VIEWPORT-STABLE / LOUD-FAILURE / MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS / PDF-PARITY n/a (no render-surface shift, no fail path, components already module-scoped, no export path). No `MAP.md` change (no file add/remove/rename; `AnchoredMenu` still default-exports the same component — a new optional prop is not a primary-export change).
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** net-new. Searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for flash / flicker / hover / RowInfo / SourcesLegend / info-icon — every existing "flash" item (B65, B821, B837, B838, B842) is the **map/basemap tile-wipe** class (Leaflet `setView` re-raster on a docked-panel resize), an entirely different subsystem and mechanism. No prior item covers the info-popover hover strobe.

### B929 — Standards → Parcels: expose ALL parcel properties as defaults for new parcels, not just setback `[Site Planner]` (feature) #site-planner #ui  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-21 in chat with a screenshot of the Standards → Parcels card — "fix this so all the appropriate parcel properties are shown here and can be set to a default". `[x]` **SHIPPED + sandbox-verified this session (build green · 8-test unit lib · 11-check headless e2e, logged-out, draws a real parcel and reads back the stamped style).** The Standards "Defaults for new elements" → **Parcels** section exposed only **Default setback**, even though a parcel carries several more of its own properties (the ones already editable in the parcel inspector). Now the section also sets **Outline color**, **Line weight**, **Line style** (solid/dashed/dotted), and an optional **Fill** (on/off → Translucence + Fill color) as the starting values for every NEW parcel. Any parcel can still override any of these on itself in its Boundary inspector, exactly as before; per-edge setbacks remain a per-parcel property (the existing cross-link caption stays).
- Verify: sandbox — CLOSED. Pure defaults-plumbing + panel controls, fully exercisable logged-out on a blank site (no auth/GIS/real-data), so per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK it was driven headless here: set weight=5 + dash=dashed + fill=on in the panel, drew a parcel on the canvas, and read the persisted site back to confirm the new parcel was born `{weight:5, dash:"dashed", fill:"#5b6650"}`. **PDF-PARITY does not apply** — the render/export path already painted `pc.stroke/weight/dash/fill/fillOpacity` (per-parcel styling already existed and already exported); B929 only adds a way to *stamp* those fields at creation, changing no render or export code.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-21 from chat.
- **Model:** the defaults are **stamped at creation** (not resolved at render) — matching the panel's literal "Defaults for new elements" wording, so changing a default only affects parcels drawn *afterward*. This deliberately differs from the element `typeStyles` render-fallback because a parcel's fill is optional and stores `null` for "explicitly off"; a render-time `??` fallback would collide "off" with "unset". A duplicated / merged / split / imported-that-preserves parcel copies its source style and never stamps.
- **New pure export `parcelDefaultStyle(settings)` in `lib/planStyle.js`** (Node-tested, `test/parcelDefaultStyle.test.js`, 8 cases): returns only the style keys the user actually customized in `settings.parcelStyle`, so an untouched default leaves the parcel to the theme-aware built-in render fallbacks (no stroke → the theme's parcel color; no weight → 2; no dash → solid; no fill → unfilled). Fill is opt-in — `fillOpacity` rides along only with a fill color; `dash:"solid"` and `fill:null` are treated as "not customized".
- **Wiring (`SitePlanner.jsx`):** new `settings.parcelStyle` (default `{}`) + `setParcelStd` (settings-only, RC-6 not-undoable). The Standards → Parcels controls mirror the parcel inspector's Outline/Weight/Style/Fill controls but write to `parcelStyle` (color swatches use `livePick(…, false)` — no dead undo frame). Every fresh-parcel creation site spreads `parcelDefaultStyle(settings)`: `closePoly` (draw), `addRectParcel`, `importFeature` (county lookup), `parcelsFromRings` (identify-a-lot). Merge/split/duplicate untouched (source-style-preserving).
- **Guard update:** `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` B567 color-picker count 14 → 16 (the two new settings-only Standards-Parcels swatches), plus a new assertion that they pass `hist=false`.

### B923 — Clicking inside a text box / callout editor doesn't move the caret to the click point `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #ui #markup  *(owner-reported 2026-07-21 in chat — "when I'm editing text box, it doesn't seem like clicking with my mouse works to put my cursor where I want it to go." Minted **B923** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`.)*
`[x]` **FIXED + sandbox-verified this session (build green · 4774 unit tests · headless e2e proven BOTH directions, logged-out).** In the Site Planner, opening a callout/text box (or the inline-label / numeric inline editor) and then clicking with the mouse to reposition the typing cursor did nothing — the caret stayed wherever it was (autoFocus leaves it at the end of the text), so you couldn't click into the middle of what you'd typed to edit it. Root cause: the SVG canvas carries `onMouseDown={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` (it suppresses page text-selection during a canvas drag). The inline editors are `<foreignObject>` children INSIDE that SVG and stop only the POINTER event (`onPointerDown` → `stopPropagation`); **mousedown is a separate event** that still bubbled up to the SVG's handler, whose `preventDefault()` cancels the mousedown's default action — placing the text caret at the click point. Focus landed on the field but the caret never moved.
- Verify: sandbox — CLOSED. Caret placement is standard, data-independent browser behaviour, fully exercisable on a blank site with no auth/GIS/real-data → per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK it was reproduced + driven headless here (fails on the pre-fix handler, passes on the fix); not filed for a live pass. The fix touches only interactive editing, not the committed render or its PDF/print path, so PDF-PARITY does not apply.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-21 from chat.
- **Fix (`SitePlanner.jsx`, the `planner-canvas` `<svg>` `onMouseDown`):** guard the handler so it does NOT `preventDefault()` when the mousedown target is an inline text editor — `if (t.tagName === "TEXTAREA" || t.tagName === "INPUT" || t.isContentEditable) return;`. One central fix covers all three foreignObject editors (callout/text box `<textarea>`, inline-label `<input>`, numeric `<input>`) plus any future one, and canvas drags on everything else still suppress text-selection exactly as before.
- **Dedup note (DEDUPE-FIRST):** no prior item — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for caret / cursor / callout-click / foreignObject / mousedown. Adjacent to the B913 (resizable text box) / B912 (editable dimension) callout-editing lineage but a distinct defect (caret placement inside the editor, not sizing/opening it). The equivalent Doc Review text editors are plain absolutely-positioned HTML with no mousedown-cancelling ancestor, so they were already correct — no change there.
- **Verification harness:** new `e2e/dim-callout-edit.spec.js` "B923" — place a Text box, type a long string (caret at end), click near the box's left edge, assert `selectionStart` moved OFF the end (`< text.length`). Confirmed FAILING on the pre-fix naive handler (caret stuck at the end) and PASSING on the fix.

### B920 — A large unfilled/invisible closed markup swallows clicks across its whole interior `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #ui  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-21 as "NEW-1"; minted **B920** — late-bound per the collision rule after a hot race: filed as NEW-1/2/3, the numbers were reassigned as concurrent sessions merged into the same pool ahead of this branch (B914 Doc-Review resume-leak; B915 viewport ContextMenu; B916/B917; then B918/B919 Doc-Review callouts), landing on the next truly-free block **B920/B921/B922** against fresh main; code/tests/harness re-labeled to match)*
`[x]` **FIXED + sandbox-verified this session (build green · 15-test unit lib · headless e2e pass logged-out).** Root-caused on the owner's live plan (site `smrp1wrgg6u5`): a single closed markup — `kind:"polygon"`, `fillOpacity:0` (invisible), locked, bounding box ≈5,117 ft × 4,430 ft — blanketed the whole site, so clicking anywhere in its interior (all the empty corridor between the road strips) selected the invisible shape instead of the road you meant to grab; because it was also locked you just got the four-arrow move cursor and nothing happened, and "Send to Back" was powerless (it's already at the back, **and** it's a hit-AREA problem, not paint order). Root cause: an UNFILLED closed markup still set `pointerEvents:"all"` (`fillProps`, the old B155 whole-interior grab) even at `fillOpacity:0`, turning a ~5,000-ft invisible boundary into one giant click-catcher over everything below it (the markup layer paints/hit-tests **above** the element layer, so it shadowed the road elements too).
- Verify: sandbox — CLOSED (green build + `test/markupPick.test.js` (15) + `e2e/markup-reach.spec.js` "B920" logged-out all pass; the mechanism is a general, data-independent hit-test rule fully exercisable on a blank site with no auth/GIS, so per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK it was reproduced + driven headless here — an unfilled markup laid over a building, click falls through to the building — not filed for a live pass. The owner's existing Sylvestri boundary becomes non-blocking automatically once this deploys; nothing for him to do.)
- Origin: filed 2026-07-21 from chat ("NEW-1").
- **Fix (`SitePlanner.jsx` `renderMarkupNode`):** a closed markup (polygon/rect/ellipse) now grabs by its whole INTERIOR only when it is FILLED (`closedFill = fillOpacity>0`). Each closed shape renders as a **fat transparent hit companion** (`stroke rgba(0,0,0,0.001)`, `strokeWidth={MK_HIT_PX}`) UNDER a pointer-inert visible shape — the exact line/polyline technique — with the companion's `pointerEvents` = `"all"` when filled (whole-body grab, B155/B156 small annotations preserved) vs `"stroke"` when unfilled (grab only along the stroke + tolerance, interior falls through to whatever's under it). `fillProps` retired.
- **New pure lib `lib/markupPick.js`** (Node-tested, zoom-agnostic — tolerance is feet = on-screen px ÷ `view.ppf`): encodes the SAME `fillOpacity>0` rule the render uses, so the declarative hit area and the JS picker (B921 below) can never diverge. `markupHitModel`/`markupUnderPoint`/`markupsUnderPoint`/`nextMarkupSelection` + geometry helpers (`ringArea`/`pointInRing`/`distToPolyline`/`distToRing`/`boxCorners`/`ellipseRing`).
- **Dedup note (DEDUPE-FIRST):** tightens **B155/B156** (unfilled-closed-shape interior grab — right for a small annotation, pathological for a huge invisible one) without regressing them (filled shapes still grab by interior; open paths unchanged). Reconciled with the shared `src/shared/markup/hitTest.js` — its own header note says the Site Planner deliberately keeps SVG-native picking, so this stays declarative rather than re-routing through the imperative picker (which is fill-agnostic and used by Doc Review, where unfilled-interior-grab is intended). Not forked.
- **Verification harness:** `e2e/markup-reach.spec.js` "B920" drives the real SVG canvas logged-out — draw a building, lay a big UNFILLED markup rect over it, deselect, click the building's centre → the markup is NOT grabbed (`data-testid="markup-selected"` absent) AND a double-click there opens the ELEMENT properties (the click reached the building through the invisible markup); the markup is still reachable by clicking near its stroke.

  - **`src/shared/ui/contextMenuPlacement.js`** — pure `placeContextMenu({cursorX,cursorY,menuW,menuH,viewportW,viewportH,margin,gap})`: (1) anchor top-left at the cursor; (2) flip LEFT if it would overflow the right edge; (3) flip UP if it would overflow the bottom edge; (4) a final hard-clamp to an 8px margin on all four edges (covers corner clicks where both flips fire, browser zoom, and a menu larger than the viewport); (5) a `maxHeight` of viewport−2·margin so an over-tall menu scrolls. Framework-free, 7 unit tests.
  - **`src/shared/ui/ContextMenu.jsx`** — portal-to-`document.body` (escapes any `overflow:hidden`/transform-trapped ancestor), `position:fixed`, MEASURES itself in a `useLayoutEffect` (before paint — no flash) → `placeContextMenu` → applies left/top/maxHeight, hidden until placed. Re-places (not closes) on content-grow via a `ResizeObserver`. Closes on Escape, outside click, and page scroll / window resize (a scroll INSIDE the menu is exempt). Props: `x,y,onClose,width/minWidth,zIndex,margin,gap,panelStyle,className,role,ariaLabel,testId`.

### B910 — Clicking a measurement does nothing / gives no feedback on repeated clicks `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #ui  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-21 as "NEW-1"; minted **B910**)*
`[x]` **FIXED + sandbox-verified this session (build green · 13-test unit lib · 2 headless e2e specs pass logged-out).** On the canvas you draw a Distance/Area/Perimeter/Count measurement, then click it — and nothing happens: no selection, no handles, no × delete badge, no hint. Root cause (both candidate causes in the report confirmed): the Measure tool **stays active after you draw** (deliberate — so you can measure many things in a row), but the measurement's transparent hit target AND `selectMeasure` both gated on `tool === "select"`, so the measurement you'd just drawn silently swallowed every click. Every OTHER drawn item is grabbable the instant its tool hands back to Select (markups/roads call `setTool("select")` on commit, e.g. `SitePlanner.jsx:3711`); measurements never do, so they were uniquely un-clickable.
- Verify: sandbox — CLOSED (green build + `test/measureHit.test.js` (13) + `e2e/measure-select.spec.js` (2, logged-out) all pass; the interaction is fully exercisable on a blank site with no auth / no GIS, so per ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK it was driven headless here, not filed for a live pass).
- Origin: filed 2026-07-21 from chat ("NEW-1").
- **Fix (`SitePlanner.jsx` `selectMeasure` + the three measure hit targets):** (1) the hit target's `pointerEvents` now goes live in the **Measure tool too** (`canGrab = tool === "select" || tool === "measure"`), not only Select; (2) `selectMeasure` no longer early-returns off the tool — a click on a finished measurement **drops back to Select** (`setTool("select")`, so the grips/×/highlight — all gated on Select — appear immediately) and selects it; (3) **mid-draw is preserved** — while a new measurement is in progress (`tool === "measure" && measDraft.length > 0`) the click is NOT stolen (no `stopPropagation`), so it falls through to `onBgDown` to place the next vertex, even when that vertex lands on an existing measurement; (4) **repeat-click cycles the stack** — a second click at the same spot walks the selection DOWN through every overlapping measurement (**smaller-area-wins** so a tiny measurement on top of a big one is reachable first, then wraps), replacing the old "2nd+ click re-sets the same `sel`, visibly inert" behavior. Empty-canvas click still deselects (unchanged `onBgDown` path).

### B835 — Edit-time cascade gate skipped typed-duration & pin edits: a task's own end updated but successors kept stale dates (×2) `[Scheduler]` (bug) #scheduler #persistence  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-15 as "NEW-1"→**B835**; RE-OPENED as a recurrence 2026-07-16 (chat "NEW-1") — a live hs-v1 repro proved the 07-15 "self-healed, no code bug" close WRONG. Root cause found + fixed: the `updateTask` cascade gate. Per DEDUPE-FIRST this fix carries **B835**, not a new number.)*
`[x]` **RECURRENCE (×2) — IMPLEMENTED + sandbox-verified 2026-07-16; live-verified 2026-07-19 → V344 CONFIRMED PASS.**
- **Live repro (owner, hs-v1 Goose Creek MUD/District Creation):** task 82 "Remove Tract from City of Baytown ETJ" pinned start, `45cd`, end 02/28; its FS successor 83 "Petition TCEQ for District Creation" (no padlock) displayed a stale start; the whole FS chain 83→85→87→88 was frozen. Owner: "the edit committed but successors never recomputed on-screen — stale display + stale persist." Confirmed against live Supabase (`planar_data.hs-v1`): task 83 stored a start its predecessor chain can't produce.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — root cause (the 07-15 close missed it):** every scheduling edit funnels through `updateTask` (`public/sequence/index.html`), whose cascade gate was a hand-maintained OR-list: `if ('duration' in updates || 'start' in updates || …)`. It **omitted `durValue`/`durUnit`** — but the B615 typed-duration path (the grid duration cell `:8374`, the master-view cell `:11217`) commits `{durValue,durUnit}`, **never `{duration}`** — and **`pinnedStart`/`pinnedEnd`** (unpin `:9426`, unlock-finish `:9427` commit `{pinnedStart:false}` / `{pinnedEnd:false,durValue,durUnit}`). So a typed duration edit (or an unpin/unlock) resolved the EDITED task's own end (`durEdited` branch runs) but **never called `cascadeDates`** → successors kept stale dates AND the stale array was persisted. Exactly the hs-v1 repro: 82's duration changed 45cd→45d, its FS successor 83 never re-flowed. The 07-15 audit's claim "`updateTask` recomputes on every date/dependency edit" was true for `{start}`/`{duration}` but false for the `{durValue,durUnit}` + pin-toggle paths.
- **Fix:** replaced the fragile OR-list with a complete predicate — `SCHEDULE_INPUT_KEYS` + `touchesSchedule(updates)` (module scope in `index.html`, mirrored + exported in `ui-audit/stress/scheduler-engine.mjs`); the gate is now `if (touchesSchedule(updates))`. Covers `start,end,duration,durValue,durUnit,predecessors,pinnedStart,pinnedEnd,meetingBound,meetingBodyId,pinnedMeetingDate,minMeetingsAfter,deadlineForTaskId`. Non-scheduling edits (name/health/%-complete/notes/color/focused/isExpanded/responsibleParty/cost) still correctly skip the cascade. **Audit of every other mutation path** (Gantt = display-only, 0 `updateTask` calls; range-fill/master cells route through `updateTask`; delete/indent/outdent/paste/reorder use `recomputeAfterStructureChange` which already cascades; add/insert create blank tasks) confirmed the `updateTask` gate is the single point of failure — this one fix covers "EVERY scheduling-input mutation (start, finish, duration, lag, predecessor set, unpin — typed, pasted, or dragged)."
- **Secondary check (owner-requested):** a calendar-day task ending on a weekend hands off cleanly — `constrainedStartFrom` FS `addBD(Sun 02/28,1)=Mon 03/01` (no skew); unit-locked.
- **Verified (sandbox):** new tests in `test/schedulerEngine.test.js` — `touchesSchedule` fires for each scheduling key incl. the missed ones + the exact commit shapes, and is false for every non-scheduling edit; a fossil-chain test proves 83→85→87→88 re-flow to their predecessor-derived starts once the gate fires; a weekend-cd hand-off test; source guards that both files use `touchesSchedule` + carry `durValue/durUnit/pinnedStart/pinnedEnd`. Full suite (4128) + lint 0 errors + build green; `MAP.md` regenerated (new export).
- **✅ V344 (live, planyr.io, SIGNED IN, Goose Creek, 2026-07-19):** PASSED — see VERIFICATION-DONE.md. Changed task 40's duration from 5d to 12d in a single tab with no reload — the instant Enter committed, task 41 (a direct FS successor) shifted its Start/Finish on-screen immediately, and the cascade continued live through tasks 43 and 44, same tab, no reload. Then undid via Ctrl+Z: a screenshot confirmed all four tasks reverted cleanly to their original dates — no residue on the real schedule.
- **Superseded (07-15 prior pass, kept for provenance):** concluded "no current code bug; the Grand Port task-81 8/03→7/13 fossil predated the cascade-on-edit + load-recascade; the pin was a red herring (forward-only cascade proven via `planar_history`)." That reasoning about the *pin* and *forward-only cascade* stands; the "no code bug" verdict does not — the durValue/durUnit + pin-toggle gate gap is real and is what this recurrence fixes. B501 (delete-path recompute) + B836 (loud load-time drift heal) remain the siblings.
- **⚠ Owner decision (product, still open, logged in `OWNER-TODO.md`):** the old Grand Port 80→81 gap — if a ~15-working-day gap between AHJ approval and civil revisions was intended, encode `lag:15`; else 07/13 is correct. No code blocked on it.

`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session — sandbox+headless verified (24 new mitigation + 4 new pipeline unit tests, all green; app boots clean); the real-Bain-GIS derive + the priced volume it produces park in ⏳ Verify → V268.** The mitigation engine needs a 1% BFE to price compensating storage, but FEMA leaves `STATIC_BFE` at the −9999 sentinel on most AE polygons, so the readout honestly dead-ended at "no published BFE on this reach."

- **AUDIT-FIRST — the BFE genuinely wasn't on the polygon we queried.** Confirmed against the live FEMA NFHL for the Bain reach (29.7701, −95.8502): the AE zone's `STATIC_BFE` IS −9999, but the BFE lives on the SEPARATE **S_BFE line layer (NFHL sublayer 16)** — 24 whole-foot contour lines (133–146 ft, all Feet/NAVD88) cross the site — which the app never fetched. `assessHydraulicRegime`/`computeMitigation` were correct to read UNKNOWN; the gap was a missing data source, not a bug.
- **Fix (new `bfe-line-interp` provider, slotted after manual, before UNKNOWN):**
  • **GIS pipeline** (`vectorLayers.js`) — `featuresToGeoJson` now emits LineString/MultiLineString from Esri `geometry.paths` (it silently dropped every line feature before — the fabricated-empty-result trap); `simplifyGeoJson` passes non-polygons through unthinned (thinning would shift a line off the query point); new `bfeLines` (sublayer 16) + `crossSections` (14, registered-not-consumed) sources.

  • **Wiring** (`SitePlanner.jsx`) — `checkDrainage` pulls S_BFE on the same explicit click + SWR cache and derives one BFE at the fill-footprint centroid; threaded through `fmElev.derivedBfeFt`, `fmGoverningBfe` (buildability/FFE), and the mit/pond memo sigs. It NEVER writes to `settings.floodMitigation.bfeFt` (would fake a manual entry); a published static BFE, an AO zone's grade+DEPTH, and a manual entry all still outrank it.
  • **Honest labeling (owner option A)** — priced off the central estimate with the conservative upper bracket shown alongside; Yield row tagged "BFE derived", FloodMitigationCard provider "derived (BFE lines)" + a note stating the interpolation, bracket, and "screening estimate — confirm before design; type a BFE to override"; BFE input placeholder shows "~x derived"; print sheet appends "(derived BFE — screening est.)".

The zone POLYGON fetch (V257, large-area feature) never showed this gap because a floodplain polygon is far more likely to intersect a small bbox than a thin contour line is. **Fix:** widen JUST the BFE-lines/cross-sections fetch to a second bbox (`bfeSearchBbox`, `BFE_SEARCH_PAD_DEG = 0.025` ≈ 1.7 mi pad) sized to the derivation engine's own search radius; the zone-polygon fetch and the site DEM-grid fetch are unchanged (kept tight on purpose — an oversized elevation pull is wasted bytes, and zone polygons don't need the extra reach). New cache key (the wider bbox coordinates) means no stale-cache carryover from the old narrow pull.
- **Verified (sandbox):** new `floodplainMitigation.test.js` case proving a line ~2000 ft from the site (within the engine's 2500 ft ceiling) falls OUTSIDE the old tight bbox but INSIDE the widened one; new `bugHuntGuards.test.js` source guard pinning the wiring (BFE-lines/cross-sections fetch keyed to the wider bbox, zone/DEM fetch unchanged). Full suite (4527) + lint (0 errors) + build green.

Widening the fetch alone doesn't help if the pure derivation math still rejects a line that far out. **Fix (round 2):** raised the engine's own radius — `maxLineDistFt` 2500→5000 ft, `maxGapFt` 6000→10000 ft (`deriveBfeFromLines`), `maxDistFt` 2500→5000 ft (`governingCrossSectionWsel`) — defensible because BFE contours change slowly over distance on the flat Gulf-Coast reaches this tool screens (a few tenths of a foot per thousand feet is typical), so a wider "close enough to defend" radius is still a legitimate screening estimate, not a guess; the real, measured Bain distance (2980 ft) is now comfortably inside the new bounds. criteria" / "↻ Re-check") — a button click that does nothing observable is expected FOR THAT BUTTON, not evidence the derivation is still broken. **Queried the real Bain site directly via Supabase MCP THIS site): the "BFE (1% WSE)" input's auto-value ternary (`SitePlanner.jsx`, the `autoField("BFE (1% WSE)", "bfeFt", ...)` call) ONLY ever read `fm.derivedBfe` (BFE-line interp) and Only the priced `mitigation.summary` survives a reload; the discrete BFE input's live derived-value objects do NOT. **So a plain page reload (even a hard reload that busts the JS bundle cache) will NEVER show any of these three fixes taking effect — only clicking "↻ Re-check" (or "⛆ Check drainage criteria" if no prior check exists) re-runs `checkDrainage()` and rebuilds `floodGeo` fresh.** This means Michael's prior three test passes may never have actually exercised the fixed code paths at all if he reloaded-and-looked rather than re-checked. ### B899 — `next-id.mjs --against-main` silently degraded to a stale local-only max on BACKLOG-DONE.md (1.4 MB+, past the default 1 MB execSync buffer) → caused a real B896 mint collision `[Tooling]` (bug) #infra  *(self-discovered 2026-07-18 mid-session while late-binding B898's real number for the Layers-panel redesign (B898 chat brief): `npm run next-id -- --against-main` reported "highest assigned: B895" (stale) right after a concurrent session had already shipped B896/B897 to `main` for an unrelated feature (numeric-typeface unification) — this session's code/tests/comments had already been written under the provisional label **B896**, matching the just-taken number exactly. Caught before push via a manual `git show origin/main:BACKLOG-DONE.md` cross-check; renumbered this session's work to **B898** before shipping.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + unit-verified this session.** `readOriginMain` (`scripts/next-id.mjs`) calls `execSync("git show origin/main:${file}", …)` with NO explicit `maxBuffer` — Node's default is 1 MB, and `BACKLOG-DONE.md` is 1.7 MB and only grows (write-only archive). The call threw `ENOBUFS`, which the `catch { return null; }` swallowed with zero visible signal, silently degrading `--against-main` to the LOCAL-ONLY max (exactly as if `--against-main` had never been passed) — the one failure mode this flag exists to prevent, and a LOUD-FAILURE violation in the shared tooling every session's late-bind mint depends on.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: self-discovered mid-session, 2026-07-18
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `#infra` + "next-id"/"ENOBUFS"/"maxBuffer" — net-new; B755/B779/B780 built `next-id.mjs` and its collision guards but never hit this because BACKLOG-DONE.md crossed 1 MB only recently.
- **Fix:** `readOriginMain` now passes an explicit `maxBuffer: 32 * 1024 * 1024` (32 MB — comfortably ahead of the archive's growth for a long while) to `execSync`, and its catch block now writes a visible `⚠ next-id: couldn't read origin/main:…` warning to stderr for any REAL read failure (vs. the expected "no origin/main configured" case, which stays silent) — so a future failure mode is loud, not silently-wrong.
- **Verified (sandbox):** `npm run next-id -- --against-main` now correctly reports **B898** (not the stale B896) against the real fetched `origin/main`. New `test/nextId.test.js` regression coverage: `readOriginMain` reads the real 1.7 MB `BACKLOG-DONE.md` from `origin/main` in full (skips gracefully if no `origin/main` ref is fetched, e.g. an isolated sandbox — never a false CI failure) and a second test asserts the configured `maxBuffer` literal is comfortably larger than the file's actual on-disk size (so the guard can't silently rot as the archive grows past today's number). Full unit suite green (4560, incl. the 2 new tests), lint 0 errors.

### B734 — Account dropdown opens pinned to the top-left corner instead of under the account pill `[App Shell / UI]` (bug) #ui #infra  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-09 as "NEW-1"; **B734** = highest B# across both files (B733) + 1. Branch `claude/account-menu-positioning-frp60c`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + sandbox/headless-verified this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — the account dropdown is signed-in-only and the sandbox can't sign in) → V250.** Clicking the signed-in account pill ("Michael Butler" + avatar) at the header's top-right opened its dropdown (Profile / Team / Settings / Sign out) pinned to the **top-left corner** of the viewport; it now drops straight down under the pill, right-aligned, staying inside the screen edge.
- **✅ FOLDED → Done 2026-07-18** (Cowork live-verification session, signed-in on planyr.io): **V250 PASSED live — verified on BOTH the Schedule and Site tabs, the dropdown consistently anchors under the pill, right-aligned, fully on-screen, across module switches.** → VERIFICATION-DONE.md V250.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-09 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done (BACKLOG*.md + BACKLOG_OPEN.md) — **net-new**, no existing item covers the account/user/profile dropdown position. Nearest prior art to BUILD ON, NOT a dupe: **B127** (Done — built `src/shared/ui/AnchoredMenu.jsx`, the portal-to-body rect-anchored menu the account dropdown already uses; that bug was menus *clipped/behind* the rail, a different symptom). Account-name/identity-pill work (B297/B298) is the pill itself, not its menu position.
- **AUDIT-FIRST — the report's guess was wrong.** The report suspected a missing `position`/lost `position:relative`. Neither: `AnchoredMenu`'s math and the account menu's `placement="below-right"` were already correct. **Real cause:** Shell built ONE `authControl` element (with a single `acctAnchor` ref + `<AnchoredMenu>`) and the keep-alive render (2026-07-05) passes that SAME element into **every visited workspace's `AppHeader`** — up to 5 mount at once (Site map header + Site plan header + DocReview + Library + Scheduler), most `display:none`. All the button copies shared one `acctAnchor`, so `acctAnchor.current` resolved to whichever copy React committed last — usually a hidden one. `getBoundingClientRect()` on a `display:none` element is all-zeros, so `below-right` (`left = a.right - mw`) went negative → clamped to (8px, 8px) = top-left. Explains why it was fine on a fresh load but broke after switching workspaces/modes once. Every OTHER `AnchoredMenu` consumer already creates its anchor ref *locally inside its own component* (e.g. `SettingsMenu`, `ProjectBreadcrumb`) — so it never had this bug.
- **Fix:** extracted the whole auth surface into a self-contained **`src/app/AccountControl.jsx`** (own `acctAnchor` ref + `acctOpen`/`cloudNote` state per instance). Passing the same `<AccountControl/>` element to multiple `{authControl}` slots creates an INDEPENDENT component instance (independent hooks) at each fiber position, so each mounted header anchors to its OWN visible button and only the clicked one opens — the SettingsMenu/ProjectBreadcrumb pattern (MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS). Shell now just builds `<AccountControl user profileApi onOpenAuth onOpenAccount />` and keeps driving the `AuthPanel` modal; no workspace forwarder or `AppHeader` changed. Secondary class-wide hardening: lifted `AnchoredMenu`'s placement math into pure, unit-tested **`src/shared/ui/anchoredMenuPlacement.js` (`placeMenu`)**, which returns `null` for a zero-sized anchor so a mis-anchored menu stays *hidden* instead of pinning to the corner (all three placements — `left`/`below-left`/`below-right` — preserved, so no other consumer regresses).
- **Verified (sandbox/headless):** new `test/anchoredMenuPlacement.test.js` (8 cases — below-right/below-left/left anchoring, right/bottom/left clamps, zero-rect → null, missing → null) · B557 account-email null-guard test repointed to `AccountControl.jsx` (the guard rode with the code) · full unit suite green (3147) · lint 0 errors · build green · MAP.md + shared folder-pointer regenerated. Headless logged-out smoke: app boots clean, no stray menu at the corner, and another `AnchoredMenu` consumer still positions correctly (the shared-`placeMenu` refactor didn't regress it).

### B719 — Road curb/border drawn far too thick: size it to a true 6″ (0.5′) curb, to scale `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #road #ui  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-08 as "NEW-2"; minted **B719** = highest B# across both files (B718) + 1. Branch `claude/road-editing-curb-scale-r1u2sw`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + headless-verified this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — zoom-/data-density-dependent rendering + PDF/print export parity, both mandatory-live classes) → V248.** A road's edge/curb line rendered as a fat pixel band unrelated to real size; it now represents a true **6″ (0.5 US survey ft)** curb, sized `curb × ppf`, so it reads as a thin to-scale line at site zoom and grows proportionally on zoom-in.
- **✅ FOLDED → Done 2026-07-18** (this session, verification batch, B877 reconciliation): **V248 PASSED live 2026-07-18 (headless self-verify, real app) — to-scale curb + PDF-PARITY confirmed empirically (curb ratio 2.00 on screen AND in the exported print sheet).**
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-08 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** B70/B71 define the curb *contract* (6″ default / 12″ trailer, three-way draw/calc/dimension rule); B180/B181 cover curb in the *cost/area* takeoff; B601 renders the centerline road surface+curb. None address the render *stroke weight* — this is a pure visual-scale fix, no new number needed elsewhere.
- **Root cause:** the centerline road's pavement edge + curb stripes (and the legacy rect road's) were stroked with `strokeZoom(...)` — a near-constant pixel weight (≈5–7px edge / ≈3px stripe at site zoom), clamped, with no tie to the 6″ curb. A real 6″ curb is `0.5 × ppf` px (sub-pixel at overview zoom), so the strokes read as a fat band many times the true curb.
- **Fix:** new pure `curbStrokePx(curbFt, ppf, minPx)` in `lib/roadGeometry.js` (floored so it stays visible sub-pixel, NO ceiling → proportional on zoom-in). `SitePlanner.jsx` road render: the centerline pavement edge + curb stripes and the legacy rect road's border + stripes now use `curbStrokePx(roadCurbWidth(el), ppf, CURB_STROKE_MIN_PX=0.75)`. No new geometry / data — purely edge styling sized to 6″ (a 12″ trailer curb renders exactly 2× via the same formula). Selection cue stays the blue handles (B619). Export parity holds by construction (`printSheet.js` clones the live SVG).
- **Verified (sandbox/headless):** `test/roadGeometry.test.js` `curbStrokePx` cases (to-scale above floor / floored sub-pixel / non-finite guard) · `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` new B719 guard (roads use `curbStrokePx`, not `strokeZoom`) · full suite green · lint 0 errors · build green · MAP regenerated. **`ui-audit/verify-b718-b719.mjs` (logged-out, real app): the 6″ curb stripe = 1.03px at fit (vs the old ~3px band) and a 12″ curb road = 2.06px — ratio exactly 2.00, proving stroke = curb × ppf (to scale), not a fixed pixel weight; the road still renders as a filled, legible strip; 0 page errors.**
- **⏳ V248 (live, on planyr.io):** eyeball the thin to-scale curb on a real project at several zooms (and nudge the 0.75px floor up if it reads faint at overview zoom), and confirm the PDF/print export shows the same thin curb (PDF-PARITY — the export clones the live SVG so parity is expected, but this is a mandatory-live class).

- **What shipped (new deps: `lerc` + `d3-contour`, both small — the two the brief authorized):**
  - **Pure core** (`lib/demGrid.js`, `lib/contours.js`): deterministic snapped-tile grid requests (key ↔ bbox bijection; smoothing margin baked in; oversized viewports coarsen deterministically; `adjustAspectRatio=false` + size computed to match the bbox aspect exactly — a silently adjusted bbox would shift every contour, and a size mismatch on decode REFUSES loudly); LERC magic-byte sniff (the dev server SPA-fallbacks `/api/*` to index.html — "response arrived" ≠ "response is a grid"); meters → survey-ft on decode (`M_TO_FT` now exported from `elevation.js` — one conversion for every 3DEP consumer); normalized MASKED gaussian smooth (voids never bleed; unsmoothed 1-ft contours from ±0.1–0.3 ft LiDAR noise are jagged spaghetti); marching squares via `d3-contour` with **sentinel-embedded voids** (never NaN — d3's smoothing emits NaN coords and Leaflet throws) and **two strip passes** (grid-border frame + dilated-void halo, so lines BREAK at water instead of bridging or outlining it); pixel-space Douglas–Peucker (the newly exported `vectorLayers.douglasPeucker`; degree-space tolerance is anisotropic on the ground); index flag every 5 ft; sparse labels capped ~30.
  - **The repo's first Web Worker** (`lib/terrainWorker.js`, Vite `?worker`): decode/smooth/trace off the main thread; import list pinned by `test/terrainWorker.test.js` (a Leaflet/DOM import would crash at worker RUNTIME, not build time); the raw grid transfers back for the B706 readout.
  - **Leaflet glue** (`lib/terrainLayers.js`): overpass-pattern view-driven layerGroup (moveend refresh, B56d busy/pending trailing edge, `gisCache.swr` last-good painting with data age) with the terrain specifics — fetch on the MAIN thread (gisCache is localStorage-bound; proxy→direct one-shot fallback mirrors wireRaster), ONE deduped fetch+compute per tile shared with B705 and the readout, grids in a small LRU Map (a Float32Array must never ride `gisCache.write` — it JSON.stringifies unconditionally), canvas-renderer polylines (`interactive:false`; hierarchy by WEIGHT per the salience rule), white-halo divIcon labels, restyle-in-place `setOpacity`, worker-crash lazy rebuild.
  - **Registry** (`lib/layers.js`): `TERRAIN.contours` ("Contour lines (1 ft)"), `kind: "contours"` dispatch, vintage row; both surfaces pick it up automatically. **Zoom-gated ≥ 16** (honesty: at z15 a capped grid is ~6 m cells — 1-ft contours would be mush).
  - **Calibration:** the ramp test pins d3-contour's smoothed output to the cell-center convention (measured: level 20 of an x-ramp lands at exactly px 20.5), so contours, the hover readout, and the cross-section tool can never disagree by half a cell. Elevations are NAVD88 orthometric — the same vertical datum FEMA BFEs use (stated in the layer note; relevant to the future FFE-vs-BFE feature).

### B744 — "Drop site plan" overlay hint sticks after a drag leaves the window; make it non-obscuring `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-09 as "NEW-1"; provisional **B736**, renumbered **B744**; code/tests/commit keep the provisional **B736** label. `[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + LIVE-VERIFIED (V256 ✅ PASS 2026-07-18, headless synthetic-drag drive) — folded here per the B877 reconciliation rule.** The full-canvas "Drop site plan to place it on the map" drag hint could stay stuck ON after a file was dragged over the canvas and then back OUT of the browser window without dropping; and its light-theme fill was opaque, hiding existing geometry. The highlight is now driven by a dragenter/dragleave DEPTH COUNTER + a window-level reset, and its fill is a translucent accent wash (both themes) so the site stays visible under it.
- Verify: live → **V256 PASS 2026-07-18** (`ui-audit/verify-overlay-dnd.mjs` re-run 11/11 in the running app this session; the only non-drivable bit is the OS's native file-drag gesture, which is a Playwright platform limit, not one of the three named sandbox walls — recorded as driven-and-passed on the confirmable surface).
- **Part B (the real defect):** the canvas wrapper's `onDragLeave` only cleared when `e.currentTarget === e.target` (false whenever the pointer was over the child `<svg>` at exit), and the window guard listened only for `dragover`/`drop` — NO window `dragleave`/reset. An OS-file drag fires no in-page `dragend`, and its final window-exit `dragleave` can target `document`/`body` (outside the wrapper subtree), so nothing cleared the flag → the tan highlight stuck on with nothing under the cursor.
- **Fix (`SitePlanner.jsx`):** (1) both dropzones (canvas wrapper + References panel) use a per-zone dragenter/dragleave DEPTH COUNTER ref — highlight iff depth>0, force depth=0 on drop — robust against the child-crossing flicker, replacing the fragile `currentTarget===target` guard. (2) The window guard `useEffect` gains a `dragleave` listener that hard-resets ALL drag-hover flags + both counters, but ONLY when the drag truly left the window (`relatedTarget==null` **AND** pointer coords at/past a viewport edge), plus the window `drop` handler now also resets. `preventDefault` on dragover (drop stays allowed) + the panel drop's `stopPropagation` are preserved. (3) Part A spirit: the hint fill is now `color-mix(in srgb, <accent> 18%, transparent)` in both themes so geometry shows through; `pointerEvents:none` kept.
