### B758 — App white-screens when the MAIN bundle 404s during a deploy (no recovery exists for the entry chunk) `[App shell / infra]` (bug) #infra #ui  *(owner-reported 2026-07-11 from chat — "I pressed control shift r, and I guess we had just merged to change. And now the thing isn't even loading." Console showed `Failed to load resource: … 404 … index-CgI4uzRL.js`. Branch `claude/app-not-loading-merge-t7dwnu`. → V272.)*
- ✅ **V272 PASSED 2026-07-18 (sandbox headless)** — recovery mechanism proven by the committed 3-scenario harness `ui-audit/verify-boot-watchdog.mjs`; the real Cloudflare deploy-window 404 is an un-forceable opportunistic observation, not a gating step. Folded to Done per B877.
`[x]` **FIXED this session — recovery mechanism proven headless (3-scenario browser test), build green; the real Cloudflare deploy-window race parks in ⏳ Verify → V272.** A hard reload during the seconds a fresh deploy was still propagating served the current `index.html` but 404'd its entry bundle `/assets/index-<hash>.js` at the owner's edge → blank white screen. **Confirmed transient:** that exact file returned HTTP 200 minutes later, and the live entry hash rolled `CgI4uzRL → DwgvooFK` (build id `6e67849`) between two checks — i.e. active deploy churn, not a broken build.
- Verify: live — deploy timing/race class (mandatory LIVE-VERIFY); the recovery mechanism is proven by a headless 3-scenario browser test, the real-deploy trigger is owed on V272.
- Origin: owner-reported 2026-07-11 (app not loading after a merge).
- **AUDIT-FIRST — why the existing recovery couldn't help.** `src/app/chunkReload.js` + `ErrorBoundary` already recover from stale/missing **lazy** workspace chunks (via Vite's `vite:preloadError`) and from render crashes — but that code lives INSIDE the main bundle. When the ENTRY bundle itself 404s, **no app JS runs at all**, so none of that machinery exists → a permanent white screen until a manual reload. The `_headers` (index.html `no-cache`, `/assets/*` immutable) and Cloudflare's atomic deploys are correct; the one uncovered gap is the brief edge-propagation window where fresh HTML points at a not-yet-published entry chunk.
- **The fix (`index.html`, inline boot watchdog — the entry-bundle analogue of B221/B239):** a small self-contained script that is part of index.html (the one file that is never content-hashed, so it never 404s and survives the failure). It catches **(A)** a definitive load error on the entry `<script>` (capture-phase `error` listener, filtered to a not-yet-mounted app + an `/assets/*.js` script so a font/CSS/image error or a late runtime throw never trips it) and **(B)** a never-mounts timeout, then shows an honest "Updating Planyr…" message and does a BOUNDED, cache-busting reload (`?_r=<ts>` — the same param the app already strips post-boot via `stripReloadParam`) to pick up the finished deploy. Bounded to **3** auto-reloads on a definitive load error (**1** on a bare mount-timeout, so a slow-but-fine connection isn't re-downloaded to death), then an honest "finishing an update / Try again" manual screen — never an infinite loop. A successful mount **clears the retry counter** so a future, separate deploy gets a fresh budget. Bails on `navigator.webdriver` (e2e/ui-audit untouched) and the whole body is `try/catch`, so it can never itself block boot.
- **Named rules:** LOUD-FAILURE (a blank dead page becomes a visible "updating" state + bounded auto-recovery, never a silent no-op). No pure lib touched (inline HTML), so no unit test is applicable — verified instead by a headless browser integration test.
- **Verified (sandbox — headless Chromium against a local server that serves `dist/` and 404s the entry bundle for the first N loads, `navigator.webdriver` overridden to false + a `#`-hash deep-link so the app boots like a real user):** (1) **normal boot** — 1 load, app mounts, overlay never appears, no leftover state; (2) **transient race healing after 2 failed loads** — 404 → auto-reload → 404 → auto-reload → 200 → app mounts, counter cleared (the owner's exact scenario); (3) **persistent break** — exactly 3 auto-reloads (4 total loads) then the honest manual-retry overlay, no loop. All three PASS. Build green.
- **Live check owed (V272):** on planyr.io after this deploys — confirm normal boot is unaffected (the watchdog is invisible on success), and (DevTools → Network → block `/assets/index-*.js` → reload) confirm the "Updating Planyr…" overlay appears and recovers when unblocked. A real Cloudflare deploy-race can't be forced on demand from the sandbox.

### B872 — Reshape a placed rectangular building: convert-to-polygon + constrained (dock-frame) vertex editing `[Site Planner]` (feature) #site-planner #selection #ui #yield  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-16 as "NEW-1"; minted **B872** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Branch `claude/building-footprint-reshape-nxef15`. Code/tests keep the provisional label where stamped.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — the new grid-clip + dock-door RENDER is the zoom-/data-density-dependent class) → V355.** Angle an end wall or clip a corner on a placed cross-dock / single-dock building — to follow an angled property line and capture usable SF. A placed rect used to only resize; now it PROMOTES to an editable polygon and the shared B230 vertex engine drives it, with the loaded (dock) walls held straight.
- **✅ FOLDED → Done 2026-07-18** (this session, verification batch, B877 reconciliation): live-verify **V355 PASSED** — headless self-verify of the reshape confirmed the column grid CLIPS to the angled outline (zero spill past a wall) and the dock doors ride the TRUE (shortened) dock-wall segment (bay/door count drops as the wall shortens), at site-overview AND zoomed-in, with 0 page errors. → VERIFICATION-DONE.md V355.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-16 from chat (owner NEW-1).
- **Entry points:** right-click a rect building → "✎ Edit footprint (reshape)"; same as the "✎ Edit footprint…" button in Selected · Building → Footprint. Converts `el.points = elCorners(el)` (world feet, rotation baked in) + pins the dock walls.
- **Dock-frame preservation (the core design):** the loaded walls are recorded as fixed world-feet LINES (`el.dockLines`), NOT by edge index (an index shifts the moment you insert a control point on an end wall). A dock corner SLIDES ALONG its wall (drag projects onto the line, no grid snap); an end/rear vertex moves freely. v1 guards keep dock walls straight: inserting a control point on a dock edge is blocked (LOUD); deleting a dock corner is refused (consumes the Delete key, never nukes the building). `dock:"none"` → fully free editing.
- **Derived dims + downstream:** after each vertex drop, `frameBBox` recomputes `w`/`h`/`cx`/`cy` as the dock-frame bounding box, so dockSidesFor / footprintDepth·Length / the column grid / KMZ / clear-height·slab keep reading correct bounding dims; the panel Length/Depth render read-only (labeled "bounding"); footprint SF is polygon-truth (`buildingSqft` → `polyArea`). Column grid clips to the polygon ring (`clipSegmentToRing`); the dock-door count/apron repoints to the TRUE dock-wall segment (`dockSegExtent`), recounting as the wall lengthens/shortens; the truck court + its outward stack pull in to that segment (reuses the B492 clear-span trim).
- **Panel routing (fixed during the headless drive):** a reshaped building (`footEdit`) now keeps the full building inspector (Footprint reshape controls + "↺ Reset to rectangle", dock zones, structure, column grid) instead of falling through to the generic polygon inspector — the `!selEl.points` gate now also admits `selEl.footEdit`. A hand-click-drawn irregular building still gets the generic inspector (no regression).
- **Guards:** self-intersecting / zero-area / <3-vtx drop reverts to the pre-drag ring (LOUD); conversion `pushHistory` so undo restores the pristine rect. Corner bump-outs anchor to square corners → conversion is BLOCKED while any are attached (visible message, never a silent drop); the bump-out + end-wall-parking adders are disabled on a reshaped building.
- **Move/copy parity:** single-move, group-move, duplicate, and paste all carry the dock-frame box + pinned walls with the shifted ring (`shiftPointsEl` / snapshot translate) so a reshaped building never strands its dock frame at the source. Element-level sync + blob save round-trip `points`/`footEdit`/`dockLines` verbatim (no schema bump — the persistence layer stores each element as an opaque blob; agent-audited).
- **Parity:** hand-click-drawn irregular buildings (creation-time `points`, no dock frame) are untouched — prior fill-only render + fully-free editing (no regression). Only `footEdit` buildings get the constrained treatment + grid/doors.
- **New pure lib:** `lib/footprintEdit.js` (rectRing · dockLinesFor · convertBuildingToPolygon · dockLineAt · dockEdgeLine · projectOntoLine · frameBBox · dockSegExtent · translateDockLines · clipSegmentToRing), unit-tested in `test/footprintEdit.test.js` (geometry + a full reshape pipeline). Wiring in `SitePlanner.jsx`.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** EXTENDS the shared B230 vertex engine (the `el.points` case); building sibling of B718 (road control-point editing). No prior item promotes a rect building to a polygon. No new engine number.
- **Verified (sandbox):** `test/footprintEdit.test.js` (23 tests: geometry + full reshape pipeline) green · full suite **4199 green** · lint 0 errors · build green · MAP/backlog-index clean · **headless interactive drive** (`e2e/building-reshape.spec.js`, logged-out): draw a building → "Edit footprint" → the building inspector shows the irregular-footprint state → drag a corner → "Reset to rectangle", all with **0 page errors** (this drive found + fixed the panel-routing bug above).

Only one tab can edit at a time; the others are read-only…" with the owner unsure any second tab was even open. Branch `claude/library-popup-issue-4oh86u`. Minted B818 via `npm run next-id`; RENUMBERED → **B819** on merge-in of `origin/main`, which took B816–B818 + V306/V307 for the scheduler cadence work. → V308.)*
`[x]` **FIXED this session — root-caused, fixed at the pure-protocol level, and PROVEN with a standalone repro (bug reproduced true, fix drives it false) + a new regression unit test; full suite green (3755), `eslint` 0 errors, build green, lazy chunks intact.**
- **AUDIT-FIRST root cause — a regression from B669's keep-alive interacting with B313's presence banner.** The Shell keeps every VISITED workspace mounted-but-hidden for instant switching (B669, `Shell.jsx:145`), so a SINGLE tab can have several `AppHeader`s alive at once (e.g. the Library header + a kept-alive Review header on the same project). Each header runs its own `useMultiTab` → `createMultiTabPresence` (B313), and each got a **fresh random `tabId` per instance** (`multiTab.js`). Because `BroadcastChannel` delivers messages between instances in the **same document** (not only across real tabs), those same-tab headers announced the same project id and saw each other as a *different* tab → `summarizePresence` set `conflictRisk:true` → the banner fired with only one real tab open. Compounding it, the banner's "the others are **read-only** until you take over editing there" text describes a lockout the **Library doesn't have** (per-file/per-row ops, no single-active-editor lock), so it was doubly wrong there.
- **The fix (two parts, both minimal):**
  1. *`src/shared/presence/multiTab.js` — ONE presence identity per browsing context.* Added a module-scoped `documentTabId` (lazy `getDocumentTabId()`); `createMultiTabPresence` now uses `opts.tabId || getDocumentTabId()`. A module singleton is per-realm = per-tab: every instance in one tab shares the id (the existing line-71 self-echo guard then makes them ignore each other), while a genuinely separate tab is a fresh realm with its own id — so the real cross-tab warning still fires. Tests pass an explicit `opts.tabId` to simulate distinct tabs inside one realm.
  2. *`src/workspaces/library/Library.jsx` — `multiEditOk` on the Library's `AppHeader`.* The Library supports concurrent multi-tab use (no read-only lockout), so the B313 warning is inapplicable and must not show even across two genuine tabs — same contract the Site Planner uses via `multiwriterEnabled()`.
- Verify: live → **V308** — the banner renders only for **signed-in** accounts (`accountActive`), and the sandbox blocks sign-in, so the signed-in end-to-end (open the Library on a project after visiting Review in the same tab → NO banner) parks for a live click-through. The banner *logic* is proven in the sandbox (unit test + standalone protocol repro below).
- Origin: owner-reported 2026-07-13 (single-tab false banner on the Library).
- **Named rules:** AUDIT-FIRST (traced the actual delivery mechanism — BroadcastChannel delivers same-document — and reconciled B313's per-instance-id assumption against the post-B669 kept-alive reality); LIVE-VERIFY (signed-in-only render → V308); MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS n/a. No `MAP.md` change (no file add/remove/rename, no primary-export change).
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** net-new. **NOT B759** (that is the Site Planner's element-sync realtime toast "you (another window) changed X" in `elementSync.js` over Supabase Realtime — different module, message, transport, and workspace). Thematically the sibling of the B759 "false another-tab warning in one tab" family; this one is the B313 BroadcastChannel presence banner, regressed by B669's keep-alive. Related: B313 (added the banner), B669 (keep-alive), B674 (`multiEditOk`).
- **Verified (sandbox):** `test/multiTab.test.js` +1 regression case ("two instances in the SAME document never mistake each other for a second tab") — and the two existing real-BroadcastChannel round-trip tests updated to pass explicit distinct tabIds (correctly modelling two real tabs). A standalone node repro against the real `createMultiTabPresence`: distinct per-instance ids in one doc → `conflictRisk=true` (the bug); shared per-document identity → `conflictRisk=false` (fixed). Full suite **3755** green · `eslint` 0 errors · `npm run build` green · Library + AppHeader remain separate lazy chunks.
- **✅ LIVE-VERIFIED — PASSED V308 (VERIFICATION-DONE.md, 2026-07-17).**

### B788 — Route FEMA flood + other rasters through the same-origin cache proxy with a BOUNDED upstream timeout so a degraded source fails open fast, never blank `[Site Planner / GIS]` (feature) #site-planner #gis #infra #floodplain  *(coworker live-diagnosis handoff 2026-07-12 as "NEW-1"; late-bound to **B788 / V288** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. `[x]` **IMPLEMENTED (the missing guardrail) — the server-side GIS cache proxy now bounds every upstream agency fetch (`UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS = 25 s`), so a degraded source (FEMA held/killed exports 20–30 s on 2026-07-11) can't hang the Function to the platform subrequest ceiling; it fails OPEN fast instead.** AUDIT-FIRST finding that reshaped this item: the handoff's open question ("does the FEMA export already route through `/api/gis-cache`?") is **YES** — `syncOverlayLayers` routes rasters through the B445 proxy by default (`gisProxyEnabled()`), and the proxy ALREADY serves the last-good Drive copy instantly on a cache HIT and refreshes in the background (the stale-while-revalidate "never blank a previously-seen area" behavior NEW-1 asked for **already exists**). So the durable win was present; the only real gap was an unbounded server fetch on the FIRST-EVER (uncached) view of an area during an outage.
- **Fix:** a shared `fetchUpstream(fetchImpl, url, timeoutMs)` helper (`functions/api/gis-cache/_handler.js`) wraps both upstream fetches (cache-miss + background refresh) in an `AbortController` timeout; `handleGisCache` takes an injectable `upstreamTimeoutMs`. On timeout the existing fail-open path runs (cache-miss → 302 to the real agency; refresh → keep the copy already served). The cache-HIT serve-last-good path is untouched — the 25 s cap only ever affects the uncached first view.
- **Honest residual limit (documented, not hidden):** the truly-first-ever view of an area during an outage still can't paint (there is no last-good copy to serve, and no client/proxy trick invents one) — it now fails open *promptly* instead of hanging. Every previously-viewed area is immune.

- Sandbox: 2 new `test/gisCacheHandler.test.js` cases (a hanging agency + a tiny cap → 302 fail-open; the upstream fetch carries an `AbortSignal`) + the existing 13 handler cases green (the UA-header test unaffected). Full suite green · lint 0 · build green.

### B790 — FEMA flood zones showed a healthy "loaded" (blue) dot over a BLANK map during a source slowdown — honest per-layer "source slow / data may be missing" status `[Site Planner / layers panel]` (bug/feature) #site-planner #gis #ui #floodplain  *(coworker live-diagnosis handoff 2026-07-12 as "NEW-3"; late-bound to **B790 / V290** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Origin: filed 2026-07-12 from chat. Branch `claude/nfhl-service-degradation-uy5fi1`. Implemented + sandbox-verified same session per STANDING RULE #1; parked here for the live "row goes amber on a real stall" check.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED — a toggled-on raster overlay no longer reports "loaded" (blue) the instant it's added; it stays "loading" until the server-rendered image ACTUALLY lands, and flips to amber "source slow or unavailable — the map may be missing data" if the export never arrives.** This is the owner's exact complaint from the 2026-07-11 NFHL slowdown ("FEMA showing blue as if it's working, but nothing paints"). AUDIT-FIRST root cause found in the live code: `syncOverlayLayers` (`lib/layers.js`) called `onStatus(k, "loaded")` **optimistically on `addTo(map)`**, before the export `<img>` resolved — and esri-leaflet fires NO error for a silent hang, so a degraded agency (FEMA held/killed exports 20–30 s) left the row on a false blue forever.
- **Fix:** extracted the status machine into a pure, unit-testable `wireRasterStatus` (`lib/layerRequest.js`, leaflet-free): status starts at "loading"; only a real `'load'` event → "loaded"; a **stall watchdog** (`RASTER_STALL_MS = 15 s`) flips to a NEW amber `"slow"` state when no `'load'` lands in time; a real error event → "failed" (or one proxy→direct fallback first, which no longer claims a premature "loaded"); a later `'load'` clears "slow" back to "loaded" (recovery on a pan). `layers.js` now wires through it and reports "loading" (not "loaded") on add.
- **Amber, not red (KEY DECISIONS palette rule):** RED (`--danger`) is reserved for a genuine error; a stall is "too slow, data may be missing," which is retryable — so `LayerPanel` renders `"slow"` on `--warn-text` amber with an inline reason, and `combineLayerStatus` ranks it just under "failed".
- Verify: live (GIS-endpoint-behavior + zoom/data-density rendering class — the sandbox has no egress to `hazards.fema.gov` (HTTP 000), so a REAL stalled export flipping the actual on-map row to amber can only be seen on planyr.io) → **V290**.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** the map-panel counterpart to **B366** (Done — the Site Analysis *screen's* UNAVAILABLE state); no existing item makes the *layers-panel* raster status honest. Relates to but does not duplicate **B717** (panel layout/floating) — that's chrome, this is status truth. Not **B739** (Done/Verify — export composite; its loud drop is correct and untouched).
- Sandbox: 12 new `wireRasterStatus` unit cases in `test/layerRequest.test.js` (no optimistic "loaded"; watchdog→slow; load clears it; proxy fallback once; onRemove/isActive gating; recovery) + `layerPanelInfo` "slow" precedence. Full suite **3,620 green** — lint 0 errors · build green · MAP.md regenerated (new `wireRasterStatus`/`RASTER_STALL_MS` exports).
- **✅ LIVE-VERIFIED — PASSED V290 (VERIFICATION-DONE.md, 2026-07-17).**

### B843 — Terrain contour/flow layers share B36(e)'s stale-render-after-unmount gap (audit the whole view-driven-layer class) `[Site Planner / GIS · terrain]` (bug) #site-planner #gis  *(found 2026-07-15 while fixing B36(e) — the terrain layers copied the same overpass "moveend refresh + busy/pending + gisCache.swr" pattern; minted **B842**, RENUMBERED **B843** on merge — PR #630 (the B838 viewport audit) took B842 for its "keep-alive tab-return invalidateSize" item + V333 for its Doc Review fix; my V333→V333 too. Filed AND shipped same session per STANDING RULE #1.)*
`[x]` **DONE (Verify: live — V333; Leaflet can't load in the node-only test env, so no unit test).** `terrainLayer` (`lib/terrainLayers.js` — the factory behind `contourLayer` + `flowLayer`, the B703–B706 terrain overlays) checked `if (!map) return` only BEFORE its `await fresh`, so a job that resolved AFTER the layer was toggled off (`onRemove` nulls `map`) still ran `paint()` → `group.clearLayers()` + `render()` into the detached group + `onStatus("loaded")` for an off layer. The window is LARGER than evidence's — the terrain job is a heavy DEM decode + contour/flow compute, not a quick fetch.
- **Fix:** one post-`await` `if (!map) return` mount guard (after `busy = false`), identical to B36(e)'s overpass path. Like overpass, the terrain fetch rides `gisCache.swr` (cached), so it is intentionally NOT aborted (that would poison the shared cache) — just not painted. Documented inline.
- **Class audit (the "fix the class once" half — grepped every `moveend` view-driven layer under `site-planner/lib`):** `evidenceLayers.js` overpass+Mapillary → fixed in B36(e); `terrainLayers.js` → this fix; **`vectorOverlay.js` (both the boundary + pipeline/corridor layers) were ALREADY correct** — they use the stronger `mySeq = ++seq` supersession token + `!map` check after every await AND an `onRemove` `seq++` invalidation (the model pattern); **`parcelDisplay.js`** refresh is fully synchronous (reads an in-memory snapshot, no await) so it can't strand a stale async paint; `layers.js`'s esri-leaflet layers manage their own lifecycle (+ the B55 `map._loaded` probe guard). So after this, no view-driven layer paints a stale response into a detached group.
- **Verify:** lint 0 · **3998 tests** (no regression) · build green. **V333** logs the live check (toggle the terrain contour/flow layer off mid-compute → no stale contours/arrows appear, no "loaded" for the off layer).
- **SHIPPED 2026-07-15** (branch `claude/next-backlog-item-2lots0`).

**B36(e) — Abort in-flight evidence-layer fetches + guard against stale post-unmount renders** `[Site Planner / GIS]` (bug) #site-planner #gis  *(the fetch-AbortController sub-item of the 2026-06-15 bug-audit B36 cluster — recorded as a bold entry, NOT a `### B36` heading, so it doesn't read as a duplicate id; parent B36 stays OPEN for a/d — the county-resolution work tied to B13)*
`[x]` **DONE (Verify: live — V331; the Leaflet layers can't load in the node-only test env, so no unit test).** The two view-driven evidence overlays (`lib/evidenceLayers.js` — OSM Overpass power/hydrants, Mapillary detections) checked `if (!map) return` only BEFORE their `await`, so a fetch that resolved AFTER the layer was toggled off (`onRemove` nulls `map`) still ran `group.clearLayers()`, drew markers into the detached group, and fired `onStatus("loaded")` for a layer the user had turned off — and nothing cancelled the now-useless request.
- **Fix:** (1) a post-`await` `if (!map) return` mount guard in BOTH `overpassLayer` and `mapillaryLayer`, so a stale response never paints/reports into a detached group. (2) An `AbortController` on the Mapillary path (a direct, un-cached `fetch`): `fetchMapillary(bounds, token, signal)` forwards the signal; `onRemove` aborts the in-flight request; the catch swallows the resulting `AbortError`/`sig.aborted` silently (the removal owns the UI — no false "failed", no `lastKey` reset that `onRemove` already did). The Overpass path rides `gisCache.swr` (cached), so it is intentionally NOT aborted — aborting a cached fetch would poison the shared SWR cache; the mount guard alone is correct there (the request still warms the cache but never renders detached). Documented inline.
- **Verify:** lint 0 · 3989 tests (no regression) · build green. Leaflet needs a DOM (`window is not defined` in the node test env — the existing suite mocks these modules), so the layer lifecycle can't be unit-tested here; **V331** logs the live check (toggle the OSM/Mapillary evidence layer off mid-load → no stale markers appear, no "loaded" flips on for the off layer, and the request shows cancelled in the network panel).
- **SHIPPED 2026-07-15** (branch `claude/next-backlog-item-2lots0`).

### B737 — Deed importer reads legacy .doc + PDF, and accepts several deeds at once (drop-many → list → place each); fixes the DEG./MIN./SEC. bearing mis-parse `[Site Planner]` (feature+bug) #site-planner #files #metes-and-bounds  *(owner 2026-07-09 from chat — screenshot of the metes-and-bounds drop zone rejecting a .doc: "getting a notification that it can't read dot dot files. So let's fix that. And then also, I should be able to drop multiple meets and bounds in at once." Follow-up same session: "make it also read pdfs too" + supplied the real `.doc` and five real PDFs. **B737** = highest B# across both files (B736) + 1 — RENUMBERED from a provisional B736 on merge-in of `origin/main`, whose concurrent doc-review batch took B736; per repo precedent the code/tests/commit + `ui-audit/verify-b736-multiformat-deed.mjs` keep the provisional B736 label, only the backlog ID bumped. Branch `claude/dotfile-bulk-meets-bounds-ye2tb7`)*
`[x]` **DONE — shipped this session (Verify: sandbox — 12 new unit tests `test/docText.test.js` (8) + `test/metesAndBounds.test.js` DEG/MIN/SEC block (4), full suite 3184 tests green, build green, and headless end-to-end `ui-audit/verify-b736-multiformat-deed.mjs` 11/11: drops the real .doc + a text-layer PDF + a .txt at once → 3 queued rows, all three parsed to calls (PDF via the real in-browser pdf.js worker), row-click loads the textarea, "Plot all 3" runs the "Deed 1 of 3 → 2 of 3 → All 3 placed" sequence into 3 independent deed groups, zero console errors).**
- **What the owner saw:** the "2 · Plot a metes-and-bounds description" drop zone rejected `M&B - POA Parcel 3 (0.6 AC).doc` with "Can't read a .doc here…", and dropping several files only ever read the first.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST):** `readDeedFile` (`shared/files/docxText.js`) handled only `.docx` (a ZIP of XML) + plain text. A legacy `.doc` is a different binary entirely — an OLE/Compound-File container with the text stored via a *piece table* — so it fell through to the friendly-but-dead-end throw. The drop zone had no `multiple`, and both handlers hard-indexed `files[0]`.
- **Fix:**
  - **Legacy `.doc` reader** — new dependency-free `shared/files/docText.js` (`docToText`): parses the CFB container (FAT/DIFAT + **mini-FAT**, the path a real deed's small Table stream always takes), the Word FIB (guards `wIdent`, **nFib ≥ 193** so Word 6/95 don't slip through and mis-read, `fEncrypted`, `fcClx`/`lcbClx`), and the CLX **piece table** — decoding each piece with the native `TextDecoder("windows-1252")` (compressed) or `"utf-16le"`, clamped to `ccpText`. windows-1252 is load-bearing: surveyors' minute/second marks are 0x92/0x94 (→ U+2019/U+201D), which a naive `String.fromCharCode` turns into control chars the bearing parser drops. Nesting-aware field-code handling; loud, specific errors (very-old/encrypted/corrupt → "Save As .docx or paste"). Same hand-rolled, dependency-free spirit as `docxText.js`.
  - **PDF reader** — new `shared/files/pdfText.js` (`pdfToDeedText`), **lazily imported** so pdf.js stays out of the Site Planner bundle until a PDF is actually dropped (own 1.5 kB chunk). Pulls the embedded text layer via pdf.js (the engine the Review workspace already uses) and **reflows** word-wrapped survey courses back onto one logical line each (`reflowLines`) — without which PDF word-wrap splits "…23 SEC. / EAST, 403.47 FEET" across lines and the bearing loses its quadrant + distance. Scanned/image-only PDFs throw loudly ("looks scanned — paste it or drop the Word file"). Owner's five PDFs: the three written descriptions parse (5/7/10 calls); the two Carlson **exhibit drawings** (plat sheets, title-block only, no prose) honestly report "no calls" — correct.
  - **Dispatch** — `readDeedFile` gains ordered `.doc`/`.pdf` branches (`.pdf` via the lazy import); `accept` + copy widened; input gains `multiple`.
  - **Multi-file intake** (`SitePlanner.jsx`) — `readDeed(file)` → `readDeeds(files)`: reads every file (one batch-guarded commit via `deedReqRef`), builds a `deedQueue` of `{name, calls, exceptions, closes/gap, error}`, auto-loads the first readable into the textarea (single-file drop unchanged). New queue list UI (renders at ≥2) with per-file summaries + red rows for unreadable files; clicking a row loads it; the textarea edits the active row. **"Plot all"** threads a queue through `pobMode` and advances through **one** `advanceDeed` helper (all `anchorEncumbrance` exits routed through it, so no early-return aborts the run); the POB banner is now dynamic ("Deed K of N — name"); the per-deed basis-of-bearings align hint is gated to single plots (skipped mid-run to avoid banner churn + an O(parcels) solve per deed); per-deed notes roll into the final "All N placed — verify: …" summary.
  - **Bearing parser fix (bundled, found via the real deed):** the `BEARING_SRC` degree/minute/second separators matched the single-char class `[°ºo*:d-]` *before* the spelled-out words, so the bare `d` ate the "D" of "DEG" and the stray "E" was mis-read as the East quadrant — every "N/S ## DEG. ## MIN. ## SEC. E/W" bearing lost its minutes/seconds and read West as East. Reordered to match "deg"/"min"/"sec" (optional trailing period) first. `NORTH 02 DEG. 29 MIN. 38 SEC. WEST` now → N 2°29'38" W (az 357.51, not 2°). All 13 existing parser tests still pass; also now reads fully spelled-out "87 degrees 04 minutes 16 seconds".
- **Named rules:** LOUD-FAILURE (every unreadable file → a specific visible error, never a silent empty), AUDIT-FIRST (reconciled the reader against the actual dispatch seam), MODULE-SCOPE-COMPONENTS (queue list is inline JSX, no new inner component). Docs: `MAP.md` + `shared/CLAUDE.md` pointer regenerated/updated same commit; real fixtures committed (`test/fixtures/deeds/deed-poa-parcel3.doc` + `.pdf`, `deed-simple.txt`).
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** not a recurrence — no prior B# covered `.doc`/PDF deed reading or multi-file deed drop (B-metes work to date was single-file .docx/.txt + the parser + deed↔parcel align).
- Verify: sandbox

Origin: filed 2026-07-09 from chat. Branch `claude/site-planner-shift-click-select-si6ipm`)*
`[x]` **DONE — shipped this session (Verify: sandbox — 12 unit tests `test/parcelSelect.test.js` + headless `ui-audit/verify-b735-shift-accumulate.mjs` 9/9: plain-click A shows no merge banner; plain-click A then Shift-click B → "2 parcels selected" (A kept); Shift-click B again toggles off → 1 (A retained); plain-click empty canvas clears the set; end-to-end plain-select A + Shift-add B → Merge fuses the two lots + clears the selection; plus a resurrection-guard check that removing the seeded parcel doesn't bring it back on the next Shift-click — caught by an adversarial review pass). lint 0 · 3160 tests · build green.**
- **Repro (owner):** click parcel A (it selects), hold Shift and click parcel B → A deselected and only B was selected, so the 2-parcel set the Merge needs never formed and Merge stayed disabled.
- **Root cause (AUDIT-FIRST — confirmed in code):** the Site Planner keeps TWO parcel-selection stores — `sel` (the ONE primary parcel, drives the props panel / move) and `combineSel` (the SET picked for the Combine/Merge tool). A plain click selects into `sel`; a Shift-click accumulated into `combineSel` **and** reset `sel` to the clicked parcel. So A — plain-clicked, thus only ever in `sel`, never in `combineSel` — was silently dropped, and Shift-clicking B just moved the single highlight to B while `combineSel` held only `[B]`. (The bug only showed on the natural *plain-click-then-Shift-click* flow; Shift-clicking BOTH parcels already worked, since both went to `combineSel`.)
- **Fix:**
  - New pure `lib/parcelSelect.js` → `extendMergeSelection(current, clickedId, { primaryId, isActive })`: **SEEDS** the set from the current single selection (`primaryId`) the first time you Shift-extend, then toggles the clicked parcel. Reuses the shared `nextSelection` reducer (`shared/markup/selection.js`, B569) for the toggle math — one source of truth, no drift between workspaces — and layers on the two Site-Planner-specific rules: the seed, and the B170 inactive-parcel guard (never ADD an inactive parcel, but an already-picked one can always be removed). 12 unit tests.
  - `SitePlanner.jsx`: a new `shiftPickParcel(id)` wrapper drives `extendMergeSelection` from `sel`; the three Shift-click entry points (canvas body `onBgDown`, boundary `startMoveParcel`, left-rail parcel row) now call it instead of the bare `toggleMerge`. `shiftPickParcel` also OWNS `sel` (the call sites no longer `setSel` after it): a click that ADDS a parcel makes it primary, but a click that REMOVES one falls `sel` back to the last remaining picked parcel (or clears) — never leaving `sel` on the just-removed parcel, which would otherwise **re-seed and resurrect** it on the next Shift-click (a defect an adversarial review pass caught + a headless resurrection-guard check now pins). A **plain** click on a parcel (boundary tap in `onUp`, unlocked press, rail row) or a genuine **tap on empty canvas** (tagged `tapEmpty`, tiny-travel-only so a pan never wipes the set) now clears `combineSel` — matching "plain click replaces the selection." `startMergePick` (the B720 button) also seeds from `sel` so pressing Merge keeps your already-selected parcel.
  - Merge precondition is already enforced (Merge disabled below 2 picks; `mergeParcels` refuses non-adjacent lots) — the blocking `alert()` for "don't all share a boundary" was swapped to the app's non-blocking `flashWarn` (no dialog-box UI). Full greedy fusion of 3+ lots with partial shared edges is a separate `mergeRings` concern, unchanged here.
- **Gotchas checked:** the road/vertex-insert Shift+click already yields to a merge-pick when the press is inside another parcel (B718), so no shortcut collision; every parcel in the set renders with the same solid-blue picked style (no per-parcel opacity fade); empty-click deselect ignores drags/pans.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** NOT a recurrence of **B443** (that fixed Shift-clicks that never *registered* — a marquee stole the interior click; that fix is intact). This is a distinct root cause — the `sel`/`combineSel` two-store reconciliation B443 never touched. Related: B442/B444 (merge-banner z-index/layout), B720 (click-to-pick merge mode), B420 (interior click-through), B170 (inactive-parcel exclusion).
- Verify: sandbox

### B718 — Road control-point editing: right-click Add/Remove + Shift-click add (reuse the shared vertex engine) `[Site Planner]` (feature) #site-planner #road #ui  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-08 as "NEW-1"; minted **B718** = highest B# across both files (B717) + 1. - Origin: filed 2026-07-08 from chat
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** this EXTENDS the shared B230 Bluebeam vertex engine (`editablePath`/`hitEditPath`/`insertVtx`/`deleteVtx`) — which shipped before the B599 centerline-road model and so excluded roads (its `sel.kind==="el"` branch keyed off `el.points`; roads store `el.pts` + a parallel `el.vtx` treatment list). Predecessors B141/B147 added vertex-edit to measures/markups; B599/B600 built the road model — none added road control-point add/remove. No new number minted for the engine: this is the road slice of the same engine.
- **What shipped:** two pure, unit-tested helpers in `lib/roadGeometry.js` — `insertRoadVertex(pts,vtx,edgeIndex,pt)` (splices the point + a matching `{}` treatment, staying length-matched; the new interior vertex defaults to arc and renders straight until dragged because the projected point is collinear on its sparse segment) and `removeRoadVertex(pts,vtx,index)` (returns null for an endpoint or a 2-point road) + `canRemoveRoadVertex`. `SitePlanner.jsx`: `editablePath()` returns a `{layer:"road", pts:el.pts, closed:false, min:2, edgeTolFt:…, noEndpointDelete:true}` case (checked before the polygon `el.points` case); `hitEditPath()` honors a per-path `edgeTolFt` (≈ strip half-width, so a Shift-/right-click anywhere on a wide road projects onto the centerline); `insertVtx`/`deleteVtx` gain a `road` branch that keeps `pts`+`vtx` in lock-step and re-syncs the strip bbox via `reRoad`; the plain-click + context-menu wiring arms only INTERIOR road vertices for the Delete key (an endpoint/body leaves selVtx null so Delete still removes the whole road — no behavior change there).
- **Also fixed (latent bug this surfaced):** the Shift-insert `onOtherParcel` guard used `pc.id !== (path.layer==="parcel"?path.id:null)`, which was true for EVERY parcel when editing a road/el, so a road inside a parcel (the normal case) could never Shift-insert. ### B690 — Cold-start crash: a fresh/incognito client tripped the whole Site module into the error boundary (one points-less parcel record kills the finder) `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(surfaced 2026-07-07 as V231 #18 in the Cowork element-sync live run: fresh client → "Site couldn't load" error card right after boot. Minted **B690** = highest B# across both files (B689) + 1. DEDUPE-FIRST — no existing B# covers the finder acreage crash class; distinct from the B592 union tripwire (merge-time) and B54 (empty-list scare): this is a RENDER throw.)*
`[x]` **DONE — diagnosed to the exact line from the minified production stack, fixed + sandbox-verified same session (Verify: sandbox — the crash is a pure render throw, fully reproducible headless).**
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-07 from the Cowork V229–V231 run report (V231 #18)
- **Diagnosis (from the live stack, confirmed by rebuilding the deployed commit):** the reported minified frames `ym→Hp→Ij` in the `SitePlannerApp` chunk were mapped by building 40884e6 (the deployed build) locally with Supabase env configured — they are **`shoelace` → `siteAcres` → `MapFinder`** (`MapFinder.jsx`). `siteAcres` guarded `site.parcels?.length` but ran `shoelace(p.points)` unguarded — a stored record whose parcels array holds a parcel WITHOUT a `points` array (attr-only / legacy / a malformed row round-tripped verbatim through storage or `site_elements`) throws `undefined.length`, and because the finder's site list + map-marker tooltip call `siteAcres` for every record, ONE bad record crashes the entire Site workspace into its error boundary. (MapFinder's own map-drawing path already skips such parcels — `p.points?.length` — the acreage helpers just never got the same guard.)
- **Fix:** guard the two ring-area helpers at the read boundary — `shoelace` (`MapFinder.jsx`) and the planner's `polyArea` (`SitePlanner.jsx`) return 0 for a missing/empty ring, so a degenerate parcel reads "no boundary" in the list and contributes 0 area on the canvas instead of killing the module. Value-preserving for every real ring.
- **Regression net (the reason this escaped):** every headless smoke seeded a well-formed site, so the fresh-client and bad-record paths were never exercised. `ui-audit/verify-b671-element-sync.mjs` now additionally runs (5) a **NO-SEED cold start** — a truly fresh context must boot the Site module with zero page errors and no error-boundary card — and (6) a **bad-record boot** — a seeded site whose parcel has NO points must list as "no boundary" without crashing. Both new checks pass against the fixed build.
- **Negative control (diagnosis proven, not just plausible):** running check (6)'s seed against the UNFIXED deployed commit (40884e6, rebuilt locally) reproduces the production failure verbatim — the Site error card with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')" — while the fixed build lists the record as "no boundary". Also confirmed the React boundary swallows the throw (no `pageerror` fires), which is why the smokes detect the error CARD text, not page errors alone.
- **Note on the live repro's confound:** the crash fired right after the "[Supabase] connected" console line, which made it look auth/boot-order-related — it isn't. That line is just the phase-1 connection test resolving at about the same moment the finder first renders the stored list; the trigger is purely the bad record. Signing in "resolving" it is consistent: the signed-in pull merges/normalizes a different store copy.

### B688 — Header crumb didn't live-update when you rename the CURRENT project (Review / Library) `[Header-Nav / Review + Library]` (bug) #ui #doc-review #library  *(owner report 2026-07-07 with screenshot: "I changed the name below and it should auto update but didn't." Minted **B688** = highest B# across both files (B687) + 1. DEDUPE-FIRST — distinct from B439 (row snap-back) and the B191/B204 planner-crumb-live-via-`commitSiteLabel` path.)*
`[x]` **DONE — shipped + sandbox+headless-verified this session (Verify: sandbox). 2,840 unit tests green (+4 `resolveCurrentName` cases) · build green · `ui-audit/verify-review-rename-header.mjs` 6/6, with a negative-control run confirming it reproduces the owner's exact symptom pre-fix.**
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-07 from chat (screenshot)
- **Repro (owner's screenshot):** in **Review**, rename the open project in the Row-1 switcher dropdown — the dropdown ROW updated to the new name and the store persisted it, but the breadcrumb crumb ABOVE the dropdown kept the OLD name until a reload/project-switch.
- **AUDIT-FIRST root cause:** the shared `ProjectBreadcrumb` renders the crumb from the `currentProject` **prop**. In the Site-Planner planner header that prop tracks a rename live (routes through `commitSiteLabel` → `setSiteLabel`), but **Review** (`markupProject`, a `useMemo` keyed on `[projectId, meta.projectId, meta.project]`) and **Library** (`libraryProject`, recomputed per render) derive it from the **route id** and never re-derive the NAME from the store on a same-tab rename. So `commitRename → storeRename → refresh()` updated the breadcrumb's own list (the row) but not the parent's prop (the crumb) → stale crumb.
- **Fix (self-contained in the shared component — one place fixes Review, Library, and cross-tab):** new pure `resolveCurrentName(currentProject, projects)` in `projectModel.js` prefers the freshly-refreshed switcher list's name for the current project, falling back to the prop (cold/empty list, or a project not in the list) — never a regression. `ProjectBreadcrumb` now renders `currentName = resolveCurrentName(currentProject, projects)` for the crumb. Because the list is refreshed on rename **and** on the cross-tab `storage` event, a rename in another tab now updates the crumb for free too. Controlled hosts (Scheduler) are unaffected — they feed a fresh `projects` list + `currentProject` back over the bridge; the planner header is unaffected — its prop is already live and the list agrees (synchronous store write before `refresh()`).
- **Files:** `src/shared/projects/projectModel.js` (+`resolveCurrentName`, +export), `src/shared/ui/ProjectBreadcrumb.jsx` (import + `currentName` in the crumb span), `test/projects.test.js` (+4), `ui-audit/verify-review-rename-header.mjs` (new headless spec), `MAP.md` (regenerated — new export).
- **Nothing on the owner's end.** All paths are visible logged-out (same code path signed-in — the fix is display-only, independent of cloud), so no auth-only surface and no `V###` needed.

- Origin: filed 2026-07-06 from chat
- **Anti-overlap self-thinning (the real fix, before you touch a knob):** `inlineLabelEls` floors the effective spacing to the label's OWN on-screen width + ~50% breathing room (`minGapPx = labelLen·fs·0.9`, converted back to feet at the live zoom), and takes the LOOSER of that and the requested feet-spacing. So restamps can never physically overlap, a SHORT label keeps its per-type/typed spacing at working zoom (unchanged), and only labels that would collide are thinned — which also self-thins further on zoom-out. Deliberately NOT a big fixed floor (an earlier `max(150, …)` draft dominated every zoom and made the spacing control inert — caught by the adversarial review and fixed before merge). Mirrors the `dimCalloutVisible` / label-collision level-of-detail patterns.

One undo frame per commit. **No schema migration** — the fields ride through `markups`/`migrateRoad` verbatim (additive, like B620's `inlineLabel`). Defaults keep the per-type spacing (150/350/700) · size 11 · halo on; a short label at working zoom renders exactly as before, only overlapping / zoomed-out cases thin. The "background on" state reuses the existing white halo (`paintOrder` stroke `#fff`) for legibility over aerial; "off" removes it. Panel controls live in a render-body FUNCTION `inlineLabelControls` (returns JSX, not a `<Component>` — no remount).
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** direct follow-on to **B620** (inline line labels — shipped the renderer + per-type spacing); this adds the per-label knobs + self-thinning the owner asked for on live use. Not a recurrence — B620's behavior held; these are net-new controls. Not shared with Doc Review (`inlineLabelEls` lives only in `SitePlanner.jsx`; DocReview has no labeled-line renderer).
- **PDF-PARITY note (pre-existing, honest):** the export path (`buildExportSvg`) CLONES the live SVG, so inline-label density in a PNG/PDF tracks whatever zoom the export ran at. This zoom-dependence already existed pre-B678 via the `minSegPx` LOD (B620); the anti-overlap min-gap mildly amplifies it but is far gentler than the rejected fixed floor. No `data-export="skip"` on the label, so halo/size/spacing render identically on screen and in export at a given zoom. ### B679 — Double-click a callout or text box to enter edit mode `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat 2026-07-06, arrived as "NEW-2"; minted **B679** — see B678's renumber note. Branch `claude/polyline-label-controls-6hvn8e`.)*
`[x]` **Shipped this session (Verify: sandbox — proven with a REAL physical double-click gesture headlessly). Covered by `verify-b678-681-label-callout.mjs` (callout, text box, AND line all open their editor on a real double-click) + a source guard.** Double-clicking a callout / text box did nothing — the `onDoubleClick` handler existed but never fired for the user: `startMoveCallout` calls `setPointerCapture` on pointerdown to keep a drag alive past the SVG edge, and pointer capture SUPPRESSES the browser's synthetic `dblclick` (the B620 harness even worked around this by dispatching a raw event).
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-06 from chat
- **Fix — reconstruct the browser's own double-click test:** `e.detail` is 0 on a `pointerdown` (per the Pointer Events spec — click-count only rides mouse events), so a small `isDoubleTap(e, id)` replays the native rule — a second press on the SAME feature within **350 ms AND within 14 px** of the first (time **and** distance gates). Added to `startMoveCallout` (box part), `startMoveMarkup` (line/polyline/easement), and `startMoveEl` (non-grouped centerline road) → opens the in-place editor instead of starting a move. The **distance gate is what stops a "click here to select, then press over there to drag" gesture from misfiring as an edit** (an adversarial-review finding — fixed before merge). Edits only **UNLOCKED** features (a locked line/road stays select-only — also a review finding). Opens the same editor the old `onDoubleClick` did (`beginEditCallout` / `beginEditInline`), kept as a secondary path. Also restores the promised double-click-to-edit for the B620 inline labels (same root cause), so the tool hints ("double-click to edit") are now true for callouts, text boxes, and labeled lines/roads.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** the shipped `onDoubleClick` wiring (B620/B32) was present but non-functional under pointer capture — this is the missing gesture reconstruction, not a duplicate. No prior double-tap helper (grepped `isDoubleTap` / `setPointerCapture`).

Signed-out mode is untouched (the engine only activates cloud-active).

- Origin: filed 2026-07-06 from chat
- **New:** `lib/elementSync.js` (the injectable diff engine), `lib/elementApi.js` (commit_elements RPC wrapper + fetch + pure unload keepalive), `lib/zOrder.js` (explicit z utilities) + `test/elementSync.test.js` / `test/elementApi.test.js` / `test/zOrder.test.js`.
- **Diff-based committer:** a shadow map of last-committed elements keyed by (kind,id), diffed at the central autosave effect — so all ~68 scattered `setEls` sites, undo/redo (snapshot restore re-commits as a normal rev-checked edit, NO special case), paste, generation, and prunes are covered by construction. Boundaries: create/delete immediate, ~750ms per-element trailing debounce for text/live-pickers, `flushElems()` at the onUp gesture-end sites (groupMove, markup-draw, and the draw/resize/vertex fallthrough) for immediacy. A group drag / 30-element paste commits as ONE batch RPC. The engine SEEDS its shadow from the site's current rows before diffing (a ready-gate), so a plain load never re-creates existing elements.
- **Rev-guarded LWW:** every commit sends its expected rev; a miss adopts the RPC's returned current row and re-commits local on top (last-write-wins) via the debounce cadence (never a hot loop), emitting a typed conflict event that B673 will turn into a toast. Per-SITE serialized batches (reuse `serializeWrites.js`) → two commits to the same element can't interleave (retires the B528/B529 in-tab write-write race class). Dirty queue + exponential backoff (1s→30s ×5 → 'failed', stays queued) surfaced through the existing cloud badge (syncing(n)/retrying/failed) + `reportClientEvent` — LOUD-FAILURE. Unload keepalive posts pending ops straight to the RPC endpoint.
- **z_index (v12):** the `Z_LAYER` type table still dominates paint order; `z` replaces ARRAY POSITION as the within-type tiebreak in `byZ` (render + hit-test now deterministic by (type-layer, z, id)). `SITE_MODEL_VERSION` 11→12 assigns a gapped z (`ensureZ`, idx*1024 — the same rule as the B670 SQL backfill) only when missing, returning the same reference untouched otherwise (no re-load churn). New elements get a top-of-collection z assigned in the engine and patched back onto the canvas so the row's `z_index` and `data.z` agree (the B672 rebuild reads z from data). Fixtures + the identity/idempotence tests updated for the additive field.
- **Dual-write (sequencing amendment held):** the whole-doc blob save + `deletedIds`/union-merge machinery are UNCHANGED this phase — reads stay on the blob until B672's cutover, so a row-commit failure risks nothing. Killing the blob write path moves to B672.
- **⏳ V221 (signed-in):** the engine only runs cloud-active, which the sandbox can't reach — the live check confirms edits land in `site_elements` (rev bumps, new-element z on top, group = one batch, offline dirty-queue flush). See VERIFICATION.md V221.
- DEDUPE-FIRST: net-new (see B670); supersedes the whole-doc save path's write side for signed-in use.

### B643 — Eager parcel identify prefers the authoritative county CAD over the statewide fallback, so FBCAD's OWN data shows (not just the false notice suppressed) `[Site Planner / GIS]` (enhancement — follow-on to B634)  *(spun out of the B634/V194 fix, 2026-07-03; minted **B643** = highest real B# across both files (B642) + 1 on merge-in of `origin/main` — concurrent sessions took B636–B642 for the detention-rules batch; branch `claude/cowork-verification-planyr-pxwda7`)*
`[x]` **Shipped this session — completes the V194 job.** B634 (`isStatewideBackup`) made the false "county server unavailable" notice honest, but it left the underlying eager RACE untouched: the statewide TxGIO layer still out-raced FBCAD's Esri identify, so a Fort Bend click could select TxGIO's coarser statewide copy (no false notice now, but missing FBCAD's native appraisal values — V194 step 3). This makes the authoritative source actually win.
- **Fix (`lib/arcgis.js`, `MapFinder.jsx`):** identify candidates are tagged `statewide` (in `resolveCandidates`); `identifyParcelEager` now **prefers a healthy real CAD** — a real-CAD hit resolves immediately, while a statewide hit waits a bounded `BACKUP_GRACE_MS` (~1.2s) for any still-in-flight real CAD before it's accepted. ### B635 — Gantt labels collide with bars at low zoom (task/milestone/summary, incl. "Utilities" touching its own bracket) `[Scheduler / Gantt]` (bug) — shipped with the B396 dep-arrow-anchor re-report  *(owner-dropped from chat 2026-07-03 as "NEW-2" alongside the dep-arrow "NEW-1"; first filed **B629**, RENUMBERED to **B635** on merge-in of `origin/main` — concurrent sessions took B629–B634 while this was in flight; B635 = highest real B# across both files (B634) + 1. The branch `claude/gantt-dep-arrow-anchors-0pwz6f`, its commit, and ALL in-code/test/harness labels keep the provisional **B629**. NEW-1 was folded into **B396** as a re-report — see the B396 re-report addendum below; both halves ship in one PR.)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + headless-verified + shipped the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/gantt-dep-arrow-anchors-0pwz6f`).** At low (~33%) zoom on the Pappadoupolos Gantt, labels overprinted bars — a milestone name crowding an adjacent bar, a leaf name running into the row below, and a **summary caption sitting on its own bracket** ("Utilities"). Root cause: labels were placed per-row with no band confinement, so at compressed horizontal zoom (narrow bars → more labels flip to "above"/beside) a label's box bled ~2px into the neighbouring row; and the summary caption's fixed font was taller than the headroom above its bracket once the row compressed.
- **Own-row band confinement (the structural fix).** `placeGanttLabel` gained an optional `rowH` → `confineY()` clamps every label's vertical box into its OWN row band `[rowTop, rowTop+rowH]`. Because rows are disjoint vertical bands, a confined label **cannot geometrically overlap another row's bar or label** — the whole class of cross-row collisions is designed out rather than resolved case-by-case. A pure no-op when `rowH` isn't passed, so nothing else changes. Both render paths pass it.
- **Summary caption auto-fit.** New `fitCaptionFs(baseFs, headroom)` shrinks a summary caption's font to the room above its bracket (floored at 6.5px for legibility), so "Utilities"/"Wastewater"/"Water" always clear their own span even at the minimum row height. Applied on-screen and in the print `buildGanttSVG`.
- **Testability.** Bar/bracket/diamond glyphs now carry `data-gantt-bar` (+ `data-gantt-kind="summary"`) so overlaps can be measured against real DOM boxes.
- **Mirrored in the print path** (`buildGanttSVG`) — same `rowH` confinement + caption fit; its existing B402 label de-collision stays as a defensive second layer.
- **Verified:** lint **0 errors** · **2241** unit tests (scheduler anti-drift #10/normPreds updated for the shared `glyphEdges` refactor) · build green · JSX transpiles. Headless **V202** — NEW `ui-audit/verify-gantt-dep-anchors.mjs` renders the scheduler at ~33% zoom with start-date labels on (it VENDORS the CDN libs + routes them locally, so the Babel app actually renders in-sandbox — the wall that blocked V196): **0** label↔bar, **0** label↔label overlaps, "Utilities" caption bottom ≤ its bracket top, no name taller than a row band. Updated `verify-gantt-labels-deps.mjs` (V114) still green across L/C/R. **Live ~33%-zoom sign-off on the real Pappadoupolos data is tracked in V202** (owner asked Cowork to confirm live — zoom/layout-dependent).
- **NEW-1 (dep-arrow directional anchors) shipped in the same PR but under the B396 re-report** (no new B#, per owner) — see the **RE-REPORT #3** addendum on B396.

### B634 — False "statewide backup — county's server is unavailable" notice on HEALTHY Fort Bend parcel clicks (TxGIO won the eager race) `[Site Planner / GIS]` (bug) — high  *(found by the Cowork signed-in verification on planyr.io 2026-07-03 as **V194 FAIL** — the false amber notice fired on every Fort Bend click even though FBCAD returned HTTP 200 with the right parcel; first filed **B630**, RENUMBERED to **B634** on merge-in of `origin/main` — a concurrent session (`claude/stitch-not-aligned-overlay-s2wbdx`) took **B630–B633** for the Stitch align-gate batch; B634 = highest real B# across both files (B633) + 1. The commit, PR #486, and all in-code/test labels keep the provisional **B630**. Branch `claude/planyr-verification-gis-2z72mw`)*
`[x]` **Fixed + shipped this session.** After B613 switched Fort Bend to FBCAD's Esri-hosted layer, every Fort Bend click still flashed the amber **"Statewide backup — Fort Bend county's server is unavailable; shown from TxGIO"** notice — a false alarm the B613 change was meant to end.
- **Root cause — the eager RACE, NOT the circuit breaker (the live report's leading hypothesis was close but off).** The click path (`identifyParcelEager`, `arcgis.js`) queries the county CAD and the statewide TxGIO layer **in parallel and takes the first to answer**. Its doc comment assumed "real CADs are listed before the statewide fallback, [so] a healthy county still answers first" — but list order does NOT govern a parallel race. FBCAD's Esri FeatureServer identify is a hair slower than TxGIO's, so **TxGIO kept winning the race**; the winning `hit.county` became the statewide key, and the old flag `viaBackup = STATEWIDE_KEYS.includes(hit.county) && realPrimaries.length > 0` (`MapFinder.jsx`) read "statewide answered" as "the county server is down." The breaker was demonstrably **closed** (the live network capture shows the app calling FBCAD and getting **200 on every click**), and it already correctly ignores "200 + 0 features" (B245) — so the breaker was never the problem.
- **Fix — decouple the "backup" label from the race, key it off real availability.** New pure `isStatewideBackup(hitCounty, { realPrimaries, queried, statewideKeys })` in `lib/sourceHealth.js`: a statewide answer is a genuine "backup" **only when NO real CAD for this point was queryable this click** — i.e. every real primary had its breaker open and was dropped, so TxGIO was the only source left. When a healthy CAD **was** queried (whether or not it won the race), statewide merely being fastest is no longer treated as an outage → no notice. Wired into both the map-click (`handleClick`) and search-select (`selectParcelAt`) paths, replacing the two identical `viaBackup` expressions. A genuine outage (real CAD breaker opens) still surfaces the honest backup notice, and the imported parcel/appraisal data is unchanged.
- **Verified:** lint 0 · full suite **2333 tests green** (post-merge with origin/main; +6 new `isStatewideBackup` cases in `test/sourceHealth.test.js`: race-lost ⇒ no notice, breaker-open ⇒ real backup, statewide-only area, border straddle keeps at least one real CAD, defensive empties) · build green · doc-pointer audit ✓. The live click-through (no false notice on a healthy Fort Bend lot; the honest notice still appears when FBCAD is genuinely forced down) is owed as **V194** — this sandbox's Chromium egress is reset by the agent proxy on every GIS host (`net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`), so the live map can't be driven here.

### B630 — Don't force Stitch's Align gate onto sets that can't be stitched (schedule/legend / all-NOT-TO-SCALE) `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (feature — product call)  *(Cowork brief 2026-07-03 "NEW-1"; minted **B630** = highest real B# across both files (B627) + 1; branch `claude/stitch-not-aligned-overlay-s2wbdx`)*
`[x]` **Fixed + shipped this session.** Opening the JACINTOPORT mechanical set (14-page schedule/legend/code-summary set, resumes as `kind:"stitch"`) used to show **13/14 sheets flagged "⚠ Not aligned"** — a false demand, because the set has no match-line seams to stitch and is not to scale. Now such a set is classified a **reference set** and the align gate is dropped entirely.
- **Classifier:** `isReferenceSet(placed, ftPerUnit)` (`lib/stitchGeom.js`, pure + unit-tested) — true when **≥2 placed sheets, NO match-line seam on any sheet, no composite scale, AND ≥1 sheet positively `notToScale`** (a legend/notes/schedule/"NTS" sheet). The `some(notToScale)` requirement is the guard (added after the adversarial review) against a **real plan set aligned by a shared corner** — that case is also seam-less + uncalibrated but has ZERO not-to-scale sheets, so it's never misclassified and keeps the manual-Align affordance. `loadStitch` **back-fills `notToScale`** for pre-B631 saves via a background re-read of each source's page metadata (the same reader the drop path uses; best-effort, token-guarded, only ever upgrades a sheet to not-to-scale), so the owner's JACINTOPORT set (whose legend/notes sheets read not-to-scale) is still caught on resume. Fail open: any seam OR any calibration OR no not-to-scale sheet ⇒ a real plan, gate unchanged.
- **UI:** when `referenceSet`, the canvas overlay + sidebar "Align before measuring" nag are suppressed, and a **dismissible steer** — *"These look like reference sheets (not to scale) — there's nothing to stitch or measure here · [Open as single sheets]"* — offers a jump to single-sheet Review (`onReview`). `blockedOverUnaligned` gives a reference-set-specific message if the user still tries to measure.
- **Verified:** lint 0 · full suite green (fixtures: JACINTOPORT reference set → flagged; a match-lined plan set → NOT flagged; a calibrated scale-less set → NOT flagged; <2 sheets → not a set) · build green · logged-out headless smoke (Stitcher mounts + renders clean). Signed-in click-through on the real JACINTOPORT card → **V200**.

### B631 — Suppress the "Align before measuring" gate + overlay on NOT-TO-SCALE placed sheets `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (bug — false gate)  *(Cowork brief 2026-07-03 "NEW-2"; minted **B631**)*
`[x]` **Fixed + shipped this session.** A sheet with no plan scale can never be measured, so its "Align before measuring" gate was a false demand. New pure predicate `isNotToScale(meta)` (`lib/sheetRead.js`) = an explicit title-block "NOT TO SCALE" (`scale.explicit==="nts"`) **or** a text-dense non-drawing sheet (`textDense` — notes/specs/legend/schedule, B379); it's deliberately FALSE for a merely-unlabeled plan sheet (that keeps Calibrate+Align). The flag now rides on the placed object — set in `addSheet`/`addGroup` from the read meta, persisted in `buildSnapshot`, read back in `loadStitch` — and a NOT-TO-SCALE sheet renders **no align overlay + no sidebar nag** (the existing measure-block still applies). Scaled sheets are unchanged; local-scale measuring on unaligned-but-scaled sheets stays out of scope. Unit-tested (explicit-NTS / text-dense true; unlabeled-plan false).

### B632 — "Not aligned" overlay balloons over the sheet at low zoom `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (bug — rendering)  *(Cowork brief 2026-07-03 "NEW-3"; minted **B632**)*
`[x]` **Fixed + shipped this session.** The overlay lived inside the zoomed world group at a constant ON-SCREEN size (`ls = n/zoom`), so at the ~1–15% zoom needed to see a whole set the warning text + dashed border ballooned over each small sheet and read as "broken." New pure `alignBadgeMetrics(screenMin)` (`lib/stitchGeom.js`) sizes the badge to the sheet's on-screen footprint: **font ≤ ~11% of the sheet's smaller on-screen side** (and never > the old 22px), border likewise; below ~54px the badge **collapses to an outline-only dashed border** (no text), and the label shortens to "⚠ Not aligned" below 150px. The render uses an `lc(px)` helper (`px / (view.zoom * sheetScale)`) to convert the desired on-screen px into the sheet's local units. Visually unchanged at normal zoom; a small legible fraction at low zoom. Unit-tested at every tier + non-finite/negative inputs.

### B633 — Stitch places the same page multiple times; no dedupe (8 unique pages shown as 14) `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (bug — duplication)  *(Cowork brief 2026-07-03 "NEW-4"; minted **B633**)*
`[x]` **Fixed + shipped this session — the biggest visible defect in the owner's set.** `addSheet`/`addGroup` appended to `placed[]` with no already-placed guard, so a re-click stacked exact duplicates; `loadStitch` then re-rendered them on every open (owner's live JACINTOPORT draft `rvmqn4oltqlyaio`: 14 placed entries / **8 unique** — p1×4, p2×3, p28×2 → two identical M0.01 sheets side by side).
- **New pure module `lib/stitchDedupe.js`** (unit-tested): `isPlaced(placed,srcId,pageNum)` + `dedupePlaced(placed)` (collapse exact `(srcId,pageNum)` repeats, keep the FIRST = index-0 world frame + its transform; returns `{placed,removed}`).
- **(a) Add-time guard:** `addSheet` no-ops an already-placed page; `addGroup` filters already-placed pages (whole-group re-click ⇒ quiet "already placed" notice). **Both** re-check inside the `setPlaced` updater against the freshest array (added after the adversarial review — the top-of-function `placedRef` check can be stale under a rapid double-click), so a concurrent double-add can't double-place.
- **(b) Load cleanup + re-persist:** `loadStitch` runs `dedupePlaced` on the loaded array, then a `dedupeResaveRef`-gated `useEffect([placed])` calls `saveNow()` once to re-persist the cleaned array (local mirror **and** cloud). Guardrail: ONLY exact `(srcId,pageNum)` repeats collapse — two distinct pages that merely share a printed sheet number are never merged. Confirmed `reconcile` (`reviewStore.js`) picks the newer copy WHOLESALE (never merges arrays), so duplicates can't re-inflate on the cloud↔draft merge.
- **Verified:** unit test proves the owner's 14→8 collapse with the world frame retained + order preserved; distinct-page/same-number kept separate; no-op on unique arrays. lint 0 · full suite green · build green. Signed-in re-persist round-trip (open the real card → 8 sheets → reopen still 8) → **V200**.

### B627 — Chambers County "can't click / GIS is down": TxGIO disabled the parcels `/query` op — route outlines via `/export`, clicks via `/identify` `[Site Planner]` (bug) — high  *(owner-reported 2026-07-03 "figure out why i cant click / why chambers county gis is down"; minted **B627** = highest real B# across both files (B626) + 1 after merging `origin/main` — a concurrent session took B625/B626 for the deed-alignment work below; branch `claude/chambers-county-gis-down-ttqfnv`)*
`[x]` **Fixed + shipped this session.** Chambers County parcels are served by the **TxGIO statewide parcel MapServer** (`feature.geographic.texas.gov/.../Parcels/stratmap_land_parcels_48_most_recent/MapServer/0`), which is also every county's outage fallback (`STATEWIDE_PARCEL_LAYER`). **Root cause (confirmed live):** TxGIO **disabled the layer `/query` + `/find` operations** on that service — both now 400 with `"Requested operation is not supported by this service."` (extendedCode -2147220222) — even though the layer metadata still advertises `capabilities: Map,Query`. The service's **`/identify` and `/export` ops still work.** Because the app renders parcel outlines with esri-leaflet's **`featureLayer` (which draws by QUERYING)** and identifies a clicked lot with a **point `/query`**, both went dark on Chambers: **no outlines painted AND no lot could be selected** — exactly "can't click / GIS is down." Working counties (HCAD/FBCAD, whose `/query` is healthy) were unaffected.
- **The two symptoms, both root-caused to the same dead `/query`:** (1) `makeParcelLayer` → `EL.featureLayer` renders via `/query` → blank Chambers (no lines); (2) `queryAtPoint` → point `/query` → capability error → click selects nothing.
- **Fix — outlines via `/export`:** new `makeParcelImageLayer` (an esri `dynamicMapLayer` → server `/export` image, `transparent`+`minZoom`-gated) and a single smart entry point `makeParcelDisplayLayer(url)` that routes **only** the known query-disabled `STATEWIDE_PARCEL_LAYER` to the image overlay; every other (queryable) CAD stays the styleable vector `featureLayer` (which also backs the instant B441 client-side click highlight). Applied at both display sites — MapFinder's Select-parcels tool and SitePlanner's in-planner Add-parcel outline. `parcelDisplay.js`.
- **Fix — clicks via `/identify`:** `queryAtPoint` now wraps its `/query` in try/catch; on the **specific** capability error (`isQueryCapabilityError`) **and** only for a `/MapServer/<id>` layer, it retries the MapServer **`/identify`** op (`identifyAtPoint`) — building a small synthetic map frame around the click and returning the parcel that actually **contains** the point (even-odd PIP) in the same `{geometry:{rings},attributes}` shape. A real timeout/network/other error still surfaces as an outage; FeatureServers are untouched; **self-heals** (the fallback never fires once TxGIO re-enables `/query`). `arcgis.js`. The eager multi-county click path + circuit breaker heal automatically (a successful identify records the source healthy), so the "statewide backup / unavailable" notices clear too.
- **Honest residual (documented, self-healing):** typed **ID/address search** on Chambers stays down until TxGIO restores `/query` (text search needs `/query` or `/find`, both dead — `/identify` is spatial-only). The app already degrades to "search unavailable — pan/zoom (click the lot) instead," which works. Noted in `counties.js` + surfaced to the owner.
- **Verified:** lint 0 · **2222 tests green** (+7 new `queryAtPoint → /identify` fallback tests: capability-error classification, retry-and-select, picks the containing polygon from multiple hits, no-fallback on a non-capability error / on a FeatureServer, null on empty identify) · build green. **The SHIPPED code, run in Node against the LIVE TxGIO service, now selects real Chambers lots** — ONEOK Mont Belvieu storage `PROP_ID 46351`, Anahuac ISD `PROP_ID 438`, both with geometry — via the identify fallback; **Harris/HCAD confirmed to still use the fast `/query` path** with no needless fallback; the `/export` image returns real transparent parcel linework (200/png). The in-browser click-through (outlines paint + click selects) is owed as **V198** — this sandbox's Chromium egress is reset by the agent proxy for every GIS/basemap host (`net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`), so the live map can't be driven here; harness `gis-verify/chambers-parcel-click-verify.mjs` is ready for planyr.io/CI.

### B620 — Inline line labels (text riding along a line) as an alternative to callouts `[Site Planner]` (feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-02 as "NEW-6"; deferred that session as not-urgent, then picked up + expanded by the owner 2026-07-02; minted **B620** = B619 + 1; branch `claude/site-planner-backlog-impl-rm7ma4`)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-07-02.** A line/polyline/road/easement can carry an optional `inlineLabel` that renders **along the feature itself** (e.g. `18" SANITARY SEWER` on the line) — no separate callout needed. Owner-expanded scope + behavior:
- **Applies to drawn lines/polylines, roads, AND easements**, with **per-feature label density** (owner: "a sewer is small and needs more references, a road far fewer, an easement in between"): the label **repeats along the path** at a per-type spacing — line/polyline **150 ft**, easement **350 ft**, road **700 ft** (always ≥1, centered, when shorter than the spacing). - Each instance is **rotated to its local segment**, **auto-flipped** into `[-90,90]` (never upside-down — `((a%180)+180)%180; if(a>90)a-=180`), **offset above the centerline**, in the feature's **own color + a white halo**, **LOD-gated** (hides when the on-screen segment can't fit the text; returns on zoom-in), and — unlike selection chrome — **appears in PNG/PDF exports** (no `data-export="skip"`).
- **Edited two ways:** a panel **"Inline label"** field in each feature's Properties, **and double-click the feature** to type in place (`editInline` state + `beginEditInline`/`commitEditInline`, mirroring the callout editor). Double-clicking a centerline **road** opens the label editor; its type/actions menu stays on **right-click**.

Panel fields push **one undo frame per edit** (onFocus), not per keystroke (a review follow-up). **No schema/migration** — `inlineLabel` rides through verbatim (`markups: arr(...)`; roads spread through `migrateRoad`).
- **Verified:** lint 0 · **2206 tests** green (+ `bugHuntGuards.test.js` B620 guard: auto-flip math, per-type spacing, own-color+halo, non-sticky, no export-skip, all 3 render sites) · build green · headless `ui-audit/verify-b620-inline-label.mjs` **12/12** (render on all types, angle∈[-90,90] incl. the flipped line, own color + white halo, density gradient 9-line vs 2-road, export survival, LOD hide/restore, double-click editor, typing updates, non-sticky). An adversarial review found no high/medium defects; its two low findings (per-keystroke undo on the new panel fields; boundary-easement label skipping the closing edge) were fixed.
