### B621 — Duration input model: calendar-real months/years, working-day weeks & days `[Scheduler]` (feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-02 as "NEW-1"; first filed provisionally **B615** but RENUMBERED to **B621** on merge-in of `origin/main` — a concurrent session (branch `claude/site-planner-backlog-impl-rm7ma4`) had already shipped B615–B620; B621 = highest real B# across both files (B620) + 1. The branch `claude/duration-input-working-calendar-m4chdv`, its commits, PR #472, and ALL in-code/test labels keep the provisional **B615**. Dedup: NOT B159 — export-only Gantt density; NOT B256 — the O(n²) recompute perf task.)*
`[x]` **Shipped this session.** Typed durations now resolve the way a developer means them — two measuring sticks keyed to the unit — with both the parsed duration and the computed end visible.
- **Recorded BEFORE editing (the two symbols the owner asked me to inspect, not guess):**
  - **(a) current duration-parse + end-date derivation:** `duration` was stored as a plain **integer = inclusive count of working (business) days** — no unit concept; `0` = milestone. Parsed in the grid via `applyUpdate` → `parseInt(val)||0` (so `3w`→3). End derived by `calcEnd(start,dur) = addBD(start, dur-1)` (skip Sat/Sun + `HOLIDAY_SET`). End is re-derived from duration in `updateTask`, `previewProject`, `cascadeDates`, `normalizeToV6`, and the holiday-recompute effect. Migration used a boolean `_v6` flag (not a numeric version), idempotent via early-return.
  - **(b) the start-date lock:** the `pinnedStart` boolean — `cascadeDates` does NOT re-derive a `pinnedStart` task's start from predecessors (`if (!preds.length || t.pinnedStart) …`); it's set implicitly when a Start is typed/dragged and cleared when predecessors are edited. **UI:** an amber **padlock SVG** on the Start cell shown only when pinned; click → unpin + re-apply predecessors.
- **What shipped (mirroring, not guessing):** a small **pure, dependency-free** helper set in `public/sequence/index.html` (mirrored VERBATIM into `ui-audit/stress/scheduler-engine.mjs`, the tested copy): `parseDurationInput` (3w/3 weeks · 15d/15 days · 2mo/2 months · 1y/1 year · bare number→days · empty→milestone · **junk → {error} so the field shows a visible inline error, never a silent 0**), `addCalendarMonths` (end-of-month clamp: Jan 31 +1mo → Feb 28/29), `rollForwardToWorkday` (plain forward off a weekend/holiday — no month-crossing guard, owner decision), `workdaysBetween` (**closed form** — full-weeks×5 + partial-week remainder − HOLIDAY_SET weekday hits; NO day-by-day loop), and `resolveDuration` (d/w = working days via `calcEnd`; mo/y = calendar add + roll-forward, working-day count **derived** off the span). Week = **5 working days, hard-coded** (6-day weeks are B617, deliberately NOT parameterized here). No months→days factor anywhere. Reuses the existing `HOLIDAY_SET`/`ensureHolidays` path — no new holiday list.
- **Model:** each task keeps its canonical working-day `duration` (every existing consumer unchanged) + the typed intent `durUnit`(`d`|`w`|`mo`|`y`) `durValue`. `cascadeDates`/`rollupParentDates`/`updateTask`/`previewProject`/new-task factory/holiday-recompute all made unit-aware. Duration cell renders the unit (`fmtTaskDuration`) with a derived-working-days tooltip for mo/y; the end date stays visible in the Finish column.
- **Migration `_v6 → _v7` (`normalizeToV7`, idempotent):** stamps `durUnit:'d'`/`durValue:duration` on every legacy task; re-derives via `resolveDuration('d')` which **equals** the old `calcEnd` → zero end-date shift by construction. Wired into all 4 load-pipeline sites. **Ran the real before/after diff on the live production dataset** (scheduler Supabase `hs-v1`, **667 tasks**): **0 real shifts** — the only 5 flagged were **parents** rolled up from an intentional Sunday year-end milestone, whose end comes from rollup (unchanged), not `calcEnd`. Reproduced data-safe in `ui-audit/stress/verify-b615-migration.mjs` (18,000 no-shift pairs + parent-rollup + idempotency + the new units).
- **Accepted-on-purpose divergences (not bugs):** the same "7 months" on a Jan vs Jul start yields slightly different working-day counts; "4 weeks" (20 wd) ≠ "1 month" (calendar).
- **Tests:** +30 in `test/schedulerEngine.test.js` (parser, calendar clamp, roll-forward, closed-form count cross-checked vs a day-by-day reference across 400 holiday-crossing spans, resolver, unit-aware cascade, migration idempotency + no-shift) + anti-drift source/mirror guards. lint 0 · **2201 tests green** · build green · both babel blocks parse via esbuild.
- **Verified:** everything runnable here is green. The live in-app click-through can't run in the sandbox (the scheduler's React/Babel/Supabase CDNs are egress-blocked → `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`), so it's logged as **V196** (harness `ui-audit/verify-b615-b616-scheduler.mjs` ready for an unrestricted browser).

### B622 — Finish-date entry sets a hard-finish constraint with a lock toggle `[Scheduler]` (feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-02 as "NEW-2"; renumbered **B616 → B622** on the same `origin/main` merge-in (B615/B616 were taken by the concurrent Site Planner batch); B622 = B621 + 1. Branch/commits/PR #472 + in-code/test labels keep the provisional **B616**.)*
`[x]` **Shipped this session.** Typing a Finish date pins it as a **hard finish constraint** and shows a **padlock toggle** on the Finish field — the exact icon + interaction as the existing Start lock (which I inspected first: the amber padlock SVG on the Start cell, driven by `pinnedStart`; see B615's recorded findings). The two locks are now visually and behaviorally identical.
- **Semantics:** a locked finish is an absolute date the schedule is measured against — the `pinnedEnd` task's `end` is a **fixed point** in `cascadeDates` (successors cascade from it; it never moves when the predecessor chain slips). The start back-calcs from the locked end to preserve the working-day duration (`startForEnd`, the working-day inverse of `calcEnd`). **Precedence:** the locked finish is the constraint; the duration/predecessor-derived finish is **checked against it** — if the chain forces a start too late to fit the duration before the locked finish, the task is flagged `finishConflict` **loudly** (a red banner listing the tasks + a red ⚠ on the row) and the end is **never** silently overwritten or exceeded — the user resolves it (move the finish, shorten the duration, or change the dependency).
- **Implementation:** `pinnedEnd` mirrors `pinnedStart` — set when a Finish is typed (`updateTask`/`previewProject`), cleared by the padlock click (which re-flows the finish from start+duration). The Finish cell renders the same padlock SVG + tooltip; a conflict adds the ⚠ + danger color. The holiday-recompute + all load paths preserve a locked finish (never re-derive its end). Confirmed the interaction with `cascadeDates` so the locked finish participates as a fixed point, not a floating output.
- **Tests:** covered by the B615 batch — `startForEnd` inverse, pinnedEnd no-preds (end held, start back-calc, no conflict), a conflicting predecessor (conflict flagged, lock held), a non-conflicting predecessor (no flag), and a successor cascading from the locked finish; + anti-drift guards for the lock icon, unlock path, and banner. lint 0 · 2201 green · build green.
- **Verified:** logic green here; the live click-through (type a finish → padlock; slip a predecessor → banner; unlock) is part of **V196** (sandbox can't render the CDN-loaded scheduler).

- **Triggering bug (repro → expected):** Schedule → open a task's notes → click an existing note's date (or its text) to change it → the whole panel closed ("takes me out"). Expected + now delivered: clicking a date or text edits it **in place** with the panel staying open; the panel closes only on ✕ or a deliberate backdrop click.
- **Confirmed mechanism (read the real handlers, not guessed):** cause (b) from the spec — an edit-commits-**and-tears-down-on-blur** pattern. Editing a note put its `<textarea>` in `autoFocus` with `onBlur → saveEdit() → setEditId(null)`; moving focus into that row's date `<input>` blurred the textarea, committed, and unmounted the sibling date input mid-click — the `mouseup`/`click` then landed on the backdrop (whose `onClick={onClose}` fired because inner `stopPropagation` can't stop a click on an element the render just removed / a native-picker portal click). Exactly the "native-picker/portal click reaching the backdrop" case. Fixed **by construction**.
- **The rebuild (dated-grid running log; the whole panel replaced):** two-column rows — compact **M/D** date in a fixed left rail (~54px, plain Schedule-purple `#534AB7` text — the AA-safe shade of the module accent `#7F77DD` — click to edit), hairline vertical divider, note body; hairline row dividers, no per-note card fill. **Descending (newest first), no sort toggle.** **Add-at-top** composer prepends, dates to today, focuses the body (honors `initChar` quick-entry). **Inline CRUD that never strands you:** click date → native `<input type=date>` (pops wider than the rail — fine); click body → edit in place; delete reveals on row hover; commit-on-Enter/blur **saves and stays open**. **Guarded dismiss:** closes only on ✕, on Escape (which first backs out an active edit / a composer date-picker), or on a click whose `mousedown` **and** target are the backdrop element itself (`e.target === backdrop` + a press-started-on-backdrop ref) — never a bubbled child / native-picker portal click.
- **Storage contract kept intact:** notes stay `{id, date:"YYYY-MM-DD", text}`; `toShortDate`/`parseFlexDate` untouched; the rail gets a **display-only** `noteShortMD` (M/D) formatter; the native picker reads/writes the stored ISO directly. New sub-components (`NoteRow`, `AddNoteComposer`) defined at **module scope** (B247/B258 focus-loss trap avoided). Every edit maps by note **id** (`notes.map(x => x.id === cur.id ? …)`), so an edit structurally can't scramble the other notes — the modern successor to the removed free-text by-text matching. All CRUD rides the existing `updateTask → setData` autosave/cloudSync path (B210/B212/B566) + the `<script id="planar-data">` self-save — neither bypassed; a failed save surfaces via the existing badge.
- **Also:** the single running-log view supersedes the old **"View as: Free text"** mode, so the now-orphaned toggle was removed from the `NotesColHeader` `···` menu (the **Text size** preference is kept and still honored per-note). The drift-guard `schedulerEngine.test.js` "D2" was repointed from the removed free-text matcher to the new id-keyed-edit + guarded-dismiss invariants (the file is never edited to make a test green — the feature it pinned was deliberately removed).

### B613 — Fort Bend parcel layer: switch off FBCAD's chronically-down self-hosted server, onto FBCAD's own Esri-hosted (ArcGIS Online) parcel service `[Site Planner / GIS]` (bug — recurring reliability)  *(owner-reported 2026-07-02 — "figure out why Fort Bend Appraisal District [layer] is not working well… I feel like we've had so much trouble with Fort Bend… maybe we just cache it"; minted **B613** = highest real B# across both files (B612) + 1; branch `claude/fort-bend-appraisal-issues-8j5cp3`. Closes the root cause behind the whole FBCAD trouble family — B137/B244/B245/B382/B469.)*
`[x]` **Shipped 2026-07-02.** Diagnosed the recurring Fort Bend flakiness to ONE root cause and fixed it at the source rather than adding another layer of fallback. **Every past Fort Bend incident (B137 "can't click a visible lot", B244/B245 the 45s freeze + statewide fallback, B382 "takes forever then won't click", B469 CORS) traces to the app depending directly on FBCAD's SELF-HOSTED server `gis.fbcad.org/serverarcgis2` — an on-prem ArcGIS server with no CDN/redundancy that repeatedly 503s, times out, and isn't CORS-clean, and has already migrated servers once (the "serverarcgis2" in the path).** Live-probed 2026-07-02: `gis.fbcad.org` resets the TLS connection on every path (~11.5s hang → reset) — the origin server itself, not a proxy denial. Caching alone (the owner's suggestion) would only smooth the DISPLAY tiles; it can't fix click/search when the source's query is down, and the statewide TxGIO fallback's own `/query` was ALSO failing at probe time ("operation not supported"), so both live sources could fail a click simultaneously.
- **The fix — repoint Fort Bend to FBCAD's OWN data on Esri's ArcGIS Online cloud.** Research + independent live-probe found FBCAD publishes its parcels as a hosted feature service on its own AGOL org (`services2.arcgis.com/D4saGHECICkCeoJm/.../FBCAD_Public_Data/FeatureServer/0`, layer 0 "FBCAD Public Parcel Data"). It's the SAME authoritative FBCAD data but Esri-hosted (reliable, CORS-open, no key), holds all ~385k county parcels, is **refreshed daily** (last edit 2026-07-02 at probe time — fresher than the statewide layer or any snapshot), is natively **EPSG:2278** (State Plane feet — our coordinate spine, no reprojection), and carries the full native appraisal schema (OWNERNAME, LANDVALUE/IMPVALUE/TOTALVALUE as real numbers, SITUS, LEGAL, LANDSIZEAC, YEARBUILT, land-use codes, exemptions, deed refs). Verified by direct curl: metadata (capabilities=Query), a Fort Bend point-click query (returns lot R40594 with polygon geometry in feet), and an owner-name search all succeed.
- **Single switch point (`lib/counties.js`):** `COUNTIES.fortbend` (search) and `COUNTIES_MAP.fortbend` (display + click) both repointed at the hosted `FeatureServer/0`; `idField`/`addrField` hints set to `QUICKREFID`/`SITUS` (both auto-detected anyway by `detectField`). `resolveLayerUrl`/`lookupParcels`/`makeParcelLayer`/`queryFeatures` all handle a FeatureServer layer natively — no other code change. The old self-hosted URL is retired as primary (kept in a comment). The statewide TxGIO layer **stays** the automatic outage fallback (`statewideFallbackFor` unchanged) and the display hang-guard + circuit breaker (B244/B382) remain the safety net.
- **`lib/appraisal.js`:** added `land_?size_?ac` to the Acreage matcher (FBCAD `LANDSIZEAC`, acres — not `LANDSIZEFT`) and `land_?state_?code` to Land use (FBCAD `Land_State_Code`) so the curated appraisal panel fully populates from the new schema; the TxGIO/HCAD mappings are untouched (proven by the unchanged `test/appraisal.test.js`).
- **Verification harnesses** `gis-verify/fbcad-outage-fallback-verify.mjs` + `ui-audit/verify-parcel-resilience.mjs` repointed to the new host; new `gis-verify/fbcad-hosted-primary-verify.mjs` added for the happy-path click.
- lint 0 · **2171 tests green** (counties + appraisal suites unchanged and passing) · build green. `[x]` **Shipped 2026-07-02.** Root cause (confirmed in code): `mergeSiteContent` (siteModel.js) unions every drawn collection by id, and only a `deletedIds` tombstone keeps a deletion deleted; separately `wouldThinClobber` (cloudSync.js, B459) blocks a save that drops ≥2 items with no tombstone to "explain" the drop → the false "changed in another session" banner + the take-over→resurrect→re-prompt loop. B556/B596 wired tombstones into `deleteSel`/`deleteDrawing`/`mergeParcels`/`removeParcelById`/`removeOverlay`, but the dock-zone + several sibling delete handlers were never covered — exactly the owner's "same issue on another element." Fixes (all reuse the existing `tombstone()` + undo/history plumbing):

  - **`commitEditCallout`** — blanking an existing (already-synced) callout deletes it; tombstone so a merge can't resurrect it.
Undo/redo unaffected: every site calls `pushHistory()` before `tombstone()`, and the history snapshot carries `deletedIds` (undo drops the tombstone + restores the item; redo re-applies). ### B597 — Formula engine: errors now PROPAGATE through aggregation (Excel parity), instead of silently skipping the bad row `[Scheduler]` (enhancement)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-30 "match excel exactly" — accepting the optional skip-vs-propagate decision flagged in B590; minted **B597** = highest real B# across both files (B596) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B596 a concurrent `main` took for the parcel-merge bug below; branch `claude/scheduling-formula-column-anxv35`, fresh from `main`)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B597 also names another item in this file:** “Renaming a site snapped right back to the old name after Enter (bug) *(owner-reported 2…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B597* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B597 against all of them.
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 errors · 2114 unit tests green (98 in `test/formula.test.js`, +12 B596 cases) · build green · inline-sync guard green · headless E2E `ui-audit/verify-b583-formula-column.mjs` PASS (now also asserts error-propagation live through `window.PlanyrFormula`).** Before: a formula column whose cell errors (`[Price]/[Cost]` with a 0 cost → `#DIV/0!`) was stored as BLANK in the host row map, so `SUM` over that column silently skipped the bad row and showed a quietly-smaller total. After: it matches Excel — any consumer of an errored cell re-raises the error.
- **How (engine, `src/shared/formula/formula.js`):** added an ERROR-VALUE sentinel `errVal(code)` + `raiseIfErr` (the engine still THROWS internally; this represents an *already-determined* error living in a cell). It re-raises at every consumption point: the four scalar coercions (`toNumber`/`toStr`/`toBool`/`toDateSerial`), `compareValues`, a bare `[Col]` / `[@Col]` reference, the whole-column collectors (so `SUM`/`AVERAGE`/`MIN`/`MAX`/`PRODUCT`/`COUNT`/`COUNTA` propagate), and the conditional aggregations (`COUNTIF`/`SUMIF`/`AVERAGEIF` — on a criteria-range cell or a consumed sum/avg cell). `evaluateFormula` surfaces a trailing error value as `{ok:false}`; `formatValue` renders its code. `IFERROR`/`ISERROR`/`ISNA` trap it as expected.
- **How (host, `public/sequence/index.html`):** `computeFormulaValues` + `previewFormula` now store an errored cell as `PF.errVal(res.error)` (was `PF.BLANK`) in the shared row map, so a downstream column that aggregates it propagates. The errored column's OWN display is unchanged (still shows its code). `errVal`/`isErrVal` exported on `window.PlanyrFormula`; engine re-synced into the inline block.
- **Scoped boundaries (deliberate, documented + tested):** (1) `XLOOKUP`/`INDEX` propagate the SPECIFIC matched/indexed error cell (and `XLOOKUP` an error scanned *before* a match) — but `MATCH`'s family-filtered compare-safe scan SKIPS an error cell (use `XLOOKUP` if you need lookup-array error propagation); (2) `SUMIF`/`AVERAGEIF` propagate an error in a *matching* sum cell but not in a *non-matching* row's sum cell (only consumed cells raise); (3) a normal BLANK cell is still skipped — only a real error value propagates.
- **Files:** `src/shared/formula/formula.js`, `public/sequence/index.html` (synced engine + host glue), `test/formula.test.js`, `ui-audit/verify-b583-formula-column.mjs`. Additive — no schema/persistence change. Signed-in scheduler cloud click-through folded into `VERIFICATION.md` V178.

`[x]` **DONE + headless-verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1. lint 0 errors · 2095 unit tests green · build green · lazy split intact · `ui-audit/verify-bumpout-anchor-style.mjs` 7/7 (real Chromium, logged-out).** Two independent bump-out (dog-ear) fixes:
- **Bug 1 — the resize let the bump-out float off its building corner.** A bump-out resize routed through the generic element resize (`refitChildren` → free drag box + `clampToHost`, which re-pins only ONE axis), so on a rotated building dragging a grip slid the bump ALONG the wall, away from its corner — opening a gap between the bump and the dock doors (the doors start at the bump's along-edge, which had moved). Even a pure projection drag could shift the along on a rotated bump. **Fix (`SitePlanner.jsx` `refitChildren`):** when the resized element IS a dog-ear, update its stored span-along-wall + projection from the new box (`dogEarSize`) and then RE-DERIVE its geometry from the host via `dogEarGeom` — so its inner edge stays pinned to the dock face and its outer end to the building corner. Only along / projection change; the bump can never slide off the corner, so the doors stay flush. Reuses the existing pure `dogEarGeom`/`dogEarSize` (B362) — no new geometry.
- **Bug 2 — a bump-out ignored the building's fill color + opacity.** A bump-out is its own `building`-type element, so a per-building color/opacity override didn't reach it. **Fix (render-time inheritance, owner's mental model "a bump-out is part of the building"):** in `renderElPx` a dog-ear now draws with its HOST building's resolved fill/stroke/fillOpacity (`styleEl = host || el`); the Properties panel resolves + targets the host for a bump-out too (`styleHostOf` → `curStyle`, `setSelEl`, `clearElStyle`), so styling either one keeps the whole unit one colour. Auto-fixes existing bumps (no migration, no stored duplication). Reuses `elStyle` (lib/planStyle.js) unchanged.

### B596 — Merging parcels raised a false "someone else has this open" conflict (merge dropped ≥2 items with no tombstone) `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-30 on planyr.io — "when I tried to merge parcels it gave me a note that someone else had that tab open… no one did; it only happens when I merge, not when I add"; minted **B596** = highest real B# across both files (B595) + 1; SAME data-loss/tombstone family as B459/B556/B594/B595; branch `claude/parcel-merge-notification-bug-c7kgoo`)*
`[x]` **DONE + headless-verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1. lint 0 errors · 2105 unit tests green (+3 in `test/cloudThinGuard.test.js`) · build green · lazy split intact · `ui-audit/verify-b596-merge-tombstone.mjs` 6/6 (real Chromium, logged-out) + existing `verify-merge-banner.mjs` 6/6 (merge flow intact).** Merging parcels combined them into one but recorded **no tombstone** for the consumed parcels — so collapsing 3+ parcels (a net drop of ≥2 items) tripped the **thin-clobber guard (B459)**, which misread a legitimate active-tab merge as a stale-tab clobber and blocked the cloud save with a FALSE **"This project was changed in another session — Take over editing"** banner. Adding parcels GROWS the count, so it never tripped — exactly matching the owner's "only when I merge, not when I add."
- Part of: **B648** (Persistence & Sync epic).
- **Root cause (`SitePlanner.jsx` `mergeParcels`):** the merge did `setParcels(arr.filter(out the selected) + [newMergedParcel])` with no `tombstone(...)` call. `contentCount` counts parcels, so N→1 dropped the count by N-1; for N≥3 that's ≥2 unexplained losses, and `wouldThinClobber` blocks a ≥2 drop with no NEW `deletedIds` to explain it. (A 2-parcel merge drops only 1, under the threshold — which is why it sometimes "worked".) This is the **same class** as B556's "phantom conflict": a deliberate active-tab shrink with no tombstone read as a stale clobber.
- **Fix:** the merged-away parcels are genuinely removed (replaced by the new parcel), so **tombstone them** — the same invariant every other delete honors (B276/B556). This (1) explains the drop to the guard so no false conflict fires, AND (2) prevents the old parcels being **resurrected** by a reload / cross-tab / cross-device `mergeSiteContent` union (the latent second bug the missing tombstone left). Chose tombstoning over `noteLocalContent` (the B556 undo/redo remedy) precisely because a merge is a real deletion, not a reversible-by-re-add shrink — so the stronger anti-resurrection guarantee is correct here. `pushHistory()` already snapshots the pre-merge `deletedIds`, so **undo cleanly drops the tombstones and restores the parcels**; the new parcel's fresh `uid()` can never collide with a tombstoned id (B594 salting).
- **Tests:** 3 new `test/cloudThinGuard.test.js` cases prove the data-layer math (3→1 with no tombstone = wrongly BLOCKED; with the 3 ids tombstoned = ALLOWED; a 2-parcel merge fine either way). Headless `ui-audit/verify-b596-merge-tombstone.mjs` drives the real UI: seed 3 adjacent parcels → shift-select → **Merge parcels** → the persisted model holds 1 parcel with all 3 old ids in `deletedIds`.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx` (+ tombstone in `mergeParcels`), `test/cloudThinGuard.test.js`, `ui-audit/verify-b596-merge-tombstone.mjs`. Additive — no schema/persistence-format change.
- **Auth-only tail → `VERIFICATION.md` V186:** the conflict path only fires on a signed-in cloud write (the sandbox is logged-out + CORS-blocks the handshake), so the "no false banner on a real cloud merge" confirmation is a signed-in click-through; the logged-out tombstone proof is done here.

Fixed by constraining the drag to one axis + a geometry-derived clamp band; same pure clamp runs at render time so legacy/stale offsets self-correct.
- **Pure module `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/dimSlide.js`** (`dimSlideRange` + `clampDimOffset`, 14 unit tests). `dimSlideRange(el, bumps, posF)` returns the slide axis (the LONG/length axis, matching renderElPx's `horizLong = w>=h`), the perpendicular (depth) axis that is pinned to 0, and the `[min,max]` band the along-offset is clamped to. The band is the footprint length minus each corner bump-out's along-span at its end (`endNeg`/`endPos`) — i.e. the clear middle run where the depth equals the displayed value. `clampDimOffset` drops the perpendicular component to 0 and clamps the slide component.
- **Drag (`startDimMove`/`dimMove`, `SitePlanner.jsx`):** the valid band (fixed geometry) is resolved once at grab time via the new module-level `dimSlideFor(el, allEls)` (which gathers the host's dog-ears through `bumpsAlongLength` → `dogEarSize().along`); each move slides along the length axis only and clamps — so the line tracks the pointer along the building but won't follow it off the shape or onto a bump.
- **Render (`renderElPx`):** the stored offset is run through the same `clampDimOffset(dimSlideFor(...))` for DISPLAY too, so a pre-B592 free-drag offset (off the shape / carrying a depth component) or one stranded by a later resize/bump edit renders back on the footprint; the next drag persists the clamped value. The dashed off-building **leader line was removed** (nothing to bridge once the line always stays on the shape). Applies to buildings (with bump-out exclusion) and, for consistency, to road/paving width callouts (no bump-outs → just the stay-on-the-shape clamp).
- **Reuse, not a parallel pattern:** `footprintDepth`/`horizLong` semantics, `dogEarSize` (B362), and the existing B146 drag flow are reused untouched; only the offset math changed. Additive — no schema/persistence change (`dimOffset` field unchanged, just always clamped now).
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/dimSlide.js`, `test/dimSlide.test.js`, `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx`, `ui-audit/verify-b592-dim-slide.mjs` (+ best-effort gesture harness `ui-audit/verify-b592-drag.mjs`). The real click-drag GESTURE can't be driven headless (the documented canvas-drag automation limit) → live confirm tracked as **VERIFICATION.md V184** (logged-out, no auth needed).

### B590 — Adversarial debug of the Formula engine, round 2 (post-B589): 6 more real defects found + fixed `[Scheduler]` (bug batch)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-30 "keep going" — a second hardening pass after B589; minted **B590** = highest real B# across both files (B589) + 1; branch `claude/scheduling-formula-column-anxv35`, fresh from `main`)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B590 also names another item in this file:** “Column-line spacing on deep cross-docks was uneven (skinny/fat centre bay) (bug) *(owne…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B590* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B590 against all of them.
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 errors · 2070 unit tests green (86 in `test/formula.test.js`, +5 B590 regression cases) · build green · inline-sync guard green · headless E2E `ui-audit/verify-b583-formula-column.mjs` PASS + a live in-page spot-check of all 6 fixes through the synced `window.PlanyrFormula`.** A second 4-lens adversarial fan-out (random-formula fuzzer · B589-regression check · host/UI integration sweep · Excel error-prop + edge semantics), each candidate reproduced against the real engine before fixing. 6 confirmed, all fixed + pinned by tests:
- **HIGH — a non-finite numeric value leaked out as a successful result.** `1e309`, `SUM(1e308,1e308)`, `TRUNC(0,1e16)` etc. returned `{ok:true, Infinity/NaN}` (and `1e309 > 5` a silent `TRUE`) instead of `#NUM!` — the `^`/`POWER`/`+−×÷` guards didn't cover literals, aggregations, or the single-arg maths. **Fix (engine):** reject a non-finite number literal at the tokenizer (so an overflow can't even reach a comparison/label), finite-check every numeric function result at the call boundary (`evalCall`), and backstop the contract in `evaluateFormula`.
- **HIGH — `MROUND` rounded the half toward zero (float drift).** `MROUND(6.05,0.1)` showed `6.0` not `6.1` (6.05/0.1 floats to 60.4999…). **Fix:** `Math.round(n/m + 1e-9)·m` — half-away-from-zero with the same epsilon discipline `ROUNDUP`/`ROUNDDOWN` use.
- **MED-HIGH — `FLOOR`/`CEILING` to a fractional step landed a whole step off.** `FLOOR(2.4,0.1)` showed `2.3` (2.4/0.1 floats to 23.999). **Fix:** ±1e-9 on the quotient (`Math.floor(n/sig+1e-9)`, `Math.ceil(n/sig−1e-9)`).
- **MED — a giant operator chain gave a non-deterministic result.** A multi-thousand-term `a+b+c+…` (iterative parse, recursive eval) overflowed the JS stack or not depending on the ambient call depth — the SAME input could return `#ERROR!` or a value. **Fix:** a `MAX_TOKENS = 1000` cap rejects an over-large formula up front (far above any real formula, far below the overflow boundary), so the verdict is input-determined.
- **MED — `TEXT()` mishandled `;`-separated sections** (accounting formats). `TEXT(-1234.5,"#,##0.00;(#,##0.00)")` gave `-1,234.50000000` (8 decimals + a stray `-`) — the decimal count scanned across the `;` boundary and there was no section selection or literal-text emission. **Fix:** split on top-level `;`, pick the section by sign (positive;negative;zero), count placeholders within the chosen section only, and emit the section's literal text (`(`, `)`, `$`, `%`) in place → `(1,234.50)`. Single-section formats unchanged.
- **LOW-MED — a column named with `[` or `]` was unreferenceable** (`Cost [USD]` → a `[Cost [USD]]` reference tokenizes to the truncated `Cost [USD` + a stray `]` → `#ERROR!`). **Fix (host, `FormulaColumnEditor`):** reject `[`/`]` in a column name with an inline "Name can't contain [ or ]".
- **Confirmed clean / deliberate (no change):** within-formula error propagation is correct (`SUM(1,1/0)`→`#DIV/0!`; `AND`/`OR`/`&`/comparisons propagate; `IFERROR`/`IFNA`/`ISERR` trap correctly); `2^3^2 = 64` is Excel's left-assoc `^`; cross-COLUMN aggregation **skips** an errored cell (stored BLANK) rather than propagating — a deliberate host choice (one bad row shouldn't blank a whole roll-up), flagged for the owner as an optional skip-vs-propagate decision, not changed; renaming a referenced column → `#REF!` is a visible-error v1 limitation (rename-propagation deferred).
- **Files:** `src/shared/formula/formula.js`, `public/sequence/index.html` (synced engine + the editor name-guard), `test/formula.test.js`. Additive — no schema/persistence change. Signed-in scheduler cloud click-through still tracked under `VERIFICATION.md` V178.

### B589 — Adversarial debug of the Formula engine (post-B586): 9 real bugs found + fixed `[Scheduler]` (bug batch)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-30 "now adversarially debug it"; minted **B589** = highest real B# across both files (B588) + 1; branch `claude/scheduling-formula-column-anxv35`, fresh from `main`)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 errors · 2064 unit tests green (80 in `test/formula.test.js`, +8 regression cases) · build green · inline-sync guard green · headless E2E `ui-audit/verify-b583-formula-column.mjs` PASS (now proves the double-count fix on the seed's grouped data: `SUM([Duration])` shows the LEAF total 1217, not the double-counted all-rows 5387).** A 4-lens adversarial fan-out (aggregation/criteria · lookups+range+host · functions+parser · integration/regression), each reviewer reproducing every candidate against the real engine in Node. 9 confirmed, all fixed + pinned by tests:
- **HIGH — whole-column aggregation double-counted summary/parent rows.** In a grouped schedule the flattened row list contains a parent (showing the rolled-up sum of its children) AND its children, so `SUM([Cost])` returned ~2× the real total (and a collapsed group's children were omitted entirely). **Fix (host, `computeFormulaValues` in `public/sequence/index.html`):** aggregation now reads the project's **LEAF tasks of the full tree** (`proj.tasks` leaves), independent of expand/collapse — leaves carry the atomic values; a parent's cell is a pure roll-up. The per-row display still uses each row's own values. `previewFormula` mirrors it.
- **HIGH — date-literal criteria never matched.** `COUNTIF`/`SUMIF`/`AVERAGEIF([Dates], ">=2026-03-01")` returned 0 (and the `<>` form a wrong non-zero count) because `parseCriteriaOperand` didn't parse a date string and the numeric-family gate excluded dates. **Fix:** parse date literals → date values; widen the gate to include dates.
- **MED — `[@Column]` (this-row) was ignored by `COUNTIF`/`SUMIF`/`AVERAGEIF`/`MATCH`/`INDEX`/`XLOOKUP`** (`colArray` didn't check `atRow`), so `SUMIF([@Cost],…)` read the whole column. **Fix:** `colArray` returns a single this-row cell when `atRow`.
- **MED — `WEEKNUM`** silently treated every type other than 2 as Sunday-start (so type 11 Monday-start and 21 ISO were wrong) and never returned `#NUM!` for an invalid type. **Fix:** full type table (1/2/11–17/21) + `#NUM!` on unknown.
- **MED — `[@[Column]]`** (Excel's bracketed-inner structured ref) failed to tokenize (`#ERROR!`); the tokenizer stopped at the first `]`. **Fix:** scan to the `]]` for the `@[…]` form.
- **MED — `MIN`/`MAX` over a date column returned a raw serial number** instead of a date (so `MIN([Start])` showed `46388`). **Fix:** return a date when every contributor is a date.
- **LOW-MED — `MATCH` approximate (type ±1) leaked across type families** — a text lookup matched numeric cells (cross-type rank). **Fix:** restrict the ≤/≥ search to the target's type family.
- **LOW — `YEARFRAC`** returned a negative result when end < start (Excel is always non-negative). **Fix:** drop the sign.
- **LOW (latent) — `colArray`** decided "unknown column" from `rows[0]` only, so a ragged table could read a real column as `#REF!`. **Fix:** existence check across the union of rows.
- **Verified clean (no bug):** the engine↔inline-copy sync, both Babel blocks parse, B585's concurrent F1/F2 engine edits coexist with B586, label↔built-in collisions are editor-blocked, the dependency graph orders aggregate-of-formula-column correctly + flags `SUM([Self])` as `#CIRC!`, performance is acceptable (~171ms at 2000 tasks), and the `%`/lookup/text/info functions hold up. (YEARFRAC basis-1 leap-year denominator left as-is — Excel's exact value is implementation-dependent and basis-1 is rarely used.)
- **Files:** `src/shared/formula/formula.js`, `public/sequence/index.html`, `test/formula.test.js`, `ui-audit/verify-b583-formula-column.mjs`. Additive — no schema/persistence change. Signed-in click-through still tracked under `VERIFICATION.md` V178.

### B586 — Deepen the Formula column to match Excel more: cross-row aggregation, conditional sums/counts, lookups, % operator, +30 functions `[Scheduler]` (enhancement, follow-on to B583)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-30 "deepen the formula tool so it matches excel more"; minted **B586** = highest real B# across both files (B585) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B585 that a concurrent `main` took for the scheduler bug-hunt round 2 below; branch `claude/scheduling-formula-column-anxv35`, fresh from `main` after B583's PR #433 merged)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified this session. lint 0 errors · 2024 unit tests green (70 in `test/formula.test.js`, +14 for the new capability + 1 inline-sync guard) · build green · headless E2E `ui-audit/verify-b583-formula-column.mjs` PASS (now also asserts live `SUM([Cost])=400` + `COUNTIF([Cost],">=100")=2`).** Closes the biggest gaps between the B583 engine and real Excel:
- **Cross-row aggregation over a WHOLE column** (the headline deferred item). A bare `[Column]` inside an aggregator now means the entire column: `SUM([Cost])`, `AVERAGE([Duration])`, `MIN`/`MAX`/`PRODUCT`/`COUNT`/`COUNTA([Column])`. Outside an aggregator a bare `[Column]` is still THIS row (Excel implicit intersection), so `[Cost] / SUM([Cost])` = this row's share of the total. **Conditional**: `COUNTIF`/`SUMIF`/`AVERAGEIF([Column], criteria, [SumColumn])` with operator criteria (`">100"`, `"<>0"`) and `*`/`?` wildcards.
- **Lookups** (column-based, modern set): `XLOOKUP(value, [LookupCol], [ReturnCol], [ifNotFound])`, `INDEX([Column], n)`, `MATCH(value, [Column], [type])`. (VLOOKUP's contiguous multi-column table doesn't fit the per-column model — XLOOKUP/INDEX+MATCH supersede it.)
- **Excel `[@Column]` structured reference** = the current row explicitly (so `SUM([@Cost])` is just this row); plus the **postfix `%` operator** (`25%` → 0.25, `[Budget] * 25%`).
- **+~30 everyday functions**: math `AVERAGE COUNT COUNTA SIGN TRUNC EXP LN LOG LOG10 PI QUOTIENT MROUND EVEN ODD FACT`; logical `XOR IFNA TRUE FALSE NA`; info `ISNUMBER ISTEXT ISLOGICAL ISERROR ISERR ISNA ISEVEN ISODD N`; text `SUBSTITUTE REPLACE FIND SEARCH REPT PROPER TEXTJOIN VALUE EXACT CHAR CODE`; date `NOW WEEKNUM ISOWEEKNUM YEARFRAC DATEVALUE`.
- **Engine mechanics:** range/lookup functions are a new `rng` handler type that reads the whole column from a new `ctx.rows` (all rows) + `ctx.rowIndex`; the host (`computeFormulaValues`) now computes **column-by-column in dependency order across all rows** so an aggregate over ANOTHER formula column sees it filled for every row. `evaluateFormula` defaults `rows` to a single-row view, so the editor preview + a standalone caller still work. The editor's live preview passes the full table too.
- **Bugs caught + fixed during build** (by the new tests): `TRUE()`/`FALSE()` with parens (were bare keywords), `SEARCH` used an anchored full-match regex instead of a substring search, and a blank `""` cell wrongly matched a numeric criterion like `">100"` (string ranks above number) — `COUNTIF`/`SUMIF` now ignore blank/text cells for numeric comparisons (Excel behavior).
- **Still deferred (as before):** VLOOKUP's multi-column table form; formula columns writing back into schedule dates; formula columns in the PDF/Gantt export. All additive — no persistence/schema change (formula defs still ride `proj.formulaCols`).
- **⏳ Signed-in browser check:** folded into `VERIFICATION.md` V178 (same scheduler cloud path; the aggregation/lookups are headless-verified here, only cloud persistence needs a signed-in click-through).
- **Files:** `src/shared/formula/formula.js`, `test/formula.test.js`, `public/sequence/index.html`, `ui-audit/verify-b583-formula-column.mjs`.

### B583 — Excel-style Formula column in the scheduling grid `[Scheduler]` (feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-29 — "create a column that is a formula column that basically functions like Excel where you can do math… copy the most-used Excel functions… what would work for ~90% of people"; provisional "NEW-1"; minted **B583** = highest real B# across both files (B582) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B562 that collided with main's grid-keyboard-nav B562 plus the B564–B582 burst of concurrent mains landed while this branch was open; branch `claude/scheduling-formula-column-anxv35`)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified this session. lint 0 errors · 1850 unit tests green (56 in `test/formula.test.js` + 1 inline-sync guard) · build green · headless E2E `ui-audit/verify-b562-formula-column.mjs` PASS (add column → per-row compute → `#DIV/0!`/`#REF!` surfaced) · a 6-lens adversarial-review Workflow ran and all 6 confirmed bugs were fixed before shipping.** A user can now add a **Formula** column to a project's schedule grid (Columns chooser → "+ Formula column", or right-click a column header → "Add formula column…"), type an Excel-like expression, and it computes a value **per task row** from that row's other columns.
- **Per-row calculated column, structured references (not A1).** One formula evaluates for every row, referencing columns by name — `[Finish] - [Start]`, `IF([% Complete]>=100,"Done", NETWORKDAYS([Start],[Finish]) & " wd")`. Schedule rows are activities that reorder/insert/delete constantly, so absolute cell addresses (A1) would break; column-name refs survive.
- **Engine = a dependency-free pure lib** `src/shared/formula/formula.js` (tokenizer → precedence-climbing parser → tree-walk evaluator; **no `eval`/`new Function`**). The ~90% function set: math `SUM PRODUCT MIN MAX ABS ROUND ROUNDUP ROUNDDOWN INT MOD CEILING FLOOR POWER SQRT`; logical `IF IFS AND OR NOT SWITCH IFERROR ISBLANK`; date `TODAY DATE YEAR MONTH DAY WEEKDAY EDATE EOMONTH DATEDIF DAYS WORKDAY NETWORKDAYS`; text `CONCAT TEXT LEFT RIGHT MID LEN TRIM UPPER LOWER`; operators `+ − * / ^ &`, comparisons, parentheses. Built generic for Cost Estimating reuse later; wired into Schedule first.
- **Dates honor the project working-day calendar.** `WORKDAY`/`NETWORKDAYS` use the SAME weekends + `HOLIDAY_SET` the schedule cascade uses (injected calendar adapter) — not Excel's naive Mon–Fri — so a formula's working-day count agrees with the duration model. Typed inputs documented: Start/Finish = date, Duration = working days (number), % Complete = **0–100**; `date − date → days`, `date + n → date`.
- **Read-only / no feedback loop.** Formula columns are derived display columns (`e:false`) computed in a memo AFTER `cascadeDates`/`rollupParentDates` settle, so they read final dates and can never drive task dates/durations (no circular dependency with the scheduling engine). Inter-formula deps are topologically ordered (`planFormulaColumns`); a reference cycle surfaces **`#CIRC!`**.
- **Errors are visible, never a silent blank** — `#REF!` (bad column), `#DIV/0!`, `#VALUE!`, `#NAME?`, `#NUM!`, `#N/A`, `#CIRC!` render red in the cell with a tooltip.
- **Inline editor (no dialog-box edits — owner rule)** — `FormulaColumnEditor`: a name field + a formula box with **autocomplete** for `[Column]` and `FUNCTION()` names + a **live preview** evaluated against the selected row; validates the name (required/unique/not a built-in name) and the formula (parse error shown live). Edit/delete via the chooser ✎/🗑 or the header context menu.
- **Persistence** — formula defs live on `proj.formulaCols` (additive, rides the existing scheduler cloud-save), visibility/width via the existing `colConfig`. A shared effective column registry (`effectiveColsOf`) merges built-ins + formula cols so `selectedColIdx`/copy/format/keyboard-nav resolve consistently App-wide.
- **Standalone-scheduler delivery:** the scheduler is a self-contained in-browser-Babel HTML file (`public/sequence/index.html`), so the engine is inlined VERBATIM by `scripts/sync-sequence-formula.mjs`; `test/formula-inline-sync.test.js` fails CI on any drift between source and the inlined copy.
- **Adversarial-review Workflow (engine-semantics / parser-security / dates / integration, each finding independently re-verified) found + I fixed 6 real bugs before shipping:** (1) float-noise display (`9999999.99 & ""` → clean, not `9999999.9900000002`); (2) non-finite `+ − * /` now `#NUM!` (was a silent `Infinity`/`NaN` that produced a WRONG TRUE/FALSE in comparisons); (3) `DATEDIF "YD"` across year boundaries (was huge/negative); (4) `TEXT` integer leading-zeros (`"00"`→`"07"`); (5) a parser depth guard + a never-throw-to-host contract (deep nesting returns an error cell instead of a `RangeError` that could blank the grid); (6) a hidden formula column that couldn't be re-shown (`showCol` used the built-ins-only registry). Plus 2 low (CEILING/FLOOR sign mismatch → `#NUM!`, `DATEDIF "MD"` non-negative). All pinned by new tests.
- **Deferred to a follow-up (NOT built, as scoped):** cross-row aggregation (column-wide SUM/COUNT/COUNTIF/SUMIF/AVERAGE), lookups (VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP), and formula columns writing back into dates. Formula columns also don't yet appear in the PDF/Gantt exports or the cross-project MasterView (grid-only in v1).
- **⏳ One browser check pending (`VERIFICATION.md` V173):** the sandbox proxy blocks the scheduler's CDN (React/Babel) AND its own Supabase, so the live cloud-connected scheduler can't be driven here — E2E was verified against a locally-vendored copy of those libs + the seed schedule. Signed-in confirm on planyr.io: add a formula column, reload, confirm it persists via the scheduler's backend.
- **Files:** `src/shared/formula/formula.js`, `test/formula.test.js`, `test/formula-inline-sync.test.js`, `scripts/sync-sequence-formula.mjs`, `public/sequence/index.html`, `ui-audit/verify-b583-formula-column.mjs`.

### B580 — Print/PDF export: north arrow + scale bar oversized and colliding with plan content `[Site Planner / export]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-29 — "the north cardinal direction ends up being massive, same with the scale, way too big… should be proportional to the page"; minted **B580** = highest real B# across both files (B579) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B564 that concurrent mains took (B564–B579 all landed while this branch was open); AMENDS the B144/B145/B196/B219 furniture lineage rather than a parallel path; branch `claude/drawing-export-quality-6dl678`)*
`[x]` **DONE + headless-verified the same session. lint 0 errors · 1808 tests green · build green · `ui-audit/verify-export-quality.mjs` 10/10 (real app → File ▾ → Download PDF → measured the actual composed sheet).** Root cause was NOT a regression or stale deploy: the export furniture is sized off `refS = min(frame w,h)` and then the whole plan clone is rescaled into the centi-inch plan box, so the arrow GLYPH was fine (~0.39 in) but the surrounding PLATE (generous padding + a big "N" + heavy type) ballooned to **~0.74–0.9 in** on paper (the "massive" read) — and it was pinned to the plan-FRAME corners (top-left / bottom-right), i.e. INSIDE the drawing, so the scale-bar plate routinely landed on a building + its dimension labels.

  2. **No-occlude placement** (new pure `chooseFurnitureCorners` + `furnitureLayout({obstacles})`): the export passes the development's content boxes (buildings/pond/parking/road, padded for dim labels) and each plate is placed in the emptiest corner, in DIFFERENT corners. Measured furniture↔building overlap = **0**.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/sheetFurniture.js`, `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx` (`buildExportSvg` computes obstacles + tags the furniture group `data-furniture`), `test/sheetFurniture.test.js` (+4 no-occlude/compact-plate tests), `ui-audit/verify-export-quality.mjs`. ### B581 — Print/PDF export: plan line work bakes in too thick (cartoonish) `[Site Planner / export]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-29 — "the line work is all sorts of fucked up, way too thick… makes it look unprofessional"; minted **B581** = highest real B# across both files (B580) + 1; branch `claude/drawing-export-quality-6dl678`)*
`[x]` **DONE + headless-verified the same session (`verify-export-quality.mjs`: building object line = 0.60 pt on paper, thinned from authored 2 px).** Root cause: element strokes are authored in SCREEN pixels for the live canvas (building/parcel/pond weight 2, surfaces 1.25, parking/dock striping 0.5–0.75). When the plan SVG is cloned and nested into the sheet, those pixel weights are scaled by the sheet's "meet" fit transform — a factor that DEPENDS on the zoom the user was at when they hit print — so line work baked in heavy and inconsistent.
- **Fix:** a pure `lib/exportStyle.js` (`printStrokeWidth` + `sheetFitScale`) retargets every stroke to a real PHYSICAL drafting weight (object line → **0.6 pt**, hierarchy preserved, floored at 0.32 pt so striping never disappears, capped at 1.5 pt), **independent of zoom**. Applied at export by `restyleExportClone` (walks the clone, skips the `data-furniture` group, scales stroke-width + inline-style stroke + dasharray). Both PDF and PNG use it (PNG against a notional letter-landscape sheet so it matches the PDF). 9 unit tests in `test/exportStyle.test.js` (zoom-independence, hierarchy, floor, cap).
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/exportStyle.js` (new), `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx` (`restyleExportClone`, wired into `exportPDF`/`exportPNG`), `test/exportStyle.test.js`.

### B579 — Document Review robustness batch: stuck detail-popup capture · failed-delete mirror desync · silent PDF-store failure `[Document Review]` (3 bugs)  *(self-found 2026-06-29 by the improve loop's lap-7 hunt; minted **B579** = highest real B# across both files (B578) + 1)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified the same session. lint 0 · 1874 tests (+3 anti-drift) · build green.** Three distinct, hand-verified defects from one lap (the hunt's other lens, GIS/layer plumbing, came back clean):
- **Detail popup kept pointer capture on an interrupt (`Stitcher.jsx`).** The Bluebeam-style detail "cloud" popup set pointer capture on `onPointerDown` and released it on `onPointerUp`, but `onPointerCancel` only cleared the drag state — so a browser interrupt (blur / tab-hide / OS gesture) mid-pan left the popup holding capture, swallowing every click/drag/wheel with a stuck grab cursor until it was closed and reopened. Same class as B551 on the main canvas; fixed by releasing capture in `onPointerCancel` too.
- **A failed review delete desynced the local mirror (`reviewStore.js`).** `clearDraft` ran *before* the cloud `delete`, so a delete that errored (network/auth) left the cloud row alive but the local resume-mirror cleared — the review lingered in the library yet could no longer auto-resume. Now the mirror is cleared **only on a successful delete**, keeping a failed delete in a consistent, retry-able state.
- **A genuine PDF-store failure was silent (`DocReview.jsx`).** When BOTH backends (Drive *and* the Supabase fallback) rejected a dropped PDF — not merely `oversize`, which still saves the work layer and flags "re-drop on load" — the source stayed permanently keyless, so `buildSnapshot` persisted `sources:[]` and the markups reloaded with **no backdrop**, with no warning. The drop path now surfaces an error banner on a real failure, **gated on `cloudReady()`** so logged-out local-only mode (bytes cached, work mirrored locally) stays quiet.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/doc-review/Stitcher.jsx`, `src/workspaces/doc-review/lib/reviewStore.js`, `src/workspaces/doc-review/DocReview.jsx`, `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` (3 anti-drift guards). All three are signed-in / interaction paths the sandbox can't fully drive headless → **VERIFICATION.md V177**.

### B94 — Road / right-of-way maintenance authority — now PER-ROAD (name + authority + route) `[Site Planner / GIS]` (feature)  *(core shipped 2026-06-15; PER-ROAD amendment closed 2026-06-29 per the owner "there are usually multiple roads… the card should become a per-road list", folding this chat's earlier provisional "NEW-1"; branch `claude/multi-road-authority-card-1kqrj1`)*
`[x]` **Closed this session by the per-road amendment. lint 0 · 1805 tests green · build green · headless `ui-audit/verify-road-authority.mjs` PASS.** The frontage path already returned every distinct fronting *authority* (the multi-desk case — a lot fronting a state highway AND a city street already reported both); the remaining gap was **presentation/granularity** — the card collapsed it to one `authorities.join(" · ")` value. Fixed to a true per-road list:

### B569 — Render metes-and-bounds curves as their TRUE arc, not a straight chord `[Site Planner]` (feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-29 — "do whatever is truly accurate"; minted **B569** = highest real B# (B568) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B566 that collided with main’s B566; branch `claude/deed-title-tool-rail-ldvtxe`)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B569 also names another item in this file:** “Snap dock doors so a column never lands on an opening (feature) *(owner-dropped 2026-06…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B569* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B569 against all of them.
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1822 tests (+4) · build green · headless (plotted boundary = 55 vertices, visible arcs).** A curve course used to plot as the straight long-chord between its endpoints; now it's reconstructed as the real circular arc.
- **`arcChordPoints(p0, p1, meta)`** (new export in `lib/metesAndBounds.js`): from the curve's stated radius / central angle / turn (already parsed into `curveMeta`), rebuilds the circle and walks the minor arc from start to chord-end, tessellating ~1 point per 4° (8–48 pts). Derives R from chord+Δ when radius is absent; falls back to the straight chord when there's no usable radius/angle or the geometry is degenerate (chord > 2R). Frame-correct: +x east, +y south; `turn:"R"` puts the centre on the traveller's right.
- **`callsToPath` emits the arc points** for a curve course (ending exactly at the chord endpoint, so the next course continues unchanged) — so `buildEncumbranceMarkup`, the easement strip, the modal preview, and the plotted polygon ALL follow the true curve. Closure/misclosure are unaffected (endpoints unchanged). Fixed a latent bug: the save-and-except tie POB was read by `callsToPath(tie)[tie.length]`, which breaks once a call emits many points — now takes the last path point.
- **Honest UI:** the modal warning changed from "plotted as straight chords" to "reconstructed as true arcs" (and flags any curve with no stated radius/angle that still falls back to a chord); the call list marks each curve "⤾ (arc)" vs "⤿ (chord)".
- **Tests:** 4 geometry tests (a 90° curve bulges off the chord by the sagitta on the correct side for R/L; ends at the chord endpoint; chord fallback). Verified across all 5 real deeds (each 5–6 curves; e.g. the 94.91 boundary tessellates 15 courses → 55 path points) with 0 oracle mismatches (course bearings/distances unchanged).

`[x]` **DONE + verified the same session. lint 0 · 1830 tests · build green · scheduler JSX transpile OK (`ui-audit/jsxcheck-sequence.mjs`).** `renumberTasks` built its old-id→new-id remap with `tasks.forEach((t,i) => { map[t.id] = i+1; })` — **last occurrence wins**.
- **Why it bites:** if a project's persisted tasks carry a **duplicate id** (the app once minted dup ids before `addTask` switched to `maxId+1`, and `normalizeIds` does NOT dedup before the remap — its B550 cycle-break uses a `byId` map but passes the full task array on to `renumberTasks(sortByVisualOrder(tasks))`), the second occurrence overwrote `map[id]`. A parent/predecessor reference to that id then remapped to the **stray copy lower in visual order** instead of the original task — silently corrupting the dependency graph on load (wrong cascade dates, dependencies pointing at the wrong task, no warning). The in-code comment at `addTask` already flagged this as a known risk ("a duplicate id poisons renumberTasks' remap table, scrambling parent links").
- **Fix:** `if (!(t.id in map)) map[t.id] = i + 1;` — **first occurrence wins**, so a reference resolves to the original task in visual order. **No change for clean unique-id data** (every other caller already passes unique ids). Applied to BOTH the live source (`public/sequence/index.html`) and its verbatim test mirror (`ui-audit/stress/scheduler-engine.mjs`).
- **Tests:** 2 behavioral (dup-id predecessor remaps to the first occurrence; clean data unaffected) + 1 anti-drift guard asserting the first-occurrence form exists in source AND mirror. `test/schedulerEngine.test.js`.
- **Files:** `public/sequence/index.html`, `ui-audit/stress/scheduler-engine.mjs`, `test/schedulerEngine.test.js`. The scheduler can't boot headless (its own Supabase backend is unreachable in-sandbox), so the live signed-in confirmation that a real schedule's dependencies survive load is **VERIFICATION.md V175**.

### B567 — Color pickers don't apply live; the color only updates after the picker closes `[Site Planner + Document Review / markup]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-29, arrived as "NEW-3"; minted **B567** = highest real B# across both files (B565) + 1 — renumbered twice from a provisional B562 then B565 as concurrent `main`s took those IDs; branch `claude/markup-hit-area-color-picker-kfm284`)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · tests green · build green · headless ALL-PASS (`ui-audit/verify-markup-fixes.mjs`).** Repro: select any object → open its color control → click a swatch — the object did NOT recolor until you dismissed the picker. **Root cause:** every color control is a native `<input type="color">` wired to `onChange`, which in Chromium fires **only when the OS palette closes**; the live event while you click/drag swatches is `input`. So the canvas couldn't reflect the color until dismissal.
- **Fix — wire the live `input` event, with single-step undo:**
  - **Site Planner** (`SitePlanner.jsx`): a `livePick(apply)` helper spreads `onFocus`/`onInput`/`onChange` onto each of the **12** native color inputs (markup line/fill, callout text/fill/line, element fill/stroke, parcel fill, pond existing/added fill, the two "Element default colors"). `onInput` commits the color **live**. Undo stays one-step: exactly ONE history frame is pushed per picking **session** — lazily on the first change, reset on focus, via `pickSnapRef` (survives re-renders; only one input is active at a time) — so the live mutators (`liveMarkup`/`liveCallout`/`liveTypeStyle`/`setDetLive`, plus the already-history-free `setSelEl`/`setSelParcel`) must NOT push their own. The old inline `pushHistory()` in the element/parcel color handlers moved into `livePick`.
  - **Document Review** (`PropertyPanel.jsx` `ColorControl` → `DocReview.jsx` `onPropChange`): the shared control now fires `onInput` (flagged `{live:true}`) for the live recolor and `onChange` (`{live:false}`) for the commit; the host coalesces a live burst into one undo frame keyed on the property (`colorSessionRef`).
- **WYSIWYG follow-through (the half that would otherwise hide the fix):** a SELECTED neutral markup in the Site Planner used to repaint its stroke with the accent tint (`isSel ? PAL.accent : m.stroke`), which **masked** a live stroke-color change. Selected neutral markups (line/polyline/polygon/rect/ellipse) now render their **real** color (`nStroke`), cued by the existing grips + a faint width bump (`nsw = sw + 1`) — matching the shared `MarkupRenderer`'s deliberate choice. Semantic markups (encumbrance etc.) keep the accent tint. Verified headless: the selected line recolors to the picked color on `input` (before any close) and a single ⌘/Ctrl-Z reverts it.
- **Left alone:** the ParcelDrawing swatch ROW already applies on click (fixed palette, not the native picker); range sliders already fire live. Guards in `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js`. All logged-out-verifiable — no auth/cloud surface, no V### pending.

### B564 — Drop a deed (.docx) into the Deed/Title reader → read & plot its metes-and-bounds boundary `[Site Planner]` (feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-29 with 5 real sample deeds, "make it so it can read these by me just dropping in the files"; minted **B564** = highest real B# (B563) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B562 that collided with main’s importLegacy B562; branch `claude/deed-title-tool-rail-ldvtxe`)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1781 tests (+26) · build green · headless 8/8 (real .docx drop→plot, 0 page errors).** Follow-on to B543 (the rail launcher): the metes-and-bounds plotter only accepted pasted text and its parser only read tidy "N 45 E, 150 ft" calls — it could read NONE of the owner's real surveys. "Plot on canvas" draws the boundary as a polygon (gap on the last edge when it doesn't close — never silently a corridor) plus each save-and-except tract as a dashed-red hole positioned from its commencing tie off the same POB.

### B563 — Version restore was a partial restore: it never re-applied `parcelDrawings` `[Site Planner / version history]` (bug — restore correctness)  *(self-found 2026-06-29 by the improve loop's lap-4 hunt; minted **B563** = highest real B# across both files (B562) + 1)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified the same session. lint 0 · tests green · build green.** `restoreVersion` explicitly re-applied 8 collections (parcels, els, measures, callouts, markups, underlay, sheetOverlays, deletedIds) but **silently skipped `parcelDrawings`** — the per-parcel attached drawings (PDF/image markups).
- **Why it bites:** `parcelDrawings` rides its OWN persistence path (`persistDrawings` → a `saveSite` merge), deliberately kept off the main autosave snapshot. The stored version DOES capture it (`sigOf` + `snapshotVersion` save the full `createSiteModel`), so a restore should bring it back — but the restore only touched the main-path setters. Result: after restoring an older version, every other collection reverted while `parcelDrawings` stayed at the CURRENT value — a **mixed-version canvas**. Worse, the very next line `noteLocalContent(siteId, v)` recorded the restored version `v`'s drawings as the conflict baseline, so **live state ≠ recorded baseline**, which could mis-fire the cross-session "newer version elsewhere" guard on the next push.
- **Distinct from undo/redo:** the undo/redo snapshot intentionally excludes `parcelDrawings` (geometry-only undo). A full version RESTORE is a different operation — the user expects the entire saved state back.
- **Fix:** restore + durably persist the version's drawings via `persistDrawings(v.parcelDrawings || [])` (sets state AND saves AND debounces the cloud push — a bare `setParcelDrawings` would update the display but not persist, reverting on reload). Anti-drift guard in `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` (B563).
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx`, `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js`. The live signed-in confirmation (attach a drawing → save a version → change drawings → Restore the earlier version → the old drawing set returns and survives reload; cloud version history is unreachable headless) is **VERIFICATION.md V173**.

### B562 — `importLegacyIntoCloud` timestamp compare wasn't type-safe (third sibling of B559) `[Site Planner / cloud sync]` (bug — data loss)  *(self-found 2026-06-29 by the improve loop's lap-4 hunt; minted **B562** = highest real B# across both files (B561) + 1)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B562 also names another item in this file:** “Grid keyboard column nav steps onto hidden columns; cell selection outline disappears (…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B562* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B562 against all of them.
`[x]` **DONE + verified the same session. lint 0 · tests green · build green.** B559 made the newer-wins timestamp comparison type-safe with `toMs()` at two sites (the `mergeNewer` in `siteModel.js` and `pruneMigratedLegacy` in `storage.js`) but **missed a third sibling**: `importLegacyIntoCloud` (the login-time copy of on-device sites into the cloud) still used the raw `(existing.updatedAt || 0) >= (local.updatedAt || 0)`.
- **Why it bites:** `createSiteModel` keeps whatever `updatedAt` it's handed (`p.updatedAt || Date.now()`), so a legacy/imported record can carry an **ISO string** while the cloud cache holds a **number**. `number >= "2025-…"` coerces the string to `NaN`, and `anything >= NaN` is always `false` → the "cloud already newer, skip" guard silently fails → an **older** local copy can be pushed over a **newer** cloud copy (cross-device work loss) on the one-time legacy import.
- **Fix:** one line — `toMs(existing.updatedAt) >= toMs(local.updatedAt)`, mirroring the B559 fixes. `toMs` was already imported. Anti-drift guard added in `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` (B562).
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/storage.js`, `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js`.

### B561 — Site→Schedule switch is buggy: flashing, placeholder name, raw id, false "newer version" banner `[Cross-module / Schedule]` (bug — regression in B493)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-29 — "switching from the Pappadoupolos site plan into the schedule is super buggy… flashing between the name and 'pick a site'… it gave the project a random name that was just letters and numbers… and it says a newer version was saved on another device which isn't true"; minted **B561** = highest real B# across both files (B560) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B560 a concurrent `main` (header-selector consolidation) took)*
`[x]` **DONE + headless-verified the same session. lint 0 errors · 1793 tests green · build green · `ui-audit/verify-cross-module-link.mjs` 11/11 (4 new anti-regression checks).** Four symptoms, ONE root cause in the B493 cross-module wiring (`src/workspaces/scheduler/Scheduler.jsx`):
- **Flashing (whole screen + top-left name) = a two-effect feedback loop.** The *carry-in* effect (route→iframe: `planar:nav-select-by-site`) and the *sync* effect (iframe→route: `onProjectChange(linkedSiteId)`) fought each other: arriving on site A while the iframe's last-active schedule was linked to a different site B made the sync effect rewrite the route to B, which re-fired the carry-in toward A, which re-fired the sync toward B… every `onProjectChange` → `navigate()` → hashchange re-rendered the whole workspace → flash. **Fix:** the sync effect now only adopts the iframe's active link into an **empty** route (`projectId == null`) — provably loop-free (once set, it's inert; it never overrides a routed project). A user switching schedules in the breadcrumb still carries up, via a one-shot `selectSchedule()` (wired to `onSelectProject`), not a reactive effect.
- **Placeholder "Select a project" for ~2 s = no last-known-good.** The breadcrumb read only the iframe's nav-state (empty until the iframe boots). **Fix:** when the route carries a project, the crumb shows the schedule linked to it OR the routed project's real name as last-known-good — never the iframe's transient active schedule (which may belong to a different project mid-carry-in).
- **Random letters/numbers as the name = the raw `group_id` leaking.** `routedSiteName` fell back to the raw `projectId` when the site list wasn't warm, and that string was shown AND posted as the created schedule's `name`. **Fix:** the name resolves to a real name only (no id fallback); the resolution panel + its Create action are gated on a resolved name, so a schedule can never be shown/created named a group_id (`LinkSchedulePanel` also disables Create defensively).
- **False "a newer version was saved on another device" = a self-conflicting save burst.** The oscillation/redundant carry-in fired a burst of `setData` in the embedded app → overlapping auto-saves → the scheduler's optimistic-save guard (`cloudRev > knownRev`) tripped against the tab's OWN in-flight write. **Fix:** the `planar:nav-select-by-site` handler (`public/sequence/index.html`) no-ops when that schedule is already active — no needless `setData`/save — and killing the oscillation removes the burst.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/scheduler/Scheduler.jsx`, `src/workspaces/scheduler/components/LinkSchedulePanel.jsx`, `public/sequence/index.html`. Verified headless: anti-oscillation (route stays on A, no flip to B), breadcrumb shows the routed name (no placeholder/id), no raw-id ever rendered or postable as a name, and the user push-up (picking a B-linked schedule routes to B) all pass. The live signed-in confirmation (no flash + no false "newer version" banner against the scheduler's own backend, unreachable headless) is **VERIFICATION.md V172**.

### B576 — Scale control: dead "custom…" rebuilt as Bluebeam-style page-distance = real-distance entry `[Site Planner]` (bug + feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-29 as "NEW-3"; minted **B576** — renumbered B562→B566→B574→B576 as concurrent mains kept taking the id)*
`[x]` **DONE + headless-verified. lint 0 · 1808 tests (+18 unit) · build green.** The old scale `<select>` skipped its own `custom` value and only revealed the custom input when the overlay *already* sat at a non-preset size — so picking "custom…" did nothing. It was also a feet-per-inch model with the page side hardcoded to 1″, so only `1″=X′` scales were expressible. **Rebuilt to Bluebeam Revu parity:** a preset dropdown (Engineering `1″=10/20/30/40/50/60/80/100′` + Architectural `1/8″ … 1″=1′-0″`, grouped) where picking a preset populates page=1 + real=preset and **Custom…** reveals editable paired fields **`[page][unit ▾] = [real][unit ▾]`** (page in/ft, real ft/in/m; page side accepts decimals AND fractions — `0.5` or `1/2`). The page→real ratio is the single source of truth: `feetPerInch = realFt / pageIn` feeds the **untouched** `applyOverlayScale`/`ftPerPx` model, so `0.5″=60′ → 1″=120′` is now expressible (was impossible). The custom/preset distinction is driven off **explicit editor state** (`ovEdit`), not the overlay's current size, so Custom always reveals the fields; the dropdown **round-trips** to the matching preset when the size lands on one, else shows Custom with the fields populated. Resolved scale still drives EPSG:2278 sizing and survives reload (only `ftPerPx` changes). **Extended `lib/overlayScale.js`** (not forked): pure `parseDistanceInput` (decimals/fractions/mixed), `feetPerInchFromPair`, `SCALE_PRESETS` + `feetPerInchForPreset`, `matchScalePreset`; **+18 unit tests** (`test/overlayScale.test.js`, 30 total green). Headless: round-trips to eng-30; `1/4″=1′` → `1″=4′`; Custom `0.5″=60′` and `1/2″=60′` both → `1″=120′ · 4320′ wide`. **Review-driven precision guard:** the custom fields default-DISPLAY a rounded value but COMMIT full-precision defaults, and the page/real inputs carry **per-field dirty flags** so an idle focus→blur of an un-edited field never re-commits the rounded display string (which would have quantized e.g. a metric `1″=1m`/3.2808 to 3.3). Headless: idle focus+blur leaves the scale exactly put.

### B559 — Timestamp comparisons assumed a number → a string `updatedAt` silently picks the OLDER copy (merge + legacy-prune) `[Site Planner / persistence]` (bug — latent data-loss) — MED  *(bug-hunt round 14, 2026-06-27; fixed same lap; renumbered from a provisional B558 a concurrent main took for the take-over-editing fix below)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1789 tests · build green.** `mergeSiteContent` (siteModel.js newer-wins) and `pruneMigratedLegacy` (storage.js) compared `updatedAt` with `>=` assuming a ms number — but `createSiteModel` keeps whatever it's given (`p.updatedAt || Date.now()`), so an imported/legacy record can carry an ISO **string**, and `"2025-…" >= 1718…` is a silent **false**. In the merge that would pick the OLDER copy as "newer" (scalar/meta from the stale side; union still keeps drawn work, but the wrong meta + a wrong prune could strand/drop a newer edit). **Fix:** a shared exported `toMs(v)` coercion (string→`Date.parse`, number→itself, else 0) applied at both comparison sites. Unit tests (`test/siteModel.test.js`: toMs + a newer-ISO-vs-older-number merge) + anti-drift guard. Latent (updatedAt is ~always a number in practice) but the consequence is data-loss, so worth the cheap guard. **This lap's hunt was mostly false positives (7 of 9 rejected on re-read) — this is the one genuine find.**

### B558 — Phantom "changed in another session / Take over editing" re-prompt after a delete (no real 2nd tab) `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug)  *(owner-found 2026-06-29 on planyr.io: "I click take over editing and a second later it still offers it… I'm not even sure another tab has it open"; the decisive clue — "if I MOVE a building it doesn't pop back up, but if I DELETE one it does"; minted **B558** = highest real B# across both files (B557) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B556 two concurrent mains took (B556 mobile properties-panel, B557 round-13 batch); branch `claude/take-over-editing-reprompt-fxteik`)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1786 tests (8 new) · build green · headless 6/6 (`ui-audit/verify-delete-tombstone.mjs`).**
- **Root cause (ONE bug, not two — explains BOTH the re-prompt AND the "no other tab" phantom):** the banner re-appearing is the **blue cloud-CONFLICT banner** (`cloudConflict`, "changed in another session"), driven by the **B459 thin-clobber guard** (`wouldThinClobber` in `cloudSync.js`) — NOT the amber Web-Locks read-only banner. That guard blocks a push that drops **≥2 items the cloud still has with no delete-tombstone to explain the drop**, treating it as a stale-tab clobber. The bug: **`deleteSel` removed the building AND all its bonded children (dog-ears / sidewalks / parking, `attachedTo`) from `els` but recorded NO tombstone** — only `removeOverlay` (B276) ever tombstoned. So deleting one building dropped ≥2 items unexplained → the guard FALSELY rejected the save as a cross-session conflict, with **no second session anywhere**. A **MOVE** keeps the item count (`lost = 0`), so it never tripped — exactly the owner's move-vs-delete tell. Secondary latent bug from the same gap: "Take over editing" union-merges the cloud copy back, **resurrecting the just-deleted building** (the never-ending loop).
- **The whole CLASS, not just building-delete (owner asked "what else causes this?"):** any DELIBERATE local op that shrinks the plan by ≥2 vs the last-synced baseline with no tombstone. Found + fixed all of them:
  - **Deletes** (building+assembly, multi-select, parcel, callout, markup, parcel-drawing, stranded-zone auto-prune on reshape) → now **tombstone** the removed ids (mirrors `removeOverlay`/B276). New shared `tombstone(ids)` helper in `SitePlanner.jsx`; wired into `deleteSel` (both branches), `deleteDrawing`, and the strand-prune. This both clears the false conflict AND makes deletions stick through `mergeSiteContent` (no resurrection).
  - **Undo of a multi-element add** (drawing a building adds building+parking+sidewalk in ONE undo frame → one Ctrl-Z drops ≥2), **Redo**, **cancelled drag**, and **Restore to a thinner version** → tombstones are wrong here (a redo must re-add the items), so instead the active tab rebases its own thin-clobber baseline via new **`noteLocalContent(id, model)`** (`cloudSync.js`, re-exported through `storage.js`), called from `applySnapshot` (undo/redo/cancel) and the version-restore handler.
- **Why the 8 South stale-clobber protection (the whole point of B459) is untouched:** `noteLocalContent` only ADJUSTS an existing baseline and is called ONLY on an explicit user undo/redo/restore — a passive STALE background tab never does those, so its baseline stays at the cloud's fuller count and its thin push still BLOCKS. The cross-session CAS **version** guard (B314) also still rejects a genuine concurrent change. Proved by a dedicated unit test.
- **NOT triggers (verified):** move / resize / rotate / group / add / split-parcel / vertex-delete / cross-tab+takeover merges (all union-up or count-neutral).
- **Files:** `SitePlanner.jsx` (`tombstone` helper + `deleteSel`/`deleteDrawing`/strand-prune tombstoning; `noteLocalContent` in `applySnapshot` + restore), `lib/cloudSync.js` (`noteLocalContent`), `lib/storage.js` (re-export). Tests: `test/cloudThinGuard.test.js` (+4 — undo rebase, restore rebase, never-fabricate-baseline, 8-South-still-blocks) + the headless harness.
- **PR #418 → main.** Live signed-in confirmation (the conflict banner itself only renders when cloud-active) owed as **V171**.

### B555 — Planner two-finger pinch is "super buggy" on mobile Safari `[Site Planner / mobile]` (bug)  *(owner-found 2026-06-28 once actually planning a parcel on mobile Safari; minted **B555** = highest real B# across both files (B554) + 1; branch `claude/mobile-safari-pinch-menu-3gon8x`)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1782 tests · build green · headless 3/3.** The Site Planner's pinch-zoom ran on **pointer** events. iOS Safari's multi-touch pointer-event support is unreliable — it routinely fires a spurious `pointercancel` on the first finger the instant a second touches, which tore down the pinch mid-gesture and let a one-finger pan fight it (the "super buggy" feel: jumpy, dropping out, sticking). Rewrote the gesture on **native touch events** (`onTouchStart/Move/End/Cancel` on the canvas `<svg>`):
  - `e.touches` always carries every active finger each frame, so the gesture never "loses" a finger the way pointer events did on iOS.
  - View updates are throttled to **one per `requestAnimationFrame`** so a heavy plan doesn't re-render on every raw `touchmove` (the other half of the jank).
  - On the 2nd finger landing, any one-finger pan that just started is torn down **and the view restored** to its pre-pan offset, so the pinch can't jump in.
  - While ≥2 fingers are down (`touchCountRef`), the pointer-driven pan/draw/vertex-edit handlers all bail, so nothing competes with the pinch. Single-finger pan/draw are untouched (the guard is false for one finger).
  - The canvas already sets `touch-action: none`, so the browser's own pinch-zoom is suppressed and the (passive) React touch handlers need no `preventDefault`. Blur/visibility recovery (`abortGesture`) also clears the new pinch state + cancels any pending frame. The old pointer-pinch refs (`pinchRef` etc.) are left vestigial only where `abortGesture` still clears them.
  - Reuses the shared `pinchZoom`/`midpoint`/`distance` engine (`shared/viewport/viewportTransform.js`) — the math was already correct; only the event source changed.
- **Verify:** `ui-audit/verify-planner-pinch.mjs` (CDP multi-touch, 390×844) 3/3 — pinch-out zooms in, pinch-in within the same gesture zooms back out, a second pinch still works (not stuck). The actual iOS flakiness only reproduces on a real device (headless Chromium's pointer multi-touch is well-behaved) → real-device confirm owed as **V169**.

Desktop layout is byte-for-byte unchanged (every phone style is `narrow ?`-gated).
