### B550 — Scheduler: a parentId cycle in loaded data could hang the tab (recursive tree-walks) `[Scheduler / robustness]` (bug — hardening)  *(filed round 10; fixed round 11, 2026-06-27)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1782 tests · JSX parse OK · build green.** `public/sequence/index.html` has many recursive parent→child tree-walks. **Sharpened analysis vs the original filing:** `sortByVisualOrder`'s `walk(null)` actually CANNOT loop on a cycle — a cyclic node's parent chain never reaches `null`, so it's unreachable from the null-root walk (it's just orphaned). The genuine hang is the **arbitrary-root** walks — `getSubtreeIds` (outdent) and the per-op `walk()` closures (delete/indent/insert) — which START at a specific node that can itself be inside a cycle (e.g. `1→3→2→1`), infinite-looping. **Fix (one place protects all):** a cycle-break pass at the data-load boundary in `normalizeIds` — for each task, walk its ancestor chain with a `seen` Set; if it loops, null that task's `parentId` (degrade to a root). After load the in-memory data is acyclic, so EVERY downstream walk terminates. The UI already prevents *creating* a cycle live, so the load path was the real exposure. Deliberately did NOT add a `visited` guard to `sortByVisualOrder` — it can't loop on a cycle anyway, and the guard would have changed duplicate-id handling (dropping a dup → data-loss regression). Faithful copies in `ui-audit/stress/scheduler-engine.mjs`; tests in `test/schedulerEngine.test.js` (3-task cycle broken, valid hierarchy unchanged, arbitrary-root-walk safety) + anti-drift guard. No persistence migration (load-time normalize, lossless — a cyclic task just becomes top-level).

### B551 — Stitcher left pointer-capture held on a blur/visibility abort → frozen grab cursor `[Doc Review / Stitcher]` (bug — event binding) — MED  *(bug-hunt round 10, 2026-06-27; fixed same lap; renumbered from a provisional B548 a concurrent main took)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1774 tests · build green.** The pan-interrupt recovery (`abortGesture`) needs the pointerId to `releasePointerCapture`, but the window-blur / visibility-hidden handlers called it with NO argument, so `pid != null` was false → capture was never released. Alt-tabbing mid-pan left the SVG with a frozen grab cursor that swallowed clicks until refocus. **Fix:** store `pointerId` in `drag.current` on pan-start and have `recover` pass `drag.current.pointerId` so the capture is actually released. Anti-drift guard added. **⏳ Runtime eyeball (pan + alt-tab → no stuck cursor) → V167.**

### B544 — PDF export leaked a blob URL via an 8-second revoke timer `[Site Planner / export]` (bug — resource leak) — low  *(bug-hunt round 9, 2026-06-27; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1772 tests · build green.** The Download-PDF path created an object URL and revoked it on an 8s `setTimeout`, so rapid re-exports (or navigating away) accumulated blob URLs in memory. **Fix:** revoke immediately after the synthetic `click()`, matching the proven PNG-export path in the same file (which already revokes inline). Anti-drift guard added.

### B545 — MapFinder address search had no request-token → a slow result clobbered a newer search `[Site Planner / map]` (bug — stale response) — MED  *(bug-hunt round 9; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1772 tests · build green.** `goAddress`/`selectParcelAt` awaited geocode + parcel-identify with no generation guard, so two quick searches raced: a slow first could land after the second, setting `parcelInfo` (and ADDING a parcel) for the wrong address, and its `finally` cleared the shared busy flag mid-second-search. **Fix:** an `addrTokRef` generation counter — `goAddress` claims a token and drops its result if a newer search started; `selectParcelAt` takes the token and neither applies info NOR adds the (stale) parcel once superseded. Reuses the codebase's existing cancelled-flag pattern. **⏳ Rapid-search runtime check → V165.**

### B546 — Stitcher calibration could display a non-finite scale ("1\" ≈ ∞'") `[Doc Review / Stitcher]` (bug — number display) — MED  *(bug-hunt round 9; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1772 tests · build green.** The composite-scale readout gated on `ftPerUnit ?`, but `Infinity`/`NaN` are truthy, so a corrupt loaded `ftPerUnit` (or a future bad calibration) would render "Scale set · 1\" ≈ ∞'". **Fix:** `Number.isFinite(ftPerUnit) && ftPerUnit` on both the color and the text; plus a belt-and-suspenders `u >= 1` guard in `commitCalibrate` so a near-zero span can never produce `Infinity` (mirrors `doCalibrate`, also catches NaN). Anti-drift guard added.

### B547 — Stitcher takeoff rollup could show "NaN ac · NaN sf · NaN ft" `[Doc Review / Stitcher]` (bug — number display) — MED  *(bug-hunt round 9; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1772 tests · build green.** The stitched-takeoff totals rendered `totals.areaSf`/`totals.distFt` unguarded; one degenerate measure (NaN from malformed/loaded geometry) propagates through the reduce and shows "NaN" for the whole rollup. **Fix:** `Number.isFinite` guard on each total, falling back to "—" (matches the per-measure display's conditional). Anti-drift guard added.

### B540 — Address geocoder conflated "service unreachable" with "address not found" `[Site Planner / geocode]` (bug — honesty/UX)  *(filed round 5; fixed round 8, 2026-06-27)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1761 tests · build green.** `geocodeAddress` returned `null` for BOTH a real "no candidates" result AND any network failure — so when the lookup host was down/blocked, the user was told the address doesn't exist (and might abandon a valid one). **Fix (B540 contract):** track `reachedAny` (did any provider respond OK?). Return `{lat,lon,label}` on a hit, `null` only when a provider was REACHED and authoritatively found nothing, and `{ error }` when NO provider was reachable. Both callers updated to show the distinct "lookup unavailable" message vs "not found": `MapFinder.goAddress` + `SitePlanner.addByAddress` (each gained `if (hit && hit.error) …`). `test/geocode.test.js` updated (the old "null on throw" test now asserts `{error}`) + 3 new contract tests. Anti-drift guard added.

### B541 — Cloud-sync badge popover closed itself on benign sync-state churn `[Shared / UI]` (bug — UX)  *(filed round 5; fixed round 8)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1761 tests · build green.** `CloudSyncBadge` keyed its error-boundary on `String(state)`, remounting the whole badge (and discarding the inner `Badge`'s open popover) on every save-cycle transition. **Fix:** the boundary is no longer remounted via a `key`; instead it takes a `resetKey` prop and clears a transient crash in `componentDidUpdate` when it changes. So the popover survives state transitions (the Badge's own effect still closes it when the state stops being actionable) while crash-recovery is fully preserved (a crash clears on the next state change, as before) and the badge still always renders the live `state`. Anti-drift guard added. **⏳ Signed-in eyeball that the detail popover stays open across a save cycle → V164** (same signed-in session as the B528/B529 check).

### B528 — Doc Review: overlapping same-id cloud saves false-tripped the self-conflict guard → autosave lockout `[Doc Review / persistence]` (bug — concurrency) — HIGH  *(filed round 4; fixed round 7, 2026-06-27)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1752 tests · build green.** `usePersistence`'s `writeNow` (debounce flush + visibility/unmount/manual flush) could fire a second cloud write for the same review id BEFORE the first resolved; both read the same `reviewVersions[id]`, so the loser failed the CAS and was reported as a foreign "conflict" — which trips `canCloudSave` and silently stops autosave until reload (no data loss, but alarming + sticky). **Fix:** a per-id write serializer (`src/shared/cloud/serializeWrites.js` `makeWriteSerializer`) wraps `upsertReview` → the second write for an id WAITS for the in-flight one, so it reads the version that write threaded back and the CAS succeeds. The genuine cross-device guard (`casUpsert`) is untouched. Unit test `test/serializeWrites.test.js` models the exact race (serialized → both succeed; naïve → one false-conflicts) AND asserts a real stale version still conflicts. Anti-drift guard added. **⏳ Signed-in runtime confirm (rapid edit + tab-hide doesn't flip to "saved elsewhere") → V164.**

### B529 — Site Planner: overlapping same-id cloud saves false-tripped the self-conflict guard `[Site Planner / persistence]` (bug — concurrency) — HIGH  *(filed round 4; fixed round 7)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1752 tests · build green.** Same root cause in `cloudSync.cloudUpsert` (Site Planner). **Fix:** the SAME shared serializer wraps `cloudUpsert` per site id, so serialization also keeps the B459 thin-clobber content baseline (`siteContent`/`siteTombs`) fresh for the second write. Lifting the latch into one shared helper means the two modules can't drift. Covered by the shared `test/serializeWrites.test.js` + an anti-drift guard. **⏳ Signed-in runtime confirm → V164.**

### B533 — 3DEP elevation converted metres with the international foot, not the US survey foot `[Site Planner / units]` (bug) — low  *(bug-hunt round 5, 2026-06-27; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1733 tests · build green.** `elevation.js` used `M_TO_FT = 3.280839895` (international foot) while the whole project — EPSG:2278 State Plane, `FT_PER_M` in `shared/coordinates` (B57b) — is US survey feet (3937/1200). A ~0.0002% drift (~0.66 ft per 100 m), low-impact today (elevation is transient/screening-only) but inconsistent with every other foot in the app and a latent error if a ditch invert is ever persisted. **Fix:** `M_TO_FT = 3937 / 1200`. Anti-drift guard in `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js`.

### B534 — Stitcher boot-resume IIFE had no rejection handler → unhandled promise on a resume failure `[Doc Review / Stitcher]` (bug) — MED  *(bug-hunt round 5; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1733 tests · build green.** The mount effect that resumes the last stitch session ran an async IIFE with no `.catch`; a throw from `loadReview`/`currentUid`/`reconcile`/`loadStitch` was an unhandled rejection. **Fix:** `.catch(() => {})` on the IIFE — `loadStitch` owns its own `busy` via `finally`, so swallowing falls cleanly to the empty stitcher instead of a half-started boot. Anti-drift guard added.

### B535 — DocReview boot-resume IIFE had no rejection handler → unhandled promise `[Doc Review]` (bug) — MED  *(bug-hunt round 5; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1733 tests · build green.** Same class as B534 in `DocReview.jsx`: the boot-resume IIFE guarded only the localStorage reads; `currentUid`/`loadReview`/`reconcile`/`loadSingleReview` awaited outside any catch. **Fix:** `.catch(() => {})` — `loadSingleReview` owns its own "Opening…" overlay via `finally`, so a resume failure falls to the empty state (the documented intended behavior). Anti-drift guard added.

### B536 — Stitcher addGroup: one failed page-render silently aborted the WHOLE group-drop (no sheets, no message) `[Doc Review / Stitcher]` (bug) — MED  *(bug-hunt round 5; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1733 tests · build green.** `renderPageToImage` inside addGroup's page loop had no per-page guard; a single corrupt page threw past the loop (the `finally` cleared `busy`, so not a stuck spinner — but `setPlaced` never ran, so a drop of N pages produced NOTHING with no explanation). **Fix:** per-page try/catch collects `renderFailed`, skips the bad page, and the notice now reports "N page(s) couldn't render (re-drop to retry)" — or, if every page failed, an explicit "couldn't render … re-drop" instead of a silent no-op. Anti-drift guard added.

### B537 — buildFilingPlan crashed ("not iterable") on a set missing pageNums `[Doc Review / auto-filing]` (bug) — MED  *(bug-hunt round 5; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1733 tests (+2) · build green.** `disciplineSplit.buildFilingPlan` spread `...s.pageNums` in three places (the `allSeen` reduce + the `claimed`/`entries` build) with no guard; a malformed `decision.sets` entry lacking `pageNums` threw and crashed filing. **Fix:** `...((s && s.pageNums) || [])` at all three sites → a missing array degrades to empty, not a throw. Behavioral tests in `test/disciplineSplit.test.js` (single + multi-discipline malformed input → no throw).

### B538 — sheetScale fracToNum allowed a zero denominator → Infinity/NaN `[Doc Review / scale]` (bug) — low  *(bug-hunt round 5; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1733 tests · build green.** `fracToNum` divided user-supplied callout text without a zero-denominator guard ("5/0" → Infinity, "0/0" → NaN). Downstream `parseSheetScale` range checks neutralize it today, but the helper should not leak non-finite values. **Fix:** return 0 when the denominator is 0 (both mixed and plain fraction branches). Anti-drift guard added.

### B539 — currentAccessToken: one corrupt auth-token blob aborted the whole scan → signed-in user looked signed-out to the keepalive push `[Auth / Storage]` (bug) — MED  *(bug-hunt round 5; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1733 tests · build green.** `supabase.currentAccessToken` wrapped the WHOLE key-scan loop in one try/catch, so a single corrupt/truncated `sb-*-auth-token` blob threw at `JSON.parse` and returned null — missing any later valid session (the B452 keepalive unload-flush would then push as anonymous → a contributing factor to "edits not saved"). **Fix:** parse each entry inside its own try/catch so a bad key is skipped and the scan continues. (The agent's first-pass fix — a type-check after JSON.parse — was rejected: the throw happens AT JSON.parse, before any check; only a per-iteration try works.) Anti-drift guard added.

Unit tests assert the hosts pass + spoofs still blocked (`test/gisProxyCore.test.js`). (Complements B517, which moved the TxRRC overlays off hctx.net onto the already-allowlisted texas.gov.)

### B511 — Site Planner: pruneMigratedLegacy dropped a NEWER logged-out site by id alone → silent data loss `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug) — HIGH  *(bug-hunt round 2, 2026-06-27, adversarially confirmed; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1716 tests (+3) · build green.** `pruneMigratedLegacy` (runs in `pullCloud` on every sign-in) deleted any on-device legacy site whose id merely EXISTED in the cloud map, with no timestamp check — so: create a site logged-out → sign in + migrate (legacy copy kept) → sign out → edit it logged-out → sign back in → the NEWER local edit was deleted before the migration modal (`pendingLegacyCount`, which keeps a legacy id newer than cloud) could ever surface it. **Fix:** prune only when `cloudMap[id].updatedAt >= legacy[id].updatedAt` (the inverse of `pendingLegacyCount`'s predicate), so B473's duplicate-reclamation still works but a newer local copy survives. Exported the function + 3 unit tests (`test/storage.test.js`: keeps-newer, prunes same/older, keeps cloud-absent). **⏳ Signed-in end-to-end flow → V160.**

### B512 — Doc Review: parseSheetScale read a rise:run SLOPE/grade ratio (or a clock time) as the drawing scale → silent mis-calibration `[Doc Review / parsing]` (bug) — HIGH  *(bug-hunt round 2; fixed same lap)*

### B504 — Site Planner: truck-court paving double-subtracted a corner bump-out footprint → yield understated impervious/coverage `[Site Planner / yield]` (bug)  *(bug-hunt 2026-06-27, adversarially confirmed; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1707 tests (+4) · build green.** Since B492 `relayoutSide` trims a same-side truck court IN to the clear face between corner bump-outs (`usableCourtSpan` → the court element's `w`/`h` already excludes the bump column), but the yield loop (`SitePlanner.jsx`) STILL subtracted the bump's full footprint (`e.w*e.h`) from `paving` when a same-side court existed — a stale de-double-count whose overlap no longer exists post-B492. Net: paving/impervious understated by the bump area (~3300 sf on the 55×60 default) and `open` overstated by the same; only fired when a building had both a same-side truck court AND a corner bump-out. **Fix:** removed the spurious de-double-count block — the court area already excludes the bump, and the bump (type `building`) is counted in `bldg`, so there's no remaining overlap to remove. Premise locked by new `usableCourtSpan` unit tests in `test/dockZones.test.js` (along = full − bumpStart − bumpEnd, asymmetric shift, 1-ft floor). **This clears the entire 2026-06-27 bug-hunt queue (B500/B510, B501–B509).**

### B505 — Doc Review: Stitcher `loadStitch()` rejection unhandled → noise + stuck `pendingStitch` `[Doc Review / stitch]` (bug) — MED  *(bug-hunt 2026-06-27, adversarially confirmed; fixed same lap)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1703 tests (+anti-drift) · build green.** `loadStitch()` awaits PDF/Drive/Storage I/O that can reject, but its caller `loadStitch(loadReq).then(() => onConsumeLoad())` had no `.catch` — a corrupt/partial PDF surfaced an unhandled rejection AND `onConsumeLoad()` never ran, so the load stayed half-consumed (`loadedId` already set → effect won't re-fire). **Fix:** added `.catch(() => onConsumeLoad && onConsumeLoad())` so the request is always consumed (`Stitcher.jsx`). ### B501 — Scheduler: deleting a task never recomputed parent roll-ups / cascade → stale summary dates `[Schedule]` (bug) — HIGH  *(bug-hunt 2026-06-27, adversarially confirmed; fixed same lap)*

### B510 — Markup: Dimension tool showed "—" instead of its calibrated length `[Shared / Markup]` (bug) — HIGH  *(filed AND fixed the same lap per STANDING RULE #1; surfaced by the 2026-06-27 bug-hunt Workflow — found by two independent hunters, adversarially confirmed)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1691 tests (+1) · build green.** The Dimension tool is declared `measureOutput:"length"` (`tools.matrix.js`) and rendered via `measureLabel` in `MarkupRenderer.jsx`, but `measureValue` (`src/shared/markup/measure.js`) had no `dimension` branch — it fell through to the generic return with no `lengthFt`, so `measureLabel` printed **"—"** for every calibrated Dimension (the tool's whole purpose — a ticked line labelled with its real length — was broken). Verified empirically: pre-fix `measureLabel({kind:"dimension",pts:[{0,0},{10,0}]}, 2)` returned `"—"` while the identical distance returned `"20.0 ft"`. **Fix:** `measureValue`'s distance branch now also handles `dimension`, preserving `m.kind` so it reports the calibrated `lengthFt` while callers still render the ticked variant. Deliberately NOT added to `MIN_MEASURE_PTS`/rollup — a dimension is an annotation, not a takeoff total, so totals are unchanged. New regression test in `test/takeoff.test.js` (`measureLabel` → "20.0 ft" calibrated / "set scale" uncalibrated / no-throw on empty). Pure-function fix; the on-canvas label is the visible win.

### B500 — Pond grading tool produced invalid slope contours + floor (acute-corner spikes, no valid floor, silent mis-report) `[Site Planner / detention]` (bug)  *(owner-found 2026-06-27 on the live triangular pond off Hwy 6 N: "the pond drawing tool … calculates how the pond curvature/slopes would work … does not seem like it worked whatsoever"; civil-engineer read attached; provisional "NEW-1"; minted **B500** = highest real B# (B499) + 1; branch `claude/pond-storage-site-plan-pzkjnf`)*
`[x]` **DONE + headless-verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1. lint 0 errors · full suite 1694 tests (+19 new: pondOffset 8, pondContours 11) green · build green · `ui-audit/verify-pond-contours.mjs` 9/9 (real Chromium, logged-out) on the actual acute-triangle repro.** The B497 contours reused the codebase's hand-rolled `offsetPolygon` (per-edge miter/bevel), which **spiked and self-intersected at acute corners**, returned a single ring (no pinch-off / no split), re-formed a bogus same-winding polygon past half-width (so the `aBottom===0` over-taper guard **silently misfired** → wrong area/volume, no warning), and `smoothRing` then rounded the garbage. Root-and-branch fix:
- **`[x]` Robust offset via clipper-lib** (new `lib/pondOffset.js`, pure/unit-tested): `offsetInward(ring, dist)` runs Clipper's `ClipperOffset` with **round joins** (rounds contour corners — also how earthwork actually grades) in the planner's **feet frame** (no reprojection), normalising orientation so a negative delta always shrinks. Returns an **array of rings**: `[]` on clean pinch-off, `[r]` normally, `[r1,r2,…]` when a basin splits — never a spike, never throws (degenerate/bowtie input → `[]`). `maxInwardOffset(ring)` binary-searches the max inscribed reach.
- **`[x]` `pondContours` rewritten** (`lib/pondGeom.js`): each level carries `rings[]`; stops at pinch-off; reports `feasible` + `maxDepth = maxInwardOffset/slope`. `smoothRing` (Chaikin) **deleted** — round joins already produce true smooth geometry; smoothing distorted areas.
- **`[x]` `detentionStorage` rewritten** (SitePlanner.jsx): stage areas from `offsetInward`; **average-end-area volume** integrated only over slabs that actually exist (a basin that daylights before design depth no longer inflates the number); returns `feasible`/`maxDepth`. 1-entry memo so panel+label+chip don't re-run the offsets each frame.
- **`[x]` Fail LOUD on infeasibility** (silent-failure rule): renderer draws the real partial contours **plus** a red on-canvas `⚠ Too deep — max ≈ N′ at S:1`; panel states the exact max gradeable depth and that the volume shown is for that achievable basin; the on-plan "Holds …" line reports the **achievable** depth `(max)`, not the over-stated design depth.
- **Untouched on purpose:** `offsetPolygon` stays for **parcel setbacks** (per-edge variable offset a uniform buffer can't express) and `expandPolygon` for pond "push banks out" — neither is the reported bug.
- **Dep:** added `clipper-lib` (CAD-grade polygon-offset engine) to the lazy `SitePlannerApp` chunk (+~29 kB gzip). *(Investigated the civil-engineer-suggested JSTS first; jsts 2.12 ships no package entry point → unimportable under Vite/vitest, so used clipper-lib, which is purpose-built for offsetting and imports cleanly — same robust round-join + multipolygon + pinch-off behaviour.)*
- **⏳ Visual-over-live-aerial eyeball → VERIFICATION.md V157** (headless draws over the gray surface, not live tiles).

Remaining ongoing-loss *incidents* are tracked separately (B134/B473 track), not this drop. No new code owed for B124.

- **Stage contour lines (the topographic depth rings).** Each ring is the inward offset of the top-of-bank footprint at a depth below the top — exactly the construction `detentionStorage` already uses (`offsetPolygon(ring, slope*down)`), so the rings and the storage numbers come from one source and can never disagree. ### B494 — Schedule module loading overlay sticks for a full 9 s "sometimes" (slow/buggy ready signal) `[Scheduler / loader]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-27 — "fix the loading icon for the scheduling module, seems kind of slow or buggy sometimes"; minted **B494** = highest real B# (B493) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B493 a concurrent `main` took for the cross-module-link feature)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified (branch `claude/pdf-viewer-quality-x40e5a`). lint 0 · 1641 tests · build green · NEW headless `ui-audit/verify-scheduler-loader.mjs` 3/3 (+ diagnostic `observe-scheduler-loader.mjs`).**
- **Repro (headless, observed):** switch to the Schedule module → the "assembling schedule" loading overlay (`ModuleLoader`, B224) sat visible for the FULL **9 s** before cross-fading out, regardless of how fast the embedded `/sequence/` app was. Root cause: the overlay only dropped on the embedded app's FIRST `planar:nav-state` message, whose ONLY backstop was a lone `setTimeout(…, 9000)`. So whenever that first signal was slow or missed — a network hiccup, the embed's deps loading slowly, the embed not yet interactive — the loader stuck for a flat 9 seconds (the "slow/buggy sometimes").
- **Fix (`Scheduler.jsx` + a tiny responder in `public/sequence/index.html`):** make the ready signal **reliable + bounded**. (1) **Handshake** — on the iframe's `onLoad` the shell posts `planar:nav-request` (retried ~every 380 ms for ~2.3 s, in case the embed's own listener isn't attached yet); the embedded app answers by re-emitting `nav-state` from `latestData` (a no-op until its data has loaded), so a missed/slow first emit can no longer strand the loader — it drops the instant the embed is interactive. (2) **Bounded fallbacks** — reveal the embed ~2.5 s after its document loads even if it never answers (a slow/broken embed shouldn't hold a full-screen spinner), with a 6 s absolute backstop if `onLoad` itself never fires. `markReady()` + a ref make every path idempotent (one cross-fade). The proactive `nav-state` fast path is unchanged, so a clean boot still drops the loader immediately.
- **Verified:** `verify-scheduler-loader.mjs` 3/3 (real built shell, the embed stubbed via request-interception so the handshake/fallback paths actually run — the real embed's CDN is blocked in the sandbox so its iframe never finishes loading here): a **responsive** embed drops the loader at **~520 ms** via the handshake (was 9000 ms); a **silent** embed is bounded to **~3000 ms** (onLoad+2.5 s), not 9 s, and doesn't drop prematurely. Diagnostic `observe-scheduler-loader.mjs` shows the sandbox worst case (embed never signals, `onLoad` never fires) improved 9.5 s → 6.5 s (the backstop).
- **Follow-up filed (deliberately deferred):** the embed still `await`s a Supabase round-trip (no local cache) before first paint → genuine first-load instant-ness is **B495**.
- **⏳ Live/signed-in check → VERIFICATION.md V153** (the real embedded app's `nav-request` responder needs its CDN + Supabase, blocked here).

### B493 — Connect projects across modules: a schedule linked to a site (also CLOSES B477) `[Cross-module / Schedule ↔ Site ↔ Review]` (feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-27 — "connect the projects within modules, like I have pappadoupolos in schedule and site planner but I don't have a way to connect them… or create a schedule connected to a site"; branch `claude/cross-module-project-connections-bemcqi`; minted **B493** = highest real B# across both files (B492) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B491 that concurrent `main` PRs took for B491/B492 while this was in flight)*

- **The gap:** a project = a Site Planner **site group** (`group_id`). Site↔Review already follow the same project (Review reads the shared `sites` table by `project_id=group_id`), but the **Schedule** is the embedded `/sequence/` iframe with its OWN backend + numeric project ids — "Pappadoupolos" there had no link to the site. Land on a site with no linked schedule → a `LinkSchedulePanel` resolution card: **Create a schedule for this site** / **Link an existing one** (same-named suggestion + manual picker).
- **Files:** `siteModel.js` (v9 fields + migrate), `storage.js` (`setScheduleLink`/`scheduleLinkOf`), `shared/projects/projectModel.js`+`projects.js` (surface the hint + pure `suggestNameMatch`/`normalizeProjectName`), `public/sequence/index.html` (nav-state carries the link; new inbound `nav-select-by-site`/`nav-link`/`nav-create-linked`; outbound `link-changed`; `addProject` accepts name+link), `scheduler/lib/navState.js` (`findBySiteId` + carry link through `sanitizeProjects`), `scheduler/Scheduler.jsx` + new `scheduler/components/LinkSchedulePanel.jsx`, `app/Shell.jsx` (`onScheduleLinkChanged` → mirror), `shared/ui/ProjectBreadcrumb.jsx` (📅 connectedness chip). +28 unit tests across navState/projects/siteModel.
- **Verified:** the new React-wrapper path end-to-end headless (panel → suggested match → link mirrors `scheduleProjectId` onto the site store → panel closes once linked) via the same-origin bridge contract; the embedded `index.html` edits parse clean (Babel, zero page errors).
- **⏳ Live-edge (signed-in, both backends):** the genuine cross-iframe round-trip needs the Schedule's own Supabase (unreachable from the sandbox) → VERIFICATION.md **V152**.

### B492 — Bump-outs vs. sidewalks & truck courts: sidewalk should span the full building side; truck court should pull in between bumps + be length-editable `[Site Planner / dock features]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-27 — "sidewalks should default to the full side of the building when I add or edit bump outs … I can't edit truck courts length along the dock and [it should] get pulled in when I put a bump out"; branch `claude/sidewalks-truck-courts-bump-outs-0u7o6v`; minted **B492** = highest real B# (B491) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional **B488** that concurrent `main` PRs (#377 PDF-viewer / #380 schedule-output / pen-test) took for B488–B491 while this was in flight)*
`[x]` **DONE + headless-verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1. lint 0 errors · full suite 1625 tests (+11) green · build green · NEW `ui-audit/verify-b492-bump-sidewalk-court.mjs` 11/11 (real Chromium, logged-out).** Three coupled defects in how a building's corner **bump-outs** (dog-ears) interact with its **sidewalks** and its **truck court**, fixed at the shared geometry so the canvas + the panel agree:
- **`[x]` Sidewalk now spans the FULL building side incl. the bump-out.** Was: a bump-out grew the perpendicular sidewalk by a *fixed* 60′ (`adjustSidewalkForBump`), ignoring the bump's real projection and not following a later resize. Now: new pure `sidewalkSpanForBumps(b, swSide, bumps)` (`lib/dogEar.js`, unit-tested) recomputes the strip's run + along-centre from the wall length **plus every bump-out that lengthens that wall**; `sidewalkFullRunPatch`/`relayoutBumpSidewalks` (SitePlanner) re-lay it on bump **add / remove / resize** and when a sidewalk is added to a wall that already has bumps — preserving the strip's thickness + outward offset. (Headless: left/right sidewalks 300′→**420′** with two 60′ bumps; back to 300′ on removal.)
- **`[x]` Truck court PULLS IN to the clear dock face between the bump-outs.** Was: `layoutZone` hard-locked the court to the full wall (`along = b.w/b.h`), so the paving overlapped the bump corners (only the dock *doors* pulled in). Now: pure `usableCourtSpan(full, bumpStart, bumpEnd)` + an optional 5th `opts` arg on `layoutZone` (zone 0 only) pull the court in to `full − bumpStart − bumpEnd`, centred on the clear face — the **same `bumpAlong` model the door renderer already uses**, so doors + court agree. Trailer/buffer keep the full wall (a 60′ bump doesn't reach them). Wired via `courtBumpOpts` in `relayoutSide` (so add-zone / depth-edit / building-resize all benefit) + an explicit re-lay on bump add/remove/resize. (Headless: court 600′→**490′** with two 55′ bumps, stays centred.)
- **`[x]` Truck-court length is now USER-EDITABLE along the dock.** New **“Truck court length (ft)”** inline field on the selected court (next to its depth), `setCourtLengthAll`/`courtLengthShown` store `alongLen` per dock side; relayout caps a typed length to the clear face so it never re-overlaps a bump. (Headless: set 300′ → court along-span = 300′.)
- **Reuse, no new primitives:** reuses `bumpSidewalkSide`, `dogEarSize`, `SIDE_N`, `rot2`, `swSide`, `findCourtIn`, `relayoutSide`, `outwardUnit`; the old fixed-increment `adjustSidewalkForBump`/`isBumpSidewalk` were deleted (no remaining callers). Logged-out-verifiable (pure planner canvas) — no signed-in path owed.

### B488 — Document Review PDF viewer quality: wire pdf.js support assets (fonts/CMaps/ICC/WASM) + supersample the detail layer + deeper zoom & snappier settle `[Doc Review / Markup]` (task — quality)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-27 "improve the PDF viewer quality… I'm sure it's lacking somehow"; minted **B488** = highest real B# (B487) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B486 that a concurrent `main` (#374/#376) took for the team-RLS + schedule-input fixes)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified (branch `claude/pdf-viewer-quality-x40e5a`). lint 0 · 1599 tests · build green · NEW headless `verify-pdfjs-assets.mjs` 9/9 (incl. a fix↔control A/B) + `verify-docreview-viewer.mjs` 13/13 (no regression).**
- **ROOT GAP:** `loadPdf` called `getDocument({ data })` with NONE of pdf.js v6's asset URLs — but v6 ships its render-support assets as on-disk folders (`pdfjs-dist/{standard_fonts,cmaps,iccs,wasm}`) that are NOT bundled into the worker. Verified against the installed worker source: without `wasmUrl` BOTH the WASM and the JS-fallback image decoders fail to load (both build their URL from `wasmUrl`), so **JBIG2 (scanned B&W) and JPEG2000/JPX (scanned colour/aerial) images decode to BLANK**; ICC colour is explicitly disabled (`warn("No ICC color space support due to missing wasmUrl")`); Symbol/ZapfDingbats + CID/CJK glyphs drop without `standardFontDataUrl`/`cMapUrl`. Exactly the surfaces a survey/scan review hits.
- **FIX:** (1) new inline vite plugin `pdfjsAssets()` (`vite.config.js`) exposes the four folders at `<base>pdfjs/<folder>/` — streamed from node_modules in dev (`configureServer`), emitted verbatim into the build (`generateBundle`, fixed `fileName` → no content-hashing) so they stay in lock-step with the installed pdfjs version (no committed, drift-prone blobs). (2) `loadPdf` (`doc-review/lib/pdf.js`) passes `cMapUrl`+`cMapPacked` / `standardFontDataUrl` / `iccUrl` / `wasmUrl` derived from `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` (root-absolute → resolves identically on the main thread, inside the worker, and under any deploy subpath). Production-safe: no `/* /index.html` SPA catch-all and the `/assets/*` rule never matches `/pdfjs/*` (B449), and Cloudflare serves real static files before consulting `_redirects`.
- **ALSO (crispness/responsiveness, same module — high-value low-risk set from the audit synthesis):** the DETAIL layer now supersamples to a 2× density floor even on a 1× monitor (`DETAIL_DENSITY_TARGET`/`DETAIL_DENSITY_CAP`, `renderBudget.backingScale`, still budget-clamped) for cleaner anti-aliased CAD linework/text — the residual "softer than Bluebeam" gap left after B415 (which only restored *device* density); the settle debounce dropped **140→90 ms** (sharp detail returns sooner after a gesture); `VIEW_MAX` **6→10** (read the finest survey bearing/dimension text); the whole-page backdrop floor `BACKDROP_PX_BUDGET` **8e6→16e6** (the soft floor *during* a gesture on a retina E-size sheet rises ≈73→103 dpi; no-op on a 1× monitor; under Safari's single-canvas cap); the detail pan-halo margin **0.25→0.40** (a decisive flick-pan stays sharp to its leading edge); and the high-dpi density cap **2→2.5** (a 3×/4× panel renders a bit denser). +4 budget unit tests (15 total).
- **Verified:** `verify-pdfjs-assets.mjs` 9/9 — serves all four asset types (200; wasm as `application/wasm`); the pdf.js **WORKER** fetches `FoxitDingbats.pfb` + `FoxitSymbol.pfb` from `/pdfjs/standard_fonts/` (a CONTROL with the getDocument wiring reverted drops to 6/8: no worker font fetch + logs "Cannot load system font: ZapfDingbats/Symbol"); zero degradation warnings; sheet non-blank; detail backing = **2.00×** on a 1× display. `verify-docreview-viewer.mjs` 13/13 — zoom-anchor/pan/sheet-switch/fit/count/drag/text all unaffected (also repointed its stale "Library" boot to the `#markup` route, B418).
- **Follow-ups filed (deliberately deferred):** remaining render-engine polish → **B489**; an optional-content (OCG) layer toggle → **B490**.
- **⏳ Live-edge:** production serving of `/pdfjs/*` on planyr.io → VERIFICATION.md **V149**. Verified this session against the Cloudflare **branch-preview** deploy (same Pages project + build that serves planyr.io): all four `/pdfjs/*` asset types return 200 with correct content-types (`application/wasm`, `application/x-font-type1`, `application/vnd.iccprofile`, `application/octet-stream`) and none falls through to the SPA `index.html`; the post-merge planyr.io curl is the last confirmation.

### B487 — Schedule module: input edits silently dropped, mangled, or left stale state `[Schedule / inputs]` (bug batch)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-27 — "find all the bugs you can as it relates to the inputs for the schedule module and fix them and ship"; branch `claude/schedule-input-bugs-jtfplb`; minted **B487** = highest real B# (B486, the concurrent team-RLS fix) + 1 — the B526 hit in BACKLOG-DONE is a CSS hex, not an id)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified. lint 0 · 1613 tests (+16) · build green · esbuild JSX transform OK · NEW headless `ui-audit/verify-schedule-input-bugs.mjs` 8/8 (real Chromium, logged-out).** A fan-out review of every user-input path in the embedded scheduler (`public/sequence/index.html`) found six places where a reasonable typed value was silently lost, mangled, or left the model inconsistent. All fixed at the input boundary; the engine itself was already hardened (B246–B251).
- **`[x]` Predecessor edits validated (self / unknown / cycle).** New pure `validatePredEdit(tasks, id, parsed)` (in index.html + mirrored to `ui-audit/stress/scheduler-engine.mjs`, 7 unit tests): drops self-references (existing Fix #16), references to task ids that don't exist in the project (were stored + displayed as a live dep but did nothing — `cascadeDates` filtered them), and references that would close a **circular dependency** (A→B→A produced silently-arbitrary dates) — each surfaced with a toast. Wired into `applyUpdate`.
- **`[x]` Grid date input hardened.** A date cell can now be **cleared** (empty → `""`, was silently reverted); an **unreadable** date gives a toast ("Couldn't read that date…") instead of silently reverting; and **Finish before Start** is rejected with a toast instead of silently collapsing the task to a 0-day milestone and discarding the typed date.
- **`[x]` Finish on an unscheduled task.** Setting a Finish on a task with no Start used to set `duration = ""` (rendered a bare "d") and the typed finish was then wiped by the cascade (`calcEnd("",…)===""`). It now anchors a 1-day task on that date (start=end, duration=1). Added a defensive duration-cell render guard so a stray empty duration can never show a bare "d".
- **`[x]` Indent / outdent / paste now recompute roll-ups.** `indentTask`, `outdentTask`, `indentTaskById`, `outdentTaskById`, and `pasteTaskAfter` changed `parentId` but never ran `cascadeDates`/`rollupParentDates`, so the old and new parents kept **stale summary start/end/duration** until the next in-subtree date edit. New shared `recomputeAfterStructureChange` (= `rollupParentDates(cascadeDates(...))`, the same recompute `updateTask` runs) is applied in all five handlers before renumber.
- **`[x]` Master ("All tasks") grid duration clamp.** It lacked the project grid's `Math.min(100000, …)` upper bound, so a fat-fingered duration there could freeze the layout. Clamp added to match.
- **`[x]` Export cover fields escaped.** The PDF/print cover **Date** (`cfg.docDate`) and **Prepared for** (`cfg.preparedFor`) were interpolated raw while their four siblings used `escapeHtml` — a typed `<`/`&`/quote corrupted the cover (and was an injection vector into the generated preview). Both now use `escapeHtml`.
- **Verified here (logged-out headless):** `verify-schedule-input-bugs.mjs` 8/8 — board boots with all fixes in (proves the whole Babel block still parses), and self-ref / nonexistent-id / circular-dependency / Finish-before-Start / unreadable-date each toast with no uncaught errors. Plus `validatePredEdit` units + `rollupParentDates` move-rollup unit + anti-drift string guards in `test/schedulerEngine.test.js`. *(Sandbox quirk: the board's React/Babel CDNs are closed to the browser here, so the harness used locally pre-downloaded copies via `SEQ_VENDOR=<dir>`; in CI/normal envs run it with no env var.)*
- **⏳ Three running-app click-throughs → VERIFICATION.md V148** (indent roll-up widening visible in the grid; Finish-on-blank-task showing "1d"; export-cover escaping in the generated PDF) — not drivable as cleanly headless, covered here by unit + anti-drift + the boot check.
- **Scope note (NOT a bug):** the on-screen Gantt has **no bar drag/resize** (bars are click-to-select only; the only chart drag is whole-canvas pan, and the Snap/Free toggle drives the grid↔Gantt split divider) — so there's no second date-input path that could disagree with the typed/`addBD` path. New/inserted tasks are intentionally born blank (unscheduled until given a date or predecessor). Both confirmed during the review.

### B486 — SECURITY: a non-owner team member could RE-HOME a shared project to another team `[Site Planner / Team / RLS]` (bug, security)  *(found 2026-06-27 by an owner-requested Team Workspaces bug audit; minted **B486** = highest real B# (B485) + 1)*
`[x]` **Fix WRITTEN + committed (`db/team_rehome_guard.sql`); ⏳ owner must RUN it in Supabase to activate (like every team migration). lint 0 / build green (SQL-only + docs — no app code).**
- **The bug:** `db/team_sharing.sql`'s `update own or team …` policies enforce sharing via WITH CHECK, whose second branch `(team_id is not null and is_team_member(team_id))` only checks the RESULTING team_id. RLS WITH CHECK can't see the OLD row, so it can't distinguish "kept the same team" from "moved to a different team." A NON-OWNER member who belongs to two teams could therefore UPDATE the owner's shared row and change its `team_id` from team X to team Y (a team the member is on) — re-homing the owner's project and cutting team X (and the owner, if not on Y) out of access. Contradicts the documented owner-only re-home/unshare intent. (Unshare-to-null was already owner-gated — only re-home-to-another-team slipped through.)
- **Why it's not an emergency (but should be run before teams go live):** it requires a member on two teams with the project shared to one — and the team feature isn't actively used yet (no invites sent; B406's signed-in round-trip is still owed, V118). So no real team with overlapping members exists today; the exposure is latent.
- **The fix (`db/team_rehome_guard.sql`):** a BEFORE UPDATE trigger `guard_team_rehome()` on `sites`/`doc_reviews`/`file_facts` that raises `42501` if `team_id` changes and `old.user_id <> auth.uid()` — i.e. only the row OWNER may change `team_id` (share/unshare/re-home); teammates edit CONTENT freely (team_id unchanged → allowed). Idempotent; SECURITY INVOKER (reads OLD/NEW + auth.uid(), no RLS bypass). Audited the rest of the team surface too (teams.js, teams.sql helpers + invite-claim, casUpsert owner-preservation, team_storage.sql) — all sound; this was the one real gap.
- **⏳ Owner step (handed over + OWNER-TODO):** run `db/team_rehome_guard.sql` in the Supabase SQL editor. Verify (2 accounts) → VERIFICATION.md V147.

### B472 — Restore the parking-field split as a true EXPLODE into individual rows + aisles `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-25 as "NEW-1" — "with a parking field selected there's no longer a tool to split it into its rows + drive aisles; it worked before"; minted **B472** = highest real B# across both files (B471) + 1)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + headless-verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/restore-parking-split-tool-hgdg7f`).** *NOTE — this session was push-to-branch only; no PR/merge to `main` was opened (next session/owner merges). Kept in Open until merged.*
- **GROUNDED THE REPORT FIRST (git log/blame).** The split control was **NOT removed** — not in the markup-engine unification (B423–B432) the brief flagged, nor anywhere else (zero removing commits). `splitParkingRows` + the pure `splitParkingPieces` (B130) were intact and wired in **two** places (the Parking panel + the right-click "Parking" menu). So the "lost in the consolidation" hypothesis is **refuted**; nothing was reintroduced as a fork.
- **The REAL gap (why the owner saw it as gone/wrong):** the existing tool split a field into double-loaded **MODULE** elements — each piece *still* bundled 2 rows + 1 aisle — so a 2-module field gave a **2-element** result, and it was hidden below 3 rows. That is exactly the owner's complaint: *"do not collapse the aisle into a row or force a 2-element result."*
- **Fix — a true explode into the field's constituent bands.** New pure `explodeParkingBands(h, sd, ai)` in `lib/parking.js` returns the ordered `{kind:"row"|"aisle", depth}` sequence (rows pair into double-loaded modules exactly as the field was built — aisles = ⌈rows/2⌉; depths always sum to `h`, so stall count + pavement are preserved). `splitParkingRows` now maps each piece to an **independent, separately selectable element**: a **stall row → `type:"parking"`** (one-row depth, renders a single row) and a **drive aisle → `type:"paving"`** (a plain lane). Counts scale: single-loaded (1 row+aisle) → **2**, double-loaded → **3** (row, aisle, row), 8-row field → **12** (8 rows + 4 aisles).
- **Behaviour decisions made explicit (per the brief):** *destructive but cleanly UNDOABLE* — replaces the parent + `pushHistory()` so Ctrl+Z restores it (never vaporizes geometry); pieces are editable-layer geometry (never touches any imported backdrop); child centres are derived from the parent edges (rotated local offsets, depths sum to `h`) so **no coordinate drift**; curbs auto-suppress at the new seams via the existing `edgeAbutsPaving` (parking/paving are both paved neighbours). The control is now offered whenever the field explodes to **≥2 real pieces** (was ≥3 rows), and a degenerate/empty field (or a bare already-exploded single row) **surfaces a loud notice instead of a silent no-op** (and the gate hides the button there too). Renders for **already-saved** fields, not just freshly-drawn (reads only persisted `h/w/rot/cx/cy/cfg`).
- **Dedup:** net-new — NOT B130/B131 (parking *generation* + boundary clip) and NOT B416 ("Split **a parcel**" = lot boundary). REUSES the B130 `lib/parking.js` math + the `carStalls` band model; the B130 `splitParkingPieces` (module split) + its tests are left intact (no fork).
- **Verified:** lint **0 errors** · **1560 tests** (+9 `explodeParkingBands`/no-op) · build green · headless **V138** (`ui-audit/verify-b472-explode-parking.mjs`, **9/9**): a double-loaded module → 3 elements (2 parking rows + 1 paving aisle, depths sum to 60′); a 6-row field → 9 elements; a bare exploded row no longer re-offers the control.

### B475 — Markup breadcrumb switcher and the Markup Library read different project sources and can diverge `[Doc Review / Shared header]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-26 as "NEW-1"; minted **B475** = highest real B# across both files (B474) + 1 — the B25431/B5263 hits in BACKLOG-DONE.md are CSS hex colours, not IDs)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/markup-switcher-cache-divergence-ceprhv`).** *NOTE — push-to-branch only this session; no PR/merge to `main` opened. Kept in Open until merged.*
- **Repro (grounded in code, not guessed):** sign in on a device that hasn't opened the Site Planner this session (cold/empty local cache), go straight to Markup, open the breadcrumb "▾" project switcher → it showed no/stale projects, while the Markup **Library / Files** drawer listed the real cloud projects. Same `sites` table, two read paths: the breadcrumb runs **uncontrolled** in DocReview (no `projects` prop) → `shared/projects/projects.js listProjects()` → `loadSitesList()` → the Site-Planner local cache (`planarfit:sites:cloud:<uid>`, only filled after a Site-Planner cloud pull). The Library uses `reviewStore.listProjects()` → a **live Supabase** query. Purely a source/freshness divergence (IDs are consistent — `groupId` === `group_id`), contradicting B191's "no parallel project store" intent.
- **Fix (option 2 from the hint — warm the cache, don't fork into a controlled list):** new `warmProjectsIfEmpty()` in `projects.js` — when signed in **and** the on-device project cache is empty, it runs the SAME `pullCloud(uid)` the Site Planner runs on login (no-ops logged-out or already-warm; never throws), populating the shared cache both paths read. `ProjectBreadcrumb`'s uncontrolled mount effect now kicks it off once and re-`refresh()`es when it lands. New `activeUid()` getter on `storage.js`. Chosen over passing a controlled `projects` prop because that path drops the breadcrumb's rename/delete + cross-tab `storage`-event refresh and mismatches the project shape (no `updatedAt`/`relTime`) — warming fixes the actual root cause and benefits every uncontrolled host with no behavior change.
- **Dedup:** net-new; touches the shared breadcrumb + projects helper only (no change to controlled mode / Schedule). Verified: lint **0 errors** · **1571 tests** · build green (DocReview still its own lazy chunk).
- **⏳ One signed-in spot-check (owner, planyr.io):** on a fresh tab/device, open Markup signed-in without touching the Site Planner first → the breadcrumb switcher now lists the same projects as the 🗂 Files drawer. (Sandbox can't reproduce — sign-in is blocked there; the cold-cache path is signed-in-only.)

### B481 — Large site-plan overlay didn't re-render after reload (stranded on the "Re-add" placeholder despite the raster being in IndexedDB) `[Site Planner / overlay]` (bug)  *(Cowork signed-in verification 2026-06-26, "NEW-1" — a 7.5 MB overlay showed "Re-add … not synced to this device" after reload though its ~10 MB raster sat in IndexedDB; minted **B481** = highest real B# (B480) + 1)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified (branch `claude/exciting-wright-yb6ruz`). lint 0 · 1597 tests · build green · NEW headless `verify-b480-overlay-large.mjs` 8/8 + `verify-b474-overlay-idb.mjs` 7/7 (no regression).**
- **Repro (Cowork, signed-in):** load a >~5 MB image as a sheet-overlay → it stores in IndexedDB (`raster:<proj>:overlay:<id>`, ~10 MB) with localStorage small → reload → overlay shows the "Re-add … not on this device" placeholder, even though the bytes are in IndexedDB *on this device* and the record carries an `idbKey`. The same large image as the **aerial underlay re-rendered fine** (separate, simpler effect).
- **ROOT CAUSE (not Cowork's guess of "gates on storageKey" — the effect DOES try `idbKey` first, SitePlanner.jsx:3551).** The overlay rehydrate effect had a `cancelled`-flag stranding race: a SLOW `idbGet` of a multi-MB raster was discarded whenever any other setState re-ran the `[sheetOverlays]` effect before the read resolved — the result was dropped AND never re-fetched, so the overlay sat src-less forever. A small raster resolves before any re-render (why the 7/7 small-overlay test always passed); the underlay uses a separate effect (why it worked).
- **FIX:** apply each rehydrate result via a functional patch-by-id guarded on `!x.src` (safe across re-runs — fills only an overlay still present + still src-less), and DROP the `cancelled` guard so a slow `idbGet` is never stranded. Plus the placeholder now reads "Loading drawing…" when an `idbKey` OR `storageKey` exists (recoverable) and only "Re-add … image not on this device" when neither does.
- **Verified:** `verify-b480-overlay-large.mjs` 8/8 — a 2.1 MB overlay (idbKey only, no storageKey, heavy src off the cap) re-renders after reload + view churn, no placeholder. Original 7/7 overlay test unchanged.
- **⏳ Signed-in re-confirm of Cowork's exact 7.5 MB case → VERIFICATION.md V146.**

### B480 — "Take over editing here" was a pointless loop (conflict → take over → bounce to map → same conflict); lock/conflict scoping confirmed PER-PLAN `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug, HIGH PRIORITY)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-26 live on planyr.io — "it's a fucking pointless loop … it needs to be site specific"; minted **B480** = highest B# (B479) + 1)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified (branch `claude/exciting-wright-yb6ruz`). lint 0 · 1597 tests (+3) · build green · headless `verify-readonly-takeover.mjs` 7/7 (no regression).**
- **Repro (owner, signed-in):** editing a plan that was ALSO open in another tab on the same computer → the cloud version-CAS (B314) correctly flagged "changed in another session" + offered "Take over editing here." Clicking it ran `window.location.reload()`, which (a) bounced to the MAP (out of the plan) and (b) re-entered the version race with the still-open other tab, so reopening the plan re-flagged the SAME conflict → an endless take-over → map → conflict loop that never resolved.
- **ROOT CAUSE:** `takeOverEditing` reconciled a conflict by reloading ("boot union-merge"). The reload left the planner AND, because the other tab still held the lock / kept the cloud version ahead, the reloaded tab's stale optimistic-version token (`siteVersions[id]`) still mismatched the cloud → conflict again.
- **FIX — reconcile IN PLACE, never reload:** Take over now (1) steals the per-plan Web Lock + broadcasts a yield so the other same-browser tab steps down to read-only and STOPS pushing; (2) calls the new focused `reconcileSiteFromCloud(id)` (`cloudSync.fetchSiteForReconcile` — a single-row fetch that refreshes `siteVersions[id]` to the cloud's CURRENT version + returns the cloud copy; deliberately NOT `pullCloud`, whose fire-and-forget re-push could race our own push and re-trigger the conflict); (3) unions the other session's content into the canvas (nothing lost from either side); (4) clears the conflict — the state change drives a single autosave push at the fresh version → it lands, this tab becomes the active editor, and you never leave the planner.
- **Scoping CONFIRMED already correct (owner's 2nd ask) — PER-PLAN, not module-wide.** The editor lock name is `planyr-editor:<siteId>` (`setProject(siteId)`, SitePlanner.jsx ~1629) and the cloud version-CAS is keyed `siteVersions[<siteId>]`. Two people on DIFFERENT projects/plans share NEITHER → zero contention; only two sessions on the SAME plan contend (correct — that's exactly the case being arbitrated). No code change needed; verified in code.
- **Tests:** `test/reconcileSite.test.js` (3) — the version-token refresh that breaks the loop. Existing read-only take-over headless 7/7 (no regression — the logged-out lock hand-off path is unchanged).
- **⏳ Signed-in confirm → VERIFICATION.md V145** (the cloud-conflict reconcile only fires signed in; the sandbox is logged-out).

### B478 — Resume-into-planner: a signed-in deep link / refresh bounced to the finder (route stripped to `#/`) `[Site Planner / Persistence / Routing]` (bug, HIGH PRIORITY)  *(Cowork re-confirmed ❌ 2026-06-25 on planyr.io — see VERIFICATION.md V13/V28; minted **B478** = highest real B# across both files (B477) + 1)*

- **ROOT CAUSE (pinned in `SitePlannerApp.jsx`):** on a **signed-in** deep link/refresh the user's cloud sites aren't in the local store at the first synchronous render (auth + `pullCloud` are async), so `activeSiteId` is momentarily null even though the route names a project. - **FIX:** a `bootResolved` gate (new pure `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/bootResume.js`) holds BOTH the URL sync and the dangling-pointer cleanup until the first auth + pull settles (true from the start when there's no Supabase to wait on, so logged-out is byte-identical). The resume target is now one shared, unit-tested `pickResumeTarget` (used by the first-render boot AND the post-pull resume, so they can't drift). The `bootResolved=true` flip is batched with the resume's `setActiveSiteId`, so the URL-sync effect only ever sees the resolved view.
- **Verified:** lint **0 errors** · **1585 tests (+11 `test/bootResume.test.js`)** · build green · logged-out headless **8/8** (`ui-audit/verify-resume-into-planner.mjs` — deep-link + reload stays in the planner, route intact, `currentSite` preserved, 0 page errors) + `verify-new-site-save.mjs` **10/10** (no regression). **The signed-in async-gap repro can't run in the sandbox (no Supabase → no gap), so the signed-in confirm is owed — `VERIFICATION.md` V143.**
- **Dedup:** net-new; the resume regression sat under V13/V28 (which referenced B124/B125/B134 — those were the *data-durability* halves, already ✅). This is the *resume-into-planner* half. Distinct from B477 (Schedule project carry).

### B471 — Saving stalled with no banner / couldn't take over; cross-session+device conflict now has a real "Take over" + auth-transition tracing `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug/robustness)  *(owner reported a recurrence 2026-06-25 right after B466 shipped — "it's literally not saving… I should be able to take over… maybe open on another PC"; minted **B471** = highest B# (B470) + 1)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified (branch `claude/exciting-wright-yb6ruz`). lint 0 · 1528 tests · build green · headless V (`ui-audit/verify-readonly-takeover.mjs`, 7/7 — the read-only take-over path is intact after the handler reorder).** Owner correction taken on board: it was **NOT** a second tab on his PC. The exact incident cause is **un-pinned and I won't pretend otherwise** — "no banner + a fresh tab fixed it" most fits a STALE loaded build (an old tab from before B455/B458/B459/B460 + this batch deployed), whose recurrence is self-resolved by the now-deployed fixes on reload; a silent token lapse is ruled out (a real SIGNED_OUT bounces to the map, a 401 shows the red banner — neither matches "still in the plan, nothing obvious"). Rather than build a speculative banner for a cause that doesn't match the symptoms, this closes the two real gaps + makes the next occurrence precisely diagnosable:
- **B466's take-over only reached SAME-browser tabs (Web Locks are per-browser).** A plan open in another SESSION/DEVICE blocks saving via the version-conflict path (B314 CAS), which only had a passive "Reload" button. `takeOverEditing` now handles BOTH: same-browser → steal the Web Lock + push in place; cross-session/device conflict → flush to the device mirror then reload, whose boot UNION-merges (this device ∪ the other session — nothing lost, B453) and resumes saving at the fresh version. The conflict banner now reads "your changes **aren't reaching the cloud** … **Take over editing here**" (was "Reload"), so there is ONE consistent take-over for every blocked-save reason.
- **Auth transitions are now traced** — `reportClientEvent("auth-signed-in"/"auth-signed-out")` in `SitePlannerApp.applyUser` (only on a real change; the same-user re-emit returns early). The cloud-save path is gated on being signed in, so a silent session change was previously invisible to telemetry; now a "saving stopped after my session changed" report is diagnosable after the fact via `window.pfTelemetry.recent()` / `public.client_errors`.
- **Honest limit (deferred, not built):** true simultaneous multi-device single-editor locking (forcing a remote PC read-only) needs a cloud editing-lease (heartbeat + realtime) — the deferred per-site-sharing / multi-device territory. An **inaccessible** remote tab is idle and, post-B460, doesn't advance the cloud version, so it can't block this device anyway; the conflict take-over covers the actively-editing-elsewhere case. Work is never lost (device mirror B458 + boot union-merge B453).

### B466 — "Opened in another tab" recovery was broken: reload didn't take the lock; no way to take over or force-save `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug/feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-25 as "NEW-3"; minted **B466**; depends on B464)*
`[x]` **DONE + headless-verified (branch `claude/exciting-wright-yb6ruz`). V (`ui-audit/verify-readonly-takeover.mjs`, 7/7): two tabs of one browser context share Web Locks → tab B goes read-only, "Take over editing here" makes B active AND hands tab A down to read-only via the cross-tab bus.**
- **`editorLock.takeOver()`** (`src/shared/presence/editorLock.js`): STEALS the Web Lock (`{steal:true}`) so this tab is unambiguously the editor even if the other tab is gone or on an older build, THEN broadcasts a `yield` on a BroadcastChannel so the prior holder steps down to read-only cooperatively. Steal-first-then-broadcast so the prior holder's re-request queues behind the steal. Degrades open where Web Locks is unavailable. (+3 unit tests: steal-makes-active, bus hand-off, degrade-open no-op.)
- **`takeOverEditing()` (SitePlanner):** the banner button calls `takeOver`, then flushes the live canvas to the device mirror AND force-pushes to the cloud (`cloudPushWithWatchdog`) — so the pent-up un-synced work reaches the cloud immediately. The B459 thin-clobber + B314 CAS guards still protect that push (a genuine conflict surfaces the loud BLOCKING banner + reload-merge; never a silent overwrite), so takeover-and-push is safe.
- **Reload-recovery premise CORRECTED (flagged):** "work done before reload is lost on reload" is mitigated by B458 — a read-only tab's edits ARE written to the device mirror immediately, so boot's union-merge restores them; the remaining gap (cloud sync) is what takeover closes. The brief's "manual Save now / force flush" is subsumed by "Take over editing here" (the only SAFE way to push from a read-only tab is to first own the lock; the device mirror already keeps the work, so a user is never stranded). The B313 presence banner copy was updated to the single-active-editor reality.

### B467 — Restore's "can be undone" guarantee was unverified; Restore wasn't lock-gated `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-25 as "NEW-4"; minted **B467**)*
`[x]` **DONE + unit-verified (branch `claude/exciting-wright-yb6ruz`). lint 0 · 1528 tests (storage.test.js +3) · build green.** The Version History dialog promises "your current version is backed up too, so a restore can be undone," but that relied on the autosave's shape-DEDUPED snapshot firing after the restore — which can no-op (same collection shape, different content) → restore overwrites current work with no real undo.
- **Fix (`storage.js` + `restoreVersion`):** `snapshotVersion(model, { force })` now **returns whether it persisted** and `force` bypasses the shape-dedup; new `backupNow(id)` force-snapshots the current stored state and returns true only when a backup actually persisted (or there's genuinely nothing at risk — empty/missing record). `restoreVersion` (a) is **lock-gated** — a read-only tab can't Restore (loud message + the takeover way out); (b) flushes the live canvas, then **verifies `backupNow` before replacing** — if the backup can't be written (device storage full) it CANCELS the restore loudly + emits a `restore-backup-failed` telemetry event, rather than destroying current work on a false promise. Fits the verify-it-persisted / no-silent-success discipline.

### B470 — pdf.worker "TT: undefined function" Trusted Types warning — triaged benign `[Document Review / PDF]` (task)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-25 as "NEW-7", low priority; minted **B470**; CLOSED benign)*
`[x]` **CLOSED — triaged benign, no code change (branch `claude/exciting-wright-yb6ruz`).** Confirmed the repo enforces **no** Content-Security-Policy and **no** `require-trusted-types-for` directive anywhere (checked `public/_headers`, `index.html` meta, all `functions/`, `vite.config.js`). So the `TT:` log from `pdf.worker.min.mjs` is pdf.js's own internal Trusted Types feature-PROBE during worker bootstrap (it looks for a TT policy to harden itself; with no enforcing policy it falls back to the normal path) — purely informational, no render impact, matching the owner's "PDF rendering appears to work." Adding a TT policy solely to silence a harmless log would add complexity and risk breaking the worker, so no change is warranted; re-open only if a strict CSP is ever introduced (then pdf.js needs its `pdfjs` policy allow-listed).

### B461 — Right-click context menu for site-plan overlays (Copy / Duplicate / Paste / z-order / Lock / Align to base / Delete) `[Site Planner / overlay]` (feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-25 as "NEW-1"; minted **B461**; surface confirmed by the owner — see below)*
`[x]` **DONE + headless-verified (branch `claude/wizardly-mccarthy-oi8xl7`). lint 0 · 1517 tests · build green · V137 (`ui-audit/verify-b461-b462-overlay-menu.mjs`, 13/13, logged-out).** **Flagged + corrected the premise:** the brief tagged this `[Document Review]` and assumed an "overlay & version-compare surface" there — that surface does **not exist** in Doc Review yet (unbuilt Track-2 item). Rotation is a persisted real-world angle (degrees on the model) so the alignment survives zoom/pan/reload; the base parcel is never mutated. **Guards:** refuses a **locked** overlay with a visible reason; rejects a **degenerate** (too-short) edge rather than applying a NaN rotation; "no parcel to align to" flashes a clear message; one undo step; re-aligning replaces the prior rotation.

The now-orphaned `bumpRot` helper was removed; `spinBtn`/`NumInput` stay (still used elsewhere).

### B460 — Opening/reloading a plan re-pushed it and bumped `version` with no edit → spurious "changed in another session" conflicts `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug, UX)  *(Cowork Phase-B flag #2, 2026-06-25; minted **B460** = highest real B# (B459) + 1)*
`[x]` **DONE + unit-verified (branch `claude/youthful-volta-ns1n75`). lint 0 · 1506 tests (storage.test.js +2 net) · build green.** Data-safe before the fix (B459's CAS + content guard means the re-push can't clobber), but the version churn was firing a benign-but-scary loud "reload to merge" banner in any OTHER open tab/device.
- **Root cause:** `mergePulledSites` `toPush` re-pushed a row when `(local.updatedAt) > cloud.updatedAt` — and B458's immediate per-edit mirror write advances the local `updatedAt` on every edit while the cloud push is debounced/lagging, so EVERY reload re-pushed identical content, bumped `version`, and made other sessions see a (false) conflict.
- **Fix (`storage.js`):** new stable `contentSig(model)` (drawn collections sorted by id + tombstones, as JSON; both sides are `createSiteModel`-normalized so identical content hashes equal). `toPush` now re-pushes ONLY when the row is cloud-absent OR `contentSig(merged) !== contentSig(cloud)` — i.e. the merge actually ADDED/CHANGED/DELETED content. `map[id]` is the union (⊇ cloud) so this never pushes a thinner row; a no-op re-open pushes nothing (no version churn → no spurious conflict). A real add/move/**tombstoned delete** still re-pushes (delete propagation preserved — explicit regression test). Dropped the obsolete `updatedAt >` and `contentCount >` clauses.
- **Live confirm (no spurious conflict on a benign two-tab re-open) → Cowork / VERIFICATION.md V135.**

### B459 — The cloud save guards the version NUMBER but not CONTENT, so a stale/thin tab silently overwrote a fuller cloud row `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug, DATA-LOSS — the actual 8 South 5-building killer)  *(owner pushed back on the 400ms-debounce story 2026-06-25 — "a 400ms gap can't lose 5 buildings I watched save"; he was right; minted **B459** = highest real B# (B458) + 1)*
`[x]` **DONE + unit-verified (branch `claude/youthful-volta-ns1n75`). lint 0 · 1504 tests (cloudThinGuard.test.js +9) · build green.** Owner's skepticism was correct and is the key insight: the 400 ms debounce (B458) can only ever lose the ONE edit in flight — it cannot explain losing 5 buildings placed over minutes and watched save. Losing 5 needs a SECOND failure, which I'd wrongly waved off as "benign" (the Q3 re-push); Cowork independently refused to take it on faith.
- **Root cause (proven by code audit):** the CAS guard (`optimisticUpsert.js` `casUpsert`) is `WHERE id=… AND version=…` — it compares the version SCALAR only, **never the `data` content**. So a tab holding a stale/thin model (e.g. road-only after a bad load / the deploy-crash reload) at a version that still MATCHES the cloud would PATCH right over a fuller cloud row (5 buildings → road-only) and bump the version, badge still "Saved" (it did save — the wrong, thinner copy). There was **no fetch-merge and no content check** anywhere on the write path.
- **Fix (`cloudSync.js`):** alongside `siteVersions` we now remember the **content baseline** we last synced per site — `siteContent` (item count) + `siteTombs` (tombstone count) — populated by `cloudList` (from the cloud row) and advanced on every successful write. New pure `wouldThinClobber(model, baseCount, baseTombs)` blocks a push that would drop **≥2 items the cloud still has with no delete-tombstone to explain it** (`lost = (baseCount − newTombstones) − contentCount(model) ≥ 2`). `cloudUpsert` returns `{ ok:false, conflict:true, thinned:true }` on a hit → the existing **B455 loud + blocking** conflict banner fires; because the write is REFUSED, the cloud stays intact and the next reload union-merges the fuller copy back (no loss). The keepalive forced-reload push (B452) is guarded the same way. Legit incremental **undo** (≤1 unexplained drop/push) and any **tombstoned delete** pass through untouched.
- **Why ≥2, not ≥1:** an undo-of-a-synced-add drops exactly 1 non-tombstoned item — common; the stale-tab clobber drops the whole divergence (5+) in one push. The threshold cleanly separates them; a rare large legit drop trips a recoverable "reload to merge", never silent loss.
- **Closes the loop with B458/B453:** B458 keeps the on-device mirror current; B453 union-merges on boot; **B459 stops the cloud being thinned in the first place.** All three together make the 8 South loss-shape impossible.
- **Live signed-in two-tab / stale-tab clobber repro → Cowork Phase B / VERIFICATION.md V134** (self-tests are logged-out; the clobber path needs auth + the cloud).
- **Follow-up noted:** Document Review's `reviewStore` cloud upsert has the same version-only CAS shape (different content model) — mirror the guard there next (low priority; the owner's loss was a Site Planner plan).

### B458 — Autosave debounced the on-device mirror too, so a reload-within-400ms lost the edit everywhere `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug, DATA-LOSS)  *(follow-up to B452/B453 after Cowork's live Phase-A diagnosis on prod, 2026-06-25; minted **B458** = highest real B# (B457) + 1)*
`[x]` **DONE + headless-verified (branch `claude/youthful-volta-ns1n75`). lint 0 · 1495 tests (storage.test.js +3) · build green · V133 (`ui-audit/verify-immediate-mirror.mjs`, 6/6, logged-out).** This is the REAL structural fix the 8 South building-loss needed — B452 (keepalive on the app's own forced reload) and B453 (boot union-merge, verified correct) were necessary but not sufficient.
- **Root cause (Cowork reproduced on prod, confirmed against the merged code):** the Site Planner autosave (`SitePlanner.jsx` ~L1438) debounced **everything** by 400 ms — the localStorage mirror (`planarfit:sites:cloud:<uid>` / `:v1`) AND the version-history snapshot were both written only inside `setTimeout(saveSite, 400)`. So a reload/crash within 400 ms of an edit lost the building from cloud, the on-device mirror, AND history **at once**, and boot's union-merge (`mergePulledSites`/`mergeSiteContent`, correct per B453) had nothing fuller locally to restore. *Push-abandoned, structural — not a CAS conflict* (matches Cowork's mechanism conclusion; Document Review already split immediate-mirror from debounced-cloud in `usePersistence.js`, so only the Site Planner was the laggard).
- **Fix:** the autosave effect now writes the device mirror **immediately** on every edit, decoupled from the debounced cloud push. `storage.js` `saveSite(partial, { skipHistory })` gained an option; the **immediate** write is a DEFAULT save (history ON — `snapshotVersion` backs up the prior version before overwriting, the B126 thinning safety net, AND makes the rollback snapshot reload-safe), coalesced to ~50 ms so a same-shape drag can't thrash `writeSites` (and `snapshotVersion`'s count-based sig-dedup already skips same-shape frames). The **settle tick** (400 ms) keeps the cloud push and passes `{ skipHistory: true }` so it can't double-snapshot. Conflict/read-only/CAS gates on the cloud push are unchanged; the immediate local write always runs (a local save is always safe — it's the whole recovery net).
- **Flagged correction vs the approved plan:** the plan put `skipHistory` on the immediate write; that would have lost the prior version on a thinning edit (the B126 safety net). Moved history ONTO the immediate write instead — strictly more correct AND makes history reload-safe too. (Unit-test'd: immediate-then-settle backs up the prior version exactly once per shape.)
- **Reconciled Cowork's other audit Qs (no code beyond B458):** Q2 boot does union-merge (it was only moot because the input was debounced away — B458 fixes the input). Q3/Q4 the version-creep-on-open is the benign CAS-guarded boot re-push (`pullCloud` `toPush`) — can't clobber a fuller row; left as-is (tightening it risks under-pushing).
- **Live signed-in cloud round-trip (survive-a-reload with a real cloud row) → Cowork Phase B / VERIFICATION.md V133** (self-tests run logged-out).

### B449 — SPA fallback serves index.html for a missing /assets/* chunk (masks a 404 as a text/html MIME error) `[App Shell / Deploy]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-24 as "NEW-1"; shipped same session per STANDING RULE #1)*
`[x]` **DONE (branch `claude/youthful-volta-ns1n75`). lint 0 · 1468 tests · build green. Live-edge 404 confirmation delegated to Cowork (the sandbox's vite-preview can't reproduce Cloudflare's edge — verified it serves index.html for a missing /assets path, which is exactly the masking bug, but only Cloudflare honors `_redirects`).** Repro: requesting a content-hashed chunk a newer deploy deleted (`/assets/SitePlannerApp-<deadhash>.js`) returns 200 + index.html (text/html) instead of a real 404 → the browser tries to parse HTML as a JS module and dies with "Expected a JavaScript module script … MIME type text/html" / "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module".
- **Root cause:** the Cloudflare Pages project answers unmatched paths with index.html (SPA not-found handling), which catches missing `/assets/*` too. There was no in-repo routing file to stop it.
- **Fix:** added **`public/_redirects`** (copied to `dist/` like `public/_headers`) with **NO** `/* /index.html 200` catch-all — Planyr uses HASH routing (`#/…`, `src/app/route.js`), so every real navigation already lands on a static file and no catch-all is needed. A single rule `/assets/*  /404.html  404` forces a missing chunk to a real 404 (Cloudflare serves real static files BEFORE `_redirects` rules, so it can NEVER 404 a live asset — only a deleted one). Added a tiny dependency-free **`public/404.html`**. Confirmed `_redirects`/`_headers`/`404.html` all emit to `dist/`. The brief's prescribed catch-all was the WRONG fix here (it would *cause* the masking); flagged + corrected.
- **Deduped:** related to B221/B239 (stale-chunk recovery) but distinct — this is the server-side 404 honesty those rely on.

New pure `recoveryStage(arrivedViaFreshReload, now, lastReloadAt)` → `reload | stuck | cooldown`; `installChunkReloadGuard` captures `hasReloadParam(win)` BEFORE `stripReloadParam` tidies it and only auto-reloads on `reload` (so `stuck`/`cooldown` surface to the ErrorBoundary instead of looping — one automatic attempt, then a manual escape). `ErrorBoundary.jsx` shows a distinct **"Planyr is finishing a deploy — try again in a minute"** message whose **Try again** clears the cooldown stamp (`clearReloadGuard`) before reloading. ### B453 — Boot reconciliation must UNION-merge the on-device mirror with the cloud pull `[Persistence]` (bug, DATA-LOSS)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-24 as "NEW-5"; verified same session)*

### B454 — Root-cause: how a building-loss got past the active B314 CAS guard `[Persistence]` (bug, diagnostic)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-24 as "NEW-6"; investigated same session)*
`[x]` **DONE — written root cause + audit (branch `claude/youthful-volta-ns1n75`).** Audited every write to `public.sites` / `public.doc_reviews`:
- **(a) CAS-bypass via a raw `.upsert` — RULED OUT.** The only raw `.upsert` of the `data` column are the degrade fallbacks in `cloudSync.js`/`reviewStore.js`, which fire ONLY when the `version` column is absent (migration ran 2026-06-20, so they don't). `sharing.js` raw updates touch `team_id` only (never `data`). The merge re-push (`pullCloud` `toPush`) and `setProjectStatus` both route through the guarded `cloudUpsert`. No unguarded `data` write exists.
- **Most likely cause = (b) conflict-then-strand during the concurrent deploy.** The fuller (5-building) state existed only in a tab whose every save **conflicted** (a racing/thin tab advanced the version), so the buildings stayed local-only there; meanwhile a thin tab that DID hold the current version won the CAS and wrote the road-only row. The conflict banner was **dismissible and didn't block**, so editing continued, every save re-conflicting. Then the **forced reload** (the chunk-crash incident) landed in a context whose durable local cache was the thin copy, so the boot merge had nothing fuller to union. Secondary possibility: an erroneous `deletedIds` tombstone (the only way `mergeSiteContent`'s union drops a building). `mergeSiteContent` proven to union `els` by id otherwise.
- **Closed by:** **B452** (keepalive cloud push on forced reload) + **B455** (conflict is now loud+blocking, and the Web Locks read-only lockout stops a stale/thin tab winning the CAS over the active one). **B453** is the recovery net. **B456** explains why the snapshots looked unusable (the "0 buildings" label hid recoverable history). Reconcile with Cowork's live two-tab repro before final conclusions; the fixes are correct either way. Regression coverage: the B453 incident-shape test + the B455 `canCloudSave` gate test.

Site Planner's conflict banner lost its dismiss ✕ (blocking) and is reworded ("Saving is paused… Reload to merge"); Doc Review gates the same via the pure `canCloudSave(status, readOnly)`.
- **(2) Web Locks single-active-editor lockout (the deferred half of B313).** New `src/shared/presence/editorLock.js` (`createEditorLock` + pure `lockRole`): only ONE tab holds the editor lock per project; a second tab on the same plan/review goes **read-only** and can't push over the active one — the direct structural fix for the stale-tab clobber. Degrades OPEN where Web Locks is unavailable; hands off automatically when the active tab closes. Site Planner shows a read-only banner; both gate the cloud push (+ keepalive) on `readOnly`.
