### B445 — Site-plan overlay drop target has no affordance + the panel isn't a dropzone `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-24 via screenshot as "this does not allow anything to actually be dropped in, should work like enterprise software"; minted **B445** = highest real B# across both files (B444) + 1)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B445 also names 2 other items in this file:** “GIS layer imagery caching, server-side (Drive-backed, cross-device) — SHIPPED *(2026-06…” · “GIS layer imagery caching, server-side (Drive-backed, cross-device) (feature) — roadmap…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B445* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B445 against all of them.
`[x]` **Fixed + shipped (branch `claude/hopeful-turing-1x24sg`). lint 0 errors · 1425 tests · build green · headless V131 (`ui-audit/verify-overlay-dnd.mjs`, 7/7).**
- **Repro (owner):** Site Planner → open the "Site-plan overlay" panel → its copy says "Drop a site-plan PDF onto the map (or browse)", but dragging a file over the panel gives **zero feedback** and releasing it does nothing (or the browser opens the PDF in a new tab) → reads as broken / "doesn't allow anything to be dropped in."
- **Root cause (confirmed in code):** the canvas wrapper (`wrapRef`, `SitePlanner.jsx`) already HAD a working `onDragOver`/`onDrop` → `addOverlayFile`, but (1) there was **no drag-hover affordance** so the live zone looked dead, and (2) the **left panel itself** (where the cursor goes — the "Add site plan…" button + copy live there) had **no drop handlers**, so a release there hit the browser default. On narrow screens the panel is `position:absolute; zIndex:1100`, outside the `wrapRef` subtree, so its drops could never reach the canvas handler.
- **Fix (`SitePlanner.jsx`), reusing the existing ingestion path (`addOverlayFile` → `openOverlayFile`/`uploadOverlayFile`) + the Doc-Review `FileBrowser` dropzone pattern:**
  1. **Panel is now a real dropzone** — the overlay `Section`'s button + copy are wrapped in a dashed-border `<div>` that highlights on hover (accent border + `PAL.accentSoft` bg, anti-flicker via `e.currentTarget === e.target`), routes drop → `addOverlayFile`, and shows "Drop to add this site plan" while dragging. The button stays the click-to-browse path.
  2. **Canvas "drop to place" hint** — a full-bleed dashed overlay (`pointerEvents:none`, above the SVG's `zIndex:1`) mounts only during an active file drag, with a centered "Drop site plan to place it on the map" pill.
  3. **Window-level guard** — a `useEffect` blocks the browser's default file-drop everywhere (`dragover`/`drop` preventDefault when the drag carries Files), so releasing a few pixels off-target no longer navigates away / opens the PDF (the core "nothing happens / data loss" feeling).
- **Edge cases:** multi-file drop takes the first file + `flashWarn`s ("one overlay placed at a time"); panel `onDrop` `stopPropagation`s so it can't double-fire to the canvas; all new colors use the existing `PAL` theme tokens (no raw hex), keeping WCAG AA.
- **Deduped:** distinct from the Doc-Review file-drop dropzones (`ProjectFilesDrawer`/`FileBrowser`) — this is the Site Planner *site-plan overlay*, a separate surface; the pattern was reused, not the component.

### B446 — Dropping/opening a file gives no clear signal it registered `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-24 as "NEW-1"; fixed same session per STANDING RULE #1)*
`[x]` **DONE + verified (branch `claude/vibrant-pascal-wkg50i`). lint 0 · 1434 tests · build green · headless V131 (`ui-audit/verify-open-feedback.mjs`, 6/6, logged out).** Owner repro: drop a PDF (especially with a doc already open, or open from the Files panel) → no immediate, unmistakable sign anything is happening; it can look like nothing registered ("silence is a crash").
- **Root cause:** `setBusy(true)` existed but the only "Opening…" text rendered in the EMPTY state. The B294 drop-over-open path and the `openReview`/Files-panel/`loadSingleReview` paths render no empty state, so they showed no loading signal at all; a non-PDF reject set `err`, which the canvas never displays, and a null drop / `loadReview→null` could no-op silently.
- **Fix:** a canvas-level **"Opening &lt;name&gt;…" overlay** (`data-testid="opening-overlay"`, spinner + filename, reuses the `spin` keyframe) driven by `busy`, rendered in BOTH the empty-state and the canvas branches (so it covers the prior sheet on a drop-over-open). `busy`/`busyLabel` are now set on EVERY entry path — `openFile`, `openReview`, `loadSingleReview` — and cleared in token-guarded `finally`s so a rapid switch can't let an older load's finally hide the newer overlay. **Silence-is-a-crash:** `openFile` surfaces a null drop + a non-PDF reject + a read failure on the always-visible `openErr` banner (role="alert") AND the inline `err`; `openReview` surfaces a missing-row and a `loadReview→null`. A superseded (older) load stays intentionally silent — the newer load owns the feedback.
- **Deduped:** a GAP in **B294** (which only wired the drop *handler*, not feedback) + the **B405/docIntent** open paths — not a duplicate of any.

### B447 — Switching between files is flaky and "forgets which file I was on" `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-24 as "NEW-2"; fixed same session)*
`[x]` **DONE (branch `claude/vibrant-pascal-wkg50i`). Code complete + logged-out paths verified V131; the auth-only switch-determinism check (two saved cloud reviews) logged for a signed-in live pass in VERIFICATION.md V131.** Owner repro: open A, switch to B, switch back to A → A's backdrop/markups/calibration/view/breadcrumb don't reliably return; clicking the file list feels like it drops the doc you were on.
- **Root cause (the clobber):** the debounced autosave's pending cloud write is cancelled the instant a switch changes the persistence `deps` (the effect cleanup clears the timer), so the outgoing review's last edit lived ONLY in the synchronous localStorage mirror. `openReview` then loaded the **stale cloud copy** by id and never reconciled with that mirror — so switching back overwrote the newer local state with the older cloud one.
- **Fix:** `openReview` now (1) `await saveNow()` to **flush the outgoing review's pending write** before the incoming load begins, and (2) loads the incoming via `reconcile(await loadReview(id), readDraft(uid, id))` so it picks up that file's newer local mirror if the cloud is behind — exactly the pattern the resume-on-mount path already uses. The lazy-mount **resume effect was confirmed to already stand down** for an in-workspace switch (its `booted`-once guard + `projectId` early-return + `bootDocIntentRef` mean it never races an explicit `openReview`), matching the cross-workspace docIntent contract the brief asked to mirror.
- **Depends on B448** (the in-memory bytes cache) so a switch-back is reliable even while the file's first upload is still in flight.
- **Deduped:** a GAP/regression of **B52** (the load-supersede token, intact) + the resume/docIntent fix — not a duplicate.

### B448 — Backdrop vanishes on switch/reload while a fresh drop's upload is still in flight `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-24 as "NEW-3"; fixed same session)*
`[x]` **DONE (branch `claude/vibrant-pascal-wkg50i`). New pure `lib/sessionBytes.js` + 5 unit tests (1434 total); logged-out render-from-cache verified V131; the keyless-mid-upload signed-in confirm logged V131.** Owner repro: drop a PDF, then immediately switch files (or reload) before the Drive/Supabase upload resolves → the source is still **keyless** (no storageKey/driveKey), so the backdrop can't be re-fetched and you land on the re-drop banner / a blank canvas with orphaned markups.
- **Fix:** a session-lifetime **byte cache** (`sessionBytes`, module-scoped Map keyed by `srcId`, capped FIFO at 8) holds the dropped **File** (never a raw ArrayBuffer — pdf.js transfers a buffer to its worker and detaches it; a File re-reads cleanly). `openFile` caches the bytes the moment a srcId is minted; `fetchSourceBytes` checks the cache **before** `classifySource`/Drive/Supabase, so a dropped backdrop stays viewable for the rest of the session regardless of upload state. Survives the lazy DocReview workspace unmounting/remounting (a tab switch mid-upload). Only when the bytes are truly absent does the precise B405 re-drop banner show.
- **Deduped:** net-new — the safety net that makes B447's switch-back reliable mid-upload; complements (does not replace) B405's source-state taxonomy.

### B442 — Merge/Clear banner buttons unclickable; canvas grab-cursor + pan bleeds through `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-24 via screenshot+voice as "NEW-1"; minted **B442** = highest real B# across both files (B441) + 1)*
`[x]` **Fixed + shipped (branch `claude/gallant-euler-sk8kwd`). lint 0 errors · 1421 tests · build green · headless V (`ui-audit/verify-merge-banner.mjs`, 6/6).**
- **Repro (owner):** Select tool → Shift-click 2+ parcels → the floating "N parcels selected · Merge parcels ⏎ · Clear" banner appears → hovering Clear showed the canvas **grab hand** (not a pointer), and clicking it **panned the map** instead of clearing the selection; Merge was likewise dead.
- **Root cause (confirmed in code):** the banner is a sibling of the SVG canvas under `wrapRef`, and the SVG carries `zIndex:1` while the banner had **no z-index** (auto). A positioned `zIndex:1` paints *over* an auto sibling, so the transparent canvas sat on top of the banner — it swallowed the clicks and showed its own `cursor:grab`. The buttons' own `cursor:pointer` never won because the press never reached them.
- **Fix (`SitePlanner.jsx`, merge-banner block ~L6871):** gave the banner an explicit **`zIndex:6`** (clears the SVG's `1`, below the slide-in tool rail) so its buttons are the topmost element — clicks land, the pointer cursor applies, Clear runs `setCombineSel([])`, Merge runs `mergeParcels()`, neither starts a pan. Added defensive `onPointerDown`/`onMouseDown` `stopPropagation` on the banner container (belt-and-suspenders for any future reparenting under a pointer-handling ancestor — the z-index is the actual fix). Applied the **identical guard to the sibling parcel-edge easement banner** (`tool==="easement" && easeMode==="parceledge"`), which had the same latent bug.
- **Dedup:** NOT **B271** (that fixed interrupted-gesture recovery via pointercancel/blur — a stuck-capture *recovery* path); this was a plain missing z-index on a normal press. NOT **B441** (that was MapFinder county-map identify *latency*; this is the planner's banner stacking). Cross-referenced both.

### B443 — Shift-click parcel multi-select unreliable / "needs several tries" `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-24 as "NEW-2"; minted **B443**)*
`[x]` **Fixed + shipped (branch `claude/gallant-euler-sk8kwd`). Headless-verified: 4 interior shift-clicks → "4 parcels selected" on the first try (`ui-audit/verify-merge-banner.mjs`).**
- **Repro (owner):** with the Select tool, Shift-clicking parcels to add them to the merge selection often didn't register — it took several clicks.
- **Root cause (confirmed in code — broader than first hypothesized):** **B420** makes a parcel's *interior* click-through — only its ~12px boundary hit-stroke grabs the press. So a Shift-click on the parcel **body** misses the parcel and falls through to the canvas background handler `onBgDown`, whose `tool==="select" && e.shiftKey` branch started a **marquee select** (not a merge-toggle). The pick only registered when the click happened to land on the thin boundary line → the "click a couple times" feel. (Secondary, rarer: when a parcel is *unlocked + selected*, the capture-phase vertex-insert `onCanvasVtxDownCapture` could steal a Shift-click meant to merge a neighbor sharing that edge.)
- **Fix (`SitePlanner.jsx`):**
  - `onBgDown` select+shift branch (~L1990): before starting a marquee, ray-cast (`pointInRing`) the press against the parcels; if it lands inside one, `toggleMerge(hit.id)` + select it and return. Topmost (last-drawn) parcel wins, matching the boundary-stroke path. Gated on `settings.parcelSelect` (respects the "Select parcels: off" browse mode). Marquee still works on genuinely empty canvas.
  - `onCanvasVtxDownCapture` (~L2508): the Shift+edge vertex-insert now yields when the press is inside *another* parcel's body — that's a merge-pick on a neighbor, not an edit of the selected path — letting it fall through to the merge-toggle.
- **Verified after B442** (a residual stuck pointer-capture from the banner bug could have masked this) on a clean canvas.

### B441 — Parcel selection feels laggy: paint the highlight optimistically on click, confirm via identify in the background `[Site Planner / map]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-24 from a ChatGPT thread as "NEW-1"; minted **B441** = highest real B# across both files (B440) + 1)*
`[x]` **Built + shipped (branch `claude/hopeful-brown-q7q4jo`). lint 0 errors · 1421 tests · build green.**
- **Repro (owner):** clicking a lot on the live county map took a variable delay — sometimes a couple seconds — between the click and the parcel highlighting. Root cause (confirmed in code): `MapFinder.handleClick` did `setBusy(true)` then `await identifyParcelEager(...)` — a network identify against the county ArcGIS REST service(s) — and only painted the highlight + pushed the selection AFTER that promise resolved. The variable multi-second lag was county-server round-trip latency, not client compute.
- **Fix — optimistic local highlight, then reconcile (no network on the felt path):**
  - The county parcel outlines are already drawn client-side as esri-leaflet vector `featureLayer`s (`makeParcelLayer`). New `optimisticHitAt(latlng)` hit-tests those already-loaded features (cheap `getBounds().contains` reject → ray-cast on the outer rings) and returns a hit shaped like an identify hit. New pure `geoJsonToEsriFeature` (arcgis.js) converts the display layer's GeoJSON polygon into the same esri-shaped `{geometry:{rings},attributes}` the highlight/select path already consumes — so the on-screen outline feeds the **exact same** `addParcelHit` pipeline (one source of truth, B233/B22 keys intact). Prefers a real county over the statewide TxGIO backup (mirrors identify's source priority), then the tighter parcel when several overlap.
  - `handleClick` now paints the optimistic highlight **synchronously, before** the identify starts → the click feels instant. The `await identifyParcelEager(...)` still runs in the background as the authoritative confirm (still feeds the circuit breaker via `onSettled` → `recordSourceResult`, B244 unchanged). On return it **always rolls back the optimistic outline and rebuilds from the identified geometry** (full-res + real account/address attrs), so the IMPORTED parcel is never the simplified display outline. No flash — the remove+re-add happen in one synchronous turn after the await.
  - **Reconcile cases:** identify confirms the same parcel → seamless real-geometry swap; identify returns a different/refined parcel (multipart per B36c, or a statewide-backup relabel) → optimistic rolled back, authoritative added (multipart still highlights every tract); identify finds nothing / errors → optimistic highlight **visibly rolled back** + the existing "No parcel right there" / "server isn't responding" message (B245 wording preserved).
  - **Instant local toggle-off:** new `selectedHitAt(latlng)` — a click inside an already-highlighted parcel now deselects it with **zero** network round-trip (we already have its geometry).
- **Edge cases handled:** display layer zoom-gated (`PARCEL_MINZOOM` 14) → when nothing's loaded under the click, `optimisticHitAt` returns null and we fall back to the original await-identify-with-busy behavior (never fabricate a highlight from nothing). Optimistic add only fires when the parcel isn't already highlighted, so a rollback can never strip a pre-existing selection. `selectParcelAt` (address-search select, B233) shares the same reconcile pipeline; the optimistic step is click-only (an address select already runs after a `flyTo`, so there's no felt lag there).
- **Tests:** +3 unit tests for `geoJsonToEsriFeature` (Polygon flatten + attrs, MultiPolygon flatten, null/non-polygon) round-tripping through `outerRingsLngLat` (test/arcgis.test.js, 19 in that file). lint 0 errors · full suite 1421 green · build green.

### B429 — New tools: Arc, Dimension, Pen, Highlight, Eraser, Snapshot `[Doc Review / Markup]` (feature) — NEW-6, part of the B423 umbrella  *(2026-06-24)*
`[x]` **Built + shipped (branch `claude/determined-shannon-p7unj4`). lint 0 · 1390 tests · build green. ⏳ signed-in draw round-trip → V125.**
- **6 new tools** added to DocReview tool rail and wired end-to-end:
  - **Arc** (`multiPoint`): click start → click end → click a point on the curve; auto-commits on 3rd `onDown`. Renders as a quadratic Bézier (`Q ctrl`) where ctrl = 2·p3 − (p1+p2)/2. Live preview during first two points.
  - **Dimension** (`twoPoint`): drag end-to-end; renders line + two perpendicular witness ticks (±7 px) + a centred calibrated length label. Added to `MEASURE_KINDS` in MarkupRenderer so it gets the label from `measureLabel`.
  - **Pen** (`freehand`): pointer-capture press-drag; accumulates pts on `onMove`, commits on `onUp` (min 2 pts). Renders as a stroked open polyline.
  - **Highlight** (`freehand`): identical gesture to Pen. `TOOL_DEFAULTS` forces `stroke:#fbbf24`, `strokeWidth:12`, `opacity:0.35` (clamped to ≤0.5 in renderer so it stays translucent even if the user overrides).
  - **Eraser** (`region`): drag a rubber-band box; `eraseInBox` removes any `pen`/`highlight` markup whose pts intersect the box — never touches other kinds. Hit-test treated as rect-interior so a partly-drawn eraser box shows a live rectangle.
  - **Snapshot** (`region`): drag a box; commits a `snapshot` markup. Renders as a dashed rect + a camera emoji at the centroid.
- **Arrow** = arrowhead toggle on Line (already in `arrowStart`/`arrowEnd` property column via B428 matrix — no standalone rail button needed per locked owner decision).

- **`TOOL_DEFAULTS`** map provides per-tool style overrides between `propStyle` (user sticky) and column defaults; currently used for Highlight.

### B421 — Markup z-order ("Arrange"): Bring to Front / Forward / Send Backward / to Back via Bluebeam shortcuts + a right-click menu `[Doc Review / Markup]` (feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-23 as "NEW-1"; minted **B421** = highest B# across both files (B420) + 1; deduped net-new)*
`[x]` **Filed AND built + verified + shipped to main the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/gallant-turing-mcempv`). lint 0 · 1335 tests · build green; headless `ui-audit/verify-b421-arrange.mjs` 17/17 (V122).**
- **What:** when two markups overlap on a sheet, control which draws on top — Bluebeam's four Arrange ops on the selected markup (Bring to Front, Bring Forward, Send Backward, Send to Back), reachable two ways from ONE shared core: keyboard chords and a new right-click context menu. Net-new — there was no z-order control before.
- **Core (one engine, both entry points):** new pure module `src/workspaces/doc-review/lib/arrange.js`. `reorderWithinPage(markups, id, mode)` permutes the selected markup within its **same-page** siblings (draw order IS z-order — the overlay paints `pageMarks` in array order, so the last same-page entry is on top), then splices the reordered group back into the global array **without disturbing other sheets' markups** (they keep their absolute slots, so an arrange never silently shuffles another sheet's stack). Returns the SAME array reference on a no-op (already at that end / a lone markup / unknown mode) so a top/bottom arrange skips the history push + state write. `arrangeFlags(markups, id)` reports `{page, count, index, atTop, atBottom}` for the greying. `DocReview.arrange(mode)` wraps it with `pushHistory()` so every arrange is one undoable step (B303) and persists for free (markups are already saved/mirrored).
- **Keyboard:** the existing `onKeyRef` handler gains an arrange branch **before** the `if (mod) return` early-out (which previously handed every other modified key back to the browser, so a branch after it would never fire). Gated on `mod && sel`; matches **`e.code`** (`BracketRight`/`BracketLeft`), NOT `e.key` — Shift turns `e.key` `]`→`}`, which would silently miss the Bring-to-Front chord. ⌘ works via the existing `e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey`; the INPUT/TEXTAREA guard already blocks firing mid-text-edit. `]`=up / `[`=down, Shift=jump to the end: `⌘/Ctrl+]` Forward · `⌘/Ctrl+Shift+]` Front · `⌘/Ctrl+[` Backward · `⌘/Ctrl+Shift+[` Back.
- **Right-click menu:** new `onContextMenu` on the viewport runs the existing `hitTest` (B33) at the cursor — a hit selects that markup and opens the menu at the cursor; a **miss** does nothing (no `preventDefault`, so the native browser menu shows over blank canvas — never an empty custom menu). The menu is **portalled to `<body>`** (`createPortal`, the same escape-the-clip pattern as `AnchoredMenu`/the Site-row context menu) so the canvas's `overflow:hidden` + stacking can't clip it; cursor-positioned + viewport-clamped; dismissed on click-away / right-click-away / **Escape**. Items: the four Arrange ops (with platform-aware shortcut hints), a divider, then **Edit text…** (text notes only, reuses the B293 inline editor) and **Delete** (reuses the existing `pushHistory` + filter-by-id). Arrange items **grey out** at the top (Front/Forward) / bottom (Back/Backward) of the stack; a lone markup disables all four. Not opened while an inline editor / calibrate entry is active.
- **Scope / parity:** built in `DocReview.jsx` (the single-sheet markup surface). **Skipped `Stitcher.jsx` deliberately** — it renders only `measures` (distance/area), with no overlapping fillable markups (rect/cloud/text), so an Arrange menu there would be empty/no-op. Toolbar buttons for Arrange are out of scope (shortcuts + right-click only) — an easy follow-up.
- **Tests:** `test/arrange.test.js` — **14 unit tests** (all four ops; single-step Forward/Backward are inverses; SAME-reference no-ops at the ends / lone markup / unknown id / unknown mode; other-sheet slots preserved through an interleaved-page reorder; input not mutated). ### B420 — Parcel grabs only by its boundary/setback, not its interior (free the interior for building work) `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-23 as "NEW-1", live; minted **B420** = highest real B# across both files (B419) + 1 — B416–B419 were taken by concurrent PRs #313/#314/#316 while this was in flight; branch/commits/code tags first read B417, renamed on the merge-in of main)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + headless-verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/vigilant-cerf-6rvxga`). lint 0 · 1320 tests · build green; new regression harness 7/7.**
- **Repro (owner, live):** in Select mode, clicking anywhere inside a lot's interior selected the parcel and popped the parcel menu — even when you were trying to edit a building/element sitting in that lot; a press in the open interior near (but not on) a footprint grabbed the parcel. **Expected:** a parcel is grabbable only by its boundary edge or its setback line; the interior is click-through (presses fall to whatever element is painted on top, else the background pan — exactly as on empty canvas). Appearance unchanged; hit-area change only.
- **Root cause (code-confirmed):** the visible parcel `<polygon>` (`SitePlanner.jsx`, parcels render block) carried `pointerEvents="all"`, so the whole fill was a hit target even when `fill:"none"`; both `startMoveParcel` and `onContextMenu` → `setParcelMenu` fired from any interior point.
- **Fix — boundary-only hit model:** the visible polygon is now `pointerEvents="none"` (its fill never captures, even when a translucent fill is toggled on — boundary-grab stays consistent regardless of fill state; deliberately NOT `"painted"`, which would re-arm the interior whenever a fill is set). A companion transparent **fat hit-stroke** on the same ring (`stroke="rgba(0,0,0,0.001)"`, `strokeWidth={12}`, `pointerEvents="stroke"`) carries `startMoveParcel` + the context menu — reusing the B146 easement-edge fat-stroke technique. ~12 px is **zoom-independent** because `f2p` (`worldToScreen`) already projects feet→screen pixels, so the polygon is drawn in pixel space (the existing easement-edge picker uses the same flat `12`; no division by zoom needed). The **setback outline** gets the same fat hit-stroke for active parcels (owner explicitly wanted "boundary OR setback"); a shared `onParcelContext(e,id)` opens the parcel menu from either grab target.
- **Preserved (re-verified, no regression):** B310 click-vs-drag + B311 "Select parcels" toggle (both keyed on `startMoveParcel`, which now fires from the boundary instead of the fill), Shift-click-to-merge (`toggleMerge`), align-edge picking (`alignToParcelEdge`), unlocked-parcel drag-to-move, and B230 shared vertex editing (it hit-tests at the svg root via `editablePath`/`hitEditPath`, independent of the fill, so vertex handles + insert/delete are untouched). The B311 tooltip was reworded "click a lot" → "click a lot's edge or setback line" (label only, no logic change).
- **Distinct from B155/B156 (the inverse, not a contradiction):** those make small markup-shape *interiors* grabbable (correct for annotations). A parcel is a *container*, so boundary-grab is the right inverse. **Layers on B310/B311**, does not replace them.
- **Verified (V121):** new `ui-audit/verify-b420-parcel-boundary-grab.mjs` **7/7** — interior click does NOT select, boundary click selects, setback-line click selects, right-click parity (interior opens no menu, boundary opens it), no page JS errors. Repointed `verify-b310-b311` / `verify-edge-runs` / `verify-edge-runs-irregular` off the now-dead interior-click / `pointer-events="all"` selectors → all green; `verify-b221-b222` (a pond element on a parcel still selects + its vertices insert/delete 4→5→4→3), `verify-parcel-split-control`, `verify-b383-add-parcel`, `verify-parcel-resilience` all still pass.
- **Deduped:** net-new. NOT B155/B156 (markup interiors — the inverse), NOT B310/B311 (gesture/toggle — preserved), NOT B146 (reuses its technique), NOT B213 (inactive parcels already draw no setback line).

### B414 — Doc Review (Library) sheet flashes white on zoom-settle — double-buffer the re-raster `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-23 as "NEW-1"; first filed as B412, but a concurrent `main` (PR #311) took B412/B413, so **renumbered B414** = the next free ID)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/confident-edison-lpbco9`). 1273 tests · lint 0 · build green; headless-verified.**
- **Repro:** open a sheet in the Library/Markup canvas, zoom in/out; ~140 ms after the gesture settled the sheet flashed blank/white before the sharp render appeared (Bluebeam never flashes on the same file).
- **Root cause (code-confirmed):** the single visible canvas was re-rastered on every zoom settle; reassigning `canvas.width/height` clears it to transparent, revealing the white page-box `<div>` (`background:"#fff"`) behind it, and the `page.render()` that refills it is async (pdf.js worker) → a visible blank gap each settle.
- **Fix:** `pdf.js` `renderInto` now rasterises into an OFF-SCREEN canvas and blits the finished frame onto the visible canvas (`drawImage`) in one synchronous step — the compositor never sees the cleared canvas. It bails on `isStale()` so a superseded render never blits a stale frame (B40 guard kept; off-screen also sidesteps the same-canvas throw). The biggest contributor in practice is B415's backdrop (the whole-page layer no longer re-rasters on zoom at all), but the double-buffer makes EVERY swap (page change + the detail settle) flash-free.
- **Verified:** `ui-audit/verify-b414-b415-render.mjs` D1 (backdrop backing dims unchanged across a zoom → can't blank) + D3 (detail layer polled through a settle, never caught blank — min opaque centre pixels > 0). Foundation for B415.

### B415 — Doc Review (Library) render is softer than Bluebeam on large sheets — viewport-clipped two-layer rendering `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-23 as "NEW-2"; first filed as B413, renumbered past main's B412/B413 (PR #311) to **B415**; depends on B414)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/confident-edison-lpbco9`). 1273 tests · lint 0 · build green; headless-verified.** Net-new architectural item that **supersedes the whole-page raster path B247/B265/B327/B329** (extends that path, does not fork a second renderer).
- **Repro:** Planyr's linework/text was visibly softer than Bluebeam side-by-side, most pronounced on large (E-size) civil sheets and when zoomed in.
- **Root cause:** the viewer rasterised the ENTIRE page into one canvas at a single density; the ~24 MP backing-store budget (`renderBudget.backingScale`, B327/B247) was spent across the whole sheet, so on a big sheet density dropped below full (even <1×) everywhere to stay under budget — even though only a small window is visible. Bluebeam rasters only the visible region at full resolution.
- **Fix (two-layer, additive over B414; the page-box + SVG-overlay CSS model is byte-for-byte unchanged, so markup/zoom-anchor geometry is untouched):**
  - **Backdrop** — the whole page at a FIXED, zoom-independent density (`backdropDensity`, ~8 MP budget) painted once per page, filling the page box. It never re-rasters on zoom (so it can't flash white) and is always present as a no-white floor.
  - **Detail** — only the visible page-rect (+ a 25% margin) at full device dpr (cap 2), budget-bounded on the REGION not the page (reuses `backingScale` on the region size), re-rastered on pan/zoom settle (double-buffered via B414) and positioned over the backdrop. Because the detail backing store is ~viewport-sized, the budget stops forcing low density → on-screen resolution stays native at any sheet size/zoom.
  - Pure region/density math (`visibleRegion`, `tileCovers`, `backdropDensity`, `BACKDROP_PX_BUDGET`) in `renderBudget.js` (+13 unit tests in `test/renderBudget.test.js`); region render path (`renderInto` with a `transform` offset + canvas-clip) in `pdf.js`; two-canvas viewport + settle-driven `renderBackdrop`/`renderDetail` in `DocReview.jsx`. The B40 race guard + B39 destroy are kept; the imported drawing stays a display-only backdrop.
- **Verified (`ui-audit/verify-b414-b415-render.mjs`, 11/11, E-size sheet @ deviceScaleFactor 2):** zoomed to 2.6×, the **detail layer renders at 2.00× native device density** while the OLD whole-page raster would be **0.95× at the same zoom → 2.11× sharper**; backdrop fills the page box and stays opaque through the zoom; markup overlay still draws. Regression: the B329 viewport harness (`verify-markup-viewport.mjs`) still 13/13 (pan / cursor-anchored zoom / calibration survival / measurement geometry / sheet-switch), plus `verify-docreview-viewer` 13/13 and `verify-delete-markup` 10/10.

### B207 — Google Drive storage backend behind the adapter — LIVE & DEPLOYED `[Server]` (feature)  *(arrived as "NEW-2"; provisionally B204, renumbered **B207** — `main` took B203–B205; closed out 2026-06-23)*

### B405 — Files browser: opening a file failed with one conflated/silent banner — split into a precise taxonomy `[Document Review]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-23 as "NEW-2"; minted **B405** — renumbered from a provisional B402 that a concurrent `main` (#297) took for a Scheduler item; folds in the standalone "oversize banner copy" item)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + unit-verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/brave-brown-jb1n2l`).**
- **Grounded against the real repo FIRST (the brief was written blind).** The corrected open path is `FileBrowser.open(f)` → `onOpenReview(row)` → `openReview` → `loadReview(row.id)` (re-fetches the FULL Postgres record by id) → `loadSingleReview` → `fetchSourceBytes`. So the brief's "the Files-browser reshape drops storageKey/driveKey" hypothesis does **NOT** hold at the open hop — the lightweight browser row is never the `src`; the full record (with `data.sources[]` carrying the keys) is re-fetched. Confirmed and flagged rather than rebuilding the (working) upload path.
- **Real defect = the read failure was ONE bucket, and one case was SILENT.** `fetchSourceBytes` returned silently on a missing source (`if (!src) return` → a blank canvas, no banner) and collapsed every other cause into a single `"Couldn't fetch …"`, so oversize / never-stored / stored-but-unreachable / signed-out all read identically (and the oversize copy said "was too large to store in the cloud", which would go stale once B207's Drive cutover lifts the cap).
- **Fix — one taxonomy, four hard-distinct states** (`src/workspaces/doc-review/lib/sourceState.js`, new · pure · **15 unit tests** `test/sourceState.test.js`): `classifySource` + `sourceUnavailableMessage` + `fileWarn`. States: **oversize** (names the 50 MB per-file cloud limit — durable, never "coming soon") · **not-stored** (a source record with no key → re-open to UPLOAD; this is the old silent path, now surfaced) · **fetch-failed** (had a key but bytes didn't come back → transient/retryable "couldn't load just now") · **signed-out** (sign in to view). `DocReview.fetchSourceBytes` classifies pre-download and, after a keyed download returns nothing, distinguishes fetch-failed vs signed-out; every line ends "(your markups are saved)".
- **"Re-open it" already uploads-and-rebinds (verified by reading the path, no change needed):** the banner's "Re-open file…" → `openFile` reuses the srcId on a same-name re-drop and never changes `reviewId`, so markups stay bound to the same document id (no orphaning), `storeSource` re-uploads, and `buildSnapshot` persists the new key.
- **One vocabulary across surfaces:** `FileBrowser` + `ProjectFilesDrawer` queue warns now call the shared `fileWarn` (was three drifting copies).
- **Live caveat (the brief's own note):** the universal "every file fails" symptom is a LIVE storage/auth class the logged-out sandbox can't reproduce (most likely the `doc-review-files` Storage bucket/RLS not provisioned, or legacy keyless rows) — the code fix makes whatever the live cause is **name itself** precisely + offer a working recovery; a signed-in pass on the deployed site (cohort/owner) confirms the render. lint 0 errors · 1228 tests · build green · `DocReview` lazy chunk intact.

### B390 — PDF/Print Exhibit table columns mis-sized: oversized Task-Name gap + truncated Start/End/Duration `[Scheduler]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped from chat as "NEW-1" 2026-06-22; filed B385, **renumbered B390** — concurrent `main` (PRs #290/#291/#292) took B385–B389 while this batch was in flight, so B390–B392 are the real next free IDs)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + headless-verified (V113, 10/10) + merged via PR #293 the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/practical-edison-ggcm1k`).** Three symptoms, **one** cause: in the split-view (table + Gantt) exhibit the columns were sized by **fixed widths, not fitted to content** — a large dead band between TASK NAME and START, Start/End rendering clipped (`06/2…`, `09/0…`), and DUR clipped (`1…`, `4…`).
- **Root cause:** the split table used `table-layout:fixed` at a hardcoded ~50%-of-page width, with fixed per-column px from `COL_DEFS` and the **Task-Name column at `w:null`** — so Name absorbed ALL the leftover width (the giant gap) while the fixed **42px** Start/End and **28px** Duration columns were too narrow for `MM/DD/YY` / multi-digit durations and clipped via `overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis`.
- **Fix — content-fit width model.** New pure, DOM-free module-scope helpers (above `buildPDFHtml`, so preview + print + tests agree): `approxTextPx(str,fs)` approximates rendered width from per-character advances for the exhibit's Inter face (deliberately generous so a fixed-format value never clips); `layoutExhibitCols(specs,opts)` lays columns out from their content-fit base, lets a user drag-override win, clamps each to `[min,max]`, makes the **table block exactly its columns' total**, and gives the Gantt the rest — never below `EXHIBIT_MIN_GANTT` (240px), shrinking the **flexible** columns (name/owner/predecessors/cost) toward their min, then a uniform scale, only if the columns would crowd the chart. `buildPDFHtml` measures each visible column's widest value across **all** selected projects (the exhibit stacks them under one shared header) via a plain-text `cellText` + a `COL_FIT` profile (font px, clamp range, flex flag, the Status dot+gap extra), then sizes the split from the result.
- **Per the brief:** the short fixed-format columns (Start/End/Duration/%/Status) are **NOT flexible** — a date is never the value that gets clipped to make room; only Name/Owner/Predecessors/Cost cap + ellipsize. **Respects the column on/off checkboxes** (only the turned-on `colDefs` are measured/sized). Tables-only mode (no Gantt) is **untouched** — its auto-layout already content-fits, so the bug was split-only; the fix is scoped there.
- **Shared verification (B390/B391/B392):** lint **0 errors** · **1210 tests** (1201 + 9 new in `test/exhibitCols.test.js`, with a faithful copy in `ui-audit/stress/exhibit-cols.mjs` + anti-drift guards) · build green · JSX transpiles (`jsxcheck-sequence`) · `Scheduler` lazy chunk intact. Headless **V113** (`ui-audit/verify-exhibit-columns.mjs`, **10/10**, drives page → sequence iframe → preview iframe on the real app): Start **and** End dates render in full with no ellipsis clip (`12/27/26`, `07/23/25`, `02/02/27`); Duration full (`389d`, `21d`); Task-Name content-capped (no runaway gap, name=280px); Gantt keeps a real share (322px); year-boundary divider lines present; a resize handle drags **live** (53→87px) and the new width **round-trips/persists** through the parent re-render. Screenshot: `ui-audit/screens/exhibit-fixed-zoom.png`. (Re-verified after merging `main` — main's B388 Schedule-toolbar lift moved the Export control into the shell header, so the harness opens it there; still 10/10.)

### B386 — Dependency connectors draw phantom arrows to unscheduled (blank-date) tasks `[Scheduler]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-22; arrived as cross-chat "NEW-1"; filed B385, **renumbered B386** — a concurrent `main` (PR #289) took B385 for the Site Planner parcel-identify feature while this was in flight, so B386 is the real next free ID)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + headless-verified + SHIPPED the same session per STANDING RULE #1 — merged to `main` via PR #290 (squash `e4fdb2f`), branch `claude/gifted-rubin-0adp7h`.** (The PR/commit title still reads "B385" — written before the concurrent-collision renumber surfaced; the canonical ID is **B386**.)

**Repro (Pappadoupolos, Schedule → Split/Gantt):** the "Wastewater Treatment Plant Design" branch (rows 11–13) are *unscheduled stubs* — blank start/finish, 0d, so no bar and no milestone diamond. A dependency link still terminated at/from one of them and the arrow was drawn into empty space (the "purple pointing at nothing" the owner saw).

**Diagnostic fork (done first, as the brief required) → branch #1: genuine unscheduled stubs, NOT a silent date-calc failure.** Blank/unscheduled tasks are a deliberate, first-class state: `mkt` creates them (`start=""`, `dur=""`), `rollupParentDates` leaves a parent blank when *all* its children are blank (so the blank parent over blank children in rows 11–13 is the *designed* outcome), `cascadeDates` leaves a task blank when no predecessor yields a start, and BOTH the bar renderer (`isBlankDates` guard) and the PDF-export connector loop (`!pt.start||!pt.end||!t.start||!t.end`) already skip blank-date geometry. The date engine is correct — the rows are intentionally undated. The single defect: the live `GanttView.depLines` was the one draw path *missing* that guard, so it computed `xOf("")` → `NaN` and emitted a phantom path.

**Fix (`public/sequence/index.html`):** (1) `depLines` now skips any link whose predecessor OR successor has blank dates — exactly the guard the export already uses, so no connector is drawn to no-geometry. (2) Per the "don't silently hide it" preference, each blank-date Gantt row now shows an explicit, horizontally-sticky **"Unscheduled"** tag, so the empty row reads as intentional rather than a glitch. 0-day *dated* milestones (rows 10, 16) keep their diamond AND their links (`start===end`, both truthy) — no regression.

**Verified:** headless **V109** (`ui-audit/verify-unscheduled-deps.mjs`) — phantom connectors gone (dep-line count **1**, **zero** `NaN` paths), the one fully-dated link still draws, both blank rows tagged & visible; **proven to FAIL with the guard reverted** (3 dep paths, 3 `NaN` coords, 0 tags). lint **0 errors** · **1201** unit tests green · build green · `Scheduler` lazy chunk intact · existing scheduler harnesses still pass (no-crash 6/6, bugfixes ALL PASS, picker 8/8, rowfill-bars PASS). Cloudflare Pages deploy succeeded on the PR.

**Deduped — NET-NEW.** Not B380 (Scheduler.jsx nav-state render-crash — different file/cause), not B381 (toolbar hidden by a CSS over-reach — different surface), and NOT the concurrent **B385** (Site Planner parcel-identify — a different module entirely, just an ID collision). No existing Open or Done item covers dependency-connector geometry.

### B382 — Parcels in the Fort Bend / Harris seam "take forever to load" then "can't be clicked" while a county CAD host is down `[Site Planner / Map]` (bug)  *(owner-reported from chat 2026-06-22 — "Fort Bend, Cadd … isn't working … takes forever to load, and then … it doesn't work"; minted **B382** — highest B# across both files was B381 (concurrent main PR #285 took B381 for the Schedule-toolbar restore while this was in flight); a recurrence of B244/B137 territory, deduped against them)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + headless-verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/confident-meitner-j3tv25`).** Two symptoms, ONE upstream cause confirmed with LIVE probes (not guessed): **FBCAD (`gis.fbcad.org`) was down again** — timed out / slow-503 at 12–15s from both Node and headless Chromium — while HCAD and the statewide TxGIO host were up (the exact B244 condition, recurred 2026-06-22). The two existing mitigations didn't fully cover it:
- **Symptom 1 ("forever to load") — the DISPLAY layer had no timeout.** B244's 8s `AbortController` lives only in `fetchJson` (the click/identify path). The visible purple parcel outlines are an esri-leaflet `featureLayer` (`makeParcelLayer`, `MapFinder.jsx`) that bypasses `fetchJson`, so when FBCAD hangs the outline layer spins with no recovery. **Fix:** `addDisplay` now arms an 8s hang-guard for a real county layer (armed on the layer's `requeststart`, disarmed by `load`, so a below-outline-zoom view never false-flags); on timeout/`requesterror` it pulls the dead layer, records the host as failing (feeds the breaker so CLICKS skip it too), and leans on the always-present statewide TxGIO outlines for that ground — keeping what you SEE == what you can SELECT (the B137 rule). The **statewide layer is exempt** from the guard: a slow statewide outline is allowed to finish rather than be pulled (a slow outline beats no outline — that "took a while but worked" wait IS this layer; pulling it would leave nothing to see OR click).
- **Symptom 2 ("can't click the lots") — every click waited on the hung host.** `identifyParcelDetailed` used `Promise.allSettled`, which waits for EVERY candidate — so even though TxGIO answered, each click stalled the full 8s on FBCAD's timeout before resolving, reading as "clicking does nothing." **Fix:** new `identifyParcelEager` (`lib/arcgis.js`) resolves the moment the FIRST source returns a lot (real CADs are queried before the statewide fallback, so a healthy county still answers first), and feeds the circuit breaker the full per-source health via an `onSettled` callback once the slow ones finish (so the next click skips the dead host). The no-hit verdict still waits for all to settle, so "reached a server, no parcel" vs "couldn't reach any server" stay honest (B245). `handleClick` + the address-search `selectParcelAt` both switched to it.
- **Tests/verify:** +3 unit (`test/arcgis.test.js`) — eager returns the hit WITHOUT tripping/awaiting the hung source's timeout then feeds the breaker for both; the no-hit path reports responded/errors honestly; a real-CAD hit is preferred over the statewide one. Full suite **1201 green** (unchanged after merging main — PR #285 added a Playwright harness, no vitest tests), build green, esri-leaflet 3.0.19 `requeststart`/`load`/`requesterror` event contract confirmed present. Headless **V107** (`ui-audit/verify-parcel-resilience.mjs`) — run against the LIVE failing hosts tonight: select mode loads with **0 uncaught errors**, the map stays alive through the full FBCAD hang window (no freeze), and a click resolves in a **bounded 8.1s** (the AbortController cap on the worst-case no-hit path) instead of the open-ended 12–30s+ the raw hung hosts give. (A real lot with a fast source resolves in ~1–4s, per the unit tests.)
- **Forward note:** tonight the statewide TxGIO *query* op was itself slow (its metadata was fast, but spatial queries timed out 30s+ from Node) — so when FBCAD is down AND TxGIO query is degraded, even the universal fallback is slow. This fix makes the click *bounded and non-freezing* and keeps see==click, but it can't make a slow statewide host fast. If TxGIO-query slowness becomes chronic, the roadmap **GIS layer caching** item (stale-while-revalidate parcel outlines) is the durable answer.

### B381 — Restore the missing Schedule toolbar controls (regression) `[Schedule]` (bug)  *(arrived as cross-chat "NEW-1" 2026-06-22; first filed B380, renumbered **B381** — concurrent main PR #284 took B380 for the Schedule render-crash fix while this was in flight, so B381 is the real next free ID; net-new, the completion of B203)*

NOT a dup of main's **B380** (a separate intermittent Schedule *render-crash* race in `Scheduler.jsx` — different file, different cause, shipped the same day), nor B341 (chrome hardcoded-color/token regressions), nor the Markup `toolbarContent` relocation.

### B380 — Intermittent render crash on Schedule load ("Cannot read properties of undefined"), caught by the workspace ErrorBoundary `[Scheduler]` (bug)  *(arrived as cross-chat diagnosis brief "NEW-1" 2026-06-22; minted **B380** — highest B# across both files was B379; net-new, deduped vs B221/B239 stale-chunk + B315 undo-race)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + headless-verified (V105) the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/relaxed-dijkstra-sokq4a`).** Opening the Schedule module would intermittently show the workspace ErrorBoundary's **non-chunk "Try again / Reload page"** fallback with a `<pre>` of the "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '…')" form; **Try again** (a state reset, not a reload) recovered cleanly. Confirmed NOT the stale-chunk family (B221/B239) — the boundary took the genuine-render-crash path and a pure re-render fixed it.
- **Root cause — reproduced, not guessed.** The Schedule shell embeds the standalone Gantt in an iframe (`/sequence/`) and bridges that app's project list to the shared Row-1 breadcrumb over postMessage (`planar:nav-state`). The shell derives the breadcrumb's current project with `projects.find((p) => p.id === activeId)` (the brief's #1 candidate, `Scheduler.jsx`). The embedded app builds its list as `Object.values(data.projects).map(p => ({id, name}))`; while ITS own data is still loading it can transiently emit a **sparse / not-yet-resolved** list containing an `undefined`/null entry. One such entry makes `p.id` throw **inside the Scheduler's render** → caught by the workspace boundary. A pure re-render recovers because the steady-state list is well-formed, which is exactly why it presents as intermittent. The brief's other candidates (`AppHeader`/`ProjectBreadcrumb` `p.id`/`p.name`, `useProfile/displayName` in `Shell.jsx`) were each verified **already null-safe** (signed-in + real-iframe headless repro, 0 crashes); the deref that actually throws is the Scheduler's `.find`.
- **Fix — guard at the source (not optional-chaining at every call site).** New pure, unit-tested `src/workspaces/scheduler/lib/navState.js` (matches the B315 pure-module precedent): `parseNavState(message)` validates source/type and routes through `sanitizeProjects(list)`, which coerces the inbound list to an array of plain `{id, name}` objects — **dropping the null/undefined/primitive entries that are the only values that throw on a later `p.id`/`p.name` read**; `deriveCurrentProject(projects, activeId, section)` never throws and never returns `undefined` (Dashboard/reports → null; a stale activeId not in the list → null, the empty/loader state). `Scheduler.jsx` routes both the inbound message and the current-project derivation through these. One **data-entry guard** in the shared `ProjectBreadcrumb` (`(controlled ? controlledProjects : internalProjects).filter(Boolean)`) hardens its own `p.id`/`p.name` map for any controlled caller. The race is **removed** so the (now-rare) genuine crash still stays visible — NOT widened `isChunkLoadError`, NOT a blanket ErrorBoundary auto-retry (per the brief).
- **Behaviour preserved.** For the real embedded app's well-formed `{id,name}` payload the output is identical to the previous inline logic — only the not-ready/malformed shapes are made safe.
- **Tests/verify:** +12 unit (`test/schedulerNavState.test.js`) — sanitize drops the throwing entries / keeps real objects, parse validates + sanitizes, derive is null-safe on the race/Dashboard/stale-id paths. Full suite **1198 green**, lint **0 errors**, build green, `Scheduler` lazy chunk intact. Headless **V105** (`ui-audit/verify-scheduler-no-crash.mjs`, 9/9) — the first-render race shows the loader/empty (no boundary), a deliberately malformed nav-state doesn't crash the header and the good projects still render, signed-in-with-late-profile doesn't crash; **proven to FAIL (boundary + page error) with the guard off**, so it's a real regression net. Existing `verify-schedule-picker.mjs` still **8/8** (no regression to the bridge/switch/dashboard).

### B378 — Sheet labels are garbage on text-dense (general-notes / specs) sheets `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(arrived as cross-chat "NEW-1" 2026-06-22; minted **B378** — highest B# across both files was B373, so B378 is the real next free ID; extends/hardens B266 + the shared `sheetMeta` reader, deduped against B266/B348)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + headless-verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/ecstatic-maxwell-6y8aq1`).** A structural general-notes set labelled "atrociously": body boilerplate shown AS the sheet title ("…reproduced or used without…", "CJ DENOTES…"), the same cross-referenced number on several rows ("Structural · S202" ×4), and a mix of those with plain "Sheet N." Root cause: every read was tuned for a normal drawing (sparse plan + one dense title-block strip); a notes sheet (wall-to-wall text, no drawing area) violates all of those assumptions at once. Fixed at the shared reader so BOTH the Markup sidebar and the Stitcher benefit:
- **Title scorer was backwards (`readSheetTitle`, `sheetMeta.js`).** It scored `lineHeight × letterCount`, which *rewards* long sentences — so the copyright block and a legend row outscored the real short title. Re-weighted to **prefer font height, with a small word/letter cap** (a title is a few words, not a sentence): candidates over 7 words / 48 letters are dropped, height dominates the score, letters only break ties. Added a **boilerplate filter** (`property of` / `reproduced` / `copyright` / `denotes` / `continued` / "may not be …") to the existing skip list. Net: "GENERAL NOTES" wins over the boilerplate it used to lose to.
- **The "band-first" guarantee was fictional for the number (`readSheetMeta`).** `parseSheetNumber` ran over the whole-page joined string, and its `(?:no\.?|#)?` is optional, so a body cross-reference ("SEE DWG S202") was grabbed as THIS sheet's number — identical on every sheet that referenced it. Made the number read **title-block-zone-scoped**: from the detected band, or — when a dense notes sheet defeats the density-based band detector — from the right/bottom edge **strip** where title blocks live; only a non-dense sheet may fall back to the whole-page read. So the sheet's OWN number ("S-001") is read and the body cross-ref ("S202") is excluded.
- **`reconstructLines` merged across the full page width.** Two items sharing a baseline but ~900 pt apart (a title-block label and a far-left body note) were joined into one "line", which then failed the title filter as "too wordy" — losing the title entirely on a notes sheet. Now **splits a row on a large horizontal gap** (generous threshold — far bigger than any intra-phrase word gap, so "MATCH LINE … SEE SHEET C-6" still joins), so a title-block title can't bleed into a body line.
- **Sidebar gate too weak (`DocReview.jsx`).** The old `hasReal = sheetNumber || titleBlock` let a bare band authorize a title-derived label. Replaced with a `trustedTitle` gate: a title is surfaced only when it came from a real band, OR is corroborated by a zone-read number, OR the sheet is a recognized text page (general notes/specs) — else it falls back cleanly to the discipline item, then the number, then "Sheet N." Singles now show the real title ("GENERAL NOTES · S-001") instead of a generic discipline label.
- **Identical adjacent numbers = a misread → drop it.** New pure `markAdjacentDuplicateNumbers` (`sheetGroups.js`) clears a sheet number that repeats on an adjacent page (a real set never prints the same # twice in a row) and lowers confidence, so the no-band fallback can't produce a run of identical wrong rows. Applied in both the Markup consumer (`DocReview` `orderedMeta`) and the Stitcher path (`readSheets`).
- **Tests:** +9 unit (`sheetMeta`/`sheetGroups`/`sheetRead`): the title scorer ignores boilerplate, the number is zone-scoped (reads S-001 not the S202 cross-ref), `textDense` is flagged, the dedup clears adjacent duplicates. Full suite **1153 green**, lint 0 errors, build green, `DocReview` lazy chunk intact. Verified **V104**.

### B379 — False auto-calibration ("·≈") on general-notes / specs sheets `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(arrived as cross-chat "NEW-2" 2026-06-22; minted **B379** — next free ID after B378; relates to B267 `statedCalibration`, deduped against it)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + headless-verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/ecstatic-maxwell-6y8aq1`).** On the same structural set, pure-text notes sheets (S00x) showed "·≈" (auto-calibrated) even though they carry no plan scale, while sheet 1 correctly read "NOT TO SCALE." Root cause: `parseSheetScale` matches a scale-looking string **anywhere** in the dense notes text, and `statedCalibration` only gated on a standard plot size — so a 36×24 general-notes sheet with a stray "1\"=20'" in its body auto-calibrated. Auto-calibrating a non-drawing sheet silently mis-scales it (crash-severity per "never auto-guess" — a wrong calibration poisons every downstream takeoff).
- **Fix — classify the sheet, then gate.** `readSheetMeta` now computes a **`textDense`** flag (a general-notes / specifications / legend sheet): true when the title is a notes/specs/legend/index title, or the drawing area is saturated with sentence-like prose (≥10 lines of ≥6 words — plans carry only short labels). `statedCalibration` **returns 0 when `textDense`**, so such a sheet is left uncalibrated ("not present" ≠ "couldn't parse", per B267) rather than silently scaled. A real plan sheet (sparse drawing-area text, a stated scale in its title block) still auto-calibrates exactly as before.
- **Tests:** +1 unit (`sheetRead`: a textDense sheet with a stated scale on a standard plot → 0) plus the `textDense` true/false assertions under B378. Verified **V104** (the same harness asserts the notes sheet shows no "·≈" while the plan sheet still does).

### B374 — Area measurements can't be selected by their filled interior (dead-centre hit target) `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(owner-reported from chat 2026-06-22 — "no easy way to delete this little triangle … insane"; minted **B374** — highest B# across both files was B373; batch B374–B377)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + headless-verified + shipped the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/youthful-mccarthy-xjcotz`).** Michael's "triangle" was an **uncalibrated Area measurement** — its value label falls back to the literal string **"set scale"** when a sheet has no feet-per-page-unit (`measureLabel`, `lib/takeoff.js`). Clicking the triangle's body to select it (the natural first step to delete it) did nothing.
- **Root cause:** in `DocReview.jsx` `hitTest`, **rect/cloud** got a point-in-bbox interior test (B33) but **area fell through to the generic measures branch — nearest vertex/segment only**. The Area polygon renders FILLED (`fill="#0e749022"`), so it reads as a solid clickable object while its **interior was a dead hit target**; only a click on the thin edge/a vertex registered, and at low zoom (e.g. 26%) that band is nearly impossible to hit → the measurement felt undeletable.
- **Fix:** added an `m.kind === "area"` branch to `hitTest` — `pointInPoly(p, pts)` returns d=0 for a click anywhere inside the polygon. `pointInPoly` is now **EXPORTED** from `lib/takeoff.js` (the same ray-cast already behind `centroidOf`, not a 2nd copy; handles concave outlines). A <3-pt / degenerate area still selects by its edge or vertex via the fallback (now incl. the **closing edge**, which the old branch skipped — also applied to perimeter). Added a **smaller-shape-wins tie-break** on interior (d===0) hits so a small markup sitting on a big filled area isn't swallowed by the area underneath.
- **Verified (V104):** new `ui-audit/verify-delete-markup.mjs` **10/10** (chromium-1228, 0 page errors) — draws an uncalibrated "set scale" Area, then: a **centroid click selects it** (stroke 2→3), a click **outside does NOT** select (hit test stays specific), and Delete removes it. No regression: V72 viewer **13/13**, B300–B302 green. lint 0 · 1144 tests · build green.

### B375 — No on-canvas delete control for a selected markup (deletion was keyboard-only) `[Doc Review / Markup]` (feature) — pairs with B374
`[x]` **Same session/branch.** Even once a markup is selected, removing it was **Delete/Backspace only**, plus a "Delete selected" button buried in the (collapsible) Takeoff panel — nothing on the canvas where the user is looking, so deletion wasn't discoverable. Added a clear **× button anchored to the selected markup's top-right**, rendered OUTSIDE the `pointerEvents:none` overlay (like the inline text/calibrate editors) so it takes its own click; `stopPropagation` on pointer-down keeps that click from starting a pan/draw underneath. Runs the same one-undo-frame path as the Delete key (`pushHistory` → filter out the id → `setSel(null)`). Hidden while editing text / calibrating. Theme tokens only (`--danger-text` fill + `--on-accent` glyph — AA in both themes; no raw hex). Verified in V104 (× appears on the selection and deletes the markup).

### B376 — Per-item delete in the Takeoff list (all markups) + a deletable measure list in the Stitcher `[Doc Review / Markup + Stitch]` (feature)
`[x]` **Same session/branch.** The hit-test-independent removal path, so anything can always be taken off — even on a dense sheet or when not in Select mode.
- **Markup:** the Takeoff "This sheet" list now lists **every markup** (measures + redline rect/cloud + text notes), not just measurements; each row is click-to-select **and carries its own × delete**. Empty-state copy → **"Nothing on this sheet yet."** (the old "No measurements yet" would mislead now that redlines/notes are listed).

### B377 — Scanned-sheet OCR worker threw "logger is not a function" on every page (error storm) `[Doc Review / Stitch + OCR]` (bug)  *(found while headless-verifying B374–B376; minted **B377**)*
`[x]` **Same session/branch.** Surfaced by the Stitcher harness runs: a page with no text layer triggers the B352 Tesseract OCR fallback, and the worker threw **`TypeError: logger is not a function`** repeatedly (13× in one B300–B302 run). **Root cause:** `defaultMakeWorker` (`lib/ocr.js`) passed `logger` — always `undefined`, since no caller supplies one — straight into `createWorker({ …, logger })`. Tesseract invokes `logger` on the **main thread** for every progress packet the worker posts back, and an explicit `logger: undefined` **clobbers Tesseract's own default no-op**, so each message threw. **Fix:** default `logger = () => {}` (still injectable for a real progress UI later). Confirmed gone in the unminified dev build (0 `PAGEERROR`) and across all Stitcher harnesses — **B300–B302 uncaught JS errors 13 → 0**. OCR unit tests unaffected (they inject the recognizer, bypassing the default worker). NB the WASM core + English model still load from the jsDelivr CDN at runtime; only the logger crash was in scope.

### B373 — Restore the compact, app-wide cloud-sync indicator in AppHeader Row 1 `[App Shell / all workspaces]` (feature)  *(arrived as cross-chat "NEW-1" 2026-06-22 — a provisional label colliding with the older NEW-1 open-file intent + the B365/B372 NEW-1 markers/delete items; first filed **B366**, renumbered **B373** — a concurrent `main` (PRs #277/#278) took B366–B372 (GIS Site Analysis resilience + source registry, delete-persistence) while this was in flight, so B373 is the real next free ID)*
`[x]` **Filed AND shipped + headless-verified the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/vibrant-dijkstra-i3ddzg`).** The small save-status indicator the owner expected in the header had drifted away: the Site Planner showed a **text** chip ("Synced ✓"), Document Review had moved its chip out of Row 1 down to the Row-2 Reviews control (B358), and the Stitcher carried its own — so there was no single, compact, app-wide indicator, and the owner's design intent (a **cloud glyph + check, no "Saved" text**) had been lost. Worse, the failure mode that made it "disappear" was a silent drop-to-blank on error. Restored as **one shared component, app-wide, that goes LOUD on a failed write and never silently vanishes.**
- **New shared `src/shared/ui/CloudSyncBadge.jsx`** — a compact cloud glyph (no text label) driven by the **normalized `saveState` every workspace already computes** (so it reflects the REAL cloud write, never an optimistic always-green). Pure exported `cloudBadgeView(state)` is the whole truth-table → glyph + color + loud/actionable flags. States, each visually distinct (not text-dependent): **synced** = quiet green cloud-check (the resting default); **saving** = amber cloud-up, pulsing; **offline** = amber cloud-pause (saved on device, will sync); **error** = **LOUD** red cloud-slash + a red ring, click → popover with what-failed + **Retry now**; **local** = muted "device" glyph (signed out); **null** = nothing (no project/doc loaded — legitimately empty, not a hidden error).
- **The crash-severity guardrail in code (the headline ask):** the badge wraps itself in a small error boundary (`CloudBadgeBoundary`) that, if the badge ever throws while rendering, shows the **loud error glyph instead of returning null** — the exact "silent unmount" that made the old indicator vanish. Keyed on `state` so a transient throw clears once inputs change, and so it tracks live state across module/project switches without going stale.
- **`AppHeader` renders it once, in Row 1, from `saveState`** — so it's genuinely shared across Site / Schedule / Markup. New optional `onRetrySave` + `saveDetail` props let a workspace supply the retry action and a tailored popover message (e.g. "reload to merge" for a conflict, where a blind retry is wrong).
- **Site Planner:** retired the text `plannerSaveSlot` chip (the compact badge replaces it); wires `onRetrySave={retryCloudSave}` (suppressed for a conflict, which needs a reload) + a conflict `saveDetail`. The loud failure **banners** (cloudSaveFailed / cloudConflict) stay as the can't-miss interrupt; the badge is the always-present at-a-glance state.
- **Document Review + Stitcher:** new pure exported `docSaveState(status, signedIn, idle)` (in `usePersistence.js`) maps the doc-review raw status onto the normalized vocabulary — **a failed/conflicting write → "error" (LOUD)**, idle (nothing loaded) → null (no cry-wolf at rest), signed-in → synced, signed-out-with-content → local. DR feeds it to AppHeader; the **Stitcher has its own chrome (no AppHeader), so it renders its own `CloudSyncBadge`** in its toolbar — same glyph, same loudness, everywhere.
- **Retired the now-redundant Row-2 ReviewsBar save chip** (its `chipFor` + `SaveIcon`) so a module never shows two competing save indicators — the app-wide Row-1 badge is the single source. ReviewsBar is now purely the filing control. Removed the obsolete `test/reviewsBadge.test.js`; its "failed-write-is-loud / no-cry-wolf" contract migrated to the new badge test.
- **Tests:** new `test/cloudSyncBadge.test.js` (13) locks the contract — **a failed save is never visually identical to "all good"** (distinct glyph + color + loud flag), null shows nothing, the crashed fallback is loud, and the doc raw→normalized mapping keeps failures loud. Full suite green post-merge (lint 0 errors, build green; `SitePlannerApp`/`DocReview` lazy chunks intact).
- **Verified (V103):** two headless harnesses (chromium-1194, 0 page errors). `ui-audit/verify-new1-cloud-badge.mjs` **20/20** — every state present and visually distinct, error is loud + click-to-Retry fires the handler, null renders nothing, and **a crashed badge falls back to the loud glyph (does NOT vanish)**. `ui-audit/verify-new1-header-integration.mjs` **5/5** — the badge is wired into the **live** Row-1 header with a project open, shows the honest on-device state logged-out (not a fake green "synced"), and **survives switching modules** (Site → Markup hides it when nothing's loaded → back to Site restores it). ### B372 — A deleted site reappears (delete not persisting) `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-22 from chat as "NEW-1"; first filed B366, renumbered **B372** — a concurrent `main` (PR #277) took B366–B371 (GIS Site Analysis resilience + source registry) while this was in flight, so B372 is the real next free ID)*
`[x]` **Filed AND fixed + headless-verified + pushed the SAME session per STANDING RULE #1 (branch `claude/cool-ride-pm0m2l`).** Deleting the HOLLISTER site brought it back — on a hard reload (path A) **and** mid-session with no reload (path B). Crash-severity per the silent-failure principle: a delete that looks successful in the UI but doesn't stick is silent data divergence.
- **ONE root cause for both paths (so kept as one item — the owner said split only if path B were independent).** The site you delete from the map is, in the common case, the one you had **open**: opening it sets `activeSiteId`, and "Back to map" only flips the view — the `SitePlanner` stays **mounted (hidden)**, keyed to that `activeSiteId`. Deleting it calls `deleteSiteGroup` → `setActiveSiteId(null)`, which **unmounts** that planner; its unmount cleanup `persistOrDrop()` (and the `beforeunload`/visibility flush + any queued debounced autosave) then ran `saveSite()` for the just-deleted id, **re-writing the row**. (a) The existing in-planner `deletedSelfRef` guard only covered the *single-plan* delete from inside the planner, NOT the map's whole-site delete. (b) **Path B:** the resurrected record sits in the local store and re-surfaces on the next `refreshSites()` (any map↔plan nav). (c) **Path A:** on reload, `pullCloud`'s heal-the-split sees a local-only row the cloud is missing and **re-pushes it to the cloud**, making the resurrection permanent. This also explains "maybe it's just that project" — it was the one he had open; sites never opened this session had no mounted planner to resurrect them.
- **Fix 1 — kill the resurrection at the one chokepoint (`lib/storage.js`).** A per-tab session tombstone `recentlyDeleted` (Set): `deleteSite` adds the id; `saveSite` refuses to **re-create a deleted, currently-absent row** (`if (!existing && recentlyDeleted.has(id)) return false`). EVERY resurrection path (unmount persist, beforeunload/visibility flush, debounced autosave, a cross-tab storage echo) funnels through `saveSite`, so this closes all of them — not just the one the bug surfaced. A normal edit-save (record still present) and a brand-new site (id never deleted) are untouched; `stageLegacySite`/`importOneSiteToCloud` lift the tombstone so a deliberate same-id re-import still works; it's per-tab and clears on reload (by then the delete has settled).
- **Fix 2 — make a real cloud-delete failure LOUD (never a phantom success).** `cloudDelete` now uses `.delete(…).select("id")` so a 0-row no-op (already gone, or an ownership/RLS mismatch) is distinguishable from a real removal, and a thrown/4xx error returns `{ok:false}`. `deleteSite` **returns** that promise; `deleteSiteGroup`/`deletePlan` AWAIT it, and on a genuine error show a red **"Couldn't delete … from the cloud — it may reappear when you reload"** banner and **re-pull** so the list reflects the honest truth instead of a fake success. (Decision: a 0-row delete is treated as success, not an alarm — a local-only site never pushed to the cloud legitimately removes 0 rows, so alarming on 0-row would cry wolf; RLS also means a row a user can *see* is a row they *can* delete. We alarm only on an actual error, which is the silent case that mattered. This refines the owner's literal "0 rows = failure" into the safer rule that won't false-alarm.)
- **Why the ownership-mismatch theory didn't pan out as the cause (checked first, as asked):** RLS `select` is `auth.uid() = user_id`, so a row visible in the list is owned by the current user — a foreign-owned row would never appear to be deleted in the first place, and wouldn't return from `cloudList` on reload either. The real mechanism was the mounted-planner resurrection above. `cloudDelete` is still hardened to surface a true permission/network error loudly.
- **Verified (V102):** new `ui-audit/verify-b372-delete-durable.mjs` — boots into the planner for HOLLISTER, returns to the map (planner stays mounted), deletes it, and asserts on the **store source-of-truth** + the rendered list: **6/6** (Chromium, logged-out, 0 page errors), incl. not-resurrected immediately, no mid-session reappearance after a list refresh, and still-gone after reload (Schiel preserved). **Proven to have teeth — with the guard disabled the harness FAILS exactly as reported (`store ids = [s2,s1]`, card returns, survives reload).** Plus **9 new unit tests** (`test/deletePersistence.test.js`: `interpretDelete` row-count/error matrix + the end-to-end resurrection guard). **lint 0 · build green · `SitePlannerApp`/`DocReview` lazy chunks intact** (full suite re-run green post-merge).
- **Note for the signed-in tail:** the loud-banner path on a *genuine cloud-delete error* can't be driven logged-out (the sandbox CORS-blocks Supabase auth); its logic is unit-locked (`interpretDelete`) and the local resurrection (the actual bug) is fully headless-verified. A one-line signed-in confirm is noted in VERIFICATION V102, not owed from Michael.

### B366 — Screening resilience + honest error taxonomy (a 503 is not "CORS") `[Site Planner / Analysis]` (bug)  *(arrived as coworker-brief "NEW-1" 2026-06-21; minted **B366**)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-22 (branch `claude/nice-cori-ghm37q`).** The screen fired ~8–10 ArcGIS `/query` calls **all at once**; under that burst hosts (even Esri-hosted ones) returned transient **HTTP 503**, with **no retry** (one blip → permanent UNKNOWN) and **every** failure mislabeled "Couldn't reach the GIS server (network or CORS)" though CORS is fine on every endpoint. (A 503 whose error response lacks the CORS header surfaces to `fetch` as an opaque "Failed to fetch" — which is exactly why the catch-all blamed CORS.)
- **New shared `lib/gisFetch.js`:** `fetchArcgisJson` = one resilient fetch — **AbortController timeout** + **jittered exponential-backoff retry** (3 attempts) on a transient 5xx/429/network/timeout + automatic **GET→POST** when a dense-polygon URL gets over-long. `classifyGisError` → an honest `{kind, message, retryable}` taxonomy: `http-5xx`/`http-4xx`/`arcgis`/`timeout`/`network`/`offline` — **never** a blind "CORS" (a bare "Failed to fetch" reads "couldn't reach / temporarily unavailable", since in-browser a header-less 503 is indistinguishable from a real CORS block and a retry usually clears it). `pLimit` concurrency limiter.
- **`runSiteAnalysis` now throttles the WHOLE fan-out** (environmental + jurisdiction + road) through ONE pool of **3** — the burst that provoked the 503s is gone.
- **State machine:** new **`unavailable`** finding status (retryable; amber; a per-source **↻ Retry** control), **visually + semantically distinct from `absent`/"None found"** — a failure is NEVER read as clear (the silent-error guard). The honest reason (e.g. "HTTP 503 — temporarily unavailable") is surfaced; jurisdiction/road use the same shared classifier.
- **Tests:** `test/gisFetch.test.js` (15 — retry-then-succeed, give-up-after-budget, no-retry-4xx, arcgis-200-error-body, POST-for-long-URL, pool max-in-flight, honest-not-CORS). Live headless `gis-verify/site-analysis-resilience-verify.mjs` **11/11** (V101): forced-503 → honest "503", Retry present, 0 "network or CORS", 0 page errors. lint 0 · build green.
