### B364 — Mobile: pinch-zoom crash ("null is not an object … .mid") + multi-tab banner falsely nagging logged-out users `[App Shell / Site Planner / Doc Review]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-21 from a mobile screenshot: opened on phone, "moved around for a sec" → Site Planner error boundary fired; **separately** a "open in another tab" banner appeared though he wasn't signed in and shouldn't carry cross-session state.)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/mobile-session-state-bug-omeec4`).**
- **Crash root cause:** the two-finger pinch handler (`applyPinch`, B331) read `pinchRef.current.mid` *inside* the `setView` updater. On mobile a finger can lift between scheduling the update and React running the updater — `reseedPinch` nulls `pinchRef.current` — so the deferred updater dereferenced null (`null is not an object (evaluating '…​.current.mid')`) and the workspace's error boundary showed "Site Planner hit an error and couldn't load." **Fix:** snapshot `pinchRef.current` into a local before `setView` in **both** `SitePlanner.jsx` and `doc-review/DocReview.jsx`, so the updater uses the captured baseline and can't hit null.
- **Multi-tab banner root cause / scope:** the B313 same-project-in-another-tab warning fired for **logged-out** sessions too, where it's just a false mobile nag (the banner exists to protect saved *cloud* work, not anonymous device-only browsing). **Fix:** gated to signed-in accounts only — new `accountActive` prop on `AppHeader` (defaults off) plumbed `Shell (!!user) → SitePlannerApp/SitePlanner/DocReview/Scheduler → AppHeader`; presence is fed a null project and the banner is suppressed when logged out. Logged-out = fresh, quiet.
- **Tests:** `test/multiTab.test.js` (10) still green (pure protocol unchanged); `ui-audit/verify-multitab.mjs` rewritten to assert the new behavior (two logged-out tabs on the same project → **no** banner in either) — **3/3 (V99)**. build green.

### B362 — Bump-out (dog-ear) resize doesn't persist; reverts to the 55′×60′ default on any host refit `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-1" 2026-06-21, confirmed live on project **Jacintoport** — cloud site `smqdxst8pf3g`, bump-outs `e8986`/`e8987` both stuck at default 60×55. First filed **B357**; renumbered **B362** — a concurrent `main` (#268/#269) took B357–B361 (Markup header de-clutter + Scheduler) while this was in flight, so this is the real next free ID. **Folds in** the long-deferred triage item "building bump-outs aren't clamped when the host shrinks" — now closed here.)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/festive-newton-90t0zh`, PR #271).**
- **Repro:** select a building bump-out, resize it, then resize/edge-drag/numerically-resize the host → the bump snapped back to 55′×60′. **Root cause:** a dog-ear stored no size of its own — `dogEarGeom` always recomputed w/h from the constants `DOGEAR_W`/`DOGEAR_D`, and `refitChildren`→`fitDogEar`→`dogEarGeom` ran for every dog-ear on each host resize, discarding the user's dimensions.
- **Fix:** extracted the bump geometry to a pure, unit-tested **`lib/dogEar.js`** (`dogEarGeom`/`dogEarSize` + the defaults). A resized bump now **records its span along the dock wall + its projection** (`along`/`proj`) on its `dogEar` tag (captured in `refitChildren` the moment the bump is the resized element); `fitDogEar` re-anchors **position + host angle only**, preserving the stored size. The along-span is **CLAMPED to the wall — never reset** — when the host shrinks past the corner (closes the deferred "not clamped" item), and **springs back** when the host grows again. Knock-on correctness: the **dock-door layout** now avoids a bump by its actual span (not a flat 55′), and the **yield panel** says "N bump-outs · sizes vary" instead of falsely claiming "55′×60′" once a bump is resized.
- **Schema:** `SITE_MODEL_VERSION` 6→7; the new `along`/`proj` fields ride inside `els`, lossless/idempotent through `createSiteModel` (absent ⇒ the 55′×60′ default, so every existing bump is unaffected).
- **Tests:** new `test/dogEar.test.js` (5) — default 55×60 + flush-at-corner, the `dogEarSize` inverse, **the exact repro (resize bump → resize host → size preserved)**, clamp-then-spring-back on host shrink, host-rotation carry. Coordinated with B363 (resize re-syncs angle *without* resetting size). **lint 0 · 1066 tests · build green · `SitePlannerApp` lazy chunk intact.** Live: `ui-audit/verify-b362-b363.mjs` 6/6 (V98).

### B363 — Bonded children (bump-outs, court, sidewalk) keep a stale rotation when the host is re-angled `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-2" 2026-06-21, confirmed live on **Jacintoport** — host `e8984` at rot 0° but all four bonded children (`e8985` court, `e8986`/`e8987` bump-outs, `e8988` sidewalk) at 359.035°, the whole assembly ~1° off the building. First filed **B358**; renumbered **B363** — `main` #268/#269 took B357–B361 in flight.)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/festive-newton-90t0zh`, PR #271).**
- **Root cause:** a bonded child's rotation was only copied from the host at create/refit time (`dogEarGeom`/`makeStrip`/`oppTrailerGeom` set `rot: host.rot`); the only thing that re-copied it was `refitChildren`, which runs on host **resize only**. So any state where child rot ≠ host rot — a host placed at a parcel-bearing angle, children added, the host later straightened by a path that didn't carry them — was left visibly off-angle until the next resize.
- **Fix (1) — derived invariant, re-applied on ANY host geometry change.** A bonded box child's angle is now a derived value: `host.rot` + its fixed quarter-turn offset (0/90/180/270 — sidewalks/courts/bump-outs share the host angle; side-parking/wall-trailers sit at a +90/180/270 turn). A shared pure `bondedChildRot`/`quarterOffset` (`siteModel.js`) + a `resyncBondedRot` pass is now folded into **every** host-geometry path — resize (`refitChildren`) **and** rotate (`rotateAssemblyTo` *and* the rotate-handle drag) — so a child can no longer be stranded off-angle (previously only resize re-synced, and only some child types).
- **Fix (2) — one-time repair in migrate.** `normalizeBondedRotations` runs inside `createSiteModel` (the migrate path → fires on every load), re-anchoring a drifted child to the host's **current** frame: its angle snaps to `host.rot + offset` **and** its centre is rotated about the host centre by the stale delta (a host straightened without its children leaves their *positions* stale too, not just the angle value). **Idempotent + identity-preserving** for already-correct data; safe because a bonded box child is only ever at a quarter turn, so any other angle is drift, not intent (points-based children skipped). This **repairs Jacintoport and any other already-diverged project the moment it's opened**, and persists on the next save.
- **Coordinated with B362:** `refitChildren` captures the bump size **before** the rotation resync, and resync only touches `rot` — so re-syncing a child's angle never resets a resized bump.
- **Schema:** `SITE_MODEL_VERSION` 6→7 (shared with B362).
- **Tests:** new `test/bondedRotation.test.js` (6) — the quarter-turn offset math, **the full Jacintoport repair (rot AND position re-anchored)**, idempotency + identity-preservation on correct data, points-children skipped, version-bump guard. **lint 0 · 1066 tests · build green.** Live: `ui-audit/verify-b362-b363.mjs` 6/6 (V98) — drifted assembly straightens on load, user-sized bump keeps 80×70 across a save/load round-trip.

### B354 — Markup yield panel miscounts redline annotations as "uncalibrated measurements" `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(owner chat 2026-06-21 "keep going" — Markup-tool stress test; minted **B354** — next free after B353)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/stitch-tool-stress-test-1tvw5b`).** Stress-testing the Markup yield panel turned up a real miscount. The panel warns **"N measurement(s) on uncalibrated sheets are excluded"** from `rollup(markups, calByPage)` — but `rollup` was handed the WHOLE markup list (measurements **and** redline annotations: rect / cloud / line / arrow / text), and any non-measurement kind on an *uncalibrated* sheet fell into `measureValue`'s generic branch (`calibrated:false`) and incremented `uncal`. So drawing a redline cloud or adding a text note on an uncalibrated sheet made the panel falsely warn "1 measurement(s) … excluded" when **zero** measurements were made (and could mislead a reviewer into thinking a real takeoff was dropped). `rollup` now tallies **only** the measurement kinds (`distance/perimeter/area/count`, derived from the existing `MIN_MEASURE_PTS` so there's one source of truth) and skips everything else (and null entries) outright. Totals were already correct (redlines never matched the area/perimeter/distance branches); only the `uncal` warning was wrong. `lib/takeoff.js`. **New `test/markupRollupStress.test.js` — 6 adversarial tests** (redlines don't inflate `uncal`; redlines on a calibrated sheet aren't summed; a true uncalibrated measurement still counts; all four measure kinds total correctly; null/unknown-kind entries don't crash; a non-finite page calibration excludes the measure). Existing 16 takeoff tests still green; full suite **994 tests**, lint 0 errors, build clean. Pure-logic fix — no live-browser verification needed.

### B350 — Stitcher: aggregated notes/legend across the set + Bluebeam-style detail-callout "cloud" `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (feature)  *(owner chat 2026-06-21 "make it great on all the other stuff"; minted **B350**)*

`[x]` **Built + headless-verified 2026-06-21.** Two upgrades to the stitch tool, both backed by pure shared readers so they're unit-tested away from pdf.js:
- **Notes/legend, captured across the whole set (never lost to the crop).** The auto-stitch crop (B338) hides each sheet's title-block band — where the **general notes / legend** usually live. A new pure reader `src/shared/files/sheetNotes.js` (`parseNotes` finds each `GENERAL/GRADING/KEYED NOTES`, `LEGEND`, `ABBREVIATIONS` block; `aggregateNotes` merges every placed sheet's blocks, **dedupes** repeated boilerplate, and **flags a note that didn't appear on every sheet** with the sheet(s) it came from — so a note that **changes page to page** is surfaced, not buried). Wired into `readSheetMeta` (each page now carries `notes`) and shown in the pinned **Composite key** as an expandable "Notes & legend · N" section.

Each callout renders as a clickable hotspot ring on the placed sheet; clicking it **pulls up that detail in a floating cloud popup** that renders the referenced sheet (reused from a placed sheet, or rendered on demand from a loaded PDF), **centered on the named detail** when the target sheet labels it — pan/zoomable, so you never leave the current drawing. Honest fallback: a target that isn't in the set yet says so. New toolbar **Details** toggle; hotspots only grab clicks in Pan mode (measure/align/calibrate pass through).

### B352 — Scanned-sheet OCR: read image-only drawings into the auto-assembly pipeline `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (feature)  *(owner-requested 2026-06-21 right after B335–B339: "Add ocr capabilities if I don't have that"; minted **B352** — was B340's OCR tail; a very hot `main` (B341–B351 + V88–V92) consumed every earlier number this session)*
`[x]` **Shipped + verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/loving-newton-t7gzpq`).** Fills the dormant OCR seam B336/B337 left wired, so a **scanned / image-only** drawing (no text layer) now reads, groups, stitches, crops, and auto-calibrates through the SAME pipeline as a vector PDF.
- **How:** `doc-review/lib/ocr.js` renders a no-text page to a canvas (`renderPageToOcrCanvas`, pdf.js, density-capped ≤24 MP) and runs **Tesseract.js** (WASM, in its own worker) to recover the text **with per-word bounding boxes**, then `wordsToItems` converts those boxes into the exact `{ str, x, y, w, h }` page-unit items `sheetMeta.readSheetMeta` (B336) already consumes — so OCR'd pages feed the title-block/scale/match-line reader identically. Low-confidence words are dropped (consistent with "never auto-guess").
- **Lazy + cheap on the common path:** `createOcrRunner` only spins up the worker when a no-text page is actually hit (a normal vector set pays nothing); the Tesseract orchestrator is a separate ~16 KB chunk and the WASM core + English model load from a pinned CDN (jsDelivr — reachable from Cloudflare Pages) only on first use, then browser-cached. The drawing's pixels never leave the browser. The Stitcher shows a "Reading scanned sheet (OCR)…" status while it runs.
- **Verified:** **7 unit tests** (`test/ocr.test.js` — the bbox→page-unit conversion, lazy single-worker reuse + dispose, fail-soft, and a scanned title block flowing through `readSheetMeta` to the right sheet number / title / scale / match-line) **+ a LIVE headless run** (`ui-audit/verify-b352-ocr.mjs`, **V93**): the real Tesseract engine loads from jsDelivr in Chromium and reads a "scanned" title block + match line — "GRADING PLAN / SHEET NO. C-5 / SCALE: 1\"=40' / MATCH LINE - SEE SHEET C-6" — recovering C-5, the title, the 40-scale, and the C-6 target. lint 0 · full suite green · build green; DocReview lazy chunk intact, Tesseract split into its own on-demand chunk. **OCR-path stress-hardened the same session — see the B352 stress addendum below.**
> **Dedup:** this is B340's OCR tail, pulled forward on owner request; B340 keeps the 3 remaining computer-vision tails (graphic scale-bar, geometric edge-match, legend symbol-union). Distinct + complementary to main's stitch-engine stress-tests and Stitcher-component bug sweeps (this session) — those predate OCR and never touch `ocr.js`.

**Stress addendum (owner: "stress test it") — B352.** Adversarial pass over the OCR layer (the stitch-engine stress tests predate OCR and didn't cover it). It turned up + fixed one real **non-finite poison** (the same class the engine stress-test fixed in `stitchGeom`): a **non-finite bbox coordinate** (NaN/±Infinity — which a noisy scan can emit) slipped past `wordsToItems`' `x1 <= x0` guard (`NaN <= NaN` is `false`), pushing a NaN item that would poison the whole reader (title-block density → NaN, line sort → undefined). `wordsToItems` now requires all four box coords **finite** + the box non-inverted, guards a 0/NaN/negative/Infinity render scale and non-finite page dims, and coerces non-string OCR text. New `test/ocrStress.test.js` — **15 tests** across malformed boxes, broken Tesseract shapes (`extractWords`), every orchestration failure (render/recognize/worker-creation throw → null; all-low-confidence → graceful no-text record), the OCR→`readSheetMeta`→grouping integration (a garbage scan stays standalone; an unreadable number isn't force-merged; clean scans group through NaN noise), and a **300-iteration randomized fuzz** asserting no non-finite item ever leaks and `readSheetMeta` always returns a finite [0,1] confidence. **LIVE stress** (`ui-audit/verify-b352-ocr.mjs`, 9/9): the real engine reads a clean scan AND — the dangerous case — emits **0 words on a blank page and on pure noise (no hallucinated sheet number/title)**, and a small-font degraded render doesn't throw. Full suite **959 tests**, lint 0, build clean.

### B351 — Auto-filing matcher: close two browser-path MISFILE vectors `[Doc Review / Auto-file]` (bug)  *(owner chat 2026-06-21 "keep going" — stress-testing adjacent to the stitch tool; minted **B351** — next free after B350)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/stitch-tool-stress-test-1tvw5b`).** Continuing the "stress-test / look up how to break things" pass into the auto-filing project matcher (same risk class as the stitcher: **a misfile is worse than an unfiled file**). The browser matcher (`matchProject.js` `scoreProjectInText`) searches the sheet's raw text, so it had two false-positive vectors the server twin (`server/filing/matcher.js`, which compares *extracted fields* with exact equality) avoids by construction — both could **auto-route a drawing onto the wrong project**:
- **Short IDs matched as a substring of the separator-stripped whole document** — `normId(wholeText).includes(id)` matched a 4-digit job / 6-digit parcel number as a coincidental substring spanning unrelated words (e.g. job `"1045"` inside `"…210455…"`, or a parcel inside a longer run). Now matched by **boundary-aligned equality** against `idWindows` (the normId of each run of ≤5 *adjacent* tokens), so a real id split by punctuation/space (`1234567-000-001`, `1234567 000 001`, `KG-2025`) still matches but a coincidental digit run can't manufacture a confident match.
- **Scattered name words scored 0.8 (auto-filed)** — a 2-word common name like *Katy Grand* whose words merely appear *somewhere* on an unrelated Katy-area / Grand-Parkway sheet auto-routed there. A full-**phrase** hit still scores 0.9 (auto-files), but a scattered all-words hit now scores **0.55 — below the 0.6 auto-file floor**, so it can corroborate another signal via noisy-or but never auto-route by itself ("never auto-guess").
- Also hardened `scoreProjectInText` to tolerate a `null` entry in the projects list (the `= {}` default only caught `undefined`).
- **Untouched:** the shared `decide()` thresholds (`minConfidence 0.6` / `minMargin 0.15`) — only the client-specific text-search *scoring method* changed, so the decision contract stays in parity with the server matcher. **New `test/matchProjectStress.test.js` — 11 adversarial tests** (substring-id rejection + real split-id recall, scattered-name-no-autofile + phrase recall + corroborated match, empty/junk/ambiguous/huge-blob/malformed-input). Existing 8 matcher tests still green; full suite **968 tests**, lint 0 errors, build clean. ### B343 — Stitcher tray hides a file whose grouping failed (its pages become unreachable) `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (bug)  *(owner chat 2026-06-21; first filed B341, renumbered **B343** — main #244 took B341/B342)*

Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B343* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B343 against all of them.
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21.** The background read→group (B335) sets a file's `groups` to `[]` on any read exception. The tray's grouped view rendered `p.groups.map(...)` → **zero entries**, so a file that failed to group showed nothing and the user had no way to add its pages (the "all pages" toggle was their only escape, with no hint it was needed). Now a file is shown in grouped mode only when its read produced **≥1 logical sheet** (`hasGroups`); an empty/failed group result falls back to the raw per-page list for that file (groupSheets always yields ≥1 run for a readable page, so empty == failure). `Stitcher.jsx` `trayItems`/`anyGroups`.

### B344 — Removing the world-frame (index-0) stitch sheet strands a leftover un-aligned sheet `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (bug)  *(owner chat 2026-06-21; first filed B342, renumbered **B344** — main #244 took B341/B342)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21.** The first placed sheet is the world frame (`aligned:true`); the Align button + "Not aligned" chip are gated on `i > 0`. Removing the frame promoted a still-`aligned:false` sheet to index 0, where it **lost its Align button yet stayed measurement-blocked** (`measureOverUnaligned`) — an unrecoverable stuck state (measuring errored "Align that sheet…" with no Align affordance). New `removeSheet` helper promotes the new first sheet to the frame (`aligned:true`) on removal, restoring the "index-0 is the frame" invariant. ### B347 — Seeded auto-stitch fallback gives no endpoint-order cue (reverse clicks flip the sheet 180°) `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (bug)  *(owner chat 2026-06-21; first filed B345, renumbered **B347**)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21.** When auto-stitch (B337) can't place a sheet but knows its seam side, manual Align is **pre-seeded** with the moving sheet's two seam endpoints (`detectedEndpointsFor`) and the user clicks the two matching points on a placed sheet. Nothing showed WHICH seed was "first" vs "second", so clicking the matching points in reverse order silently rotated the sheet 180° via `solveM`. The seeded flow now draws **numbered markers (1, 2)** at the moving sheet's seed endpoints (its current position), so the click order is unambiguous. Additive render only; no geometry change.

### B350 — Stress-test the drawing stitch tool: harden the auto-stitch against bad PDF sets `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (task)  *(owner chat 2026-06-21: "stress test the stitch tool, look up how to break things and implement strategies to do so"; **renumbered twice in a very hot number space** — first shipped as B341 (PR #248), bumped to B348 when a concurrent `main` kept B341 for theming-contrast (PR #244), then bumped again to **B350** when THREE more sessions collided on B348 (PR #255 calibrate-box, a Markup-sidebar feature, and this). B350 was the next free after B349 at this push; the other two B348 entries belong to other already-merged sessions and are left as-is. Code comments + tests + harness all carry B350.)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B350 also names another item in this file:** “Stitcher: aggregated notes/legend across the set + Bluebeam-style detail-callout "cloud…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B350* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B350 against all of them.
`[x]` **Shipped + verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/stitch-tool-stress-test-1tvw5b`).** Adversarial pass over the stitch core (`stitchGeom.js`, `autoStitch.js`, `sheetGroups.js`, `sheetMeta.js`) — drove each engine with the inputs a messy real-world PDF set throws at it and fixed four ways it could **fail silently** (the worst kind here: a bad transform flings a sheet off-canvas, or — worse — butts two drawings together at the wrong size/place and the takeoff reads a confident wrong number). All four follow the owner rule **"a wrong stitch is worse than an un-stitched one"**: when a signal is unreliable the sheet is left **unplaced → manual-Align safety net**, never auto-guessed.
- **Non-finite endpoints (NaN/Infinity) used to slip past the degenerate-baseline guard** — `Math.hypot(NaN) < 1` is `NaN < 1` → `false`, so a NaN coordinate (bad read / mis-built drawing area) reached `solveM`, produced a NaN matrix, and poisoned the sheet transform **and** the whole composite's bbox (every `Math.min/max` over it → NaN). `alignBaselinesDegenerate` now rejects any non-finite point. (`stitchGeom.js`)
- **Contradictory match-line labels produced a wrong (overlapping/mirrored) stitch** — if both sheets claimed the seam on their "right", `buildAdjacency` trusted it. It now treats the **geometric opposite** as the source of truth and **drops the edge** when a sheet's own label contradicts it (→ manual Align). (`autoStitch.js`)
- **Mismatched page sizes were silently rescaled** — a similarity fit from two endpoints will shrink/blow up a half-size detail page to make the seam meet. `autoPlaceGroup` now rejects a placement whose implied scale strays past **`MAX_STITCH_SCALE` (±25%)** and leaves the sheet for manual Align. (`autoStitch.js`)
- **Grouping chained across a major rollover** — the packed `ordinal` (major·100+minor) made `C-1.99 → C-2.00` look consecutive (and could collide two codes onto one ordinal). `consecutiveCodes` now compares the parsed major/minor by numbering level, so a rollover starts a new logical sheet. (`sheetGroups.js`)
- **New `test/stitchStress.test.js` — 29 adversarial tests** across 8 break-strategy groups (non-finite/degenerate coords, contradictory seams, size mismatch, cycles/duplicates/self-refs/missing targets, sheet-code edge cases, reader junk/empty/huge input, a **300-iteration randomized fuzz** asserting the partition + finiteness + scale-band invariants, and the measure-over-unaligned guard). Full suite green (**879 tests**, lint 0 errors, build clean). Pure-engine + DI hardening, so no live-browser verification needed; the manual-Align safety net and text-layer path are unchanged. **(Round 1 — PR #248, merged 2026-06-21.)**

**Round 2 — reader / grouping / calibration path (follow-up, same B350).** After round 1 hardened the placement geometry, a second adversarial pass over the text reads and takeoff math turned up one real functional gap and locked in the rest:
- **A set numbered past sheet 99 was invisible to grouping AND auto-stitch** — `parseSheetNumber` capped the major at `\d{1,2}`, so `C-100` read as `""`, while `parseSheetCode` (sheetGroups) and the match-line `SHEET_REF` (sheetMeta) both already accepted 3 digits. A sheet with no readable number can't be chained by contiguity or found in the seam graph's by-number index, so a `C-100…C-110` plan set never grouped or stitched. Bumped the **label-anchored** read to `\d{1,3}` (still requires a "SHEET NO." label, so the `A195` grid-ref guard is intact). (`titleBlockParse.js`)
- **New `test/stitchReaderStress.test.js` — 13 tests**: 3-digit sheets now read + group + auto-stitch end-to-end (incl. through the wired `readSheetMeta`); date reading rejects impossible months/days/years and picks the newest under a huge-blob load; takeoff math (`dist`/`polyArea`/`pathLength`/`centroidOf`/`measureValue`/`measureLabel`) degrades on too-few / collinear / concave / coincident / non-finite input and **never fabricates a number** — a non-finite calibration reads a safe sentinel ("set scale" / "—"), never a plausible-looking figure. Full suite green (**892 tests**, lint 0 errors, build clean).

**Round 3 — LIVE interactive stress (headless browser).** Rounds 1–2 fuzzed the pure engines; round 3 attacks the one surface they can't reach — the real React interaction layer — with a new headless harness **`ui-audit/verify-stitch-stress.mjs`** (V92, **14/14 checks, 0 page errors**) driving a synthetic 4-page civil set: **(S1)** a degenerate manual Align (two coincident reference clicks) is refused and the sheet is **not flung**; **(S2)** measuring over a not-yet-aligned sheet is **blocked** and commits nothing; **(S3)** an interrupted pan (window `blur` mid-drag) doesn't crash or stick; **(S4)** ± zoom-button spam **clamps** at 5%/800%; **(S5)** a 45-click random fuzz across all tools never crashes the Stitcher. The hypothesized "remove a sheet mid-Align → deref `undefined.M`" crash was found **already guarded** (the sibling session's B344 fix, `if (!sheet) { setAlign(null); … }` in `onDown`) — so this round adds a permanent interaction regression net rather than a new fix. No source change; harness + V-log only.

### B321 — `deleteReview` orphans the Drive copy when the cloud record can't be read `[Doc Review / Files]` (bug)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-1" 2026-06-21; minted **B321**)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/bold-bohr-hohz2x`).** Deleting a review no longer leaves source bytes orphaned in Google Drive (or Supabase Storage) when the cloud record read misses.
- **Already shipped (B207 Drive wiring):** the brief's primary point — "there is no Drive delete anywhere in the code" — was already addressed: `deleteReview` removes every `sources[].driveKey` through `deleteFromDrive` (a `DELETE /api/files?key=…`) alongside the Supabase `BUCKET.remove(keys)`.
- **Residual fix (this session):** if `loadReview(id)` returns `null` (a transient network miss), `sources` was `[]`, so **neither** the Supabase objects **nor** the Drive objects were removed. `deleteReview` now falls back to the synchronous **local mirror** (`readDraft(uid, id)`, which carries the same `sources[]` incl. `storageKey` + `driveKey`) to recover the file list, so cleanup still runs. Best-effort and in parallel; it never blocks the row delete, and the legacy `<uid>/<id>/` folder sweep is unchanged.
- **Verified — lint 0 · 788 tests · build green** (8 new in `test/docPersistence.test.js`); doc-review lazy chunk intact. The storage path is auth-gated (cloud + Drive), so the unit tests assert the graceful-degrade contract; a signed-in delete-with-Drive is the live check (logged in VERIFICATION).
> **Dedup:** primary already done under B207; this is the loadReview-null residual. Distinct from B38(a) (upsert re-file orphaning).

### B322 — "Open PDF…" and every Stitcher sheet upload to Supabase only, never Drive `[Doc Review / Stitch + Files]` (bug)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-2" 2026-06-21; minted **B322**)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/bold-bohr-hohz2x`).** Interactively-opened single sheets and **all** stitched sheets now go through the **same Drive-first / Supabase-fallback path** as filing, instead of Supabase-only.
- **One shared storage policy:** added `reviewStore.storeSource(srcId, blob, { projectId, discipline, fileName })` — push to Google Drive (the primary home); only if Drive doesn't take it, fall back to Supabase Storage. `fileNewReview` was refactored to call it too, so there's a single source of truth for "where a source's bytes live" (no more two slightly-different copies of the policy).
- **Call sites:** `DocReview.openFile` and `Stitcher.openFiles` now call `storeSource` (were `uploadSource` → Supabase only) and persist `driveKey`; both `buildSnapshot`s carry `driveKey`; `Stitcher.loadStitch` reads back Drive-first then Supabase (`DocReview.fetchSourceBytes` already did). 
- **Why it matters:** (a) these files now live in Drive like filed ones (the "Drive is the primary file home" direction); (b) they **bypass Supabase's 50 MB per-file cap on the happy path** — an E-size sheet or a large multi-sheet set that used to silently flag `oversize` ("re-drop on load") now stores in Drive; (c) stitched sheets carry a `driveKey`, so a stitched set can read its sheets back from Drive.
- **Verified — lint 0 · 788 tests · build green** (`storeSource` degrade-path test); doc-review lazy chunk intact. The full Drive round-trip needs the (not-yet-deployed) Drive backend + sign-in, so it's the live check; the fallback to Supabase keeps today's behaviour until Drive is on.
> **Dedup:** net-new; the viewer (B288–B296) and stitch-guard (B300–B302) batches never touched the storage backend choice. Pairs with B321 (Drive delete) and B323 (keyless-source window).

### B323 — A source saved with a null key during the upload window becomes unfetchable on a quick reload `[Doc Review]` (bug)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-3" 2026-06-21; minted **B323**)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/bold-bohr-hohz2x`).** A file opened and then reloaded **before its upload resolved** no longer strands the backdrop with a pointer the loader can't fetch.
- **Cause:** `openFile`/`openFiles` set the source into state immediately with `storageKey:null` (and no `driveKey`), which made it an autosave dep; the debounce + the synchronous local mirror could capture that **keyless** source before the upload's `.then(setSource w/ key)` ran. A reload in that window saved a record pointing at a source with no key → `fetchSourceBytes` couldn't fetch it → a permanent "re-open it to view", even though the bytes may have landed.
- **Fix:** `buildSnapshot` now persists a source only when it's actually stored — `isStoredSource(s) = !!(s.storageKey || s.driveKey || s.oversize)`. While a just-opened/added file is still uploading (keyless), it's **omitted** from the saved `sources`, so a mid-upload reload can't save a broken pointer; the markups still save, and once the upload resolves the source is persisted normally (its key change re-triggers autosave). Applied to both the single-sheet and the per-sheet Stitcher snapshots. (`oversize` still counts as "stored" → the existing graceful "re-drop on load" path is unchanged.)
- **Verified — lint 0 · 788 tests · build green** (`isStoredSource` unit tests: keyed/drive/oversize ⇒ persistable; keyless/absent ⇒ not); doc-review lazy chunk intact.
> **Dedup:** net-new; shares the `isStoredSource` predicate with B322's snapshots. Backdrop-only loss (markups were always safe).

### B324 — A genuine edit made within the post-open suspend window isn't flagged dirty → never reaches the cloud `[Doc Review]` (bug)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-4" 2026-06-21; minted **B324**)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/bold-bohr-hohz2x`).** An edit made right after opening/resuming a review (inside the ~1.5 s programmatic-load window) is now mirrored, flagged dirty, and reaches the cloud.
- **Cause:** the autosave effect early-returned for the whole suspend window (B19), skipping **both** the local mirror **and** `dirtyRef=true`. The unmount/hide flush gates its cloud upsert on `dirtyRef`, so an edit in that window never reached the cloud (lost cross-device, or entirely on a tab crash before flush). The window is armed at load-start, so it usually elapsed harmlessly during a large PDF's fetch — it bit on small/cached PDFs.
- **Fix:** the per-tick decision is now a pure, unit-tested `lib/autosavePlan.js → planAutosave({enabled, empty, loadEcho, suspended})`. The programmatic-load **echo** is identified precisely by a `loadEchoRef` flag (armed by `suspendSave`, consumed on the echo tick) rather than by the blunt time window, so it's still skipped — but a **genuine edit**, even inside the window, now **mirrors + flags dirty** (so it's recoverable on-device AND flushes to the cloud); only its **debounced cloud re-save** stays suppressed while suspended, preserving B19's "don't re-stamp the just-loaded snapshot" intent (and B44's "no re-upsert of unchanged data on a mode toggle").
- **Verified — lint 0 · 788 tests · build green** (`planAutosave` unit tests cover: load echo ⇒ consume only; edit-in-window ⇒ mirror+dirty, no debounce-save; edit-out-of-window ⇒ mirror+dirty+save; blank/disabled ⇒ nothing).
> **Dedup:** net-new; interacts with B19 (suspendSave) + B44 (dirty-gated flush), both preserved. Not covered by any open item.

### B325 — Stitcher pan crash: "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'panX')" when a pan is interrupted `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-21: "its broken, i was on the stitcher and it broke"; minted **B325** — a hot `main` had reached B324)*
`[x]` **Fixed + shipped 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/awesome-feynman-i7wypf`).** The pan handler's `setView` updater read `drag.current` **inside** the deferred updater. That updater runs in React's render phase, which for a continuous `pointermove` can be deferred a tick; a discrete event in between — `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, or the **B270** blur/visibility gesture-abort — nulls `drag.current` first. Reading the ref then dereferenced null and threw in the render phase → the Document Review **error boundary** caught it ("hit an error and couldn't load") and the whole stitcher went down. A real user hits this by tab-switching / losing focus / a pointer-cancel mid-pan. **Fix:** capture the drag origin into a local and close over it via a pure `panTo()` helper in `lib/stitchGeom.js`, so an aborted gesture can't crash the deferred updater. **Verified:** 4 unit tests (`test/stitchGeom.test.js` — math, null-ref-survival, + a teeth test that the OLD ref-reading pattern throws `/panX/`) and a headless harness (`ui-audit/verify-b325-pan.mjs`: a normal pan moves the world; 12 mid-pan aborts → no error boundary, 0 `panX` errors; pan still works after). lint 0 · build green. VERIFICATION **V84**.

### B316 — Light / dark / system theme with cool-gray light palette `[AppHeader / theming]` (feature) — foundation-scale  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-20; arrived as "NEW-3"; minted **B316** — next free after B272)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B316 also names another item in this file:** “Hard-block (not just warn) measuring over a not-yet-aligned stitch sheet (bug) *(owner …”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B316* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B316 against all of them.
`[x]` Add a theme selector with three modes — **Light**, **Dark**, **System** (`prefers-color-scheme`). App is currently hard-locked to one look; this adds the switch. **Both modes are net-new full surface palettes** (owner decision 2026-06-20, see below): Light = cool gray-white surfaces; Dark = a genuine dark-*surface* mode (dark content panels), **retiring** today's warm cream/paper work area.
> **✓ DECISION (owner, 2026-06-20) — "build a true dark mode":** the app today is **not all-dark** — content surfaces are a warm **cream/paper** ("drafting") palette (`body #efeadf`, panels `#f6f3ec`, ink `#26231e`) under **dark graphite chrome** (top bars + rail, `#14110e`/`#191613`). Asked whether "keep the existing dark unchanged" meant preserve today's cream-content + dark-chrome look, or build a real dark-*surface* mode, the owner chose the latter: build a **genuine dark-surface** Dark mode (dark content panels) and **retire the cream**, alongside the cool-gray Light. **Consequence for scope:** *both* themes are net-new surface palettes — the only "existing dark" that survives is the dark **chrome** (bars/rail); the dark **content-surface** values (dark equivalents of surface-page / surface-raised / borders / text) **don't exist yet and must be designed**, and every one of the ~886 color spots needs a proper two-way (light↔dark) mapping, not a one-way "add light." This increases effort vs. preserving the current look and reinforces the multi-pass-foundation plan below.

> **🔁 UPDATE 2026-06-21 — design RESOLVED + decomposed into B317–B320 (building this session).** The owner ran the theming design through a ChatGPT visual pass; the returned spec settles every open question here. Implemented as four sibling children of this umbrella: **B317** (infrastructure), **B318** (full palette + theme-aware chrome), **B319** (work-surface canvas/sheet), **B320** (contrast + status). B316 stays as the umbrella/record. **Canonical visual reference: `planyr-theming-mockup.html`** — match its *rendered* result, not just raw hexes. ⚠ Owner named that file as the reference but it is **not in the repo** as of this update — request a copy to keep in-repo + diff against. **Two assumptions in THIS item are now reversed/resolved:** (1) ~~"the dark chrome survives unchanged in both themes"~~ → **chrome now themes WITH the app** (light theme = light chrome, dark theme = dark chrome); a permanently-dark bar in an otherwise-white app forces constant pupil readjustment — worst case for eye strain (see B318). (2) the net-new dark surface palette **and** the two-value accent-text question are now **fully specified** in B318. Retire the warm cream, the old always-dark warm chrome (`#14110e`/`#191613`), and the ember accent (`#e8590c`).

**Mechanics (from the owner's spec):**
- Drive theming off `data-theme="light|dark"` on `<html>`. All colors as CSS variables, both themes fully defined.
- **System** resolves via `prefers-color-scheme` and must update **live mid-session** — attach a `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')` change listener.
- Persist the choice (light/dark/system) in **localStorage as source-of-truth on load**; mirror to the `profiles` row (NEW-1) for cross-device. localStorage wins on first paint to avoid a network round-trip.
- **FOUC gotcha (do this FIRST):** an inline script in `index.html <head>` that reads the stored choice (or system pref) and sets `data-theme` **before React mounts** — otherwise every load flashes the wrong theme. ("FOUC" = flash of un-themed content.)
- Theme control lives in the **account dropdown (NEW-2)** or **Settings** — consolidate, don't duplicate.
- Files likely touched: `index.html` (inline pre-paint script), a `ThemeProvider`/context, the token stylesheet (`src/index.css`), the account dropdown (NEW-2), the `profiles` mirror via the NEW-1 hook.

**Light-mode surface tokens (cool gray-white — owner-verified legible):**

| Token | Light value | Dark value |
|---|---|---|
| surface-page | `#F3F5F8` | existing locked dark |
| surface-raised (cards) | `#FFFFFF` | existing locked dark |
| border-default | `#E1E5EB` | existing |
| border-strong (hover) | `#CDD3DC` | existing |
| text-primary | `#1B1E26` | existing |
| text-secondary (muted) | `#565E6E` | existing |
| text-tertiary (hints) | `#8B92A1` | existing |

> ⚠ **Per the decision above, "Dark value = existing" for the *surface* rows is now a net-new true-dark surface palette to be designed** (dark page / dark cards / dark borders / light-on-dark text), NOT the current cream. Only the dark **chrome** (bars/rail) pre-exists. The owner's Light column is fixed; the Dark surface column needs its cool-neutral dark equivalents specced as part of the build.

**Accent pair model:** each module accent is **two tokens** — a **fill/brand** value (unchanged, locked hexes — these already live in `src/shared/ui/moduleAccent.js` as `MODULE_ACCENT`) and an **on-light text** value (tuned, AA-passing as foreground). The `-text` token is theme-dependent.

| Module | fill (both modes) | text — light mode | text — dark mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| Site | `#1D9E75` | `#0F6E56` | `#5DCAA5` |
| Schedule | `#7F77DD` | `#534AB7` | `#AFA9EC` |
| Markup | `#EF9F27` | `#8A5410` | `#EF9F27` |

- **On-fill text rule (both modes):** text/icons **on** an accent fill — Site & Schedule fills carry **white** (`#FFFFFF`); **Markup (amber) fill carries dark text** (`#412402`). White-on-amber is unreadable; enforce wherever a status/tab chip uses the amber fill.
- **Usage rule:** accent-as-**fill** (tab band, active indicator, status-chip bg) → **fill** token. Accent-as-**foreground** (colored text, thin icons, links) → **`-text`** token, never the fill token.
- **Edge case — status palette:** the locked status tokens (Pursuit / Active / On Hold / Complete / Dead) need the same discipline. For each status color used as text/icon on a light surface, **derive programmatically** the nearest variant that clears **AA ≥ 4.5** as foreground on `#FFFFFF`/`#F3F5F8`; keep originals as fills with the same on-fill rule. **Flag any status color whose foreground variant can't reach 4.5** for review (don't hand-pick).
- **Constraint (unchanged):** module accents stay confined to the **top tab row only** — light mode doesn't change that.

> **Build plan / scope (grounds the "foundation-scale" tag) — REUSE, don't rebuild:**
> The app has **no central theming layer today**: ~**886 hardcoded hex literals across ~30 files**, **9 local `PAL` objects** (`SitePlanner.jsx`, `MapFinder.jsx`, `AuthPanel.jsx`, `ParcelDrawing.jsx`, `DocReview.jsx`, `Stitcher.jsx`, `ProjectLibrary.jsx`, `ProjectFilesDrawer.jsx`, `ReviewsBar.jsx`), inline styles throughout, plus literals inside `src/index.css`. `MODULE_ACCENT` (`moduleAccent.js`) is already the single source for the **fill** colors → extend it with the `-text` counterparts rather than re-listing hexes. `BrandMark` already takes a `surface="dark|light"` prop (theme-aware) → just feed it the active theme. The Scheduler is an **iframe** (`public/sequence/index.html`) with its **own** colors → needs its own token sheet or a postMessage theme bridge (separate surface).
> Recommended sequence: **(1)** define the full token set for both themes in `:root` / `[data-theme]`; **(2)** FOUC inline script; **(3)** `ThemeProvider` + `matchMedia` live listener + localStorage persistence; **(4)** migrate the 9 PALs + inline literals + `index.css` literals to consume tokens (the bulk — do it per-workspace, verifying each surface); **(5)** AA-derive the status palette; **(6)** theme the Scheduler iframe; **(7)** wire the control into NEW-2/Settings + the NEW-1 cross-device mirror. A shell-only/partial theme that leaves the canvas/map/doc-review hardcoded would be a **misleading half** (per the "finish the job" rule) — so this ships as a deliberate multi-pass foundation, ideally after NEW-1 + NEW-2 land.

### B317 — Light / Dark / System theme infrastructure `[Global / theming]` (feature) — child of B316; build FIRST  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-21 via ChatGPT spec; arrived as "NEW-1"; minted **B317**)*
`[x]` Build the theming foundation every module inherits. **Ships together with B318–B320; build B317 first (they depend on it).**
- **Token system:** CSS custom properties driven by `data-theme="light|dark"` on `<html>`. Components reference **tokens only**, never raw hex. **Extend** the existing locked token set (`:root` vars in `src/index.css` + the per-file `PAL` objects) rather than starting fresh — repoint them at tokens.
- **Three modes:** Light, Dark, System. **System** follows the OS via `window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')` and must **live-update** when the OS flips — attach a `change` listener, don't read once at load.
- **Persistence:** store the choice in `localStorage['planyr.theme']`; **default System** on first run.
- **No theme flash (FOUC):** apply the resolved theme in a tiny inline `<head>` script **before first paint**, so the page never flashes the wrong colors before React boots.
- **Switch UI:** three-way control in Settings and/or the **row-1 settings menu in `AppHeader`**.
- Files: new `ThemeProvider`/context, the global token stylesheet (`src/index.css`), `AppHeader`, `index.html` (pre-paint script).
> Lineage: the **infrastructure half of B316**. Finalizes B316's FOUC/ThemeProvider/matchMedia/localStorage mechanics. localStorage is source-of-truth on load; the `profiles` cross-device mirror stays a later additive follow-on, not a prerequisite.

### B310 — Accidental parcel selection while panning the planner canvas `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-1" 2026-06-20; first filed B300, renumbered **B310** — concurrent `main` consumed B300–B309)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-20 (branch `claude/blissful-mccarthy-dkozi0`).** With parcels rendered, grabbing the planner canvas to pan kept registering as a parcel select — `startMoveParcel` (`SitePlanner.jsx`) fired `setSel` on pointer-**down** and `e.stopPropagation()` blocked the background pan, so a press anywhere on a lot selected it whether the gesture was a click or the start of a drag. Navigating across lots felt like constantly clicking into them.
- **Fix — click-vs-drag discrimination on the parcel layer.** A press on a **locked** parcel (the default every county-pulled / drawn lot carries — created `locked:true` in all six creation paths) now starts a **PAN** (`drag.current.mode:"pan"`) tagged with the parcel id + the press origin (`tapParcel`, `downX/downY/downT`), instead of selecting. On pointer-**up** (`onUp`) it counts as a deliberate **click → select** only if travel ≤ `PARCEL_CLICK_SLOP_PX` (**5px**, measured in SCREEN px so it's zoom-independent) **and** the press was < `PARCEL_CLICK_MS` (**400ms**); any larger/longer movement panned and leaves the selection untouched. Uses Pointer Events + `setPointerCapture` (already the canvas's model) so the up fires even if the pointer left the polygon, and the gesture joins the existing `abortGesture` recovery (`capturePidRef`) so an interrupted parcel-pan can't strand the grab cursor (B271-class).
- **Preserved:** a deliberately **unlocked** parcel still grabs-to-move on press (you unlocked it to reshape/move it — matches elements); the full-polygon hit area is unchanged (we gate on gesture *intent*, never shrink the target); Shift-click-to-merge and align-edge picking still work. Space / the Pan tool remain the always-on pan escape hatches.
- **Verified — lint 0 · 712 tests · build green; `SitePlannerApp` lazy chunk intact.** Headless on the built app (`ui-audit/verify-b310-b311.mjs`, logged-out, seeded one locked parcel): a deselected→**click selects** (stroke→#c2410c / width 3); a **drag of 95px pans and does NOT select** (stroke stays #5b6650 / width 2, the parcel's on-screen box shifted +95px), **0 page JS errors**. Logged as **VERIFICATION V78**.

`[x]` **Done 2026-06-20 (branch `claude/blissful-mccarthy-dkozi0`).** A **Row-2 toolbar toggle** ("Select parcels", next to Snap, shown only when the plan has parcels) as a hard-off fallback for pure browse/measure workflows where zero accidental selection is wanted. **Non-hijacking default = ON:** click a lot to select it, dragging always pans (normal selection works out of the box thanks to B310, so the toggle isn't the primary gate). **OFF:** a press on a parcel is click-through — `startMoveParcel` returns *without* `stopPropagation`, so the event falls through to the background pan exactly as if it landed on empty canvas; a click never selects. Turning it OFF also drops any current parcel selection so browse mode is clean.
- **Persistence:** stored as `settings.parcelSelect` (default `true` in `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`), so it rides the existing per-project Site Model `settings` save/restore path — saved per project, restored on reopen. No new store, no localStorage key.

### B315 — Undo (Ctrl+Z) unreliable after moving a building `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-1" 2026-06-21; renumbered B310→B313→**B315** as a very hot `main` twice consumed the number — B310/B311 parcel click-vs-drag + B312 auto-filing, then B313/B314 multi-tab + optimistic-concurrency)*
`[x]` **Fixed + headless-verified 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/ecstatic-ritchie-ihzkym`).** Moving a building then pressing Ctrl+Z now reverts the **entire** move in one step, every time (was: sometimes nothing, sometimes a partial revert).
- **Root cause (confirmed by reading, NOT guessed — the brief's hypothesis #2, the race):** the drag-move transaction boundary was already correct — `startMove`/`startMoveParcel`/`startGroupMove` push history **once** at drag-start, nothing during the drag, nothing on pointer-up (so hypothesis #1, per-frame pushes, did **not** apply). The defect was that `stateRef` — the single source both for the snapshot pushed onto the undo stack AND for the baseline `undo()` compares against (the B32 no-op dedup `histKey(stateRef.current)` check) — was updated in a **passive `useEffect` (no deps)**. A ref written in a passive effect lags the committed render by a paint, so a quick undo↔drag sequence could snapshot/compare a **stale** state → revert to the wrong frame (partial) or skip the frame in the dedup loop (does nothing). Timing-dependent ⇒ intermittent, matching the fuzzy repro.
- **Fix:** (1) `stateRef.current` is now assigned **during render** instead of in a passive effect, so `pushHistory`/`undo`/`redo` always read the TRUE current state — the race window is gone. (2) Extracted the stack + dedup into a **pure, unit-tested** module `lib/history.js` (`createHistoryStack({ keyOf })` → push/undo/redo/drop/canUndo/canRedo), matching the `stitchGeom.js` precedent; `undo`/`redo` take the live state **explicitly**, so the stale-ref class of bug can't recur. (3) **Interrupted-drag edge case** (brief's list): Esc / lost-focus / pointer-cancel **mid-move** now reverts to the pre-drag snapshot stashed on `drag.current` and drops the dangling frame (`cancelActiveMove` in `abortGesture`), so a cancelled drag leaves no half-recorded command.
- **Edge cases covered + verified:** one drag = one undo (full revert); redo restores; two moves = two undos (one each); multi-select/group move = one push = one undo (geometry-agnostic stack); independent transactions don't clobber each other (a move-undo doesn't touch an unrelated vertex edit); Esc-mid-drag cancels cleanly.
- **Verified:** lint 0 · **full suite green** (11 new in `test/history.test.js`, incl. a deterministic repro of the stale-baseline failure mode) · build green. Headless on the built app (`ui-audit/verify-b315.mjs`, chromium-1194, logged-out): drag a building 300px → **one Ctrl+Z snaps it fully back, Δ=0.0px** (not partial); redo; two-moves-two-undos; Esc-mid-drag revert; **0 JS errors**.
> **Dedup:** net-new. **Related but distinct from B32 (done)** — B32 stopped no-op edits from polluting the stack (the *dedup* the `while`-loop does); B315 is the *stale-baseline race* that made even a clean move-frame revert wrong/skipped. NOT a duplicate of any open item; no open item covered undo-after-move. Kept as ONE item (the brief said split only if the diagnosis turned out to be redo- or multi-select-specific — it wasn't; the race affects all undo, redo + multi-select already work as separate transactions).

### B308 — Server-side Mapillary token proxy so the street-level layer works for all users `[Site Planner / functions]` (feature)  *(coworker-chat "NEW-1" 2026-06-20; first filed B303 then renumbered **B308** — concurrent `main` landed a Doc Review batch on B303–B307, so both can't share the number)*
`[x]` **Built + shipped 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/busy-allen-ofgy9l`).** The "Poles & hydrants from street imagery" layer now works for **every visitor with no per-user token**, and the Mapillary access token never reaches the public bundle or any client request URL — it lives only as an encrypted Cloudflare Pages Secret the owner set (`MAPILLARY_TOKEN`, Production). Resolves the audit's *token-in-bundle* + *token-in-URL* LOW findings; honours the KEY DECISION "Mapillary token is a secret."
- **Pages Function** `functions/api/mapillary/[[path]].js` reads the token from the runtime binding `context.env.MAPILLARY_TOKEN` (NOT `import.meta.env`/a `VITE_*` var) and forwards to the Graph API. **Guardrails** (pure helpers in `functions/api/mapillary/_proxy.js`, unit-tested): allow-list ONLY `map_features` + fields `id,object_value,geometry`; **Origin check** (same-origin / `*.planyr.io` / `*.planyr.pages.dev`, foreign Origin → 403); bbox/limit validation; short edge-cache (`max-age=300`) to cut quota. **Dormant-graceful:** no token (e.g. a Preview deploy, which doesn't have the secret) → 503 + empty `data`, the client shows "not available here", never a hard error.
- **Client:** new leaflet-free `lib/mapillaryClient.js` (`mapillaryRequestUrl`/`pickDetections`); `evidenceLayers.fetchMapillary` calls the same-origin `/api/mapillary/map_features` with **NO `access_token`** by default (a pasted token = an optional power-user override straight to Mapillary). Removed the no-token gate in `mapillaryLayer` + `syncOverlayLayers` and the `needsSetup` flag on the layer; the LayerPanel box is now "Works automatically — (Advanced) use your own token". `.env.example` + README document the secret-lives-in-Cloudflare rule.
- **Verified:** lint 0 · **722 tests** (10 new, `test/mapillaryProxy.test.js`: allow-list, Origin, limit-clamp, and the client default carrying no token) · build green; **0 `MLY|` token literals + 0 `VITE_MAPILLARY_TOKEN` in `dist/`**. Headless on the built app (`gis-verify/mapillary-proxy-verify.mjs`): toggling the layer with no token → it loads via **same-origin `/api/mapillary/map_features`**, **0 token leaks** in any request URL, **no** direct `graph.mapillary.com` call, graceful degrade in preview, **0 JS errors**.
- **⏳ LIVE confirm (the one piece the sandbox can't do — a Pages Function needs the Cloudflare runtime):** on planyr.io Production after the next deploy, zoom ≥ 16 over a covered area → pole/hydrant dots render via `/api/mapillary/…`, token nowhere in page source/bundle/URLs. Logged in VERIFICATION. (The owner already set the secret, so this is just the deploy + a coworker eyeball.)
> **Dedup:** net-new; builds on B285/B286 (Mapillary rename + gating). The cleanup half (drop the dead `VITE_MAPILLARY_TOKEN` read) stays as **B309** `[~]`, held until this is confirmed live.

### B303 — Undo / redo for Document Review markups + calibration `[Doc Review / Markup]` (feature)  *(arrived as "NEW-1" 2026-06-20 owner chat; provisionally B283, renumbered **B303** — concurrent `main` consumed B283–B302; batch B303–B307)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-20 (branch `claude/stoic-faraday-th9mp8`).** Repro: place/delete/move a markup or measurement, press Ctrl/⌘-Z → nothing happened; the workspace had no history at all, so a mis-edit was unrecoverable. **Fix:** **Ctrl/⌘-Z undo, Ctrl/⌘-Shift-Z + Ctrl-Y redo** in BOTH `DocReview.jsx` (single sheet) and `Stitcher.jsx` (stitched set), plus on-canvas **↶ / ↷** buttons (disabled when there's nothing to undo/redo).
- **Pattern reused, not reinvented:** mirrors the Site Planner's `pushHistory` — `pastRef`/`futureRef` of editable-state snapshots taken **by reference** (DocReview `{markups, calByPage, calInfo}`; Stitcher `{measures, ftPerUnit}`), with a `histKey` signature so `undo` **skips frames identical to the current state** — the **B32/B105 lesson** that a stray push can't make Ctrl-Z look like a no-op. `pushHistory()` fires only on a REAL mutation; the background stated-scale auto-scan (B267) deliberately does NOT push. History resets when the document context changes (open new PDF / load / new review).
- **Covers `main`'s viewer edits too:** a markup **move** (B293, committed on pointer-up) and a **text create/edit/delete** (B293 inline editor) each push one frame, so the new editing affordances are undoable as well as plain draws.
- **Poly-vertex placement:** mid-draw, Ctrl-Z (and Backspace/Delete) step back the **last placed vertex** of a polygon/area/count draft before falling through to full undo / delete-selection.
- **Verified headless** (`ui-audit/verify-b303-b307.mjs`): draw a rect → Ctrl-Z removes it → Ctrl-Shift-Z and Ctrl-Y each restore it; undo disabled before any edit; same proven in the Stitcher.

### B304 — Manual Calibrate validates input (no more silent mis-calibration) `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-2" 2026-06-20 owner chat; provisionally B284, renumbered **B304**; batch B303–B307)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-20 (branch `claude/stoic-faraday-th9mp8`).** Repro: Calibrate → click two points → at the length prompt type a non-decimal form (e.g. **"1/8"** or **"1:240"**) → `parseFloat` returned **1** and the sheet calibrated to a wrong scale with NO warning, silently poisoning every downstream measurement; gibberish ("abc") silently did nothing. **Root cause:** `parseFloat(window.prompt(...))` stops at the first non-numeric char, and the invalid branch `return`ed with no feedback.
- **Fix:** replaced `window.prompt` with an **inline on-canvas entry box** (honoring the owner "no dialog boxes" rule, like `main`'s B293 text editor) backed by a new tested parser **`parseFeet`** (`lib/parseLength.js`). It validates the WHOLE string: accepts plain feet (`120`, `120.5`, `120'`), **feet-and-inches** (`38'-7 3/4"`), and explicit fractional feet (`12 1/2 ft`); **rejects** scale ratios (`1:240`), bare ambiguous fractions (`1/8`), non-numeric junk, and zero/negative — each with a clear inline message. A bad entry keeps the box open to fix; a blank cancels. Applied in BOTH `DocReview.jsx` and `Stitcher.jsx`.
- **Dedup:** distinct from **B267/B268** (auto-calibrate / scale cross-check) — the **manual-entry** path they don't cover. Clears the **calibration** half of the B155/B156 "no dialog boxes" note; `main`'s B293 already converted the **text** prompt, so only ParcelDrawing's calibrate prompt remains under B155.
- **Verified:** unit — `test/parseLength.test.js` (7 cases incl. the exact "1/8" / "1:240" / "abc" bugs). Headless — the inline box opens (no prompt), **rejects "1/8" and stays uncalibrated**, rejects "1:240" as a ratio, and **accepts "100" → sheet calibrated** (single sheet + Stitcher).

### B307 — Measurement labels sit at the path midpoint / true centroid `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-5" 2026-06-20 owner chat; provisionally B287, renumbered **B307**; batch B303–B307)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-20 (branch `claude/stoic-faraday-th9mp8`).** Repro: a Distance label rendered on the first endpoint (`pts[Math.floor((len-1)/2)]` resolves to `pts[0]` for a 2-point line); an Area label sat at the vertex average, which can fall outside a concave (L-shaped) region. **Fix** (new pure helpers in `lib/takeoff.js`): **`midOfPath(pts, closed)`** anchors distance/perimeter labels at the true **arc-length midpoint**; **`centroidOf(pts)`** anchors area labels at the **area-weighted centroid**, and when that lands outside a concave shape it drops to the midpoint of the widest interior scanline span so the label stays **inside**. Wired into `DocReview.jsx` (distance/perimeter/area) and `Stitcher.jsx` (area). Coexists with `main`'s B296 (the label's 1-dp numeric format) — B307 is the label's POSITION.

### B300 — Stitcher alignment has no degenerate-baseline guard; coincident clicks fling the sheet with a garbage transform `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-1" 2026-06-20 owner chat; first filed B288 then renumbered **B300** — concurrent `main` consumed B288–B299; batch B300–B302)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-20 (branch `claude/admiring-hypatia-xjv8a1`).** Repro (numerically verified): in Stitch, aligning a sheet means clicking two matching points; if the two clicks on the moving sheet (or the two reference points) land on ~the same spot, `solveM`'s `lb = Math.hypot(vb) || 1` **masked the zero baseline** and returned an extreme similarity transform (e.g. `solveM(b1==b2, A1, A2 100 apart)` → ×100 scale, e/f ≈ −500), throwing the sheet far off-canvas at huge scale — silently, and Stitch has no undo. **Fix:** extracted the pure stitch geometry (`fwd`/`inv`/`solveM`/`sheetBBox`) out of `Stitcher.jsx` into a unit-testable **`lib/stitchGeom.js`**, and added **`alignBaselinesDegenerate(b1,b2,A1,A2)`** + `MIN_ALIGN_BASE`, which rejects an alignment whose moving-sheet baseline `|b2−b1|` **OR** reference baseline `|A2−A1|` is below a small threshold (mirrors DocReview's Calibrate "line too short" guard). The align commit checks it **before** `solveM`: on a degenerate baseline it shows the banner ("Those two points are too close together — pick two points farther apart…") and restarts the alignment at step 0, leaving the sheet **untouched**; only a healthy baseline applies the transform (and now also stamps the sheet `aligned:true`, see B301).
- **Verified:** 8 unit tests (`test/stitchGeom.test.js`, incl. the runaway-scale case the guard blocks + `solveM` scale/rotation recovery + `fwd`/`inv` round-trip) and **headless on the built app** (`ui-audit/verify-b300-b302.mjs`, chromium-1228): a degenerate Align shows the banner and the sheet's `<g transform>` is **unchanged** (not flung); a real Align still succeeds. lint 0 · build green; DocReview lazy chunk still splits (stitchGeom rides inside it).
> **Dedup (batch B300–B302):** net-new — no existing item covers the stitch alignment math. NOT main's single-sheet-viewer **B288–B296** (zoom/pan/markup-edit) nor its auto-filing **B299** (server-side title-block read), all different surfaces; distinct from **B181/B182/B183** (the *map* placement cascade) and **B130/B131** (parking). Shares `lib/stitchGeom.js` with B301.

### B301 — Measuring over a not-yet-aligned sheet silently uses the composite scale → wrong quantities `[Doc Review / Stitch]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-2" 2026-06-20 owner chat; first filed B289 then renumbered **B301**; batch B300–B302)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-20 (branch `claude/admiring-hypatia-xjv8a1`).** Repro: add a second sheet (it drops at identity scale, offset to the right) and draw a Distance/Area over it **before** pressing Align — the measurement applied the single composite calibration (ft per world unit, defined by sheet 1), so if that sheet's real scale differed the reading was **silently wrong** (and even at a shared scale its position/rotation could be off). **Fix:** each placed sheet now carries an **`aligned`** flag — the first sheet *is* the world frame (auto-aligned `true`); every later sheet starts `false` and flips to `true` only when its Align completes (B300's commit path). Unaligned sheets are **flagged visually** — an amber dashed "⚠ Not aligned — click Align" overlay on the canvas, plus a "⚠ Not aligned — measurements may be off" chip + amber-emphasized Align button in the Placed-sheets list. Committing a Distance/Area whose points fall over an unaligned sheet (**`measureOverUnaligned`** / `sheetContains` in `lib/stitchGeom.js`) raises a **warning banner** ("Heads up: that measurement is over a sheet that isn't aligned yet — Align it first…"). **Warn, not block** (the app's "surface it loudly, let the user decide" principle). The flag is persisted in the stitch snapshot and restored on load — older saves default their non-base sheets to aligned, so nothing already-saved is falsely flagged.
- **Verified:** unit tests for `sheetContains` + `measureOverUnaligned` (warns only over an `aligned:false` sheet; never over the base or with no sheets) and **headless**: a fresh 2nd sheet shows the canvas overlay + the panel chip, a measurement over it shows the warning, and a successful Align clears both. lint 0 · build green.
- **↑ Superseded by B316 (2026-06-21, owner call "don't let it measure on uncalibrated things"):** the **warn** became a **hard block** — a Distance/Area point over an un-aligned sheet is now refused at click time (`blockedOverUnaligned`, nothing commits), and the chip reads "Not aligned — Align before measuring." `measureOverUnaligned`/`aligned`-state unchanged. See B316 / V83.

### B302 — Degenerate 2-point Area (0 sf) and 2-point Perimeter (single segment) are committable `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-3" 2026-06-20 owner chat; first filed B290 then renumbered **B302**; batch B300–B302)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-20 (branch `claude/admiring-hypatia-xjv8a1`).** Repro (numerically verified): `finishDraft` committed Area/Perimeter at ≥2 points, but a real polygon needs ≥3 — a 2-point Area saved as **0 sf** (shoelace) and a 2-point Perimeter drew closed yet measured only the single segment (10 ft for a 10-unit span at 1 ft/u, not the 20 ft a closed loop implies), leaving meaningless zero/half entries in the takeoff list. **Fix:** added **`MIN_MEASURE_PTS` + `canCommitMeasure(kind,n)`** to `lib/takeoff.js` (area/perimeter ≥3, distance 2, count 1 — matching what `polyArea`/`pathLength` actually need) and gated **both** finish paths on it — Enter/`finishDraft` and (after merging main's B291 phantom-point fix) double-click/`onDbl` — so a 2-point Area/Perimeter is a no-op (the draft is cleared) whichever way you finish, consistent with the existing count min-point guard. Other kinds (distance/rect/cloud/calibrate) are unaffected.
- **Verified:** unit tests for `canCommitMeasure` (the ≥3 / 2 / 1 contract) + the degenerate-geometry rationale (2-pt area = 0; a 2-pt "closed" path = one 10-unit segment, not 20; a real 3-pt loop closes 3+4+5=12) and **headless**: a 2-point Area finished by Enter or double-click commits nothing and the takeoff stays "No measurements yet", while a 3-point Area commits one polygon. lint 0 · build green.
> **Dedup:** minor severity (clutter, not corrupted totals — a 0-sf area contributes 0 to the rollup), filed with B300/B301 but a separate surface (`takeoff.js` / single-sheet Markup). Complements main's **B291** (which stripped the double-click's phantom points) by also enforcing the ≥3 minimum on that finish path.

### B299 — Auto-filing: drop a drawing → it reads the title block → matches a project → files itself `[Document Review / Server + Files]` (feature)  *(owner HANDOFF 2026-06-20; first built as B270, renumbered through a very hot `main` that consumed B270–B298 — incl. a different **B270** (Project Files drop-zone queue) and a different **B297** (account profiles) — so it landed at the real next free ID **B299** at merge time)*
`[x]` **Built + wired + tested this session (branch `claude/sleepy-archimedes-gts4wa`).** The auto-filing **backend tranche**: drop a PDF → a server-side title-block read → match to one of the named projects → auto-route + auto-name, with a "needs filing" tray for anything it can't confidently match. Server-side because the read uses an **API key that must never reach the browser** (KEY DECISIONS) — it lives in the `/server` compute layer (Cloud Run), distinct from Supabase. Status mirrors the convert (B238) / Drive (B207) backends: **code complete, fully unit-tested, wired through the UI, gated dormant** until the owner provisions Cloud Run + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + `DOC_FILING_URL`.
- **Title-block reader** `server/filing/titleBlockReader.js` — mirrors the client `titleReader.js` request shape (model `claude-opus-4-8`, adaptive thinking, a `json_schema` output, the PDF as a base64 `document` block) but runs **server-side** and calls the Messages API over **raw `fetch` with an injectable `fetchImpl`** (like `server/convert/aps.js`), so the Cloud Run image stays dependency-free and the read is unit-testable without a key. **One read, two payoffs:** the same pass captures the FILING fields (project / number / address / parcel / discipline / sheet # / title / revision / date) AND the PLACEMENT-readiness facts (scale callout + bar, north arrow, drawn boundary, stated coord system, labeled dimensions) in the shape of `src/shared/placement/placementFacts.js`. Pixel-geometry (scale-bar length in px, dimension endpoints) is deliberately left to the later CV step (B268/B183) — the read captures presence + printed values, never guessed geometry. `parseStatedScaleFeetPerInch` handles engineer's (`1"=40'`) + architectural (`1/4"=1'-0"`) scales, NTS→null.
- **Matcher** `server/filing/matcher.js` (pure) — scores each project on parcel/account (exact) → job number (exact) → address (token overlap) → name (token overlap), combined noisy-or; **never auto-guesses** (a misfiled drawing is worse than an unfiled one). A confident SINGLE project → `matched`; **no / multiple / low-confidence** → `needsFiling` with a reason (`no-readable-identifiers` / `no-match` / `ambiguous` / `low-confidence`). Thresholds tunable via env. `scoreProject` is transparent (lists the signal it matched on). Auto-name `server/filing/naming.js` mirrors the canonical `reviewStore.composeTitle` "<Project> - <Item> - YYYY.MM.DD".
- **Service + HTTP** `server/filing/filingService.js` (read → match → decision + the index row) + `server/filing/server.js` (`POST /file` body = PDF bytes, `X-Planyr-Projects` header = base64 JSON; `GET /health`) — honest status codes (200 real decision / 400 / 413 / 422 unreadable / 503 not-configured), **never a 200 with a junk decision**. `Dockerfile` (no native binary, no npm install — built-ins only) + `README.md`. The reader/service/server are injectable end-to-end (mirrors `dwgConvert.test.js`).
- **File-facts index (Supabase Postgres, NOT /server)** — `src/workspaces/doc-review/db/file_facts.sql`: `public.file_facts` (one small row per filed drawing: project / discipline / sheet / revision / date / match confidence / needs-filing / placement jsonb), RLS private-by-default identical in shape to `doc_reviews`, indexed `(user_id, project_id, discipline, doc_date desc)` for the north-star "map → project → discipline → latest set" without re-reading the PDF. Client I/O `reviewStore.upsertFileFacts/listFileFacts` (degrade gracefully if unmigrated) + pure helpers `lib/fileIndex.js` (`toFactsRow`, `mergeFactsIntoReviews` — surfaces captured placement on the drawer's review rows).
- **capturePlacementFacts wired (deliverable #4)** — `src/workspaces/doc-review/lib/autofiling.js` is the real `createIndexProvider`: `capturePlacementFacts` + `autofile` ride the SAME server read. `backendReady` reflects `VITE_AUTOFILE_ENABLED` honestly (false by default → UI never claims "auto-detected" while dormant). Same-origin proxy `functions/api/file.js` (verifies the Supabase session, forwards to Cloud Run `DOC_FILING_URL`; 503 until set). The drawer drop handler auto-files when `backendReady`, else the **exact** prior manual path (a 404/503 is a graceful SKIP, like the Drive path) — **no regression**.
- **Verified — lint 0 · 602 tests (52 new: `test/docFiling.test.js` 37, `test/autofiling.test.js` 15) · build green; doc-review lazy-chunk split intact.** Headless on the built app (`ui-audit/verify-b299-autofiling.mjs`): the Project Files drawer opens, the new `autofilingProvider`/`fileIndex` imports evaluate in a real browser, **0 page/console errors**, auto-filing dormant by default (no spurious "it files itself" behavior). The signed-in drop→read→file round-trip + the live read are the deploy-gated checks (sandbox blocks sign-in + no key) — logged as **VERIFICATION V74**.
- **Dedup:** this is the backend that fills the `createIndexProvider.capturePlacementFacts` seam B180/B181 stubbed and the auto-filing roadmap item; it WRITES THROUGH the Drive substrate (B207) and feeds the placement cascade (B182/B183). Distinct from B266/B267/B268 (the in-Markup sheet-label/scale siblings of the read pass) — those share the title-block read principle but run browser-side on the open sheet; this is the filing index. **Owner to-do (deploy, when ready):** `gcloud run deploy` `server/filing/` + set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (server-side) + point `DOC_FILING_URL` at it + set `VITE_AUTOFILE_ENABLED=1` + run `db/file_facts.sql` once.

### B297 — First/last name capture at signup + a real `profiles` table `[Auth / Backend]` (feature)  *(arrived as "NEW-1"; first labeled B271, renumbered **B297** — concurrent `main` consumed B271–B296)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-20 (branch `claude/eloquent-edison-6anmlb`).** Names are now persisted in a queryable **`public.profiles`** table (one row per `auth.uid()`), not just in auth `user_metadata` — the scalable foundation for the B2B direction (org/role/prefs later). The signup form already collected First/Last/Org; that path is unchanged (still seeds `signUp({ options: { data } })`), but a DB **trigger** now copies those into the table so there's one queryable source of truth for display.
- **Migration (idempotent, run once in the Supabase SQL editor):** `src/workspaces/site-planner/db/profiles.sql` — the `profiles` table (`id uuid pk → auth.users on delete cascade`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `org`, `updated_at`); **RLS private-by-default** (the same select/insert/update own-row shape as `public.sites`/`public.doc_reviews`, `auth.uid() = id`, no cross-user reads, no delete — the row lives/dies with the user); a `handle_new_user()` **SECURITY DEFINER trigger** on `auth.users insert` that inserts the matching row from `raw_user_meta_data` (the trigger route avoids the client-side follow-up-insert race — the row always exists before the user can read it); and a **backfill** that seeds rows for all existing users (null names are fine — the UI falls back, see B298). `on conflict (id) do nothing` throughout so re-running is safe.
- **Client I/O + hook (additive, reuses the existing anon client + session — no new keys):** `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/profile.js` (`loadProfile`/`saveProfile`, mirrors `cloudSync.js` shape; throws on a real fetch error so "no row" ≠ "offline"; `saveProfile` also best-effort syncs the name into auth `user_metadata` so the table and the auth record never disagree and the offline fallback stays fresh) and `src/shared/profile/useProfile.js` — the `useProfile(user)` hook returning `{ profile, loading, displayName, firstName, org, initial, reload, save }`, with a stale-fetch guard (a slow load can't show the previous user's profile) and an optimistic local update on save so the pill refreshes instantly.
- **Verified — lint 0 · 572 tests (562 + 10 new) · build green.** The never-blank display chain is pure-extracted (`displayNameFor`/`firstNameFor`/`orgFor`/`initialFor`) and unit-tested in `test/profileDisplay.test.js` (profile wins over metadata; First Last → first → last → metadata → email; whitespace-only trims to email; empty only when there's no user). The actual cloud round-trip (real profiles table read/write while signed in) needs a signed-in click-through — the sandbox proxy CORS-blocks auth — logged as **VERIFICATION V73**.
> **Dedup:** builds on the existing email/password auth (Supabase Phases 2–4) and the `AuthPanel` signup form (which already had the name fields). Distinct from the Site Model `status` reuse (B14) — this is per-*user* identity, not per-*project* lifecycle. The deferred `planarfit:* → planyr:*` localStorage rename is untouched (separate item).

### B282 — Opening a file from the global Project Files panel no-ops on the first click when launched from another workspace `[Doc Review]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-20, repro'd in the signed-in session; arrived as "NEW-1"; first filed B270 then renumbered **B282** — concurrent `main` consumed B270–B281 (incl. a different B270, the Project Files drop-zone queue) while this was in flight, so B282 is the real next free ID. "NEW-1" is only a scratch label — B180/B206/B266/B270 also "arrived as NEW-1".)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-20 (branch `claude/wonderful-galileo-abbbus`).** From the Site side, opening the global **🗂 Files** panel (with a project like Jacintoport open) and clicking a filed document (e.g. the MEP set) switched to the **Markup** tab but landed on the empty **"Open or drop a construction PDF"** placeholder — the document did **not** open; it stayed empty even after a multi-second wait, with **no console errors** (silent). The breadcrumb also reset to "Select a project". Clicking the **same file a second time** (now that Document Review was mounted) opened it correctly. 
- **Root cause (confirmed via the repro).** Document Review is a **lazy-loaded workspace** — the Shell renders only the active workspace (`React.lazy`/`Suspense`), so DR's code doesn't mount until you first enter the tab. The **global** Project Files drawer lives in the Site Planner (`SitePlanner.jsx`), and its open handler was `onOpenReview={() => onShellSwitch?.("doc-review")}` — it **switched workspaces but threw away the clicked review row entirely**. So in the same tick the app switched to DR *and* dropped the open request; DR mounted fresh and booted to its default/resume state, never opening the clicked file. The second click worked because DR was by then already mounted and its **own** in-workspace drawer wires `onOpenReview={openReview}` (the real handler). (The in-workspace path was never broken — only the cross-workspace one.)
- **Fix — persist the open-intent across the mount, mirroring the existing `navIntent` pattern.** New **`docIntent`** channel in `Shell.jsx`: `openReviewInDocReview(row)` stashes a **token-stamped** `{ kind:"open-review", row }` and *then* switches to `doc-review`; the Shell passes `docIntent` + `onOpenReviewInDocReview` to every workspace (parallel to the `navIntent`/Dashboard plumbing). The Site Planner's global drawer now calls `onOpenReview={(row) => onOpenReviewInDocReview?.(row)}` (threaded `SitePlannerApp` → `SitePlanner`), handing the **whole review row** up. `DocReview` consumes the pending intent in a mount/update effect (`openReview(row)`), guarded by a **module-scoped `lastConsumedDocToken`** (same technique as `SitePlannerApp`'s `lastConsumedNavToken`) so a plain tab switch-back never re-fires the last open.
- **No race with resume.** DR's boot effect (resume-the-last-review) now **stands down** when a fresh open-intent is present at mount (captured once via `bootDocIntentRef`), so the two async loads can't fight and silently land the wrong file.
- **Breadcrumb carries through.** `markupProject` is **seeded from the fresh intent** at mount (handling both a `listReviews` row's `project_id` and a loaded record's `projectId`), and `openReview` re-confirms it after load — so the project context no longer flashes to "Select a project".
- **Can't fail silently again.** `openReview` is hardened: it wraps `loadReview` in try/catch and, when the row can't be loaded (removed row / cloud unreachable), shows a **visible dismissible error banner** ("Couldn't open …") with a **Browse Files…** retry, instead of the previous bare `if (!rec) return`.
- **Verified — lint 0 · 550 tests · build green; the DocReview / SitePlannerApp / ProjectFilesDrawer lazy chunks all still split (workspace isolation intact).** Headless smoke on the **built** app (`ui-audit/verify-new1.mjs`): Document Review **mounts and remounts cleanly** with the new `docIntent` prop + ref capture + intent effect + hardened `openReview` + error banner — **zero JS errors** on a fresh mount AND after an unmount/remount.
