### B183 — Editable layers decouple from backdrop during pan while loading `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-1"; filed provisionally as B177, renumbered **B183** — concurrent `main` took B176–B181, so this is the real next free ID after B181/B182.)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-19 (branch `claude/nice-heisenberg-r6lmf1`).** On a freshly-loaded site, grabbing and panning before load settled made the drawn layers (massing/parcels/markup) visibly offset from the aerial for a frame or two, then snap back. **Root cause (confirmed, not the pasted race-condition theory):** in Planyr the SVG *is* the source of truth and the basemap follows it, so the layers can't reproject against a stale transform — the decoupler was **B65's own ghost snapshot**. A `commit` clones the basemap into a frozen overlay held until the fresh tiles `load`; while loading, that `load` is delayed so the snapshot lingered, and a pan moved the live SVG while the **frozen** snapshot stayed put → the aerial lagged the drawn layers until the snapshot expired (hence "only early on, then snaps back"). **Fix:** drop any lingering snapshot the instant a new gesture starts (`dropGhost()` at the top of the transform path), so a pan is tracked by the live CSS transform (welded to the SVG) and the backfill covers any reveal; a fresh snapshot is taken only at the next commit. **Verified headless** (`ui-audit/diagnose-decouple.mjs`, retina + throttled, pan immediately after load): **0 %** of pan frames have a snapshot on top (idle baseline has one, correctly dropped on the first pan). lint 0 · 257 tests · build green.

### B182 — Basemap tiles missing at high zoom ("Map data not yet available") `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-1"; filed provisionally as B176, renumbered **B182** — concurrent `main` took B176–B181 (jurisdictions/tax + cost takeoff), so this is the real next free ID.)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-19 (branch `claude/nice-heisenberg-r6lmf1`).** Zooming in deep showed gray "Map data not yet available" placeholder tiles instead of imagery. **Root cause (measured, `ui-audit/diagnose-zoomdepth.mjs`):** Esri World Imagery is native to **z19**; `detectRetina` (added in B170 for sharpness) fetches **one zoom level higher** than the display zoom, so at deep zoom on a retina display the detail layer requested **z20** (168 requests), which Esri answers with the placeholder image. `maxNativeZoom:19` didn't account for the retina offset. **Fix:** drop the detail layer's `maxNativeZoom` by 1 on retina (`L.Browser.retina ? maxNative-1 : maxNative`), so the highest native fetch is z19 and beyond that it **upscales the deepest real imagery** instead of fetching nonexistent tiles — exactly the requested "clamp to deepest available zoom, scale the last good tiles up; never put placeholders over the plan." **Verified:** max tile zoom requested now **19** at both retina (DSF 2) and non-retina (DSF 1), **0** placeholder/empty responses (was 168). The coarse backfill (`maxNativeZoom:13`) was already clamping correctly. lint 0 · 257 tests · build green.
> **Follow-up → B218 (2026-06-20):** this fix was applied only to the **planner-canvas** backdrop (`SitePlanner.jsx` GEO_BASEMAP). The **map-finder** imagery layer (`MapFinder.jsx`) had the same `detectRetina` (from B170) but never got this retina clamp, so the placeholder still showed there on a retina display. B218 brought the identical clamp to the map finder (every dropdown source) + capped the labels overlay. Both call sites now clamp.

### B180 — Verify paving area excludes curb footprint `[Cost]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-1"; minted **B180** — highest B# across both files was B179, so this is the real next free ID. Prerequisite for B181's paving-area trim.)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-19 (branch `claude/determined-feynman-l7c61b`). Investigated → confirmed correct by construction, and locked it in.** There was no pre-existing *cost* paving figure to fold curb into — the only paving area the app derived was the **impervious/SF** metric, where including the curb band is *correct* (curb is impervious surface), so that stays untouched. The new cost takeoff (B181) derives paving from the road's **face-of-curb-to-face-of-curb travel width** (`roadTravelWidth` = `min(w,h) − 2·curb`), which **excludes** the curb by definition: a 30′ FC-FC road yields 30′ of paving, never 31′. So the defect the brief warned about (folding the 6″ curb each side into paving) cannot occur — the cost math reads travel width, not the full element rectangle.
> **Locked against regression:** `roadQuantities` (in `lib/costTakeoff.js`) takes the FC-FC width explicitly and a unit test asserts a 30′ FC-FC × 1000′ barrier-curb road = exactly **30,000 SF (3,333.33 SY)** of paving with curb **outside** that width — so a future change that folded curb back in would fail the suite. **Live-confirmed in-browser:** a seeded 26′-cross road (FC-FC travel 25′) reads **1,611 SY** in the Yield panel (25 × 580 ÷ 9); had curb been folded in (26′) it would read 1,675 SY — the 1,611 proves the exclusion. 300 tests green, lint 0 errors, build green.

### B181 — Curb as a separate linear quantity type with curb-type attribute `[Cost]` (feature)  *(arrived as "NEW-2"; minted **B181** — next free ID after B180.)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-19 (branch `claude/determined-feynman-l7c61b`).** A road segment now derives **two independent, separately-priced quantities**:
> - **Paving** — an AREA item, **square yards (SY; 1 SY = 9 SF)** = length × FC-FC paving width ÷ 9. Width is stored/derived as **face-of-curb to face-of-curb** (the drivable surface), so a back-of-curb dimension can't silently inflate it.
> - **Curb** — a LINEAR item, **linear feet (LF)** = length × curbed-side count. **Both sides counted** (a 1,000′ road curbed both sides = 2,000 LF).
>
> **Curb carries a `curbType` attribute that selects its unit price:** `none` / **`barrier`** (vertical ~6″ lip, no gutter pan) / **`curb-gutter`** (curb + flat concrete gutter pan, typ. 18–24″). For **curb-and-gutter**, the gutter pan rides with the curb LF item, so **paving trims by the pan width on each curbed side** (`paving = FC-FC − panWidth × sides`); pan width is a property of the curb-and-gutter type (default 2.0′/24″, editable). Curb LF is split **barrier vs curb-and-gutter** in the rollup so each rides its own price.
> **Implementation:** new pure library `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/costTakeoff.js` (`roadQuantities`, `costRollup`, curb-type readers) — no React, fully unit-tested (`test/costTakeoff.test.js`, 15 cases). Road-element fields are additive/optional (`curbType`, `curbedSides`, `panWidth`) and persist losslessly through the Site Model (els pass through untouched; no `SITE_MODEL_VERSION` bump). UI: a **"Curb & paving (cost)"** group in the road inspector (curb-type dropdown, curbed-sides Both/One, gutter-pan width, live per-segment SY/LF readout — inline editors only, no dialogs) and a collapsible **"Road cost (screening)"** section in the **Yield** panel (site-wide Paving SY + Curb LF by type, **user-supplied** unit-price inputs — blank by default, never a hardcoded $/LF — and a priced subtotal).
> **Hook left for later (not built):** `roadQuantities` tags each curb run `curbCategory: "linear"` so a future **radius/corner curb** category (often a higher unit price) can be broken out as its own priced line without reworking the rollup.
> **Verified:** 300 tests green (15 new), lint 0 errors, build green, lazy-chunk split intact. **Live headless (logged-out preview):** Yield → "Road cost (screening)" renders **Paving 1,611 SY · Curb · barrier 1,160 LF** with the FC-FC caveat and unit-price inputs, **zero page errors** (`ui-audit/verify-cost.mjs`).

### B65 — White flashing on zoom/pan and general redraw `[Site Planner / map]` (bug)
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-19 (branch `claude/nice-heisenberg-r6lmf1`).** Zooming/panning a located site flashed (originally white) as the aerial blanked between redraws. **Root cause, measured not guessed** (headless probe `ui-audit/diagnose-flash.mjs`): the basemap view-lock effect called `map.setView(center, z, {animate:false})` on *every* planner `view` change; Leaflet's `setView`→`_resetView` fires `viewreset`, whose GridLayer handler `_resetAll` **wipes and reloads all tiles**, so each wheel step blanked the aerial for a frame (loaded tiles collapsed **22 → 2**), exposing the backdrop.
> **Fix shipped (two parts):**
> 1. **Mitigation (commit `cf26912`):** the basemap container backdrop was `PAL.paper` (`#f4f1ea`, near-white) → any gap read as a *bright* flash. Changed to a neutral mid-dark gray (`#3f3f3f`) **only while the aerial is on** (stays `PAL.paper` with the aerial off so the SVG-off background still matches). Bright flash → dim blink.
> 2. **Real fix — seamless transform-based zoom (commit `af10d1c`):** stop re-`setView`-ing on every frame. Hold Leaflet at a committed center/zoom and, for the small deltas of a live gesture, CSS-`transform` (translate+scale) the whole map container so the already-loaded tiles (and the shared FEMA/NWI overlay layers, which live on the same map) scale to track the gesture — no tile reload, no wipe, no flash. A debounced (180 ms) `setView` re-renders crisp once the gesture settles. First paint / resize / >1.5-zoom-level jumps commit immediately so the aerial is never scaled into a blurry mess. Transform math: `scale = getZoomScale(z, committed)`; translate so the desired center maps to the container centre (matches the SVG, which renders at true scale every frame), `transform-origin:0 0`. Container CSS transforms don't affect Leaflet's coordinate math (it uses cached `_size`/pixel-origin, and `clientWidth` is layout-box, unaffected by transform), so alignment is preserved.
> **Tested + rejected on the way:** flipping the map to `zoomAnimation/fadeAnimation:true` made it *worse* (gap frames 1→4, min loaded still 2) and reintroduces SVG-desync risk — not used.
> **Verified headless:** `diagnose-flash.mjs` now reports **0 gap frames** (min loaded 8, was 2); `ui-audit/verify-zoom-align.mjs` confirms the drawn building/parcel stay locked to the aerial through the transform and after the crisp commit (no jump). lint 0 errors · 257 tests · build green. **Live confirmation on planyr.io still nice-to-have** (a one-frame flash can't be captured headless), but the mechanism + alignment are proven. **Note:** Document Review's PDF viewer uses a different (canvas raster) renderer, not Leaflet — if zoom-flashing shows there too it's a separate fix, tracked if/when reported.
> **Follow-up 2026-06-19 (same branch) — kill the blank-backdrop reveal during the gesture.** After the flash fix shipped, the owner saw (screenshot) large flat cream patches while panning/zooming a project. Cause: the CSS-transformed basemap container (`geoWrapRef`) slid/scaled and exposed the canvas's `PAL.paper` (`wrapRef`) behind it. Fix (no new dependency): wrap the basemap in a **static clip box** (`inset:0`, `overflow:hidden`, dark `#3f3f3f` bg, never transformed) holding an **oversized inner map div** (`inset:-GEO_OVERSCAN`, `GEO_OVERSCAN = 320` px). The map now overhangs the viewport by 320 px on every side with `keepBuffer` tiles already loaded, so a normal pan/zoom transform reveals **real imagery**; anything beyond the overhang shows the **static dark backdrop**, never the cream page. The transform math is unchanged (it already uses `map.getSize()/2`, which adapts to the larger container, so basemap↔SVG alignment is preserved). Verified headless: `ui-audit/pan-reveal.mjs` (a hard mid-pan drag) now shows imagery edge-to-edge with no cream; `verify-zoom-align.mjs` still shows the geometry locked to the aerial through the transform + crisp commit. lint 0 errors · 257 tests · build green.
> **Follow-up 2 2026-06-19 (same branch) — kill the whole-screen "flash to black" on zoom-out.** Owner: zooming out from a building flashed the entire screen dark, even parts already loaded. Cause: the crisp re-render (`commit`) calls `map.setView`, whose Leaflet `viewreset`→`_resetAll` **removes ALL tiles and reloads them**, so for one frame the dark backdrop showed everywhere. Fix = **ghost-buffer the commit**: before the `setView`, clone the current basemap container (with its live CSS transform baked in) into a frozen overlay (`geoGhostRef`) pinned on top; the fresh tiles load underneath; on the tile layer's `load` event (or a 1.4 s fallback) the ghost is removed — so the old picture stays visible until the new one is ready and the wipe is never seen. Also dropped the old non-buffered ">1.5 levels → hard commit" branch; the crisp re-render now fires on settle (160 ms) OR once accumulated zoom drift passes ~0.75 levels, both **ghost-buffered** so a mid-gesture re-base no longer flashes. Verified headless (`ui-audit/zoomout-frames.mjs`, samples a continuous wheel zoom-out and measures the fraction of dark-backdrop pixels per frame): worst-case dark coverage **1.6 %** (UI edges only) — no full-screen black at any frame (was a brief whole-screen wipe). Alignment + crisp settle unchanged (`verify-zoom-align.mjs`). lint 0 errors · 257 tests · build green.
> **Follow-up 3 2026-06-19 (same branch) — fix the slow gray initial load (regression).** Owner: after the above, a freshly-opened site sat on the gray backdrop for ~10 s before the aerial appeared. Cause: the overscan (2.5× viewport) **×** detectRetina (2× density) ≈ **4× the tile bytes** on first paint, so on a real connection the detail tiles took ~10 s to cover (the sandbox is too fast to feel it — reproduced with Playwright CDP network throttling at ~1.2 Mbps: time-to-coverage **9.1 s**). Fix = a **coarse "instant" backfill layer**: a second `L.tileLayer` under the detail layer capped at `maxNativeZoom: 13` (a handful of large-area tiles, no detectRetina) that loads near-instantly and blankets the view with blurry imagery, then the heavy detail layer is added **only after the backfill paints** (`bf.once("load", addDetail)` + a 600 ms fallback) so its many retina tiles don't flood the connection and starve the coarse ones. Result (same 1.2 Mbps throttle): time-to-coverage **9.1 s → ~3 s** (blurry), detail then sharpens on top to the full 45 tiles; on a normal connection the coarse coverage is ~instant. No regression to the interactive fixes (zoom-out flash still 1.6 %, pan still full-imagery). `addDetail` guards against the aerial being toggled off mid-wait. lint 0 errors · 257 tests · build green. Harness: `ui-audit/initial-load.mjs` (optional `THROTTLE=1`).

### B170 — Fix retina/HiDPI tile requests so the aerial basemap renders sharp `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-2"; filed provisionally as B168, renumbered **B170** — concurrent `main` (`claude/brave-galileo-wm8gti`) took B167 + B168 for unrelated map items, so this is the real next free ID; was gated on B169)*
`[x]` Gated on B169 (the diagnostic), which confirmed the dominant blur causes were **(a) HiDPI tiles never requested** and **(b) the planner's fractional zoom** — so the source-swap fix path (B171/NEW-3) was correctly NOT triggered, since the imagery source isn't the problem.
> ✅ **Done 2026-06-19** (branch `claude/awesome-darwin-7ui0qm`). Added **`detectRetina: true`** to **both** Esri World Imagery tile layers — the map finder (`MapFinder.jsx`, `L.tileLayer(bm.tiles, …)`) and the planner backdrop (`SitePlanner.jsx`, `GEO_BASEMAP`). On a HiDPI display (`devicePixelRatio > 1`) Leaflet now requests **one-zoom-higher native tiles and renders them at half size** (downsampled = crisp) instead of upscaling 1× tiles (= soft). This also sharpens the planner's *fractional* zoom (`zoomSnap:0`, driven by `ppfToZoom`) because it prefers downsampling a higher-zoom tile over upscaling a lower one. **Kept the Esri source** (per the NEW-2 constraint) and **did NOT touch the planner map's `zoomSnap:0`** — snapping that map to integer zoom would desync the aerial from the feet-space SVG (the deliberate ppf→zoom scale lock); `detectRetina` only changes which tiles are fetched + their display size, never the map's CRS zoom, so the lock is untouched. **Self-verified in a real headless browser** (`gis-verify/retina-basemap-verify.mjs`, simulating `deviceScaleFactor` 1 vs 2 over a Katy parcel): at standard density the map requests **z11** tiles; at retina density it requests **z12** (one level higher = 2× pixel density), with **0 failed/gray tiles** at either density (no coverage regression) — logged **VERIFICATION V43**. lint **0 errors** · **257 tests** · build green; `SitePlannerApp` lazy chunk intact. (The sharpness gain is invisible at the sandbox's `devicePixelRatio = 1`, so the *visible* improvement is best confirmed on Michael's own retina/4K display — but the higher-density tile request is proven engaged.)

### B169 — Diagnose basemap blur: retina/DPR vs. fractional zoom vs. source resolution `[Site Planner]` (task)  *(arrived as "NEW-1"; filed provisionally as B167, renumbered **B169** — concurrent `main` (`claude/brave-galileo-wm8gti`) took B167 + B168 for unrelated map items, so this is the real next free ID)*
`[x]` Diagnostic only — instrument + report the root cause of soft aerial imagery **before** any provider change (the fix paths are B170 + B171).
> ✅ **Done 2026-06-19** (branch `claude/awesome-darwin-7ui0qm`). Root cause established from the two tile-layer call sites (both the **Esri World Imagery** source, `server.arcgisonline.com/.../World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}`) plus a live headless instrumentation:
> - **(a) Retina/HiDPI NOT requested — CONFIRMED, primary.** Neither `L.tileLayer` set `detectRetina` (nor any `@2x` / `tileSize:512`): the map finder (`MapFinder.jsx:291`) and the planner backdrop (`SitePlanner.jsx:1043`) both fetched **1× tiles**, which the browser then **upscales** on any `devicePixelRatio > 1` display (most modern laptops / 4K monitors) → soft. This is the most likely "it looks blurry on my screen" cause.
> - **(b) Fractional zoom — CONFIRMED for the planner backdrop.** The planner map runs **`zoomSnap: 0`** (`SitePlanner.jsx:1031`) and its zoom is driven **continuously** from `ppfToZoom(view.ppf, lat)`, so the raster is almost always displayed at a **fractional** zoom = interpolated = blurred (independent of DPR). The map finder uses Leaflet's default integer zoom, so it's not affected by (b) — only (a).
> - **(c) Genuinely low-res source — RULED OUT as primary.** Esri World Imagery is **native to z19** (`maxNativeZoom: 19`, ~0.3 m/px) with good Houston-metro coverage; both layers merely *display* past native (21/24), so the only "source" softness is upscaling past z19 at very tight zoom — not a stale/low-res source. Verified live (Katy parcel): tiles return **HTTP 200** with no gray/missing tiles at the working zooms.
> - **Live instrumentation:** `gis-verify/retina-basemap-verify.mjs` drove the headless map at `deviceScaleFactor` 1 vs 2 and recorded the **zoom level of every World_Imagery tile actually requested** + load status. Confirmed the pre-fix behavior (1× tiles, no DPR awareness) and gave the before/after baseline for B170.
> **Outcome → fix routing:** causes (a)+(b) are real and fixable **without** changing the imagery source → **B170** (add `detectRetina`, keep Esri, don't snap the planner's locked zoom). Cause (c) is not the issue, so **B171** (license-clean high-res source evaluation) stays **gated** — only revisit if B170 proves insufficient by eye on a real retina display. lint 0 errors · 257 tests · build green (no app-code change in this diagnostic item beyond the verify harness).

### B166 — Geometry check reads wrong county acreage (homesite carve-out, not total) `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-3"; minted B166)*
`[x]` **Repro (owner-reported):** parcel `0440110000065` — Appraisal panel + drawn boundary agree (17.00 AC vs 17.06 ac) but the geometry check screamed **"county 0.50 ac vs 17.06 ac (3,312% off)."** The 0.50 ac was the **HOMESITE carve-out** (Legal: "PT TR 4D (HOMESITE)"), not the total tract.
> ✅ **Done 2026-06-19** (branch `claude/busy-carson-1zuiuq`). Confirmed root cause against the **live HCAD parcels layer** field list: the record carries **both** `Acreage` (total) **and** `acreage_1` (a sub-acreage) — both match the acres regex, and `countyAcres()` used `keys.find(...)` which returned whichever came first (the homesite ~0.50). Fix in `SitePlanner.jsx` `countyAcres()`: collect **all** acreage-named fields, drop any whose name marks it a sub-acreage (`home_site|homestead|hs_|hmst|exempt|imprv|improv`), and take the **MAX** of what remains — the total tract is always the largest, so a homesite/ag/exemption carve-out can never win. County-agnostic (fixes the statewide carve-out pattern, not just this parcel). Distinct root cause from B75 (that was a m²-vs-acres unit misread; the TxGIO unit handling is untouched). lint 0 errors · 257 tests · build green.

### B154 — Delete key intermittently needs two presses to remove a selected element `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-1"; filed provisionally as B151, renumbered **B154** — concurrent `main` took B150–B153 (easement tool) plus a second B151 (multipart parcel), so this is the real next free ID; the implementing commit references the bug as NEW-1)*
`[x]` Repro: click an element to select it, press Delete — sometimes it deletes on the first press, sometimes it takes two ("works when I was already on the canvas; fails when I came from a panel/button first"). **Root cause (confirmed, but NOT the report's first guess):** the keydown handler is **already** `window`-level — so it isn't a focus-scope problem. The real cause is a **stale closure via passive-effect re-binding:** `onKey` is created inside a `useEffect`, and although `sel`/`multi` are in its deps, the effect re-binds the listener **after** the commit/paint. A Delete pressed in the brief window right after a selecting click runs the *previously* bound `onKey`, which closed over the old `sel` (often `null`) → the guard `(sel || multi.length)` was false → no-op, no `preventDefault`; the next press (listener now re-bound) works. Under a heavy render (this is a ~6k-line component) the window widens enough to be hit intermittently.
> ✅ **Done 2026-06-18** (branch `claude/gallant-lovelace-82konu`). Added live `selRef`/`multiRef` mirrors (synced during render — a passive effect would lag the same window) and made the **Delete/Backspace branch read the refs**, and `deleteSel` read `selRef.current`/`multiRef.current`, so deletion always acts on the *current* selection no matter which listener instance fired — no second press. The handler stayed `window`-level (no scope change). Also **hardened the existing typing guard** — it already bailed when `document.activeElement` is INPUT/SELECT/TEXTAREA (so Delete never nuked canvas elements while editing a field); extended it to **`contentEditable`** too. The lone same-tick `setSel(x); deleteSel()` caller (the element context-menu Delete) is unaffected — the element is already selected when that menu opens, so the ref holds it. lint **0 errors** · **230 tests** · build green; `SitePlannerApp` lazy chunk intact. **Self-verified in a real headless browser** (built app): (A) select an element → one Delete removes it (2→1); (B) touch a tool/panel button, then select an element, then a **single immediate** Delete still removes exactly one — the reported flow, now first-press reliable; zero console errors. Logged as **VERIFICATION V40**.

### B144 — Scale bar clips off-frame and isn't measurement-grade in print/export `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-1"; filed provisionally as B141, renumbered **B144** — concurrent `main` PR #114 had already taken B140–B142 and PR #117 took B143, so this is the real next free ID; the implementing commit still references the provisional B141/B142)*
`[x]` Repro: Print/PDF (and PNG export) of the map view → the scale bar's max label ("500") clipped at the right frame edge, the "0" floated above the bar instead of under the start tick, and the segments read as noise rather than a measured ruler. **Root cause (confirmed):** the export reused the *on-screen* scale bar's **screen-pixel** sizing (`scaleBarFt.px ≈ 120 px` + fixed `28`/`30` px offsets) and screenshotted it into a differently-sized export frame, so it overflowed; labels were also drawn *above* the bar with no plate.
> ✅ **Done 2026-06-17** (branch `claude/gallant-lovelace-82konu`). New pure module **`lib/sheetFurniture.js`** draws the furniture **sized in OUTPUT units and anchored to the export FRAME**, not the screen: everything is a fraction of `refS = min(frame w,h)`, so it lands at a fixed physical size on the page (on a letter sheet the short side ≈ 8.5 in → safe-area inset ≈ 0.38 in). The scale bar now **snaps to a round real-world distance** (`pickScaleBar`, from 50/100/200/250/500/1000 ft + smaller/larger steps for extreme zoom) that best fills a target width band **without exceeding a hard ceiling** (so it can't clip); **alternating black/white segments**; **tick marks at 0 / midpoint / max with the numbers centered directly under their ticks**; a **"FEET"** unit label; on a **translucent legibility plate** so it reads over light pavement or dark canopy. The graphic bar stays the source of truth (its length encodes the distance, so it survives image rescaling — no "1 in = X ft" text scale). Recomputes on zoom. `buildExportSvg` (`SitePlanner.jsx`) composites it into the print/PNG viewBox; the old screen-pixel furniture block + the now-unused `scaleBarFt` were removed. **Also applied on-screen** (owner asked to "fix the site planyr app too"): the live canvas uses the same primitives via `buildScreenFurnitureSvg` (viewport-anchored, fixed modest size) so the app matches the print. **Workspace confirmed Site Planner only** — Document Review has no print furniture (nothing shared to fix twice). lint **0 errors** · **222 tests** (18 new in `test/sheetFurniture.test.js`: round-distance snap, no-clip ceiling, safe-area anchoring, plate/label/FEET render, no compass rose, screen variant) · build green; `SitePlannerApp` lazy chunk intact. **Self-verified in a real headless browser** (drove the built app: drew buildings → File ▾ → Print / pick frame → Print, captured the actual print page; also captured a PNG export and the on-screen corners) — scale bar fully inside the frame, round **0 / 125 / 250 FEET**, no clipping. Logged as **VERIFICATION V34**. Shared root cause + fix with **B145**.

### B143 — Text box edits like Bluebeam: Enter = newline, click away / Esc to finish `[Site Planner]` (bug) — follow-up to B142

Two causes, both fixed to match Bluebeam's Text Box markup (researched against the Bluebeam Revu docs — "finish by selecting away or pressing Esc"; a text box is multi-line):

- **Enter committed (single-line behavior):** Enter now inserts a **newline**; you finish by clicking away or Esc (Esc keeps the text). Placeholder updated to "Type; click away or Esc to finish".
- Empty box is still removed when you click away without typing (matches Bluebeam).

### B132 — Detention pond expansion: lock an existing pond as a baseline, then read the storage gained `[Site Planner]` (feature)
`[x]` Done 2026-06-17 (branch `claude/practical-noether-ln1f46`). Owner workflow: trace an existing on-site detention pond, lock it as the baseline, then enlarge it (drag banks out and/or deepen) to read the **added detention** in acre-feet. Built entirely on the existing pond machinery — no parallel store, no new schema bump.
- **Panel** (`SitePlanner.jsx`, pond branch of the selected-element inspector): the **Detention storage** section gains a **"Lock as existing pond"** button. Locking snapshots the current footprint ring (world feet: `selEl.points` or `elCorners`) **plus its own depth/freeboard/slope** into `el.det.baseline`, so the comparison is frozen and apples-to-apples. Once locked, an **"Expansion vs. existing"** box shows **Existing** / **Proposed** storage and a live **"Storage gained +X.XX ac-ft"** (green) — or **"Storage lost"** (red) when shrunk below baseline — plus the cubic-feet delta. **Clear** removes the baseline (keeps depth/freeboard/slope).
- **Increase = `detentionStorage(proposed) − detentionStorage(baseline)`** — the *same* prismoidal/taper function for both sides, so the delta can't drift from a method mismatch. Reflects both footprint growth and any depth/slope change.
- **Canvas ghost** (`renderElPx`): the locked baseline ring draws as a faint **dashed outline** under the pond so the expansion is visible. Handled for both the irregular-polygon branch (drawn in world feet directly) and the rotated-rectangle branch (a counter-rotated `<g>` undoes the element's `rotate(el.rot)` so the world-feet ghost lands true). `pointerEvents:none` so it never interferes with selection/drag.
- **Persistence:** `baseline` rides inside the already-persisted `el.det` (additive, lossless) — survives save/reload, no `SITE_MODEL_VERSION` bump. Honest framing kept: "screening only — confirm with your civil engineer."
- **Scope (owner-chosen):** "just the increase." Deliberately **excluded** for now (offered, declined): a required-vs-provided "is it enough?" check against added impervious, and a solver ("grow this much to hit a target"). Easy follow-ons if wanted.
- **Verified:** lint 0 errors (14 pre-existing warnings, none in new code) · **191 tests pass** · build green · lazy-chunk split intact (`SitePlannerApp` own chunk). Browser click-through logged as **V25** in `VERIFICATION.md`.

### B128 — Split tool: correctly cut concave parcels (general multi-piece straight cut) `[Site Planner]` (bug → enhancement)  *(minted B127 on-branch; renumbered B128 after `main`'s #85 concurrently took B127 for the rail/header dropdown fix — the implementing commit still says "B127")*
`[x]` Done 2026-06-17 (branch `claude/inspiring-gates-qrhziq`). Closes the QA marathon's last "substantive bug still present" hand-off and supersedes the long-deferred **B31**.
- **The data-corruption fear was already mitigated, and that was verified, not assumed.** The hand-off carried an `[S2/HIGH]` "Split corrupts area on concave parcels — saved silently, no error." That premise was **stale** (written against pre-#48 code): `performSplit` already had a concave-cut **backstop guard** (area-conservation + per-piece self-intersection check, from the B74–B92 batch) that *refuses* a bad cut with a warning instead of saving corrupted geometry. Confirmed by replicating the live `splitPolygon` + guard and fuzzing **320k random concave cuts** (combs/L/U/stars) against a Monte-Carlo point-membership oracle: **zero** wrong splits slipped past the guard; every 4/6/8/10/12-crossing cut was rejected. So there was no silent `siteSqft`/FAR/coverage corruption to fix.
- **The real remaining gap was capability, not safety.** Because the old `splitPolygon` only paired the two extreme-`t` crossings, a straight cut that crosses a concave lot **4+ times** (which honestly yields **k+1** pieces for `2k` crossings — e.g. 3 for a U cut across both prongs) could only ever produce 2 overlapping/omitting "halves," so the guard always **refused** it. Net user-visible behavior: "the Split tool won't cut an L/U/notched lot through its reentrant part."
- **Fix — a correct general slice.** Extracted the parcel-split geometry out of `SitePlanner.jsx` into a new pure, tested module **`lib/polygonSplit.js`**: `splitPolygonByLine(points,A,B)` classifies each vertex to a binary side (guarantees an even crossing count — no odd-parity tangency bug), inserts a crossing node on every sign-change edge, **pairs ALL crossings even–odd along the cut line** (each pair is an interior chord), and traces every resulting piece (walk a boundary arc → hop the interior chord to its partner → continue), dropping zero-area slivers. Returns the natural set of pieces (`>=2`) or `null`. The bent-polyline cut moved over too as `splitPolygonByPath` (unchanged logic). `performSplit` now replaces the one parcel with **N** parcels and keeps the area/self-intersection guard as a backstop, so the result can never be worse than before (a rare near-vertex-grazing degenerate sliver still self-intersects → still refused).
- **UX change to note:** a straight cut through a notched lot now creates **all** the real pieces (e.g. 3 parcels for a U-shaped lot), instead of declining. Convex and 2-crossing concave cuts are byte-for-byte the same two pieces as before.
- **Validation:** new `test/polygonSplit.test.js` (11 cases: convex halving, L 2-crossing, **U → 3 pieces with exact areas + membership**, 3-tooth comb → 4 pieces, line-misses/degenerate → null, bent-path cut, and a 1,500-cut randomized area+membership property check). Standalone prototype passed the 300k-trial oracle (0 area / 0 membership failures; ~0.003% near-degenerate self-int → safely refused). Full suite **163 tests** (was 152, +11) · lint **0 errors** · build green · lazy-chunk split intact. Owner approved shipping; merged to `main` via PR.

### B114 — Snapping always on; can't be suppressed during a drag `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-1")*
`[x]` Done 2026-06-16 (branch `claude/epic-dirac-3ljl49`). Dragging an element (e.g. a road) near a neighbour flush-snapped it to that neighbour's edge with no per-move escape, so you couldn't drop it at a deliberate offset (a 15-ft buffer behind trailer parking). Root cause: the existing "Alt-drop to place free" only skipped the *bond* at drop (`onUp`'s `!e.altKey` guard); the element had already been moved to the flush-snapped position during `onMove`, so Alt never placed it freely — and there was no keyboard toggle. Fix:
- **Hold-to-suppress (the standard CAD pattern):** a new `altSnapOffRef`, re-armed from `e.altKey` on every `onBgDown`/`onMove`, makes the live snap = `settings.snap && !altSnapOffRef.current`. `snap()`/`snapPt()` read it (so grid snap, draw, vertex, and placement all honour Alt), and a per-frame `snapOn` gates the inline paths the core helper doesn't cover — the ambient neighbour flush-snap (`edgeSnapCenter`), resize/edge-resize-to-grid, and rotate-to-15°. Holding Alt bypasses ALL of them for that one move and re-enables on release. Shift-drag (deliberate align+bond) is unaffected.
- **Toggle + shortcut + default OFF:** the toolbar button stays, plus a new **S** shortcut and the Site-defaults checkbox toggle snap; "off" fully disables every snap path above. Per owner request snap now **defaults OFF (free movement)** and is a **global drafting preference** (a tool mode), not a per-site attribute: it lives in `localStorage` (`planarfit:snap`, default off) via `loadSnapPref`/`saveSnapPref`/`setSnap`, seeded at the settings `useState` and preserved across JSON import, so the per-site saved `snap` is ignored on load (every existing site started free, regardless of its baked-in `snap:true`). Turning it on persists across sites/reloads until turned off. (`settings.snap` is still the field every read site uses — it just mirrors the pref now.)
- **Visible state:** the toolbar pill now reads `Snap 10′` ↔ `Snap off` (green/grey dot, `aria-pressed`), the Site-defaults checkbox is relabeled "Snap to grid & neighbours (S)", the Select-tool hint says "hold Alt to bypass snap & place freely • toggle snap with S", and the shortcuts panel gains `S → Toggle snap` and `Alt drag → Bypass snap`. Build green; lazy-chunk split intact. **Browser-verify** logged in VERIFICATION.md.

### B11 — Remove the county pre-selection gate; click anywhere, auto-resolve the county `[Site Planner / map]` (feature)
`[x]` Today the user must pick a county (e.g., Harris vs. Fort Bend) *before* clicking a parcel. Remove that gate — the user should be able to pan/click **anywhere** and select any parcel without choosing a county first; the unnecessary upfront choice just adds friction.
- Parcel geometry is published per **county appraisal district (CAD)** — the county agency that maintains the parcel map and ownership data (Harris County Appraisal District, Fort Bend Central Appraisal District, etc.). So "click anywhere" means the backend must **resolve which county the clicked point falls in** (point-in-county lookup) and route the parcel query to that county's CAD service automatically.
- Handle the **county-boundary case** gracefully (a click near a line, or a multi-parcel selection that straddles two counties → query both services and merge results).
- This also removes the county dropdown from the header, feeding **B10**.
> Done 2026-06-14 (this PR — B7–B12 batch). County gate removed. The map resolves every configured CAD county's parcel layer up front; a click is auto-routed via `candidateCountiesForPoint` (coarse per-county bbox pre-filter, padded so borders overlap → a straddle click queries both) + `identifyParcelAcross` (parallel point-identify across candidates, first hit wins, a down county is skipped not fatal, no match fails gracefully — no parcel, no crash). The selected parcel's resolved county rides into the planner hand-off so the saved site still records its county. The county dropdown is gone from the map header. **Interim:** the Layers panel defaults to the Harris/Houston jurisdiction (same as the prior app default) so the Houston utility overlays stay available with no county picked — per-area jurisdiction resolution is a future refinement.

### B66 — Top-left Site Planyr dropdown renders behind the lower header row `[global UI]` (bug)
`[x]` Clicking the top-left module (product) switcher opened its dropdown *behind* the planner's context bar / map header, so it couldn't be used. Root cause: the Shell `<header>` (which holds the dropdown) and `<main>` (which holds the workspace) were siblings, neither establishing a stacking context, so the dropdown menu (`zIndex:50`) competed in the **root** stacking context against the planner context bar (`SitePlanner.jsx`, `zIndex:60`) and the map header (`MapFinder.jsx`, `zIndex:1000`) — and lost.
> Done 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/b64-b66-runtime-ui-fixes`). Fixed in `src/app/Shell.jsx`: `<main>` now establishes a stacking-context floor (`position:relative; zIndex:0`), capping ALL workspace content (the context bar's 60, the map header's 1000, in-workspace modals) beneath it, and `<header>` is lifted above it (`position:relative; zIndex:1`). The global switcher dropdown now always paints over the workspace regardless of the lower bars' internal z-indexes; the shell-level AuthPanel (`zIndex:5000`) still sits above everything. More robust than just bumping the menu's number (which would depend on the exact stacking tree). Build passes.

### B68 — Opening a project with saved elements renders a blank screen (`cfgOf is not defined`) `[Site Planner]` (bug) — crash, high
`[x]` Opening a project that has saved layout elements (e.g. **"Schiel Road"**) blanked the whole page; the console showed `ReferenceError: cfgOf is not defined`, thrown inside the `els.map` during render — so empty/new projects (iterating over nothing) didn't crash, which is why only populated projects blanked. **Root cause:** `cfgOf` is a component-scoped helper (`SitePlanner.jsx:2449`, it closes over `settings`), but it was *also* called at `SitePlanner.jsx:5237` inside `renderElPx` — a **module-level** function that receives `settings` as a parameter — where the component-scoped `cfgOf` is not in scope. It shipped because it compiles fine; a build-only CI check can't see an unresolved identifier at runtime. This is exactly the "disjoint-but-interdependent concurrent merge" failure mode called out in **B63**: a parking `cfgOf` call site (added with B29/B59 in PR #22) landed in a scope where the helper isn't visible, and the clean merge + green build hid it. (Arrived from a parallel chat as provisional "NEW-1"; minted **B68** here — B67 is reserved by the in-flight PR #23 — and deduped: no prior blank-screen item existed.)
> Done 2026-06-15 (branch `claude/loving-knuth-6n43df`, pending PR). Three parts. **(1) Fix:** `renderElPx` now resolves `cfgOf` locally from its `settings` param (identical semantics to the component's), so the parking branch no longer references an out-of-scope symbol. **(2) Build-time guard (the real prevention):** added a minimal ESLint flat config whose headline rule is `no-undef`, run as a CI step before the build (`npm run lint`) — verified it flags the exact bug (`5237:38 'cfgOf' is not defined`) on the pre-fix file, so this whole class of dangling reference now fails the build instead of shipping a blank page. **(3) Hardening:** each lazy workspace in `Shell.jsx` is wrapped in a React `ErrorBoundary` (keyed by workspace id), so a future render crash shows a legible "couldn't load this view" fallback (Try again / Reload) instead of unmounting to a blank page — the shell, the switcher, and the other workspace keep working. `lint` / `test` (30 pass) / `build` all green.

### B355 — Default new-site-plan name to lettered concepts (Concept A, B, … AA) `[Site Planner]` (feature)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-1" + "NEW-2" 2026-06-21 — two near-identical drops of the same request; deduped into ONE item, minted **B355** = next free after B354; implemented + verified same session)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified (2026-06-21), on branch `claude/hopeful-galileo-0xbh0q`.** New site plans now default to **Concept A, Concept B, …** instead of "Plan 1, Plan 2". **Dedup note:** NEW-1 and NEW-2 are the same feature; NEW-1's "scope: per-site, resets per site" and NEW-2's "within project scope" resolve to the **same thing in this codebase** — a "project" *is* a Site Planner site group, and a plan's letter sequence runs within that group (exactly where the old `Plan N` numbering lived). No conflict, so they fold into one. **Design (all points honored):** (a) **per-site** — every site's first concept is "Concept A"; the sequence resets per site group; (b) **continues past the highest existing letter, never reuses a gap** — if "Concept B" exists but "A" was deleted, the next is "Concept C" (so a name a teammate remembers is never silently re-pointed); (c) **past-Z is spreadsheet-style** — Concept Z → AA → AB → … (bijective base-26, never crashes at the 27th); (d) **stays user-editable** — this only sets the default; (e) **no retroactive rename** — existing "Plan N" names are left untouched (they don't parse as concepts, so a site that already has "Plan 1" simply gets "Concept A" as its *next* new plan; the legacy-group migration in `storage.js` still writes "Plan 1" for old un-grouped records). **Implementation:** pure, unit-tested `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/conceptName.js` (`numberToConcept`/`conceptLettersToNumber`/`parseConceptIndex`/`nextConceptName`), wired into the three creation paths in `SitePlannerApp.jsx` (`newSiteFromMap` → "Concept A"; `newPlanSameParcel` → `nextConceptForGroup`) + the blank-site first-save default in `SitePlanner.jsx` + the `createSiteModel` fallback in `siteModel.js`. **Verified:** new `test/conceptName.test.js` 14/14 (A–Z, AA/AB roll-over, round-trip, gap-not-reused, legacy "Plan N" ignored); full suite 1055/1055; lint 0; build green. Eligible to move to BACKLOG-DONE on merge.

### B353 — B331 pinch regression: the new pinch handlers clobbered Site Planner vertex editing `[Site Planner / Markup]` (bug)  *(found by owner-requested stress test of B331, 2026-06-21; fixed + verified same session)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified (2026-06-21), on branch `claude/gifted-heisenberg-a6zlvt`.** Stress-testing the just-shipped B331 pinch (#245) surfaced a **real, live regression**: on the Site Planner SVG the pinch handlers were added as a *second* `onPointerDownCapture`/`onPointerMoveCapture` on the same element, and **JSX silently keeps only the last duplicate** — so the pre-existing vertex-edit capture handlers (`onCanvasVtxDownCapture`/`onCanvasVtxMoveCapture`) were dropped. Net effect: **selecting a parcel/polygon vertex, shift-click-insert-vertex, and the insert-on-edge hover hint all stopped working** — on mouse *and* touch. The build was green and the minimal lint gate has no react plugin, so nothing caught it. **Fix:** merge the two capture lines into one prop each (pinch first; the vertex handler runs only when a pinch is NOT engaged, `if (!pinchRef.current)`) — mouse + single-touch editing restored, pinch still wins when it engages. **Hardening (same pass):** a shared `reseedPinch` re-baselines the gesture to whatever fingers remain on every add/remove, and a 3rd+ finger is absorbed instead of starting a competing pan/draw — a partial lift or extra finger can no longer jump or corrupt the zoom. **Permanent guard:** `test/noDuplicateJsxProps.test.js` AST-scans every `.jsx` (via the already-present `@babel/parser`) and fails if any element repeats an attribute — kills this build-invisible clobber class for good. **Verified (V94):** new `ui-audit/verify-pinch-stress.mjs` 15/15 (adversarial multitouch: 30-cycle storms, clamp saturation, coincident fingers/no-NaN, 3-finger + partial lift, interrupt recovery, mouse-path survival) + verify-pinch 5/5 + all viewport/rail/viewer regressions green; 1015 unit tests; lint 0; build green. Eligible to move to BACKLOG-DONE on merge.

### B329 — Markup canvas pan + zoom parity with the Site map (one shared viewport engine) `[Doc Review / Markup]` (feature)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-1" 2026-06-21; filed B313 → B320 → renumbered **B329** as a hot `main` twice took the number)*
`[x]` **Merging via PR #238 → `main` (2026-06-21).** One shared viewport engine (`src/shared/viewport/viewportTransform.js`: `worldToScreen`/`screenToWorld`/`zoomAround`/`panBy`/`fitView`/`shouldPan`) now drives the Site map, the Markup canvas, AND the Stitcher. The Markup viewer was re-architected scroll-box → transform (`view={scale,tx,ty}`): **free pan in any direction** (the old scroll box couldn't slide past a fit-width sheet — the "only scrolls vertically" repro), cursor-anchored zoom, **Bluebeam pan/tool collision** (middle-mouse always pans; Space-hold pans; Select on empty pans, on an object selects/moves; a drawing tool draws), **view-transform-only** (markups stay page-unit, calibration untouched), and a perf path that rescales the existing bitmap during a zoom and re-rasterises crisply (debounced) on settle. The Site map + Stitcher migrated their pan/zoom math to the same engine, **byte-identical** (unit-tested) — verified unchanged. Trackpad pinch (ctrl+wheel) routes through the wheel path; touchscreen two-finger pinch is **B331** (follow-up).
> **Verified (V84):** 43/43 headless — `verify-markup-viewport.mjs` 13/13 (free pan L/R/down, cursor-anchored zoom 0.1px drift, calibrated measurement reads identical feet through zoom+pan + stays calibrated, middle-mouse pans-without-drawing, draw+select-move, sheet-switch keeps zoom), `verify-siteplanner-viewport.mjs` 6/6 (Site map unchanged), `verify-docreview-viewer.mjs` 13/13 (B288–B296 still green) + viewportTransform unit tests. ### B331 — Touchscreen two-finger pinch-zoom on the Markup canvas + the Site map `[Doc Review / Markup + Site Planner]` (feature)  *(owner-requested 2026-06-21 right after B329/B330; minted **B331** — next free after B324)*
`[x]` **Built + verified (2026-06-21), on branch `claude/gifted-heisenberg-a6zlvt` — ready to ship.** One shared pinch helper now drives both canvases: `viewportTransform.js` gains `midpoint`/`distance`/`pinchZoom(v, prevMid, currMid, factor)` — the touch counterpart of `zoomAround` (zoom by the finger-distance ratio about the gesture's previous midpoint, then translate so that anchored point follows the fingers to the new midpoint, so a pinch both zooms AND pans). The Markup canvas (`DocReview.jsx`) wires it bubble-phase (its children are `pointerEvents:none`, so the gesture reaches the host); the Site map (`SitePlanner.jsx`) wires it **capture-phase** + `stopPropagation` (touches land on the SVG `<rect>` children which carry their own handlers, so the pinch must intercept first). Both paths are **gated on `pointerType==='touch'` + exactly 2 active pointers**, so the verified mouse/trackpad/wheel (ctrl+wheel) path is byte-for-byte untouched; **view-transform only** — stored geometry/calibration never move. **Verified (V88):** `verify-pinch.mjs` 5/5 (REAL trusted multitouch via CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` on a `hasTouch` context — Site map spread/pinch 1.25→4.71→1.53 px/ft, Markup canvas 603→2009→670 px, 0 errors) + all mouse-path regressions green on the same build (`verify-markup-viewport` 13/13, `verify-siteplanner-viewport` 6/6, `verify-markup-rail` 11/11, `verify-docreview-viewer` 13/13, the merged Stitcher set `verify-b335-b339` 13/13); +4 unit tests (850 total); lint 0; build green; lazy chunks intact. ### B326 — "CAD" discipline is misclassified as reference, so CAD drawings can't be placed on the map `[Doc Review / Files]` (bug)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-1" 2026-06-21; minted **B326** — first filed B321, renumbered as concurrent `main` #239 took B321–B324 then #241 took B325)*
`[x]` **Repro:** file a drawing under the **CAD** discipline → in Project Files it gets the "reference" tag, no "Place on map" button, and it lands in "Reference docs" instead of "On-the-map docs". CAD is the most placeable class of all (it's literally the drawings). **Cause:** `shared/files/fileFacts.js` `SPATIAL_DISCIPLINES` omitted "CAD", so it fell through to the `DOC_CLASS.REFERENCE` default (intentional only for genuinely-ambiguous cases like "Other"). **Fixed this session (branch `claude/modest-turing-wixo1y`):** added "CAD" to `SPATIAL_DISCIPLINES` so it classifies spatial (gets the Place-on-map action + the spatial saved-views); "Other" still defaults to reference. New unit test alongside the existing `classifyDocClass` tests. lint 0 · 802 tests · build green. Shipping via PR #240 → `main`.

### B327 — Canvas memory budget isn't enforced at high zoom; a large sheet can allocate ~500 MB and OOM the tab `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-2" 2026-06-21; minted **B327** — first filed B322, renumbered past main #239's B321–B324 + #241's B325)*
`[x]` **Repro (numerically verified + headless-confirmed):** an E-size sheet (2448×1584 pt) at 600% zoom allocated a ~140 MP / ~533 MB RGBA backing store — far past the "≤ ~24 MP" the code claimed. **Cause:** `lib/pdf.js` `backingScale` floored the density at 1× (`Math.max(1, …)`), which DEFEATED the budget once the CSS area (base×scale) alone passed ~24 MP — a 1× backing store was already over budget and kept growing with zoom → out-of-memory tab crash, not graceful degradation. **Fixed this session (branch `claude/modest-turing-wixo1y`):** extracted the budget math to a pure, unit-testable `lib/renderBudget.js` and let the device-pixel density drop BELOW 1× when needed, so total backing pixels stay ≤ ~24 MP at ANY zoom (a slightly soft raster on a huge sheet at 600% beats an OOM crash). The CSS box stays exactly base×scale, so the markup overlay + zoom-anchor math are untouched (no geometry change). New `test/renderBudget.test.js` proves ≤24 MP holds for scales 0.5–6 × dpr 1–3; headless `ui-audit/verify-b322-b40.mjs` reads a real 6090×3940 = 24.0 MP canvas at the 600% max (V85). Builds on B247/B265. lint 0 · 802 tests · build green. Shipping via PR #240 → `main`.

### B328 — Project Files "Filed / On-map" badge can never show "On-map" `[Doc Review / Files]` (bug, minor)  *(arrived as coworker-chat "NEW-3" 2026-06-21; minted **B328** — first filed B323, renumbered past main #239's B321–B324 + #241's B325)*
`[x]` **Repro:** every file in the drawer showed "○ filed", never "● on map", even for a placed spatial drawing. **Cause:** `fileState` returns ON_MAP only when `isSpatial(f) && f.placed`, but the lightweight `listReviews` query never selected `placed` (and nothing wrote it), so `f.placed` was always falsy. **Fixed this session (branch `claude/modest-turing-wixo1y`):** (a) `listReviews` now pulls just the flag out of the data jsonb (`placed:data->placed`, not the heavy payload; falls back to the core columns on any error → degrades to "filed", never regresses); (b) `toFileFact` parses it whether it arrives as a JSON boolean or text; (c) new `reviewStore.markReviewPlaced(id)` is the write half, called from the drawer's "Place on map" confirm so a placed file flips to On-map on reopen; (d) `fileIndex.mergeFactsIntoReviews` now OR-ins `placed` so a facts-index row without `placement.placed` can't silently un-place a placed review. New tests in `fileFacts.test.js` + `test/fileIndex.test.js`. Note: the full auto-placement backend (B182) is still unbuilt — this makes the badge LIVE for the manual placement flow that exists today; B182 will set the same flag at true completion. lint 0 · 802 tests · build green. Shipping via PR #240 → `main`.

### B288 — Single-sheet review can't be zoomed by wheel / pinch / Ctrl-scroll (only the ± buttons) `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-1" 2026-06-20; minted **B288** — renumbered from B273, consumed by concurrent `main`)*
`[x]` **Repro (confirmed live on planyr.io 2026-06-20):** open a PDF in Document Review (single-sheet, not Stitch) → wheel / pinch / Ctrl+scroll over the drawing → nothing (stuck at 31%); the only zoom is the toolbar ±. **Expected:** wheel / Ctrl-scroll / pinch zoom the drawing, anchored on the cursor. The fix already exists here — the Stitcher's `onWheel` (`Stitcher.jsx` ~L171) does cursor-anchored zoom; port it to the single-sheet view (`DocReview.jsx`). Primary "can't zoom" complaint.
> ✅ Shipped (PR #220 → `main`). A native non-passive `wheel` listener on the scroll viewport → `zoomAround(factor, cursorX, cursorY)`: changes `scale`, stashes the page-unit point under the cursor, then a `useLayoutEffect` keyed on the re-rendered `dims` nudges `scrollLeft/Top` so that point stays under the cursor. Ctrl/Cmd+wheel and plain wheel both zoom (trackpad pinch arrives as Ctrl+wheel). Shares the anchor path with B290. Headless-verified (V72).

### B289 — No drag-to-pan in single-sheet review `[Doc Review / Markup]` (feature)  *(arrived as "NEW-2" 2026-06-20; minted **B289** — renumbered from B274)*
`[x]` Zoomed in, there's no way to grab-and-drag the drawing to move around — no hand tool, no space-drag — so navigation relies entirely on the scrollbars. (Scrollbars do work and reach the whole sheet, so this is a usability gap, not a blocker.) **Expected:** drag-to-pan (a Pan/hand tool and/or hold-Space to pan), matching the Stitcher, which already pans via pointer-drag (`Stitcher.jsx` ~L158/L168).
> ✅ Shipped (PR #220 → `main`). New **Pan** tool (hand) + **hold-Space** in any tool; pointer-drag adjusts the scroller's `scrollLeft/Top` by the negative pointer delta (pointer-capture so a fast drag doesn't drop). Cursor shows grab/grabbing. Releases capture + clears state on pointerup/pointercancel (so it can't reproduce B271's frozen-cursor lockout). Headless-verified (V72).

### B290 — ± zoom isn't cursor-anchored `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug, minor)  *(arrived as "NEW-3" 2026-06-20; minted **B290** — renumbered from B275)*
`[x]` `zoom()` only changes `scale`; it doesn't hold a focal point, so the detail you were looking at drifts and you re-scroll after each step. **Expected:** zoom toward the cursor (or hold the viewport center fixed), like the Stitcher's cursor-anchored wheel zoom. Pairs with B288.
> ✅ Shipped (PR #220 → `main`). The ± buttons now call `zoomAround(factor)` with the viewport centre as the anchor (same scroll-anchor path as B288), so the centre of what you're looking at stays put across a zoom step. Headless-verified centre drift 0.6px (V72).

### B291 — Double-click to finish a Count/Area/Perimeter adds 1–2 phantom points (inflates counts, distorts areas) `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug) — takeoff correctness, HIGH  *(arrived as "NEW-4" 2026-06-20; minted **B291** — renumbered from B276)*
`[x]` **Repro:** pick Count, click N items, then double-click to finish (as the tool hint instructs) → the count reads N+2 with two stray dots at the double-click spot; same root cause distorts Area/Perimeter (extra/duplicate vertices at the closing click). Cause: each pointerdown appends a point (`DocReview.jsx` onDown), and a double-click fires TWO pointerdowns before `onDoubleClick`→`finishDraft` commits. Enter finishes cleanly; only the advertised double-click path is broken. **Expected:** double-click finishes without adding the doubled vertices. The Site Planner already solved this with a shared `finishActiveDrawing()` + `removeLastVertex()` — reuse that approach.
> ✅ Shipped (PR #220 → `main`). `onDbl(e)` strips any trailing draft points coincident (≤ ~6px screen) with the double-click location before committing the poly/count, so the two pointerdowns the browser fires for a double-click can't survive as phantom vertices. Enter path unchanged. Headless-verified: 3 clicks + double-click → exactly 3 count dots, not 5 (V72).

### B292 — Zoom level resets to fit-width every time you switch sheets `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug, minor)  *(arrived as "NEW-5" 2026-06-20; minted **B292** — renumbered from B277)*
`[x]` **Repro (confirmed live 2026-06-20):** zoom Sheet 1 to 134%, click Sheet 2 → it snaps back to 31% (fit-width); zoom is lost on every sheet change. Cause: the sheet button calls `setScale(0)`. **Expected:** keep the current zoom across sheet switches when reviewing a set.
> ✅ Shipped (PR #220 → `main`). The sheet button no longer forces `setScale(0)`; switching sheets re-renders the new page at the current scale. The fit pass still runs on first open and on the explicit Fit / Fit-page buttons. (Merged cleanly with main's B267 per-sheet scale tooltip on the same button.) Headless-verified (V72).

### B293 — Can't move or edit a markup after placing it (Select only allows delete) `[Doc Review / Markup]` (feature)  *(arrived as "NEW-6" 2026-06-20; minted **B293** — renumbered from B278)*
`[x]` Today Select supports delete only — a misplaced redline/measurement/text note has to be deleted and redrawn, and placed text can't be re-edited. Key design points: drag a selected markup to reposition it (commit once on pointer-up, coords stay in page units); double-click a text note to edit it. The ParcelDrawing surface already implements move + edit-text (B67) — mirror it here.
> ✅ Shipped (PR #220 → `main`). Select-mode interior drag translates a markup's page-unit points live and commits once on pointer-up (a sub-3px drag is still a plain click-select; interior drag moves, never pans — per B155's locked rule). Double-click a text note opens an **inline `<input>` overlay** at the note (Enter/blur commit, Esc cancel); text **creation** routes through the same inline editor (opening on pointer-UP so the click's own focus change can't blur+discard it), removing Doc Review's `window.prompt` for text (KEY DECISION "no dialog-box edits" + the B155 note). Calibrate's prompt is left as-is (tracked under B155). Adjacent to B155 + B156, which stay open. Headless-verified move + create + edit (V72).

### B294 — Dropping a PDF only works on the empty screen, not once a document is open `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug, minor)  *(arrived as "NEW-7" 2026-06-20; minted **B294** — renumbered from B279)*
`[x]` **Repro:** with a PDF open, drag another PDF onto the canvas → nothing (you must use "Open another…"). The drop handler is bound only to the empty-state view; the Stitcher accepts drops anywhere. **Expected:** dropping a PDF over the open document opens it (reuse the existing re-drop/source-binding path).
> ✅ Shipped (PR #220 → `main`). The canvas/viewport now carries the same `onDragOver`/`onDrop` as the empty state, routed through the existing `openFile` (which already re-binds a re-dropped source by name so its markups stay attached). (Verified by code + the proven openFile path; a synthetic file-drop isn't in the headless harness.)

### B295 — "Fit" only fits width; tall/portrait sheets can't be viewed whole `[Doc Review / Markup]` (feature, minor)  *(arrived as "NEW-8" 2026-06-20; minted **B295** — renumbered from B280)*
`[x]` The fit logic computes width-only (`avail / base.width`), so a portrait/tall sheet overflows vertically and can't be seen in one view. Add a fit-to-page option (min of width-fit and height-fit) alongside fit-width.
> ✅ Shipped (PR #220 → `main`). New **Fit page** button next to **Fit**; the fit pass reads a `fitMode` ('width' | 'page') and uses `min(availW/baseW, availH/baseH)` for page-fit. Headless-verified Fit-page fits the whole sheet where Fit-width overflows (V72).

### B296 — Linear measurements round to whole feet, inconsistent with area's 2-decimal acres `[Doc Review / Markup]` (bug, minor)  *(arrived as "NEW-9" 2026-06-20; minted **B296** — renumbered from B281)*
`[x]` `measureLabel` prints distance/perimeter via `f0` (whole feet) while area shows 2-dp acres (`takeoff.js`) — a 150.6 ft line reads "151 ft". For takeoff precision, show at least one decimal on linear measures.
> ✅ Shipped (PR #220 → `main`). `measureLabel` now formats distance/perimeter with one decimal (`f1`); area (acres 2-dp / sf whole) unchanged. Covered by a unit test (`test/takeoff.test.js`).

### B206 — Storage-adapter discipline: confine all backend-specific logic to one module `[Server]` (task)  *(arrived as "NEW-1"; provisionally B203, renumbered **B206** — `main` took B203–B205)*
`[x]` Shipped 2026-06-19 (branch `claude/laughing-ritchie-k5narx`). A **single storage-adapter module is the only thing the app talks to for file ops** (save / fetch / list / move / rename / delete / share-link). The app references files **only by Planyr's own stable keys** — never a Google Drive file id, Drive folder path, or Drive sharing handle. The adapter's internal **mapping table is the only place Planyr-key ↔ backend-id translation exists**; no backend id leaks past it. **NEW-2/3/4 all sit behind this.**
- **What shipped:** `server/storage/adapter.js` (the only entry point — save/fetch/list/move/rename/remove/shareLink, all returning result objects, never throwing), `idMap.js` (the sole Planyr-key↔backend-id translator; in-memory store now, Supabase-Postgres-backed later), `result.js` (the `{ok}` result + `attempt()` wrapper), and `index.js` (server-side assembly — the one place creds are read). **20 unit tests** (`test/storageAdapter.test.js`) incl. the **acceptance test**: an "app consumer" written only against the adapter behaves identically across two different backends, and a list never exposes a backend id (an unbound backend object is invisible to the app).
> **Dedup:** the adapter is the **bytes** layer; the **index of file facts** (B180's `fileFacts` view-model + the `doc_reviews` table) is the separate catalog layer that records *which* file is *what* — they meet only at the Planyr key. Existing direct Supabase-Storage calls (`reviewStore.uploadSource/downloadSource`, `overlayStorage.js`) are the **adoption targets**: route them through the adapter when the Drive backend goes live (so the swap is verified end-to-end with real creds), not as risky blind surgery now.

### B208 — Share-by-link via a link-provider abstraction (Drive links now, Planyr links later) `[Server]` (feature)  *(arrived as "NEW-3"; provisionally B205, renumbered **B208** — `main` took B203–B205)*
`[x]` Shipped 2026-06-19. Sharing emits a link from a **single link-provider interface** (`server/storage/linkProvider.js`). For now it returns the backend's **native Drive share link** (recipients see a familiar Google Drive link — intentional, keeps the owner's company comfortable). **ALL link generation routes through this one interface**, so switching later to Planyr-native signed links (`planyr.io/s/<token>` → backend mints a temporary signed URL, serves bytes through the adapter) is a **one-place change** (`kind: "planyr"` + a `signer`). No Drive link call is hardcoded in UI/app code. **Tested** both kinds (Drive-native via the backend; Planyr signed via an injected signer; not-configured fails visibly).
> **Non-goal (deferred):** drag-a-file-out-of-the-browser-into-an-email — a desktop sync-client gesture; the owner uses Drive directly for that for now.

### B209 — File operations must surface success/failure; no silent file failures `[Server]` (task)  *(arrived as "NEW-4"; provisionally B206, renumbered **B209** — `main` took B203–B205)*
`[x]` Shipped 2026-06-19. Every adapter op (upload, fetch, move, rename, delete, link-generation) returns a **visible success/failure result** (`server/storage/result.js`): the adapter **never throws** and **never reports a half-finished op as success** — a throwing backend, a backend `{ok:false}`, or an unmapped key all surface as `{ ok:false, error }`. **Same severity class as the silent cloud-save failures that caused prior data loss.** Covered by the no-silent-failure tests in `test/storageAdapter.test.js`.
> **Dedup / align:** this **extends** the existing save-status-visibility guarantee (B125 — make cloud save status visible, no silent failures) to **Drive file operations**; it is the storage-layer contract, surfaced in the UI through the same honest-status pattern the persistence layer already uses (don't build a parallel status system — when the adapter is adopted, its `{ok:false}` feeds the existing save badge / banners).
