### B151 — Multipart parcel: clicking the smaller tract selects the wrong piece (only the largest part highlights/imports) `[Site Planner / map]` (bug) — relative of B36c  *(owner-reported 2026-06-18, "Pearland"; minted B151 — `main` concurrently took B147–B150, so this is the real next free ID)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B151 also names another item in this file:** “Import easement from a metes-and-bounds description (feature) *(arrived as "NEW-2"; min…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B151* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B151 against all of them.
`[x]` Repro (owner): Pearland, account **`0440520000010`** ("TRS 3 & 5 (AG-USE)", 15.5 AC, situs "0 DEL PAPA"). Clicking the **meat** of the parcel registers the account (selection count ticks up) but the clicked piece **does not highlight** — instead the **adjacent piece to the right** lights up. Owner clarification: *"I didn't click on a county line — it just won't let me click the parcel in the meat of the parcel."*
> **Root cause (confirmed by live endpoint probes AND a live headless-browser repro, not assumption).** `0440520000010` is a **HARRIS** parcel (HCAD + the statewide TxGIO layer agree; identical geometry), but it is **MULTIPART** — two physically separate tracts under one account: a **west tract ~6.66 AC** and an **east tract ~8.12 AC**, with a *different* parcel (`0440520000002`) between them. The geometry helpers in `arcgis.js` (`largestRingLngLat`/`featureToParcel`) deliberately returned only the **single largest ring** (the B36c "biggest |area| ring can't be a hole" pick). So a click anywhere in the parcel resolves the right account, but the highlight (`MapFinder` `handleClick`) and the planner import only ever drew/added the **east (largest) tract** → clicking the **west** tract appeared to select the neighbour, and planning the site silently **dropped ~6.66 AC** (card showed 8.12 AC, not ~15). Disproves the pasted brief's guesses: the parcel is Harris (not Brazoria/"missing county"); click coords round-trip exactly in EPSG:4326 (no SR bug — verified the geometry the app sends matches the click latlng); IDs are present and the highlight is drawn from geometry, not the ID field; the query is a true `esriSpatialRelIntersects` point-in-polygon (no nearest/buffer). The seam *does* exist (the parcel's south edge is the diagonal Harris/Brazoria line; a click just over it selects a Brazoria parcel that lives only in the statewide TxGIO layer) but that was **not** the owner's symptom — multipart was.
> **Fix (minimal + shared; branch `claude/nifty-bohr-mtz70c`).** New `outerRingsLngLat(feature)` in `lib/arcgis.js` returns **every outer-boundary ring** of a (possibly multipart) feature, classifying outers vs. holes by winding **sign** (so a separate small tract is kept even when a hole's |area| exceeds it — the B36c size trap), holes dropped, each ring opened. Wired into **all three** parcel-import paths so it's fixed everywhere, not per-symptom: (1) **map-click select** (`MapFinder.handleClick`) now highlights all parts via Leaflet **multipolygon** nesting (`[[part],[part]]`, not a hole-punch) and stores `rings`/`latlngsList`; `computeAssembly` emits **one planner parcel per part** in the shared frame (full acreage) and the cursor hit-test checks every part; (2) **in-planner identify → Add to plan** (`SitePlanner.addIdentifiedParcel`) adds every part (`ring` = largest is still kept for the jurisdiction/road straddle tests); (3) **in-planner address/account lookup → import** (`importFeature`) imports every part on one **shared** anchor so the tracts keep their true relative position. 5 new unit tests (`test/arcgis.test.js`: single ring; both tracts of a 2-part; donut drops the hole; small separate part kept despite a bigger hole; empty → []). lint **0 errors** · **230 tests** · build green; `SitePlannerApp` lazy chunk intact.
> **Browser-verified (Claude self-test, logged-out, served from the local `dist/` build).** Clicking the **west tract** now highlights **BOTH** pieces (highlight path = 2 subpaths spanning the full **1326×664 ft** parcel) and the card reads **"1 PARCEL · 14.78 AC · DEL PAPA"** (was 8.12 AC, east-only) — `gis-verify/pearland-FIXED-clickwest.png` (before: `gis-verify/pearland-mp-clickwest.png`; script `gis-verify/pearland-fix-verify.mjs`). Logged as **VERIFICATION V39**; no owner action.

### B146 — Interactive, decluttered dimension callouts (move + edit) + road-dimension fixes `[Site Planner / UI]` (feature)  *(arrived 2026-06-17; minted B146 — concurrent merges took B141–B145, so this is the real next free ID)*
`[x]` ✅ Both increments DONE + browser-verified 2026-06-17. Owner ask (2026-06-17): the red edge-dimension callouts overlap the centred name/area labels (see the B121 screenshots — the red "271" prints over "116,327 sf"). They should (1) **auto-move so they don't clutter in the first place**, and (2) be **directly adjustable** — click an element to select it, then click its dimension to grab it: **drag the dimension line to reposition it**, and (for roads) **click the dimension number to edit the width**. Apply the move interaction to **buildings, parking, and roads**. Plus two road fixes: the dimension must **track a resize** (it went stale), and roads should **resize in 1′ increments**.
> **Increment 1 — road-dimension fixes — ✅ DONE 2026-06-17 (branch `claude/determined-brown-bf86l7`), browser-verified.** (D) The road dimension callout (and the Element-panel "Travel width" field) now **derive from live geometry** via `roadTravelWidth(w,h,curb)` in `lib/siteModel.js` (unit-tested), replacing the frozen `el.travelW` that went stale after a resize — the resize handlers update w/h, so the callout now tracks. (E) Road resize (corner + edge handles) snaps to **1′ increments** (not the grid step), so a width dials to the exact foot. Self-verified headless: drew a road (dim **170′**), dragged a corner to widen it → dim updated live to **428′** (it would have stayed frozen before) — logged **V35**. lint 0 · 205 tests · build green.
> **Increment 2 — the interactive layer — ✅ DONE 2026-06-17 (branch `claude/determined-brown-bf86l7`), browser-verified** (owner chose "Full interactive"). (A) **Auto-declutter:** the dimension number now sits OUTBOARD of its line (away from the centred label), so it no longer overprints the sq-ft by default. (B) **Drag-to-move:** when an element is selected its dimension is a grab handle (a fat invisible hit-line along the dim) — drag it anywhere; the offset is stored per element as `el.dimOffset` (local feet, persisted) and a dashed **leader** points back to what it measures. Works for buildings, parking, and roads. (C) **Roads — click the number to edit the width:** clicking the dimension number opens an **inline on-canvas editor** seeded with the current travel width → `setRoadTravel`, resizing the road (the line still drags to reposition). Implementation: a `dimMove` drag mode + `startDimMove`/`editDimWidth` in `SitePlanner.jsx`, threaded into `renderElPx`; `dimOffset` rides through the Site Model additively (no migration). **No dialog boxes (owner rule, 2026-06-17 — "horrible UI"):** the width editor is a shared inline `numEdit` `<input>` overlay (commit on Enter / click-away, cancel on Esc), and the pre-existing per-edge **setback** and overlay **trace-length** `window.prompt`s were converted to that same inline editor; rule recorded in CLAUDE.md KEY DECISIONS. Self-verified headless: dragged a building's "314′" out with a dashed leader; clicked a road's "199′" → **inline box on the canvas (no dialog)** → entered 30 → road resized to a **30′** travel width — logged **V36 / V37**. lint 0 · 225 tests · build green.

### B137 — Fort Bend parcels render but aren't clickable (display covers more counties than the click queries) `[Site Planner / map]` (bug) — coupled to B11/B13/B36  *(filed as "B130" in the brief; minted B137 — `main` concurrently took B130–B136, so this is the real next free ID)*
`[x]` Repro: Map view → "✓ Selecting — click lots" → pan to a Fort Bend area (purple parcel outlines visible) → click directly on a lot → nothing selects; "No parcel right there — zoom in and click directly on a lot" fires. Harris parcels select fine at the same zoom. Expected: clicking any displayed parcel selects it, regardless of county.
> **Root cause (confirmed by live endpoint probes, not assumption).** The visible outlines and the click-query had different *coverage*. The `chambers` entry in `COUNTIES_MAP` is actually the **statewide TxGIO** parcel layer (one service covering all 254 Texas counties); its display layer (`makeParcelLayer`) has no county filter, so when zoomed in it **paints parcel outlines everywhere — including Fort Bend.** But on click, `candidateCountiesForPoint` only made TxGIO a query candidate inside the narrow *Chambers* bbox. A Fort Bend click therefore queried only **Harris** (returns nothing — verified 0 features at a Sugar Land point) and **FBCAD** — and FBCAD's host (`gis.fbcad.org/serverarcgis2`) is currently **down (HTTP 503 on every path, even the host root; Harris/TxGIO/Esri all return 200 from the same network)**. So the click had no answerer and fell through to the "no parcel" message, even though the TxGIO layer that drew the outline *does* return that exact Fort Bend lot on a point query (verified: `county:'FORT BEND', prop_id 40594`). This is precisely the brief's hypothesis #1 — display covers more than the queried source. (The brief's other guesses — separate selection service, missed reprojection, click tolerance — were ruled out: display and click share the same resolved per-county URL, `queryAtPoint` already sets `inSR:4326`, and Harris selects fine via the identical code path.)
> **Fix (minimal + structural; branch `claude/magical-ramanujan-v1dnuw`).** Marked the TxGIO source `statewide:true` in `COUNTIES_MAP` and made `candidateCountiesForPoint` (`lib/counties.js`) **always append any statewide source as a universal fallback** — so the click can always select an outline it can see. Appended **LAST**, so a county's own CAD still answers first when reachable (more authoritative, richer fields) and the statewide layer only catches clicks the county CAD didn't; the answering county is then corrected to its true CAD key by the existing **B36(a)** `countyAtPoint` relabel (already keyed on a `chambers`-sourced hit, so no extra wiring). This also makes Fort Bend selection **resilient to FBCAD being down** (TxGIO covers it) and keeps `viewCounty`/Layers-panel jurisdiction unchanged (bbox matches still lead). No change needed in `MapFinder` beyond what already existed. 5 new unit tests in `test/counties.test.js` (Fort Bend routes to fortbend + statewide fallback; fallback ordered last; no dup when in-bbox; Harris still leads; out-of-bbox still gets statewide). lint 0 errors · **180 tests** · build green; lazy chunk split intact.
> **Coupled to B11/B13/B36:** same county-resolution theme. Does NOT close B13-pt1 (true point-in-county polygons vs. the bbox pre-filter) — that's still the deferred, more-accurate routing; this is the resilience/coverage fix that makes "click anywhere selects the parcel you see" hold today. Browser confirmation (real click on a Fort Bend lot) logged as **VERIFICATION V29**; no owner action.

### B133 — NWI wetlands: restored from the live `fwsprimary` raster host + verified in-browser `[Site Planner / GIS]` (bug) — follow-up to B129  *(filed as "B130" in the hand-off; renumbered B133 — concurrent merges already took B130 (parking, #95), B131 (print overlay, #96) and B132 (detention pond, #99), so this is the real next free ID)*
`[x]` **Owner-spotted (2026-06-17).** Our configured NWI host `fwspublicservices.wim.usgs.gov/wetlandsmapservice/…` returns HTTP 500 (confirmed down in B129 — an agency-side outage). The owner opened the official USFWS **Wetlands Mapper** (`https://fwsprimary.wim.usgs.gov/wetlands/apps/wetlands-mapper/`) and the wetlands render fine — i.e. the data is LIVE on the **sibling host `fwsprimary.wim.usgs.gov`**; only the `fwspublicservices` alias is erroring. The likely fix is a one-line URL swap. **DO NOT ship it blind — verify in a browser first (the whole point of B129).**

**The fix (one line, `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/layers.js`, `STATEWIDE.wetlands.url`):** swap the host `fwspublicservices.wim.usgs.gov` → `fwsprimary.wim.usgs.gov` (path identical) →
`https://fwsprimary.wim.usgs.gov/wetlandsmapservice/rest/services/Wetlands/MapServer`

**PREREQ before you can verify (owner action — may already be done):** `fwsprimary.wim.usgs.gov` must be in the **egress allowlist** (owner asked 2026-06-17; egress changes only take effect in a NEWLY started session). Sanity-check reachability:
`curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'Origin: https://planyr.io' 'https://fwsprimary.wim.usgs.gov/wetlandsmapservice/rest/services/Wetlands/MapServer?f=json'`
- `403` + "Host not in allowlist" → not allowlisted yet; stop, tell the owner.
- `500` → fwsprimary now down too; hold (and re-check whether `fwspublicservices` recovered).
- `200` → reachable; proceed.

**⚠️ THE risk to settle in-browser (don't skip):** an out-of-band probe of `fwsprimary` on 2026-06-17 returned a *real* **403** (NOT the egress block — a server 403). That *might* mean `fwsprimary` only serves its own mapper and refuses cross-site / non-browser requests (Referer/Origin/UA/WAF). If our app's `<img>` export gets 403'd cross-origin from planyr.io, wetlands STILL won't draw. Public ArcGIS export endpoints usually allow cross-site, so it's *probably* fine — but confirm by eye. (CORS specifically doesn't block the picture: if `fwsprimary` sends no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, the esri metadata fetch fails but the image still loads via the CORS-exempt `<img>` — PR #60 resilience — so it should render anyway.)

**Verify (browser already set up — `.claude/` SessionStart hook installs Chromium; Playwright recipe + screenshots from B129 are under `gis-verify/`):** on planyr.io or a branch preview, toggle **Wetlands (NWI)** at **zoom 14+** over a known wetland (Sheldon Lake, the Greens/Halls Bayou greenways, or the Katy Prairie west of town). Confirm BOTH: (a) the `…/export?f=image` request returns **HTTP 200 `image/png`**, and (b) the green/blue wetland polygons actually **paint** on the map (do NOT trust the status dot — it lies). Like FEMA, NWI may be source-scale-gated, so zoom in.

**Then:**
- **Renders →** ship the swap (branch → PR → green build → merge) and update the `wetlands` comment in `layers.js` (it currently says "keep the canonical URL"; note that `fwspublicservices` went down 2026-06 and we moved to the `fwsprimary` sibling — the host USFWS's own live mapper uses — with the date).
- **403s cross-site / doesn't render →** do NOT swap. Leave `fwspublicservices` (it may recover; the honest "service unavailable" message already shipped in B129), and note the `/server` proxy as the durable fix (serves through our own origin, sidesteps both CORS and any cross-site refusal). Report to the owner.

**Key files:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/layers.js` (`STATEWIDE.wetlands.url` + the `wetlands` comment block) · browser tooling `.claude/hooks/ensure-browser.sh` · evidence `gis-verify/` · context B129.
> ✅ **Done 2026-06-17** (branch `claude/fervent-albattani-yyp0qe`). **The "one-line, same-path host swap" premise was wrong on both counts — but wetlands are back on, browser-verified.** What the investigation actually found: (1) the old `fwspublicservices` host is **still HTTP 500** across its whole catalog; (2) `fwsprimary` is reachable this session (so it's egress-allowlisted), but it has **no `/wetlandsmapservice/…` path (404)** — the assumed identical path doesn't exist there; (3) `fwsprimary`'s dynamic **vector** `Wetlands/MapServer/export` returns an HTML Web-Adaptor interstitial (not an image) and its `/0/query` 500s, so a dynamicMapLayer swap would NOT render; (4) the live data the official USFWS Wetlands Mapper actually draws is a **pre-rendered RASTER image service** at `/server/rest/services/Wetlands_Raster/ImageServer` — a different host AND a different service type. **Fix:** point `STATEWIDE.wetlands` at that raster URL and switch it from the defaulted `dynamicMapLayer` to **`kind:"esriImage"`** (esri `imageMapLayer`, the same path 3DEP uses); dropped the now-irrelevant `layers:[0]` and rewrote the comment block with the real story. Wetlands is render-only (no click-identify anywhere), so losing the vector layer's queryable attributes costs nothing today. **Verified in a real headless browser** (esri-leaflet `imageMapLayer` over Sheldon Lake, `gis-verify/wetlands-verify.{html,mjs}`): the `exportImage` request returns **HTTP 200 `image/png`**, the service metadata fetch returns **200 JSON**, and the standard NWI symbology (navy open water = Sheldon Lake, greens = vegetated wetlands) **paints** — screenshot `gis-verify/wetlands-fwsprimary-verified.png`. **B130's flagged cross-site-403 risk is DISPROVEN:** the host **reflects any `Origin`** in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (confirmed for `https://planyr.io`, localhost, and an arbitrary origin), so esri-leaflet's `useCors:true` image loads cross-site with no refusal; the earlier out-of-band 403 did not reproduce. lint **0 errors** · **197 tests** · build green (count after merging the latest `main` in; the change adds no tests — a GIS source swap is verified in-browser, like B129/FEMA) · `SitePlannerApp` lazy chunk intact. Browser pass logged as **VERIFICATION V26** (and supersedes V20's "wait for fwspublicservices to recover" re-check trigger). If `fwsprimary` ever 403s/500s, the honest "service unavailable" path (B129) still applies and the durable fix remains a `/server` proxy through our own origin. **Shipped to `main` via PR #101.** **⚠️ Correction (see B135):** that raster turned out to be a **100 m-per-pixel** source, so wetlands rendered as coarse **BLOCKS**, not true shapes — B135 switches to the crisp **vector** `Test/Wetlands_gdb_split` MapServer (`layers:[1,2]`), which is the Wetlands-Mapper look.
> **Follow-up (deferred, low priority — captured so it's not lost):** the **unused** future GIS-caching engine `lib/vectorLayers.js` (imported nowhere in the app yet; built for the Track-1 "GIS layer caching" roadmap item) still references the dead `fwspublicservices` host for both its vector `/query` and its `imageFallback`. There is **no drop-in vector replacement on `fwsprimary`** (its `Wetlands/MapServer/0/query` 500s and it exposes no FeatureServer — only the raster renders), so when that engine is eventually wired up, NWI there must either use the raster (no per-polygon `WETLAND_TYPE`) or wait for the `fwspublicservices` vector host to recover. Left as-is for now since it's not live and can't be browser-verified.

### B135 — Wetlands draw as coarse 100 m blocks (raster), not true polygons — switch to the crisp vector MapServer `[Site Planner / GIS]` (bug) — follow-up to B133
`[x]` **Owner-spotted (2026-06-17).** After B133 turned NWI wetlands back on, they painted as chunky ~100 m green/blue **blocks** instead of the true wetland shapes the official USFWS Wetlands Mapper draws. Cause: B133 pointed at `fwsprimary`'s `Wetlands_Raster/ImageServer`, which is a **100-m-per-pixel raster** (`pixelSizeX/Y = 100`) — inherently blocky at any zoom, and carrying no Cowardin class labels.
> ✅ **Done 2026-06-17** (branch `claude/fervent-albattani-yyp0qe`). Found and switched to the real **crisp vector** source. Investigation: `fwsprimary`'s production `Wetlands/MapServer` is an empty dynamic shell (export + query both 500); the polygons the Mapper draws live in the **staging** service `…/server/rest/services/Test/Wetlands_gdb_split/MapServer`, where layer 0 ("Wetlands") is empty and the data is split into **layer 1 = Wetlands_CONUS_East** and **layer 2 = Wetlands_CONUS_West** (Texas is in West). **Fix:** `STATEWIDE.wetlands` is now a **`kind:"dynamic"`** esri `dynamicMapLayer` (esri `/export f=image`, like FEMA) at that MapServer with **`layers:[1,2]`** (covers the lower-48). **Verified in a real headless browser** (`gis-verify/wetlands-verify.{html,mjs}`, now the vector variant): the `…/export?…layers=show:1,2&f=image` request returns **HTTP 200 `image/png`** with **true-shape polygons + NWI class labels** (PFO1A / PSS1A / PUBH…) over Sheldon Lake — screenshot `gis-verify/wetlands-fwsprimary-vector-verified.png` — and the host is **CORS-clean** (echoes `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://planyr.io`). Source-scale-gated (layer `minScale ~1:250k`) — like FEMA, zoom to about city level to see polygons. **CAVEAT (also in the code comment):** `Test/` is a USFWS **staging** path during their host migration; it may be renamed/removed when the production `Wetlands/MapServer` is repopulated (revisit then, or if `fwspublicservices` recovers) — and the app already degrades to the honest "service unavailable" path (B129) if it disappears. lint **0 errors** · **197 tests** · build green; `SitePlannerApp` lazy chunk intact. Browser pass logged as **VERIFICATION V27**. How I found it: loaded the live USFWS Mapper in a headless browser to read its real service refs (`gis-verify/mapper-capture.mjs`).

### B117 — Draw-tool palette can't scroll to its bottom on desktop → SHAPES group unreachable `[Site Planner]` (bug)
`[x]` Repro: open Site Planner on a normal laptop viewport; the dark draw-tool rail (the **Tools / Site elements / Shapes** palette) is taller than the screen but won't scroll to the end — the SHAPES group and anything below it sits past the fold and is unreachable. Expected: the rail scrolls cleanly to its last row at any viewport height, with the full list reachable. **Confirmed cause:** the rail container in `SitePlanner.jsx` sets `overflowY: narrow ? "auto" : "visible"`, so it only scrolls inside the phone/`narrow` overlay (B113); on the desktop path `overflowY:"visible"` + `flex:none` with no height bound lets the content spill off-screen with no scrollbar. Fix: give the rail `overflow-y:auto` on the desktop path too and bound its height to the viewport — it already sits in a flex row, so add `min-height:0` on the column so it can shrink-and-scroll; confirm the last row is fully visible.
> Not a dup of **B107** (that reworked the *mode-tab* column — Yield/Parcel/Element/Aerial/Overlay/Setup — and found it already fits) or **B113** (that added only the *phone* slide-in overlay, with its own `overflow:auto`; the desktop layout was left byte-identical, so this desktop scroll gap is untouched). Michael described it as the "left" rail; in the current build this palette renders on the **right** (dark chrome) — same element, identified here by its Tools/Site-elements/Shapes content. Pairs with **B118** (shorter rows overflow less often), but this is the underlying bug — even a short rail must stay fully reachable.
> ✅ **Done 2026-06-16** (branch `claude/eager-brahmagupta-7sagg0`). The rail container (`SitePlanner.jsx`) now uses `overflowY: "auto"` on the desktop path too (was `narrow ? "auto" : "visible"`) plus `minHeight: 0`, so it shrinks inside the height-bounded flex body row and scrolls to its last row at any viewport height — the SHAPES / Measure / Annotate groups below the fold are now reachable. Desktop layout otherwise byte-identical; the phone/`narrow` overlay path is unchanged. lint 0 errors · 138 tests · build green.

### B118 — Tighten draw-tool button height to fit more of the rail without scrolling `[Site Planner]` (task)
`[x]` The site-element and shape buttons are two-line (a primary label + a secondary descriptor — e.g. "single-load", "drive / court", "24′ travel", "free draw", "back-in storage", "detention basin") with generous vertical padding, so the rail overflows and forces scrolling for the core tools. Increase density: (1) cut the top/bottom padding on each row and tighten the gap/line-height between the primary label and the secondary descriptor; (2) shrink the secondary-descriptor text one step (it's supporting detail, not the label). Goal: fit at least through the whole **Site elements** group without scrolling on a standard laptop. ### B127 — Measure-type dropdown (and the other rail/header menus) render behind/clipped by the rail `[Site Planner / UI]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-3"; minted B127 — next after B126)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B127 also names another item in this file:** “Two-tab convergence: a stale tab could thin the durable store; open tabs didn't live-sy…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B127* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B127 against all of them.
`[x]` Repro: in the right tool rail, open the **Measure** tool's mode dropdown (the **▾** caret next to "Length"). Expected: the menu opens above all adjacent UI — fully visible and clickable. Actual: the flyout was partially/fully hidden — clipped by the rail, painting "behind" the neighbouring rail/zoom rail. **Root cause = the two classic CSS layer traps, both introduced/exposed by B117.** The rail container (`SitePlanner.jsx`) sets `position:relative; zIndex:30` (a **trapped stacking context** — caps every child's z-index against the canvas/map siblings no matter how high) **and** `overflowY:"auto"` (B117 changed this from `narrow ? "auto" : "visible"` to always `"auto"` to fix the desktop scroll-to-bottom). Per the CSS spec, once `overflow-y` is non-visible the `overflow-x:visible` **computes to `auto`** too, so the rail now clips horizontally — and these flyouts open sideways out of the rail (`right: calc(100% + 10px)`), so they got cut off. You cannot have a vertically-scrolling rail that also lets a child overflow sideways, so bumping z-index can't fix it.
> ✅ **Done 2026-06-17** (branch `claude/sweet-pasteur-5kd1p4`). Built the **durable, shared fix** the brief asked for: a new reusable **portal** popover layer `src/shared/ui/AnchoredMenu.jsx` (`ReactDOM.createPortal` to `document.body`) — the menu mounts at the document root, escaping **both** any ancestor stacking context **and** any `overflow:auto` clipping at once. It positions itself against its trigger via `getBoundingClientRect` (`position:fixed`, viewport-clamped, repositions on scroll/resize), measures-then-reveals so there's no flash, and keeps the click-away backdrop. z-index 4000/4001 = the app's existing modal layer (matches `ParcelDrawing`'s portal; above the map, below `AuthPanel`'s 5000). **Migrated every instance of the trapped pattern in the workspace** — not just the one menu: the 5 rail flyouts (**Measure**, Boundary, Building dock, Car-Parking rows, Road width) and the 3 header menus (**Site ▾**, **Plan ▾**, **File ▾**). Visuals/placement/widths unchanged. lint 0 errors · **152 tests** · build green; lazy chunk split intact (`AnchoredMenu` rides in the `SitePlannerApp` chunk). **Follow-up candidate (not done):** the Document Review `ReviewsBar` "Reviews ▾" dropdown is the same class in the other workspace — it opens downward and uses its own styling (not `menuPanel`), so it's left for a focused doc-review pass; the shared component now lives in `src/shared/ui/` so adopting it there is trivial. Browser pass queued as **VERIFICATION V16**. **Not merged to `main` — owner review first.**

### B126 — Data-loss ROOT FIX: sync kept the whole last-saved copy (a thinner one erased a fuller one) + automatic local backups `[Persistence]` (bug) — DATA-LOSS, critical
`[x]` Follow-up to **B124/B125**. The shipped B124 fix stopped whole *sites* from vanishing on pull, but buildings could still disappear *inside* a surviving site: both `saveSite`/the cloud and `mergePulledSites` reconciled two copies by **whole-record newer-`updatedAt`-wins** with **no content merge**, so any copy saved last with fewer buildings (a stale tab, a second device, a partial/mid-load save) silently overwrote the fuller one — and `pullCloud`'s re-push then propagated the thin copy to the cloud. Owner hit this: ~12 projects emptied while the last-edited one (SCHIEL, intact at ~10 buildings / 24 building-elements once bump-outs are counted) survived. Free-tier Supabase → no PITR, so the emptied sites weren't server-recoverable; owner opted to **fix forward** (quick to recreate) and harden against recurrence.
- Part of: **B648** (Persistence & Sync epic).
> **Fixed 2026-06-16 (branch `claude/zen-sagan-9otrll`).** (1) **Content-preserving merge** — `siteModel.js` gains `mergeSiteContent(a,b)`: scalar/meta come from the newer copy, but every drawn collection (els, markups, measures, callouts, parcels, sheetOverlays, parcelDrawings, elevation cross-sections) is **unioned by id**, so a building present in EITHER copy survives; a stripped inline raster is healed from the copy that still has it. `mergePulledSites` now uses it (was whole-record newer-wins) and re-pushes whenever the merge produced more content than the cloud had, so kept work reaches the cloud instead of being stranded. (2) **Automatic local version history** — `storage.js` snapshots the prior version of a site on every `saveSite` into a capped, slimmed (geometry-only), local-only ring (`planarfit:sites:history:v1`); `snapshotVersion`/`listVersions`/`getVersion` back the planner's **Plan ▾ → Version history…** dialog, which restores any earlier version (the replaced state is itself snapshotted, so a restore is reversible). **Trade-off documented:** a delete made in only one copy can reappear once (recoverable by deleting again) — per-item tombstones are the fully-correct future hardening, and the version history makes any surprise recoverable meanwhile. lint **0 errors** · **152 tests** (8 new: union-keeps-all, two-device union, per-id newer-wins, image-heal, end-to-end no-thinning + re-push, history captures/restores/de-dupes) · build green. Browser pass queued as **VERIFICATION V15**. **Not merged to `main` — owner verification first.**
> **★ Status corrected 2026-06-17 (this session): MERGED + DEPLOYED** via **PR #83** — confirmed live on planyr.io (the deployed `SitePlannerApp` chunk carries `planarfit:sites:history:v1` + the **Plan ▾ → Version history…** dialog). The "not merged" note is stale; the Version history restore is available to the owner now (key to **B136** recovery — local/per-device only). Effectively DONE (eligible to move to ✅ Done).

### B127 — Two-tab convergence: a stale tab could thin the durable store; open tabs didn't live-sync `[Persistence]` (bug) — follow-up to B126
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B127 also names another item in this file:** “Measure-type dropdown (and the other rail/header menus) render behind/clipped by the ra…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B127* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B127 against all of them.
`[x]` Found by the **V15** cohort run. **No data loss** (B126's automatic backup recovered the fuller copy), but a rough edge: with the SAME site open in two tabs, a stale tab's save/flush **blind-overwrote** the durable store with its thinner copy, so the two tabs could **disagree on reload** until the stale tab closed + one edit healed it.
> **Fixed 2026-06-16 (branch `claude/zen-sagan-9otrll`).** (A) **`storage.js` `saveSite` now folds a stale write into the store** instead of blind-overwriting: a per-TAB `lastSeenAt[id]` (set by `loadSite`/`saveSite`) distinguishes "I'm the current writer" (plain replace → single-tab deletes still stick) from "another tab advanced the store since I last synced" (content-merge via `mergeSiteContent` → never thins). So the durable store + every reload now always hold the union. (B) **`SitePlanner.jsx` adds an idle-guarded `storage`-event listener** that folds another tab's save into the open canvas (union — never drops either tab's work; only-if-changed to avoid churn/ping-pong; skipped while mid-drag/draw/typing), so two open tabs converge **live** without a reload. 2 new unit tests (stale-write folds; single-tab delete still sticks). lint 0 err · **154 tests** · build green. Re-test under **VERIFICATION V15** (two-tab case).

### B130 — Parking tool: "Split into rows" tiles single-loaded rows — generate double-loaded modules + correct curb logic + rename `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-1"; minted B130 — next after B129)*
`[x]` **Repro:** draw a car-parking area, click **"Split into rows."** **Current (wrong):** the field is tiled as `[stall row + drive aisle]` repeated down its whole depth — single-loaded throughout, a full aisle against every row (the most pavement-hungry layout; ~40% more depth per row than needed, so fewer rows fit and stall yield comes in low). **Expected:** tile a **double-loaded module** — two stall rows sharing one aisle.
- **Generation logic.** Repeating module = double-loaded: stall row + aisle + stall row. At 90°: 18′ + 24′ + 18′ = **60′ module**; stall width 9′ default. **Single-load only where geometry forces it:** the top row against a building face/sidewalk, a row against a property line, or a final strip too shallow for a full 60′ bay. **Remainder:** if the last band can't fit a full 60′ module, drop a single-loaded row or hand the strip back as leftover/landscape — **never insert another full aisle to fill it.**
- **Orientation:** rows parallel to the building face by default; fall back to the polygon's **longest edge**.
- **Parameters to expose:** stall width (8.5–9.5′, default 9′), stall depth (default 18′), aisle width (default 24′ at 90°), parking angle (90/60/45°), single- vs. double-loaded.
- **Curb logic (6″ curb).** Apply one 6″ curb around the **perimeter** of the paving, wherever pavement meets non-paving (dirt, landscape, building face, property line). **Never at internal seams** — aisle-to-stall-row inside a module, or stall-row-backing-onto-stall-row between stacked modules (that's continuous paving). **No curb across drive-aisle openings** where vehicles pass (entry throat, aisle-to-aisle, aisle-to-street) — there pavement meets pavement, so the meets-non-paving rule already skips it. A **dead-end aisle terminating against landscape DOES get a curb** (terminus, not blockage). Test: vehicles cross the edge → gap, no curb; vehicles stop at the edge → curb.
- **Rename:** change the button **"Split into rows" → "Split rows/aisles"** (it splits the field into stall rows + drive aisles). *(Owner 2026-06-17: explicitly NOT "Generate parking" / "Lay out stalls" — those don't fit; "Split rows/aisles" is the label.)*
- **Out of scope (tracked separately, large lift):** clipping the field to the parcel boundary.
> **Dedupe / reconcile — EXTEND the existing parking + curb code; do NOT build a parallel generator.** A double-loaded parking engine, the depth-stepping model, and a derived-curb system already exist (built in **PR #38** + **PR #86**), so most of NEW-1 is implemented and only specific gaps are genuinely open. Map of exists-vs-open:
> - **Double-loaded field-fill is already built and correct** — not single-loaded. `carStalls(w,h,cfg)` (`SitePlanner.jsx` ~375) tiles `mod = 2·rowDepth + aisle` (two stall rows per aisle) with a single-loaded trailing remainder only when a full 60′ module won't fit; defaults are already `stallW 9 / stallDepth 18 / aisle 24 / parkAngle 90` (~line 656) with 90/60/45° + per-element `cfg` overrides surfaced (Setup ~5765, per-element ~5380). So the **un-split** field already matches the spec (**B69**, Done). **The "single-loaded throughout" repro is `splitParkingRows` (~line 3619), not the fill:** clicking "Split into rows" evenly divides the depth into N independent one-row elements, each of which re-renders single-loaded — that is the live bug to fix.

### B15 — Import JSON drops callouts & markups, and leaves stale ones on the canvas `[Site Planner]` (bug) — DATA-LOSS, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed in audit PR. `importJSONFile` (SitePlanner.jsx ~2459) set parcels/els/measures/settings/underlay but **not** `callouts`/`markups`, although `exportJSON` writes them. Result: (a) imported callouts/markups are discarded; (b) the currently-open plan's callouts/markups aren't reset, so they bleed into the imported plan and get persisted on the next autosave. Fix: `setCallouts(d.callouts || [])` + `setMarkups(d.markups || [])` in import (symmetric with export).

### B16 — `isBlankSite` ignores `markups` → markup/encumbrance-only sites are silently deleted on leave `[Site Planner]` (bug) — DATA-LOSS, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed in audit PR. `isBlankSite` (SitePlanner.jsx ~795) omits `markups`, so a site whose only work is drawn markups or a plotted metes-and-bounds **encumbrance** is treated as blank: the autosave guard skips it and `persistOrDrop` *deletes* the un-located record on unmount. Fix: include `markups` in `isBlankSite` and in the autosave guard object.

### B17 — Doc Review local mirror saved without `updatedAt`; `reconcile` compares mismatched fields `[Document Review]` (bug) — DATA-LOSS risk, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed in audit PR. `buildSnapshot` (DocReview.jsx/Stitcher.jsx) omits `updatedAt`, so `flushLocal()→writeDraft` mirrors a record whose `data.updatedAt` is stale/absent; `reconcile` then compares cloud `updatedAt` vs draft `_localAt` (different events/clocks) and can let a stale local draft shadow a newer cloud copy. Fix: stamp `updatedAt: Date.now()` in `buildSnapshot` so the mirror and the cloud `data` carry a consistent timestamp.

### B18 — Last-debounce-window edits flush local-only and are lost when `pullCloud` blind-replaces on next login `[Site Planner]` (bug) — DATA-LOSS, high
`[x]` The beforeunload/visibility/unmount/site-switch flushes call `saveSite` (local cache) but **never** `pushSiteToCloud`; `pullCloud` then *replaces* the per-user cache wholesale on next login, discarding any edit made in the final ~400 ms before close that the debounced cloud push missed. Fix options: make `pullCloud` merge by `updatedAt` (keep the newer side), and/or push on `pagehide` via `fetch(..., {keepalive:true})`/`sendBeacon`. (Bigger change — left for review.)

### B19 — Resume-on-mount re-saves the just-loaded review with a fresh `updatedAt` `[Document Review]` (bug) — correctness, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `doc-review/b19-resume-resave`): `useReviewPersistence` exposes `suspendSave(ms)` which parks a suspend window; the autosave effect early-returns while it's active. `loadSingleReview` arms it once (single commit); `loadStitch` arms it at start and re-arms before its async `setPdfs`/`setPlaced` commits, so a programmatic load never re-stamps just-loaded data with a fresh `updatedAt`. `loadSingleReview`/`loadStitch` set state → the debounce deps change → autosave writes the loaded snapshot back with `updatedAt: now`, so a resume can stamp stale data as newest and (multi-tab) clobber a newer cloud edit. Fix: a `suspendSave` ref set during programmatic load, early-returning from the autosave effect for that tick.

### B21 — Down overlay re-probes & repaints the error banner every 45 s forever; background errors share the click-instruction slot `[Site Planner / map]` (bug) — correctness, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed in audit PR. `PROBE_TTL` (40 s) < the 45 s re-probe interval, so a genuinely-down enabled layer re-probes and re-fires `onError` every tick, repainting the bottom-left banner indefinitely; that banner is also the only `err` slot, so a background layer hiccup masks the "click a lot" guidance until a user action clears it. Fix: de-duplicate identical error toasts and auto-clear background layer errors after a timeout.

### B22 — Rapid parcel clicks race → duplicate selection + leaked highlight polygon `[Site Planner / map]` (bug) — correctness, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/map-gis-robustness`) — defensive: `handleClick` now removes any pre-existing hilite for a key before overwriting (no orphaned `L.polygon`) and dedupes the `selected` entry by key (no double-counted acreage). NOTE: in the current code the toggle check runs AFTER the `await`, so two clicks resolve sequentially into a correct toggle and the described double-add doesn't actually reproduce — these guards close the theoretical gap without an in-flight ref that would drop a legitimate second-lot click. `handleClick` is async with no sequence guard; two fast clicks on the same lot can both take the "add" branch (the toggle check runs before the first `await` resolves), producing a duplicate `selected` entry (double-counted acreage) and an orphaned `L.polygon` left on the map. Fix: guard with an in-flight ref / request id, and remove any pre-existing hilite for a key before overwriting.

### B23 — `ditchStats` returns `NaN` profile distance for a single elevation sample `[Site Planner]` (bug) — correctness, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed in audit PR. elevation.js only guards `length === 0`; with exactly one sample, `i/(n-1) = 0/0 = NaN` flows into the cross-section profile/labels. Fix: treat `< 2` samples as insufficient (`return null`), letting the caller's "no samples" path handle it.

### B24 — `measureLabel` prints `"NaN"` / can crash on degenerate measurement points `[Document Review]` (bug) — correctness, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed in audit PR. takeoff.js `measureLabel`/`measureValue` have no finite/length guard; an empty `distance` markup dereferences `m.pts[0].x` (throws) and short polys can render `"NaN ft/ac"`. Fix: guard missing/short `pts` and non-finite values.

### B25 — Metes-and-bounds: curve calls silently parsed as straight chords; no unreadable-call flagging `[Site Planner]` (bug) — correctness, high
`[x]` `CALL_RE` has no `radius`/`arc`/`delta`/`chord` handling; given a curve call it matches the chord bearing+distance and dead-reckons it as a straight segment, with no `dropped`/`unparsed` signal — so the traverse is silently wrong and the UI can't warn. (Roadmap already wants "parse curves; flag unreadable.") Fix: detect curve calls and either tessellate the arc or return `{unparsed:true, raw}` so callers can flag them.
> Progress 2026-06-15: deferred from the round-2 correctness PR — flagging/tessellating curve calls needs parser + UI work validated against real deed text (risk of breaking the working straight-call parser for Harris/FBCAD); left Open for a focused pass with sample deeds.

### B26 — Metes-and-bounds: parser gaps (dash-DMS unparsed, deg>90 accepted, loose closure floor) `[Site Planner]` (bug) — correctness, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/correctness-round2`): (a) `-` added to the degree/minute separator classes so `S 12-15 W` parses; (b) `parseCalls` skips any call with `deg > 90`; (c) the `pathCloses` absolute floor dropped 25 ft → 5 ft (the 2% relative term kept), so a small lot can't falsely "close" on 25 ft of misclosure. (a) The header advertises `S 12-15 W` but the DMS separator classes exclude `-`, so dash-separated bearings return `[]` (silently dropped). (b) The degrees group `[0-9]{1,3}` accepts a quadrant bearing > 90° (e.g. `N 145 E`) and plots it. (c) `pathCloses` floors tolerance at `max(25, 2%·perim)` so a small lot can be declared "closed" with a 25-ft misclosure, hiding parse errors. Fix: add `-` to the separator classes; reject/flag `deg>90`; drop/shrink the absolute closure floor and always surface the misclosure.

### B27 — Enter-to-commit power-line trace uses stale `tracePts`/`traceMode` `[Site Planner]` (bug) — correctness, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed in audit PR. The keydown effect closes over `traceMode`/`tracePts` but they're not in its dep array, so pressing Enter to finish a trace reads stale values (often `[]`). Fix: add `traceMode`/`tracePts` to the effect deps (double-click already worked because it's a fresh prop).

### B28 — `mergeRings` collinear-cleanup threshold is area-based (scale-dependent) `[Site Planner]` (bug) — correctness, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/correctness-round2`): the corner test now thresholds the perpendicular deviation `|cross|/hypot(c−a)` (> 0.1 ft), so it's scale-independent. The corner test `Math.abs(cross) > 1` compares twice-triangle-area in ft² (scales with edge length), so on long edges a real slight bend can be dropped (or noise kept), distorting a merged parcel boundary/acreage. Fix: threshold the *perpendicular distance* `|cross|/hypot(c−a)` against a small foot tolerance.

### B29 — Parking +/− shrink guard ignores per-field `cfg` overrides `[Site Planner]` (bug) — correctness, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/b58-b62-planner-correctness`): `parkBand(el)` and `canShrink` now derive the band from `cfgOf(el)`, matching `growParking`. `parkBand()`/`canShrink` use global `settings.stallDepth/aisle`, but `growParking` uses `cfgOf(el)`; for a field with per-element cfg the on-canvas − handle is enabled/disabled against the wrong row size (guard disagrees with the actual op). Fix: compute the band from `cfgOf(el)` in the guard too.

### B30 — Markup/measure minimum size is in feet, not pixels → silently discarded when zoomed out `[Site Planner]` (bug) — minor, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/correctness-round2`): the minimums are now `3 / view.ppf` ft (a ~3px drag), so a deliberate drag isn't silently dropped at any zoom. The `dist(a,b) >= 2` / `w,h >= 2` minimums are world-feet; at low ppf a deliberate multi-pixel drag can be < 2 ft and the markup/measure is dropped with no feedback. Fix: make the minimum pixel-based (scale by view ppf).

### B31 — Two-point Split returns null when both crossings share an edge `[Site Planner]` (bug) — minor, low
`[x]` `if (lo.i === hi.i) return null` uses only the extreme-`t` hits, so a valid straight cut across a concave parcel (whose first/last crossings land on the same edge while valid interior crossings exist) silently no-ops. Fix: when `lo.i === hi.i`, pick the two crossings with distinct edge indices that yield two ≥3-vertex rings.
> Progress 2026-06-15: deferred from round-2 — the same-edge multi-crossing case is fiddly concave-polygon geometry (minor/low) that's hard to validate without runtime cases; left Open to avoid shipping a bad split.
> **Superseded 2026-06-17 by B128 (Done):** the whole concave multi-crossing case (not just the same-edge sub-case) is now handled by a correct general slice in `lib/polygonSplit.js` — see B128 for the validated fix.

### B32 — Undo stack polluted by `pushHistory` on no-op edits `[Site Planner]` (bug) — minor, high
`[x]` `beginEditCallout` and the dock/type `onChange` handlers call `pushHistory()` before/without an actual change, so cancelling a callout edit or reselecting the same dropdown value adds an undo frame (first Ctrl+Z appears to do nothing). Fix: push history only when a mutation is actually applied.
> Progress 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/correctness-round2`): the **callout** half is fixed — `beginEditCallout` no longer pushes history on open, and `commitEditCallout` pushes only when the text actually changes (cancel or commit-unchanged adds no frame). Re-checked the **dock/type dropdown** half — it's a NON-ISSUE: a native `<select>` `onChange` fires only on an actual value change (re-selecting the already-selected option doesn't fire it), so it never adds a spurious frame. The callout half was the real bug; B32 is resolved.

### B33 — Doc Review redline shapes (rect/cloud/text) are unselectable except at corner points `[Document Review]` (bug) — minor, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `doc-review/followup-minors`): `hitTest` is now shape-aware — rect/cloud select across their whole body (point-in-box ± tolerance), text selects across its rendered label box, and measures select on nearest vertex OR segment (so a line body selects, not just its endpoints). `hitTest` measures distance only to stored vertices; rect/cloud store two corners and text one point, so clicking an edge or body never selects them (hard to select/delete redlines). Fix: shape-aware hit testing (point-in-rect, distance-to-segment, text bbox).

### B34 — Doc Review single-viewer `render()` calls `setScale` internally → re-entrant render race `[Document Review]` (bug) — correctness, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `chore/audit-tail-grind`): the fit-to-width scale is computed in its OWN effect (when `scale===0`); `render()` returns early until a concrete scale exists and no longer calls `setScale`, so it's a pure draw and the double-render / `dims` mismatch is gone. In fit-to-width mode `render` calls `setScale(s)` then keeps drawing; the `scale` change re-fires the render effect, so two renders run and `dims`/canvas can briefly mismatch the overlay. Fix: compute fit scale in a separate effect; keep `render` a pure draw at a concrete scale.

### B35 — `listProjects` status display is fragile (newest-row-wins; fallback drops status) `[Document Review]` (bug) — minor, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `doc-review/followup-minors`): `listProjects` returns `status:"unknown"` (not `"active"`) when the value is missing or the status read fell back to the no-status query, and `ProjectLibrary` renders a neutral "Status?" placeholder for an unknown status (still settable) — so a failed read no longer silently reports every project as "active." (Group-consistency is unchanged: status is group-wide per B7, so newest-row stays a fair representative.) Status is read from whichever group row sorts first by `updated_at`, and if the `status:data->>status` select errors the fallback query omits status so every project shows the default "active" — silently misreporting lifecycle. Fix: resolve status group-consistently and surface "unknown" rather than defaulting to active on a failed status read.

### B37 — Cloud/auth hardening `[Site Planner / auth]` (bug) — low/minor
`[x]` 🔧 partially fixed in audit PR. (a) **fixed:** `cloudDelete` now scopes by `user_id` AND `id` (was RLS-only). (b) **fixed:** the autosave cloud push had no `.catch`, leaving the save badge stuck on "Saving…" on a rejected upsert. (c) **fixed:** `metaRef` omitted `county`, so a save whose merge-base lacked county could normalize it to null — now self-contained. (d) **fixed:** `testConnection` now accepts any https origin (custom Supabase domains) — PR #27; the `pullCloud`-failure-empty-library half was fixed separately as B54 (#21).

### B39 — PDF.js documents are never `destroy()`'d → growing memory leak across a review session `[Document Review]` (bug) — leak, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `chore/audit-safe-fixes-b39-b45`): the prior doc is destroyed before swap (DocReview `setPdfDoc` helper) and the Stitcher destroys docs as they leave state via a diff effect, plus an unmount cleanup in both. `loadPdf` returns a `PDFDocumentProxy` (worker + retained ArrayBuffer); every replacement just overwrites `pdfRef.current` / `pdfs[].doc` (openFile, load, resetSingle, resetStitch, loadStitch) with no `.destroy()`, and there's no unmount cleanup. A repo-wide grep for `.destroy()` in doc-review is empty. Heavy construction sets leak MBs per open; the stitcher holds N docs at once. Fix: destroy the prior doc before replacing, destroy each removed/replaced source in the stitcher, and add an unmount effect that destroys the live doc(s). (Deferred from the audit PR only to avoid editing files a parallel agent was reading — will fix in the consolidated pass.)

### B40 — Superseded PDF render tasks are never cancelled `[Document Review]` (bug) — perf, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `chore/audit-safe-fixes-b39-b45`): `renderPageToCanvas` now exposes its `RenderTask` (an `onTask` callback); `render()` keeps it in a ref, `cancel()`s the prior one before each render and on unmount, and swallows `RenderingCancelledException`. `renderPageToCanvas` creates `page.render(...)` and only awaits its promise; `render()` discards the stale *result* via the `renderTok` token but never calls `task.cancel()`. Rapid page/zoom changes pile up overlapping renders and can hit PDF.js's "cannot use the same canvas during multiple render operations" (throw/torn output). Fix: return the `RenderTask`, keep a ref, `cancel()` before starting a new one and on unmount; treat `RenderingCancelledException` as a no-op.
> **Amendment — residual same-canvas race, fixed 2026-06-21 (branch `claude/modest-turing-wixo1y`).** (Folded in from a coworker-chat note, not a new item.) The B40 fix had a hole: `renderTaskRef.current` is only populated AFTER `await pdf.getPage()` inside `renderPageToCanvas`, so during render #1's getPage await, render #2 starts, finds `renderTaskRef.current` still null (nothing to cancel), and both proceed to `page.render()` on the same canvas — the exact "Cannot use the same canvas during multiple render operations" error B40 targeted, swallowed, leaving the canvas on a superseded sheet. **Fix:** `renderPageToCanvas` now takes an `isStale` predicate and checks it right BEFORE `page.render()`; `DocReview.jsx` passes `() => tok !== renderTok.current`, so a render superseded mid-getPage bails (returns null) before it touches the canvas — only the newest render draws. Verified: lint 0 · 802 tests · build green; headless `ui-audit/verify-b322-b40.mjs` shows 0 same-canvas errors across rapid switches (V85). Shipping via PR #240 → `main` (with the B326–B328 batch).

### B41 — Global keydown effects have no deps array → re-subscribe on every render (hot path) `[Document Review]` (bug) — perf, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `chore/audit-safe-fixes-b39-b45`): both now bind the `keydown` listener ONCE (`[]` deps) and dispatch through an `onKeyRef` refreshed each render, so the handler keeps live closures without re-subscribing on every render. DocReview.jsx and Stitcher.jsx register their `keydown` listener in an effect with no dependency array (the `}); // eslint-disable-line` pattern), so the handler is removed+re-added after *every* render — and `onPointerMove`→`setCursor` re-renders dozens of times/second while drawing. Fix: register once with `[]` and read `draft`/`sel`/handlers from refs inside `onKey`.

### B42 — `SitePlannerApp` rebuilds `siteGroups` (a Map over all sites) every render `[Site Planner]` (bug) — perf, medium
`[x]` ✅ already addressed (verified 2026-06-15): `siteGroups` is already `useMemo`'d on `[sites, activeSiteId]` in `SitePlannerApp.jsx` (with a "stable identity" comment) — the IIFE the audit flagged had since been converted, so no code change was needed. `const siteGroups = (() => { … })()` runs unconditionally each render, allocating a fresh array passed as the `sites` prop to `MapFinder` — O(n) per render and a referential-stability hazard that defeats child memoization. Fix: `useMemo(…, [sites, activeSiteId])`. (Safe, small — will fix in the consolidated pass.)

### B43 — `applyUser` auth-event handling has no sequence guard → races on fast auth transitions `[Site Planner / auth]` (bug) — correctness, medium
`[x]` `applyUser` is async (`setActiveUser` → `await pullCloud` → `refreshSites`); overlapping auth events (INITIAL_SESSION→SIGNED_IN, or fast sign-out/in) can interleave so `prevUid.current`/`clearCloudCache` run out of order and clear/point at the wrong user's cache. Fix: capture a monotonic token before the await and bail stale completions (the file already uses a `live` guard elsewhere).

### B44 — Doc Review async refresh/flush lack in-flight guards `[Document Review]` (bug) — minor
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `doc-review/b19-resume-resave`, alongside B19): (a) the flush now gates its cloud upsert on a `dirtyRef` (set on a real edit, cleared on a successful write), so a single↔stitch toggle with no change no longer re-upserts; (b) `ReviewsBar.refresh` is token-guarded (latest wins) and its outside-click listener moved to its own effect; (c) `ProjectLibrary.refresh` is token-guarded too, so an overlapping/late refresh (incl. `fileDrop`'s) can't clobber newer state. (a) `useReviewPersistence`'s unmount cleanup unconditionally fires a cloud `upsert` on every single↔stitch mode toggle (wasteful double-write even when nothing changed) — gate on a dirty flag. (b) `ReviewsBar` re-runs `listReviews()+listProjects()` on every `signedIn` flip while open and has no in-flight guard, so a slow resolution can clobber newer state; (c) `ProjectLibrary.fileDrop` calls `refresh()` in `finally` even if the drawer closed, and overlapping refreshes can interleave. Fix: split outside-click vs fetch effects and add an `ignore`/AbortController guard; `useCallback` the refreshers.

### B45 — Stitcher keeps large PNG data URLs for every placed sheet in state `[Document Review]` (bug) — perf, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `chore/audit-safe-fixes-b39-b45`): `renderPageToImage` now returns a `URL.createObjectURL` blob URL (data-URL fallback), and the Stitcher revokes URLs as sheets leave state via a diff effect + unmount cleanup. `renderPageToImage` returns `canvas.toDataURL("image/png")` at scale 2 and each placed sheet stores that multi-MB base64 string in `placed[].href`; reloads/re-binds regenerate them without releasing the old ones (data URLs can't be revoked). Fix: use `canvas.toBlob` + `URL.createObjectURL`, track and `revokeObjectURL` on remove/replace/unmount.

### B46 — `LayerPanel` Mapillary token desyncs across its two instances `[Site Planner]` (bug) — minor
`[x]` The token is seeded once via `useState(() => mapillaryToken())` in each `LayerPanel` (map + planner both render one); typing in one doesn't update the other's local `tok`, and an externally-set token isn't reflected on reopen. Fix: lift the token to shared state (alongside `overlays`) or read from a subscribable source.

### B47 — ArcGIS `where`-clause hardening (LIKE wildcards + auto-detected field names) `[Site Planner]` (bug) — security, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/map-gis-robustness`) — **part (b)**: the parcel-lookup `where` builder now validates `idField`/`addrField` against `/^[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$/` before interpolating, so a hostile/compromised (or user-pasted) layer's metadata can't inject a field name that escapes the `scopeWhere` county confinement. **Part (a)** — escaping `%`/`_` LIKE wildcards via an `ESCAPE` clause — is **deferred** (must verify Harris/FBCAD accept `ESCAPE` before shipping; low risk — read-only public data). A security pass found the rest of the app **clean** (Supabase queries are parameterized with no injection surface; RLS/storage policies sound; secrets handled correctly; all text/SVG render paths are React-escaped). The one item: the parcel-lookup `where` builder escapes the user *value*'s quotes (`'`→`''`, blocks the realistic breakout) but (a) does not escape LIKE wildcards `%`/`_` (a value of `%` enumerates rows — minor, public read-only data; the statewide TxGIO/Chambers layer is still confined by `scopeWhere`), and (b) interpolates `idField`/`addrField` **unescaped** — and those come from live layer metadata (or a user-pasted "Service / layer URL"), so a hostile/compromised endpoint could inject a field name that defeats the `scopeWhere` county confinement. Read-only/public so not critical. Fix: validate the detected field name against an identifier allowlist (`/^[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$/` and/or `meta.fields.some(f=>f.name===idField)`) before interpolating, and escape `%`/`_` with an `ESCAPE` clause (verify the CAD datasources accept `ESCAPE` before shipping — don't break Harris/FBCAD search).

### B48 — Client-side Anthropic key (title reader) + reusable HTML-escape helper `[Site Planner]` (bug) — note, low
`[x]` `lib/titleReader.js` instantiates the Anthropic SDK in the browser with `dangerouslyAllowBrowser:true` and the user's own key from `localStorage` (`planarfit:anthropicKey`). This is the documented BYO-key, no-backend pattern (not a committed/bundled secret), but the key is localStorage-resident and reachable by any script on the origin. ### B49 — Document Review file-input validation `[Document Review]` (bug) — crash/correctness

### B50 — Export/print & prompt robustness `[Site Planner]` (bug) — minor
`[x]` 🔧 partially fixed in audit PR. ### B51 — Stitcher async handlers have no in-flight guard → re-entrant interleave corrupts placed sheets `[Document Review]` (bug) — data-loss, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `doc-review/async-safety`): `loadStitch` sets a `loadingRef` while it rebuilds `pdfs[]`/`placed[]`, and `openFiles`/`addSheet` bail when it's set — so a click during a load can't have its sheet clobbered by the load's blind `setPlaced(out)`. (`bindSource` stays unguarded; it's internal to `openFiles`.) `openFiles`/`addSheet`/`bindSource`/`loadStitch` each `setBusy(true)…await…finally setBusy(false)` but none *reads* busy as a re-entrancy guard, and they mix functional updates (`addSheet`: `setPlaced(arr=>[...arr,…])`) with snapshot overwrites (`loadStitch`: `setPlaced(out)`). Clicking "add sheet" while a load is mid-await lets the load's blind `setPlaced(out)` clobber the just-added sheet. Fix: `busyRef` guard at the top of each, or disable the tray/open while busy; prefer functional updates / reconcile rather than overwrite.

### B52 — Doc Review load/open paths lack a cancellation token → opening B while A loads mixes the two `[Document Review]` (bug) — correctness, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `doc-review/async-safety`): both load paths capture a `loadTok` at start and bail before each post-await `setState` if a newer open superseded them — `loadStitch` before `setPdfs`/`setPlaced`; `loadSingleReview`/`fetchSourceBytes` before `setPdfDoc` (destroying the late doc) — so opening B while A loads can't land A's PDF/sheets on B. `loadStitch` (Stitcher) and `openReview`→`loadSingleReview`→`fetchSourceBytes` (DocReview) run long await chains (download + loadPdf + render) and then unconditionally `setState` (reviewId, meta, markups, pdfRef, placed) with no "is this still the requested review?" check. Open review A then B quickly and A's late resolution overwrites B's PDF/sheets while ids/markups are B's — and the autosave then persists the mix under the wrong id. Fix: capture a token (the requested `rec.id`) in a ref and bail before each post-await `setState` if superseded (mirror the single-sheet `renderTok` pattern). Related to B19.

### B53 — In-planner `identifyAt` lacks a token → second click shows/adds the wrong parcel `[Site Planner]` (bug) — correctness, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/map-gis-robustness`): `identifyAt` captures an `identifyTok` at call start and bails before `setIdentifyRes` if a newer click superseded it (matches the single-sheet `renderTok` pattern). `identifyAt` (SitePlanner) sets `{busy:true}`, awaits `resolveLayerUrl`/`queryAtPoint`, then unconditionally `setIdentifyRes({attrs,ring,…})`. Clicking P2 before P1 resolves lets P1 overwrite P2's result, so the panel/`addIdentifiedParcel` use the wrong lot. (Distinct code path from the already-logged MapFinder `handleClick` race, B22.) Fix: a token captured at call start, checked before the post-await `setState`.

### B54 — `pullCloud` overwrites the per-user cache with `{}` when a cloud fetch errors `[Site Planner]` (bug) — data-loss-shaped, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/b54-cloud-pull-guard`): `cloudList` now THROWS on a real fetch error (vs. a genuinely-empty result); `pullCloud` catches it, SKIPS the cache write, and returns `{ ok:false }`, so the cache (the user's last-known sites) is preserved; `applyUser` then shows a dismissible "showing your last synced copy" banner instead of a silent empty library. B18's separate half (merge-by-`updatedAt` + `sendBeacon`-on-pagehide) stays open — it carries a delete-resurrection subtlety, so it's deliberately left under B18. `cloudList` returns `[]` on *error* (cloudSync.js), so `pullCloud` can't tell "no sites" from "fetch failed" and blind-writes an empty map to the per-user cache; signing in while offline/unreachable thus shows "no sites" and wipes the local cloud cache to empty (data safe in Supabase, but a scary empty state that the user might start recreating into). Fix: have `cloudList` throw/return a status on error; `pullCloud` must skip the cache overwrite on error and surface a "couldn't load" state. (Sharpens B18/B37d into a concrete fix.)

### B55 — Fire-and-forget promises without `.catch` → unhandled rejections; async continuations touch torn-down objects `[Document Review / Site Planner]` (bug) — minor
`[x]` `uploadSource(...).then(...)` (DocReview + Stitcher), the `usePersistence` unmount/visibility `flush()` cloud upsert, and the `probeService(...).then(...)` overlay continuation all lack `.catch`, so a rejected Storage/DB/network call is an unhandled rejection. The `probeService` continuation also does `lyr.addTo(map)` after the await with no map-teardown guard (can throw if the map was removed mid-probe). Fix: add `.catch(()=>{})` to the fire-and-forget calls (matching the `pushSiteToCloud(...).catch` convention) and guard `addTo` with `map._loaded`.

### B56 — Assorted async UX/robustness `[Site Planner / Document Review]` (bug) — minor
`[x]` Grouped: (a) `goAddress` double-submit — Enter isn't gated by `busy` (only the Go button is), so two geocodes can race the `flyTo`; (b) transient `overlapWarn` messages each schedule their own `setTimeout(()=>setOverlapWarn(""))` with the id discarded, so a stale clear blanks a newer warning (and `runXSection` has no in-flight guard); (c) `setProjectStatus` upserts group rows serially and ignores per-row failure, returning `ok:true` even if one plan kept the old status (inconsistent group status) — use `Promise.allSettled` and report partial failure; (d) the evidence layers drop `moveend` events that arrive while a fetch is in flight (no trailing-edge refresh), so the last view may never load; (e) the doc-review mutation handlers (`del`/`onStatus`/`fileDrop`) call `refresh()` after an await with no open/mounted guard.
> Progress 2026-06-15: (a) shipped in #30, (d) in #33; **(c) done here** (branch `chore/audit-tail-grind` — `setProjectStatus` now writes the group's plans in parallel via `Promise.allSettled` and returns partial-failure counts); (e) covered by the B44 in-flight guards (PR #32). **(b)** — the `overlapWarn` stale-timer — left open: the clean fix is a single timer-ref `flashWarn` helper across ~12 call sites (or a uniform auto-clear effect that would flatten per-message durations); minor UX, not worth churning 12 sites.
> **(b) done 2026-06-17 (branch `claude/keen-curie-2ic2cg`) — this closes B56 (a/c/d/e already shipped).** A single timer-ref `flashWarn(msg, ms)` helper now owns the warning toast: it cancels any pending auto-clear *before* showing a new message, so a stale timer from an earlier warning can no longer blank a newer one. All 32 message-setting `setOverlapWarn(...)` sites route through it — transient ones pass their duration; sticky instructional prompts pass `ms=0` (no auto-clear, but they still cancel a prior timer so a stale clear can't wipe them either). The bare `setOverlapWarn("")` clears (Escape, Cancel, toggle-off) stay as-is: a later `flashWarn` cancels any lingering timer, and a fired timer just re-blanks an already-empty toast. Also fixed the second half of (b): `runXSection` got the missing in-flight guard (`xsecBusyRef` bails a second cross-section run while one is still sampling, reset in `finally`), plus an unmount cleanup that clears the pending timer. lint 0 err · 174 tests · build green · lazy split intact. Browser-verify logged as **V23**.

### B58 — Ditch cross-section drops no-data DEM samples without preserving position → wrong pond depth `[Site Planner]` (bug) — correctness, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/b58-b62-planner-correctness`): `sampleProfile` now keeps no-data as `null` (position preserved), and `ditchStats` places each surviving sample at its true fractional distance and takes banks from the end-most VALID samples. `sampleProfile` (elevation.js) does `.filter(v=>isFinite(v))`, discarding position; `ditchStats` then assumes uniform spacing (`d = i/(n-1)*lenFt`) and takes `bankFt = (elevFt[0]+elevFt[n-1])/2`. 3DEP commonly returns no-data over water/low ground, so surviving samples aren't evenly spaced — the profile x-axis is distorted, and if the true endpoints were no-data the "bank" is taken from interior points, so `depthFt` (the headline number applied to the pond's available depth) is wrong. (Distinct from the B23 1-sample NaN.) Fix: map each sample to its fractional position BEFORE filtering; treat leading/trailing no-data as missing banks rather than substituting interior points.

### B59 — Parking render/count/panel ignore per-element `cfg` → "Drive aisle on the far side" toggle is inert `[Site Planner]` (bug) — correctness, high
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/b58-b62-planner-correctness`): all three `carStalls(...)` calls now pass `cfgOf(el)` (which merges `{...settings, ...el.cfg}`), so a field's per-element `flipDepth`/depth/aisle/angle take effect in count + render — the "Drive aisle on the far side" toggle works. The renderer, metrics, and panel all call `carStalls(el.w, el.h, settings)` with the GLOBAL settings, never `cfgOf(el)`, so a parking field's per-element `cfg` (notably `flipDepth`, and side-parking strips created with `cfg`) has no visual/count effect — the panel's "Drive aisle on the far side" checkbox writes `cfg.flipDepth` but nothing reads it for drawing. Trailer rendering correctly uses `el.cfg`, so it's an inconsistency. Fix: use `cfgOf(el)` (which merges `{...settings, ...el.cfg}`) in the three `carStalls(...)` call sites.

### B60 — Detention bottom area spuriously non-zero when the basin over-tapers `[Site Planner]` (bug) — correctness, medium
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/b58-b62-planner-correctness`): `areaAt` now compares the offset ring's SIGNED area to the footprint's and returns 0 on a winding-sign flip (over-taper), so the bogus positive bottom is gone and the "tapers to a point" guard fires. `detentionStorage`'s `areaAt(down)` returns `offsetPolygon(ring, slope*down)` area; when `slope*depth` exceeds the footprint's inradius, `offsetPolygon` yields an inverted (flipped) ring rather than null, and the self-check uses `polyArea` (abs value), so a bogus positive "bottom" passes. Result: overestimated prismoidal volume and the "Basin tapers to a point — reduce depth/slope" guard (`aBottom===0`) never fires. Fix: detect collapse via a signed-area sign flip (or offset distance ≥ inradius) and return 0.

### B61 — Two-click road drawn shorter than it is wide mis-assigns the length/cross axis `[Site Planner]` (bug) — minor
`[x]` Road creation sets `w:len, h:roadWidth+2*curb`, but downstream infers the cross axis from `min(w,h)` (curb render `el.w>=el.h`; `roadTravel` `min`; resize `el.h<=el.w`). A stubby road (`len < cross`) has `w<h`, so curbs draw on the wrong edges and the length/width fields control the swapped axis. Fix: tag an explicit length axis at creation and key rendering/resize off it (or clamp `len>=cross`).
> Progress 2026-06-15: deferred from round-2 — a complete fix needs an explicit length-axis tag threaded through render/resize/roadTravel; a creation-time clamp alone leaves resize able to reproduce it. Left Open for that focused change.

### B62 — Utility-route corridor leaves a visible gap to the fitting pad `[Site Planner]` (bug) — minor, cosmetic
`[x]` 🔧 fixed 2026-06-15 (branch `site-planner/b58-b62-planner-correctness`): the route now includes the pad centre (`pts=[source, entry, padC]`), so the corridor reaches the fitting pad. `buildUtilRoute` buffers `pts=[source, entry]` where `entry` is on the wall, but the pad sits outside the wall (`entry + normal*(padSize/2+3)`), so the drawn corridor never reaches the pad. Fix: include the pad center in the route (`pts=[source, entry, padC]`) before buffering. (Math/easement-width/overlap checks are otherwise correct.)
