### B67 — Attach & mark up a site-plan drawing on a parcel `[Site Planner]` (feature)
`[x]` **Done 2026-06-16 (browser-only tranche complete: MVP + increments 2a/2b/2c).** Let the user attach an existing site plan (PDF or JPEG; CAD/DWG out of scope for v1) to a selected parcel and draw on top of it with the full existing markup/element toolset, saved as a persistent, named file tied to that parcel. The pattern mirrors Document Review's **immutable-backdrop + editable-layers-above** model and its Supabase persistence — reuse those patterns, don't stand up a parallel drawing engine or store. (Related to but distinct from B14, which files drawings under *projects* in the Document Review workspace; this attaches to a *parcel* in the Site Planner and marks up with the planner's own tools.)
- **Entry point.** After clicking a parcel (e.g. the Schiel Road site), offer "Attach drawing" / "Open markup." Allow **multiple drawings per parcel** (a parcel may have several plan sheets).
- **Backdrop = immutable layer.** The imported PDF/JPEG is the locked backdrop (architecture invariant: imported drawing = immutable; user content lives on editable layers above). PDF → rasterize the chosen page to an image for display; if multipage, let the user pick the page.
- **Markup layer = editable.** Reuse the current `els` + `markups` suite (lines, polylines, polygons, text, dimensions, freehand — whatever the suite already supports), not a separate drawing engine.
- **Anchoring v1 = pixel-relative to the backdrop.** Store markup coordinates **normalized to the backdrop's intrinsic pixel dimensions (0–1 fractions, not screen pixels)** so zoom/pan can't corrupt geometry. Nothing may assume the backdrop is screen-sized.
- **Forward-compat for georeference (deferred).** Persist the backdrop's **intrinsic dimensions** and (for a PDF) **page size/DPI** alongside the markup — the minimum needed later to compute a pixel→Texas-State-Plane (EPSG:2278) transform without re-marking. No georeferencing UI in v1; just don't discard the data that makes it possible.
- **Persistence.** Save as a named file/record associated with the parcel through the existing Supabase save/load + RLS path (**private by default**). Reopening restores backdrop + markup layer.
- **Out of scope v1 (follow-ons):** CAD/DWG import; real-world georeferencing; and **overlaying the marked-up plan onto the live map/aerial** — that last is the "overlay onto site" goal that converges with the ★ north-star ("map → drawings → latest set") and the shared coordinate spine. Flagged here as a follow-on, not v1.
> Cross-ref 2026-06-15: the deferred "overlay onto the live map/aerial" follow-on noted just above is now a filed item — **B72** (drag-drop a site-plan PDF onto the map, place by hand) + **B73** (scale calibration / precise alignment). B67 stays distinct (parcel-attached markup in *pixel* space), but shares the immutable-backdrop + PDF-rasterize + Supabase machinery — build them on the same primitives.
> Progress 2026-06-16 (branch `claude/laughing-babbage-hrxgct`): **browser-only MVP shipped + screenshot-verified.** Select a parcel → Parcel panel → **"＋ Attach a drawing (PDF / JPG)"** → it rasterizes the file (reusing the B72 `openOverlayFile` engine — PDF.js via dynamic import, off the main thread; image path too) and opens a full-screen **`ParcelDrawing`** markup modal: the imported file is an **immutable backdrop** and you draw on an editable layer above it with **Select / Pen / Line / Box / Text**, a colour picker, delete, fit/zoom/pan. **Markups are stored PIXEL-RELATIVE (0..1)** of the backdrop's intrinsic dims, so zoom/pan can't corrupt them (verified: a seeded rect + text land exactly on the backdrop). **Multiple drawings per parcel** (listed in the panel, open/delete). **Persistence:** additive Site Model field **`parcelDrawings`** (`SITE_MODEL_VERSION` 4→5, `parcelDrawingsOf` selector, `slimForCloud` strips the raster like the overlay/underlay); saved via a `saveSite` MERGE + debounced cloud push, so it needs no new wiring through the autosave path and **existing sites are unaffected** (empty field = no-op). **Forward-compat:** the backdrop's intrinsic dims (PDF points) ride with each record for a future pixel→EPSG:2278 transform. The modal **portals to `<body>`** so its toolbar clears the shell header (B66 stacking floor). **lint 0 · 56 tests (incl. a new parcelDrawings test) · build green.** ⏳ **Deferred to a focused increment 2 (B67 stays `[ ]`):** (a) the **multipage page-picker** (page 1 only today; `pageCount` is stored); (b) **Supabase Storage backing** of the source file so the raster reloads cross-device (today the raster is local + stripped from the cloud row → a re-login shows a "re-attach to view; markups saved" placeholder, exactly like B72's first increment; **markups always persist**); (c) richer markup parity with the planner's full suite (dimensions/measure, freehand smoothing) and on-backdrop markup editing/move (today: draw + select + delete + recolour). Runtime-verified headless via `ui-audit/screens/parcel-drawing.png`; please also try it on planyr.io with a real PDF.
> Progress 2026-06-16 (increment 2a — page-picker, branch `claude/laughing-babbage-hrxgct`): **multi-page PDFs now prompt a "Pick a sheet" dialog** at attach (lists all `pageCount` pages; the chosen sheet rasterizes via the B72 `rasterizePage`, reusing the already-loaded PDF for page 1; the record is named `"<file> — p.N"`). The PDF proxy is kept alive only for the pick then destroyed (no leak). Single-page PDFs and images skip the dialog. Removes limit (a). lint 0 · 138 tests · build green.
> Progress 2026-06-16 (increment 2b — Storage backing, branch `claude/laughing-babbage-hrxgct`): **the source file now backs the backdrop in Supabase Storage for cross-device reload.** On attach, the original PDF/image is uploaded (background, fallback-safe) to the existing private `doc-review-files` bucket at `<uid>/parcel-drawings/<siteId>/<drawingId>.<ext>` (new `uploadParcelDrawingFile` in `overlayStorage.js`, uid-first so the existing Storage RLS holds); the returned `storageKey`+`ext` persist on the record (kept through `slimForCloud`, which only strips the raster). Opening a drawing whose local raster is missing (cross-device — the cloud row's `src` was stripped) **rehydrates** it: download bytes → `rasterizeStoredPdf(bytes, page)` for PDFs, or `downloadOverlayDataUrl` for images, with a "Loading the drawing from the cloud…" state. Delete now also best-effort-removes the stored object. All fallback-safe (logged-out / >50 MB / error → keeps the local raster, no regression). Mirrors B72's overlay Storage-backing exactly. This **closes limit (b)**. Remaining for B67: (c) richer markup parity (dimensions/measure, move/edit existing markups). lint 0 · 138 tests · build green; **cohort to confirm the cross-device round-trip live** (`VERIFICATION.md` V9) — can't be exercised headless (needs a signed-in session + Storage).
> Progress 2026-06-16 (increment 2c — richer markup, branch `claude/laughing-babbage-hrxgct`): **closes limit (c); B67 → done.** In `ParcelDrawing.jsx`: (1) **move** any existing markup — in Select, press-and-drag a shape/text to reposition it (cursor shows ⤧move; a transient `moving` overlay avoids a save per pointer-move, commits once on release, pixel-relative throughout); (2) **edit text** in place (double-click — preserved); (3) a **Measure tool + one-time Scale calibration**: draw a **Scale** line and enter its real length → sets feet-per-pixel; the **Measure** tool then labels each line's true length in feet (teal chip), live while drawing. The calibration is stored as a `type:'calib'` markup, so it **persists through the same `onSave(markups)` channel** — no extra plumbing. Verified headless (`ui-audit/screens/parcel-drawing.png`: a 0.26-wide measure line reads **124 ft** against a 200-ft / 0.42-wide scale ✓). Optional future niceties (not blocking): resize/rotate handles on a selected shape. lint 0 · 138 tests · build green.

### B69 — Paving "+" over-increments from a single-loaded bay `[Site Planner]` (bug)
`[x]` Repro: start from the ~42–47′ paving cross-section (one parking row + one drive aisle — a single-loaded bay = parking on one side of the aisle only) and click "+". **Observed:** it added two parking rows plus another drive aisle (a full double-loaded module). **Expected:** "+" adds exactly one parking row — from a single-loaded bay it converts to double-loaded (parking both sides of the existing aisle, ~60–65′); a new drive aisle is inserted only once the current aisle is already double-loaded; each click steps by one row, never a two-row module. (Filed from a parallel chat as provisional "NEW-1"; minted **B69** here — B67/B68 were already taken on `main`.)
> Done 2026-06-15 (branch `claude/nice-wozniak-2k2v9c`). **Root cause:** `growParking` stepped depth by a whole `stallDepth+aisle` band per click, but the renderer/counter (`carStalls`) re-flows the field into *double-loaded modules* (2 rows share 1 aisle), so a single band of added depth re-striped into ~2 extra rows + an aisle — the jump the report saw. (Distinct from the already-fixed B29/B59, which were per-element `cfg` plumbing in the same area, not the increment model.) **Fix:** two pure helpers — `parkDepthForRows(n)= n·stallDepth + ⌈n/2⌉·aisle` and its inverse `parkRowsForDepth(h)` — model double-loading explicitly; `growParking` now reads the current row count and sets the depth for `n±1`, so the increment alternates +stallDepth (single→double-loads the last aisle) / +stallDepth+aisle (adds a new aisle) exactly as specced. `setParkCfg`, `splitParkingRows`, `canShrink`, and the two "Split into rows" `≥2` gates were moved onto the same row model so depth↔rows stays consistent; the "+" button/tooltip relabelled "＋ Row" / "Add one parking row" (was "Row + aisle"). Verified: 42→60→102→120→162 (rows 1→2→3→4→5, +18/+42/+18/+42), round-trip `rows↔depth` clean for n=1..8; build + tests pass.

### B70 — Curbs: derived auto-placed bands with visual / calc / dimension rules `[Site Planner]` (feature)
`[x]` Curbs are derived auto-placed thin bands — not user-placed, draggable, or deletable; they float to stay attached to their surface as rows are added/removed. Default = 6″ mono curb ("mono" = single monolithic pour, no gutter pan), occupying 0.5′ of plan-view width. **Placement:** terminal (the outermost band of every section gets a curb on its far/back edge); sidewalk transition (a curb between a sidewalk and the parking/drive it abuts — sidewalk behind, pavement dropping at the curb face); never a building-side curb. **Three-way representation, one rule for all sections (standard / truck court / trailer alike):** always *drawn*; always in the *calculations* (area, yield, paving SF, the width feeding any math → 18′ stall + 24′ aisle + 0.5′ = 42.5′; a 135′ court = 135.5′); never in the *displayed dimension* (reads 42′, 135′, 185′ — to the face of curb; the 0.5′ lives only in geometry + calc).
> Inspection first (what already existed): **roads already implemented the exact three-way contract** — a road's footprint includes its 6″ curbs (`h = travelW + 2·curb`), the curbs are drawn as lines, area uses `w·h` (curb included), and the on-canvas dimension shows `travelW` (curb excluded). So the *pattern* was proven; the gap was that **parking, paving/truck-court, and trailer carried no curb at all** (no draw, no calc, no rule). Built only that gap, generalizing the road contract to the other paved types.
> Done 2026-06-15 (branch `claude/nice-wozniak-2k2v9c`). A single derived-curb model (`curbEdgesOf(el, allEls)`, a **module-level** helper — no `cfgOf`/component scope, so it's safe inside `renderElPx`; cf. B68) is the one source feeding both the drawn band and the math: terminal curb on the edge pointing **away** from the host building (so never building-side); a sidewalk-transition curb on the inner edge when a sidewalk/landscape strip sits between the pad and its host; both depth ends for a free-standing field. The element's `w/h` stays the **face-of-curb** size, so (a) the displayed dimension already excludes the curb with no change, and (b) the curb is derived on top and *floats* to the terminal edge as rows change — no stored geometry. **Calc:** `curbAreaOf` (Σ edge-length·width) is added to the element's paving/parking/trailer bucket and thus to impervious — so a 200′ bay reads 8 500 sf (eff. 42.5′) and a 300′ court reads 40 650 sf (eff. 135.5′), while the on-canvas label still reads 42/135. **Draw:** a thin band whose width *scales* (so the 12″ option visibly doubles the 6″), kept legible by its stroke when the 0.5′ is sub-pixel at low zoom. Roads untouched (excluded from the new model; they keep their own curbs). Build + tests pass.
> Deferred nuance (kept minor, not blocking): the sidewalk-transition and free-field-both-ends cases are geometric heuristics (same-host + inboard; ±depth ends) rather than an explicit stored curb edge; polygon (irregular) pads are out of scope for the auto-curb. Revisit if a future case needs a hand-placed/overridden curb edge.

### B71 — Per-element curb override on trailer parking (6″ → 12″) `[Site Planner]` (feature)
`[x]` Selecting a trailer-parking element exposes a curb selector: default 6″, option 12″ (heavier curb to take trailer-tire/dolly abuse). 12″ = 1.0′ of plan-view width (double the 6″ curb's 0.5′) — real plan width, not a taller face/reveal (height unchanged). Flows through the same three-way rule as B70: drawn in the visual field, included in calculations (a trailer section with a 12″ terminal curb counts the full 1.0′ in area/width math), excluded from the displayed dimension (185′ still reads 185′). Build the property globally underneath (any band could carry it) but surface the control only on trailer parking for now.
> Done 2026-06-15 (branch `claude/nice-wozniak-2k2v9c`). The width is a global per-element field `el.curbW` (`CURB_6 = 0.5` / `CURB_12 = 1.0`) read by `curbWidthOf(el)`, so any band *could* carry it; the **6″ / 12″ control is surfaced only in the selected-trailer panel** (`setCurbW`). It rides the B70 model end-to-end: the drawn band scales to 1.0′ (visibly double), `curbAreaOf` counts the full 1.0′ in the SF/width math, and the displayed dimension is untouched (still face-of-curb). Trailer fields show no on-canvas dimension number today, so there's nothing to wrongly include the curb in; the rule holds the moment one is shown. Verified: a 12″ curb on a 300′ edge = 300 sf vs the 6″ 150 sf; build + tests pass.

### B74 — "New plan, same parcel" drops the site's county → identify/jurisdiction defaults to Harris `[Site Planner]` (bug) — medium

### B75 — Chambers county-acreage check ~10.76× wrong; flags every correct parcel as a huge mismatch `[Site Planner]` (bug) — high
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. The TxGIO statewide source (Chambers) names its already-in-acres fields `GIS_AREA`/`LEGAL_AREA` (with a sibling `*_UNIT`), which the `countyAcres` acres-regex didn't match → it fell through to a projected `st_area` in m², ÷43560 (ft²/ac) → ~10.76× too small; the old "tenx" m² guard also corrected the wrong way (÷ instead of ×). `countyAcres` now prefers `gis_area`/`legal_area` when the sibling unit says "Acres"; the geometry-check badge detects an m²-misread Shape area and shows the **corrected** acreage (a correct lot reads ✓, not "900% off ▲"). Badge-only — never fed the yield math (which uses the drawn polygon).

### B76 — Cross-county OBJECTID selection-key collision mis-toggles parcels `[Site Planner / map]` (bug) — medium

Key is now namespaced `"<county>:<oid>"`. (Distinct from the B22 rapid-click race; the dedupe/hilite guards there are unchanged.)

### B77 — `fileNewReview` ignores upload failure → silently files an unopenable document `[Document Review]` (bug) — medium
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. A non-oversize `uploadSource` failure (network/RLS/transient 5xx) was stored as a normal source (`storageKey:null, oversize:false`) and `fileNewReview` returned `ok:true` with no feedback. It now returns `{ uploadFailed }`, and `ProjectLibrary.fileDrop` collects failures and alerts ("filed, but the upload failed — re-drop on open to view"). ### B78 — Parking/trailer stall layout can infinite-loop (freeze) on a degenerate config `[Site Planner]` (bug) — critical (latent)
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. `carStalls`/`trailerStalls` compute `mod = rowDepth*2 + aisle` then `mods = floor(h/mod)` and loop `mods` times; `mod===0` (0 stall-depth + 0 aisle) makes `mods` Infinity → an unbounded band loop that hard-freezes the tab (and a 0 stall-width/`tw` made `perRow` Infinity → unbounded render loop). The current UI clamps these inputs (`min` 1/8/1), so it's **not reachable from the fields today** — the live freeze a sibling audit saw was a transient mid-deploy regression — but legacy/`cfg`-merged data could still hit it, so added an early-return guard (`mod>0 && pitch>0`; `tw>0`) to both.

### B79 — Negative/zero Grid size infinite-loops the grid render; size fields have no upper bound `[Site Planner]` (bug) — high (latent)
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. `gridLines` used `step = settings.gridSize` directly; a 0/negative step made `for (x…; x += step)` never terminate (freeze). Clamped `step = Math.max(0.1, +gridSize || 10)`. The Grid field's `min={1}` already blocks it from the UI; this hardens the loop itself. Also added `max={MAX_DIM}` (100000 ft) to the element Width/Depth fields so a fat-fingered/pasted size can't produce absurd geometry or SVG-coordinate stalls.

### B80 — Underlay calibration divides by zero on a 0 ft/px underlay `[Site Planner]` (bug) — low
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. `applyCalibration` guarded `knownFt>0`/`measured>0` but not `underlay.ftPerPx>0`; a degenerate underlay → Infinity/NaN placement (image flies off-canvas). Added `underlay.ftPerPx > 0` to the guard (covers the derived `sy` too).

### B81 — Self-intersecting / near-zero polygons accepted everywhere → silently wrong area `[Site Planner]` (bug) — medium
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. Parcel/element/measure-area close handlers only gated on vertex count; a bow-tie outline closes and `polyArea` (abs shoelace) returns the *net* area (lobes cancel) with no warning, corrupting siteSqft → coverage/FAR/parking/detention. Added `polySelfIntersects` + `flashPolyWarn` on close (parcel / drawn element / measured area): warns on a self-crossing or ~zero-area outline (accepts but flags, so the number isn't trusted silently).

### B82 — Calibrate tool is a silent no-op with no underlay `[Site Planner]` (bug) — low
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. Calibrate sits in the main toolbar (selectable with no underlay); clicks hit `if (!underlay) return` silently. Now flashes "Calibrate needs an underlay — drop an aerial/screenshot first."

### B83 — Copy/Duplicate carries dangling host/court metadata `[Site Planner]` (bug) — low
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. Paste/duplicate stripped only `attachedTo`, keeping `truckCourt`/`forCourt`/`dogEar`/`oppSide`/side-park/sidewalk tags — so a copied child carried court metadata pointing at nothing (refit/trailer logic reads it). Added a shared `detachClone` that strips all relational tags on clone. (Copying a host building's whole attached assembly is a separate enhancement — noted, not done.)

### B84 — Metes/POB plot silently cancels when no bearings parsed `[Site Planner]` (bug) — low
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. `anchorEncumbrance` returned silently when the description produced 0 calls (e.g. an unreadable format). Now warns "No bearings were recognized…", with a separate message when the calls can't form a shape. (The underlying curve/dash-DMS parser gaps stay under B25/B26.)

### B85 — Empty callout left on Escape; zero-length cross-section makes a degenerate profile `[Site Planner]` (bug) — low
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. The global Escape cleared `calloutDraft` but not an in-progress empty *new* callout — now calls `cancelEditCallout()` (added `editCallout` to the keydown effect deps so the closure stays fresh). `runXSection` now requires `lenFt > 1` (a same-point cross-section produced NaN profile distances).

### B86 — Split tool corrupts area on concave parcels `[Site Planner]` (bug) — high
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16 (complements B31). `splitPolygon` keys off the extreme-`t` crossings, so a straight cut across a concave parcel (4+ crossings) can yield overlapping/omitting halves whose areas don't sum to the original → wrong siteSqft + every downstream yield. Added an **area-conservation + self-intersection guard** in `performSplit`: if the two pieces don't conserve area (±2%) or come out self-intersecting, the cut is rejected with "that cut crosses the parcel ambiguously — try a straight cut between two opposite edges," instead of saving corrupted geometry. (A full polygon-clipping rewrite for multi-piece concave cuts stays deferred per B31.)

### B87 — `Infinity` / scientific-notation in a numeric field bypasses the min-clamp → NaN geometry, persisted as null `[Site Planner]` (bug) — high
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. `NumInput.commit` rejected only `isNaN`, but `parseFloat("1e999")`/`"Infinity"` return `Infinity` (not NaN) and `Math.max(min, Infinity)===Infinity`, so a non-finite value slipped through — Grid=Infinity made `snap` return NaN (every new coord NaN), a size=Infinity drew nothing, and `JSON.stringify` then persisted NaN/Infinity as **null** (permanent corruption). Now requires `Number.isFinite(n)` and applies a default `1e7` upper cap when no explicit `max`; `snap` also guards a non-finite/≤0 grid (falls back to 10). Closes the persist-as-null source (B91).

### B88 — Type confusion: a record whose `parcels`/`els` isn't an array crashes the whole app `[Site Planner]` (bug) — medium
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. `createSiteModel` kept any truthy value (`p.parcels || []`), so a tampered/legacy/bad-sync record with a non-array collection flowed into `parcels.reduce(...)` → `TypeError` → blank app on load. Now coerces every collection (`Array.isArray(...) ? ... : []`) and `settings` to an object. Added a unit test (40 tests pass). (The B68 error boundary already contained the blank-screen; this stops the throw so the site actually loads.)

### B89 — "Travel widths" free-text feeds road geometry → NaN roads `[Site Planner]` (bug) — medium
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. The road-width preset list `.split(",")` of the free-text field offered any token (e.g. `abc`) as a selectable width; drawing with it did `+"abc" = NaN` → a NaN road persisted as null. The preset list now keeps only finite, positive numeric tokens.

### B90 — No cross-tab reconciliation: a second tab's finder list goes stale `[Site Planner]` (bug) — medium→low
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. Added a `window` `storage` listener that refreshes the finder list when another tab changes the site store. **Re-scoped on inspection:** the audit's "whole-store clobber" doesn't actually reproduce — `saveSite`/`deleteSite` already read-modify-write the latest store per call, so a second tab editing a *different* site can't wipe the first's work; the real symptom was a stale list, which this fixes (logged-in tabs now also pick up each other's cloud-cache writes).

### B91 — NaN/Infinity coordinates persist as `null` (corruption amplifier) `[Site Planner]` (bug) — low
`[x]` Addressed-at-source 2026-06-16. The non-finite *sources* are now closed (B87 NumInput/snap, B89 road widths, plus the B78/B79 freeze guards), so no path feeds a non-finite coordinate into a save. A deep on-save geometry sanitizer was deliberately NOT added — rewriting stored points risks corrupting valid geometry, worse than the rare amplified case it would catch.

### B92 — Unbounded text/emoji/RTL in annotations bloats the SVG/record `[Site Planner]` (bug) — low
`[x]` Fixed 2026-06-16. Callout/text annotations now cap at `maxLength={2000}`. (Injection was already safe — XSS payloads render escaped.)

> **Triaged but NOT changed (still open / deferred, by decision):** building bump-outs aren't clamped when the host shrinks (medium, geometry — risk-deferred); `deleteSite` cloud delete stays fire-and-forget (zombie only if the delete fails — B-class edge); over-quota save still drops the underlay and reports success (graceful-degradation, minor); `currentSite` pointer global-not-per-user (low). County straddle/out-of-coverage messaging stays under **B13/B36**; metes curve + dash-DMS under **B25/B26**; bundle size / Anthropic-SDK / Mapillary-token / Nominatim / deploy-churn remain LOW/infra.

### B93 — Jurisdiction identify: city limits, ETJ & county `[Site Planner / GIS]` (feature) — SHIP target (promoted from deferred 2026-06-17)
`[x]` Click any point — or, **on explicit request**, run on the active parcel — and get back which jurisdictions it falls in: incorporated city (or "unincorporated"), any city **ETJ** (extraterritorial jurisdiction), and county (Harris, Fort Bend, Montgomery, Galveston, Brazoria…). **Trigger: click / explicit request only — NOT auto-loaded on every parcel.**
- **Interaction:** a map click runs a point-in-polygon "identify" against the loaded boundary layers; also identify-on-demand for the active parcel. **Test the whole parcel, not just its centroid** — flag boundary-straddle (e.g. partly City of Houston, partly unincorporated Harris Co.) and list *every* jurisdiction it touches rather than forcing one answer.
- **Coverage:** Houston-metro priority cities (Houston, Baytown, Missouri City, Sugar Land, Pearland, …), but driven by a **source registry**, never per-city hardcoded logic — adding a city = adding a registry row, not new code.
- **Source-priority chain (the crux):** query in fallback order per layer — authoritative city source where it publishes good GIS (e.g. Houston / COHGIS) → regional backbone (**H-GAC**, the Houston-Galveston Area Council, whose GIS covers the 13-county region) → statewide backbone (**TxDOT Open Data**, which publishes city limits + ETJ statewide). **One generic ArcGIS-REST connector** parameterized per source; a registry row stores endpoint URL, layer ID, and a field map. (Same connector serves **B94** — build it once.)
- **Field mapping:** every source names the city field differently (`CITY_NM` / `NAME` / `MUNICIPALITY` …). The registry normalizes each source's schema into one internal shape so the UI is source-agnostic.
- **Reuse existing GIS infra — do NOT build a parallel system:** same cache (**B96**), same per-layer honest status + visible data-age, same ~45 s self-heal re-probe, same Texas State Plane frame.
- **Screening-only framing:** ETJ is volatile (Texas law now lets landowners petition out of a city's ETJ; annexations move city limits) — label results screening-only, always show source + age, never present as a legal/official determination, keep a visible "verify with the jurisdiction" note.
- **Build step before wiring (evidence-first):** confirm each candidate endpoint actually responds and carries the expected fields, then calibrate against a few parcels whose jurisdiction is already known. Don't assume an endpoint/schema exists — verify it.
> **Relationship to B13 / B36 (county-resolution theme) — not a duplicate, but adjacent.** B13-pt1 and B36(a)/(d) have been *waiting on a county-boundary polygon dataset* to replace the coarse per-county **bbox** pre-filter (true point-in-county CAD routing + straddle merge). B93 introduces exactly that data path — county boundary polygons loaded via the new source registry + point-in-polygon. So B93's county layer **is** the dataset those items need: land it and B13-pt1 / B36(a)/(d) can be closed or folded in. They're still distinct items (B13/B36 = *internal CAD-routing*; B93 = a *user-facing* city/ETJ/county identify) — build them aware of each other so the boundary data loads once, not twice.
> **Endpoint verification needs network egress (2026-06-15, filing session):** the build-before-wiring step above is blocked from a default web session — outbound to the GIS hosts (`server.arcgisonline.com`, `services.arcgis.com`, `gis.h-gac.com`, TxGIO/TxDOT) returns `403 host_not_allowed` from the environment egress proxy. Recipe: in the environment editor set **Network access → Custom** (keep "Also include default list of common package managers" checked so npm/GitHub still work) and add, one per line: `*.arcgis.com` (TxDOT + city AGOL services), `*.arcgisonline.com`, `gis.h-gac.com` (H-GAC), `*.geographic.texas.gov` (TxGIO), plus `www.gis.hctx.net` + `gis.fbcad.org` (HCAD/FBCAD, for calibrating against known-jurisdiction parcels). **The proxy is fixed when a session starts**, so the change applies to a NEW session — not the one that saved it. Verify the hosts respond, then do the verify/calibrate pass before wiring.
> **Progress 2026-06-15 (branch `claude/festive-davinci-0oco2n`): egress unblocked → endpoints verified + calibrated → connector built, tested, wired.** The allowlist recipe above took effect in a FRESH session (the proxy picks up the policy at session start, not mid-session): all GIS hosts now reachable — `server.arcgisonline.com` / `services.arcgis.com` (AGOL) / `feature.geographic.texas.gov` (TxGIO) / `www.gis.hctx.net` all 200; H-GAC + FBCAD are *allowed* but upstream-503 right now (not a proxy block). **Verified + calibrated against known ground:** city limits = TxGIO `City_Boundaries/Texas_City_Boundaries/MapServer/0` field `city_name` (downtown Houston → "Houston"); county = TxDOT `Texas_County_Boundaries/FeatureServer/0` field `CNTY_NM` (same point → "Harris" / FIPS 48201). **ETJ has no statewide layer** — only per-city / regional publishers (H-GAC for the metro); kept as a registry row that honestly reads "source not wired" rather than faked. **Built `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/jurisdiction.js`:** ONE generic, registry-driven ArcGIS-REST connector on the B96 SWR cache — `JURISDICTION_SOURCES` rows (url/layer/field-map/query-kind), `normalizeFeature` (each source's schema → one internal shape), and `identifyJurisdiction(lng,lat,{ring})` which tests the WHOLE parcel via a polygon-intersect so a boundary **straddle** lists every city/county touched (point fallback when no ring); honest per-source status + visible data-age; screening-only. **Wired** into the planner's Identify panel as an explicit-request "⚖︎ Jurisdiction & road authority" button (never auto-loaded, per spec). **23 unit tests** (`test/jurisdiction.test.js`, injected fetch + cache); `lint` (0 errors) / `test` (68 pass) / `build` green; lazy chunks still split. **Remaining (kept `[ ]`):** wire a real ETJ source (H-GAC when its server recovers, or per-city COHGIS rows); **live browser confirmation** (CORS from the app origin + on-map render — same handoff as B96); and the **B13/B36 fold-in** (this county layer IS the boundary dataset those items were waiting on — close/merge in a follow-up so the data loads once).

Houston-only by design (the priority metro); other cities' ETJ are additive registry rows. `normalizeFeature` gained a `nameConst` fallback so a single-jurisdiction layer with no city-name column still resolves ("Houston"). ### B129 — [HAND-OFF] GIS overlays: NWI wetlands CORS + the cached-vector experiment — needs a real browser to finish `[Site Planner / GIS]` (bug/task)
`[x]` **The probe-resilience fix below LANDED via PR #60 (2026-06-16); this item now tracks the REMAINING browser-only work** (confirming FEMA renders, the NWI CORS question, and the reverted vector experiment). **Written for a future session that HAS a browser.** This session had none (CI container), and the GIS hosts are egress-blocked from it (`curl …?f=json` → HTTP 403 "Host not in allowlist: hazards.fema.gov / fwspublicservices.wim.usgs.gov"). So map *rendering* could only be judged from the owner's screenshots — which repeatedly misled me into saying "it works" when it didn't. **Do not trust a layer's green "loaded" status as proof of rendering: it is set the instant the layer is attached, BEFORE the image loads.** Only a human/browser confirms a visible overlay.

**Symptom (owner-reported on planyr.io + the PR #60 preview):** toggling **Wetlands (NWI)** throws a layer error. First `network / CORS error` (the health *probe*), then after a fix `Could not parse response as JSON … CORS` (esri-leaflet's internal *metadata* fetch). **FEMA flood zones** seemed to load (green status; faint hatching in one screenshot) but its *visible* rendering was never actually confirmed — the owner's pushback ("what makes you think it's working?") is the honest state.

**Root-cause analysis (UNVERIFIED in a browser — confirm before acting):**
- NWI host `fwspublicservices.wim.usgs.gov` appears to refuse cross-origin browser requests (CORS): both the `?f=json` health probe AND esri-leaflet's metadata/service-info fetch fail. Its `f=image` export *should* still paint via a CORS-exempt `<img>`, but esri's metadata `requesterror` fires regardless. FEMA host `hazards.fema.gov` appears CORS-clean.
- The (now-deleted) `kind:"vector"` overlay never rendered. Strong suspicion: an esri raster/image layer must be added **directly to the map**, not nested inside an `L.layerGroup`. Reverted rather than debugged blind.

**What PR #60 MERGED (the safe, shippable part of branch `claude/nice-dirac-029jok`). Net diff vs `main` = just `layers.js`:**
1. `probeService` returns `unreachable:true` on a CORS/network throw; `syncOverlayLayers` then adds the image layer anyway — a CORS-blocked *probe* no longer kills a layer.
2. A layer `requesterror` no longer drops the layer or fires the red toast — just a quiet per-layer "failed" status; `'load'` flips it back to "loaded".
FEMA/NWI are on the proven `dynamicMapLayer` (`f=image`) path. `lib/vectorLayers.js` (pure fetch/paging/style/decide engine, 31 tests, from #58) is on `main` but **UNWIRED groundwork**. (The branch's MapFinder/SitePlanner edits were dropped at merge — they pre-dated and would have undone main's B105/tab work; only the `layers.js` fix landed.) `lint` 0 / `test` 138 / `build` green.

**Questions a browser settles in minutes (DevTools → Network / Console):**
1. Does **FEMA** draw a *visible* flood overlay on the preview? (Confirm/deny — ignore the "loaded" status.)
2. Does the **NWI** `export?f=image` request fire, return 200, and produce an `<img>` *despite* the metadata `requesterror`? Or does esri block the export?
3. NWI response headers — is `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` present on `/MapServer`, `/export`, `/0/query`? Is the block total or endpoint-specific? Did it change recently (the DONE list says wetlands once worked)?

**Next steps (after browser triage):**
- **FEMA:** confirm it draws a *visible* overlay (the merged probe-resilience fix should keep it alive even if its probe is blocked).
- **NWI:** (a) swap to a CORS-clean wetlands endpoint (browser-test alternates — a USFWS ArcGIS Online hosted layer, a tiled service, etc.; edit `STATEWIDE.wetlands.url` in `lib/layers.js`); or (b) route via the `/server` proxy (the documented durable fix for flaky agency hosts — serves through our own origin, no CORS); or (c) leave it (screening-only).
- **Vector engine (`lib/vectorLayers.js`):** if revived, render via **direct map-add** and browser-test. Remember these overlays are used at area-scale, where the server-rendered image is the right tool; vectors only pay off zoomed in tight. The deleted `vectorOverlay.js` is recoverable from git (branch commits `49e2a1b` / `2f89c19`).

**Key files:** `lib/layers.js` (`STATEWIDE`, `syncOverlayLayers` dispatch, `probeService` `unreachable`, softened `requesterror`), `lib/vectorLayers.js` + `test/vectorLayers.test.js` (unwired engine), `VERIFICATION.md` V20 (the live-test item for the merged fix).

> **✅ DONE 2026-06-17 — verified in a REAL headless browser (Chromium/Playwright, live on planyr.io), branch `claude/gallant-wright-c3sjwd`.** Prior sessions had no browser and guessed; this one settled the open questions with evidence.
> - **FEMA flood zones — CONFIRMED RENDERING.** `/export?f=image` → **HTTP 200 `image/png`**, `<img>` paints (sampled **25.9%** non-transparent at zoom 15: teal `(0,224,224)` Zone AE, orange `(224,128,0)` floodway, red `(224,0,0)` boundaries — standard NFHL symbology tracing Buffalo/White Oak Bayou through downtown Houston). **CORS-clean:** `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://planyr.io` on the metadata GET, `/export`, AND the OPTIONS preflight. **Scale caveat (the source of prior "is it even working?" confusion):** NFHL sublayers 27/28 are gated AT THE SOURCE to `minScale ~1:36,112`, so they draw nothing at city-wide zoom (≤~z13) and only appear at ~zoom 14+. ### B417 — Trailer parking generated on non-dock sides `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-23 as "NEW-1", with screenshots; first minted B416 → renumbered **B417** after concurrent PR #313 took B416 for Split-a-parcel)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B417 also names another item in this file:** “Paste lands at the cursor in BOTH the Site Planner and Review canvases (feature) *(owne…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B417* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B417 against all of them.
`[x]` **Fixed + shipped 2026-06-23 via PR #314 (branch `claude/exciting-allen-i2eq2k`) — lint 0 · 1285 tests · build green · headless V120 (`ui-audit/verify-b416-b417.mjs`).** Branch/PR/commits + code/test tags + the harness filename retain the originally-minted B416/B417 (collision-renumber convention).
- **Repro (owner screenshots):** a 580′(w) × 664′(h) building. Because h > w the dock sides resolve to **left/right**, yet a 135′ truck-court stack (court → trailer → buffer) sat **stranded on the TOP** — a non-dock short side. Trailer parking must appear ONLY on dock faces (`dockSidesFor(b).dockSides`): single-load → one dock side, cross-dock → both, never a non-dock side.
- **Root cause (evidence-first — the filed hypothesis was off):** the named suspect (the legacy opposite-dock trailer row `OPP_TRAILER_D` / `oppTrailerGeom` / `fitWallTrailer`) was **already dead**, gated on an `oppSide` tag nothing creates. The REAL leak: a dock-zone stack is **pinned to the side it was created on** (`truckCourt.side`); when a building's long-side axis flips (a reshape) or its dock preset changes, `relayoutAllSides` re-laid the stack on the now-non-dock side and nothing pruned it. `trailerSides` from the old inline `dockSidesOf` was confirmed unread and dropped.
- **Fix:** new pure, unit-tested `lib/dockZones.js` helpers — `dockSidesFor` (one shared rule for canvas/panel/depth/guard), `strandedZoneIds`, `pruneStrandedZones` — prune a stranded stack **on reshape commit** (pointer-up, so one undo restores size + apron), **on dock-preset change** (`changeBuildingDock`), and **on plan open** (`useState` init → existing stranded plans self-heal). Removed the dead opp-trailer path. +10 dockZones unit tests incl. the requested "zero trailer elements on a non-dock side" for BOTH presets; headless V120 (stranded-on-top → pruned; identical stack on a real dock side → kept, so the prune is targeted).
- **Deduped:** net-new; REUSES the B228/B229/B239/B242/B246 dock-zone machinery (consistent, not a fork); shares `dockSidesFor` with B418 but an independent root cause + test path.

### B149 — Hide fine-detail annotations when zoomed out (level-of-detail tiering) `[Site Planner / UI]` (feature) — ✅ DONE  *(arrived as "NEW-3"; minted B149 — next free ID after B148. - **Original ask / recommended mechanism:** tag each annotation with a **tier** — *overview* (building names/SF, site totals) / *site* (building-footprint dims, parking-module dims) / *detail* (sidewalk, drive-aisle/road widths, sub-aisle dims) — and gate visibility by current map scale, made **self-tuning** by a **minimum on-screen length**: a width callout only draws when the feature it measures projects to at least ~40 px on screen (resolution-independent; no hand-tuned zoom-step breakpoints).
- **2026-06-23 owner amendment (folded in):** at site-overview zoom the **"5′ Sidewalk"** centred label and the fine width/edge dimension callouts (e.g. the "30′/40′" drive/aisle ticks bracketing the sidewalk run) **still painted** — illegible clutter. Locked decision: **drop the label + width dimension only; KEEP the thin strip geometry** (a 5′ strip is ~1 px at that scale; pop-in/out of the geometry on zoom would flicker — geometry-hiding is a separate scope, not silently added). Edge case respected: this must NOT also suppress the building name/SF or the B148 site-summary chip (overview tier — always visible).
> **★ SHIPPED + VERIFIED 2026-06-23 (branch `claude/nice-cannon-0zbom0`).** Implemented the tier gating on **B121's engine** (`lib/labelLayout.js`), reusing the existing `dimCalloutVisible(ppf)` / `DIM_CALLOUT_MIN_PPF` gate rather than a parallel one:
> - New pure helper **`detailLabelVisible(featureFt, ppf)`** + **`DETAIL_LABEL_MIN_PX`** = `dimCalloutVisible(ppf) && featureFt*ppf >= DETAIL_LABEL_MIN_PX` — the shared dimension-callout zoom gate is the FLOOR, refined by B149's min-on-screen-length rule keyed on the feature the callout measures.
> - **Detail tier:** the sidewalk/landscape/buffer **width labels** (the `el.type === "sidewalk" || "landscape"` branch in `SitePlanner.jsx` — skipped from the label-candidate pool when hidden, so the geometry stays) **and** the **paving/road** red edge-dimension **widths** (`renderElPx`). **Site tier:** a building's footprint depth stays on `dimCalloutVisible` (unchanged). **Overview tier:** building name/SF + the site-summary chip — never zoom-gated. A SELECTED paving/road keeps its dimension so the click-to-edit / drag handle never vanishes mid-edit (buildings keep their exact prior behaviour).
> - **Calibrated in-browser (B149 says tune it live):** the planner hard-caps zoom at **ppf 8**. At 40 px the narrowest real strip (5′ sidewalk) would only reveal at exactly 8.0 ppf (the max, zero headroom, float-boundary flicker), so `DETAIL_LABEL_MIN_PX` was tuned to **30 px** → the 5′ strip reveals at ppf 6 with headroom, while staying hidden at site-overview (~0.2–0.5 ppf) and working zoom (0.35). ### B562 — Grid keyboard column nav steps onto hidden columns; cell selection outline disappears `[Schedule]` (bug) — ✅ DONE
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B562 also names another item in this file:** “`importLegacyIntoCloud` timestamp compare wasn't type-safe (third sibling of B559) (bug…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B562* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B562 against all of them.
*(owner-reported 2026-06-29; fixed + verified same session)*

**Symptom:** In the Schedule **Grid** view, on a project whose Columns chooser hides columns that sit
*between* two visible ones (the reporter's layout hides Health/Status/Owner, which live immediately
left of Cost in the master registry), clicking a Cost cell then pressing **ArrowLeft** made the blue
cell-selection outline **vanish** for ~3 presses before it reappeared on Successor. Same defect on
ArrowRight off Successor, on Tab / Shift+Tab, on Shift+Arrow range extension, and on Tab / Shift+Tab
while editing a cell.

**Root cause (`public/sequence/index.html`):** the cell cursor `selectedColIdx` is an index into the
**master** column registry `COLS` (16 cols), but the grid renders only the project's **visible** columns
in display order and draws the outline where `COLS.indexOf(c) === selectedColIdx`. Navigation stepped
`selectedColIdx` by ±1 through the master registry (clamped only at 0 and the highest visible index),
so it landed on hidden columns — which have no rendered cell, so no outline. The lower clamp
`Math.max(0, i-1)` also targeted master index 0 (`id`), itself often hidden.

**Fix:** every column move now walks the **visible columns in display order**, not raw `COLS` ±1.
- New pure, unit-tested module `src/workspaces/scheduler/lib/gridColNav.js`
  (`visibleColMasterIdxs` / `snapToVisible` / `stepVisibleColByIdx` / `stepVisibleCol`); the algorithm
  is mirrored inline in `public/sequence/index.html` (`stepVisibleColIdx` + `visibleColIdxs` /
  `stepGridCol`) because that standalone Babel page can't import from `src/`.
- Routed through it: plain Arrow Left/Right, Tab/Shift+Tab, the Shift+Arrow range `c2`, and the three
  in-cell editing Tab handlers (via a `tabStep` helper + a `colMasterIdxs` prop on `Cell`, replacing the
  old end-only `maxColIdx`/`colCap` clamp). `lastGridColIdx` removed (superseded).
- Cursor stays a master index (smallest blast radius — `COLS[selectedColIdx]` reads and the
  `selectedColIdx === ci` render check keep working unchanged).
- **Secondary (same root):** a GridView effect snaps `selectedColIdx` to the nearest visible column if
  its column gets hidden via the Columns chooser (or the initial `id` column is hidden), so the outline
  never silently vanishes on a layout change.
- Also fixed the horizontal scroll-into-view calc, which summed *hidden* columns' widths (`COLS.slice`)
  and could scroll to the wrong place — now measured from the rendered display order (`colOrder`).

**Reference already correct:** the Dashboard table (`MasterView.handleTableKey`) indexes into
`activeCols` directly (visible-column space) — the grid now matches that model.

**Verified:** `test/gridColNav.test.js` (20 unit tests); full suite **1813** green; lint 0 errors;
build green; headless `ui-audit/verify-grid-hidden-col-nav.mjs` **12/12** (seeds the hidden
Health/Status/Owner layout, asserts ArrowLeft from Cost keeps the outline and lands on Successor, plus
clamps, plain Tab, and in-cell Shift+Tab). → V173.

### B610 — Silent-failure gap: a filed drawing whose Drive key↔id mapping write failed read as "saved ✓" then went missing on next open `[Server / storage]` (bug)  *(surfaced 2026-07-02 when Michael reopened the old storage-adapter/Drive handoff — the NEW-1…NEW-4 vision — and asked "have we drifted"; the review found this live bug; minted **B610** = highest real B# across both files (B609) + 1; branch `claude/storage-adapter-drive-discussion-6m5236`. Extends the **B209** no-silent-failure guarantee to the durability-mapping layer — folds INTO B209, not a parallel mechanism.)*
`[x]` **Fixed + verified this session. *Moves to BACKLOG-DONE on merge.***
- **Root cause:** after Drive bytes uploaded OK, the durable Planyr-key↔Drive-id write (`public.drive_files`) was **best-effort** — `adapter.save` fired `idMap.bind(...)` and discarded the result (`server/storage/adapter.js`); `idStoreSupabase.set` only `console.warn`ed on a failed write and returned `undefined`; the resumable-upload COMMIT (`functions/api/files/resumable.js`) ignored the outcome too. So a failed mapping write still reported `ok:true` → the upload showed "saved ✓", but nothing could resolve the file → `downloadFromDrive` missed it and the drawing was silently gone next open. Exactly the class B209/NEW-4 exists to prevent.
- **Fix (honest failure + best-effort rollback, no orphan):** `idStoreSupabase.set` now returns `{ok}`; `idMap.bind` normalizes any store result to `{ok}` (a legacy `undefined`-returning set = success → back-compat, so only an explicit `{ok:false}` rolls back). `adapter.save` checks the bind result and, on `{ok:false}`, rolls the just-uploaded bytes back (`backend.remove`) and returns a visible `fail(...)` — the client then falls back to Supabase (small files) or flags re-drop (large), truthful and orphan-free. The resumable COMMIT does the analogous Drive-file rollback (`client.del(fileId)`) and returns 502.
- **Also (lower severity):** `reviewStore.deleteReview` swallowed Storage/Drive cleanup failures yet still reported `ok` → orphaned bytes, silently. It now returns `{orphaned, cleanupFailed}` and the Library shows a dismissible "a copy may linger — remove it in Google Drive" notice (data isn't lost; the row delete stays authoritative → a notice, not a red banner).
- **Tests:** `test/storageAdapter.test.js` (rollback on mapping-failure + back-compat), `test/idStoreSupabase.test.js` (`set` returns `{ok:false}`/`{ok:true}`), `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` anti-drift guard. lint 0 · full suite **2163 green** · build green.
- **Verified:** everything runnable here is green. The signed-in Drive round-trip (force a `drive_files` write failure → honest failure + no orphaned Drive file) is auth-gated + Drive-backed, so it's logged as **V191**.

### B600 — Road curve geometry: per-vertex sharp/arc/smooth + feasibility-clamped radius `[Site Planner / drawing]` (feature)  *(owner-dropped 2026-06-30 as "NEW-2"; minted **B600** = B599 + 1; depends on B599 — renumbered from a provisional **B597** a concurrent `main` took for the site-rename-revert item; in-code labels keep the provisional **B597**)*
`[x]` **Shipped this session. *Moves to BACKLOG-DONE on merge.*** New **pure, dependency-free** `lib/roadGeometry.js` + `test/roadGeometry.test.js`, matching the repo's pure-lib pattern (`metesAndBounds.js`, `polygonSplit.js`) — **no JSTS** (B150 avoided it deliberately).
- `roadCenterline(pts, vtx, { defaultRadius })` → a **tessellated dense polyline** (the rendered centerline) that B601 offsets. Per interior vertex `treatment`:
  - **Sharp** — radius 0, hard corner (vertex unchanged). `sharp == input polyline`.
  - **Arc** — circular **fillet tangent to both segments**, radius **feasibility-clamped** so the run-up `T = R·tan(θ/2)` never exceeds half the shorter adjacent segment (θ = deflection angle), emitted as short tessellated segments. **Default treatment.**
  - **Smooth** — vertex is a **through-point of a Catmull-Rom-style interpolating curve** (tangent from neighbours), tessellated — for tracing curves off an aerial.
- Treatment is **per-vertex and convertible after drawing** (pen-tool style): click a road vertex on the canvas to select it, then flip **sharp ↔ arc ↔ smooth** in the Element panel (Arc seeds the class default radius, editable). No global tool mode, no spacing threshold — dense clicks + the clamp produce smoothness naturally. `minRadiusOfCurvature` (circumradius of consecutive triples) backs the B602 civil check, uniformly for arc and traced/smooth runs.
- **Tests (21):** clamp never overruns a segment; arc tangent at both ends; spline passes through its points; sharp == polyline; tessellation density scales with `tessDeg`; min-radius recovers a known circle + finds the tightest along a mixed alignment; + the B602 class-threshold math.

### B597 — Renaming a site snapped right back to the old name after Enter `[Site Planner]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-30 on planyr.io — "I renamed a site in the site planner module and pressed enter and it went right back to the old name"; minted **B597** = highest real B# across both files (B596) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B596 that a concurrent `main` took for the parcel-merge-conflict item; the commit/PR keep the provisional **B596** label; branch `claude/site-planner-rename-revert-dk6yoq`)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B597 also names another item in this file:** “Formula engine: errors now PROPAGATE through aggregation (Excel parity), instead of sil…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B597* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B597 against all of them.
`[x]` **Fixed + headless-verified this session. *Moves to BACKLOG-DONE on merge.***
- **Root cause — TWO independent revert bugs, both surfacing as "the name comes back":**
  1. **(primary) The header breadcrumb dropdown (planner view).** The project switcher owns a local list (`internalProjects`) yet the Site Planner ALSO supplies `onRenameProject`. `ProjectBreadcrumb.commitRename` only re-read that local list in its bare `else` branch, so when `onRenameProject` was present it wrote the new name to the store but never refreshed the list — and a same-tab store write doesn't fire the native `storage` event — so the just-edited row (and the crumb) kept the OLD name. An instant revert on essentially EVERY site rename.
  2. **The map's YOUR SITES list, multi-plan sites.** The list passes a *representative plan* id; `renameSiteGroup`/`renameSite` treated it as a group id. For a site whose newest plan isn't the group anchor, `loadPlansOfGroup(planId)` matched nothing → no save → revert (and, signed in, nothing pushed to the cloud).
- **Fix:**
  - `ProjectBreadcrumb.commitRename` now refreshes the local list + nudges the other `planarfit:sites` surfaces for BOTH branches whenever it is uncontrolled (Schedule's controlled mode still relies on its bridge prop).
  - `renameSiteGroup` (storage) and `renameSite` (SitePlannerApp) resolve the incoming id to its group (`groupOf(loadSite(id))`) before renaming + cloud-pushing, so a group id OR any plan id within it renames the whole site.
- **Tests:** +4 `test/storage.test.js` cases (rename by group id · by a NON-anchor plan id · single-plan · unknown-id no-op).

### B594 — Freshly drawn polyline (or any markup) vanishes mid-session: a per-tab id counter let a new item reuse a tombstoned id, which `mergeSiteContent` then stripped `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug) — DATA-LOSS, critical  *(owner-reported 2026-06-30 on planyr.io — "I drew a polyline and it disappeared… could it be a save/overwrite issue?"; arrived as "NEW-1"; minted **B594** = highest real B# across both files (B593) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B591 that a concurrent `main` took for the Scheduler-r3 item (and B592, which it took for the dim-slide item); the in-code comments, commit/PR titles, and the `verify-b591-polyline-id.mjs` harness filename keep the provisional **B591**; SAME symptom family as B134 but a DISTINCT, newly-found root cause — see the fold note; branch `claude/polyline-save-overwrite-u3l49r`)*
> ⚠ **SHARED ID — B594 also names another item in this file:** “Bump-out: resizing it slides it off the corner (gap to the dock doors), + it ignores th…”. Nothing was renumbered (B308704): a renumber would silently repoint every existing *see B594* at one twin. Read a cross-reference to B594 against all of them.
`[x]` **Fixed + unit-verified this session — the id-collision root cause. *Moves to BACKLOG-DONE on merge.***
- **Investigation (audit-FIRST, as the brief demanded): a 6-dimension parallel auditor sweep + a two-skeptic adversarial verify pass (refute-the-claim + check-the-fix) over the whole persistence layer.** 18 candidates raised, 15 refuted; **3 survivors all converged on ONE root cause** (a CONFIRMED verdict that I could not refute), correcting the owner-session's initial guess (a missing immediate local mirror — already shipped as B458).
- **Root cause (NOT B134's #3 debounce-flush or #4 silent-error — a sixth, previously-unidentified cause):** drawn-element ids came from a single per-tab module counter `uid() = "e"+_id++` (`SitePlanner.jsx`), and `ensureIdAbove` re-seeded that counter at load from **only `parcels`+`els`** — never `markups`/`measures`/`callouts`/`deletedIds`. So the load-bearing invariant the tombstone system rests on (literally commented "ids are never reused, so tombstoning by id is safe") was **FALSE**: (a) after reopening a plan the counter could sit BELOW a markup id already deleted (its id sitting in `deletedIds`), so a freshly drawn polyline was minted with a **tombstoned** id; (b) two tabs of the same plan re-seeded identically and minted **colliding** ids. When `mergeSiteContent` then ran (cross-tab `storage` sync, take-over reconcile, or boot pull), its tombstone filter (`live()`, `siteModel.js`) **stripped the just-drawn polyline** → it vanished mid-session with no reload, and the thinned model was persisted to device + cloud (a later reload lost it again). The immediate B458 mirror is a sole-tab plain replace that KEEPS the polyline, so the B473 read-back's count check passed — which is exactly why nothing alarmed at draw time (→ B595).
- **Fix (the verifiers explicitly REJECTED the tempting fixes — weakening `mergeSiteContent`'s tombstone filter / a `localOnlyIds` carve-out — as regressing B276/B556/B480; the endorsed fix is unique ids):**
  - **New pure `src/shared/ids.js` (`createIdMinter(salt)` + `randomIdSalt()`).** `uid()` now carries a per-tab **salt** (6 random lowercase letters) appended to every id, so two tabs/sessions can never mint the same id and a fresh add can never equal a retained tombstone. Salt is **letters only**, so `seedAbove`'s `parseInt(replace(/\D/g,""))` still recovers the sequence number for ordering. Legacy short ids ("e5") keep working; no data migration.
  - **`ensureIdAbove` now seeds from EVERY id-bearing collection + tombstones** (markups/measures/callouts/deletedIds, not just parcels+els) at both call sites (restore + import) — defense-in-depth + monotonic ordering.
  - **Comment at the tombstone helper updated** to record WHY reuse is now impossible (the salt), so the invariant can't be silently re-broken.
- **Tests (assertions land with the code, B432):** new `test/idMinter.test.js` (7) — sequential salted mint, two-salt non-collision (the two-tab case), `seedAbove` digit-parse across mixed collections + tombstones, a reopen-low-counter case, `randomIdSalt` digit-free, AND an **end-to-end pair through the real `mergeSiteContent`**: a salted new markup whose numeric part matches an old tombstone is KEPT, while a CONTROL with the colliding bare id is stripped (proving the exact mechanism).
- **Verified:** `npm run lint` **0 errors** · full suite **2072 green** (+7) · `npm run build` green (lazy split intact; `src/shared/ids.js` folds into the planner chunk). The signed-in, two-tab live reproduction on planyr.io (sandbox is logged-out, cross-tab needs auth) = **V185**.
- **Dedup / fold vs B134:** same "work disappears" symptom FAMILY, but B134's open candidates were #3 (debounce-flush) and #4 (silent save error) — this is a **distinct sixth root cause** (id reuse → tombstone strip). Kept as its own item with its own test path; B134 amended to cross-reference. Ships with **B595** (the detection half).

### B595 — The "changes aren't being saved" notice fired AFTER the loss; the on-device read-back verify was count-only, blind to a same-count drop `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug)  *(owner-reported 2026-06-30 — "the notification popped up too late"; arrived as "NEW-2"; minted **B595** = B594 + 1 — renumbered from a provisional B592 (a concurrent `main` took B592 for the dim-slide item); in-code comments + commit/PR keep the provisional **B592**; same branch; ships with B594; the open half of B134's #4 + B125's loud-failure scope)*
`[x]` **Fixed this session — membership-anchored read-back + a cross-tab merge tripwire. *Moves to BACKLOG-DONE on merge.***
- Part of: **B648** (Persistence & Sync epic).
- **Why the notice lagged (found in the same audit):** the immediate B458 mirror verifies the on-device write by **count** (`drawnCount got < want`). A same-count swap — one item dropped while another lands, exactly the B594 tombstone/id-collision fold — leaves `got==want`, so the count check is **blind** to it; the loss only surfaced later when the thinned cloud push tripped a CAS conflict / the user noticed. So the indicator was a lagging symptom, not an edge-of-loss alarm.
- **Fix:**
  - **Read-back now verifies by MEMBERSHIP, not just count:** `writeMirror` collects the ids it just wrote and confirms each one read back; a missing id flips the loud `localSaveFailed` banner **within the ~50ms mirror** (edit-anchored, not push-anchored) + records `save-verify-failed{ missingId }`. No cry-wolf — it only fires when an id we literally just wrote is absent.
  - **Cross-tab merge tripwire:** the `storage` handler now asserts the union never drops a live id without a tombstone explaining it; if it ever does (a future regression of the B594 class), it goes LOUD to telemetry (`merge-dropped-live`) instead of silently shrinking the canvas. Reuses the B468 telemetry pattern.
  - **Cross-tab convergence signature is now id-membership, not collection counts** (`SitePlanner.jsx` `onStore`): a same-count remote swap (other tab deleted one item + added another) used to be skipped by the count-only `sig()`, leaving two tabs permanently divergent — now they converge (and a pure remote delete re-hydrates).
- **Verified:** covered by the B594 gate (lint 0 · 2072 tests green · build green). The live signed-in confirmation that a genuinely non-landing save now flips the badge promptly is folded into **V185**.
- **Dedup:** folds into **B125** (loud-failure scope) + **B134 #4** (silent save error) rather than minting a parallel mechanism; the net-new ask — detection must cover the **silent same-count no-op**, not only writes that throw — is what this adds.

### B491 — Security pen-test pass (2026-06-27): cross-user PDF read in team storage + OAuth token-page hardening `[Security / RLS + edge]` (security)  *(owner-requested "exhaustive penetration tests"; 5 parallel surface audits — edge Functions, edge proxies, OAuth, Supabase RLS, client XSS/secrets; minted **B491** = highest real B# (B490) + 1 — renumbered from a provisional **B488** a concurrent `main` (#377) took for the PDF-viewer-quality audit; the original commit message still reads B488)*
`[x]` **Filed + the two real fixes shipped + lower-priority items triaged the SAME session (branch `claude/resume-planner-persistence-36zqh1`, PR into `main`).** Owner SQL/dashboard steps in `OWNER-TODO.md`.
- **Overall verdict (honest, not padding): the app is well-built.** Edge Functions verify a real Supabase JWT and derive the tenant uid from the *token* (no IDOR); the GIS/Mapillary proxies have a robust WHATWG-host allowlist (no SSRF, token only ever goes to the fixed Mapillary host); client XSS is neutralised by React auto-escaping + consistent `esc()`/`escapeHtml()` in the three string-templated SVG/HTML builders; no server-only secret reaches the bundle (the `sk-ant-`/`ANTHROPIC`/`refresh_token` hits in `dist/` are placeholders / SDK var-names / grant-field names); and the team **management/invite** RLS correctly blocks self-escalation (admin-gated invites, SECURITY DEFINER funcs pin `search_path`, recursion avoided). Most surfaces returned SAFE.
- **`[x]` SHIPPED — Finding A (the one serious bug): cross-user PDF read via `can_read_shared_review_file` (`doc-review/db/team_storage.sql`).** The team-shared-file Storage SELECT policy granted read on any object whose path appeared in *some* team-shared review's `data->sources[].storageKey` — but `data` is attacker-writable on one's OWN rows, so a user could create a review they own, share it to a team they're on, and list a **victim's** path (`<victim_uid>/…`) to read the victim's private PDF (confused-deputy IDOR on the private `doc-review-files` bucket). **Fix:** require `(storage.foldername(p_name))[1] = r.user_id::text` so a readable object must belong to the review's true owner; a fabricated source can then only ever resolve to the attacker's own files, while legit shares still resolve. **Live impact today is gated** (needs the victim's exact path — uid + project + discipline + a 7-char random `srcId` — realistically known only to a *former* teammate; and no teams are live yet) → **run `team_storage.sql` before inviting anyone** (OWNER-TODO, with B486). HIGH severity if exploited; not actively exploitable by an outsider today.
- **`[x]` SHIPPED — Finding B (hardening): OAuth consent callback (`functions/api/auth/google/callback.js`)** now HTML-escapes every interpolated value (the refresh token + Google's error strings) and sends `Cache-Control: no-store` + `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on the one page that can render a secret. Pure-win, zero functional change. (These routes are a dormant one-time owner bootstrap — the token is already minted and must NOT be re-minted — so this is latent-risk reduction.)
- **Deliberately NOT auto-fixed (real but lower-priority / would risk regressions or are owner/infra actions — left here, not shipped, to avoid bloat):**
  - **Email-confirmation trust (config).** Invite-claim trusts the JWT email as verified; if Supabase "Confirm email" were OFF, a user could claim a co-worker's invite. Primary fix = the dashboard setting (OWNER-TODO); a SQL `email_confirmed_at` gate on the signup trigger was NOT added (the trigger fires *before* confirmation, so gating it would break invite-at-signup — needs careful design, deferred).
  - **OAuth CSRF `state` + caller authz** on the dormant consent routes (`start.js`/`callback.js` are unauthenticated). Standard hardening, but the routes shouldn't be exercised at all in steady state (don't re-mint the token), and a JWT gate on a top-level browser redirect is architecturally awkward (no Authorization header on a navigation). Deferred as latent-only.
  - **Optimistic-concurrency `version` reset.** A teammate can write an arbitrary `version` on a shared row, defeating the compare-and-swap anti-clobber guard (integrity, within-team only). A monotonic-`version` BEFORE-UPDATE trigger would fix it but risks breaking *all* saves if the client increment ever diverges — deferred pending a safe rollout.
  - **`client_errors` telemetry:** anon INSERT has no rate-limit/size-cap (spam/cost; READ side is correctly closed — no cross-user read). Length caps could silently drop large stacks → left to platform rate-limiting.
  - **Public proxy rate-limit** (`/api/mapillary/*`, `/api/gis-cache/*`): no code-level rate limit (quota-abuse ceiling only; targets are public agency hosts). Best as a Cloudflare WAF rule (infra, not code).
  - **`underlay.src` import scheme** not validated (a crafted import/shared plan could load a remote tracker image — content-spoof/privacy, NOT XSS; React keeps it inert). Optional `^data:image/|^https?:` allowlist if teams share plans widely.
  - **Scheduler separate Supabase project RLS** (`public/sequence/index.html`, ref `ksetjztkplttbcehyicv`): its hardcoded key is confirmed **anon** (not service_role), but that project's table RLS can't be verified from the repo → owner confirm `planar_*` tables have RLS enabled (ties to the B408 consolidation decision).
- **Dedup:** net-new security item; the shipped Finding A is distinct from B486 (re-home guard) — both are team-sharing RLS gaps to run before going live, different policies.

### B490 — PDF viewer: optional-content (OCG) layer toggle `[Doc Review / Markup]` (feature) — ✅ DONE 2026-07-03 (batch `claude/backlog-review-batch-vfz167`)
A "▤ Layers" control in the Review toolbar shows/hides a PDF's optional-content groups (e.g. turn off Electrical to see just the site plan). New pure `lib/ocg.js` (`ocgLayerList` + `deriveLayerVisibility`) iterates pdf.js's OptionalContentConfig — v6 has **no `getGroups()`**, so it uses the `[id, group]` iterator; `renderInto` threads the retained config via `optionalContentConfigPromise`; `DocReview` extracts the config on load (`readOcg`, guarded on `pdfRef` against a superseded load), lists the groups in a **portaled `AnchoredMenu`** popover (escapes the toolbar row's `overflow:hidden` clip — a hand-rolled popover was clipped), and re-rasters both layers on toggle. Visibility is **in-memory** (a view filter, never the immutable markups). **Required a pdf.js polyfill:** the modern ESM build calls `Map.prototype.getOrInsertComputed` (a TC39 proposal) but — unlike the legacy build — doesn't bundle it, so `getOptionalContentConfig()` threw; added a guarded polyfill in `lib/pdf.js`.
Verified: new `test/ocg.test.js` + full suite **2225** green · lint 0 · build green + DocReview lazy chunk intact · headless `ui-audit/verify-ocg.mjs` (**8 checks**, hand-authored 2-layer OCG fixture `e2e/fixtures/sample-ocg.pdf` via `ui-audit/make-sample-ocg-pdf.mjs`): the Layers button appears, the popover lists Electrical+Plumbing and is genuinely **visible (not clipped)**, unchecking Electrical re-rasters red→0 while blue persists, re-checking restores it, no page errors. Screenshot eyeballed.

### B155 — Markup selection hit-testing: grab unfilled shapes by their interior, consistently at any zoom `[Document Review + Site Planner / UI]` (bug)  *(arrived as "NEW-1"; minted B155 — `main` concurrently took B147–B154 (easement tool, multipart parcel, Delete-key fix), so this is the real next free ID; provisionally B150 then B154 in earlier drafts — both numbers were taken by `main` while this was in flight)*
`[ ]` **Repro (owner-reported 2026-06-18):** drawing markups are too finicky to select — an **unfilled rectangle only selects when you click its border stroke** (the thin line), not its interior, so you have to "grab exactly on the line." At low zoom even the stroke is hard to land. **Expected:** forgiving, predictable selection for **every** markup type — clicking anywhere inside a closed shape grabs it, and the "grab feel" is the same whether zoomed way in or out.
- **Rendering approach (inspected — fix differs by surface, all THREE confirmed SVG):**
  - **Document Review (`DocReview.jsx`)** — *already correct, the reference implementation.* A centralized `hitTest(p)` (added under **B33**) already does interior-selection for `rect`/`cloud` (point-in-expanded-bbox), bbox for `text`, and nearest-vertex-OR-segment for measures, with a **screen-space tolerance** (`tol = 10/scale`). **Generalize THIS pattern; don't reinvent it.**
  - **Site Planner main canvas (`SitePlanner.jsx`, markup render ~L4698)** — neutral shapes (`rect`/`ellipse`/`polygon`) rendered `fill:"none"` with selection wired to each element's own `onPointerDown` → interior was dead, **stroke-only**. (Filled `els` and the special `utilRoute`/`encumbrance`/`traced` markups already select fine because they paint a real fill.)
  - **Parcel-drawing markup (`components/ParcelDrawing.jsx`, B67)** — the **Box** tool, identical defect: rect `fill:"none"` + element-level `onPointerDown` = stroke-only. (Text markups are positioned `<div>`s, so their box already selects.)
- **✅ Increment 1 — interior-grab for CLOSED shapes — DONE 2026-06-18 (branch `claude/busy-knuth-3q9cyn`):** the minimal, owner-requested rectangle fix. `pointerEvents:"all"` on closed markup shapes (`rect`/`ellipse`/`polygon` in `SitePlanner.jsx`; the `rect`/Box in `ParcelDrawing.jsx`) makes the **fill area a hit target even when unfilled**, so a click anywhere inside selects (and drags — both surfaces' move handlers already `stopPropagation`, so an interior grab won't also pan). This is the **same `pointerEvents="all"` technique B142 already shipped for text/callout boxes**, now extended to the neutral shape markups that B142 missed; Doc Review had the equivalent via B33. Open paths untouched (see below). **Self-verified headless on the Site Planner (V41): drew an unfilled markup rect → Escape deselects (handles vanish) → clicking its INTERIOR centre re-selects it (resize/rotate handles reappear) → PASS.** ParcelDrawing's identical one-attribute change was not separately driven (needs a drawing attached + rasterized), logged under V41 as low-risk-by-analogy.
- **🔲 Remaining (the "all the other elements" tranche — the actual handoff):**
  1. **Shared `hitTest`, one source of truth.** Lift Doc Review's hit-test into shared code (`src/shared/` — alongside the coordinate stub) as `hitTest(point, element, { tolerancePx, zoom }) → boolean|distance`, and route **all three** surfaces' selection through it, replacing the per-type/per-element click logic. The ported Site-Planner measurement tools (B116) and Doc Review share the same coordinate spine and should select identically — don't fork per workspace.
  2. **Tolerance is screen-space, converted at test time.** Default **6px**, `tolerance_world = tolerancePx / zoom` (Doc Review already does `10/scale`; standardize). This is what makes the grab feel zoom-independent.
  3. **Per-element rules:** *closed* (rect/ellipse/polygon/cloud) → point-in-shape **+** stroke buffer (cloud hit-tests its underlying polygon, not the scalloped path); *line/arrow* → point-to-segment ≤ tol, arrowhead included; *polyline/freehand/pen* → nearest-segment ≤ tol (factor in stroke width); *text* → full bounding box (single-click select, double-click edit), even with no border/fill; *callout* → text-box bounds OR leader line; *point/count* → generous ~8px screen radius (no area to aim at); *measurements* (linear/polyline/area) → matching shape rule **and** the value label is part of the hit region. **Measurements are takeoff-critical — treat hard-to-select or wrong-element selection as HIGH severity (same as a wrong number).**
  4. **✅ Open-path forgiving hit area — DONE 2026-06-29 (Site Planner; owner re-reported the Line being far harder to grab than a Polyline).** `line`/`polyline` were still stroke-only after Increment 1 (the `<line>`/`<polyline>` rendered `fill:"none"` so only the 2px painted stroke caught clicks). Both now carry a transparent **fat hit-stroke** (`MK_HIT_PX = 12`px → ~6px each side, zoom-independent since `f2p` projects feet→screen px) on a wrapping `<g>` that owns the select/drag handler; the visible stroke is `pointerEvents:"none"`. Reuses the B146/B420 technique. Headless-verified (`ui-audit/verify-markup-fixes.mjs`: a click ~5px off the line selects, ~40px off does not). Doc Review's open paths were already covered by the shared `hitTest.js` (`PICK_TOL_PX = 6`). The `pen` kind only exists in the shared engine (Doc Review), already handled. **Still open below:** the shared-`hitTest` unification for the Site Planner surface (increments 1–3, 5–7).
  5. **Z-order resolution:** hit-test top-of-stack downward, select the first hit; tie-break **smaller-area wins** (a small shape on/inside a large unfilled one stays grabbable). Empty-canvas click deselects.
  6. **Move-by-interior-drag vs. pan** stays explicit: select-mode interior drag = move element; pan-mode drag = pan. (Already true post-Increment 1; keep it true in the shared path.)
  7. **Resize/move handles win** over anything behind them, with a few px of screen-space slop.
- **Acceptance:** click inside an unfilled rect → selects; within ~6px of any stroke at any zoom → selects; zoom 10× in then out → identical grab feel; two overlapping shapes → topmost, and a small shape inside a big unfilled one → the small one; line/polyline/pen segment within tol → selects; anywhere in a text box → selects, double-click → edits; interior drag moves and never pans; empty click deselects.
> **Dedup / reconciliation — build on what's shipped, don't fork:**
> - **B142 + B143 (DONE) — the direct precedent.** B142 already set `pointerEvents="all"` on the **text/callout box** so its whole interior selects even with no fill (explicitly "to match Doc Review's shape-aware hit test"); B143 finished the Bluebeam-style text editing (Enter = newline, click-away/Esc to finish, via a `pointerEvents:"all"` click-out catcher). So **text-box selection + editing is already done on the Site Planner side — do NOT redo it here.** Increment 1 is the same fix applied to the shape markups B142 didn't cover. B141 likewise added measurement vertex-editing "consistent with Doc Review's shape-aware select."
> - **B33 (DONE)** is the reference hit-test — Increment 1 brought the other two surfaces up to its rectangle behaviour; the shared-`hitTest` tranche generalizes B33 rather than replacing it.
> - **B146 (DONE)** already introduced (a) the **transparent fat hit-stroke** for grabbing a thin line and (b) the shared inline **`numEdit`** on-canvas editor that replaced `window.prompt`. Reuse (a) for open-path markups here.
> - **Owner "no dialog boxes" rule (KEY DECISIONS, 2026-06-17):** Doc Review's **Text** tool is inline (B293) and **Calibrate** (Doc Review + Stitcher) is now inline with validation (**B304**) — no more `window.prompt` in those flows. **Only remaining:** **ParcelDrawing's calibrate** (`window.prompt`) → convert to the inline `numEdit` pattern; fold in here, don't file separately.
> - **Distinct from B149/B121 (LOD + label collision):** those govern what's *drawn* at a given zoom; this governs what's *selectable* when clicked. Keep separate.

### B156 — Hover highlight on the markup under the cursor (pre-click affordance) `[Document Review + Site Planner / UI]` (feature)  *(arrived as "NEW-2"; minted B156 — next free ID after B155)*
`[ ]` In **Select** mode, highlight the markup currently under the cursor — the element that *would* be selected on click — before the click lands, so you can see what you're about to grab. Subtle outline/glow; never disturbs the immutable PDF/drawing backdrop layer. **Depends on B155's shared `hitTest`** and must use the **same topmost/smaller-area resolution**, so the hover preview always matches what a click selects. Out of scope for B155 (a separate, lower-priority affordance) — minted net-new so B155 can ship without it.
> **✅ SHIPPED 2026-07-03 (B155 + B156 together, branch `claude/backlog-review-batch-vfz167`) — one shared selection picker + a pre-click hover preview.**
> - **B155 — the JS-picker surface now shares ONE picker (`src/shared/markup/hitTest.js` `pickMarkup`).** The shared picker was upgraded to the Document Review REFERENCE feel (it was previously *weaker* than DocReview's inline picker): a new `scoreMarkup(m, p, tol, markerTol, scale)` returns `{ d, interior }` mirroring DocReview's inline `hitTest` exactly — rect/cloud/snapshot tol-expanded box interior, ellipse radii+tol, the full **text box** (6.5 px/char × 16, screen-sized via `scale`) + **callout** body & leader, `area`/`polygon` `pointInPoly` interior, nearest vertex/segment for open & measure kinds — and `pickMarkupIndex` scores every markup and picks **nearest → smallest bbox-area (B374) → top-most** on ties. **Document Review** was re-routed onto it: its 66-line inline `hitTest` is deleted, replaced by a one-line `pickMarkup(pageMarks, p, view, { tolPx: 10 })?.id` wrapper (behaviour-preserving, verified). **The Site Planner was DELIBERATELY left on its SVG-native picking** (per-element `pointerEvents:"all"` interiors + a 12 px fat hit-stroke on lines + top-most via DOM paint order): it already delivers the shared rules declaratively via the browser's own hit-testing, and re-routing it to the imperative picker would have REGRESSED `easement`/`encumbrance` (the shared tool matrix doesn't classify them closed -> they'd lose interior-grab) and `ellipse` (bbox vs. true ellipse), while rewriting the mature multi/group/drag/vertex-edit interaction stack for **zero user-visible gain**. So the *selection semantics* are unified (one rule set, honoured on both surfaces) even though the Site Planner's *mechanism* stays SVG-native — the smaller, safer edit (CLAUDE.md "keep shared edits small + additive; no big-bang rewrite"). The owner-reported interior-grab bug that opened B155 was already fixed on all three surfaces (increment 1 + the open-path fat-stroke); this closes the "one source of truth" tranche for the JS-picker surface + gives DocReview the WYSIWYG text-box/smallest-area rules from one place.
> - **B156 — a subtle pre-click hover glow shows what a click will grab, on both surfaces.** A shared `.mk-hover` CSS class (a two-tone light-under-dark `drop-shadow`, mirroring the selection chrome so it reads on both a light sheet and a dark aerial) glows the markup under the cursor in Select mode — never recolouring it, never touching the immutable backdrop. **Document Review** computes the hovered id on the idle pointer-move path with the SAME `pickMarkup` wrapper the click uses (hover == selection by construction) and wraps ONLY the hovered markup (overlay DOM otherwise unchanged, so existing selectors/exports are untouched). **The Site Planner** sets the hovered id from each markup's own `onPointerEnter`/`onPointerLeave` — the browser's hit-testing, the exact geometry that decides a click — so its hover matches its click by construction; the hovered subtree carries `.mk-hover`. Never shown on the already-selected markup.

### B757 — ＋ Add parcel menu: mismatched header font sizes + over-explaining copy `[Site Planner / UI]` (bug) — ✅ SHIPPED 2026-07-11 — `Verify: sandbox`
Origin: filed 2026-07-11 from owner chat (screenshot of the ＋ Add parcel menu).
