- **Root cause of the size mismatch:** the "🔍 Identify" and "✏️ Draw" option headers live inside `<button style={menuItem(...)}>`, which sets `fontSize: 12.5` on the button (inherited by its child `<div>`s). Fixed by giving all three option headers an explicit `fontSize: 13` (and keeping descriptions at the existing `fontSize: 11`), so sizing no longer depends on which wrapper element happens to host each option.
- **Copy pass (all three options), `SitePlanner.jsx` ~L9504–9547:**
  - **"Identify from county GIS" → "🔍 Click a lot on the map"**, description → "Property lines from the county appraisal district light up on the aerial — click one lot or several." (plainer term than the jargon "GIS"; explains what the click does rather than just naming the mechanism).

  - **"✏️ Draw a new boundary"** header kept; description replaced "Trace a lot by clicking points on the canvas; close on the first dot" (stating the obvious mechanic) with "For a lot that's not in county records yet" (states *when* to reach for this option instead).
  - Disabled-state copy for both GIS-dependent options (no georeferenced plan yet) unified from two slightly different jargon-y sentences ("Identify needs a georeferenced plan...", "Add-by-address needs a georeferenced plan...") to one consistent plain sentence: "Add a parcel from the map first to turn this on."
  - The one other place this menu's old label was echoed in copy — the "align to deed" empty-state warning (`flashWarn` at ~L8663) — was updated to reference the new "＋ Add → Click a lot on the map" path so the two don't drift.
- **Verified:** `npm run build` green. `ui-audit/verify-b383-add-parcel.mjs` updated for the new copy (its two now-passing assertions were already stale against unrelated hint text, fixed in the same pass) — **22/22 checks pass** headless against the built app, incl. the disabled-state copy, the Identify→click→add flow, and Draw arming with no origin. `ui-audit/verify-b384-add-by-address.mjs` — **5/5** unchanged (it didn't assert the removed sentence). Screenshot confirms all three headers now render at identical size. Pure client-side copy/style change, no data path touched — `Verify: sandbox` is correct, no live check needed.
> - **Verified:** 21 shared-picker unit tests (`test/markupHitTest.test.js` — reference-parity: interior `d=0`, outline distance, text-box far-end hit, callout body+leader, perimeter interior-grab, **smallest-area-beats-top-most incl. the small-UNDER-big case**, tolerance override) + the full **2249-test** suite green · lint **0 errors** · build green with `SitePlannerApp`/`DocReview` lazy chunks intact · **headless both surfaces** (`ui-audit/verify-b155-b156.mjs`, logged-out): hover glow appears on interior-hover, clears on leave, carries `.mk-hover`, and **clicking the exact hovered point selects the same markup (hover == click)** — 15/15 checks, no page errors. ### B780 — Audit the 58 historical duplicate ids + close the cross-file (live↔archive) collision gap `[repo / tooling · workflow]` (tooling) #infra  *(owner chat 2026-07-11 — "Should we examine the 50 duplicates to see if there's a risk to the codebase?" Follow-up to B779, which surfaced them. `B780` late-bound against fresh main.)*
`[x]` **DONE this session — examined every duplicate id the B779 warning surfaced and closed the one guard gap the audit exposed. AUDIT VERDICT: 58 collisions (37 B# + 21 V#), ALL genuine (two different features sharing a number — zero benign re-listings; classified by title-similarity, `sim < 0.35`), but ZERO runtime risk: the ids appear in code only inside comments (provenance breadcrumbs), nothing executes on them, no data path reads them. The residual risk is workflow-only (a lookup landing on the wrong item — bounded by AUDIT-FIRST) and is now capped by the guard below.**
- Verify: sandbox — the cross-file guard was PROVEN red on an injected live↔archive collision (a fresh id heading added to BOTH `BACKLOG.md` and `BACKLOG-DONE.md`) and green on revert, with the live-only test correctly unaffected; baseline-honesty + not-a-no-op unit cases included. Full suite green, lint clean.
- Origin: owner chat 2026-07-11 (risk question on the B779 duplicate findings).
- **The gap:** B779's uniqueness guard checked the LIVE files only — but most of the 58 historical dupes formed ACROSS files, via the race where session A ships and ARCHIVES its item while session B's same-numbered item stays open (the two headings land in different files, so the live-only check never sees them). That path was still open for future collisions.
- **The fix:** `KNOWN_LEGACY_ID_COLLISIONS` (`scripts/next-id.mjs`) — the 58 audited ids frozen at their exact counts (B445/V45 ×3, rest ×2) — plus `newCrossFileCollisions()` and two new `test/idUniqueness.test.js` cases over the FULL live+archive pair: any id newly collided, or any grandfathered id collided one more time, fails the build. A baseline-honesty case forces the allowlist to only ever SHRINK (clean a legacy dup → delete its row in the same commit), so a stale baseline can't mask a collision on a recycled id.
- **Why grandfather instead of renumber:** the legacy dupes are load-bearing history — renumbering either side breaks scattered cross-references in the write-only archives (V entries citing B#s, code comments citing both meanings), `--against-main` already prevents minting over them, and they carry no runtime dependence. Recorded, capped, and shrinkable beats risky archaeology.

### B874 — Stuck flood-refresh: the "Refreshing flood data…" spinner never clears (×1 — edit path) `[Site Planner / yield]` (bug — crash-severity class) #site-planner #yield #floodplain #gis  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-16 post-ship as "NEW-1"; minted B874 by the B873 audit, IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-17 after the Cowork live pass confirmed it AMBIENT. Branch `claude/detention-verdict-delta-bugs-l3mm1l`. **V renumbered 357→358 on merge — main's V357 (single-occupancy dock) merged first.** Recurrence 2026-07-17 (×1) — see below.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — timing/race + real-project-data, needs a signed-in Tsakiris fresh-load) → V358.** Cowork live: a fresh hard-reload with ZERO edits already showed "Refreshing flood data for the drawn area…" stuck >60s, Detention frozen at 38.30 — ambient, not edit-triggered. The single blocker (freezes/starves steps 2,3,6,7,9 and gates B868/B869). **Measure-before-patch root cause (traced in code):** the fetch-record writer stored `fetchRec.env` via `Math.round` (a min can round UP, a max DOWN → the stored envelope SHRINKS below the drawn geometry); the reader (`drainFactsNow`) compares the RAW geometry with `envelopeContains(..., tol 0)`. So on a fresh load with unchanged geometry the containment FAILED → `revalidationNeed` returned `env-exit` (need:true) permanently → and `drainAutoRefreshing = drainReval.need || busy` showed "Refreshing…" forever even though the single auto-attempt was spent and nothing was in flight.
- ✅ **DONE — live-verified 2026-07-18 (V358 PASSED, planyr.io verification handoff):** the edit-path flood-refresh is bounded (success ~10s / terminal by ~30s, never endless).
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-16 from chat (post-ship block); confirmed live by the Cowork pass.
- **Root fix — canonical envelope:** new `canonEnv` (`factRevalidation.js`) rounds OUTWARD (floor mins, ceil maxs) so the stored env always CONTAINS the geometry; `ENV_TOL_FT = 2` slack in `fetchStaleForEdit` + `revalidationNeed`'s env-exit absorbs the whole-foot gap. Writer + reader now agree by construction — no ambient env-exit.
- **Bounded state machine:** the spinner is decoupled from `drainReval.need` — it shows only for a REAL in-flight/armed auto fetch; a wanted refetch whose one attempt is spent + not in flight is a TERMINAL `drainAutoStalled` state ("⚠ Couldn't refresh — ↻ Re-check"), never an endless spinner. The whole pull is raced against a 30s timeout (a black-holed fetch can't leave `busy` latched). A manual ↻ clears the one-attempt guard so the target can auto-retry.
- **Also fixes** the ambient false `drainFetchStale` (NEW-2's stale-hold) and the in-section RE-CHECK chip (B867) that rode the same env-rounding trigger.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** distinct new symptom on B860's refresh surface (cross-linked); the env-rounding is a defect in B832/B860's fetch-record.
- **Verified (sandbox):** `factRevalidation.test.js` (+6: canonEnv contains, REGRESSION proof the old Math.round tripped env-exit, unchanged-geometry not-stale, real growth still trips, guards). Full suite (4241) + lint 0 errors + build green.
- **🔁 Recurrence 2026-07-17 (×1) — the EDIT-PATH re-fetch was still unbounded (Cowork live pass on the deployed #656 build).** The #656 fix bounded the ambient ON-LOAD spinner (canonEnv), but on any boundary change the re-fetch spinner still hung >60s with NO success-settle and NO timeout→terminal (mitigation stuck "UNKNOWN", terminal error never shown), on a normal nudge AND a far-outside drag. **Measure-before-patch:** the fetch itself is 30 s-race-bounded + the FBCDD samplers are 8 s-bounded, so the hang lives ABOVE the fetch in the DERIVED spinner state — two unbounded branches: (a) the "armed" branch (`drainReval.need && !attemptSpent && !busy`) stayed true forever when the auto-refetch timer bailed on the 20 s rate floor / a hidden tab WITHOUT marking the attempt spent — no fetch, no terminal, no re-arm; (b) a `busy` left latched by a superseded early-return or a black-holed promise had no ceiling.
- **Recurrence fix — an independent WATCHDOG bounds BOTH branches (`DRAIN_STUCK_MS = 45 s`, > the 30 s fetch timeout so a slow-but-completing pull isn't cut off; pure `fetchWatchdogFired`):** Watchdog #1 — a `busy` fetch still in flight at the ceiling is ABANDONED (bump `drainTok` so its late resolve no-ops) and dropped to a terminal error with a working ↻. Watchdog #2 — a WANTED-but-unfired armed episode at the ceiling spends its one attempt (→ the terminal `drainAutoStalled` state) + forces a re-render. Plus the rate floor is FOLDED INTO the auto-refetch delay (`max(base, floorRemaining)`) so the attempt always fires (→ busy → watchdog-bounded) instead of being silently dropped. Guarantees the spinner ALWAYS terminates (success ≤ fetch latency, else terminal ≤ 45 s).
- **Recurrence verified (sandbox):** `factRevalidation.test.js` (+5: ceiling > 30 s, fresh-episode-not-fired vs over-ceiling-fired, custom ceiling, no-episode-never-stuck, non-finite guard). Full suite (4255) + lint 0 errors + build green. V358's acceptance already tests the edit path (boundary edit → refresh + flash; forced-fail → terminal, never endless) — it stands.
- **⏳ V358 (live):** see VERIFICATION.md — now covers BOTH the ambient on-load AND the edit-path re-fetch (success-settle, forced-fail terminal).

### B876 — Single-occupancy left dock: element inspector REPLACES the docked panel, never stacks above it `[Site Planner]` (feature) #site-planner #ui #selection  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-16 as "NEW-1"; minted **B876** — renumbered from a late B873 collision: a concurrent session's B873/V356 (verification-targeting audit) merged to main first, so this item reconciles-on-merge to B876/V357. Branch `claude/single-occupancy-left-dock-lcml17`. Amends B656/B733 — supersedes the companion-stacking layout.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session; parks in ⏳ Verify (Verify: live — owner asked for a Cowork/planyr.io eyeball; the deterministic interaction is already proven by a headless e2e) → V357.** Before, opening a selected element's inspector while a rail panel (e.g. Yield) was docked rendered the inspector STACKED above the docked panel — two panels at once. New rule: the dock holds at most ONE panel, always. The inspector now TAKES OVER the dock; to see the inspector AND another panel, detach one to a floating card (B717) first.
- ✅ **DONE — self-verified headless 2026-07-18 (V357 PASSED):** single-occupancy dock takeover + restore + floating-coexist proven by `e2e/single-occupancy-dock.spec.js`.
- Verify: live
- Origin: filed 2026-07-16 from chat (owner NEW-1).
- **Takeover, not stack:** when the inspector OPENS on desktop (`propsMatches` — B750's explicit open: a double-click, or the Properties tab; a plain single click still just SELECTS, B750 preserved) a layout effect sets `leftPanel → "properties"`, memoizing the panel it replaced in `dockMemo`. `companionOpen` on desktop is now simply `leftPanel === "properties"` — the 45%-cap "rides above another panel" layout survives ONLY on narrow (B556). Runs in a `useLayoutEffect` so the swap lands before paint (no stacked-panel flash); dock width is constant (both panels dock at `leftWidth`) so the canvas never shifts (VIEWPORT-STABLE, trivially).
- **Restore-on-close:** deselect or the inspector ✕ drops `propsFor` → the same effect hands the dock back to the memoized panel (or closes it) via the pure `dockAfterRelinquish`. A deliberate manual rail switch drops `dockMemo` first, so the manual choice wins over the memo (the resolver also no-ops when `leftPanel` already moved off "properties"). The ✕ now shows on the desktop docked inspector (was hidden in the Properties tab).
- **Floating interplay:** a floating panel is untouched by selection — floating Yield + docked inspector coexist (the intended two-at-once path). Properties stays dock-only (B733), excluded from the B717 float system.
- **Narrow/phone (B556 intact):** the takeover effect early-returns on `narrow`; a tap still only selects and the ✎ Properties pill opens the companion overlay (never a dock takeover).
- **New pure helpers:** `shared/ui/floatingPanel.js` `shouldInspectorTakeDock` + `dockAfterRelinquish` (host owns the `dockMemo` state + wiring), unit-tested in `test/floatingPanel.test.js`.
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** amends B656 (companion) / B733 (docked Properties home) — no prior item makes the dock single-occupancy; not a recurrence. Preserves B750 (single-click selects only; its live guard `e2e/click-behavior.spec.js` stays green). Code/tests keep the provisional `NEW-1` label (house rule — a late renumber touches only these heading lines, never code).
- **Verified (sandbox):** `test/floatingPanel.test.js` (+9: the two helpers) + the NEW-1 source guard in `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` green · full suite **4244 green** · lint 0 errors · build green · MAP/backlog-index clean · **headless interactive drive** (`e2e/single-occupancy-dock.spec.js`, logged-out, real app): (1) Yield docked → double-click a building → Yield replaced by the inspector (NOT stacked) → ✕/deselect → Yield restored; (2) detach Yield to a float → double-click a building → floating Yield + docked inspector coexist — both with **0 page errors**; the B750 guard (`e2e/click-behavior.spec.js`) + all floating-panel guards stay green.

### B828 — Undo records + reverts edits that previously slipped the history stack (four "undo doesn't work" gaps) `[Site Planner / Review]` (bug) #site-planner #doc-review #ui  *(owner report 2026-07-14: "debug the undo button, it doesn't seem to be working"; a fan-out audit of every undoable mutation across the three undo surfaces confirmed four distinct gaps; minted **B828**)*
`[x]` Four separate user gestures mutated undoable state without recording a history frame (or read a STALE snapshot), so clicking Undo did nothing for them — or worse, jumped back past an unrelated earlier edit. The core undo button + Ctrl+Z were never broken (markup draw/move/delete undo cleanly, e2e-proven); these are the specific paths that slipped.
- ✅ **DONE — self-verified headless 2026-07-18 (V319 PASSED):** undo/redo one-step round-trip proven by `ui-audit/verify-b828-undo.mjs` (8/8).
- Verify: live — the item bundles a timing/race sub-fix (the render-time undo mirror), a mandatory LIVE-VERIFY class; the headline case is already sandbox-proven end-to-end (below). → V319.
- Origin: filed 2026-07-14 from owner chat.
- **(1) Parcel fill "Translucence" slider** (`SitePlanner.jsx:~10361`) — a bare `onChange → setSelParcel` (which never pushes history) meant dragging translucence recorded no undo frame, though `fillOpacity` IS in the snapshot; the next Undo then misfired past it. Fixed: spread `{...sliderHistory(...)}` like every other opacity slider (the RC-5/RC-7 house rule). **SANDBOX-VERIFIED end-to-end** — `ui-audit/verify-b828-undo.mjs` (8/8, logged-out): draw parcel → enable fill → drag Translucence 0.12→0.24 → click the Undo BUTTON reverts it in ONE step (parcel+fill survive, no overshoot) → Redo restores.
- **(2) Raster overlay "Width (ft)" input** (`SitePlanner.jsx:~9918`) — typing a new width (patchOverlay `hist=false`) had no `onFocus` checkpoint, so rescaling an image overlay wasn't undoable though `ftPerPx` IS snapshotted. Fixed: `onFocus={() => pushHistory()}`, mirroring the opacity number input directly above it.
- **(3) Stitcher auto-calibrate** (`Stitcher.jsx:~362`) — auto-setting `ftPerUnit` from a grouped set's stated scale had no `pushHistory()`, so one Undo skipped straight past it and DELETED a measurement drawn before the group was added. Fixed: checkpoint before the auto-set.
- **(4) DocReview + Stitcher undo mirror was a passive effect** (`DocReview.jsx:~372`, `Stitcher.jsx:~82`) — the B315 anti-pattern: the `docStateRef`/`editRef` mirror lagged one paint behind the live state, so an undo fired right after an edit compared against a stale snapshot, treated the top frame as a no-op, and did nothing (the button stayed enabled, so it just looked broken). Fixed: assign the ref DURING RENDER, exactly like SitePlanner's `stateRef` (the proven B315 fix).
- **Guards:** `test/undoHistoryWiring.test.js` (4 tests) locks all four wirings against a silent merge revert; the pure history stack is already covered by `test/history.test.js`; full suite 3920 green + lint clean.
- **Live-pending (V319):** the overlay Width resize undo (needs an image overlay dropped in), the Stitcher auto-calibrate undo (needs a stitched multi-sheet set), and the DocReview/Stitcher rapid-edit-then-undo timing (the intermittent render-mirror race) — confirmable only in the live app.

### B644 — Scheduler embed: first COLD boot throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'projects')` + the loader overlay exceeds the 6s backstop (self-recovers) (×2) `[Scheduler / robustness]` (bug — first-paint hardening) #scheduler  *(Cowork live verification 2026-07-03, from V153; minted **B644** = highest real B# across both files (B643) + 1)*
`[x]` **DONE — self-verified headless 2026-07-18 (V211 PASSED).** Original report: the FIRST cold Site→Schedule switch on planyr.io threw a one-time `⚠️ This view failed to load — Cannot read properties of null (reading 'projects')` (~10.5s overlay, self-recovered on re-nav).
- Verify: live
- Recurrence: 2026-07-05 — owner repro (chat "NEW-5", DEDUPE-FIRST fold — same error string, same first-paint null-`projects` read): create a project via **Start blank → Schedule tab** → the same error renders **behind the connect-a-schedule modal**. Deterministic (not only the cold race); expected a clean empty state only.
- **Root cause (pinned by a live sandbox repro, not a guess):** NOT the render path — the `if (!data) return <loader/>` gate was already sound. The **shell→iframe nav bridge** (`planar:nav-select` / `nav-select-by-site` / `nav-link` / `nav-create-linked` / `nav-dashboard` / `nav-new` / rename / delete in `public/sequence/index.html`) queues `setData(d => …)` functional updaters when the shell announces the active project on a tab switch; before the async `hs-v1` load resolves `d` is **null**, and React runs the queued updater INSIDE the next `useState` mount — `Object.values(d.projects || {})` throws and lands App in the error boundary. Cold boot = the race version (the bridge message beats the slow cloud load); fresh project = the deterministic version (no schedule linked, load still pending). Captured stack: updater → `Object.useState` → `App`.
- **Fix shipped (minimal, matches the in-file `planar:view-set` precedent):** one early gate in the nav-bridge handler — drop `planar-shell` messages until `latestData.current` exists (the shell re-posts nav intents on every tab switch and retries `nav-request`, so an early drop self-heals the moment the load lands) — plus null guards in the three bridge-called helpers (`addProject` / `renameProject` / `deleteProject`) so a future caller can't regress the class.
- **Sandbox-verified 2026-07-05:** `ui-audit/verify-b644-fresh-null.mjs` (self-contained, fetches the four CDN deps once via curl, serves them by request interception): pre-fix it reproduces the exact owner error + stack; post-fix it PASSES (embed renders, zero null-`projects` errors). `jsxcheck-sequence` OK · build green.
- **✅ Live-verified 2026-07-18 (V211 PASSED, this session):** re-ran `ui-audit/verify-b644-fresh-null.mjs` (still PASS on the merged HEAD) plus a new harness `ui-audit/verify-v211-schedule-coldboot.mjs` (2/2) driving two independent brand-new browser contexts through the cold Start-blank → Schedule path — no failure banner, no null-`projects` error, clean loading skeleton confirmed by screenshot. planyr.io itself isn't directly reachable from this sandbox's headless Chromium (egress `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`, the same external-host block documented elsewhere in `VERIFICATION.md`), so the check ran against a local build of the identical merged-HEAD code `main` deploys. The loader-timing observation (item 3) is non-blocking per B494/B495 and unaffected by this fix.

### B850 — Scheduler's "open in another tab" banner was oversized, falsely claimed a read-only lock, and turned out to be unnecessary entirely `[Scheduler / Shell]` (bug) #scheduler #ui #infra  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-15 in chat, with a screenshot: "now fix it for the scheduling module, i dont know that its a bug but i dont need this large pop up" + "especially bc its just me that has it open even if i have it open in other tabs"; owner then pushed back further in the same thread — "shouldn't it just auto-reload... if I have it up in two tabs" — which triggered a second, deeper AUDIT-FIRST pass in the same session. Minted **B850** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Branch `claude/loving-albattani-mdqvse`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED this session in TWO passes — live-verified 2026-07-19 → V335 CONFIRMED PASS.** Screenshot showed the shared B313 "this project is open in another tab" banner as a large, bold, full-width (660px), non-dismissible dark strip covering part of the Scheduler's grid — for a benign case (the owner, alone, with the same schedule open in two of their own tabs).
- Verify: live — CLOSED (V335 passed)
- Origin: filed 2026-07-15 from chat (owner screenshot + three follow-up messages).
- **Pass 1 (banner too big + wording wrong):** the banner text claims "Only one tab can edit at a time; the others are read-only until you take over editing there or close them" — true for Doc Review (which wires the shared `editorLock`, `usePersistence.js`) and pre-multiwriter Site Planner, but the **Scheduler never adopted that lock at all** (grepped `src/workspaces/scheduler/` and `public/sequence/index.html` — zero hits for `editorLock`/read-only enforcement). Shrunk the banner from a bold 660px dark strip to a small dismissible pill (theme tokens replacing hardcoded hex `#3f2d12`/`#f59e0b`, a KEY DECISIONS violation fixed along the way) and gave the Scheduler its own honest copy via a `lockEnforced` prop.
- **Pass 2 (the owner was right that it shouldn't need ANY notice) — a deeper AUDIT-FIRST pass on `public/sequence/index.html` found the Scheduler is genuinely safe for two tabs, full stop:** its embedded app already runs a "multi-device live-refresh" — every 20s, plus on focus/reconnect/tab-switch, it asks the cloud whether a newer version exists. A clean, backgrounded tab reloads **silently**. A tab you're actively looking at (or that has unsaved edits) gets a small one-click "Reload" banner instead of its screen being yanked mid-look. Separately, the save path's Layer-0 concurrency guard **BLOCKS** (never applies) a write that would clobber a newer cloud version, and the blocked copy is snapshotted to Version History — nothing is silently lost. So a second Scheduler tab was never actually read-only, AND routine two-tab use converges on its own without the user needing to think about it — the outer generic banner was adding noise, not safety, and the embedded app's own precise in-context "a newer version was saved" notice already covers the one real case (a blocked save) better than any cross-workspace banner could.
- **Final fix:** the `lockEnforced` dual-copy complexity from Pass 1 was removed entirely (dead once no caller needed the softened variant) and the banner reverted to its single, always-accurate "read-only" copy — now correct for its only remaining reachers (Doc Review; Site Planner only when the multiwriter escape hatch is off). `Scheduler.jsx` instead passes **`multiEditOk`** (the same flag Site Planner/Library already use to suppress the banner outright), so the Scheduler shows NO cross-tab notice at all — matching what the owner expected.

### B846 — Idle second same-account tab makes cascade-derived elements fire false "you (another window) changed X you just edited" toasts `[Site Planner / persistence]` (bug) #site-planner #persistence #ui  *(owner-dropped 2026-07-15 as "NEW-1" — the TWO-tab path of the 7/14 multiwriter-cascade handoff (`claude/handoff-2026-07-14-multiwriter-cascade-false-conflict.md`, never minted until now — the miss that motivated B847); minted **B846** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main` — RENUMBERED from a provisional B844 on merge (PR #633, the Scheduler meeting-calendars pair, took B844/B845 first; code/tests keep the provisional NEW-1 label per the house rule). Branch `claude/loving-albattani-mdqvse`.)*
`[x]` **IMPLEMENTED + sandbox-verified 2026-07-15; live-confirmed 2026-07-19 → V334 CONFIRMED PASS.** Repro (owner, ×2: 2026-07-14 truck-court depth; 2026-07-15 Bain `smr9olizi5ue` building edit ~15:55Z): two signed-in tabs of one account on one plan, second tab idle; a cascade edit in the active tab → burst of B673 remote-upsert toasts for the DERIVED elements the gesture re-laid (paving area, sidewalks, parking fields — never the element actually touched), each "you (another window) changed a … you just edited — their version is showing"; bonded aprons can visibly separate for a beat; refresh clears it.
- Verify: live — CLOSED (V334 passed).
- Origin: filed 2026-07-15 from chat (owner-reported 2026-07-14 + 2026-07-15).
- **Root cause (per the handoff diagnosis, confirmed in code):** (1) `processResults` stamped `recent` for EVERY ok result with no user-touched vs derived distinction, so cascade outputs answered `authoredRecently` — any foreign-looking echo of them toasted "you just edited"; (2) since B674 the second tab is a live writer, and the pending-edit journal was ONE KEY PER SITE (`planyr:elements:pending:<siteId>`), so an idle tab's refetch could fold-and-clear the active tab's mid-commit journal — re-committing its in-flight edits as byte-divergent copies that passed every single-tab self-echo guard (`SitePlanner.jsx` conceded the clobber in a comment); (3) `reconcileSeedRows` could substitute MIXED shadow pairings (a newer adopted rev over an older kept json) into a refetch re-seed — the "aprons separate for a beat" churn.
- **Fix (all three handoff directions shipped):** **#1** `createElementSync` takes `isDirectEdit(kind,id,el)`; every enqueued op carries a `direct` tag (preserved through conflict/missing/exists re-enqueues; `restore()` always direct) and **only direct ops stamp `recent`** — SitePlanner supplies "bonded (`attachedTo`) elements are derived unless the gesture/selection (drag/sel/multi, stamped every render into `directTouchRef`) targeted them". **#2** new exported `semanticallyEqual(a,b,eps=1e-6)` (numbers within eps, key sets must match — gates only WHO IS TOLD, never what is written): a semantically-equal live row is now SILENT on all three read paths (conflict branch → adopt rev with our bytes, no re-commit ping-pong, no event; pending branch → no `remote-while-dirty`; no-pending upsert → no `remote-upsert`). **#3** the journal is **per-SESSION** (`planyr:elements:pending:<site>:s:<tab>`, sessionStorage-backed id): a live sibling's journal is untouchable, orphans (frozen `at` > 5 min) + the legacy key are adopted-and-swept, same-tab reload recovery unchanged; plus shadow entries whose json was KEPT under a newer adopted rev are flagged `stale` and `reconcileSeedRows` never substitutes them (fetched row stays canonical; the post-seed reconcile re-commits any newer local truth).
- **DEDUPE-FIRST:** net-new — the TWO-tab path. B757/B759/B811/B812 are the SINGLE-tab family (implemented, parked V273/V301/V303/V304) — not reopened; their guards are regression-tested unchanged. B673/B674 built the toast matrix + multi-writer cutover this hardens.
- **Verified (sandbox):** 16 new unit tests — `test/elementSync.test.js` (derived ops never claim authorship + direct guard + tag survives re-enqueue + restore/fail-open/default-direct; semantic-equality unit cases + all three silent paths + genuine-difference guards; stale-pairing seed hardening + clean-entry B759 behavior preserved), `test/elementJournal.test.js` rewritten (per-session isolation, live-sibling hands-off, orphan adoption + sweep, legacy migration, own-beats-orphan dedupe, reload recovery, session-id stability), `test/elementRows.test.js` (stale guard), `test/bugHuntGuards.test.js` (SitePlanner wiring source guards). Full suite + lint 0 errors + build green; e2e smoke/canvas specs green. Element sync runs signed-in only — the sandbox can't sign in, hence the live park.
- **Adversarial review (4-lens find→refute workflow) — confirmed findings all fixed same session:** (1) `sweepJournals` unconditionally deleted a FRESH legacy journal `readJournal` had refused to fold (a live pre-upgrade tab's crash protection destroyed) → sweep now consumes exactly the read's key set; (2) read/sweep used two `Date.now()` calls, so a journal crossing the 5-min orphan boundary in between could be swept unfolded → one shared timestamp; (3) the autosave effect reconciles BEFORE the render-effect stamp, so a single-shot edit after >10s idle enqueued against aged stamps (a directly-edited bonded child mis-tagged derived) → `stampDirectTargets()` also runs at the top of `reconcileElems`, same tick as the enqueue; (4) skipKeys-filtered journal entries were discarded with zero telemetry → now reported via `onDiscard` (LOUD-FAILURE). **Accepted, documented limitations:** browsers copy sessionStorage on "Duplicate tab", so a duplicated pair shares one journal id — for that pair only, behavior falls back to the pre-fix shared journal (strictly no worse; a liveness protocol isn't worth the boot cost, and foldJournal's baseRev guards cap the blast radius); with sessionStorage BLOCKED (but localStorage working) the per-load fallback id makes a reload's own journal look foreign for the 5-min orphan window — recovery is delayed, never lost; panel-driven edits to bonded children (e.g. "+ add zone" with the building selected) tag derived — quiet-side-only cost (a softened heads-up, never data).
- **✅ V334 (live, planyr.io, SIGNED IN, two tabs, Bain — Fort Bend, 2026-07-19):** PASSED — see VERIFICATION-DONE.md. A cascade edit (Building 3's Length spinner 769→770ft) in tab A propagated live to tab B with no manual reload (770'×280', 222,200 sf, 55 trailers) and the bonded trailer-parking apron stayed fully attached with no gap/separation; no false "another window changed X you just edited" toast appeared in either tab (screenshot-sampled, not continuous-recorded). Reverting the edit converged both tabs back to the exact original state (221,920 sf, 769'×280', 54 trailers).

### B1041 — NEW-9: a plain Site route eagerly fetched ALL 11 chunks — ~805 KB (27% of all JS) of workspaces it never runs `[Infra / Build]` (task) #infra #perf  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-9, INFRA half of a nine-item perf run — measured on production planyr.io, signed-in, Sylvestri / "Concept C — Full 275' Frontage", dpr 2.15, 1600x465. Minted **B1041** via `npm run next-id -- --against-main`. Branch `claude/chunk-prefetch-audit-xz54gh`. DEDUPE-FIRST: searched Open + ⏳ Verify + Done for prefetch/chunk/bundle/lazy-load items — **B223** (the idle module prefetch) is the item this AMENDS, not a recurrence: B223 shipped the warm-up deliberately and correctly for its stated goal; what was never true was its assumption that the idle callback runs after first paint. Not reopened — its hover-intent half survives intact.)*
`[x]` **DONE.** The item arrived scoped as "do code splitting"; measurement re-scoped it, and the original framing was wrong in a way that made this much cheaper.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-07-28 from chat
- **AUDIT-FIRST — what the code actually did.** The app was ALREADY split into 11 chunks and `React.lazy` already gated every workspace. The defect was not missing splitting: `src/app/Shell.jsx` ran `prefetchOnIdle(["scheduler","doc-review","library"])` at mount (B223), and its `requestIdleCallback` fired at **~t=304 ms — BEFORE first-contentful-paint at ~328 ms**. So B223's own premise ("nothing here runs at boot; lazy-loading still gates the first paint") was false in practice: `requestIdleCallback` fires in any main-thread gap, including gaps *during* boot while the critical path is still in flight. Worse than the bytes, `import()` fetches at HIGH priority **and evaluates** the module, spending parse/compile time in exactly the window the planner needs to become interactive.
- **Reproduced locally before editing**: a Site-route load against the real build fetched all 11 chunks, the second wave (Scheduler · DocReview · pdf · pdf.worker.min · uploadQueue · Library · folders) landing ~85 ms after the first — matching the owner's resource-timing trace exactly. `pdf.worker.min` (471 KB) rides along because Vite records the `?url` worker asset as a STATIC import of DocReview, so warming DocReview drags it in.
- **Fix.** Removed the boot-time warm entirely (`prefetchOnIdle` deleted; `Shell.jsx` effect removed). ### B1055 — PANEL-BREVITY: a house rule against panel-copy accumulation, machine-enforced `[Infra / Docs]` (task) #infra #yield #ui #testing  *(owner amendment 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-5. Minted **B1055**. The owner's stated top priority in that message.)*

- **The rule** lives in `CLAUDE.md` as a named engineering rule (**PANEL-BREVITY**) so every session picks it up automatically, and is referenced from the Definition of Done and the `/improve` gate. Seven clauses: verdict + number first with at most one short line per group · new copy REPLACES rather than accumulates (name the sentence you removed) · named state over a sentence explaining the state · numbers over prose, absolute over percentages · never the same sentence twice · honesty stays REACHABLE not VISIBLE (collapse, never delete) · report line counts before and after.

Extends the existing per-line caps (B823's 110-char `warnNote` cap, `pondCopyLint`) from "no one line may be a paragraph" to "no group may accumulate lines".
- **The escape valves are the point:** copy inside a `<Collapse>`, a `title=`/`basis=` hover, or a `keyedNote(...)` method note is EXEMPT — so collapsing gets you under budget and deleting a fact is never necessary. The guard self-tests this (moving a sentence into a fold provably reduces the count; leaving it inline provably raises it) and throws rather than reporting a comfortable zero if a region anchor ever moves.

### B1059 — Ctrl+C on a building leaves behind the elements bonded to it; and most object types can't be copied at all `[Site Planner / selection]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #ui #markup  *(owner chat block 2026-07-28, provisional NEW-2, SUPERSEDED in scope by the NEW-6 amendment minutes later — filed as ONE item because NEW-6 explicitly reconciles them as two halves of one general clipboard. DEDUPE-FIRST: no existing clipboard/copy-paste item across Open / ⏳ Verify / Done; B417 is paste-at-cursor PLACEMENT (kept), B261 is explicit Groups, B740 is multi-select shared STYLE editing — none of them own the clipboard.)*
`[ ]` One clipboard driven by the selection: every drawn kind copies, an element brings its bonded assembly, paste re-mints ids and preserves relative geometry in one undo frame.

- **AUDIT — NEW-2's two flagged premises, resolved before building.**
  **(a) Does a Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V path exist?** YES — this was a PARTIAL feature, not net-new. `copySel` /
  `pasteClip` existed but `copySel` was literally `els.find(...)`: a single-element clipboard. So the
  narrow framing was right about the mechanism and wrong about the scope.
  **(b) Is there an explicit host relation, or only geometric coincidence?** There IS an explicit one, and
  it is not limited to dog-ears: **`attachedTo`** bonds truck courts, trailer parking, dock-zone stacks,
  side parking, wall sidewalks AND dog-ear bump-outs to their host building. `deleteSel`, `nudgeSel`,
  `assemblyOf` and `duplicateGroup` already cascade over it. **No geometric-containment inference was
  invented** — the new code uses that same relation and nothing else.
  **The actual root cause** was the opposite of "no relation exists": `ORPHAN_TAGS` / `detachClone`
  DELIBERATELY stripped `attachedTo` on paste (a correct rule for a lone child pasted on its own,
  wrongly applied to a whole assembly). That branch is preserved for the lone-child case.
- **Coverage (NEW-6).** `CLIP_KINDS = el · markup · measure · callout · parcel` — every drawn kind,
  including a mixed multi-selection. **Deliberate, documented exclusions:** imported backdrops
  (`sheetOverlays` / the site underlay) keep their existing dedicated `copyOverlay`/`pasteOverlay` path,
  because copying one has to clone the raster/PDF payload and its calibration, not just geometry;
  road junctions, dock frames and dog-ears are never standalone and ride along inside their host's
  assembly. Nothing else is un-copyable.
- **The parcel trap, decided explicitly (not hand-waved).** A pasted parcel arrives **`active: false`**.
  Active parcels drive every area/yield number (B100/B170) and the copy lands on or beside the original,
  so counting both would silently double the site area the plan is sized against. Inactive = visible,
  editable, excluded from the math; one click on the Active toggle counts it when that is really wanted,
  and a toast says so on paste. `gisKey` is dropped with it — the copy is a drawn shape, not the county's
  record for that account, and two shapes must not claim one parcel id. Child elements do not attach to
  parcels (`attachedTo` is building-scoped), so nothing cascades; an easement MARKUP carrying `parcelId`
  is remapped to the copied parcel when both are copied together, and otherwise keeps pointing at the
  live parcel it was drawn on.
- **Paste contract, all four parts:** fresh ids for every object · relative geometry preserved (the whole
  set moves by ONE delta, landing bbox-centred under the cursor, honoring grid/snap) · the pasted set is
  selected afterward · ONE undo frame. Group membership is preserved under a NEW group id when the
  group-mates are copied together, and dropped when a member is copied alone. Bonded children are folded
  into their host's selection ref, so a pasted building reads as one object, not eight.
- Files: new pure `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/planClipboard.js` (+ `test/planClipboard.test.js`, 26
  tests); `SitePlanner.jsx` — `copySel` / `copyRef` / `cutSel` / `pasteClip` rewritten, the Ctrl+C/X/V
  handlers now gate on `hasCopyableSel()`, Copy rows added to the markup / measure / callout right-click
  menus, and the multi-selection delete / nudge / outline paths extended to callouts + parcels (they can
  now ride in a multi-selection because a pasted mixed set selects itself).
- **Verified in the sandbox 2026-07-28** — build green, 5784 unit tests green, and five logged-out
  Playwright drives: a callout copies + pastes with a fresh id and its text, undone by one Ctrl+Z; a
  measurement copies + pastes; a parcel copies and the copy is `active:false` with no `gisKey`; and a
  building with REAL dock zones bonded through the app's own "＋ Add dock zone" control copies with every
  bonded child, each re-bonded to the COPY (never the original), role tags intact, in one undo frame.

### B1109 — Multi-zone state plane: the projection resolves per site, not per module load `[Platform / geo]` (feature) #coordinates  *(minted via `--against-main`. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat (NEW-3).)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-07-29.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **The premise was understated, not wrong.** The zone was not chosen per app *or* per site — it was a **module constant** (`shared/coordinates/index.js:16`, with the Texas South Central Lambert parameters at :57–62 and the cone constants precomputed at import). Correct for Houston/Katy, wrong everywhere else.
- `shared/coordinates/statePlane.js` adds a zone registry (**TX South Central 2278**, **CO North 2231**, **CO Central 2232**), per-county assignment, and `resolveZone({state, county, lat, lon})` — county first (Colorado's zone boundaries **are** county lines), coarse extent second (stamped `coarse:true`, because along the Front Range Jefferson reaches north to 39.91 while Boulder and Broomfield reach south to 39.89 — no latitude split can separate them), honest `null` last.
- **Texas is bit-identical, and that is proven not asserted.** The generic Lambert engine repeats the formulas in the same operation order, so `projectToZone("tx_sc", …)` reproduces `projectToGrid` **exactly** — asserted with `Object.is` on the raw doubles, not `toBeCloseTo`. `index.js` was **not refactored**: the shared Texas path was left alone on purpose.
- **Broomfield is a documented DECISION with visible reasoning, not a silent default.** C.R.S. 38-52-101 never names it — the statute predates the county, created 2001 from parts of Adams, Boulder, Jefferson and Weld. Three of those four parents are North zone; and independently, **Broomfield's own parcel service publishes in EPSG:2876 — NAD83(HARN) / Colorado North (ftUS)**, which is real evidence rather than inference. Assigned **North**, carrying `decided:true` + a `decisionNote`. (Denver's own service publishing in **EPSG:2877** — Colorado Central — independently confirms that assignment too.)
- `test/statePlane.test.js` 21 cases: bit-identity, Colorado round trips, unit grid scale at every standard parallel, the published Denver coordinate range, county/spelling normalisation, honest nulls, and county-beats-extent.

### B1112 — Grid vs ground: surface the combined scale factor, and flag a ground-coordinate survey `[Platform / geo]` (feature) #coordinates  *(minted via `--against-main`. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat (NEW-4).)*
`[x]` **Done 2026-07-29 — the surfacing half. The transform half is filed and sized as B1106, flagged loudly rather than half-applied.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **The question the item asked first — does the app currently assume grid equals ground? — was audited, and the answer is YES, wherever it measures on the grid.** Drawn geometry uses `mapLock.js` (ground-true at the site origin by construction); screening distances use the state-plane grid (`proximityScreen.js`, `coverage.js`, `fbcdWse.js`, `deedAlign.js`, `thoroughfare/ingestTransform.js`) and are treated as ground feet.
- **Correct by accident in Texas** (Houston ~50 ft → elevation factor 0.999998, ~0.01 ft/mile), **wrong in Colorado** (Denver ~5,280 ft → combined ≈ 0.99975, **~1.3 ft/mile, ~9 in across a 3,000-ft site**), reproducing the owner's verified figures.
- `shared/coordinates/scaleFactor.js`: the LCC grid factor, the elevation factor (with optional geoid separation — the Front Range geoid sits ~55–60 ft below the ellipsoid, worth ~3 ppm, and the result says whether it was applied), their product, what it is worth per mile and over any run, a `material` flag at 1-in-20,000, and `detectSurveyFrame` classifying a survey as **grid / ground / other-scale / unknown** from corresponding survey↔grid distances. `other-scale` is a real answer, not a failure — a project can be scaled about a local origin by a factor the surveyor chose.
- **It deliberately does NOT apply the factor**, per the item's own instruction: a half-applied factor turns a known constant into an untraceable error. It also returns `known:false` with a named `missing` list rather than a plausible 1.0.

### B1102 — Map viewer: the zoom-out floor that made a second state unreachable `[Site Planner / map]` (bug) #ui #gis  *(minted via `--against-main`. Origin: filed 2026-07-29 from chat (NEW-6).)*

- **Which of the four candidates it turned out to be: none of the three the brief suspected.** It was a single hard `minZoom: 8` on the Leaflet map (`MapFinder.jsx:417`). **Not a bounds clamp** — `setMaxBounds`/`maxBounds` appear nowhere in the codebase. **Not tile coverage** — Esri World Imagery and USGS ImageryOnly both serve from z0; their `maxNative` ceilings (19/16) constrain the deep end, not the shallow end. **Not a projection chosen at init** — the map is one Web Mercator worldwide; the per-site frame (`mapLock`) belongs to the planner canvas, not the finder.
- At z8 the view spans a few counties, so there was no way to pull back and see another state at all — you could only jump by picking a site. Now `minZoom: 3`, which puts the continent on screen.
- **Verified headless** (`e2e/colorado-map-zoom.spec.js`): the real app boots, the zoom-out control is driven the way a user drives it, and the **graphic scale bar reads 300 mi** with the cursor readout over latitude 39.3° — a continental view, structurally impossible at the old floor, asserted in the units the user actually sees. Zero page errors. Also guarded statically in `test/coloradoRegistry.test.js`, which asserts the literal and that no `maxBounds` reappears.
- The landing view is still `COUNTIES_MAP.harris` — deliberately unchanged; where the app opens is a product decision, not a bug fix.

### B266080 — A permanently-red e2e suite cannot report a NEW regression: the known-red ledger + drift gate `[Infra / CI]` (task) #infra #testing  *(minted from this branch's reserved block B266080–B266095 · V63088–V63103 via `git fetch origin main && npm run next-id -- --against-main` against `origin/main` 81f9dcd. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `e2e`, `e2e-drift`, `known-red`, `ledger`, `ratchet`, `B278`, `B280`, `B281`, `B421`, `B1179`: **B278/B280/B281** built the suite and the @claude loop; **B1179** is three individual red specs and is now Done. No item covers the suite's SIGNAL being dead. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **✅ Done 2026-08-08 — shipped, mutation-proven three ways, merged.**
- Live check still owed (it needs a real GitHub Actions run, never the owner): **V63088** in `VERIFICATION.md`.
- Verify: sandbox
- **THE MEASUREMENT.** `E2E (Playwright)` failed on **17 consecutive scheduled runs** — every weekday from run #29 (2026-07-22) to run #41 (2026-08-07); last green #28, 2026-07-21. It filed correctly every time, and because it is idempotent by design all 17 reports landed as **12 comments on one issue (#762)**, unanswered for 17 days. **The alarm was not noisy, it was MUTE** — and while every run was red, a brand-new regression would have changed nothing about the signal anyone saw. Same class as the swallowing telemetry sink and the sustain window that fired least when the lag was worst.
- **WHAT SHIPPED.** `e2e/known-red.json` — a committed ledger of the cases known to fail, each with its lane, first-seen date and owning item — plus `scripts/e2e-drift-gate.mjs` (+ the pure `scripts/lib/e2eDrift.mjs`). The workflow now emits a JSON report and the **JOB'S VERDICT IS THE DIFF**, not the raw exit code.
- **IT FAILS ON BOTH SIDES, which is what stops the ledger becoming a permanent amnesty:** a failure **not** on the ledger is a new regression → red, named; a ledger entry that **PASSES** means the ledger is stale → red, so it must shrink. `--update` refuses to GROW without `--allow-grow --item B###`, so no red case is ever unowned.
- **IT COUNTS.** A set and its size, printed every run — never a duration or a rate. That distinction has paid for itself four times in this repo in two days.
- **MUTATION-PROVEN AGAINST THE REAL COMMITTED LEDGER, three ways:** the true failure set → **exit 0**; one fabricated new failure → **exit 1**, named; one ledgered case flipped to passing → **exit 1**, named. Plus 16 unit tests (`test/e2eDriftGate.test.js`) covering flaky-is-not-failed, skipped-is-not-failed, a rename that must not launder a case away, and the cross-lane isolation.
- **NOT OBSERVING beats a false green:** a missing report, an unreadable report or a report with zero cases all **exit non-zero**, because a gate that green-lights a missing input is the exact shape of the alarm it replaces.

A second `e2e-local` job now runs that lane on the same schedule, in its own ledger lane.
- **THE SECOND HALF — a false-green assertion.** Playwright's `toBeVisible()` means "non-empty box, not `visibility:hidden`". It says nothing about WHERE the box is. In real fullscreen the header slides to `y = −44`: every module tab is still "visible", unreachable by any user, and unclickable by Playwright itself. `module-keepalive`'s "the chrome came back" assertion therefore **PASSED against a page whose chrome had not come back**, and the case died one line later on a click — which is why its real subject was never reached. ### B266083 — The ratchet promised "from a fresh build" and never built anything `[Infra / CI]` (task) #infra #perf #testing  *(minted from this branch's reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST: **B1040** built the budget system, **B1144** the headroom band, **B1146** byte attribution, **B1178** is the SYMPTOM (an unreproducible baseline) and is amended by this work. No item covers the recording step itself being unsound. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **✅ Done 2026-08-08 — shipped and merged.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **THE DEFECT, in the file's own words.** `scripts/perf-ratchet.mjs`'s header has promised since it was written that it "measures the value itself, **from a fresh build**", and that "you cannot ratchet to a number you did not measure". The second half was true. The first half was a **comment**: the code called `loadBuild(join(ROOT, "dist"))` and measured whatever `dist/` was in the tree, produced by whoever last typed `npm run build`, at whatever revision the tree was in at that moment. Note the asymmetry it had lived with — the RUNTIME half of the same script interrogates its input rigorously before writing a byte; the bundle half did none of it.
- **THE FIX, three parts, all loud rather than degrading:** (1) it **builds**, into its own `dist-ratchet`, unless `--dist` names one deliberately; (2) it **refuses a working tree with uncommitted changes** to anything the bundle is a function of (`src/`, `index.html`, `public/`, `vite.config.js`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`) — a number measured from a tree no commit contains is unreproducible by construction; (3) every entry now records **`commit` + `sourceHash`**, which is what makes a baseline checkable rather than merely recorded.
- **Guarded** in `test/perfBudgetPolicy.test.js`: the mechanism is asserted (it must invoke a build, it must check `--porcelain`, the entry must carry commit + sourceHash), not the comment — the comment is what was wrong for weeks.

### B266084 — The headroom band cannot record in-band growth, so main's drift is billed to a stranger's branch `[Infra / CI]` (task) #infra #perf #testing  *(minted from this branch's reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST: **B1144** created the band, **B1146** the attribution this fix finally puts to work, **B1178** is the symptom. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **✅ Done 2026-08-08 — shipped and merged.**
- Live check still owed (it needs a real GitHub Actions run, never the owner): **V63089** in `VERIFICATION.md`.
- Verify: sandbox
- **THE MECHANISM.** Growth above the baseline but inside the band annotates and **writes nothing**. So `main` accumulates real, honest feature weight above its own recorded baseline, invisibly, one in-band merge at a time, until a later branch adds its first kilobyte and trips a ceiling that was already ~90% consumed before it existed. That branch is then told to "pay it back with an optimization" for bytes it did not add, and its only exit is to RAISE the baseline by everyone else's drift.
- **IT HAS ALREADY HAPPENED FIVE TIMES IN NINE DAYS**, every one honestly annotated and every one laundering drift: B1401 · B1405 · B1414 · B209502 · B255200, the largest reading *"main was already 73.6 KB above this stale baseline before this branch"*.
- **THE FIX USES A MEASUREMENT ALREADY BEING TAKEN.** `scripts/perf-base-stats.mjs` builds the base ref on every CI run for the NEW-3 attribution; it was only ever used to NAME movers, never to judge. Now `inherited = base − baseline` and `branch = value − base`, and **a branch is charged only its own bytes**: it fails when its own growth consumes the whole band, or when main was clean so the overage is entirely its own — and it does NOT fail for drift it cannot fix. `inherited` is printed on **every** run, breach or not, so accumulation can never again be invisible until it is 73.6 KB deep.
- **MAIN GETS NO RELIEF, and that asymmetry is the design.** Attribution applies to a pull request only (`GITHUB_BASE_REF`, with `--as-pr`/`--as-main` for testability). A push to main is judged on what main IS, so the drift surfaces on main — where a deliberate ratchet with a stated reason is the correct answer — instead of on a stranger's branch. Without that half this would be an unbounded loosening.
- **Proven end-to-end both ways** against a real build: as a pull request the inherited breach PASSES with a named line telling the reader **not** to raise the baseline; as a push to main the identical numbers FAIL. Plus 7 unit tests covering every branch of the split, including that `classify()` — main's absolute verdict — is untouched.

### B266085 — `npm run perf:baseline-verify`: does a recorded baseline rebuild from its own commit? `[Infra / CI]` (task) #infra #perf #testing  *(minted from this branch's reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST: no item covers a REPRODUCIBILITY check of the recorded numbers; **B1178** asked the question by hand and nobody answered it for nine days. Net-new.)*
`[ ]` **✅ Done 2026-08-08 — shipped and merged. Currently REPORTING RED, honestly.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **WHY IT IS A SCRIPT AND NOT A HAND TEST.** B1178's own suggested first test was cheap — check out the commit whose numbers are recorded, build it, compare — and it went unrun for nine days because it only happens if somebody thinks to do it. It now happens on demand: for every banded metric it takes the latest `ratchetLog` entry, checks that entry's own `commit` into a throwaway worktree, builds it, and asserts the recorded value is exactly what that tree produces.
- **IT COUNTS BYTES** — a recorded integer against a measured integer, reported as a byte difference. Never a duration, a ratio or a heuristic.
- **IT FAILS ON ITS OWN DEFECT, three ways:** an entry with no `commit` → **NOT OBSERVING** (not a skip); a commit not in the clone or that will not build → **NOT OBSERVING**; and **zero metrics verified → exit 1**, so a run that checked nothing can never be mistaken for a run that checked everything and found it clean. That last one was proven first: before the commits were recovered, it reported exactly that and exited 1.
- **PROVEN BOTH WAYS ON REAL DATA, which is the point** — `notesRouteJsBytes` **reproduces exactly** (634,678 = 634,678, recorded in a different session on a different day in a different container, so the toolchain is proven reproducible ACROSS environments), and three baselines are **red** at +190 B / +988 B / +4,316 B. A guard nobody has seen fail is a guard that rots green; this one has been seen both ways before it merged.
- **NOT wired into the required `build` check**, with the reason stated: it costs one full production build per distinct commit for a property that can only change when a baseline is written. The cheap half — that every new entry carries a commit at all — is asserted for free in `test/perfBudgetPolicy.test.js` on every build. The four recovered commits are stamped `"commitSource": "recovered-2026-08-08"` so archaeology is never mistaken for provenance.

### B266086 — The drift gate's own parser was written against an invented fixture and matched NOTHING `[Infra / CI]` (bug) #infra #testing  *(minted from this branch's reserved block B266080–B266095, next free after B266085. - **HOW IT WAS FOUND — by running the check the V-item named, instead of parking it.** `V63088(b)` flagged one specific quiet failure mode: *"if the JSON reporter's `file` field is absolute rather than repo-relative, every row reports as `absent`… that is the one failure mode here that is quiet, so it is the first thing to check."* Driving a real `--reporter=json` run locally showed **it was real, and there were TWO of them, not one.**
- **THE TWO SHAPE FACTS THE PARSER HAD WRONG.** (1) `spec.file` is relative to `config.rootDir` — the testDir — so it reads `pond-outlet-clear.spec.js`, while every id in this repo is repo-relative. (2) The **top-level suite of each file IS the file** (`title === file`), so including it in the title chain printed the filename twice: `pond-outlet-clear.spec.js:63 › pond-outlet-clear.spec.js › Pond outlet fields …`.

It fails **loud rather than false-green** — the `novel` path is fatal, the `absent` path is not — which is the one mercy, and it is exactly why the gate is built to fail on a shape it does not recognise. It would still have been useless noise.
- **THE ROOT CAUSE IS THE FIXTURE, AND THAT IS THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING.** `collectCases()` was written against a **hand-written** report helper in its own test file, and 16 tests passed against it. **A fixture you invented can only ever confirm what you already believed.** This is the same shape as the three harnesses this repo has already caught being silently blind — the undisposed `ElementHandle`, the seeder that made B749's cost path unreachable, the growth harness whose plan B was plan A truncated. *When the instrument and reality disagree, the instrument is the thing on trial.*
- **THE FIX + THE GUARD.** `collectCases(report, { root })` re-prefixes `spec.file` from `config.rootDir` and skips any suite that names its own file. `test/fixtures/playwright-report.sample.json` is **captured from a real `npx playwright test --reporter=json` run** (only the bulky per-result payloads dropped) and five new tests pin both facts — including the end-to-end one that would have caught this: the instrument's own output is matched against the committed ledger with nothing hand-written in between.
- **RE-PROVEN, all three mutations, on the corrected parser and in the real reporter shape:** true failure set → **exit 0, `29 ran · 29 failed · 29 on the ledger`** (before the fix that last number was **0**) · one fabricated new failure → **exit 1**, named · one ledgered case flipped to passing → **exit 1**, named.

- **FINDING 2 — the LOCAL lane's sandbox artefacts were real artefacts, exactly as predicted.** Seven rows passed on a real runner: `contour-hover-elevation:246`, `dim-callout-edit:225`, `dock-zone-host-run:163`, `parcel-tools-menu:178`, `road-branch-and-label:100`, `wall-kid-drift:137`, `wall-kid-drift:190`. The ledger's own seeding note called this and chose it deliberately over starting empty; the stale-entry half turned each into a one-line shrink. **local 32 → 25.**
- **THE DEFECT — I WOULD HAVE REBUILT THE NOISE MACHINE.** Five ci rows FAILED in #41 (after two retries each) and PASSED in #42: `canvas-gis-identify:61` and four `layer-point-hover-identify` cases. All reach an **external GIS service** and flip with that service's availability, not with the code. Under the shipped "a passing ledger row is fatal" rule, the gate goes red on every wobble in somebody else's server. **I wrote the warning myself, in this gate's own header, before I had the data: *a ledger that churns is a ledger people stop reading.***
- **THE FIX, and the reason it is not an amnesty.** An `intermittent` row's PASS is REPORTED, not fatal. It is still on the ledger, still counts toward the debt, and confers nothing on a case that is not already recorded — a brand-new failure is novel whatever anyone claims about it. **The marker demands EVIDENCE**: `{ passedRun, failedRun }`, two run numbers that actually observed both outcomes. `validateLedger()` refuses a marker without them, refuses one citing the same run twice, and the gate **refuses to judge a run at all against a malformed ledger**. Seven new tests, including that an ordinary row passing is still fatal.
- **FINDING 3 — A REGRESSION I INTRODUCED, caught by the same run.** `--reporter=list,json` **REPLACES** the config's `[["list"], ["html"]]` rather than adding to it, so `playwright-report/` was never written and the upload step reported *"No files were found with the provided path"* in **both** jobs. The artifact is where a reader goes for the failure detail the issue body deliberately no longer quotes, so making the alarm quieter while silently deleting the detail would have been a net LOSS of information. Fixed to `list,json,html`.
- **RE-PROVEN by replaying run #42's actual results against the updated ledger: exit 0**, five intermittent passes reported, no new failures, `30 case(s) remain KNOWN-RED`.

### B233153 — A detention pond on the Bain plan answers NEITHER a double-click NOR a single click — **REPRODUCED, MECHANISM CAPTURED, FIXED** `[Site Planner / selection]` (bug) #site-planner #selection #ui #pond  *(filed 2026-08-07 from the owner's live V17005 report; capture recorded and fix shipped 2026-08-08. No new number — B233153 was already open and this is the same defect, per DEDUPE-FIRST. **NEVER-PARK disposition, named as the rule requires: REPRODUCE IT AND FIX IT.** The one thing this item is NOT is another null.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — shipped 2026-08-08, and CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-08-09 on the owner's own machine. V75312 PASSED on all four parts (a/b/c/d) on planyr.io, signed in, Bain / "Concept - Original"; the full evidence is on that entry in `VERIFICATION-DONE.md`.** The root double-click resolver treats the handle layer as transparent to feature IDENTIFICATION — fixed for every element type at once, not for the pond. Reshaping was measured as a COUNT and is intact (one vertex drag moved 2 of 14 path numbers; a body drag moved 14 of 14), and both test writes were undone — his ring is unchanged at 7 vertices, max normalised delta 0.00000 after a reload.
**⛔ NOT CLOSED BY THIS: the 6×12 px road stub `e79463haroul` on the same plan.** The live sweep that discharged (d) found 35 of 36 reachable features opening Properties, and that one stub failing. It is a DIFFERENT class — the feature is smaller than its own chrome, so the size ratio rather than the vertex density — and the control run for exactly that reason proves this fix is working: on a large road, a press point covered by its own endpoint handle still resolves to the road and still opens Properties. Filed and fixed as **B278576 / B278577**.
- Verify: live → **V75312** (`Blocker: real-data` + `Blocker: auth` — the symptom was reported on Bain / "Concept A — Quiddity Hydrologic" and that is where it closes). **V30160 is CLOSED — CAPTURED**, which was its whole job.

**THE CAPTURE (owner's machine, planyr.io signed in, Bain / "Concept A — Quiddity Hydrologic", main @ #959).** A capture-phase listener at the svg root, one double-click on the pond water:

```
pointerdown#1 → path{url(#grad-water)}          ← the pond's own fill; it SELECTS, blue grips go 4 → 16
pointerup#1, click#1 → same path
pointerdown#2 → rect{transparent}               ← rect[data-export="skip"][data-testid="vtx-handle"],
click#2, dblclick → rect{transparent}             18×18, inside g[data-export="skip"][data-handle-layer="1"]
```

**That rect is one of the POND'S OWN VERTEX HANDLES.** Selecting the pond mounts the handle layer (41 nodes) and one 18px transparent hit square lands exactly on the point that was pressed. **The first press summons the thing that blocks the second.** Press 2 therefore never reaches the pond: the double-tap cannot pair (`isDoubleTap` is called from the feature's own `pointerdown`, which never runs) and the native `dblclick` retargets. Zero console output — the failure is completely silent.

**RULED OUT, with the readings.** The pond group is `cursor: move` and `pointer-events: auto`, and `elementFromPoint` resolves to the pond BEFORE press 1 — not locked, not pointer-inert, not covered beforehand. The leading hypothesis on the filed item (an exception while rendering the pond's Properties) is refuted: nothing threw.

**WHY SIX SANDBOX VARIANTS MISSED IT, and this is the part worth more than the fix.** The variable is not the SHAPE — polygon, `det` record and expansion baseline were all already covered. It is **VERTEX COUNT AGAINST HANDLE SIZE AT THE PROBE POINT.** A real pond ring has dozens of vertices so its basin edge is peppered with 18px hit squares; every seeded variant was a FOUR-vertex ring whose grips sit at four distant corners, nowhere near a centre probe. That is exactly how a green 19/19 certified a pond nobody could click.

**THE FIX — AT THE RESOLVER, NOT ON THE POND.** `lib/featureTarget.js`'s `resolveDoubleClickTarget` used to answer `null` the moment a handle-layer node was on top ("a handle owns the press"). It now **skips** it: a vertex handle is chrome belonging to the selected feature, never a feature. One rule, and every element type that renders grips is closed at once — a pond-shaped special case would have closed one report and left the parcel, the polygon element, every markup with vertex grips and every future grip open. It is the same rule `pressIsOverElementBody` beside it has always applied.
- **DRAGGING IS UNTOUCHED, and that is asserted, not asserted-about.** Grips keep their own `pointerEvents` and their own `onPointerDown`. What changed is *which feature was double-clicked* — identification, never delivery.
- **CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS gains its third instance** (after B1174's measurement chips and B1327's acreage badge), with the corollary now written into the named rule: **chrome mounted BY the first press is invisible to any check that reads the DOM before the interaction.**

**THE INSTRUMENT, which is the other half of the deliverable.** Nothing in this repo could observe the middle of a gesture. Two things fix that permanently:
- **`window.__plannerHitTarget(x, y)`** — E2E-gated, read-only, nulled on unmount like every other planner probe. It asks the app's OWN resolver what a double-click at a point would address RIGHT NOW. A harness that re-implemented the rule would test its own copy of it (the "a second hit-test is free to disagree" trap `featureTarget.js`'s header names), and a harness that agrees with itself while the app fails is how this shipped green.
- **THE TWO-PRESS INVARIANT** — press once, re-ask, require the same feature. That is the only probe shape that can see chrome which does not exist until the gesture is half-finished, and it would have caught this AND the road dimension number (B50010).

**AND A SECOND HARNESS DEFECT THE CAPTURE EXPOSED, which had blinded the whole audit.** `audit-doubleclick-properties.mjs` drove its double-clicks as two bare `down/up` pairs. **Chromium synthesises a native `dblclick` only when the second press is stamped `clickCount: 2`** — two bare pairs leave the counter at 1 and no `dblclick` is ever delivered. So every row was passing on the reconstructed double-TAP alone and the root resolver — the half that carries a real user double-click — **was never exercised at all**. That is precisely the half a grip kills. The presses are still separate (pointer capture must release between them); only the stamp changed.

**GUARDS, each mutation-proven.**
- `test/featureTarget.test.js` (29): the transparency rule, the owner's captured stack verbatim, a stack of handles, a handle that is all there is, and a handle that must not mask a feature painted between it and the one below. **Pre-fix rule ⇒ 4 red.** Plus source guards on the hook and on the hit square keeping its own `onPointerDown`.
- `ui-audit/audit-doubleclick-properties.mjs`: a new **44-vertex `surveyRing` pond fixture** (FIXTURE TRAP 8 in its header), the **two-press invariant on every feature**, and **HALF FIVE — the grip-covered press**, which selects a feature, FINDS a point where one of its own grips lands over its own body, deselects, and double-clicks there. **121/121 · 123/123 (`--labels`) · 78/78 (`--locked`); pre-fix ⇒ 39 red.** Both new halves are COUNTED and a zero fails the run, so they cannot rot green.
- `e2e/chrome-swallows-press.spec.js`: two cases on a seeded surveyed-ring pond. **BEHAVIOURAL** (pre-fix resolver ⇒ red) and **REGRESSION GUARD: a vertex handle still drags its vertex** — which counts how many ring vertices moved, because "the geometry changed" also passes when the press falls THROUGH an inert grip and moves the whole pond (mutant: `44 of 44 vertices` ⇒ red).

**Bundle cost: +0.3 KB on `bundle.siteRouteJsBytes`, measured by building the branch with and without the source change (2379.9 → 2380.2 KB).** The audit also reports +10.6 KB against the recorded baseline on this branch WITHOUT this change — that is inherited drift from merged work, not this item's, and it is stated rather than absorbed. The 0.3 KB is the read-only `__plannerHitTarget` hook, and it stays: it IS the instrument, and there is no cheaper way to observe the middle of a gesture than asking the app what it would do.

**Regressions checked, not assumed.** `npm test` 9175/9175 · `npm run lint` 0 errors · **99 e2e tests green** across every spec that exercises a double-click (click-contract, click-behavior, dblclick-properties, chrome-swallows-press, dim-callout-edit, markup-reach, measure-drag-props, measure-select, building-reshape, parcel-select-toggle, parcel-chip-move-delete, inspector-close, floating-panels, review-click-contract, ctrlz-undo, the three road specs, clipboard ×2, canvas ×2, pond-outlet-clear, single-occupancy-dock).

**Verify: live** — V75312.

### B290241 — A Colorado deed was rotated onto grid north by the TEXAS cone: 75 ft of drift, stated as a confident number `[Site Planner / coordinates]` (bug) #site-planner #coordinates  *(filed + shipped 2026-08-09 from the Colorado missing-data audit. Minted from this branch's reserved block B290240–B290255 against origin/main d36f98d. **DEDUPE-FIRST** — searched `gridConvergence`, `deedAlign`, `basis of bearings`, `B625`, `B1106`, `B1109`, `B1112`: B625 owns the empirical fit's rotational alias, B1106/B1112 own the grid-vs-ground factor. Nobody had ever asked which ZONE the convergence came from. New item.)*
`[x]` `deedAlign.gridConvergenceDeg` computed the basis-of-bearings correction from the hardcoded EPSG:2278 Texas South Central cone at every point on earth.
- Verify: sandbox — **VERIFIED on the real screen 2026-08-09** (`ui-audit/verify-colorado-deed-north.mjs`, 14/14).
- **The defect.** Convergence is γ = n·(λ − λ₀) — a function of the ZONE's cone constant and central meridian, i.e. of exactly the two things that change when you leave the zone. Measured at the owner's Johnstown ground: the Texas cone answered **−2.885°** where Colorado North (2231) answers **+0.378°**. A 3.26° error, rotating a plotted deed **75 ft off across a 1,320 ft boundary run** — and the app announced it in a toast as *"rotated 2.89° counter-clockwise for the State Plane grid convergence here"*. Every Colorado county measured the same way (Denver −2.923 vs +0.320 · Fort Collins −2.967 vs +0.270 · Colorado Springs −2.713 vs +0.590), and Chicago ground turned by **5.55°**.
- **The fix.** `resolveZone({state, county, lat, lon})` — county first (Colorado's zone boundaries ARE county lines), the coarse point envelope second — then the convergence in THAT zone. Texas resolves to `tx_sc`, whose generic Lambert engine reproduces `shared/coordinates/index.js` bit-for-bit, so Texas is unchanged by construction (asserted with a 10-dp equality against the pre-fix implementation inlined in the test). This makes `shared/coordinates/statePlane.js` its first production consumer; it rides the lazy deed chunk (`deedLazy.js`), never the boot path.
- **CONTRACT CHANGE, deliberate:** unresolvable input now returns **null**, not 0. 0 is a real answer here ("you are on the central meridian, nothing to correct") and the caller ROTATES A SURVEYED BOUNDARY by what it returns; the old sentinel collided with the meaningful value and `SitePlanner`'s `Math.abs(conv) < 0.01` read one as the other. The caller gained its own branch and a named message, and refuses to rotate.
- **On screen** (real browser, no sign-in, no GIS): Johnstown turns **+0.3784°** and says *"rotated 0.38° clockwise"*; Denver **+0.3204°**; Katy **+1.5598°**, unchanged; Chicago turns **0.000000°** and says *"Planyr doesn't carry a State Plane zone for this location — so there is no grid rotation it can compute honestly."*
- Guards, both **mutation-proven**: `test/coloradoAudit.test.js` (restore the Texas cone → 5 red; restore `return 0` → the honest-null test red) and `ui-audit/verify-colorado-deed-north.mjs` (restore the Texas cone → **6 red**, including Chicago turning 5.55°). Texas golden master green; 9,646/9,646 unit tests green.
- Bundle delta measured with and without: **+0.8 KB** on the largest chunk, +5.5 KB total. (The budget's +22.5 KB reading is mostly pre-existing drift on main, which already sits at 1495.1 KB against a recorded 1473.4 KB baseline. Baseline NOT ratcheted.)

### B290242 — `statePlane` could not read the app's own `co_`-prefixed county keys, so Denver resolved to the wrong zone `[Site Planner / coordinates]` (bug) #site-planner #coordinates  *(filed + shipped 2026-08-09, found while proving B290241 — the new test failed on the resolver, not on the formula. Minted from this branch's block.)*
`[x]` `statePlane.slugCounty` stripped `city|and|county|of` but not the `co_` ROUTING prefix, which is the form a plan actually persists.
- Verify: sandbox — proven by the same real-browser harness (Denver resolves through its county key).
- **The defect.** `counties.js` prefixes Colorado keys (`co_denver`, `co_weld`, `co_elpaso`) because Texas and Colorado both have an El Paso and a Jefferson, and that prefixed key is what a plan's `county` field carries. `zoneForCounty("CO", "co_denver")` slugged to `codenver`, matched nothing, returned null — and `resolveZone` fell through to the COARSE point envelope, which this module's own comment says cannot separate the interleaved Front Range counties. **Measured: Denver resolved to Colorado NORTH (2231) instead of Central (2232).** `coloradoRegions.js`'s own slug already stripped the prefix, so one county resolved to a regime and to no zone.
- **The fix.** One `.replace(/^co_/, "")`, matching `coloradoRegions.js` exactly. Mutation: drop it → 2 red.
- Worth knowing: this made `resolveZone` silently reachable only by its coarse fallback for every Colorado county, which is why it had never been noticed — the fallback returns a plausible zone.

- **THE REPORT.** Bain / "Concept - Original", 109 acres, the whole site fitting the viewport, scale bar reading 0–1,000 FEET. The green `+` and red `−` rendered **at full size** over Buildings 3 and 4 — the largest objects on a plan he was trying to READ — while a bump-out is a few pixels wide at that scale, so the control covered far more of the building than the thing it edits. His words: *"the plus and minus buttons here show up way too early… I shouldn't be zoomed out this far and they show up. I should have to zoom in more."*
- **⛔ AUDIT-FIRST — THE EXISTING GATE IS NOT BROKEN; IT ANSWERS A DIFFERENT QUESTION, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING.** `FEAT_BTN_MIN_PX = 72` (B225) asks whether the BUILDING's wall is big enough on screen to seat the cluster without it spilling past the footprint. That is a real question about the CONTAINER, and a 900 ft industrial building clears it at almost any zoom a site plan is read at — so on a large building the controls arm from the moment the plan fits the screen. Nothing was regressing; the gate simply never asked whether the EDIT was legible. Both gates now run, and neither replaces the other.
- **THE THRESHOLD, DERIVED AND STATED — the owner asked for the number by name.** Gate on FEET PER PIXEL, so the rule is absolute zoom rather than a fraction of the building and reads the same on a 30-acre site and a 900-acre one. The smallest feature these controls place is a corner bump-out, `DOGEAR_W` × `DOGEAR_D` = **55 ft × 60 ft**. Require its short side to render at **44 px** — comfortably larger than the 18 px control disc, so the control can never be wider than its own subject. That fixes the floor at **44 ÷ 55 = 0.80 px per foot, i.e. 1.25 FEET PER PIXEL**. At his whole-site view (well under half that) they are gone; at the floor a bump-out is 44 × 48 px and a 500 ft building spans about 400 px, which is a zoom at which placing a dock zone or a bump-out is a meaningful act.
- **FADE, NOT POP — and the boundary that keeps it honest.** Above the floor the cluster ramps from faint to full over the next 35% of zoom, so it arrives softly instead of snapping on at one wheel notch. **Opacity is presentation and never a hit-test gate:** the controls are fully clickable the whole time they are on screen, because a half-faded control that ignored a press would be its own bug. Asserted both ways.
- **It is asked with `rppf`, the RENDER view, never `view.ppf`.** Mid-gesture those differ (the view anchor, B1440/B1449), and fading against the settled zoom while the picture is at another one is exactly the mixing that rule exists to prevent. A source assertion pins it, because no visual test can see the difference at rest.
