### B427411 — Four corner radii, one scale: the chrome had eight, picked by eye, months apart `[Site Planner / UI · shared]` (task) #site-planner #ui #infra  *(owner chat block 2026-08-13, NEW-4, verbatim: "Fix it as a SYSTEM, not per component" · "a pill plus roughly two or three steps" · "A nested control inside a container must relate to its parent's radius deliberately rather than by coincidence" · "Report the scale you chose and every place you changed, and call out anything you deliberately left alone" · "Do them consistently; do not invent a second convention." Minted **B427411** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `radius`, `borderRadius`, `RADIUS`, `token`, `controls.jsx`, `B657`, `B316`, `B341`: **B657-5B** created `shared/ui/controls.jsx`'s partial `{control, pill, panel}` scale, which this ADOPTS rather than replaces; **B316–B320/B341** are the theme-token system, which is the precedent for how a shared value is mirrored to CSS. No item has ever owned corner radius as a system. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.** `src/shared/ui/radius.js` + the `--radius-*` CSS mirror.
- Verify: sandbox (harness sweeps EVERY visible element's four computed corners against the scale: 208 off-scale pre-fix → 0)
- **THE SCALE — four steps, and the numbers are NOT invented.** `pill 999 · sm 6 · md 8 · lg 12`. `8` was already the single most common radius in `MapFinder.jsx` (9 of its 23 sites) and `shared/ui/controls.jsx` already declared `{ control: 8, pill: 999, panel: 12 }` — a partial scale that never spread past that file and the Notes workspace. A rounder-looking 10/14 was drafted first and dropped: it would have been a FOURTH opinion, and it broke `test/notesModule.test.js`, which regex-parses those digits and cross-checks seven Notes components that hand-copy them. Adopting what most of the chrome already agreed on makes this a consolidation rather than a restyle, and the `controls.jsx` ↔ Notes contract survives untouched.
- **THE NESTING RULE is a function, not a number at a call site.** `nestedIn(outer, gap)` returns the concentric inner radius. Its special case is the one that was actually broken: inside a PILL, a control running the height of the bar is itself a pill — the search bar is a 42-tall pill and its Go / Select-parcels buttons were boxy chips floating inside a fully round container, which is exactly the "different edge shapes for the Find a site one" the owner described.
- **EVERY PLACE CHANGED.** `MapFinder.jsx` (all 23 sites) · `shared/ui/AppHeader.jsx` · `app/AccountControl.jsx` (the "Michael Butler" chip he named — 99/10/7 → pill/lg/sm) · `components/AuthPanel.jsx` · `shared/ui/CloudSyncBadge.jsx` · `shared/ui/ProjectBreadcrumb.jsx` · `components/JurisdictionBadge.jsx` · `components/LayerPanel.jsx` (8 sites) · `src/index.css` (the four tokens + a Leaflet override).
- **⛔ AND ONE THAT ONLY A COMPUTED-STYLE SWEEP COULD FIND: Leaflet's own stylesheet.** `.leaflet-touch .leaflet-bar a:first-child { border-radius: 2px }` has specificity (0,3,1) and outranked a two-class override; the zoom control kept its own corners no matter what the component said. Fixed by matching specificity, not by `!important`.
- **DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, as asked.** (a) The **seven Notes components** that hand-copy `{ control: 8, pill: 999 }` — they already agree with the scale numerically, and `test/notesModule.test.js` guards that agreement; repointing them is a separate, mechanical change with its own risk and no visible benefit. The panel is honest (the empty state says "Load screenshot…" and explains what an aerial is); the heading simply arrives before the thing it names.

  this is not re-audited from the same one-line report.** The brief asked which of four things was
  true; two are, and the two serious ones are refuted rather than merely unobserved:
  - **NOT (a), an unscoped query.** There is no references table and no references query. Both
    reference kinds are fields INSIDE each plan's own `sites.data` jsonb — `underlay` (the aerial)
    and `sheetOverlays` (sheet references) — read by `cloudSync.loadSite` as
    `from("sites").select("data, version").eq("id", id)`. A single-row fetch by primary key cannot
    return one row for every project.
  - **(b) IS TRUE where an aerial exists — 58 of 71 plans**, each carrying its OWN object in its OWN
    row, with its own georeference. Intended: `newPlanSameParcel` copies `underlay: src.underlay` so
    a second concept of the same land opens over the same imagery.
  - **(c) IS TRUE for the heading itself** — proven behaviourally, not by reading source. Three plans
    differing in EXACTLY ONE fact (no `underlay` key · `underlay: null` · a real aerial) all print
    "Aerial backdrop"; only the empty arms show "Load screenshot…" and only the real arm has the
    opacity/lock controls.
  - **NOT (d), a cross-project leak.** Nine `src` values repeat across plans, and every repeat is the
    SAME GROUND rather than a shared row. `fromMap` aerials store a DERIVED Esri `/export` URL built
    from the site's bbox, so identical ground yields an identical string BY CONSTRUCTION. The two
    repeats that cross a project NAME were checked individually and both are one site entered twice:
    `FM 359 RD, Fulshear` / `Woods Road` share `groupId smsrpaiqu5sv` and origin 29.74838/-95.92482
    (the B487600 restore); `2221 E LAMAR BLVD STE 790` / `4050 CR 50 JOHNSTOWN` share origin
    40.34597/-104.97794 — the same Weld County parcel, the first named by the `appraisal.js` situs
    defect that read Forestar's Arlington office address off `ADDRESS1`.
- **⛔ THE #1040/#1043 REF-COUNT INTERACTION, ANSWERED EXPLICITLY AS ASKED — NO INTERACTION, ON TWO
  INDEPENDENT GROUNDS.** The concern was that a leaked row could be counted as a legitimate holder of
  a stored file and refuse a delete that should proceed, or mis-decide which file is safe to remove.
  - **First: there is nothing for the aerial to hold.** `sharedAssetRefs.planAssetKeys` indexes an
    underlay by `storageKey` and `idbKey`. Across all 71 production plans, **0 carry either** — every
    aerial is a `fromMap` URL, which references no stored object in either tier. The aerial
    contributes no entries to the index at all today.
  - **Second: the index cannot admit a foreign row even if it did.** `collectAssetRefs` walks the plan
    list and attributes each key to the plan whose own record names it, so a holder set is by
    construction a set of real plan ids. There is no path by which one plan's row is counted under
    another's identity — which is exactly what makes the duplicate-plan case (Goose Creek ×4,
    Silvestri ×5, Bain ×3) come out RIGHT: those siblings genuinely each hold the asset, so a refusal
    to release is the #1040 fix working, not a false positive.

    touched, and no stored bytes were read for deletion or removed during the audit.

### B532112 — A probe must answer a KNOWN case correctly before it is trusted on an unknown one `[ui-audit / harness]` (task) #testing  *(owner instruction 2026-08-14, after the B519152/B525632 session's own diagnostic returned two false positives: "Write it as a checkable rule rather than a caution." Minted **B532112** from this branch's reserved block B532112-B532127 against `origin/main` d4a88a0. DEDUPE-FIRST - searched Open / Verify / Done for `positive control`, `known-good`, `teeth`, `mutation check`, `harness`, `instrument`, `FOREGROUND-OR-VOID`, `DRIVER-SCROLL`, `SYNTHETIC-KEYS`, `vacuity`: the repo has the NEGATIVE half everywhere (a guard must be proven RED - NO-ONE-OWNS-A-COMPOSITE's teeth proof, VIEW-INDEPENDENT-ONCE section 6, mintGateE2E) and **no item owns the POSITIVE half**. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — the clause is ADOPTED into `DRIVER-SCROLL-IS-NOT-APP-SCROLL` as clause 6 (owner decision 2026-08-14).** Before a probe is trusted on the case under investigation, point it at a case whose answer is already known and require it to report that known answer. A probe that cannot pass the known case is measuring something other than what it claims.
- Verify: sandbox
- Origin: filed 2026-08-14 from owner chat.
- **⛔ THIS IS THE POSITIVE HALF OF A RULE THIS REPO ONLY HAS THE NEGATIVE HALF OF, and that asymmetry is the finding.** Every existing discipline here proves a guard can go **RED** on a known-bad build - the teeth proof, the mutation check, `mintGateE2E`'s rejection path, VIEW-INDEPENDENT-ONCE's "a registered memo that was never OBSERVED fails". **Nothing requires it to go GREEN on a known-good one.** Both failures below were green-side: the probe reported a defect in code that was correct.
- **THE TWO FALSE POSITIVES, recorded because a rule without its evidence reads as theory.** Both came from `ui-audit/diagnose-aerial-backdrop-row.mjs` / `verify-aerial-empty-state-copy.mjs` in one session:
  1. **A SELECTOR THAT LEFT THE THING IT WAS ASKING ABOUT.** A page-wide `document.querySelectorAll('label input[type=range]')` swept in a slider belonging to a DIFFERENT panel, so the aerial row was reported as carrying a control it does not have. Fix: scope every query to the element under test (walk up from the row's own label), never the document.
  2. **A CONTROL READ IN A STATE THE USER WOULD NOT SEE IT IN.** The aerial row's opacity slider only renders once the row is SELECTED, so a probe that read it collapsed reported a working row broken. Fix: put the surface into the state the assertion is about before measuring it.
  - A third, on the same day, is the same species one level up: the position check compared the empty state against the OCCUPIED one and reported those two branches' **intended** difference as a regression - a control that was never a control.
- **WHAT ACTUALLY CAUGHT ALL THREE was a known-good arm sitting beside the unknown one.** The with-an-aerial arm was expected to be green and was; that it stayed green while the others failed is what localised each fault to the probe rather than to the app. **The arm was there by luck of the question's shape, not by rule** - the audit needed a three-way comparison anyway. That is the gap this closes.
- **THE CHECKABLE FORM, so this is not a caution:** a harness asserting a property must include at least one arm whose expected value is known INDEPENDENTLY of the code under test, and must fail if that arm does not report its known value. A run in which only the unknown arms are exercised is VACUOUS and must say so rather than print a score. (`ui-audit/` already has the vocabulary: `MUST_BE_PRESENT` in `count-pond-invocations`, and the vacuity guards in `verify-hidden-content-behaviour`.)
- **⛔ HOUSE RULES: YES, AND AS A CLAUSE ON AN EXISTING RULE - NOT A NEW NUMBERED RULE.** It belongs beside **`DRIVER-SCROLL-IS-NOT-APP-SCROLL`**, which is the closest fit and already carries the right machinery: that rule is *"the harness's own ACTION produced the reading"* and this is *"the harness's own QUERY produced the reading"* - the same species, and its remedy is already the discriminator pattern (drive the same control a second, known way and compare the two answers). It also joins the family **`SYNTHETIC-KEYS-DONT-EDIT`** names explicitly - *"three ways for a harness to believe its own instrument"* (with `FOREGROUND-OR-VOID`) - which would become four. **The `/CLAUDE.md` edit IS made, on the owner's explicit adoption** (2026-08-14, verbatim: *"yes, add the clause to DRIVER-SCROLL-IS-NOT-APP-SCROLL and ship it in that same PR… your reasoning for putting it there rather than minting a new rule is right and I am adopting it"*). It landed as **clause 6** of that rule, keeping the check-not-caution framing, the known-case-before-unknown-case formulation, and — at his instruction — the red/green asymmetry observation in the RULE TEXT rather than only on this item.
- **Stopping rule — MET:** adopted into `DRIVER-SCROLL-IS-NOT-APP-SCROLL` (clause 6). The machine check for the vacuous-run case is deliberately NOT bundled: the clause names the existing vocabulary (`MUST_BE_PRESENT`, the `verify-hidden-content-behaviour` vacuity guards) and making it universal is a sweep across 347 harnesses, which is its own item and not a rider on a rule edit. Stated rather than silently dropped.

### B637232 — Indent/outdent ignored a multi-row selection on BOTH entry points — only one row ever moved `[Scheduler]` (bug) #scheduler #ui #selection #keyboard  *(owner report, verbatim: "I literally highlighted all these and then press shift alt right, and it only indented the top one... that specific bug is even worse when you try and write click and then press outdent or indent. It, like, only works on the specific cell that you indented or outdented." Minted **B637232** from this branch's reserved block B637232–B637247 against `origin/main` 93da621. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `indentTaskById`, `outdentTaskById`, `multi-row indent`, `selection range`, `B255`: **B255** dedup'd the keyboard path onto the SAME by-id helpers the context menu already called — one source per direction — but neither that helper nor the context menu ever consulted the selection range, so both entry points shared this exact defect. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — shipped and headless-verified this session (44/44 checks in `ui-audit/verify-schedule-indent-outdent-delete.mjs`, incl. 3 mutation proofs).** `public/sequence/index.html`'s keyboard handler called `indentTaskById(selectedId)`/`outdentTaskById(selectedId)`, and the right-click menu called the same by-id helpers with `taskCtx.task.id` — both read a SINGLE task id and never looked at `selRange`. **Measured live before the fix** (throwaway repro against a fixture mirroring the owner's screenshot — "ALTA & Topo Survey" → "PI" → 6 children): drag-selecting rows 11–16 via the ID column, then pressing Alt+Shift+Right, moved only whichever row `selectedId` happened to be (the drag/shift-click ANCHOR — the LAST row entered during a top-to-bottom ID-column drag, or the FIRST-clicked row if the selection was made with shift-click/shift-arrow, since that branch deliberately never updates `selectedId`). Right-clicking ANY row inside the same 6-row selection and choosing "Indent →" from the context menu moved only THAT row, ignoring the other five.
- **THE FIX, one shared resolution rule for both entry points.** `rowRangeSelIds()` (new) returns every task id in the current row selection regardless of which COLUMNS it spans — unlike the pre-existing `fullRowSelIds()`, which requires a full-column span because IT exists to disambiguate "delete rows" from "clear cell content"; indent/outdent has no such ambiguity, so it never needed that restriction. `structuralTargets(anchorId)` resolves "the row range if the anchor is inside one, else just the anchor" — one function, used identically by the keyboard handler (anchor = `selectedId`) and the context menu (anchor = `taskCtx.task.id`), so the two entry points can never again diverge into "acts on the selection" vs. "acts on one row." Both call into new `indentSelectionByIds`/`outdentSelectionByIds`, which replace `indentTaskById`/`outdentTaskById` entirely (renamed, not wrapped) and dispatch to pure, unit-tested `indentSelection`/`outdentSelection` (mirrored in `ui-audit/stress/schedule-tree-ops.mjs` for `test/scheduleIndentOutdentDelete.test.js`, which also source-pins both call sites so a revert to a bare `selectedId`/`taskCtx.task.id` call fails CI).
- **SEMANTICS DECIDED, not left emergent (Smartsheet-style):**
  - **A contiguous block moves as ONE unit.** Only "root" rows — selected rows whose PARENT is not itself selected — get reparented; a selected row whose parent IS also selected is left untouched, so a parent-plus-its-own-children selection preserves relative depth for free (the child's `parentId` is never touched at all).
  - **INDENT is all-or-nothing, gated on the TOPMOST selected row.** Every root row moves to the SAME new parent (the row immediately above the topmost row, at the topmost row's own level — the pre-existing single-row eligibility rule, unchanged). If the topmost row has no eligible predecessor (e.g. it's the first child of its parent), the WHOLE block is a clean no-op — there is no sane partial result when every root row shares one destination. Verified live: selecting a parent's entire 6-child block (whose topmost is the parent's very first child) and indenting moves nothing.
  - **OUTDENT has no shared destination, so it is per-row: rows already at depth 0 are skipped individually, everything else that can outdent does, independently.** Adjacent root rows sharing the same current parent are promoted as ONE batch, not one row at a time — moving them individually re-derives "the end of the old parent's remaining subtree" against a shrinking array and reverses their relative order (measured while designing this: row A moved first landed AFTER row B, which moved second, exactly backwards). Verified live for a genuinely mixed selection (one depth-0 row + one deeper root row in the same contiguous range): the deeper one promotes, the depth-0 one is left exactly where it is, neither blocks the other.
  - **Non-contiguous selection (rows 11, 14, 16 with gaps) cannot occur and needed no design decision** — the app's entire selection model (`selRange`) is a single rectangle of rows × columns; there is no ctrl-click or other discontiguous multi-select anywhere in this codebase.
- **B463072-shaped landmine, MEASURED live, not assumed — and it does NOT reproduce here.** A leaf with a typed duration (`durValue`/`durUnit`) that becomes a parent for the first time correctly shows its ROLLED span in the duration cell (B463072 already fixed this display path — `fmtTaskDuration` reads `isSummary`). Reversed the same operation (outdented every child back out, making the row childless again) and read the duration cell again: it cleanly restored the ORIGINAL typed value, because `cascadeDates` re-derives a leaf's span from `durValue`/`durUnit` the instant a row drops out of the `parentIds` set on the next recompute pass — and `rollupParentDates` never touches `durValue`/`durUnit` in the first place, so nothing was ever stale to begin with. This self-heal is a property of the existing engine, not new code from this fix, but it applies equally to any operation (indent/outdent/delete-promote) that changes who has children, and it is now asserted in both the live harness (`ui-audit/verify-schedule-indent-outdent-delete.mjs` section E1) and unit tests.
- **Health rollup, MEASURED for both directions.** A row that GAINS a red-health descendant via indent rolls up to red once collapsed; a group that LOSES its only red child via outdent improves to gray — both read straight off the existing `computeRolledHealth`/`rolledHealthMap`, which is a pure function recomputed from the CURRENT tree on every render, so reparenting needs no special-case code to stay correct. Verified live (`ui-audit/verify-schedule-indent-outdent-delete.mjs` section E2).
- **ONE UNDO STEP for the whole batch.** `indentSelectionByIds`/`outdentSelectionByIds` each call `setData` exactly once per invocation (structurally: one function body, one `setData` call, source-pinned), which is what makes the app's existing "one `history` push per `data` change" undo mechanism restore the whole multi-row move in a single Ctrl+Z — verified live for both a 4-row indent and a 3-row outdent.
- **Predecessor/successor links survive trivially** — indent/outdent only ever change `parentId`; no task's `predecessors` array is touched.
- **`canOutdent`, used to disable the context menu's "Outdent ←" item, now reflects the WHOLE resolved target set** (computed at the call site against `structuralTargets`), not just the single right-clicked row — so a multi-row right-click correctly disables Outdent only when every targeted row is already at depth 0, rather than reading just the clicked row's own depth.
- **Adjacent cases, stated tested-or-not:** single row ✅ live+unit · contiguous block ✅ live+unit · non-contiguous — **not reachable, no code path exists for it** (see above) · selection spanning different depths ✅ live+unit (parent + its own children) · block at depth 0 outdenting ✅ live+unit (single row and a mixed multi-row selection) · a parent with children ✅ live (health rollup, B463072 check) · a milestone (duration 0) ✅ unit (indents/outdents identically to any other row; nothing here reads duration) · a leaf with a typed duration becoming a parent, and back ✅ live (section E1).
- **Nothing shipped here turns a check red that wasn't already meant to** — the three mutation proofs (single-anchor revert, the button-size revert used for the sibling delete item below, the promote transitive-walk revert) all correctly flip red, and no existing assertion was weakened to make a new one pass.
- Bundle: `public/sequence/index.html` is a static file Vite copies verbatim (never enters the JS module graph) — there is no `schedulerRouteJsBytes` budget to report a `--compare` delta against, per this branch's own brief.
- Regressions checked: `npm test` — 578 files / 11933 tests, 0 new failures (2 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change — `test/hiddenContentReads.test.js` and `test/docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js` — both reference historical git commit hashes not reachable in this sandbox's shallow clone; neither touches `public/sequence/index.html` or anything else this item changed). `MAP.md` regenerated (`node scripts/build-map.mjs`) for the new/removed exports.
- Verify: sandbox — real Chromium via Playwright, both entry points, all adjacent cases, mutation-proven. `ui-audit/verify-schedule-indent-outdent-delete.mjs` is **not wired into CI** (`.github/workflows/build.yml` invokes no `ui-audit/verify-*.mjs` script) — it exists, it is not enforced; `test/scheduleIndentOutdentDelete.test.js` (34 tests: pure-function unit tests + source-pin regexes) IS the CI-enforced half.

Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — found, measured, fixed, and re-proven in the same session, before archiving.**
- **THE GAP, MEASURED, not assumed.** B637232's original drift guard pinned four function-signature lines plus a handful of "load-bearing" regex lines inside `indentSelection`/`outdentSelection`/`promoteChildrenAndDelete`. Mutated `index.html`'s `indentSelection` so every root row reparents onto `top.id` (the topmost SELECTED row) instead of `newParent.id` (the row above it) — a real, meaningful behavioral bug, no valid English reading of "indent" — touching a line the old guard never looked at. **All 34 tests in `test/scheduleIndentOutdentDelete.test.js` stayed green.** The guard the item's own PR description called "source-pinned so a revert... fails CI" could not see a divergence inside the very function it was supposedly pinning.

Re-ran the exact same mutation against the new guard: it failed immediately, printing the literal line that diverged. Reverted the mutation, confirmed green again.
- **THE SAME TREATMENT for a second, adjacent gap the audit surfaced:** "one recompute per operation" had been argued from source inspection (one `setData(` call per function body) but never itself asserted as a standing guard. Added `it("each of the three batch operations calls setData and recomputeAfterStructureChange EXACTLY ONCE...")`, counting literal call occurrences inside each extracted body. Mutation-proven: doubled the `recomputeAfterStructureChange` call inside `outdentSelectionByIds` — the new test failed, reporting `2`, expected `1`. Reverted, confirmed green.
- **AND A THIRD GAP: the B463072 landmine and predecessor-link survival had only ever been checked LIVE** (the non-CI-enforced browser harness) or by structural inspection (predecessors array untouched by construction). Added two fast tests running `indentSelection`/`outdentSelection` THROUGH the real, pre-existing recompute engine (`ui-audit/stress/scheduler-engine.mjs`'s `recomputeSchedule` — cascadeDates + rollupParentDates, unchanged by this work): a leaf with a typed 3d duration that gains a dated child rolls to the child's span (1d) and, once outdented back to childless, cleanly restores its own typed 3d — the B463072 self-heal, now proven through the actual date-cascade math rather than argued from "rollupParentDates never touches durValue." Two more prove a predecessor link survives both indent and outdent AND stays LIVE — the moved row's cascaded date is asserted equal to its pre-move baseline, not just that the `predecessors` array is unchanged.
- **`test/scheduleIndentOutdentDelete.test.js` is now 38 tests** (was 34): the strengthened drift guard, the setData/recompute-count guard, and the four combined-engine tests.
- **Is the mirror the source of truth, or a copy — stated plainly, as asked.** `public/sequence/index.html` is the source of truth; it is what ships and what runs. `ui-audit/stress/schedule-tree-ops.mjs` is a COPY that exists only so `vitest` — which cannot execute Babel-JSX-in-HTML — can exercise the same logic without a browser. A future editor fixing a reported indent/outdent bug will almost certainly open `index.html` first, since that is what actually runs; the mirror lives in a different directory (`ui-audit/stress/`) and is easy to forget exists at all. **That asymmetry is exactly why the byte-identical guard matters** — it is the one thing standing between "edited the real file, forgot the mirror" and a test suite that keeps reporting green over stale logic.

### B637233 — Deleting a task with subtasks silently did whatever the code path did, with no choice offered `[Scheduler]` (feature) #scheduler #ui #selection  *(owner report, first form: "It's not even letting me delete this new task for whatever reason. It looks like it's because it's got subtasks. Um, however, those subtasks, should just get attached to the task above." **Superseded mid-report by the owner's own correction**, verbatim: "Oh, actually, no. Maybe it should delete all the subtasks... or allow all subtasks to get migrated to the next task above" — followed by a request for a two-choice-plus-cancel prompt, "keep it minimal," and "the action buttons must be the same size as each other" (his standing complaint about `SuccessorPromptModal`, this file's other confirmation dialog). Minted **B637233** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `deleteTasks`, `notifyRowsDeleted`, `promote`, `confirm delete`, `subtasks`: no prior item covers a delete-with-children choice; `deleteTasks`/`deleteTask` (B501-era) already cascade-delete silently and are the mechanism this wraps, not a duplicate of it. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — shipped and headless-verified this session (part of the same 44/44 run above, sections F/G2/G3).**
- **STEP 1, measured rather than assumed: there was NO explicit guard blocking the delete.** Both `deleteTasks` (multi-row) and the single-row `deleteTask` already cascade-delete a parent and its FULL subtree with zero confirmation, and a live repro against a fixture mirroring the owner's screenshot (a parent "New task" with 6 children) confirmed both the right-click "Delete Row" menu item and a full-row-selected keyboard Delete already worked — the whole subtree vanished cleanly, no block, no error. **The likely real mechanism behind what the owner saw** (also measured live): pressing the Delete KEY while a single PARENT-LOCKED cell is selected (start/end/duration/cost on a row that has children — the pre-existing "Fix #7: Delete clears a cell" branch's `isParentDateLocked` guard) does **nothing at all, with zero feedback** — that is Excel-style "clear this cell," which correctly refuses to clear a locked/computed cell, and reads exactly like "delete isn't working" if the user expected Delete to mean "delete the row." This existing per-cell-clear behavior is left alone (it is intentional, matches Excel, and is not what the owner actually wants triggered anyway); the fix instead targets the two genuine ROW-delete actions.
- **THE FIX.** New `requestDelete(taskIds)` replaces the direct `deleteTasks(...)` call at BOTH row-delete entry points (the keyboard Delete key's full-row-selected branch, and the context menu's "Delete Row"/"Delete N Rows"). If none of the targeted rows has any children, it deletes immediately — **no prompt, no extra click, exactly as before** (asserted live: a leaf delete shows zero modal). If any targeted row has children, it opens a new `DeleteChildrenModal` with exactly two choices plus Cancel — no menu, no settings toggle, no remember-my-choice, per the owner's explicit "keep it minimal":
  - **"Delete all N"** (cascade) — the whole subtree goes. Reuses the existing, unchanged `deleteTasks`.
  - **"Keep subtasks"** (promote) — new `promoteAndDeleteTasks`/pure `promoteChildrenAndDelete`: every child is reparented to the DELETED row's own parent (never "the row above," which the brief flagged as a DIFFERENT and NOT ALWAYS EQUIVALENT reading — implemented per the owner's own final correction, "they'll move up to this task's parent"). Handles a whole deleted CHAIN transitively: deleting a parent together with one of its own children (an explicitly tested adjacent case) promotes the child's own children past BOTH deleted ancestors, straight to the nearest SURVIVING one — `survivingAncestor` walks the parent chain skipping every id in the delete set, not just one level. No repositioning logic is needed for promote (unlike outdent): filtering out the deleted rows never changes the relative order of the survivors, so a promoted row already sits exactly where it needs to among its new parent's other children.
  - **"Cancel"** — closes the prompt, changes nothing (verified live: tree is byte-identical after Cancel).
- **EQUAL-SIZED BUTTONS, measured via `getBoundingClientRect`, not asserted in prose.** All three buttons render at 134.65–134.67 × 34 px (the ~0.02px spread is Chromium's own documented Blink LayoutUnit rounding on independently-shrinking flex siblings — the SAME measured floor this repo's OTHER modal's own equal-width test already tolerates, `EQUAL_WIDTH_TOLERANCE_PX=0.1` in `verify-successor-complete.mjs`). They are equal by CONSTRUCTION, not by careful tuning: all three literally spread the SAME `FOOTER_BTN_STYLE` object the successor modal already uses (only color/border differ on the cascade button), so they cannot drift apart independently the way the owner's prior complaint described. Mutation-proven: giving the cascade button its own `minWidth:220` makes the check correctly go red.
- **THE TRUE TOTAL, not the visible count — measured and decided.** The prompt's total (`totalCount`, e.g. "Delete all 9") counts every descendant transitively, INCLUDING any collapsed/hidden ones — a fixture with 6 visible children where one of them has a further COLLAPSED child (7 direct + grandchildren = 9 total) shows 9, not 6. That is the number that matters on a real construction schedule, per the owner's explicit ask ("if he deletes a row showing 6 children but the subtree is actually 11 rows deep... I want measured, not assumed").
- **Data safety, asserted as counts, not inferred.** Cascade-deleting a parent+6-descendants fixture leaves EXACTLY the 3 unrelated rows behind (before/after counts asserted). Promote-deleting the same fixture leaves EXACTLY the deleted row gone and every one of its descendants present, at the correct promoted depth, in original order (every name asserted present, order asserted, multi-level relative depth asserted). A selection spanning a parent AND one of its own children (explicit adjacent case) cascade-deletes the parent's whole subtree and nothing outside it.
- **ONE UNDO STEP for the whole delete-and-reparent**, cascade or promote — both call `setData` exactly once; verified live (one Ctrl+Z after a 9-row cascade delete restores all 9; one Ctrl+Z after a 6-child promote restores the deleted parent and the original structure).
- **The delete-children prompt is latched into the existing `overlayOpenRef`/`overlayAtKeyStartRef` guard** (`deleteChoice` added to the tracked-overlay list) so a keystroke that dismisses it can't leak through to the grid behind it — the same latch thirteen other overlays already share, extended per its own standing instruction to do exactly that for the next one added.
- **Predecessor/successor links survive**: promote only ever changes `parentId`; a link from OUTSIDE a cascade-deleted subtree into it goes dangling, which is pre-existing, accepted, LOUD-FAILURE-compliant behavior (`predUnresolved`) unrelated to this fix.
- **Adjacent cases, stated tested-or-not:** a leaf with no children ✅ live (no prompt) · a parent with one child ✅ unit · a parent with a multi-level subtree ✅ live+unit (relative depth preserved under promote) · a parent whose children have predecessor links pointing outside the subtree ✅ unit · the last remaining child of a group (group becomes childless) ✅ unit (no crash) · a multi-row selection including both a parent and one of its own children ✅ live (both cascade-deleted correctly, and the transitive-promotion case is mutation-proven separately).
- Bundle: same static-file note as B637232 above — no JS-bundle metric moves.
- Regressions checked: same run as B637232 above (`npm test` 578/580 files, 2 pre-existing unrelated failures; `MAP.md` regenerated).
- Verify: sandbox — same harness and same CI-enforcement note as B637232 above.

### B646272 — No way to move a task (or a selection of tasks) once it's on the schedule — no drag, no confidence copy/paste works either `[Scheduler]` (feature) #scheduler #ui #selection  *(owner report, voice, decoded — the transcript mangled the domain terms into nonsense; corrected here: PUD development agreement, PID = Public Improvement District, annexation. His scenario: he created new Phase 1/Phase 2 sections in an existing schedule and the permitting/entitlement tasks that belong under Phase 2 are scattered where they were originally created, with "no good way to drag and drop them where I want to," and he does not know whether copy/paste works either. He also asked, explicitly, for at least five checks and a steel-man of the approach before committing to it. Minted **B646272** from this branch's reserved block B646272–B646287 against `origin/main` 2a1b4bd5. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `drag`, `move row`, `reorder`, `Move to`, `rowgrip`, `indentSelectionByIds`, `promoteAndDeleteTasks`: **B637232** built the block-move PRIMITIVE this item reuses (`structuralTargets`/`rowRangeSelIds`, "reparent only the block's root rows") but that item is indent/outdent ONLY — moving a row to an ARBITRARY destination, dragging, and a searchable move command are all net-new. No prior item covers any of them.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE — shipped and headless-verified this session, mutation-proven, and driven once more by hand against the app's own real Grid (screenshotted before/after).**
- **STEEL-MAN, done before committing to the mechanism, as asked.** Drag-and-drop is genuinely hard to get right across a long, partially-collapsed, virtualized list, and it does NOT actually solve the owner's stated scenario as well as it first appears to: this codebase's entire selection model (`selRange`) is a single contiguous rectangle — there is no ctrl-click or other discontiguous multi-select anywhere in it (documented already, above `indentSelection`) — so a set of SCATTERED tasks (his literal situation: 12 permitting/entitlement rows created at different times, sitting at different points in the list) can never be grabbed in one gesture, by drag OR by any bulk selection mechanism, regardless of what UI sits on top. A **"Move to…" command** — pick the destination by NAME from a searchable list, invoked once per scattered task — closes his actual scenario end-to-end: it needs no aiming, no scrolling to keep both ends of the move on screen at once, and it works identically whether the destination is expanded, collapsed, or off screen. **Verdict: ship BOTH, Move-to first.** Drag is still worth having — the day-to-day case ("nudge this task up two slots," "put this one inside that group I can see") is common and drag is the natural tool for it, and the owner explicitly named it — but Move-to is what actually gathers 12 scattered tasks into a folder, which is what he asked for.
- **THE SHARED PRIMITIVE.** New pure `moveSelectionToDestination(tasks, selectedIds, destParentId, insertAfterId)` (`public/sequence/index.html`, byte-identical mirror in `ui-audit/stress/schedule-tree-ops.mjs`, drift-guarded the same way B645360 hardened indent/outdent's mirror) generalizes `indentSelection`'s block rule — "reparent only the block's ROOT rows (a selected row whose parent is also selected is left untouched)" — from "the row above, at the topmost row's own level" to an ARBITRARY destination parent + sibling position. Reparenting only the roots is what carries the rest of the block along for free: non-root selected rows AND any hidden/collapsed descendants outside the selection never have their `parentId` touched, and `sortByVisualOrder` rebuilds the whole tree purely from `parentId` — so a moved PARENT always takes its whole subtree, with **zero special-case code for "does it have children."** Refuses (returns `null`) a drop into the moved block's own descendant (cycle guard, walks the ORIGINAL tree) and a genuine no-op (dropped back exactly where it started, same parents + same relative order for every row — not just the moved ones).
- **(A) Drag-and-drop.** A small grip (`⠿`, Tabler `ti-grip-vertical`) in the ID column, real `page.mouse`-driven in every test (never a synthetic `dispatchEvent` — SYNTHETIC-KEYS-DONT-EDIT's sibling caution about untrusted events not propagating the way a real gesture does). Drop zones, read from where the cursor sits inside the hovered row: top third = insert BEFORE it (same parent), bottom third = insert AFTER it (same parent), middle third = reparent as its LAST CHILD — the ONLY way to target a COLLAPSED row's children at all, since you cannot see inside it to aim between them. Dropping into a collapsed group **auto-expands it** (built into the primitive itself, so drag and Move-to both get it for free) — the moved block is immediately visible right where it landed, which is how the owner can tell it worked without needing to see inside the group first. Honors the WHOLE active row-selection when the grabbed row is part of one, not just the grabbed row — resolved via the SAME `structuralTargets` App-level closure indent/outdent/delete already share, not a parallel notion of "what moved."
  - **Zero `setData` calls during the drag.** Every mousemove-driven repaint (the insertion line, the drop-target highlight, auto-scroll near the viewport edges) is an IMPERATIVE DOM write through refs on an internal `requestAnimationFrame` loop — never `setState`, never touches React at all — so the row list is re-rendered **zero times** for the whole gesture, however long it lasts or however far it scrolls. Measured live against a ~540-row fixture (matching the owner's real 529-task plan) with a `MutationObserver` watching the rows container through a sustained auto-scroll: **zero** `childList` mutations (no row DOM node added/removed/reordered) until the single drop-triggered commit. `moveRows` (the one call that reaches `setData`) fires from exactly one place — the mouse-up handler — never from the per-frame paint path; a source-pin test asserts this structurally (every `moveRows(` call site in `startRowDrag` lives inside `onUp`, none in the paint/tick/move functions) and a live mutation (wiring a commit into the per-frame loop, simulating a B1121-shaped regression) is proven to break the single-undo-step guarantee below.
  - **A real bug was found and fixed building this**, not shipped with it: the grip's first implementation covered the WHOLE id cell (`inset:0`), invisible until `:hover` — but `:hover` is true for the entire duration of a mousedown (the cursor always enters an element before it can press it), so gating interactivity on hover did not protect ordinary clicks at all: it silently ate every mousedown in the ID column, breaking the pre-existing row-range-select drag. Caught by a diagnostic script reproducing the exact CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS shape (chrome painted over a feature's own body swallowing the press meant for that body). Fixed by narrowing the grip to an 8px strip at the cell's left edge, permanently interactive, opacity-only on hover — it no longer overlaps where a click aiming at the row number lands, and the pre-existing selection drag was reproven working (range badge + blue highlight both fire again) before re-testing the move feature itself.
- **(B) "Move to…" command.** New `MoveToModal`, reachable from the row context menu ("Move to…", between Outdent and the clipboard group) — a searchable, keyboard-navigable list of every task in the project (by name, indented by depth, walked WITHOUT the `isExpanded` gate so a collapsed destination is still searchable and pickable) plus a "— Top level —" pseudo-entry, with the moved block's own descendants excluded from the candidate list (same cycle guard as the primitive). Commits through `moveSelectionByIds` with the ids FROZEN at the moment the menu item was clicked, not a live re-resolved selection — so the picker can't silently retarget if anything about the selection changed while it was open. Appends as the LAST child of the chosen destination and auto-expands it, identical semantics to a drag "into" drop.
- **(C) MEASURED, then fixed: Ctrl+C/X/V and the row context menu's Cut/Copy/Paste.** Stated precisely, per surface, before changing anything — **single cell**: operated on the WHOLE anchor row's subtree (not the cell), since there is no per-cell clipboard in this app. **A cell range** (multiple columns, one row): identical — the column span was never consulted. **A full-row selection** (one row, ID column): identical, correctly a no-op distinction since the range was exactly one row anyway. **A genuine multi-row selection**: this is where it broke — Ctrl+C/X and the menu's Cut/Copy operated on `selectedId` ALONE (the drag/shift-click ANCHOR), completely ignoring every other row in the range, with **no error and no indication anything was dropped**. A 6-row selection copied exactly one row's subtree. Paste then inserted only that one subtree. This is precisely the shape STANDING RULE calls "a half-working paste is worse than none" — it LOOKED like it operated on the selection. **Fixed the same way as indent/outdent/delete**: `copyTaskById`/`cutTaskById` now take an array and resolve `rootsOfSelection` (a selected parent + its own selected child collapse to ONE subtree, not two — same "root = parent not itself selected" rule the move primitive and `indentSelection` both use); `pasteTaskAfter` reparents EVERY pasted root to the paste target's parent (was: one hardcoded `sourceRootId`), keyed off a new `sourceRootIds` array on the clipboard (an old-shaped clipboard with a lone `sourceRootId` still works via a fallback, so nothing already in a user's clipboard at reload breaks). All four entry points (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, the menu's Cut, the menu's Copy) now resolve `structuralTargets(anchor)` first, identically to indent/outdent.
- **NON-NEGOTIABLES, each proven — not argued — in `ui-audit/verify-schedule-row-move.mjs`, a real headless Chromium against a throwaway fixture shaped like the owner's scenario (Phase 1/Phase 2, a COLLAPSED Phase 2, a parent task with two children, a task with an FS predecessor crossing the move, a contiguous pair for the multi-row case, a control row) — never one of his real plans, and Supabase is unreachable in this sandbox regardless (confirmed):**
  - a moved PARENT takes its whole subtree — child count AND order verified by name, before/after ✅
  - the WHOLE active selection moves, not just the grabbed row (the exact historical B637232 bug shape, now proven for move too) ✅
  - dropping into a COLLAPSED group auto-expands it, and the moved row is immediately visible directly under it ✅
  - **ONE undo step for the whole operation** — a single Ctrl+Z after a drag fully reverts it (byte-identical full-row snapshot, not just "something changed back") ✅
  - a predecessor link survives the move and stays LIVE — captured a cross-parent-move task's FS-derived Start before and after: unchanged, still genuinely driven ✅
  - **a single end-of-operation recompute** — same source-pin discipline B645360 established: `moveSelectionByIds`'s body contains exactly one `setData(` and one `recomputeAfterStructureChange(` call ✅
  - a copy/paste round trip (parent-with-children pasted elsewhere) leaves the original completely untouched, verified both by presence AND by its children still being its children ✅
  - the "Move to…" menu wiring reaches the SAME primitive, independent of drag (parentage verified via indentation LEVEL, not array position, since by the time this check runs the fixture has already been reshaped by five earlier checks) ✅
- **20/20 checks total, 12 functional + 8 mutations, EVERY mutation independently proven to flip the ONE check it targets red** (before/after band detection swapped, direct children flattened onto the destination instead of staying under the moved parent, the auto-expand line removed, `structuralTargets` (the function the ACTUAL commit resolves through) forced to ignore the range, predecessors silently dropped on reparent, a commit wired into the per-frame paint loop, copy silently behaving like cut, the menu item's own wiring removed) — nothing here is defensive code counted as a check. Two earlier mutation attempts were themselves WRONG (one mutated a code path the test's own fixture never exercises, one asserted a condition too weak to distinguish "both rows moved" from "only one did") and were caught and corrected by re-running against the real, unmutated build first and confirming the mutation's output actually differed.
- **59 tests in `test/scheduleIndentOutdentDelete.test.js`** (was 38 — 21 new): `moveSelectionToDestination` pure-function behavior (same-level reorder, reparent + auto-expand, `"start"`/`"end"`/sibling `insertAfterId`, both non-negotiables above, cycle guard, no-op guard, stale-id fallback, same-parent pure reorder) + two tests running it through the REAL recompute engine (predecessor survival, the B463072 landmine specifically for a cross-parent MOVE, not just indent) + source-pin wiring guards (the Move-to menu item, the modal's frozen-ids commit, the drag handle's own selection resolution, "no `moveRows` call outside `onUp`," copy/cut/paste's four entry points, `pasteTaskAfter`'s multi-root reparenting) + the drift-guard pair extended to the new primitive. The drift guard and two of the pure-function tests were mutation-proven against the REAL source (not just argued): disabling the cycle guard in `index.html` alone (leaving the mirror untouched) flips the drift guard red; disabling it in the mirror flips the cycle-guard unit tests red — both reverted after confirming.
- **A THROWAWAY plan, driven by hand once more** against the app's own real Grid view (the "Goose Creek" demo/seed schedule) — not a fixture import: added a task purely through the UI's own right-click "Add Subtask," typed a name, dragged its grip to the top of the list, screenshotted before and after. Confirmed live: correct renumbering, and every predecessor/successor cross-reference in the whole schedule shifted consistently with it (e.g. "5 · Hire Environmental Co…" → "6 · Hire Environmental Co…" throughout), not just the moved row's own links.
- Bundle: same static-file note as B637232/B637233 above — `public/sequence/index.html` never enters the JS module graph, no bundle metric moves.
- Regressions checked: full suite, 12003/12004 tests, 580/581 files — the one failure (`test/docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js`) references a historical git SHA (`09d9cf9d`) unreachable in this sandbox's shallow clone, reproduced identically against the UNMODIFIED pre-this-session codebase via `git stash`, so it is pre-existing and unrelated (same class as the `hiddenContentReads.test.js` shallow-clone gap B637232 noted above — which SHA-dependent test surfaces varies run to run, but at least one always does; neither touches anything this item changed). `MAP.md` regenerated (`node scripts/build-map.mjs`) for the new exports (`MoveToModal`, `moveSelectionToDestination`, `moveSelectionByIds`, `rootsOfSelection`, `levelOf` in the harness). `node ui-audit/stress/check-babel.mjs` passes (the Scheduler syntax guard).

### B655552 (×3) — Schedule grid predecessor/successor cells clip the second line, and single-link cells leave it empty `[Schedule]` (bug) #scheduler #ui  *(owner report, verbatim: "we were supposed to achieve two lines in the successor/predecessor cells so we can show 2 successors or predecessors, and if there's only one, it should then wrap to show its full name if it has a second line thats not being used." Screenshots from his real Goose Creek grid showed two cases mid-glyph-clipped ("64 - Hillwood Review o…" / "70 - PID Petition Submi", cut off at the row boundary) and four single-link cells ellipsized on line 1 with line 2 unused ("53FS+10d - Submit to…", "61 - Meet with Econo…", "63 - Municap to send…", "62 - Send milestone sc…"). Minted **B655552** from this branch's reserved block B655552–B655567 against `origin/main` 61c3888. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done for `predecessor cell`, `successor cell`, `DepCell`, `cell clip`, `two lines` (`grep -n` across `BACKLOG.md`): no prior item covers this cell's line layout. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE (round 1) — shipped and headless-verified that session (real Chromium, driving the real Format-panel row-height slider), mutation-proven both ways.**
- **ONE report, TWO distinct defects, kept separate throughout** (per the owner's own framing — different causes, either survives the other's fix):
  - **(A) the second line renders but is sliced off mid-glyph at the row's bottom edge.** `DepCell` (public/sequence/index.html) stacked two lines in a column, each with `lineHeight:1.2` on a 10px font (a natural 12px line) and `minHeight:10` — a **2px floor below what a line actually needs**. The container's own `padding:"2px 8px"` (4px vertical) plus two natural 12px lines needs 28px, but the row is fixed at `ROW_H` (24px by default) with `overflow:hidden` on both the container and each line's own box — so flexbox `flex-shrink` compressed each line down to the 10px floor and **its own `overflow:hidden` sliced 2px off the bottom of every glyph**, at the DEFAULT row-height setting.
  - **(B) a single link ellipsizes on line 1 while line 2 sits empty.** With only one item, `DepCell` rendered one populated slot and one always-empty slot — the name truncated with an ellipsis instead of using the second line's space to show more of it.
- **THE LANDMINE, measured rather than assumed.** `ROW_H = Math.min(34, Math.max(20, data.settings?.rowHeight || 24))` — a user-configurable slider from 20 to 34px (Format panel), default 24. "Make it two lines" is a function of this setting, not a single fix: **the measured threshold is 24px** (two 12px lines, once the container's vertical padding is removed — see below). At/above 24 (11 of the 15 possible integer settings, INCLUDING the default), two full, unclipped lines fit. Below 24 (20–23, the bottom 4 settings), there is not enough room for a second natural-height line at all — **DepCell now shows exactly one clean line instead of a doomed partial second one.** This is a deliberate choice, stated here per the brief's own framing: silently clipping is not acceptable, showing one line cleanly is.
- **THE FIX, one shape for both defects.** `DEPCELL_LINE_H = 12` (measured: 10px font × 1.2 line-height) and `DEPCELL_TWO_LINE_MIN_H = DEPCELL_LINE_H * 2 = 24`. `canTwoLine = (s.height || 0) >= DEPCELL_TWO_LINE_MIN_H` reads the row's ACTUAL rendered height (the same `s.height` every other cell in the row already renders at, not a re-derived guess) — `visibleCount` becomes 1 or 2 accordingly, and `extra = items.length - visibleCount` — so the existing "+N" badge (already present for 3+ items) now also covers the case where the fallback drops from 2 visible slots to 1. **(A)'s fix:** the multi-item layout's vertical padding drops from `2px 8px` to `0 8px` — 2 natural 12px lines now fit exactly inside the default 24px row with zero compression (`.drow`'s own `border-bottom` already separates rows visually, so the cell's internal padding was never load-bearing there). **(B)'s fix:** when there is exactly one item AND `canTwoLine`, the label+name renders through `-webkit-line-clamp:2` (`display:-webkit-box`, `WebkitBoxOrient:"vertical"`) instead of the fixed two-slot layout — wrapping into the second line when the name is longer than one line, and staying on one line when it already fits (line-clamp only clamps what needs it). **Found and fixed a real bug while building this**: the line-clamp span silently failed to wrap at first — it inherited `white-space:nowrap` from the shared cell style `s` (every other cell in this grid is intentionally single-line), so an explicit `whiteSpace:"normal"` override was required on both the wrap-branch container and the clamped span itself.
- **THREE OR MORE LINKS — checked both before and after, stated plainly.** Before this fix, a 3-link cell already showed item 1, item 2, and a "+1" badge — **it did NOT silently drop the third item**, a finding worth recording even though nothing needed fixing there. After this fix, that behavior is preserved at/above the two-line threshold (item 1 + item 2 "+1"), and is now ALSO preserved below it (item 1 alone + "+2", since `extra` is computed against whatever `visibleCount` actually is) — so a row-height change can never turn this into a silent drop. Mutation-proven: forcing `visibleCount`'s badge condition to always reference a hardcoded `1` (instead of `visibleCount - 1`) is exactly the kind of regression `ui-audit/verify-depcell-two-line.mjs`'s "+N" assertion is built to catch.
- **EXPORT PARITY (PDF-PARITY) — checked, and it did NOT diverge.** `buildPDFHtml`'s predecessors column (`case "predecessors": return (t.predecessors||[]).map(p=>p.id||p).join(", ");`) was ALREADY a bare comma-joined id list before this change — no task names, no multi-line layout, nothing that can clip or need wrapping (and `successors` was never an exportable column at all). This fix touches only DepCell's on-screen pixel layout, which the export never mirrored to begin with, so there is no new divergence — `test/depcellTwoLine.test.js` pins the export's bare-id-list form so a future change that DOES give the export names/lines is forced to consider this cell deliberately.
- **EDIT MODE — unaffected, checked via the real code path.** The predecessors cell already swaps to a plain single-line `<PredEditor>` `<input>` while being edited (`col.k === "predecessors"` branches to `PredEditor` before `DepCell` is ever reached) — this fix touches only the DISPLAY (non-editing) render, so typing/editing a predecessor list looks exactly as it did before: one line, live plain-English hint below it. `successors` is a derived, never-editable column, so it has no edit-mode path to affect.
- **MEASURED, not asserted, via a real headless Chromium** driving the actual Format-panel row-height slider (not a data-injection shortcut — `ROW_H` is a plain module variable updated inside a `useEffect`, so seeding `settings.rowHeight` in the boot payload alone only takes effect on a LATER render; the slider's own `onChange` is the same live-update path a real user's drag uses). At the default 24px: a 2-link cell showed BOTH lines at a clean 12px each (was: flex-compressed to 10px, `scrollHeight`(12) > `clientHeight`(10) confirmed via `getBoundingClientRect`/`getComputedStyle` on the pre-fix code); a 1-link cell with a 54-character name went from one 12px ellipsized line to a genuine 24px two-line wrap (`clientHeight` 12→24, `scrollWidth` no longer exceeding `clientWidth` — the text WRAPS rather than overflowing horizontally). At the 20px floor: every cell now shows exactly one un-clipped ~12px line plus a correct "+N" badge where items are hidden — confirmed at 20, 23, 24, 25, and 34px, both before and after this fix, with before/after screenshots of the real rendered cells.

- **Bundle: still lazy-loaded, no regression.** `AppHeader.jsx` is already the shared entry chunk every route pulls in; the added prop + a few lines of guarded JSX measure in the low hundreds of bytes and don't move the Site route's rounded total at all (2497.0 KB before and after, `node ui-audit/perf-bundle-audit.mjs`). `foodRouteJsBytes` (the food route's own lazy `FoodApp` chunk + shared deps): **918.5 KB → 918.7 KB (+0.2 KB)** for this change specifically (isolated by diffing a build of this branch against a build with this diff stashed) — well inside the metric's existing 32 KB headroom band, no ceiling raised. `FoodApp` still ships as its own `React.lazy` chunk (`dist/assets/FoodApp-*.js`, 35.04 KB / gzip 10.41 KB in this build) — confirmed it never merged into `SitePlannerApp` or the shared `index` chunk.

### B672112 — Callout leaders should have TWO segments you can manipulate, like Bluebeam `[Site Planner]` (feature) #site-planner #ui #markup  *(owner chat block 2026-08-22, provisional NEW-1: "I like on Bluebeam how the callouts have two lines in the arm as opposed to just one line... how you can manipulate the two arms." Minted **B672112 / (no live-verify V# — see Verify: sandbox below)** from this branch's reserved block B672112–B672127 against `origin/main` 7fbe151. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done across `callout`, `leader`, `tip`, `elbow`, `B919`, `B913`, `B948`, `B909`: **B919** built the N-leader (multi-arrow) model this reuses verbatim; **B913** built the width-resize grip pattern this mirrors for the new elbow grip; **B909** is the shared markup N-leader engine (`markupModel.js`), extended here rather than forked. Nothing prior gave a single leader a second segment. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — implemented and verified LIVE in a real headless browser this session (not merely unit-tested). Verify: sandbox.**
- Verify: sandbox — this is an ordinary interactive canvas feature with no auth/live-GIS/real-project-data dependency (ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK: a logged-out, no-external-GIS UI drag-drop check is Claude-doable here, so it was driven rather than parked). No `V#` was minted.
- **THE MODEL — additive, no migration, byte-identical on every plan that has never touched it.** A callout's leader gains an optional per-leader `elbow` (singular) / `elbows` (array, N-leader) field — the exact singular/plural shape `tip`/`tips` already use, `calloutElbows(c)` mirroring `calloutTips(c)`. Absent (every callout ever saved, and any new one until its elbow is dragged) means "no pinned elbow": the render computes the stub's endpoint as the box's own nearest-edge point (`nearestRectPerimeterPoint`, the SAME function that already computed the old single line's origin), so the stub is zero-length and the run IS the old origin→tip line — **provably, not just intended**, byte-identical to every callout ever saved.
- **THE THREE MANIPULABLE PARTS, per the brief.** Box drag (`startMoveCallout(..., "box")`) — unchanged, moves the label; tip drag (`"tip"`) — unchanged, re-aims the target and does NOT move a pinned elbow; **new** elbow drag (`"elbow"`) — pins that leader's elbow to wherever it's dragged (world feet, absolute — matching how `tip` already behaves, so a routing waypoint stays anchored to the ground it was placed at rather than sliding if the tip or box later move). The elbow grip lives in the always-on-top handle layer (`calloutHandles`, CHROME-NEVER-EATS-A-PRESS), a small square distinct from the round tip grip, defaulting to the same box-edge point the render defaults to — grabbable from first selection, not only after a bend already exists.
- **"Never doubles back through its own text box" — handled by construction, not a special case.** The stub's start point is *always* `nearestRectPerimeterPoint(boxRect, tip)`, recomputed fresh every render from the CURRENT box and tip — the same call that already correctly picked the nearest edge for the old single-line leader. So the DEFAULT (unpinned) elbow can never route back into the box regardless of which side the box sits on relative to the target; a user-PINNED elbow is a deliberate routing choice (an obstacle at a fixed ground point) and stays put when the box or tip move independently, exactly as a real Bluebeam elbow behaves.
- **Multi-leader (B919) composes for free.** `calloutElbows(c)[i]` is per-leader-indexed; `removeCalloutLeader` (shared `markupModel.js`) now splices the matching `elbows[i]` out when a leader is deleted (previously untouched, which would have shifted every later leader's pinned elbow onto the wrong leader, or left a stale elbow ready to misapply itself onto the next leader added) — caught and fixed via a new unit test, not observed live.
- **Translate carries a pinned elbow along.** A whole-callout move (multi-select drag, Ctrl-drag duplicate, cross-plan paste) has to move a pinned elbow with the box+tip or it strands at its old ground position. Fixed at the two shared translate functions (`markupModel.js:translate`, `planClipboard.js:translateCalloutBy`) — both already the ONE place every such move already funnels through, so no new call site was needed.
- **LIVE-DRIVEN, real headless Chromium, real drags (`e2e/callout-two-segment-leader.spec.js`, 2 specs):** placed a callout, selected it, dragged the elbow grip → confirmed a real (non-zero) stub renders and `elbow` persists; dragged the arrow tip → confirmed the tip re-aims and the pinned elbow does NOT move; dragged the box → confirmed the label moves while the tip (target) and elbow (routing waypoint) both stay anchored to the ground. Second spec seeded a plan with a LEGACY callout (`tip`+`box`, no `elbow` field — exactly what pre-existing saved plans look like) and confirmed the rendered stub is a genuine zero-length line (`<0.5px` between its own endpoints) — the "nothing on an existing plan moves" bar, proven on the real render rather than asserted from source. All 8 pre-existing callout e2e specs (`dim-callout-edit.spec.js` — B911/B912/B913/B923/B931/B932, the corner-radius zoom-invariance case) re-run green, unchanged.
- **Sandbox result:** lint 0 errors · new suites `test/calloutTwoSegmentLeader.test.js` (6, source-guard on the render/drag wiring) + `markupModel.test.js`'s new "two-segment leader" describe block (5, real pure-function assertions on `translate`/`removeCalloutLeader`) + `handleLayerOrder.test.js` extended to cover the new elbow starter · full suite 12,086/12,088 green (the 2 failures are pre-existing shallow-clone-only mutation checks unrelated to any file this item touches — see B323424 (×2)'s note for the same finding) · e2e both new specs + all 8 pre-existing callout specs green · build green.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx` (`calloutElbows`, `startMoveCallout`, the apply-on-move dispatcher, `renderCalloutNode`, `calloutHandles`), `src/shared/markup/markupModel.js` (`translate`, `removeCalloutLeader`), `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/planClipboard.js` (`translateCalloutBy`, `calloutBBox`), `test/calloutTwoSegmentLeader.test.js` (new), `test/markupModel.test.js`, `test/handleLayerOrder.test.js`, `e2e/callout-two-segment-leader.spec.js` (new).

### B679840 — Undoing a plan back to blank doesn't persist: the erased object reappears on reload `[Site Planner / Persistence]` (bug, DATA-LOSS-adjacent) #site-planner #persistence  *(owner chat block 2026-08-22, NEW-4's interaction sweep: found by the sweep itself, not reported by the owner directly — draw a callout on an otherwise-empty plan, Ctrl+Z it away, reload, and the callout comes back. Minted **B679840 / (no live-verify V# — see Verify: sandbox below)** from this branch's reserved block B679840–B679855 against `origin/main` @ `2782cf3`. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `isBlankSite`, `firstSave`, `blank`+`undo`, `blank`+`persist`: **B16** (isBlankSite omitting `markups`, letting a markup-only site delete itself) is the nearest relative — same guard, different field, already fixed — but nothing prior covers a fresh guard skipping the save on an EXISTING record reverting to blank. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — root-caused, fixed, and proven with a real debounced-autosave + localStorage round trip in headless Chromium this session. Verify: sandbox.**
- Verify: sandbox — this is a logged-out, no-GIS persistence check (ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK: draw → undo → reload is fully driveable here, including the debounced-autosave timing itself), so it was driven rather than parked. No live-GIS/auth/real-data dependency. No `V#` was minted.
- **Root cause.** The debounced autosave effect in `SitePlanner.jsx` has always skipped saving a still-blank, never-touched "Start blank" plan — the guard exists so opening a fresh blank plan and immediately leaving doesn't clutter storage with an empty record. The guard read `if (isBlankSite({ parcels, els, measures, callouts, markups, underlay, sheetOverlays }) && !deletedIds.length) return;` with no scoping: it fired on ANY blank state, including a plan that already has a saved, non-empty record on disk and is reverting to blank because the owner deliberately drew something and then hit Ctrl+Z. The canvas correctly showed the object gone; the autosave effect silently no-opped instead of writing the now-blank state over the stale saved record, so the old record — with the "undone" object still in it — sat untouched on disk and came back on the next reload.
- **The fix.** `fresh` (`!loadSite(siteId)` — true only when this plan has no existing saved record yet) already existed further down the same effect for an unrelated purpose (telling `App` to list a brand-new site); it's now computed earlier and the blank-skip guard is scoped to it: `if (fresh && isBlankSite(...) && !deletedIds.length) return;`. A plan with no prior save is still skipped while blank (the original intent, untouched); a plan that already has a saved record is never skipped, so an undo-to-blank writes through and the stale record can't survive.
- **Live-driven proof (headless Chromium, real debounced autosave + real `localStorage`, not a source read).** Seeded a plan, drew a callout on it (nothing else on the plan — the exact minimal repro), let it autosave, undid the callout (canvas confirmed empty), reloaded, and confirmed the callout does NOT come back and the saved record reads blank. Control case run alongside: a genuinely untouched "Start blank" plan (never drawn on) still produces no storage record after the same wait — confirming the fix is a no-op for the case the guard was originally written to protect, not a removal of it.
- **How this was found.** Surfaced by the NEW-4 interaction sweep (see the sweep's own summary item below), not by a direct owner report — undo history is memory-only and correctly does not survive a reload, so most of the sweep's undo checks ran (deliberately) BEFORE reload; this one repro needed the object to be the plan's ONLY content so the blank-skip guard's misfire had something to hide behind. Two false leads chased and refuted along the way, kept here so they're not re-chased: (1) undo appearing to do nothing at all across a reload is NOT a bug — undo history (`histRef`) is session-scoped by design and reloading a page is expected to clear it, same as any editor; (2) a synthetic-instrumentation pass (temporary `window.__DBG_HIST`-gated logging in `pushHistory`/`undo`, added and then fully reverted — diffed clean against a pre-instrumentation backup) confirmed undo itself was firing correctly and popping the right frame; the defect was entirely downstream, in autosave's write-skip decision.
- **Sandbox result:** lint 0 errors · new suite `test/undoToBlankPersists.test.js` (2, source-guard on the reordered `fresh`/guard wiring, incl. asserting the old unscoped guard shape is gone) · full unit suite 12,088/12,090 green (the 2 failures are the same pre-existing shallow-clone-only mutation checks noted on B672112/B323424, unrelated to any file this item touches) · isolated Playwright round-trip (draw callout → autosave → undo → reload → confirm gone; control: untouched blank plan still produces no record) green · build green.
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/site-planner/SitePlanner.jsx` (the debounced autosave effect — `fresh` computed earlier, blank-skip guard scoped to it), `test/undoToBlankPersists.test.js` (new).
- Base: `origin/main` @ `2782cf3`.

### B689904 — Woods Road (`sms...` group `smsrpaiqu5sv`) shows two counties and two ETJs off a hand-drawn boundary's tiny edge clip, never joined as a governing peer `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #parcel  *(owner report 2026-08-22, re-dispatch after `session_01SCZpsi8zviKzo1qByRyVLX` edited this same area and hung minting its IDs without shipping — restarted clean from `main`, no branch recovery attempted. Michael: "check the Woods Road project because it says it's in multiple ETJs... it also might have said it's in multiple counties even though it's ordering a county, but it's not in two counties as far as I understand." He is right. Minted **B689904 / V363552** from this branch's reserved block B689904–B689919 / V363552–V363567 against `origin/main` 7b950f4. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳ Verify/Done for `countyEdge`, `etjEdge`, `CITY_SHARE_MIN`+county, `sliver`+county, `identifyJurisdiction`+straddle, `B276752`–`B280707`: that whole family (jurisdiction.js's header) gave CITY LIMITS an area-share sliver screen (B793/B276754) and COUNTY/ETJ never got the equivalent — this is that same fix, applied to the two roles it was never applied to. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — root-caused against the REAL production row (not the fixture the dispatch brief's own evidence pointed at), fixed, and portfolio-swept live against the real TxDOT/H-GAC/TxGIO services this session. Verify: live.**
- Verify: live → **V363552 PASSED** (GIS endpoint behavior — mandatory live-verify class). See the dated result below; this is not parked.
- **⛔ THE DISPATCH BRIEF'S OWN "EVIDENCE 1" IS REFUTED, AND SAYING SO IS THE FIRST FINDING.** It asserted "parcels = [] and parcelDrawings = []... No site polygon exists that could legitimately straddle anything" for all three named plans, checked against the `sites` table's legacy `data->parcels` jsonb column — which genuinely is empty. But that column is a MIRROR; the canonical geometry for a signed-in plan lives in `public.site_elements` (the row-synced engine — `/CLAUDE.md` → ROWS-CANONICAL-ON-SEED), queried directly against the production database (`lyeqzkuiwngunutlkkmi`, table `site_elements`, `kind='parcel'`) for this item. Every plan in the group carries ONE real, `locked:true` parcel row, id `e1454614maruai`, present since 2026-08-13, with `setbacks:[20,20,20,20,20]` — a hand-traced site boundary the owner drew and has been laying buildings out against (26–150 `el` rows per plan), not a ghost or an orphaned delete. **THE QUERY GEOMETRY THE DISPATCH ASKED ME TO "FIND AND CONFIRM" IS THIS PARCEL'S OWN RING** — not a hardcoded buffer anywhere in the code (none exists; grepped the whole tree for one and found none).
- **Root cause, measured exactly, live, against the real production `smss1gyt8yw1`/`smsrrlk9u576`/`smt0rwoodsa1` parcel ring reprojected to lon/lat and queried against the real TxDOT county layer and H-GAC ETJ layer with `returnGeometry:true`:** the 89.47-acre boundary measures **99.56% Fort Bend County / 0.44% Waller County** (0.39 of 89.47 ac — a tracing-precision sliver on the far edge, not a real straddle) and **5.20% Fulshear ETJ / 5.78% Simonton ETJ** (two genuine ~5-acre corners, not a sliver, near where the two ETJs and the county line converge). `identifyJurisdiction`'s per-role UNION query (`jurisdiction.js`) treated ANY intersection as full membership — the same defect city limits had before B793/B276754 gave city a measured AREA SHARE, with a floor (`CITY_SHARE_MIN`, 0.5%) that separates "holds it" from "merely clips the edge." County and ETJ never got that screen. So Waller joined Fort Bend with the label grammar's `+` — which reads as "and, both apply everywhere" — exactly as if the tract were genuinely half in each county.
- **The fix, two parts, in `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/jurisdiction.js`:**
  1. **County and ETJ now run the SAME area-share pass city limits already had** (`identifyCityShares`/`mergeCityAreas`, both already generic — no role-specific logic to touch) whenever a ring/boundary is present. A source that answers below `CITY_SHARE_MIN` (0.5%) is reported in a new `countyEdge`/`etjEdge` field — real, named, never dropped (LOUD-FAILURE) — but excluded from the governing `county`/`etj` list a `+` can join. A source that answers with NO geometry (an outage, a fixture) falls back to the original plain union, byte-for-byte — the same fallback contract city limits already use. A genuine straddle (both sides hold a real share) is untouched.
  2. **A site with NO parcel/boundary drawn now resolves too** (`SitePlanner.jsx`'s passive header-badge effect used to stay silently `null` whenever `jurActiveRings` was empty) — at the site's own ORIGIN POINT, no ring sent at all. A bare point query structurally cannot straddle (real administrative boundaries don't overlap at an exact coordinate — verified live at Woods Road's own origin: exactly one county, zero cities, zero ETJ), so `straddle` is false by construction rather than by a separate gate. `JurisdictionBadge.jsx`'s tooltip now says "Jurisdiction at the site location... no parcel or boundary is drawn" instead of "Jurisdiction of the active parcel" whenever the lookup ran without one (`badge.parcelBased`).

### B689905 — Two ETJs at a point is legally impossible; audit whether ETJ is a live query or a population-buffer guess `[Site Planner]` (bug) #site-planner #gis  *(owner dispatch 2026-08-22, NEW-2, part of the same Woods Road block as B689904. The two-ETJ case only ever arises for a RING (whole-tract) identify, which per Local Gov't Code ch. 42 is legitimate — a drawn tract CAN cross the apportionment line between two cities' ETJ, one on each side.

Driven live this session: every ETJ answer in this codebase (`etjSourcesForPoint` → `ETJ_SOURCES` in `jurisdiction.js`) is a real ArcGIS REST query against H-GAC's own hosted feature layer at `services.arcgis.com` (`HGAC_City_ETJ`), routed by the point's metro bounding box. It is NOT derived by buffering city limits by a population-based radius — no such derivation exists anywhere in this file or its dependents. The layer's own published coverage gap (it carries 34 named H-GAC cities, not all of them — B280705/`etj_baytown`'s own header) is the one honest caveat already surfaced (`etjUnmappedCities`), unrelated to this item.

### B727504 — Toolbar pass: rebuild the Site Planner toolbar to standard conventions `[Site Planner]` (bug, feature) #site-planner #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-25, full spec given verbatim: replace Undo/Redo/Zoom-to-fit/Layers glyphs with the shared Office/Google/Adobe icon-set shapes, give the File button a real border+caret, and relocate "Select parcels" out of the permanent toolbar into the parcel/site-setup context. `✅` **Done — implemented and driven headless, both themes, this session. Verify: sandbox.**
- Verify: sandbox — a logged-out, no-GIS chrome/icon change (ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK: fully driveable here), so it was driven rather than parked. No `V#` minted.
- **(a) Undo/Redo** — replaced the `↶`/`↷` text glyphs with the real Material Design Icons (Pictogrammers MDI — Apache-2.0, free for commercial use, no attribution required) `undo`/`redo` paths: the actual shared Office/Google/Adobe curved-arrow convention, not invented artwork, and never Microsoft's Fluent files. Verified point-for-point that MDI's own `redo` path is the exact horizontal mirror of `undo`'s, so "if one is filled, both are filled; if one is a 2px stroke, so is the other" holds by construction — both are single `fill="currentColor"` paths, no stroke, drawn from the one MDI source.
