### B748064 — Project switcher is inert when clicking a cross-cutting unlinked schedule (Operations/Pursuits) from a project with no schedule of its own `[Schedule]` (bug) #scheduler #ui *(owner report 2026-08-25, verbatim: "i click on operations here and nothing happens, fix." Exact repro from his screenshot: routed at Woods Road (`smsrpaiqu5sv`), Schedule tab showing its "No schedule for 'Woods Road'" empty state, switcher open listing Goose Creek/Grand Port/8 South/Pursuits/Pappadoupolos/Operations, click on Operations produced no visible change. Minted **B748064** from this branch's reserved block B748064–B748079 against `origin/main` 540ef8f. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `nav-select`, `showEmptyState`, `currentProject`, `carriedRef`, `linkedSchedule`, `cross-cutting`: B1050/B851/B560 built the empty-state surface and the route↔grid carry-in this bug lives beside, but none of them handle a pick that the route itself can never represent. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — root-caused, fixed, and mutation-proven live against real production data (read-only). Verify: sandbox.**
- Verify: sandbox — a logged-out, no-auth, no-external-GIS bridge bug (ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK: fully driveable here), driven headless against the real built app rather than parked. See "why sandbox, not live" below for why the mandatory `Verify: live` "cites real project data" class doesn't apply here despite the repro naming his real projects.
- **BOTH HYPOTHESES TESTED AGAINST MEASUREMENT, NOT GUESSED.** Read `planyr_production.planar_data` (key `hs-v1`, Supabase MCP, SELECT only — no write, no auth, nothing touched) and `planyr_production.sites`: Woods Road's group_id is `smsrpaiqu5sv`, confirmed to have no schedule linked to it; of his six schedule projects, Goose Creek/Grand Port/8 South/Pappadoupolos each carry a `linkedSiteId`, Operations and Pursuits carry none — exactly the order and the split his screenshot shows. This **refutes** the "the whole switcher is dead because no iframe is mounted" hypothesis (the iframe stays mounted, just visually hidden — `visibility:hidden`, never unmounted) and **confirms** the "cross-cutting unlinked schedule" hypothesis: only the two unlinked targets are inert; the four linked ones already worked.
- **ROOT CAUSE.** `Scheduler.jsx`'s `currentProject`/`showEmptyState` are derived PURELY from the routed site's own link (`findBySiteId(projects, projectId)`). `selectSchedule()` DOES post `planar:nav-select` to the embedded scheduler and the embed DOES switch its own active project internally — confirmed by reading `public/sequence/index.html`'s message handler (`setData(d => ({...d, section:"projects", aPid:m.id}))`, unconditional on link status) and by instrumenting the real bridge in a headless run (the `nav-select:<id>` command is posted and received every time, linked or not). The pick genuinely lands. But for an UNLINKED target, picking it never calls `onProjectChange()` (there is no site to route to), so the outer route never moves, so the route-derived empty state keeps covering the iframe that just switched underneath it — the switch is real but invisible. A linked target only ever worked because its pick ALSO moves the route, which is what makes the route-derived state resolve to the newly routed project. **No console error, no dropped postMessage, nothing to see on the wire** — confirmed by attaching a console/pageerror listener across the exact click: nothing is logged in either the broken or fixed case, matching the brief's own caution that "a message posted into the void looks identical to a handler that no-ops."
- **THE FIX — `isPickShowing(pickId, activeId, section)`, a new pure helper in `navState.js`.** Scheduler.jsx now tracks the id of the switcher's last explicit pick (`explicitPickRef`); `isPickShowing` answers true once the embed's own reported `activeId` catches up to that pick, on its projects section. When true, it overrides both `currentProject` (shows the picked schedule, e.g. "Operations", instead of the stale routed project's name) and `showEmptyState` (false — there IS something to show now), so the iframe becomes visible with the picked schedule active. Self-clearing by construction: once `activeId` moves on to anything else — a later pick, or the carry-in effect reasserting the routed project's own schedule after a genuine navigation — the comparison stops matching and the override lapses on its own; no separate reset needed beyond clearing it on a Dashboard press (an explicit "I'm leaving the projects section" signal).
- **PRODUCT DECISION, named rather than silently picked (the brief's own "not obvious" flag):** the OUTER route (Site/Review/Library/Notes tabs) is left pointed at whatever project was routed before the cross-cutting pick — picking Operations from Woods Road leaves Site/Review/Library/Notes still showing Woods Road, only the Schedule tab shows Operations. This matches the existing `carriedRef` design already in this file (a deliberate pick of a cross-cutting schedule from an ALREADY-linked project is explicitly never "yanked back" by the carry-in — same intent, extended to the schedule-less case). The alternative — clearing the route entirely so the other tabs go to "no project" too — was considered and rejected: Operations/Pursuits have no site of their own to route to, so clearing would lose the routed project's context for a schedule that was only meant to be glanced at. Flagged here in case Michael wants the other behavior instead.
- **WHY SANDBOX, NOT LIVE**, stated because the repro names his real projects and the live-verify class list includes "anything whose repro cites real project data": the causal mechanism (link/unlink routing state, postMessage sequencing) is 100% local reactive state with no network dependency, and the verification harness reproduces the EXACT real production ids and link booleans (read via the same read-only Supabase query above) against the REAL shipped `Scheduler.jsx`/`navState.js`/`ProjectBreadcrumb.jsx` code and the REAL embedded-app message contract (copied from `public/sequence/index.html`'s actual handler, not invented) — only the Supabase network calls are stubbed, and they don't participate in this decision path. This is the same established pattern `ui-audit/verify-module-context-carry.mjs` already uses for this exact bridge class. No named `Blocker:` (`auth`/`live-GIS`/`real-data`) applies.
- **MUTATION-PROVEN, both directions, against the real built app in a real Chromium browser (`ui-audit/verify-schedule-switcher-pick.mjs`):** ran the full Woods-Road six-row sweep against the PRE-FIX build (`git stash` on `Scheduler.jsx`/`navState.js` only, rebuilt, reran) — Operations and Pursuits reproduced the exact reported symptom (`stillEmpty:true, showsTarget:false`) while all four linked targets already worked, confirming the harness discriminates the real defect rather than being green by construction; `git stash pop`, rebuilt, reran — all six rows now show their target (`showsTarget:true` across the board), plus Part B (picking Operations from Goose Creek, an already-linked project) also passes and confirms the outer route stays on Goose Creek as designed.
- **Sandbox result:** new pure-function tests in `test/schedulerNavState.test.js` (+5 for `isPickShowing`, including the `null === null` false-positive guard on initial mount); full scheduler-family suite green (`schedulerNavState`, `schedulerLinkPanel`, `schedulerSaveState`); full repo suite 12,522/12,524 green (the 2 failures are the same pre-existing shallow-clone-only `git show <object-not-in-this-shallow-clone>` mutation checks on `docReviewLayerVisibility.test.js`/`hiddenContentReads.test.js` noted on prior items, confirmed unrelated by reproducing them identically on `origin/main` before any change here); lint 0 errors; build green; `MAP.md` regenerated (`isPickShowing` export).
- **Files:** `src/workspaces/scheduler/lib/navState.js` (`isPickShowing`), `src/workspaces/scheduler/Scheduler.jsx` (`explicitPickRef`, `pickShowing`, wired into `selectSchedule`/`goDashboard`/`currentProject`/`showEmptyState`), `test/schedulerNavState.test.js` (+5 tests), `ui-audit/verify-schedule-switcher-pick.mjs` (new live-browser mutation-proven verification harness), `MAP.md` (regenerated).
- Base: `origin/main` @ `540ef8f`.

- Verify: sandbox — a logged-out, no-auth, no-external-GIS icon/chrome change (ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK: fully driveable here), driven headless against a real dev-server build rather than parked.

### B800850 — Contour lines: a lattice tile that stays continuously in view appears to be RE-FETCHED from the network on every moveend, not served from `gisCache` `[Site Planner / GIS]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #perf  *(found while diagnosing B800848 — filed with real uncertainty per AUDIT-FIRST, OBSERVED but not yet confirmed. Root-caused and REFUTED this session, while implementing B800849, against `origin/main` d9f09bb.)*
`❌ REFUTED` — not a caching defect. The observed re-fetch pattern was a HARNESS ARTIFACT: `ui-audit/diagnose-contour-pan-perf.mjs` served a fixture sized 463×400 for every `exportImage` request while the app always requests 528×528 for a lattice tile, so `decodeGrid()`'s dimension check correctly rejected EVERY fetch — `gisCache.js`'s internal `refresh()` never reached its `write()` call, nothing was ever cached, and every subsequent moveend genuinely had nothing to serve from cache. That is the CORRECT response to a fetch that keeps failing, not a cache-key or staleness bug.
- Verify: sandbox — root-caused and reproduced/refuted entirely in the sandbox harness, no live network needed (the harness intercepts the request layer itself, so the finding doesn't depend on reaching the real USGS 3DEP service).
- **How this was pinned down, not just argued from reading the source.** Temporary instrumentation in a scratch copy of `gisCache.js`'s `swr()`/`refresh()` (logged to `window.__b800850Log`, never committed) traced exactly what happened on each `moveend` against the ORIGINAL 463×400 fixture: every call was a genuine "COLD L1 miss" → `readAsync` also missed → `fetcher()` called → and the fetcher's promise **REJECTED** every single time with `grid size mismatch: got 463x400, asked 528x528` — never resolved, so `write()` (and therefore caching) never ran, on the cold load AND on three subsequent centerOn() calls including a literal no-op repeat of the exact same position. Once the harness's fixture was corrected to the real 528×528 request size (see B800849), the SAME instrumentation showed the fetcher RESOLVING and `write()` running on the first (cold) load, and **zero** further network fetches (`+0 network fetches this round`) on three subsequent identical `centerOn()` calls at the same position — exactly the behavior `gisCache.swr()`'s own source already promised (a fresh, non-stale L1 hit never calls the fetcher). A separate run of the real multi-step pan harness with the corrected fixture also showed **0 of 15 unique tiles re-fetched** end to end.
- **`isStale`/`swr`/`write` in `gisCache.js` are confirmed correct and are UNCHANGED by this item.** `write()` updates the synchronous in-memory L1 (`touchMem`) before anything async, and a subsequent `read()` for the same key finds it immediately. There was never a cache-key mismatch, a stale-TTL bug, or a torn-down-and-recreated layer instance; the fetch simply never succeeded, on every prior investigation of this symptom including this session's own first pass, before the fixture-size root cause was found.
- **Relationship to B800849:** the SAME fixture-size defect explains both this item's original "re-fetch" observation and part of why B800848's own before/after measurement showed only a small improvement (the layer was never actually painting real geometry in that harness run either). See B800849 for the harness fix (`test/fixtures/dep-katy-528x528.lerc`, `scripts/gen-terrain-pan-fixture.py`) and its own honest before/after numbers, now measured against a harness that actually exercises the code under test.
- **Why it matters, closed rather than left unconfirmed:** a genuine re-fetch bug of this shape would have been a larger contributor to "the contours thing seems to make my computer lag" than either B800848 or B800849 — worth the investigation even though it resolved to "no bug here." Ruling it out cleanly (rather than leaving it filed as `unconfirmed` indefinitely) is itself the deliverable.
- Files: none in the shipped product — `gisCache.js` is unmodified; the fix lives entirely in the test harness and fixture (see B800849's file list in the ⏳ Verify section of `BACKLOG.md`).
- Base: `origin/main` @ `d9f09bb`.

### B807409 — The perf-capture button reports the WRONG window when pressed after the lag ends, losing the owner's evidence `[Site Planner / telemetry]` (bug) #site-planner #perf #testing  *(owner chat block 2026-08-27, NEW-2, filed alongside the B802400 contour-lag hunt: at 2026-08-26 21:28:33Z an AUTO capture recorded windowMeanMs 288.6/slowFraction 0.67/ratio 17.3 — a real, currently-in-progress lag. The MANUAL capture 0.6 seconds later, from the SAME tab with the SAME frame history (frames 1891 vs 1892, longTasks 141 vs 142), recorded windowMeanMs 16.1/slowFraction 0/ratio 0.96 — a clean reading, because the lag had already passed. Minted **B807409** from this branch's reserved block B807408–B807423 · V453152–V453167 against `origin/main` b59dae8. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `perfRecorder`, `manual capture`, `windowMeanMs`, `worstWindow`, `sustain window`: no prior item touches what a MANUAL capture reads versus an AUTO one — B265536/B265540/B265541 (delivery tracking, no-frames note, the frame-floor ladder) are all about what happens to a capture ONCE taken, never about which window it reads. Net-new.)*
`✅` **Done — implemented and unit-tested this session, reproducing the owner's exact reported numbers. Verify: sandbox.**
- Verify: sandbox — this is a pure state-machine defect (which window of already-retained frame history a capture reads), fully reproducible and provable with a scripted frame series; no browser, no GIS, no auth needed. ATTEMPT-BEFORE-YOU-PARK applies and was followed: driven directly rather than filed as `Verify: live`.
- **ROOT CAUSE, read directly from `perfTrigger.js`/`perfRecorder.js`.** `triggerState(s).windowMeanMs` is the LIVE sustain window `feedFrame` maintains — a rolling ~2-second (`sustainMs`) buffer of the MOST RECENT frames. `fire()` (the AUTO-capture trigger) explicitly **RESETS** that window the instant it fires (`s.winHead = s.winTail = s.winN = 0`), so the next few seconds of frames rebuild it from scratch. `perfRecorder.js`'s `capture()` used `ts.windowMeanMs`/`ts.slowFraction` — that same LIVE window — for a MANUAL capture's headline numbers (`windowMeanMs: kind === "auto" ? v.windowMeanMs : ts.windowMeanMs`). A manual press taken shortly after an auto-fire (or after any lag has simply ended on its own) reads a freshly-reset window that has only had time to refill with FAST, recovered frames — reporting the tab as smooth exactly when the owner pressed the button believing it was not.
- **THE FIX — read the FULL retained history, not just the live 2-second window.** `worstWindow(times, deltas, {spanMs, minFrames, slowBar})` (new, `perfTrigger.js`) is a pure two-pointer sliding-window-maximum scan over the recorder's already-retained frame track (`ringOrderSince(_frames, since)`, up to `captureWindowMs` — tens of seconds, far wider than the live 2-second sustain window) — it returns the highest-mean `spanMs`-wide sub-window found ANYWHERE in that history, using the SAME `sustainMs`/`sustainMinFrames` shape the live trigger's own window uses so "a window" means the same thing in both readings. `perfRecorder.js`'s `capture()` now computes this for EVERY capture (auto and manual alike) over the same `order`/`deltas`/`times` it already builds, and reports it alongside the existing live reading as five new fields: `worstWindowMeanMs`, `worstWindowSlowFraction`, `worstWindowRatio`, `worstWindowFrames`, `worstWindowAtMs` (the last one a relative offset into the capture window, the same convention `gaps`/`tasks` already use) — so a reader gets BOTH "how it's running right now" (unchanged) AND "the worst it got in the last stretch," clearly two different numbers rather than one number silently meaning two different things depending on when the button was pressed.
- **THE PRIVACY ALLOWLIST WAS UPDATED, NOT BYPASSED** — the five new fields were added to `CAPTURE_NUMERIC_KEYS` in `perfCapture.js` and populated in `buildCapture()` through the existing `num()` helper (which already omits any non-finite value, so a capture with too little retained history to find a worst window simply carries none of the five keys — never a fabricated zero).
- **VERIFIED — `test/perfWorstWindow.test.js` (6 new tests):** null/degenerate-input handling; picking out an obviously-worse window among fast neighbours; `minFrames` never letting a too-small window win, even beside a single huge spike; `slowFraction` computed correctly against a supplied `slowBar` (and omitted when none is given); and the exact reported scenario reproduced end to end — a ~2-second bad window (mean over the slow bar, matching the real 288.6 ms/0.67 report) followed by ~0.6 s of recovered fast frames, where `worstWindow()` still finds and returns the bad window (anchored at when it actually happened) while a LIVE-window-only reading over the same final state — the pre-fix behavior, computed inline in the test for direct comparison — lands on the recovered tail instead, reproducing the exact defect. `npx eslint` clean on every touched file; `test/perfRecorder.test.js` (47 tests, incl. the structural no-per-frame-allocation guard, which `worstWindow` is correctly excluded from — it runs once per capture, not once per frame) and the broader perf suites (`perfBudgetPolicy`, `perfBudgets`, `perfInstrument`) all pass unmodified.
- Files: `src/shared/telemetry/perfTrigger.js` (`worstWindow`, new), `src/shared/telemetry/perfRecorder.js` (`capture()` wiring), `src/shared/telemetry/perfCapture.js` (allowlist + `buildCapture()`), `test/perfWorstWindow.test.js` (new).
- Base: `origin/main` @ `b59dae8`.

- **ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by reading the code (not guessed): the PLANNER CANVAS never hits this bug at all.** `SitePlanner.jsx` draws a centerline road through its own `roadStripRing`/`roadDenseCenterline` (buffers the tessellated centerline by `travelW + 2*curb` via `metesAndBounds.bufferPolyline`) — it never calls `elRingFeet`. `elRingFeet` (the generic "points, or a w/h/rot box" outline) is called from exactly three places: `MapFinder.jsx` (the reported bug), `lib/kmzExport.js`, `lib/multiStyle.js`.
- **ADJACENT CASE CHECKED, per the brief's own instruction — the KMZ (Google Earth) export was NOT affected.** `kmzExport.js` already had its own `elToRingFeet(el)` wrapper (referencing B596) that special-cases `el.type==="road" && el.pts` by buffering the centerline exactly like the planner does, falling back to `elRingFeet` for everything else — and the KMZ polygon-export path (`siteToFeatures`) already called `elToRingFeet`, never the bare `elRingFeet`. **`multiStyle.js` is also unaffected**: its `selectionRingFeet` already special-cases a centerline road (`Array.isArray(o.pts) && !o.points`) BEFORE it would ever reach `elRingFeet`, returning the raw centerline as an open polyline for selection chrome — so `elRingFeet`'s road branch is dead code on that path today.
- **THE FIX consolidates rather than re-derives:** `elToRingFeet` (same formula: `bufferPolyline(roadCenterline(el.pts, el.vtx, {}), max(1, travelW + 2*curb))`, curb defaulting to 0 when absent — unchanged from the proven KMZ formula) now lives in `planStyle.js` beside `elRingFeet`; `kmzExport.js` imports and re-exports it instead of defining its own copy (its `roadCenterline`/`bufferPolyline` imports, used nowhere else in that file, were removed); `MapFinder.jsx`'s `showPlans` effect calls `elToRingFeet` instead of `elRingFeet`. The planner canvas (`SitePlanner.jsx`) was **not touched** — its own `roadStripRing` is a separate, junction-aware (`sharpAt`/`trim`) implementation used by 85 call sites across that file, and extracting it was judged too large a blast radius for this session; `elToRingFeet` deliberately mirrors its FORMULA without importing FROM it.
- **PROVEN RED then GREEN**, `test/planStyle.test.js`: a fixture matching the reported production shape (travelW 40, curb 1, ~2,000 ft centerline, stored bbox 4974.38x262.92 ft) — `elRingFeet` alone reproduces the bbox-area defect (pinned as a mutation check); `elToRingFeet` returns a ring whose area is within 0.5x-2x of `centerline_length x (travelW+2*curb)` and more than 5x smaller than the bbox. A 2-point legacy road (no travelW/curb) and every non-road element are asserted BYTE-IDENTICAL to the old `elRingFeet` output. `test/kmzExport.test.js`'s existing 39 tests (incl. its own `elToRingFeet` suite) pass unchanged post-move.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/planStyle.js` (+`elToRingFeet`), `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/kmzExport.js` (removed local copy, re-exports the shared one), `src/workspaces/site-planner/MapFinder.jsx` (call site), `test/planStyle.test.js` (new, 5 tests).
- Base: `origin/main` @ `1180af40`.

### B834576 — Every element polygon on the map route binds its own identical sticky tooltip — up to ~157 duplicate `L.Tooltip` objects per site `[Site Planner / map]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-28. Measured production element counts cited in the brief: Richfield "Concept A BN" 156, "Concept A (copy)" 156, Schiel "Plan 1" 138, Silvestri 116/115/110. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `bindTooltip`, `sitesLayerRef`, `showPlans`, `FeatureGroup`: no prior item covers the map-route site-plan render effect. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — one `L.featureGroup()` per site now carries the click/contextmenu/tooltip binding ONCE; every parcel and element polygon is added as a plain child (still individually `interactive` for hit-testing), never bound to its own tooltip.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **MECHANISM: `L.FeatureGroup` propagates every child layer's mouse/click/contextmenu events to itself** (confirmed by reading the installed Leaflet 1.9 source: `FeatureGroup.addLayer` calls `layer.addEventParent(this)`, and the Tooltip mixin's own `openTooltip` has a dedicated `instanceof FeatureGroup` branch specifically for this pattern — it is Leaflet's documented, supported mechanism, not a workaround). Binding `tip`/`openSiteNow`/`onCtx` on the group before any child exists still works correctly once children are added.
- **REPRODUCED FOR REAL, per the task's own instruction — not assumed.** `ui-audit/verify-map-plan-render.mjs` seeds 5 sites in logged-out localStorage at the task's own measured element counts (156/156/138/116/115), drives a real headless Chromium to zoom 15+, and confirms hovering across 6 distinct element polygons within one site all show the ONE shared tooltip with the correct site name (pre-fix and post-fix both pass this — see the note below on what does NOT distinguish the two).
- **⛔ ONE THING THIS DOES NOT CHANGE, stated so it isn't re-litigated: Leaflet closes+reopens its bound tooltip's DOM node on every mouseout/mouseover pair regardless of whether 1 or 157 Tooltip OBJECTS are bound** (`_openTooltip`'s `_prepareOpen` unconditionally reopens on a source change) — that DOM churn is Leaflet's own per-child-crossing behavior, not something a shared binding removes. The actual fix is the OBJECT COUNT: one `L.Tooltip` (and one `.on("click"/"contextmenu")` registration) per site instead of up to ~157 separate ones, each with its own listener closures — real memory/construction cost, and part of what B834580's rebuild-cost measurement captures.

### B834579 — Map-route element strokes are a flat 1px at every zoom 15-21, reading as a mesh of hairlines when zoomed out `[Site Planner / map]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #ui  *(owner chat block 2026-08-28. Minted **B834579** from the same reserved block. DEDUPE-FIRST: no prior item.)*

- **⛔ DELIBERATELY NOT a live per-zoom-tick recompute, and this is a real engineering tradeoff, stated rather than silently taken:** the effect that builds this layer explicitly does NOT depend on `zoom` (see its own B64 comment: a rebuild mid-gesture drops the path a press landed on, silently swallowing the click). A per-tick `setStyle` across hundreds of paths on every zoom frame was considered and rejected — it would add live per-tick work to exactly the hot path B834580 was built to protect. So the stroke weight is resolved at the zoom the layer was last (re)built at (crossing PLAN_ZOOM, or any other change to this effect's deps — filtering, selection, the site list); it does not continue thinning/fattening as the user zooms further without a rebuild. This fixes the reported case (hairline mesh at the low end, right where a plan first becomes visible) without adding a new perf risk.
- **Confirmed via a real browser render:** stroke-width read off an element `<path>` — flat `1` at both a low and a high zoom pre-fix; `0.5` at the PLAN_ZOOM crossing and `1.5` after a rebuild forced at zoom ~21 (via a real status-filter toggle, not a synthetic call) post-fix.

### B834580 — The map-route saved-site rebuild is the same synchronous `Path._project` cost B802400 round 5 fixed for the contour layer `[Site Planner / map / perf]` (bug) #site-planner #gis #perf  *(owner chat block 2026-08-28, citing #1200/B802400 round 5's mechanism by name and instructing reuse of `paintSchedule.js` rather than a second scheduler. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched for `paintSchedule`, `runBudgeted`, `PAINT_FRAME_BUDGET_MS`: `terrainLayers.js` is the one existing consumer; MapFinder's saved-site effect had none. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — reused `paintSchedule.js`'s `runBudgeted` (the exact primitive B802400 round 5 built), no second scheduler.** The saved-site layer group is now added to the map EMPTY, then every polygon construct+add — the expensive part, since Leaflet's `Path.onAdd` projects a ring synchronously the instant it's added to a layer already on the map — is queued as one op and drained a bounded time-slice at a time, yielding via a genuine `MessageChannel` macrotask between slices (the same idiom `terrainLayers.js` uses, and for the documented reason: a `requestAnimationFrame` continuation gets folded into the SAME frame as Leaflet's own queued redraw, so it can't actually hand control back between slices).
- Verify: sandbox
- **CANCELLATION**, since this rebuild can now legitimately still be running when the effect fires again (deps changing mid-paint): an epoch ref (`sitesPaintEpochRef`) bumped at the start of every `build()`; any in-flight budgeted continuation from a superseded build checks its captured epoch and silently stops rather than racing to populate/replace `sitesLayerRef.current`.
- **REAL BEFORE/AFTER NUMBER, honestly scoped.** At the task's own literal production counts (5 sites, 778 elements — matching Richfield/Schiel/Silvestri), this fast headless sandbox never crosses the browser's ~50ms long-task threshold at all, even pre-fix (max single animation-frame gap 33.4ms) — an honest property of this environment (no concurrent GIS/tile decode, presumably faster hardware than the report was filed from), not evidence the mechanism doesn't matter, since the blocking cost scales with element count by construction (confirmed by reading `LayerGroup.onAdd`: it iterates every child in one synchronous loop). `ui-audit/diagnose-map-plan-zoom-cost.mjs` proves the scaling directly at 10 sites x 300 = 3,000 elements (a deliberate stress multiple, run specifically to produce an observable number in this sandbox): **pre-fix 1 long task at 88.0ms, max frame gap 83.3ms · post-fix 0 long tasks, max frame gap 50.0ms** (right at the scheduler's own 40ms budget plus overhead, as expected).
- **NOT dropped:** the brief said to ship this "only if the road fix [B834581] does not already collapse the polygon count enough to make it moot" — it does not: B834581 changes each road's SHAPE (a thin ribbon instead of a box), not the total polygon COUNT, so the per-element synchronous-add cost this item addresses is unchanged by that fix.
- **Simplified footprint (draw boundary + building masses only, skip the rest), COSTED per the brief's request rather than assumed:** would cut the per-site polygon count roughly in half on a typical plan (buildings are a large but not dominant share of `els` on the fixture sites here) — real savings, but it changes what the map shows (parking/paving/landscape/detention would vanish from the overview entirely) and was judged a product decision outside a defect-fix session; **not shipped**, flagged here as a recommendation rather than assumed away.
- Files: `src/workspaces/site-planner/MapFinder.jsx` (`sitesPaintEpochRef`, `scheduleSaveSitesFrame`, the `ops`/`runBudgeted` rework). Tests: `ui-audit/diagnose-map-plan-zoom-cost.mjs` (new).

### B839888 — Escape doesn't get the owner out of the parcel editing tool — no clear way out `[Site Planner / parcel]` (bug) #site-planner #parcel #keyboard #ui  *(owner, verbatim: "escape doesnt work on getting out of this parcel editing tool, and theres no clear way out so lets address, i think escape would be enough, idk?" — then, narrowing, "i was splitting a parcel and couldnt get out of the splitting it option." Minted **B839888** from this branch's reserved block against `origin/main` a563614. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `keyScopeVerdict`, `focusScope`, `TEXT_ENTRY_TAGS`, `guaranteed`: **not a recurrence of B792384** (that item was an UNDECLARED key — a bare "c" — falling through a guard it should have been caught by; this is the opposite direction, a DECLARED "guaranteed" key being wrongly refused by a guard it should have passed). **Not a recurrence of B1125** either — B1125 built the Escape sweep and wrote "GUARANTEED escape hatch" in a comment, but never made the guarantee a checked property; this closes that gap. Not B311 (parcelSelect's click-through behavior — separate, see B839889) or B720 (merge-pick — unaffected by this fix's mechanism, verified below). Net-new.)*
`[x]` **AUDIT-FIRST: Escape WAS already wired** — `SitePlanner.jsx`'s big Escape branch (~line 6344) already clears `splitPath`/`mergePick`/`boundaryEdit`/every in-progress draw-tool draft and resets `tool` to `"select"`; nothing there was broken. **The real defect is upstream of it, in the shared key-scope gate that runs before ANY branch fires** (`keyScopeVerdict` in `site-planner/lib/keyContract.js`, fed by `shared/keyboard/keyScope.js`), and it is TWO bugs in the same gate:
- Verify: sandbox
- **BUG 1 — any `<input>` was classified as a genuine text-entry FIELD purely by TAG, `type` never checked.** `TEXT_ENTRY_TAGS.includes("INPUT")` (and the parallel `isTextControl` used by the focus latch) answered FIELD for a **checkbox** exactly like a real text box — and the Parcels panel's per-row "Active" toggle (the owner's screenshot: "inputs and checkboxes" visible) IS a checkbox. `keyScopeVerdict`'s FIELD branch then refused EVERY declared key unconditionally, `escape` included. Fixed the same way this repo already fixed the analogous SLIDER/PICKER cases (B464048/NEW-1 — "a guard may only refuse a key the focused control can really use"): `NON_TEXT_INPUT_TYPES` (checkbox/radio/button/submit/reset/image/file/color/hidden) now falls through to the ordinary CHROME/CANVAS latch, exactly like a focused `<button>` already did — a genuine text-like `<input>` type (text/number/email/search/tel/url/password/date/…) is untouched.
- **BUG 2 — even a genuinely focused text field refusing Escape buys nothing, because Escape types no character.** Per B1125's own words ("the GUARANTEED escape hatch"), FIELD's blanket refusal was never supposed to include it — it just did, because the FIELD branch never checked which key it was refusing. `escape` (and ONLY `escape` — a new declared `guaranteed: true` on its `KEY_CONTRACT` entry, not a blanket `entry.scope === "app"` exemption) now survives FIELD scope; undo/redo/shortcuts stay refused there on purpose, because a text box's own native Ctrl+Z must still win while it is genuinely focused. A PICKER's own Escape-closes-the-dropdown consumption (`CONTROL_CONSUMES`) is untouched too — that case self-resolves and was never "stuck".
- **⛔ MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED — which reproduction order actually triggers it, and it corrects this item's own filing brief.** A trace of the code suggested "touch the checkbox, THEN arm Split, THEN cut, THEN Escape" as the repro and asked for it to be proven RED first; driven for real in headless Chromium, it did **not** reproduce on the pre-fix build — arming Split means clicking the ✂ Split **button**, which is itself focusable and takes `document.activeElement` off the checkbox before Escape is pressed, landing on BUTTON → CHROME scope, which already allowed Escape through. What DOES reproduce (proven RED pre-fix, GREEN post-fix) is the checkbox taking focus **while the cut is already live** — exactly the owner's screenshot, checkboxes and the red cut line on screen together — with Escape pressed right after, so the checkbox is still `document.activeElement` at that instant. The suggested `fieldEdit: true` (persisted-latch) condition was also checked directly and found harmless on its own: that state resolves to CHROME, which already unconditionally allows a `scope:"app"` entry; FIELD, driven only by the CURRENTLY focused node, was the one real gate. Full measurement on the record in the e2e spec's own header comment.
- **Second bug flagged and now moot, not separately patched:** a refused Escape was SILENT (`shouldHintRefusal` never hints a non-mutating key) — exactly the case where silence is wrong, since the user presses Escape *because* they are stuck. Fixing BUG 2 removes the refusal itself for the case that mattered, so there is nothing left to hint; the remaining silent PICKER case is a working dropdown closing, not a stuck user, and hinting it would be a false alarm.
- **Adjacent modes checked, not just the one hit** — the fix is in the ONE shared gate every mode's Escape branch sits behind, so Draw / Measure / Reshape (`boundaryEdit`) / Trace / Cross-section / Easement / Print-frame / Overlay-calibrate all inherit it together; driven live for Split (the reported case) and Merge/Combine (`mergePick`) via `e2e/parcel-escape-during-split.spec.js`, both proven working with a checkbox holding focus.
- **Proven RED before the fix, in both the pure function and the real app**, per house rule: `test/keyContract.test.js`'s two new/changed FIELD-scope assertions fail on the pre-fix source (`expected true to be false` / `expected undefined to be true`); `e2e/parcel-escape-during-split.spec.js`'s discriminating case fails identically against a pre-fix production build served locally, and passes once the fix is restored and rebuilt.
- Files: `src/shared/keyboard/keyScope.js` (`NON_TEXT_INPUT_TYPES`, `isTextInputType`, `focusScope`, `isTextControl`, `touchFactsOf`'s field-group query), `src/workspaces/site-planner/lib/keyContract.js` (`escape` entry's `guaranteed: true`, `keyScopeVerdict`'s FIELD branch). Tests: `test/keyContract.test.js` (extended), `e2e/parcel-escape-during-split.spec.js` (new).
- Base: `origin/main` @ `a563614`.

### B844416 — Long-task attribution drops the source file whenever the function name is empty — every LoAF entry from an anonymous callback reads only "FrameRequestCallback" `[shared/telemetry]` (bug) #perf #telemetry  *(repro handed in directly: `perfRecorder.js`'s `observeTasks` built a script's name from `top.sourceFunctionName || top.invoker || top.sourceURL || ""`. `sourceFunctionName` is empty for every ANONYMOUS function — which covers every Leaflet-scheduled callback and every app-level requestAnimationFrame arrow — so the chain fell through to `invoker`, a non-empty CATEGORY constant (`"FrameRequestCallback"`) for all of them, and `sourceURL` was never reached at all. Measured in the owner's real production capture, 2026-08-29 20:44 UTC (build `396be34`, plan `smt7q6ar8egz`, `event:perfcap` in `client_errors`): the four worst blocks, 515–606 ms each, all carried `ltNames` index 7 = `FrameRequestCallback` and nothing else — "an animation frame ran", true of most of the app, not real attribution. Minted **B844416** from this branch's reserved block B844416–B844431 against `origin/main` 7a64249. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `sourceFunctionName`, `FrameRequestCallback`, `attributionLabel`, `sourceCharPosition`: B802400 round 5 cites the same `FrameRequestCallback` symptom string but as evidence for a DIFFERENT, already-fixed defect (unscheduled canvas paint applying a tile burst inside one rAF call stack) — that fix does not touch the attribution logic itself, so this is net-new, not a recurrence.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — when `sourceFunctionName` is empty, the recorder now names the script by its `invoker` CATEGORY plus a compact SOURCE LOCATION (the script file's basename + its character offset)** — `FrameRequestCallback:index-4f2a.js:81422` instead of a bare `FrameRequestCallback` repeated for every anonymous long frame in the app, so two different anonymous callbacks are finally distinguishable in a capture.
- Verify: sandbox

### B866784 — Formula engine: kill the quadratic whole-column aggregate + add 14 financial functions (NPV/XNPV/IRR/XIRR/MIRR/PMT/IPMT/PPMT/RATE/NPER/FV/PV/CUMIPMT/CUMPRINC) `[shared/formula]` (bug + feature) #perf #scheduler  *(dispatched as a prerequisite for a new Model/pro-forma module — bundled in one session deliberately, since both changes touch the same file and the same `FUNCTIONS` registry. An earlier audit session had prototyped and measured both on a clone; this session verified those findings against the actual code and productionised them. Minted **B866784** from this branch's reserved block B866784–B866799 against `origin/main` bbfee52. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `colArray`, `quadratic`, `NPV`, `IRR`, `PMT`, `financial function`: no prior item touches the formula engine's aggregate cost or its function registry's financial coverage. Net-new.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED — both halves.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **PART 1 (the defect, confirmed real):** `colArray()` rebuilt the ENTIRE column array from `ctx.rows` on every call, and the host (`computeFormulaValues` in `public/sequence/index.html`) calls `evaluateFormula()` once per row against the SAME shared `rows` array — so every whole-column aggregate was O(rows) work × O(rows) calls = **O(rows²)**. Measured on this machine before any fix, reproducing the brief's numbers closely: `SUM([Cost])` 2000r=133.6ms/5000r=330.8ms · `COUNTIF([Cost],">50")` 770.2ms/4606.4ms · `SUMIF([Cost],">50",[Budget])` 913.3ms/5150.4ms · `XLOOKUP([Duration],[Cost],[Task])` 94.0ms/539.9ms.
- **THE FIX, two tiers, both keyed on the `ctx.rows` array's own object IDENTITY via `WeakMap` (no manual invalidation — a fresh recalc pass builds a fresh rows array, so a stale entry can never be read; it is simply garbage once nothing references the old array):**
  1. `colArrayCache` — memoizes the built `[Column]→values[]` array itself per (rows array, column key). Fixes the O(rows) rebuild for all 13 range-aware functions unconditionally.
  2. `rngResultCache` — memoizes the ENTIRE result of a range-aware call per (AST node, rows array) whenever **every argument is row-invariant** — decided via a declared `RANGE_ARG_POSITIONS` table (which argument slots each of the 13 functions actually reads as a whole-column RANGE, lifted from each function's own existing implementation, not guessed) plus a recursive, memoized structural scan (`isRowInvariant`) of the remaining scalar arguments. This is what gets COUNTIF/SUMIF from "cached array, still O(rows) criteria-scan per row" down to "computed once, O(1) lookup for every other row."
  3. `parseFormula` also gained an LRU-ish cache keyed on source text (the host re-tokenizes/re-parses the SAME formula string once per row) — this is *also* what makes the two caches above actually hit: the SAME parsed AST node objects recur across a pass's per-row calls only because parsing is now cached.
  4. `TODAY`/`NOW`/`WORKDAY`/`NETWORKDAYS` are always treated as row-variant (conservatively) since they read `ctx.today`/`ctx.calendar`, which aren't part of the cache key.
- **⛔ THE TRAP NAMED IN THE BRIEF, hit and fixed exactly as warned:** a first draft that classified invariance by node SHAPE (any bare `[Col]` arg = hoistable) breaks `XLOOKUP([Duration],[Cost],[Task])` — the FIRST argument is a scalar this-row lookup value, not a range, so hoisting it freezes row 0's answer onto every row. Invariance is decided **per argument POSITION, per function** (`RANGE_ARG_POSITIONS`), never by shape alone. Mutation-proven: deliberately mis-declaring `XLOOKUP`'s target position (or `COUNTIF`'s criteria position) as a range immediately breaks a dedicated regression test built for exactly this trap (`test/formula.test.js` → "row-invariant caching — correctness under the SAME shared rows array").
- **ACCEPTANCE, beaten:** byte-identical results old-vs-new across all 13 range-aware functions, 28 formulas × 200 rows (the brief's own bar was 11/11 × 200 rows), including deliberately adversarial cases (row-varying MATCH/XLOOKUP target, row-varying COUNTIF/SUMIF criteria including a BARE-COLUMN criteria arg, row-varying INDEX position, a nested rng-in-rng call, an `IF` alternating between two invariant branches, and a cached `#REF!`/`#N/A` error faithfully re-thrown on every row).
- **MEASURED AFTER (this machine, not the brief's clone — numbers will differ by hardware/JIT, that's expected):** `SUM([Cost])` 2000r=4.0ms/5000r=7.3ms (**45×**) · `COUNTIF([Cost],">50")` 3.2ms/8.2ms (**562×**) · `SUMIF([Cost],">50",[Budget])` 2.5ms/5.3ms (**972×**) · `XLOOKUP([Duration],[Cost],[Task])` 8.0ms/16.9ms (**32×**). Confirmed genuinely linear (not merely "fast at this size"): SUM at 40,000 rows runs in 23ms (ms/row *falls* as rows grow, the opposite of a quadratic signature). A generous, non-flaky regression guard (`test/formula.test.js`, following the interleaved-min-of-REPS pattern already used in `test/pondViewIndependence.test.js`) asserts 8× the rows never costs anywhere near 8²=64× the time.
- **PART 2 — 14 financial functions added as ORDINARY `{ fn: ... }` entries (none range-aware), taking plain scalar arguments exactly like the existing 95:** `NPV`, `XNPV`, `IRR`, `XIRR`, `MIRR`, `PMT`, `IPMT`, `PPMT`, `RATE`, `NPER`, `FV`, `PV`, `CUMIPMT`, `CUMPRINC`. `XNPV`/`XIRR` take interleaved `(value,date)` scalar pairs (no array type exists in this engine). Every PMT/PV/FV/NPER formula is one rearrangement of the single annuity identity `PV*(1+r)^n + PMT*(1+r·type)*((1+r)^n−1)/r + FV = 0` (documented in `formula.js` next to the code, not memorized). Newton-Raphson with a bracket-search bisection fallback (`solveRoot`) serves IRR/XIRR/RATE.
- **⛔ VALIDATION CAUGHT A REAL BUG the brief's own warning predicted the SHAPE of, though not this exact one:** the first `IPMT` derivation returned the interest **charged** (a positive "amount owed grew by") instead of the interest **paid** (a cash outflow, negative — matching `PMT`'s own sign convention). The trivially-true `IPMT(n)+PPMT(n)==PMT` identity did **not** catch it (since `PPMT` is defined as `PMT−IPMT`, a one-sided sign flip in `IPMT` is silently absorbed by `PPMT` and the sum stays correct) — it was caught by the two identities that check against an INDEPENDENT external total: "sum of `PPMT` over the full term == −PV" and "`CUMIPMT`+`CUMPRINC` over the full term == `nper×PMT`". Hand-traced against a 1-period, 10%-rate, $1,000 loan (`PMT`=−1100 must decompose into `IPMT`=−100, `PPMT`=−1000) to confirm the fix rather than trust the invariant alone.
- **Per the brief's explicit instruction — where a remembered Excel constant would disagree with a structural invariant, the invariant wins, stated out loud:** no such disagreement arose here (unlike the prototype's own PMT experience, cited in the brief) — every invariant below passed against the derived formulas with no numeric constant consulted from memory at all. Invariant results (`test/formula.test.js`, 21 new test cases, all passing): `IPMT(n)+PPMT(n)==PMT` for every period, both END/BEGIN conventions ✅ · `IPMT(1)==0` under BEGIN (type=1) — the classic off-by-one ✅ · sum of `PPMT` over the full term `==−PV` (FV=0) ✅ · `FV==0` at the end of a fully amortizing schedule ✅ · `NPER`/`RATE` round-trip through `PMT` (both directions) ✅ · `RATE` converges from a supplied guess on a 30-year/360-period mortgage-shaped case ✅ · `CUMIPMT+CUMPRINC == nper×PMT`, and full-term `CUMPRINC == −PV` ✅ · `CUMIPMT`/`CUMPRINC` reject an invalid period range or domain exactly like Excel's documented `#NUM!` conditions (rate/nper/pv ≤ 0 · start<1 · end<start · type∉{0,1} — verified against Microsoft's own CUMIPMT reference, cited in-line in `formula.js`, rather than assumed) ✅ · `NPV(IRR(cfs)) == 0` (the classic Excel identity — holds despite `NPV`/`IRR` indexing cash flows from different periods, confirmed algebraically in a code comment, not just empirically) ✅ · `XNPV(XIRR(...)) == 0` with real calendar dates ✅ · `MIRR` reduces to plain `IRR` for exactly two cash flows, for ANY finance/reinvest rate (the sign-convention check) ✅ · `MIRR` on a multi-period case cross-checked against its own documented definition computed independently in the test, not trusted from the engine ✅ · `PV`/`FV`/`PMT` round-trip the annuity identity ✅ · rate=0 degenerates to plain division with no NaN ✅.
- **House rules honored:** `node scripts/sync-sequence-formula.mjs` run after every edit (`public/sequence/index.html` re-inlined, `test/formula-inline-sync.test.js` green); `MAP.md` regenerated (`node scripts/build-map.mjs`) for the new exported names threaded through. `git merge origin/main` used throughout, never rebase.
- **Scope held exactly to the brief:** engine + its tests only — no grid, UI, or new module/surface touched.
- Files: `src/shared/formula/formula.js` (`colArrayCache`, `rngResultCache`, `parseCache`/`parseFormulaUncached`, `RANGE_ARG_POSITIONS`, `isRowInvariant`/`isCallInvariant`, `finishCallResult`; the 14 financial `FUNCTIONS` entries + `pmtOf`/`fvOf`/`pvOf`/`nperOf`/`balOf`/`ipmtOf`/`solveRoot`/`findSignChange`/`irrOf`/`xirrOf`/`rateOf`/`mirrOf`/`xnpvPairs`/`cumArgs` helpers; `FUNCTION_HELP` entries), `public/sequence/index.html` (re-synced mirror). Tests: `test/formula.test.js` (39 new test cases across three new `describe` blocks: row-invariant-caching correctness, a not-quadratic perf guard, and the 14 financial functions — 122 total in the file, all passing). No new files, no new module.

### B884688 — Formula engine: A1 cell references (A1/$A$1/A1:B10) alongside the existing structured [Column] refs `[shared/formula]` (feature) #scheduler  *(dispatched as the second prerequisite for the new Model/pro-forma module, immediately following B866784 on the same file — an audit had already mapped the exact surface (the two reference-resolution chokepoints, the LOG10 collision, the address bounds); this session verified that map against the actual post-#1237 code and implemented it. Minted **B884688** from this branch's reserved block B884688–B884703 against `origin/main` 6c5d27d (fetched fresh at ship time — main had moved twice since the branch started, neither touching `formula.js`). DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open/⏳Verify/Done for `A1`, `cell reference`, `colArray`, `rangeArray`, `parseRefText`, `rewriteFormulaForCopy`, `Model module`: no prior item touches A1 addressing; B866784 (above) is the prerequisite this builds on, not a duplicate. **Note for whoever picks up the Model module itself:** `next-id --against-main` surfaced a concurrent unmerged branch, `planyr-peers/claude/model-module-spreadsheet-p7t2pp` — that is presumably the module this PR unblocks; its actual `ctx.grid` host contract (shape, cell-store representation) was not visible to this session and the shape documented below is this session's own design, not a negotiated one — worth reconciling on sight.)*
`[x]` **SHIPPED.**
- Verify: sandbox
- **Grammar implemented, exactly the six forms asked for:** `A1` · `$A$1` · `A$1` · `$A1` · `A1:B10` · `$A$1:$B$10`, case-insensitive, coexisting in the same formula as `[Column]` structured refs. Cross-sheet (`Sheet1!A1`) is explicitly out of scope per the brief and fails loudly (`#ERROR! unexpected character "!"`) rather than silently mis-parsing — agreeing with the brief's own call that a single-sheet module doesn't need it yet.
- **The surface really was as small as the brief predicted, with one further reduction found during implementation:** token types +1 (`:`) plus a new `ref`/`errlit` token class for `$`-bearing addresses and the `#REF!` literal (a bare `A1`/`LOG10` deliberately stays an `id` token — see the collision note below); AST nodes +2 (`ref`, `range`, plus a small `errLiteral` for `#REF!` — see the #REF! note below); the two resolution chokepoints named in the brief — `evalNode`'s `case "col"` (now also `case "ref"`) and `colArray()` (now also resolving `range` nodes via a new `rangeArray()`) — plus the four collector guards, unified behind one `isRangeArg(n)` predicate instead of four separately-edited one-liners. **The further reduction: `RANGE_ARG_POSITIONS`/`isRowInvariant`/`isCallInvariant` (B866784's hoisting table) needed ZERO changes** — `isRowInvariant`'s `switch` already defaults unrecognized node types to `false` (not row-invariant), so a `ref`/`range` argument in a `rng` call falls through to the existing non-hoisted path automatically and correctly, with no new case needed. Verified this is a safe default, not just a convenient one: hoisting a grid-cell read via `rngResultCache` (keyed on `ctx.rows`) would risk a stale answer if a host ever reused the same `ctx.rows` reference across two different `ctx.grid` states, since that cache has no `ctx.grid` term in its key — leaving it unhoisted sidesteps that hazard entirely rather than extending the cache key to cover a case with no current caller. `colArray`/`rangeArray` still avoid the O(rows²)-shaped defect class B866784 fixed: `rangeArray` gained its own `ctx.grid`-keyed cache, the direct analogue of `colArrayCache`, so many cells summing overlapping ranges in one recalc pass don't each re-walk the grid.
- **Collision handling — LOG10 is confirmed, LIVE, as the only collision, and Excel's own rule resolves it:** re-checked programmatically against the actual current registry (95 original + 14 financial = 109 names, not eyeballed) — `LOG10` is the sole name that also parses as a valid address (column `LOG`=8509, row 10; every other name either carries no trailing digits or, where it does, the letters run resolves past column XFD and is rejected by the same bounds check as any other over-large address). Resolved with Excel's own disambiguation, applied at the single point the parser already had the lookahead for it: the existing "identifier immediately followed by `(`" function-call check runs FIRST (unchanged, still returns immediately, `LOG10(...)` never reaches the reference check); only a bare identifier that is NOT a call and NOT `TRUE`/`FALSE` is then tested against `parseRefText` — so `LOG10(100)` is always the function, bare `LOG10` is always the reference to column LOG row 10. The same ordering is reused verbatim by the rewrite transform below (`isRefEligible`), so the parser and the rewrite can never disagree about what counts as a reference.
- **Bounds rejection — all four named cases confirmed rejected as NAMES (`#NAME?`), not accepted as refs and not producing `#REF!`:** `XFE1` (one column past XFD) · `ABCD1` (too many letters — and measured that the numeric column-value check alone is sufficient to reject every 4+-letter run without a separate length check, since even the smallest 4-letter combination `AAAA`=18279 already exceeds `XFD`=16384) · `A0` (row 0) · `A1048577` (one row past the max). `parseRefText` is the one shared bounds check — `test/formula.test.js` asserts both the end-to-end `#NAME?` behavior and `parseRefText`'s own null/non-null verdict directly, and both were mutation-proved red when the bounds check was disabled.
- **`#REF!` semantics — resolved as a literal-error AST node, not a grid-bounds check, because address-space bounds are already fully handled at parse time (rejected as a name, per above) and there is no OTHER notion of "the sheet's bounds" this engine has visibility into yet (no Model-module grid extent contract exists in this codebase to check against).** The tokenizer now accepts the literal text `#REF!` (case-insensitive) as valid input, evaluating straight to `ferr(FORMULA_ERRORS.REF, …)` — this is what makes `rewriteFormulaForCopy` (below) able to satisfy "must produce #REF!, not a crash and not a silent zero" when a copy/fill shifts a relative reference off the sheet: it writes the literal `#REF!` into the rewritten formula text, exactly as Excel itself does, and the engine now parses that back out to the error rather than choking on `#`/`!` as unrecognized characters. A grid cell that's simply beyond what the host populated (e.g. row 500 on a 50-row sheet) reads as blank, matching Excel's own "beyond the used range" behavior — never `#REF!` by itself.
- **Relative-reference rewrite on copy/fill — built as the brief specified, a pure token-level splice, separately unit-tested with no grid involved:** `rewriteFormulaForCopy(formula, sourceAddr, targetAddr)`. Confirmed: `A1+B1` copied from `A1` to `A5` → `A5+B5`; `$A$1` never moves; `A$1`/`$A1` move only on their relative axis; a range shifts both endpoints together (`A1:B10`→`A2:B11` on a one-row-down copy); a reference shifted below column A or row 1 collapses to `#REF!`; a range with only ONE endpoint pushed off the sheet collapses the WHOLE range to `#REF!` (matching Excel, not just the one bad endpoint); `LOG10(` is never rewritten while a real reference beside or inside it still is; a formula with no A1 refs at all (pure `[Column]`) or a string literal that merely looks like a reference round-trips byte-identical. Deliberately token-level rather than AST-reserialized, specifically so untouched formula text (spacing, string literals, `[Column]` refs, function names) survives byte-for-byte rather than risking a reformat.
- **Row/column INSERT and DELETE ref-shifting was NOT built, per the brief's explicit instruction** — confirmed this is the right call: a fixed-layout pro-forma with a fill handle only ever needs copy/fill, and building it would have meant inventing a sheet-structure-edit contract with no consumer yet.
- **Backward compatibility — proven three ways, not asserted:** (1) all 122 pre-existing `test/formula.test.js` cases pass unchanged; (2) an explicit 48-formula corpus of realistic Schedule/Cost-Estimating-shaped structured-ref and financial formulas evaluated against a checked-out pre-change copy of `formula.js` and the post-change file, byte-identical results on every one, 0 mismatches; (3) the `RANGE_ARG_POSITIONS`/`isRowInvariant`/`isCallInvariant` hoisting table (B866784) has ZERO lines touched in the diff, confirmed by grepping the diff for those identifiers.
- **Mutation-proved, not just written:** 5 of the new tests' guarding assertions were confirmed to go RED under a deliberate, reverted mutation of the code they check — the address-bounds check (5 tests), the LOG10 function-call-vs-reference ordering (2 tests), the `#REF!` literal tokenizer branch (2 tests), `rangeArray`'s column loop (3 tests), and the rewrite transform's off-sheet bounds collapse (4 tests) — each confirmed red under mutation, then reverted and confirmed green again before this item shipped.
- **House rules honored:** `node scripts/sync-sequence-formula.mjs` run after every edit (`public/sequence/index.html` re-inlined, `test/formula-inline-sync.test.js` green); `MAP.md` regenerated for the new exported names (`MAX_COL`, `MAX_ROW`, `parseRefText`, `colLettersToNum`, `colNumToLetters`, `rewriteFormulaForCopy`, plus the internal helpers threaded through the `public/sequence/index.html` mirror's export scan). `git merge origin/main` used throughout (twice — main moved again mid-session, `9aebd8e4`/`6c5d27d`, neither touching this file), never rebase.
- **Scope held exactly to the brief:** grammar, evaluation, and the copy/fill rewrite transform, all in `formula.js` + its mirror + its tests. No Model-module UI, grid-store, or host wiring built — that module's own `ctx.grid` shape is this session's speculative design (documented in the file header) for the next session to reconcile against the actual module.
